title: rf/route-link raises :rf.error/no-frame-context on first render — every example that renders one fails to boot at tip d1e6a707a3
description:
FOUND 2026-09-03 02:55 AUSEST by the rf2-t4jpz PRE-PILOT rehearsal, running the operator half of docs/design/hicasso/product/pilots/workspace.md. Tip d1e6a707a3.

SYMPTOM. A browser build that renders `rf/route-link` anywhere in its tree throws on first render and mounts NOTHING — #app innerHTML length 0, blank page. The throw is a CLJS ExceptionInfo carrying [:rf.error/no-frame-context], :operation :route-link, :recovery :supply-frame, :where re-frame.routing.link/route-link-render. React reports it as 'An error occurred in the <re_frame.core_routing.route_link> component'.

The message text is the standard no-frame-context ladder: 'a frame-scoped route-link ran with no frame context — no carried frame stamp and no established scope...'.

MEASURED ACROSS FOUR APPS, all compiled with 'npx shadow-cljs compile <build>' from implementation/ in a clean full clone of this tip (own node_modules, npm install exit 0), then served as static files over a local HTTP server and loaded in headless Chrome via playwright-core. Every serve root carried index.html, main.js, cljs-runtime/ and examples/_shared/, and every run reported ZERO failed requests, so nothing here is an asset or 404 artefact.

  FAILS  :examples/routing            (examples/capabilities/routing/routing/) — the canonical routing example, 10 route-link sites
  FAILS  :examples/realworld          (examples/real-apps/realworld_http/)     — pilot 1's application
  FAILS  linearlite                   (examples/capabilities/resources/linearlite/) — pilot 2's application, 1 route-link site
  BOOTS  :examples/login              (examples/core/login/)                   — no route-link; #app 643 chars, renders 'Sign in', 0 errors

The login row is the instrument control: the same harness, the same serving method, the same tip, exit 0. So the harness is sound and the discriminator is the presence of a route-link, not the build or the server.

NOT A WORKSPACE ARTEFACT. The failure reproduces identically in-repo (the repo's own shadow-cljs build, the example's own unmodified index.html, all _shared assets present, 0 failed requests) and in a pilot workspace built from :local/root per workspace.md. Both routes, same error, same :where.

NOT A URL ARTEFACT. Loading '/' and '/index.html' fail identically, so it is not the missing SPA push-state fallback.

STRUCTURE LOOKS CORRECT AT THE CALL SITES. realworld_http/core.cljs mounts [rf/frame-root {:id :rf/default ...} [root-view]] and every route-link sits inside a reg-view under root-view; linearlite/core.cljs has the same shape at core.cljs:630. So this is not an obviously mis-wired application — which is what makes three independent applications failing the same way read as a framework regression rather than three app bugs.

WHY IT MATTERS BEYOND THE EXAMPLES. It blocks rf2-t4jpz at hour zero: workspace.md step 5 is an OPERATOR boot check that must pass with the app still on Reagent BEFORE a pilot agent is dispatched, and it fails for BOTH ratified pilots. rf2-hic-063's 2026-09-02 ruling makes that check a precondition of dispatch. It also removes outcome 2's baseline — pilot 1's brief tells the agent 'it works today. Run it before you change anything', which is false at this tip.

NOTE THE BEHAVIOURAL SUITES DO NOT CATCH IT. Both pilot baselines are green at this tip (realworld 4 tests / 123 assertions exit 0; linearlite 10 tests / 51 assertions exit 0). They drive events and read subscriptions without rendering, so a render-time route-link failure is invisible to them. Examples are test-free by policy and the browser smoke coverage is one adapter-level smoke per adapter, so nothing currently renders these three apps in CI.

REPRODUCE. From a clean clone at this tip: cd implementation && npm install && npx shadow-cljs compile :examples/routing; then serve out/examples/routing/ together with examples/capabilities/routing/routing/index.html and examples/_shared/ and open it. Expect a blank page and the ExceptionInfo above. Control: the same procedure on :examples/login renders 'Sign in'.

FILED, NOT FIXED — the rehearsal is a harvest task and re-frame.routing / implementation are held by live workers.
notes:
SHARPENED 2026-09-03 03:10 AUSEST, same rehearsal, and this CORRECTS a reading in the description above.

THE RULE IS EXACT: route-link fails whenever it actually RENDERS. Not 'these apps are broken', not 'dev builds are broken'. Dev and release both fail; the discriminator is solely whether a route-link is on the screen being rendered.

THE DECISIVE PAIR — ONE BUILD, ONE SERVER, TWO URLS. linearlite's release bundle (npx shadow-cljs release app, exit 0, 217 files, 0 warnings), served as static files, loaded twice:

  /             -> matches :linearlite.app/board, board-page renders, NO route-link on screen
                   BOOTS. #app innerHTML 2295 chars, 0 page errors, full board text renders
                   ('Linearlite — optimistic issue board', the three status columns, the
                   armed-failure toggle).

  /index.html   -> matches no route, so root-view falls through to not-found-page, whose
                   single route-link (core.cljs:591, {:to :linearlite.app/board}) renders
                   FAILS. #app innerHTML 0, 1 page error, the same [:rf.error/no-frame-context].

Nothing differs but the URL. That is the cleanest possible isolation and it is why the earlier
'linearlite FAILS' row needs qualifying: the application is fine, the component is not.

THE DEV/RELEASE AXIS IS A RED HERRING — I RAISED IT AND IT IS WRONG. It looked briefly as though
the guard might be a development-only assertion elided by :advanced, because linearlite's release
booted where its dev build had not. That comparison was mine and it was invalid: I had loaded the
dev build at /index.html and the release at /. Corrected, the guard fires under :advanced too —
realworld's release build (exit 0, 332 files, 1.66MB) raises the identical error with the identical
:where. Recording the false trail because it is the natural first hypothesis and the next person
should not spend the same run on it.

FULL MATRIX at tip d1e6a707a3, every row a captured exit code and a headless-Chrome load:

  app                              route-link on loaded screen   build     result
  examples/core/login  /           no (app has none)             dev       BOOTS  (#app 643, 'Sign in')
  examples/capabilities/routing /  yes (10 sites)                dev       FAILS
  examples/capabilities/routing /  yes                           release   FAILS
  realworld_http  / and /index.html yes (navbar, every screen)   dev       FAILS
  realworld_http  /                yes                           release   FAILS
  linearlite  /                    NO                            release   BOOTS  (#app 2295)
  linearlite  /index.html          yes (not-found-page)          release   FAILS

WHAT THIS CHANGES FOR THE FIX. The failing path is the render of re-frame.routing.link/route-link-render
itself, not application wiring, not the frame-root, not the build mode, and not the workspace. Any
application that puts a route-link on screen — which is every routed application — cannot render at
this tip.

WHAT IT CHANGES FOR THE PILOTS. Pilot 1 is blocked outright: realworld's navbar carries route-links on
every screen, so no screen renders. Pilot 2's board route happens to avoid the one site, so its board
DOES render and pilot 2 has a usable baseline screen — but its card-detail work (the authoring half,
which the ruling calls the more important of its two jobs) requires routing to and from a new screen,
which is exactly the surface that fails.

NOTE ON PRIORITY. Filed P0 on the strength of 'no example renders'; the sharpened rule does not soften
it — a routed application cannot show a link to another route.
MAYOR TRIAGE 2026-09-03 03:2x AUSEST. THIS IS THE TOP OF THE DISPATCH QUEUE AND THE ONLY P0 ON THE BOARD.

WHY I AM NOT DISPATCHING IT THIS MINUTE, stated so nobody reads the delay as a judgement about severity: the fleet ceiling is 6 (Mike, in his own words) and all six slots are live. I will not displace a running worker to make room — killing live work strands uncommitted changes, which is the one thing the stranded-sweep rule forbids building around. Three of the six have been running over an hour, so a slot frees on its own; this bead takes it, ahead of every P2 already queued.

WHAT MAKES THIS REPORT UNUSUALLY CREDIBLE, and worth saying because a P0 filed by a rehearsal agent deserves scrutiny rather than reflex: it carries an INSTRUMENT CONTROL. :examples/login has no route-link and BOOTS on the same tip, same harness, same serving method, #app 643 chars, 0 errors — while three apps that DO render a route-link mount nothing at all. So the discriminator is isolated to the presence of a route-link rather than to the build, the server, the assets or the clone. It also rules out two artefact classes explicitly: it reproduces both in-repo and in a :local/root pilot workspace, and "/" and "/index.html" fail identically, so it is not the missing SPA push-state fallback. Zero failed requests on every run.

A POINTER, EXPLICITLY NOT A DIAGNOSIS. I ran one cheap history read and stopped there, because a plausible-looking candidate stated confidently is how this project has burned itself before. Commit aa9e90af7f "hicasso: retire hframe; core admits the pure frame doors inside a refusing extent (rf2-6c12m.13, rf2-t32wg)" is the most recent change touching frame-context admission that a -S search over no-frame-context surfaces. That is a place to START a bisect, nothing more. DO NOT TREAT IT AS THE CAUSE. The honest first step is the bisect the bead earns: find the commit at which :examples/routing stops booting, using the login example as the control at every step.

WHAT THE FIXING WORKER MUST NOT DO: do not "fix" this by wrapping the call sites in a frame context. Three independent applications, each already mounting [rf/frame-root {:id :rf/default ...} [root-view]] with every route-link inside a reg-view under root-view, is the shape of a framework regression, not three app bugs. If the applications turn out genuinely wrong, that is a finding and a much bigger one.

IT ALSO BLOCKS rf2-t4jpz AT HOUR ZERO: workspace.md step 5 is an OPERATOR boot check that must pass with the app still on Reagent before a pilot agent is dispatched, and it fails for both pilots. So the pre-pilot rehearsal cannot proceed past its own first gate until this lands.

FIXED 2026-09-03 by PR #9050 (worker routelink-a). Root cause, bisect and the
browser evidence are on the PR; the load-bearing findings are recorded here so a
fresh maintainer needs nothing else.

BOTH BRIEFED MECHANISMS ARE REFUTED, and the reproduction refutes them by itself.
:examples/routing's root-view is a reg-view whose body is an AMBIENT
@(subscribe [:rf.route/id]) with no explicit frame, and it renders BEFORE any
route-link. The raised error names :operation :route-link / :where
re-frame.routing.link/route-link-render, never a subs site — so the ambient
resolution in root-view had already SUCCEEDED through the React-context tier that
frame-root establishes. The scope was present and readable (refuting "frame-root
no longer establishes the scope"), and require-current-frame! admitted it for
every reg-view in the tree (refuting "the admission changed").

THE CAUSE IS STRUCTURAL, one level up from both. rf/route-link is a defwrapper
(re-frame.core-routing), so its body is (apply <hook-fn> args) — an ORDINARY
FUNCTION CALL. The :routing/route-link hook carried the registered :route/link
view HEAD, so that head ran INSIDE the component the substrate mounted for
rf/route-link itself, instead of becoming a component of its own. A plain Reagent
fn carries no {:contextType frame-context}, so (.-context cmp) was React's empty
default, views.provider/current-frame resolved nil, and route-link-render's
render-time require-current-frame! raised. This is precisely the failure mode
re-frame.views.provider/current-frame's own docstring already describes for plain
fns; nobody had noticed rf/route-link was one.

FIX: publish an element-emitting shim. The hook now returns
[(views/view-head :route/link) props & children], so the head reaches the
substrate as an element TYPE and is componentized exactly as a reg-view view is —
[rf/route-link ...] and [home-page ...] now take one path. The head is resolved
per render through view-head rather than closed over, because it is a property of
(registration x installed substrate) and the reg-view* seed is taken at ns-load
before rf/init! seats an adapter (rf2-8mkmb). SSR untouched. Confined to
implementation/routing/src/re_frame/routing.cljc; no call site was wrapped in a
frame context, and none needed to be.

THE BISECT POINTER IN THE TRIAGE NOTE WAS WRONG, and by two and a half months.
aa9e90af7f (2026-08-30) is NOT the cause. The break is fda84bb117 (2026-06-16),
"fix(routing): route-link click carries the render-time frame (rf2-o3nam4)" — the
commit that introduced the render-time require-current-frame! into link.cljc. A
-S pickaxe over that symbol scoped to link.cljc returns EXACTLY ONE commit and the
count goes 0 -> 2 across it. Measured in the browser at both ends with
:examples/login as the control (the example lived at examples/reagent/routing/
before the #4999 reorg):
  1e443dde7a (fda84bb117^)  routing BOOTS  #app 267, 0 page errors ; login 627
  fda84bb117                routing FAILS  #app 0, the identical
                            :rf.error/no-frame-context :where route-link-render ; login 627
Note what that dating means: examples/capabilities/routing/routing/ did not exist
at fda84bb117, and realworld_http / linearlite did not exist at all. The routing
example was born into a tree that already carried the defect — this was never a
recent regression.

BROWSER ACCEPTANCE (headless Chromium, static serve, 0 failed requests every run):
  :examples/routing   before  #app 0    1 page error   / after  #app 268, 0 errors
  :examples/login     before  #app 643  0 errors       / after  #app 643, 0 errors  (control, unmoved)
  :examples/realworld  (pilot 1) after  #app 2350, navbar renders, 0 errors
  :examples/linearlite (pilot 2) after  #app 3535, 0 errors
  linearlite /index.html (the bead's decisive pair, the not-found-page route-link)
                       after  #app 274 "Not found / Back to the board", 0 errors
The link also NAVIGATES: clicking "See the articles" moves / -> /articles and
re-renders, 0 page errors — so rf2-o3nam4's render-time frame capture, which
fda84bb117 existed to add, still works.

THE DURABLE REGRESSION, and why the old coverage could not catch its own case.
EVERY pre-existing route-link suite calls routing/route-link-render directly and
establishes the frame with rf/with-frame — the DYNAMIC-VAR tier, which answers
from anywhere. Not one mounts [rf/route-link ...] through a substrate, so all of
them were green about a component no application could render. New file
implementation/routing/test/re_frame/route_link_frame_context_dom_cljs_test.cljs
adds two rows in the :browser-test lane (unguarded PR-time job in test.yml) that
mount through the Reagent adapter into a real document with :ambient-frame nil,
establishing the frame ONLY through a React-context boundary — frame-provider in
one row, frame-root in the other. Proven to bite: reverting only routing.cljc to
its pre-fix blob and re-running gave exit 1 with exactly 2 failures, both the new
rows, both reporting container innerHTML = "" — the blank-page signature — while
the other 774 tests were unmoved.

GATES (exit codes captured from each runner): test:browser 776 tests / 4211
assertions 0F 0E exit 0; routing clojure -M:test 554 / 3454 0F 0E exit 0;
test:cljs 11193 / 55780 0F 0E exit 0; test-fast-pr.sh exit 0. test-fast-pr
--plan prints "No browser, bundle, adapter, Xray, MCP or tool-JVM gate is in any
tier" for this diff, which is this bead's thesis restated by the tool: the spine
cannot see this class of bug, which is why the regression is in the browser lane.

NOT FIXED, DELIBERATELY: rf2-6sqv obstructed the diagnosis exactly as the brief
predicted — the raw ExceptionInfo reaching console.error showed only
{meta: null, cnt: 7, arr: Array(14), ...}. Worked around locally by pr-str-ing
inside the (uncommitted, out-of-repo) measurement harness. Follow-on filed for the
defwrapper sharp edge underneath this: rf2-nvcp's cause generalises to any
late-bound hook whose value is a COMPONENT but whose wrapper CALLS it.
close_reason: Fixed by PR #9050. rf/route-link now renders as a component (the :routing/route-link hook emits [(views/view-head :route/link) props & children]) instead of being called as a function, so the frame-root's React context reaches it. Browser acceptance: :examples/routing #app 0 -> 268 with 0 page errors, :examples/login control unmoved at 643/0 before and after; realworld (2350) and linearlite (3535) both boot, and linearlite /index.html — the bead's decisive pair — renders its not-found route-link at 274. Durable regression added in the browser lane (route_link_frame_context_dom_cljs_test.cljs, 2 rows) and proven red against the pre-fix blob. Bisect: the break is fda84bb117 (2026-06-16, rf2-o3nam4), NOT the triage note's aa9e90af7f. Follow-on rf2-02w1 filed for the defwrapper sharp edge underneath. Note beads close on PR-open in this repo; #9050 is open and green-pending, not yet merged.

title: surface-review(ssr): close safe-redirect policy bypass and rejected hydration install claims
description:
Recommendation: repair the safe-redirect URL classification first, then make hydration's install ledger conditional on a committed seed. This focused review confirms one P1 redirect-policy bypass and one P2 hydration lifecycle defect. Both have small local repair directions; keep this task OPEN until both fixes and their focused public-path witnesses land.

Scope and revision

Owned slice: implementation/ssr/** (110 tracked files, including its src, test, deps.edn and LICENSE). Reviewed revision: 1c9ff9697b0fa3a018c7a4371e02983ad2e79b2f; HEAD was rechecked unchanged before filing. SOURCE_ROOT=C:/Users/miket/code/re-frame2. WORKTREE_ROOT=(none; read-only review).

Coverage: focused source-path review of the facade registrations and boot/install/hydrate request lifecycle; request/response/error-listener side channels and teardown; error projection's drain and render-exception entry points; streaming shell walking, continuation/fallback behavior, final payload assembly and client finalization/observer disposal; payload policy and runtime projection; render-state project/serialize/deserialize/restore; hiccup emission and shared attribute/text helpers. Inspected deps.edn's core-only production dependency and its test/production/slow-test lane split. Examined the failed-root-isolation, multi-root hydration, safe-redirect production, reserved effect guard and shared fixture coverage relevant to the two findings, and inventoried the broader emitter, projection, concurrency, teardown and DOM regression test surfaces.

Exclusions and limits: ssr-ring and ssr-node are separate owned slices; pipeline.clj was followed only to confirm how this slice's accepted redirect reaches a Location header. Core frame/router calls were followed only as hydration dependencies. This is not exhaustive execution of the 110-file slice, an independent complete audit of head/manifest/hash algorithms, or a browser/CLJS rendering or package-release certification. No broad gates, builds, dependency installs, HTTP server, network request, source edits, commits or pushes were performed. The root coordinator owns tracker durability.

Finding 1 — P1: safe-redirect accepts external browser destinations under relative-only and host-allowlist policies

Owned source: implementation/ssr/src/re_frame/ssr/response.cljc:985-997 (java.net.URI parsing), :1220-1234 (getHost/getAuthority and relative classification), :1275-1293 (relative-only and allowlist decisions), :1305-1321 (accepted original location enters response).

Trigger: an application uses the documented caller-untrusted :rf.server/safe-redirect effect for a request's next/return location with :relative-only? true or :allow ["trusted.example"]. The legitimate developer intent is to restrict navigation; the location is the attacker-controlled argument this API explicitly exists to check.

Executed public-effect reproduction, after normal adapter boot:

(rf/init! ssr/adapter)
(rf/make-frame {:id :review/redirect :platform :server})
(rf/reg-event :review/redirect
  (fn [_ [_ args]] {:fx [[:rf.server/safe-redirect args]]}))
(rf/dispatch-sync
  [:review/redirect {:location "///evil.example/path" :relative-only? true}]
  {:frame :review/redirect})
(ssr/peek-response :review/redirect)

Actual: status 302 and :redirect {:location "///evil.example/path" :status 302}. Repeating on a cleared accumulator with :allow ["trusted.example"] also accepts it. java.net.URI reports BOTH host and authority nil for this input, so relative? is true and the allowlist branch is skipped. Yet the browser-compatible WHATWG URL parser resolves:

new URL("///evil.example/path", "https://trusted.example/login").href
=> "https://evil.example/path"

A second branch has the same root cause: "//evil_example/path" reports a non-nil Java authority but a nil Java host. :allow ["trusted.example"] is guarded by host truthiness and therefore accepts it too; WHATWG URL resolves the external host evil_example. The triple-slash example already establishes a bypass with an ordinary DNS-shaped hostname and does not depend on underscore-host deployment.

Controls: "/dashboard" is accepted under relative-only; "//evil.example/path" is rejected under relative-only. Thus this is not a disabled registration, wrong platform or wholly inactive guard. The exact original location string is preserved on acceptance. Neighboring implementation/ssr-ring/src/re_frame/ssr/ring/pipeline.clj:201-258 places that original target in Location without a second URL policy decision. Its current case-insensitive header replacement is correct and is not the cause.

Expected: a destination that the browser resolves off-origin must not pass :relative-only? true; a destination with a browser host outside a supplied allowlist must not pass that allowlist. Ambiguous network references must be rejected rather than classified as safe local paths merely because java.net.URI cannot extract their host.

Impact: application code following the safe-redirect recipe can expose an open redirect despite declaring the intended restriction. This undermines return-to/login navigation policy. No claim is made that the library alone leaks tokens or bypasses authentication; those consequences depend on the consuming application.

Repair: make the checked classification agree with the browser destination, or conservatively reject the known ambiguous network-reference forms before accepting. In particular, a raw //-prefixed target cannot become relative because Java returns nil authority for an extra slash; and an authority-bearing reference with no extractable host must never skip an active host allowlist. Preserve the existing caller-trusted redirect effect and ordinary relative/allowed-http(s) behavior. Do not introduce a new URL abstraction or extra policy knobs merely to close these two concrete fall-throughs.

Acceptance:
- A public registered-event -> :rf.server/safe-redirect regression corpus rejects ///evil.example/path (and a repeated-slash variant) under relative-only and an unrelated host allowlist, leaving the response accumulator unchanged and emitting the existing appropriate safe-redirect rejection record.
- The allowlist also rejects //evil_example/path or otherwise resolves and checks its actual browser host; no hostless Java parse may waive the caller's allowlist for a network target.
- Retain passing /dashboard, ordinary relative references and explicitly allowed https destinations, and the existing protocol-relative and opaque-scheme rejection cases.
- Run the focused SSR tests in the real -Dre-frame.debug=false JVM lane; compare every counterexample's effective destination with the installed Node WHATWG URL implementation or a browser URL implementation. An end-to-end Ring Location assertion should confirm no accepted bypass reaches the wire.

Validation: process-local Java 21 / Clojure 1.12.4 loaded the checked-out sources and dispatched the real registered effect with -Dre-frame.debug=false. Evidence ai/surface-review-20260912/probe-impl-ssr-3.log and .exit, exit 0, records all five effect cases above. The source root and production property are printed. A separate non-network Node URL probe returned the destinations above, exit 0. No browser redirect or HTTP server was executed. Attempt 2 failed before loading Clojure because PowerShell split an unquoted -D argument; it is retained separately with exit 1 and is not a runtime finding or a passing result.

Finding 2 — P2: a rejected hydration payload is recorded as installed and prevents a corrected seed

Owned source: implementation/ssr/src/re_frame/ssr/boot.cljc:348-354 (claim acquired), :401-422 (dispatch then incarnation-only success inference), :494-507 (page helper reports a normal return as hydrated); implementation/ssr/src/re_frame/ssr/install.cljc:211-241 (claim-or-observe/conflict); implementation/ssr/src/re_frame/ssr/hydrate.cljc:275-284 (malformed partition rejection returns existing db without committing the payload).

Executed reproduction:

(rf/make-frame {:id :review/ssr-hydrate :platform :client})
(ssr/hydrate! {:frame :review/ssr-hydrate :payload {:rf/app-db []}})
;; returns {:rf/app-db []}; actual app-db is still {}
(install/installed-payload :review/ssr-hydrate)
;; => {:digest "d6342952" :installed-by nil}
(ssr/hydrate! {:frame :review/ssr-hydrate
              :payload {:rf/app-db {:server true}}})
;; throws :rf.error/frame-payload-conflict; app-db remains {}

The malformed map is an explicit supported refusal case in Spec 011, not a request to validate a new programmer-misuse shape. The handler correctly rejects its non-map partition, emits malformed-hydration-payload and leaves both partitions alone. The boot helper has already installed the ledger claim, however, and checks only whether the original frame incarnation remains live. A still-live frame proves neither that the event accepted the input nor that the payload committed. The rejected content therefore acquires a successful-install identity and a later valid payload conflicts with data that was never installed.

A production-mode hydrate-page! probe makes the visible consequence precise. Three roots, in order: (1) malformed payload for frame A, (2) corrected payload for the same frame A, (3) valid payload for independent frame B. Actual statuses are [:hydrated :failed :hydrated], mount callbacks run for [:bad :peer], A stays {}, A's ledger records :installed-by :bad, and B receives {:peer true}. The first return value and status falsely advertise a hydrated root; the corrected root cannot recover the shared frame.

Expected: a rejected seed leaves no successful install claim, does not run hydration verification as if server state landed, and cannot poison a subsequent valid root. Preserve the documented degraded/client-only behavior for malformed payloads and make the returned boot result consistent with the chosen rejection/fallback behavior. A successful seed followed by a failing verify or mount must keep its claim, since that state really did install.

Impact: corrupt or version-skewed server data can turn a recoverable hydration refusal into a persistent page-lifetime payload conflict, block a healthy sibling/corrected boot, and cause the host to select hydration based on a payload never applied. Destroying the frame clears the claim, but rebuilding a frame should not be necessary to undo a rejected installation.

Repair: share the existing hydration payload acceptance check before recording the claim, or carry an explicit successful-commit outcome from the seed boundary and release the exact claim when that outcome is absent. Do not treat mere live-incarnation continuity as commit evidence. Cover escaping/contained seed failures through the same transaction boundary where applicable, while preserving the existing post-seed claim-retention rule. No new payload policy, retry subsystem or broad validator is necessary.

Acceptance:
- Through ssr/hydrate!, reject malformed :rf/app-db and :rf/runtime-db partition cases without a lingering ledger entry or verification call; a subsequent valid payload for that frame installs normally.
- Through hydrate-page!, the rejected root cannot prevent a later corrected root sharing its frame from receiving the valid server state, and unrelated roots keep booting.
- Preserve identical-payload idempotence after client state changes, different-payload conflicts AFTER a real successful seed, claim retention when verify/mount fails after commit, and claim release on missing/destroyed frame paths.
- Exercise the public helpers on JVM and CLJS, including a production build/lane; do not rely only on calling hydrate-event-handler or payload-install-decision! in isolation.

Validation: actual source-loaded JVM helper probes, not mocks. Attempt 1 exit 0 demonstrates rejection -> stale claim -> corrected conflict in the ordinary posture. Attempt 5 exit 0 repeats the page-level failure with -Dre-frame.debug=false and prints the actual boot.cljc resource URL under SOURCE_ROOT. Its assertions also establish two controls: a valid repeated payload retains intervening {:local true} state, and destroy-frame! empties all three frames' ledger entries. Evidence ai/surface-review-20260912/probe-impl-ssr-5.log and .exit. Attempt 4 reached the same page failure but then stopped on a probe-only unmatched delimiter; its exit 1 is not a passing validation result. No CLJS compilation or browser hydration was run.

Known issues/history and duplication

Searched active and closed titles/descriptions for SSR, hydration, claims, poisoning and safe-redirect, plus SSR memories. Read current closure records and bounded recent history for rf2-tax2; its nil-preserving DATA digest repair is present and addresses content identity, not whether content ever committed. Read rf2-c1b1's closed repair: Ring Location replacement is now case-insensitive and cannot address which target safe-redirect approves. Current failed_root_isolation_cljs_test.cljc:320-349 covers a seed against a missing frame, and :351 onward covers failure AFTER commit; it does not cover the handler refusing a payload while its frame remains live. Safe redirect's production/guard suites cover ordinary protocol-relative, opaque-scheme, type and injection failures but contain no /// counterexample. title: skill/re-frame2: JVM with-frame recipe silently skips every test body
description:
## Scope

Correct the JVM frame-pinning recipe in skills/re-frame2/references/cross-cutting/testing.md and add the smallest skill-side regression witness in the existing re-frame2 skill eval/drift-gate surface. The library macro itself is correct and is not in scope.

## Correctness finding

The testing leaf tells JVM authors to use (rf/with-frame frame-id (fn [] ...)) as a "function form." No such function form exists. rf/with-frame is the same body-splicing macro on JVM and CLJS.

Because the thunk is a legal body expression, this does not fail loudly: the macro binds the frame, evaluates the fn literal, returns that function, and exits the binding without invoking it. In a clojure.test use-fixtures wrapper this silently prevents the test function from running. The suite can exit 0 after running zero tests and zero assertions.

## Evidence

- skills/re-frame2/references/cross-cutting/testing.md:135-148 first shows the correct macro body form, then explicitly overrides it for JVM readers with: "On JVM use the (rf/with-frame frame-id (fn [] ...)) function form."
- implementation/core/src/re_frame/core.cljc:1319-1335 defines with-frame only as a macro with arglist [frame-id body+]. There is no facade function twin.
- implementation/core/src/re_frame/core_reg_view_macro.cljc:233-251 expands it to a binding whose body is spliced directly with ~@body. A supplied fn literal is returned, not called.
- skills/re-frame2/references/fundamentals/frames.md:178 correctly says the macro expands on both CLJS and JVM. references/cross-cutting/api-cheatsheet.md:34 also gives the body form. The testing leaf is internally inconsistent with both.
- JVM implementation tests use the real fixture shape, for example implementation/core/test/re_frame/trace_test.clj:63-69 and always_on_validation_production_test.clj:108-109: (rf/with-frame frame-id (test-fn)), not a thunk literal.
- A deterministic probe run from implementation/core:

    clojure -M -e "(require '[re-frame.core :as rf]) (let [ran? (atom false) result (rf/with-frame :probe (fn [] (reset! ran? true)))] (prn {:body-ran? @ran? :returned-thunk? (fn? result)}) (result) (prn {:body-ran-after-manual-call? @ran?}))"

  Current output was {:body-ran? false, :returned-thunk? true}, then {:body-ran-after-manual-call? true}. This proves with-frame itself never invoked the taught thunk.
- A second probe installed the taught shape as a clojure.test :each fixture around a deftest whose body sets an atom and contains a failing assertion. clojure.test reported "Ran 0 tests containing 0 assertions. 0 failures, 0 errors.", returned a zero-failure summary, left the body atom false, and the process exited 0.
- The current eval corpus has no with-frame scenario, and python scripts/check_skill_re_frame2_drift.py, check_skill_eval_docs.py, check_skill_eval_packaging.py, check_skill_package_refs.py, check_skill_mcp_drift.py, and check_skill_pair_authoring_drift.py all exit 0 over this bad instruction.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. In a JVM test namespace, create an atom ran? initialized false.
2. Install an :each fixture shaped as (fn [test-fn] (rf/with-frame :app/test (fn [] (test-fn)))).
3. Define a deftest that resets ran? true and contains (is false).
4. Run the namespace with clojure.test.
5. Observe that the test body does not execute, the summary reports zero tests/assertions and zero failures/errors, and the process exits successfully.
6. Change only the fixture body to (rf/with-frame :app/test (test-fn)). The test now executes and the deliberate failing assertion makes the run red.

## Expected Behavior

Skill-generated JVM tests pin the frame with the public macro body form. A fixture must invoke test-fn inside the binding, so every test and assertion executes and failures make the declared gate non-zero.

## Actual Behavior

The platform-specific instruction wraps the test call in an uninvoked thunk. It converts a failing suite into a vacuous green run while appearing to follow the canonical testing leaf exactly.

## Failure scenario / invariant

A programmer or AI follows the testing leaf while adding frame-scoped JVM tests, commonly by writing a use-fixtures wrapper. Every test under that fixture is skipped. CI reports success, so broken event, subscription, machine, SSR, or resource behavior can ship with tests that never ran.

Invariant: a testing recipe must never turn the test runner's test function into an inert return value. The documented frame scope must execute its body on both host platforms.

## Recommended minimal fix

Delete the nonexistent JVM "function form" distinction. Teach one public shape on both platforms:

- General body: (rf/with-frame frame-id body...)
- clojure.test fixture: (rf/with-frame frame-id (test-fn))

Keep only the CLJS macro-import note that is genuinely platform-specific. Do not add a facade function twin or recommend direct binding of internal dynamic Vars.

Add one bounded regression check or eval expectation for the exact JVM fixture shape, backed by the executable zero-test control above, so the silent thunk form cannot return.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. references/cross-cutting/testing.md states that rf/with-frame is a macro on both JVM and CLJS and shows a JVM use-fixtures example that calls (test-fn) inside the macro body; no positive instruction names or demonstrates a JVM thunk/function form.
2. A focused JVM probe using the corrected fixture runs at least one named test and at least one assertion, sets a body-executed sentinel true, and exits 0 for a passing assertion.
3. The same probe with the assertion deliberately false exits non-zero or returns a summary with one failure, proving the fixture cannot skip the test body.
4. Non-vacuity: mutate only the documented/generated fixture back to (rf/with-frame frame-id (fn [] (test-fn))). The skill regression check/eval must fail, and the behavioral control must reproduce zero executed tests/assertions with the sentinel false.
5. Extend either the existing eval corpus or scripts/check_skill_re_frame2_drift.py plus its self-test with this exact platform-specific regression. The check must accept (rf/with-frame frame-id (test-fn)) and reject the positive thunk recipe without banning ordinary fn bodies elsewhere.
6. python scripts/check_skill_re_frame2_drift.py --self-test, python scripts/check_skill_re_frame2_drift.py, python scripts/check_skill_eval_docs.py, and the relevant skill packaging/reference gates pass.

## Non-goals

- Changing re-frame.core/with-frame or adding a second JVM function API.
- Redesigning frame scope, with-new-frame, capture-frame, clojure.test fixtures, or the test-support library.
- A general Markdown snippet compiler or exhaustive prose parser.
- Rewriting unrelated testing recipes, eval prompts, or skill leaves.
- Treating an explicit thunk return as illegal application code outside this positive fixture instruction.

## Related / duplicate search

Fresh all-status title, description, and notes searches covered with-frame, function form, JVM fixture, test fixture, returns the thunk, test-fn, zero tests, and skills/re-frame2. No bead owns this false-green instruction.

rf2-g9k0g is the closed adjacent surface-review task that allowed the authoring agent to run a project's declared gate; it does not cover whether the skill's JVM fixture recipe causes that gate to execute tests. rf2-czlb and rf2-6c12m.13 mention with-frame only in unrelated Hicasso boundary/capture-frame work.

SURFACES: skills/re-frame2/references/cross-cutting/testing.md + scripts/check_skill_re_frame2_drift.py (+ self-test) or the eval corpus; no hot-zone. COLLISIONS: none - live skills-shared-own holds other skill files/scripts (check_skill_package_refs.py, check_skill_mcp_drift.py), not testing.md or the re_frame2 drift script. GATES: python scripts/check_skill_re_frame2_drift.py --self-test; python scripts/check_skill_re_frame2_drift.py; python scripts/check_skill_eval_docs.py; python scripts/check_doc_slugs.py; all light, no heavy lane. AMBIGUITY: AC5 offers eval-corpus OR drift-script extension - recommend the drift-script check (accept the (test-fn) body form, reject the positive thunk recipe) as the smaller change. SHAPE: solo, first wave (small, fast).
close_reason: Fixed in PR #8822. testing.md now teaches the macro body form on both hosts with a JVM use-fixtures example invoking (test-fn) INSIDE the macro body; no positive thunk/function-form instruction remains. Rule 8 in check_skill_re_frame2_drift.py rejects a fn literal (or #(...)) in with-frame's direct body-head position, fenced and inline alike, with self-test fixtures both ways plus the real-corpus reintroduction mutation. Behavioral witness: old taught form + (is false) ran 0 tests / 0 assertions, body sentinel false, exit 0 (false green); corrected form + same assertion ran 1 test / 1 assertion, 1 failure, exit 1 (honest red); corrected form + passing assertion exit 0. Non-vacuity: Rule 8 red on the pre-fix leaf at testing.md:148 (sole finding corpus-wide), red again on the AC4 mutation, restore verified by git blob hash. Gates on rebased base 1246e4e422: drift --self-test 0, drift 0, eval_docs 0, doc_slugs 0, eval_packaging 0, package_refs 0.

title: [MERGED - PR #10128, trunk 1810a6a1f7] xray(inspector): sequential-diff-children DROPPED unpaired before-indices while its docstring promised it never could
description:
Named (not fixed) by the rf2-g61nr worker while repairing the capped-AFTER tail, and scoped out of that bead in terms. Filed so it is not re-derived.

## The claim, as reported by that worker

`sequential-diff-children` SILENTLY DROPS rows on the projection-aware path: `bi->ai`'s `zipmap` truncates to the shorter side, so the before-order walk's `when-let` yields nothing for before-indices past the after ceiling. Reported observation: **1001 rows under a 1050 header — the body SHORT of the header.** Described as rf2-zk4he's data-loss mode mirrored, and distinct from rf2-g61nr's defect (this DROPS rows; g61nr MISLABELLED them).

## What the mayor verified at source, and what it did NOT verify

Verified on branch head `2fdc40b593` of `tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/views/edn_inspector.cljs`:

- `bi->ai (zipmap survivor-bis survivor-ais)` at **`:1924`**. The worker cited `:1868`; that is wrong — `:1868` is inside the docstring. Re-derive at your own base.
- The truncation is ACKNOWLEDGED by the code's own comment at **`:1897`**: *"`zipmap` truncates to the shorter side, so the pairs it does make are the unbounded ones; the surplus after-side survivors it could not reach are emitted afterwards, in after-order, carrying `::unrealised`."*
- The before-order walk drops unpaired before-indices via `(when-let [ai (bi->ai bi)] ...)`, whose else-branch is nothing.
- **The tail-rows append that recovers unreachable rows walks `after-idxs` ONLY.** So it recovers the AFTER direction. Whether anything recovers an unpaired BEFORE index is the open question.

**NOT verified by the mayor: the 1001-vs-1050 measurement itself.** Reproducing it needs the node lane, which is a worker's to take. It is relayed here as the worker's measurement, not as established fact.

## THE TENSION IS THE FIRST TASK, AND IT IS WHY THIS IS WORTH A BEAD

`sequential-diff-children`'s own docstring, at **`:1860-1866`**, says the opposite in terms:

> "this walk emits every accessible after row — so the body may EXCEED the header by the removals struck inside the bound. **It never falls SHORT of it.** Those surplus survivors carry `::unrealised` in their before slot ... they used to be emitted by no arm of the walk at all, and vanished with nothing on screen saying so."

That paragraph is the account of rf2-zk4he, written in the PAST tense as a defect already repaired. So either:

1. the docstring's "never falls SHORT" is now FALSE and states a guarantee the code does not keep — in which case this is a real defect AND a false normative statement in the same file; or
2. the worker's 1001/1050 observation came from a path the docstring does not cover, or from a fixture that does not reach this walk — in which case the correct outcome is a measured "does not arise, because X" and a CLOSE.

**Determine which BEFORE writing any fix.** Do not assume the worker is right because it was right about its own item, and do not assume the docstring is right because it is normative-sounding prose in the file it describes. One of the two is wrong and the measurement decides it.

## If it IS a defect

The asymmetry to look at: recovery walks `after-idxs`, so an unpaired AFTER index is emitted and an unpaired BEFORE index may not be. A repair must not widen, re-base or re-order the zip — the comment at `:1897` says the existing repair was deliberately APPEND-ONLY so that an earlier warning still holds, and that constraint should be respected or explicitly retired with reasons.

Related and worth reading first: rf2-zk4he (the original vanishing-survivors defect), rf2-g61nr (the capped-AFTER mislabel), rf2-t450s (unknown-prior through container recursion). This is the fourth item in that family.

## Gate note

`edn_inspector.cljs` is a shadow-cljs lane surface — its path arms six surfaces, three of them the machine-wide exclusive. Any reproduction takes the lane.

title: False Graph preview bound: shortening collection keys changes order and exposes unbounded strings
description:
Merged-PR audit #10072 at ac59ec481f8db46741cb11a7f1988256310eccd7, source rf2-3hnvn. bound-long-strings truncates nested strings, but changes MAP KEYS and SET MEMBERS by dissoc/assoc or disj/conj in the original collection. Those operations can reorder entries and collapse distinct keys/members. Its promise that the preview prefix stays identical and that it bounds every string the printer reaches is therefore false for ordinary persistent collections.

Reproduced with the EXACT new bound-long-strings / bounded-pr-str definitions in a source-isolated Babashka CLJC probe:
1. (array-map huge-string 1 :small 2): dissoc/assoc moves the first key to the end. The original 80-character print prefix begins with the long string key; the new prefix starts {:small 2, ... . They differ.
2. A sorted map with 81 distinct string keys sharing the same first 80 characters, each mapped to a 200,000-character string: the walk bounds only the original first 80 entries. Their keys collapse to one truncated key. The formerly 81st, unvisited entry moves into the first 80 printed entries with its value still unbounded. Entry count drops from 81 to 2 in the print input, and bounded-pr-str emits 200,255 characters. The simple {:body huge-string} positive control emits 90.

Required correction: bound printing without reinserting abbreviated keys or members into their semantic collection. Preserve the original printer traversal/prefix and ensure moving the print boundary cannot expose unprocessed values. Keep the fix local to preview production; no new public policy or collection framework. Add discriminating regressions for a multi-entry long-key map and colliding string prefixes, asserting both prefix fidelity and bounded intermediate print. The same principle applies to sets.

Artifacts: ai/audit-graph-keys-audit-sep20-monitor-1.clj and ignored ai/gate-graph-keys-audit-sep20-monitor-1.log/.exit, exit 0, correct gate root audit-sep20-monitor. This is a source-isolated CLJC/JVM-compatible reproduction, not a claimed browser run. Current main was fetched and the whole production file remains byte-identical to the audited merge. No exact OPEN finding records this correction.

title: CLAUDE.md lane yield rule: 'filter on its OWN worktree path, confirm zero remain' sees only a subset of a lane build — identify by ancestry
description:
## The defect

CLAUDE.md's shadow-cljs lane bullet tells a worker told to yield to kill its run, "verifying by EFFECT
(find the spawned process, **filter on its OWN worktree path** so it cannot touch a peer's, **confirm zero
remain**)". **A command-line worktree-path filter sees only a SUBSET of a lane build's processes**, so
"zero remain" can read true while the build lives. It fails OPEN in exactly the case the instruction
exists for, since a yield happens when a second holder is already in the window.

## Measured

- **Run phase** (memory `a-name-filtered-lane-probe-cannot-see-the-run-phase`, 2026-09-18, trunk
  `0ac7fd9e3b`): `test:cljs` runs its artefact as a bare `node out/node-test.js`. Across 12 node/java
  rows, NO worktree string appeared in any command line, because the paths are relative to a process
  cwd that Win32_Process does not expose.
- **Compile phase** (mayor, 2026-09-18, §5 method reread, trunk `717bca7b5d`). Three live processes of
  one node-lane build: `node scripts/compile-node-test.cjs node-test out/node-test.js`, then `node
  <ABSOLUTE>\xrpop-h6ooa\implementation\node_modules\shadow-cljs\cli\runner.js compile node-test`,
  then `java.exe -cp test-quiet/src;test-quiet/test;core/src;...`. **Only the middle one names its
  worktree.** The source says why:
  - npm invokes the wrapper by a relative path (`implementation/package.json:27`);
  - the wrapper `require.resolve`s `runner.js` to an absolute path and spawns it with
    `cwd: IMPL_DIR` (`implementation/scripts/compile-node-test.cjs:276-284`);
  - shadow's JVM receives `shadow-cljs.edn`'s source paths as a RELATIVE classpath.
- A browser-lane build read the same way minutes later: `npm-cli.js run test:browser` (no path), then
  `runner.js` (path), then a JVM with a relative `-cp`.
- **Walking the PARENT CHAIN attributed the relative-classpath JVM (PID 107052) to its tree
  (`xrpop-h6ooa`) correctly.** Ancestry is the discriminator that works.
- A worker's lane-release report verified release in the path-filtered form, quoted verbatim from the
  rf2-y8doi.30 worker: "filtered on my own worktree path: `java.exe`/`node.exe` processes whose command
  line contains `xrshell-c18` = **0**".

**Not overshooting:** the path filter is not USELESS, because `runner.js` does carry the path. It
finds a subset, and the subset is not the whole build.

## The fix (CLAUDE.md only)

Replace the parenthetical in the lane bullet's yield rule with instructions that work:
- **Identify your processes by ANCESTRY**: note the PID of what you launched, and walk its descendants
  through `ParentProcessId`.
- **Kill the tree children-first, from PowerShell.** From Git Bash, `taskkill /T` is item (h)'s `/FLAG`
  rewrite, and `cmd /c` is the silent no-op the worktree-removal bullet records.
- **Confirm by READING every node/java row with its parent chain**: never a path filter, never a bare
  count.

Keep the rest of the bullet. The mayor-side pre-grant check is unaffected: it counts machine-wide with
no path filter, so it fails CLOSED. Say so, so nobody "fixes" it into a path filter.

**Bound the edit.** It is one parenthetical plus at most a short supporting sentence with the
measurement. It is not a new bullet, and not an instrument-list entry.

title: mayor: the clause-5 positive control is a fixed commit offset (origin/main~40) and has silently expired — 452 commits past the last matrix change, reads 0 at every trunk point this session
description:
The mayor's clause-5 positive control is a FIXED COMMIT OFFSET (`origin/main~40`), and it goes
silently dead as the trunk moves past the last workflow change — after which the clause-5 reading it
was supposed to verify is uncontrolled, while every report says it was controlled.

## The instrument

Merge criterion clause 5 asks whether a PR's check set was computed against the workflow matrix on
the trunk now. The mayor discharges it with:

    git diff <last-matrix-commit> origin/main --name-only -- .github/workflows/     # must read 0

and takes a positive control beside it, so that a zero means "the matrix has not moved" rather than
"the instrument is blind":

    git diff origin/main~40 origin/main --name-only -- .github/workflows/           # must read >=1

## Measured 2026-09-18 at trunk `9c2f9054bf`

**The control reads 0. It has read 0 at every trunk point of this session** — measured at
`fe96e0acaa`, `39f870aa43`, `e9e800c05e`, `55250a68d9`, `8727353e79` and `9c2f9054bf`, all six **0**.

The cause is simple arithmetic: the last commit touching `.github/workflows/` is `b9220b6dc2`
(2026-09-16, `ci(cljs): run the warnings-fatal wrapper on the required node-test lane`, rf2-m3iin),
and there are **452** commits since it on trunk. A window of 40 cannot reach it. Walking the offset
at today's tip: `~40`, `~100`, `~200`, `~400` and `~452` all read **0**; **`~460` reads 1**.

**So the number is not wrong, it is EXPIRED** — and it expired by the trunk advancing, which is the
one thing guaranteed to keep happening. In an earlier session, when the matrix change was recent, the
same literal control did bite; that is why it was written down, and why nobody re-ran it.

## What this did and did NOT cost

**It did NOT produce a bad merge, and the correction must not overshoot into claiming it did.** The
clause-5 reading itself was independently correct throughout: `b9220b6dc2` genuinely IS the newest
commit touching `.github/workflows/`, which `git log -1 --format=%H -- .github/workflows/` answers
without reference to any offset, and the band held at **88** across 14 ancestry-qualified PRs.

**What it cost is the verification, not the verdict.** A control that cannot bite makes an unchecked
zero read as a checked one, so the zero was decorative. That is strictly worse than taking no control
at all, because a reader — including the author on the next tick — stops asking.

**It fails in the REASSURING direction**, which is the property that let it survive: the control's
"must read >= 1" is the half a tired reader skips, and a passing-looking clause-5 line invites no
scrutiny. It was carried into **16 closed beads' close reasons** as a present-tense fact, several of
them from earlier sessions.

## The repair: make the control SELF-DERIVING so it cannot expire

Take the base from the last workflow commit itself rather than from a guessed distance:

    LAST=$(git log -1 --format=%H -- .github/workflows/)
    git diff "$LAST^" origin/main --name-only -- .github/workflows/    # control, must read >=1
    git diff "$LAST"  origin/main --name-only -- .github/workflows/    # clause 5, must read 0

Measured at `9c2f9054bf`: the control reads **1**, the clause-5 form reads **0**. This cannot go
stale, because the base is recomputed from the tree every time. It also answers a better question —
it establishes *which* commit the matrix baseline IS, rather than assuming the mayor's remembered
`b9220b6dc2` is still the newest, which is itself a carried constant.

**And it makes the matrix-commit identity checkable in the same breath**: if `$LAST` is not the commit
the mayor has been treating as the matrix baseline, the band's qualifying set is wrong and must be
re-derived. Confirmed this tick: `$LAST` == `b9220b6dc2`.

## The general shape, which is the part worth keeping

**A control expressed as a FIXED OFFSET into a moving history is a control with an expiry date and no
expiry notice.** It is the same class as the stale-constant trap already catalogued for the
check-count band — written down, moving, and stale exactly where it has to be right — but reached
through the CONTROL rather than through the measurement, which is worse, because the control is the
thing whose whole job is to detect staleness.

Prefer a control derived from the target's own history (`git log -1 -- <path>`) over any literal
offset, anywhere this pattern recurs.

## Not a gate

Nothing mechanical separates a live control from an expired one without re-running it, which is what
the self-deriving form already does inline. No new script, no CI job.

`tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/`, carries two claims about how `:rf/xray` resolves. Reported by

## THE CLAIM

The paragraph ends, in its commonest form (`filters.cljs:71-74`):

    ... which the enclosing frame boundary writes; `rf/frame-provider` and
    `rf.fresco/frame-provider` write the SAME context, so this resolves
    `:rf/xray` identically under today's Reagent-rendered shell and under
    the Fresco root Xray will own.

**Two clauses, two tenses, and they fail together.** *"today's Reagent-rendered shell"* asserts in
the PRESENT that the shell renders under Reagent; *"the Fresco root Xray will own"* asserts in the
FUTURE that Xray does not yet own one. Since rf2-k97c.3 (commit `11f8695135`) `mount.cljs` owns an
`rf.fresco/client-root` and heads `shell.cljs`'s `ShellView` under its own frame-provider, never the
installed adapter's `:render`. **The future Xray was going to own has arrived**, so the sentence is
wrong in both halves at once and has been since that commit.

`tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/static/shell.cljs:630-645` already states the corrected position
in prose and is **CORRECT, CURRENT AND NOT TO BE EDITED** — it is one of the true look-alikes. Read
it first; it is the clearest statement of the post-conversion truth in the tree.

`Reagent-rendered\s+(Static\s+)?shell`. **The two groups are DISJOINT — no file carries both.**

    panels/machine_inspector.cljs

    panels/resources.cljs
    panels/routing.cljs

**GROUP B — "Reagent-rendered STATIC shell" (5 files, 1 hit each). A DIFFERENT SUBJECT. SETTLE IT
SEPARATELY BEFORE YOU TOUCH ONE.**

    static/machines/browse_list.cljs
    static/routes/panel.cljs
    static/schemas/panel.cljs

A line-oriented grep for `Reagent-rendered shell|Fresco root Xray will own` returns **16 files**. The

description:
SHORTLIST ITEM 6 of the rf2-pk4i6 senior review, RULED BY MIKE 2026-09-16 ("rule rf2-pk4i6 as your recommendation"), actioned as the triage recommends. Source: rf2-pk4i6.3#1. Size M.

WHY IT MATTERS. `:rf.machine/update-snapshot` replaces `:data` WHOLESALE, wiping the runtime's reserved `:rf/*` keys. So the documented idiom `{:rf/patch {:data {:status :degraded}}}` silently stale-suppresses EVERY LIVE `:after` TIMER of the actor (the epoch map is gone, so timers arrive stale) and makes a spawned child finish as a SINGLETON (`:rf/parent-id` gone). It does this on keys THE PROGRAMMER CANNOT SEE -- while an action's `{:data ...}` return MERGES, so the two paths disagree about the same shape.

WHAT TO DO (as ruled):
  * Make the `:data` leg MERGE: `(update merged :data merge (:data clean-patch))` in BOTH the validated preview and the swap.
  * Change spec 005:869 from "merged onto that snapshot" to "the patch's `:data` merges like an action's".
  * Pin with one `:after` test and one spawned-child test.
  * The replace-with-carry alternative is explicitly NOT worth the second mechanism -- do not build it.

THE TRIAGE RE-VERIFIED THIS ONE: update_snapshot.cljc:148 and :165 are top-level `merge`s; transition.cljc:2075-2077 merges an action's `:data`; and `after-epoch-path` (transition.cljc:911-951) reads `[:data :rf/after-epoch ...]` with `(or ... 0)`, which is the mechanism by which a wiped epoch map turns into a stale timer. Re-verified is not re-verified AT TIP.

SEQUENCING: spec/005-StateMachines.md is HOT-ZONE and this item holds it. Surface (implementation/machines/**, spec/005) is disjoint from the item 5/9/11/14 sequence (spec/016 + resources), from the live item 2 (epoch + spec/Security.md), and from item 4's test.yml.

THE MEASURED PREMISE-FAILURE RATE ON THIS SHORTLIST IS NOW ROUGHLY ONE IN FOURTEEN, and two of the first four items also had a SUB-TASK that was wrong in a way that would have shipped: item 3's prescribed gate-regex change harvests ZERO additional categories, and item 1's prescribed pin location cannot carry a pin at all. So treat the "what to do" bullets above as the triage's PROPOSAL, verified before obeyed -- not as an instruction. THIS ITEM IS THE ONE WHERE THAT MATTERS MOST: it changes how a documented public idiom behaves, so if merging `:data` turns out to break a case the triage did not see, STOP and report rather than pressing on.

title: False: fn-alias registrations all become image-selectable with :ns
description:
Merged-PR audit #9882, merge ae305b9e57493966e09d4aae7a77e980a3215320. Source work: closed rf2-17bbi, drift-sweep item 8. This is one documentation regression: a shared image-selection sentence was applied to APIs whose registration paths do not support it.

CLAIM NOW FALSE
The newly added fn-alias docstrings in implementation/core/src/re_frame/core.cljc say registrations are "selectable only by the DEFAULT image unless the metadata stamps :ns". The new rf/image paragraph and spec/001 Production elision guidance generalize the same remedy.

COUNTEREXAMPLES AT THE MERGED COMMIT
1. reg-flow (core.cljc ~324), reg-app-schema (~385), and reg-app-schemas (~401) are frame-owned registrations, not image-selected source-store descriptors. flows/registry.cljc reg-flow writes its frame-keyed flows table; schemas/storage.cljc reg-app-schema writes schemas-by-frame at [frame-id path], and the plural delegates to it. registrar.cljc lines 24-43 explicitly documents these exceptions. Adding :ns cannot move these registrations into an explicit image; their actual target is the explicit/ambient frame. This also contradicts the adjacent, correct frame-scoped API documentation.
2. reg-resource-scope (core.cljc ~372) does use the registrar, but its wrapper discards the proposed :ns metadata. resources/scope_registry.cljc canonical-spec (~241) retains inputs, resolver, derived whole-db?, and doc; reg-resource-scope (~344-383) constructs registrar metadata from doc, rf/resource-scope, and handler-fn. With no macro source-coordinate binding, the descriptor still has nil provenance even when the caller passed :ns.

MEASURED DISCRIMINATING PROBE
On this audit worktree's actual resources classpath, with source-coords/*pending-coords* bound nil:
(scopes/reg-resource-scope :audit9882/scope {:inputs {:db [:db []]} :ns 'audit9882.scope} (fn [_ _] nil))
source-store/descriptors-for returned a nil provenance key.
The same process's ordinary registrar/register! control with {:ns 'audit9882.control :handler-fn identity} returned the named provenance key. Both assertions passed, exit 0. Thus the store honors :ns; the resource-scope fn wrapper never forwards it.

WHY ACTIONABLE
Authors following the newly documented remedy either try to image-select a frame-owned schema/flow or add metadata that silently cannot make their resource scope visible. This is misleading API guidance, not a request for a broader ownership/API redesign.

REQUIRED CORRECTION
Qualify the shared guidance to the registration paths it actually describes. Remove image-selection advice from the frame-owned flow/schema aliases and describe their frame targeting. Correct the resource-scope alias so it does not advertise the ineffective metadata remedy; the existing macro provenance route may be described where useful. Check the other newly amended aliases and the generalized rf/image/spec paragraph against each actual writer. Keep the valid explanation for source-store registrations; do not change frame ownership just to make the prose true.

Validation already completed for the rest of this PR: the new routing test has an independent own-worktree negative control (valid URL makes exactly two assertions fail), then the restored namespace passes 66 tests / 408 assertions. This finding requests documentation correction, not a routing change.
acceptance_criteria: Frame-owned flow/schema aliases describe frame targeting without image-selection claims; resource-scope no longer advertises a :ns remedy its wrapper discards; remaining new image-selection guidance is scoped to verified source-store writers; no runtime ownership redesign.

- Where: implementation/reply-conformance/test/re_frame/reply_egress_projection_conformance_cljs_test.cljc:97-113 (`ok-reply` / `error-reply` are hand-written maps) and 210-232; implementation/security/test/re_frame/security/reply_envelope_egress_security_cljs_test.cljc:62-123; implementation/shadow-cljs.edn:229-231 (the tier's stated claim); spec/Managed-Effects.md §Tracing ("Every wire-bearing value (`:value`, `:error`, …) routes through the shared `re-frame.elision/elide-wire-value` walker … never a family-private elider")

### 3. `test:tools-machines-viz` is a `:node-test`-family lane compiled outside the tally gate, and the wrapper's own roster of tally readers claims to be complete without it  [CONFIRMED] [severity: medium] [kind: correctness]

### 4. TESTING.md states the fresco JVM lane is a `--probe` absent from the roster; it is a floor-taking, unconditional required lane  [CONFIRMED] [severity: low] [kind: spec-drift]
- Where: TESTING.md:192 (`cljs_node_test` row: "its `:test` alias is a `--probe` classpath check and it is correctly absent from `scripts/test-jvm-implementation.sh`"); scripts/test-jvm-implementation.sh:141; implementation/fresco/deps.edn:149; .github/workflows/test.yml:3056-3060 (job comment still names `re-frame.bench.fresco.front.slot-cljs-test` and `front/slot.cljc`)

Control: adapters/reagent/deps.edn:28 carries it in `:main-opts` and reads 3 as well, so the count alone cannot tell them apart — the line was read. TESTING.md is right on the same page (row `implementation_jvm`, and the Kinds table) that the lane exists; only this sentence is stale.

Fail-closed, and the only in-repo nested runs (5, all in test-quiet's own tests) target namespaces with ≥1 deftest.

- The root implementation/deps.edn `:test` alias defaults to `-d test`, which does not exist under implementation/, so a bare `cd implementation && clojure -M:test` reds on the floor; the comment already says it is REPL convenience and CI runs per-artefact aliases.

Control: adapters/reagent (probe in `:main-opts`) and fresco (probe only in comments) both count 3, so `:main-opts` lines were read, not counted.

Control: the reply projection tier's 12 deftests carry 14 `trace-summary` + 11 `project-egress` calls on maps built at lines 97-113 and 0 trace-recorder / `re-frame.trace` references (security reply tier: 5 / 0 / 0; the sibling error_slot tier: 4 recorder hits).

description:
# Senior review: ssr

Reviewer persona: senior SSR/hydration engineer (Next/Remix/React streaming-SSR class), alert to HTML injection through an unescaped leaf, a hydration mismatch detected but not surfaced, a payload leaking server-only data, chunk ordering under back-pressure, a continuation registry leaking per request, and a Ring middleware swallowing an exception into a 200.
Tree: review-sep16 worktree, trunk d89a41e057
Scope read: implementation/ssr/src/** (27 files, 13537 lines, all read in full); implementation/ssr-ring/src/** (10 files, 3706 lines, all read in full); implementation/ssr-node/bin/serve.cjs + src/*.cjs (8 files, ~2700 lines, all read in full). The three test trees (135 tracked files) skimmed by name plus targeted greps for what is pinned.
Owning specs consulted: spec/011-SSR.md (§Payload scope, §:rf/hydrate, §Hydration-mismatch detection, §Mismatch recovery and configuration, §Cookie shape, §The reserved fx guard their own args, §Response accumulator, §Header replacement vs append, §Boundary nesting, §Writer concurrency model, §Payload liveness, §Failed-root isolation), spec/004B-UI-Tree-and-Conversion.md §The SSR consumption boundary, spec/004C-Roots-and-Mount.md §§6, 7, 10, spec/Security.md §XSS at output boundaries / §CRLF injection / §Open-redirect mitigation / §Trusted shell hook contract, spec/Ownership.md rows 33, 55, 58.

Overall: the slice is in good shape. Escaping is position-correct at every leaf I traced (text, attr, attr-name, raw-script, EDN-script with `</`/`<!` breakout throw, boundary ids `escape-attr`'d at streaming.cljc:111/160); the payload is fail-closed at policy, egress and incarnation-token liveness; the response/request/error-trace side channels are cleared on every frame-destroy path including the setup-failure catch (pipeline.clj:337-342); the Ring handlers never turn a throw into a 200 (5xx-before-head rule, `safe-on-error` locked 500); the Node crossing carries body markup only and refuses application-authored wording on every terminal path. The findings below are the places where a detection exists but its production-visible half is missing, or where two ends of one contract disagree about a type.

## Findings, ranked

### 1. Hydration mismatch is detected but invisible in a production build unless `:on-mismatch :hard-error`  [CONFIRMED] [severity: medium] [kind: spec-drift]
- Where: implementation/ssr/src/re_frame/ssr/hydrate.cljc:671-676 (`verify-hydration!`); contrast hydrate.cljc:146-226 (`emit-rejected-hydration!`); same pattern server-side at implementation/ssr/src/re_frame/ssr/streaming.cljc:686 (`:rf.ssr/suspense-boundary-failed`)
- What: `verify-hydration!` reports a mismatch only through the `:trace/emit-error!` late-bind hook, whose producer is gated on `debug-enabled?`, so under the default `:warn` policy a production client computes the hash, finds the mismatch, and tells nobody; the two rejection guards in the same handler route through the always-on `:error-emit/dispatch-error-record` hook and this one does not.
- Evidence: `(rf.late-bind/get-fn :trace/emit-error!)` is the only emit in `verify-hydration!`; its producer is core `trace.cljc:938` → `emit-error!`, whose body is `(when rf.interop/debug-enabled? …)` (trace.cljc:915). `emit-rejected-hydration!` (hydrate.cljc:206-226) additionally calls `:error-emit/dispatch-error-record`, whose producer `error_emit.cljc:964` is documented "Always-on (NOT gated by `re-frame.interop/debug-enabled?`)". The code comment at hydrate.cljc:671 ("Always emit the trace (monitoring integrations rely on it)") is false in a `goog.DEBUG=false` build. Spec 011:1533-1534 promises "External monitoring integrations register a trace listener and ship mismatch events" and "Default: detection on in all builds", and 011:834-840 rules that a hydration-boot outcome "must be observable in production … on the same reasoning as `:rf.error/malformed-hydration-payload`". The test tree knows: `ssr_hydration_mismatch_test.clj:46-60` (rf2-lwtlk) documents the split and leans on the `:hard-error` throw as the production witness — but `:hard-error` is opt-in, so the DEFAULT production posture is pay-for-detection, surface-nothing. Control for "no always-on record": grep `dispatch-error-record` over ssr/src finds hydrate.cljc:206/226, boot.cljc:39/495, response.cljc:1097, error_projector.cljc:70 — none inside `verify-hydration!`. Server-side sibling: a continuation that throws is contained to its fallback and reported only via `rf.trace/emit-error!` (streaming.cljc:686), while the writer failure one layer up gets both axes (ring/streaming.clj:463); spec 011:1062 says `-Dre-frame.debug=false` is "the posture an SSR host is told to run in".
- Action: decide: (A) fan a tight always-on record (`{:error :rf.ssr/hydration-mismatch :frame … :server-hash … :client-hash … :recovery …}` — identifiers and two 8-char hex strings, no payload, so no egress projection needed) through `:error-emit/dispatch-error-record` beside the trace, exactly as `emit-rejected-hydration!` does; do the same for `:rf.ssr/suspense-boundary-failed` with `{:error … :frame … :id …}`; ~15 lines total; or (B) amend 011 §Mismatch recovery items 3-4 to say the trace is dev-only and production observability requires `:hard-error`. A matches the spec's own 011:834-840 reasoning and the sibling guards.

### 2. Cookie `:expires` as a string passes the "every build" fx guard, then throws at Ring materialisation into a generic 500  [CONFIRMED] [severity: medium] [kind: spec-drift]
- Where: implementation/ssr/src/re_frame/ssr/response.cljc:274-275 (`cookie-attr-shape`); implementation/ssr/src/re_frame/ssr/server_fx_schemas.cljc:138; implementation/ssr-ring/src/re_frame/ssr/ring/cookie.clj:156-165
- What: The fx boundary accepts `:expires` as an integer OR a string, but `cookie->set-cookie-header` throws `:rf.error/cookie-invalid-expires` for any non-integer, so a string `:expires` is accepted by `:rf.server/set-cookie`, survives the drain, and blows up after the body is rendered — outside the projector, inside the outer `catch Throwable` → `safe-on-error` "Internal error" 500 with the cookie error id lost.
- Evidence: shape row `[:expires false #(or (integer? %) (string? %)) "an integer of epoch millis, or a string"]`; schema `[:expires {:optional true} [:maybe [:or :int :string]]]` with a "spec: :int" note beside it; `cookie.clj:156` `(when (and (some? expires) (not (integer? expires))) (rf.error/throw-error! :rf.error/cookie-invalid-expires …))`. Spec 011 §Cookie shape: `:expires <int-ms>`; 011:1062 (§The reserved fx guard their own args): the guard checks "attributes of the types §Cookie shape names … in every build". `:max-age` has the mirror asymmetry: a string is concatenated verbatim into `Max-Age=`. The divergence is load-bearing for two tests that use it as a post-render-throw VEHICLE — `ssr-ring/test/…/ring_test.clj:3132` and `…/ring/streaming_robustness_test.clj:460` — and both of their comments say "`validate-cookie!` … does NOT type-check :expires", which is itself stale (it does, and admits the string).
- Action: decide: (A) make `:expires` and `:max-age` `integer?` at the shape table and the schema (matches spec; the rejection lands at dispatch time with the shape-table's `:rf.error/server-fx-args-invalid`, response.cljc:283-297), and give the two tests a different post-render throw (a throwing `:html-shell` / `:head` fn); or (B) accept a pre-formatted RFC-1123 string end-to-end in cookie.clj. One type at both ends; A is the smaller change and the spec's.

### 3. ssr-node: an isolate that dies while IDLE is silent and is discovered by the next caller, who is refused instead of routed to a live isolate  [CONFIRMED] [severity: medium] [kind: correctness]
- Where: implementation/ssr-node/src/isolate.cjs:186-192 and 238-243 (`worker.on('error')` / `worker.on('exit')` after ready), isolate.cjs:410-421 (`_failPendingRender`), implementation/ssr-node/src/pool.cjs:165-171 (`acquire`)
- What: A worker that dies between renders (a scheduled callback from a completed render throwing, or a library calling `process.exit()` later) is marked `dead` but stays in `idleIsolates`; `acquire()` pops it without checking `dead`, `render()` rejects `ISOLATE_LOST 'this isolate is dead'`, and only then does `release()` start a replacement — so the next request eats a 500 (with no `afterChunks` stamp, which isolate.cjs:88-90 says a consumer needs) even when a healthy sibling is idle, and the death itself is never logged because `reportIsolateFault` is guarded on `this.pendingRender`.
- Evidence: `if (this.pendingRender) reportIsolateFault(…)` at isolate.cjs:186; `_failPendingRender` sets `this.dead = true` unconditionally (412) and only rejects when a render is pending; `acquire()` is `const idleIsolate = this.idleIsolates.pop(); if (idleIsolate) return Promise.resolve(idleIsolate);` — no `dead` check; nothing tells the pool. pool.cjs:37-39 explains the log guard by "the unguarded half … is the boot phase, which has its own diagnostic" — the post-ready idle phase is a third phase with neither. Control for "unpinned": grep `exits|idle|dead` over ssr-node/test finds the `exits` fixture only mid-render (egress.test.cjs:1294, 1320) and pre-ready (timeout.test.cjs:304-369), and `concurrency.test.cjs:118` asserting `dead === false` in another scenario; no test kills an idle worker.
- Action: give `Isolate` an `onDeath` callback the pool installs; on a post-ready `error`/`exit` with no pending render, log via `reportIsolateFault` unconditionally and have the pool remove it from `idleIsolates` and start the replacement immediately; make `acquire()` skip `dead` entries (`while` instead of `if`). Add one test row to `egress.test.cjs` with a fixture that exits on a timer after `complete`.

### 4. Wire EDN is written with `pr-str` under whatever print vars the thread inherited  [PLAUSIBLE] [severity: low] [kind: correctness]
- Where: implementation/ssr-ring/src/re_frame/ssr/ring/pipeline.clj:671 (payload), implementation/ssr-ring/src/re_frame/ssr/ring/streaming.clj:391 (delta) and :438 (final payload), implementation/ssr/src/re_frame/ssr/manifest.cljc:595 (root manifest), implementation/ssr/src/re_frame/ssr/render_state.cljc:387 (JVM→Node state partitions), implementation/ssr-ring/src/re_frame/ssr/ring/node.clj:293 (`args`)
- What: Six sites serialise data the client or the Node isolate must READ BACK with a bare `pr-str`, so a root-altered or thread-bound `*print-length*` / `*print-level*` / `*print-readably* false` / `*print-meta*` (a dev `user.clj` `alter-var-root`, or a test harness driving the handler on a REPL thread) yields `...`-truncated or unquoted EDN that the client reads as malformed → silent client-only fallback / manifest refusal.
- Evidence: Grep `print-length|print-level|print-readably|print-namespace-maps` over `implementation/ssr*/src` → 0; control: the same pattern over `implementation` finds `schemas/src/re_frame/schemas/validator.cljc:113-115` binding them for its own printing. Reading the six sites: none binds. What would confirm: run any handler test with `(alter-var-root #'*print-length* (constantly 3))` in the fixture and read the payload back.
- Action: one `wire-edn` helper in `re-frame.ssr` (`(binding [*print-length* nil *print-level* nil *print-readably* true *print-meta* false *print-dup* false] (pr-str v))`) used at the six sites. Ten lines; removes a class rather than an instance.

### 5. Spec 011 draws the default accumulator `:headers` as a map, then says it is a vector of pairs (the code is the vector)  [CONFIRMED] [severity: low] [kind: spec-drift]
- Where: spec/011-SSR.md:1030 vs spec/011-SSR.md:1137; implementation/ssr/src/re_frame/ssr/response.cljc:585
- What: §Response accumulator's "default shape" block shows `:headers {"content-type" "text/html; charset=utf-8"}` while §Header replacement vs append says "The runtime stores headers internally as an ordered vector of `[name value]` pairs" — the code is `[["content-type" "text/html; charset=utf-8"]]`, and an adapter author or an AI reading the first block would build the wrong shape.
- Evidence: read both spec lines and `default-response` in response.cljc.
- Action: change 011:1030 to the vector-of-pairs form (one line; the spec is the artefact, so fix the spec to match its own later paragraph and the code).

## Considered, left alone
- `:rf/hydrate` is registered without `:platforms #{:client}` (ssr.cljc) though 011's illustrative handler shows it — the handler gates its client-only fxs on the resolved platform itself; a server dispatch of `:rf/hydrate` is the programmer's own call.
- Duplicate boundary ids: server keeps the LAST continuation (`dedupe-continuations`), client `mount-for` targets the LAST mount — consistent with 011 §Boundary nesting (earlier placeholder keeps its fallback); dev-trace-only emission is right for a programmer error.
- The streaming writer has no per-continuation deadline — continuation render is synchronous CPU work with no I/O, the same exposure as a non-streamed render; 011 §Writer concurrency model deliberately makes the ceiling the host server's.
- Last-trace-wins error projection (a 500 then a 404 in one drain projects the 404) — documented policy; the 5xx-before-head pre-commit rule still holds on the drain-time arm.
- `ssr-middleware`'s default `:match?` catches every GET including static assets — documented default; trust the programmer to pass `:match?`.

## Instruments and controls
- `git rev-parse --short HEAD` in the worktree → `d89a41e057`.
