title: story: :extends deep-merges :network route replies (and :sub-overrides values), so a child flipping a route :ok -> :failure compiles {:reply {:ok .. :failure ..}} and the stub silently fires :ok
description:
Discovered by the senior-developer review rf2-wd2t (2026-09-13, trunk 1c9ff9697b), deliberately NOT filed as a defect: the shape was confirmed at source, the runtime symptom was not. This bead is the probe; if it reproduces, retitle as the bug (P2) and fix; if not, close with the measurement.

WHERE: tools/story/src/re_frame/story/plan.cljc:275-281 (deep merge through :extends) with context-keys at :263 (which includes :network, :sub-overrides, :db-seed); plan_network_test.cljc:256-259 rejects a reply map carrying both :ok and :failure at registration.

THE QUESTION: for a parent variant with {:network {:route {:reply {:ok ...}}}} and a child :extends it with {:network {:route {:reply {:failure ...}}}}, what does the compiled plan carry, and which branch does stub-handler fire on a live run? If the merged reply carries both keys, the child's intent (a failure case) is silently replaced by whichever key the stub reads first, and the registration-time guard never sees the merged shape because it validates bodies, not plans.

SMALLEST CHANGE if confirmed: treat the value under each route as replace-by-child (or validate the compiled plan's reply map with the same guard registration uses).

GATE: jvm-tools-story.
notes:
PROBE VERDICT (extprobe-a, 2026-09-13): REPRODUCES. Retitled as a P2 bug and left OPEN; the fix waits for tools/story/src/re_frame/story/plan.cljc, which is held by the rf2-b2mt + rf2-jjhy PR.

WHERE MEASURED: worker tree at 5b89378c45. plan.cljc, args.cljc, implementation/http/src/re_frame/http/test_support.cljc and tools/story/spec/017-Testing-Story.md are byte-unchanged between that commit and origin/main 1b285ba9a8, so every citation below holds at tip.

METHOD: a throwaway probe file loaded with `clojure -M -i <probe>.clj` from tools/story (NOT `clojure -M:test -e`, whose -e is read as --exclude). It drives the REAL paths: `rf.story.plan/variant-plan` with a `:lookup` / `:fragment-lookup` map for the plan half, and `rf.story/reg-variant` + `rf.story/run` for the live half, with the capture-only `:rf.http/managed` sentinel pattern from network_runtime_test.clj. Captured exit 0. No tracked file edited.

FIXTURE:
  route      = [:get "/api/cart"]
  parent     = {:network {route {:reply {:ok {:items [1]}}}}}
  child      = {:extends parent :network {route {:reply {:failure {:kind :rf.http/http-4xx :status 409}}}}}

RESULTS:
  A2  child plan [:world :network]  => {[:get "/api/cart"] {:reply {:ok {:items [1]}, :failure {:kind :rf.http/http-4xx, :status 409}}}}
  A3  child RAW body vs the :variant schema => nil (valid) -- so registration never sees the merged shape
  A4  the COMPILED route map vs the :variant schema => REJECTED, ":reply must carry exactly one of :ok / :failure"
  B1  CONTROL, same intent through :compose (fragment carries the :ok route, variant the :failure route) => {[:get "/api/cart"] {:reply {:failure {...}}}} -- per-route replacement
  E1  CONTROL live run, a variant with ONLY the :failure route => app-db {:error {:status :error, :error {:status 409, :kind :rf.http/http-4xx}}}
  E2  live run of the :extends child => app-db {:cart {:items [1]}} and no :error -- the stub fired :ok; the child's failure case is silently lost
  E3  live-request sentinel => [] (no request escaped the stub)

SAME SHAPE ON THE OTHER TWO KEYS (all three are in `context-keys`, plan.cljc:263, deep-merged by `merge-context`, plan.cljc:275-281):
  C1  :sub-overrides via :extends, parent {[:cart/summary] {:items [1 2] :total 2}}, child {[:cart/summary] {:status :empty}} => {[:cart/summary] {:items [1 2], :total 2, :status :empty}}
  C2  same via :compose => {[:cart/summary] {:status :empty}}
  D1  :db-seed via :extends, parent {:user {:name "a" :admin? true}}, child {:user {:name "b"}} => {:user {:name "b", :admin? true}}
  D2  same via :compose => {:user {:name "b"}}

WHY THIS IS A BUG (intent, file:line):
  - :network. `NetworkReply` requires EXACTLY one of :ok / :failure (tools/story/src/re_frame/story/schemas.cljc:649-650). The stub's contract is `{:reply <:ok|:failure>}` (implementation/http/src/re_frame/http/test_support.cljc:517), and its `stub-handler` tests `(contains? reply :ok)` BEFORE :failure (:466-481), so a both-keys reply always answers :ok. Spec 017's merge-order table says "`:network` | per-route merge" (017-Testing-Story.md:1489). The :compose half of the same slot uses shallow per-route `merge` (plan.cljc:1488-1489). The ONE sentence that literally endorses deep-merge is 017-Testing-Story.md:2741-2744 ("deep-merged root -> child: a child variant's routes merge over the parent's"), and the schema rejects exactly what that produces, so that wording is the error and the fix corrects it.
  - :sub-overrides. Spec 017-Testing-Story.md:684-687 says the variant chain "wins per query key" and the result is "one flat {query-vector value} map"; an override is a PINNED value (:744) validated against the sub's output schema. A deep-merged value is one neither author wrote. :compose already replaces per query key (plan.cljc:1424, :1432).
  - :db-seed. Deep-merge through :extends IS documented (017-Testing-Story.md:815-818, "where `:extends` context deep-merged"), so by the letter it is not part of the bug. It does diverge from :compose, which replaces per path (plan.cljc:1445-1446). The fixer's call: align it with the other two and correct :817, or leave it.

SMALLEST FIX: in `merge-context` (or at the context-merge reduce, plan.cljc:1291-1299), merge :network and :sub-overrides (and :db-seed, if aligned) per top-level key with plain `merge` -- child wins per route / query vector / seed path, exactly as the :compose path already does -- and correct 017-Testing-Story.md:2742. The existing `network-inherits-through-extends` test (plan_network_test.cljc:231-246) uses DISJOINT routes, so it stays green under per-route replacement; add the same-route :ok -> :failure :extends case beside it, plus a live-run case in network_runtime_test.clj asserting the child's :failure lands. GATE: jvm-tools-story (`cd tools/story && clojure -M:test`).

NOT an rf2-fzbj.3 finding: that held review covers loaders and args, and states that the rf2-shx4 network work is not reopened.
FENCE DISCHARGED 2026-09-13 01:15:25 AUSEST (mayor): PR #9717 merged as ac36ed93bd (rf2-b2mt + rf2-jjhy). Title prefix struck in the same act. Dispatched in wave 2.
VERDICT (extfix-a, 2026-09-13): FIXED in PR #9722.

Fix: merge-context in tools/story/src/re_frame/story/plan.cljc now takes the context key. :network and :sub-overrides (per-entry-context-keys) merge per top-level entry through :extends with plain merge, so the child wins per route and per query key. That is the rule :compose already applied to both slots. Every other context map still deep-merges.

:db-seed is deliberately unchanged. Spec 017 documents its :extends deep merge (Direct app-db seeding, item 2), and that text does not contradict itself: it deep-merges within the chain, and the chain then wins per key against fragments. It does diverge from :compose, which replaces a seed path wholesale. Aligning them is a design call, not this bug.

Spec 017: the Network world sentence that called the :extends merge "deep-merged" now says per-route, and the merge-order table carries the per-entry rule for :network and a new :sub-overrides row.

Witnesses, committed before the fix and run against the unfixed code:
- plan-network-test/network-same-route-child-reply-replaces-parent-through-extends. The parent route answers :ok and the child flips the same route to :failure. The test asserts the child's reply and that the compiled route map passes the :variant schema.
- plan-test/sub-overrides-same-key-child-replaces-parent-through-extends.
- network-runtime-test/extends-child-flipping-a-route-to-failure-fires-the-failure, a live run.

Gate jvm-tools-story (cd tools/story && clojure -M:test), captured exits:
- baseline: exit 0, 1933 tests / 7136 assertions.
- witnesses only: exit 1, 1936 / 7143, 6 failures, all in the new tests. The compiled reply carried both :ok and :failure and was schema-rejected, the live run answered :ok, and the sub-override was fused.
- after the fix: exit 0, 1936 / 7143, 0 failures, 0 errors.

The existing disjoint-route test stayed green. Not an rf2-fzbj.3 finding.

title: Incomplete: Epoch diagnostics still drop panel instance IDs
description:
Merged-PR audit #9680, landed 4139622de22bb38d5b9b022a1b1d5f78d41d1375. The new instance qualifier correctly reaches ordinary Epoch payloads and the shared Machine Inspector cascade, but three diagnostic call paths still discard it. This leaves the original per-mount lifecycle correction incomplete.

In tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/panels/epoch/view.cljs:2748, interceptor-row-view calls error-blocks with only step-key and errors; render-step:5968 still invokes render-interceptor-step without instance, and that chain has no instance parameter. At5066-5068, subscriptions-table already receives instance but its row-extras callback calls violation-blocks without it. At5222, render-subscriptions-step similarly omits (:instance ctx) from its step-level violation-blocks call. The retained two-argument helper arities at5730 and5915 explicitly delegate with nil. Consequently error-block-details:5810 and violation-block:5713 compose the old unqualified mount IDs for these paths despite a named panel.

Two Epoch mounts named left/right showing the same interceptor exception with ex-data, or the same rendered subscription schema violation, therefore still share an EDN lifecycle/width key. Detaching either can remove the surviving inspector observer and width state. Example: both named panels produce epoch/violation-explain/:subscriptions/0 for the same step-level violation. The new browser fixture seeds dispatch plus one machine transition, so it never renders these diagnostics and cannot expose the dropped arguments. All five changed blobs match the green CI head; the Epoch source remains unchanged at freshly fetched origin/main. This is a static, complete argument-flow counterexample, not a newly executed browser reproduction.

Pass the existing instance token through the interceptor step/row/error path, the subscription row-extras path and the subscription step-level violation path. Add bounded diagnostic seeds to the existing two-mount witness so each rendered diagnostic gets disjoint mount IDs and sibling teardown preserves the survivor. Keep unnamed IDs, logical site IDs, row keys and disclosure sharing unchanged. No new identity mechanism or broad test matrix is needed.
acceptance_criteria: Named Epoch mounts qualify interceptor exception ex-data, per-subscription violation explainers and step-level subscription violation explainers. A focused regression exposes each formerly dropped call argument, and two real mounts rendering diagnostics keep distinct lifecycle/width identities across sibling teardown. Existing unnamed IDs and logical site/row identities remain unchanged; existing identity and browser/node suites pass.
close_reason: Closed by mayor: PR #9689 merged to main at 4631b14080 (2026-09-11 10:53Z). Qualified the three Epoch diagnostic inspector mounts (interceptor step/row/error, subscription row-extras, subscription step-level). Witness rows W6-W9 added to epoch_machine_mount_instance_id_dom_cljs_test; sabotage run captured exit 1 / 15 failures against the unrepaired source, 0 after restore with test/assertion counts unmoved (1016/5692).

title: Incomplete: acceptance C5 discards render contamination evidence
description:
Merged-PR audit #9669, merge b2ac2f879ffd59dd052225b70de8fd4bd2fcb5a2 (2026-09-11T07:27:47Z), source rf2-k97c.3. This concerns the new acceptance instrument, not a newly observed production defect. acceptance/test_helpers/criteria.cljs:685 claims that mounting, rendering and a real Xray interaction contribute nothing to the inspected application's evidence. But app-trace-event-ids at355-361 first keeps only records with [:tags :rf.event/v]. C5's two final assertions see only that reduced vector. A leaked :rf.view/rendered record carrying :rf.view/render-key and :frame but no event vector is discarded before either assertion. It can contaminate the application's epoch :renders while this C5 stays green.

This is the exact known evidence channel documented by the existing rf2-k97c.5/rf2-tqlmq guard in mount_cljs_test.cljs:2726-2783: ei-emit-render! emits :rf.view/rendered with render-key/frame and no :rf.event/v, and that test inspects epoch :renders. That older guard models the adapter mount-site tree in the node lane; it is not a real-browser proof of the new owned-root harness across its two substrates. The negative example here is static projection analysis, not an executed sabotage.

Retain the useful event-ring assertions and add a bounded check on raw render evidence/epoch :renders after the real mount and interaction. Keep a positive application-render control so an empty render channel is not treated as isolation. A deliberate Xray render attributed to the application through the real trace emitter must redden the check. Reuse the existing evidence/epoch helpers and avoid a new filter framework.
acceptance_criteria: C5 inspects the application's non-event render evidence as well as event IDs after real Xray mount/render/interaction in both adapter arms. A positive application render is visible; an intentionally misattributed Xray :rf.view/rendered record with no :rf.event/v is detected. The case fails under that contamination and passes with the correctly scoped tool. The existing event controls remain intact.
notes:
=== IMPLEMENTED 2026-09-11, PR #9684, branch worker/acccrit-a (with rf2-t2ke, one file, one dispatch). ===

Worker worktree guard RAN and exited 0. Merge base d1c08b7c86, rebased onto origin/main
before marking ready.

## THE PREMISE HOLDS, EXACTLY AS WRITTEN

Confirmed at tip: `app-trace-event-ids` keeps only records carrying `[:tags
:rf.event/v]`, and BOTH of C5's final assertions — the `rf.xray` filter and the
exact-set assertion — read that reduced vector. A `:rf.view/rendered` record carries
`:rf.view/render-key` and `:frame` and NO event vector, so it is discarded before either
assertion can reach it.

## WHAT LANDED

C5 now reads the application's ring along BOTH axes. The existing event-id assertions
and their positive control are UNTOUCHED; a render-record arm is added beside them,
read through `trace-buffer`'s own `:operation` flat-stream filter (Spec 009 §Filter
vocabulary) rather than a new filter framework.

RAW RENDER RECORDS RATHER THAN EPOCH `:renders`, and this is a deliberate choice worth
recording because the bead named either. Two reasons. (1) The `:renders` projection is
sourced FROM these emits — the epoch artefact back-fills a post-settle render into the
causing epoch — so the raw ring is strictly UPSTREAM: contamination cannot reach
`:renders` without appearing here first. (2) THE EPOCH ARM WOULD HAVE BEEN VACUOUS IN
THIS LANE. `rf/epoch-history` is late-bound with `:on-absent :empty-vec`, so it answers
`[]` when the epoch artefact is merely ABSENT FROM THE BUILD — the same shape a clean
epoch answers with — and this harness loads Xray's `registry`, not the `install` /
`preload` namespaces that require `re-frame.epoch`. The node-lane guard in
`mount_cljs_test.cljs` reads `:renders` and is the right instrument there, because that
suite does load it.

TWO CONTROLS, both placed after every assertion about the untouched world, so neither
can contaminate what is under test:
  * POSITIVE APPLICATION-RENDER CONTROL — a genuine app-attributed render must be
    VISIBLE. The bead asked for this in terms and it is the sharpest thing in it: an
    empty render channel is not isolation, and is also exactly what a dead reader looks
    like.
  * DETECTOR CONTROL — a deliberately misattributed `rf.xray`-namespaced render, tagged
    with the APPLICATION's frame and carrying no `:rf.event/v`, must be DETECTED. This
    is the bead's "a deliberate Xray render attributed to the application through the
    real trace emitter must redden the check", kept as a permanent assertion so the
    detector cannot silently go blind later.

A MECHANISM WORTH KNOWING FOR ANYONE TOUCHING THIS AGAIN: both controls must stamp
`:rf.trace/dispatch-id`, and without it they measure NOTHING. `push-to-ring!` retains an
event only `(when (and dispatch-id frame-id))` — a frameless or uncorrelated emit
streams to listeners and is never retained (the Spec 009 §B3 ruling). These emits are
made from a test body, so no `*handler-scope*` supplies one. `stamp-dispatch-id`'s own
docstring says a caller-supplied dispatch-id wins, and `stamp-frame` only ever SUPPLIES
the routing tag and never overrides one the site set — which is also what lets the
second control attribute an Xray-named render to the application's frame on purpose.
No `:rf.event/v` is smuggled in. The reasoning is written into the source.

THE CLOSING ASSERTION IS THE BEAD'S FINDING KEPT LIVE: it re-reads the EVENT-ID arm over
the now-contaminated ring and shows it STILL reporting exactly the application's own two
event ids. So anyone who later deletes the render arm has an assertion telling them why
event ids alone were never enough.

## THE NEW ASSERTIONS ARE PROVEN TO BITE

A misattributed Xray render planted into the application's ring BEFORE C5's render
assertions turned the browser lane RED at captured exit 1, reddening exactly four C5
assertions per adapter arm (the `rf.xray`-namespaced render assertion, the
empty-evidence assertion, the positive control and the detector control) across both
arms. Only criteria 4 and 5 failed and the totals held at 975 tests / 5476 assertions,
so the plant did not crash a namespace and silence its neighbours. Plant and restore
were verified by blob hash.

## STATUS

Left OPEN deliberately: the PR is not merged. Captured gate exits are in PR #9684's
`## Quality gates` section.
close_reason:
Done. PR #9684 merged 5cd19d6e59a497d9ef4bb231e77e5bfd805c200f, at band 87 with nothing
non-terminal and a clean merge-tree against trunk.

C5 now instruments the raw render-evidence channel rather than asserting over a projection that had
already dropped it, with the positive application-render control this bead asked for so an empty
channel is not read as isolation.

THE WORKER DECLINED THE EPOCH :renders ROUTE THIS BEAD OFFERED, AND THE REASONING IS THE MOST
VALUABLE THING HERE: it would have been VACUOUSLY GREEN. rf/epoch-history is :on-absent :empty-vec,
so an absent artefact answers [], which is the same shape a clean epoch answers with -- and this
harness loads `registry` rather than the install/preload namespaces that pull re-frame.epoch in. Raw
records are also strictly upstream of that projection. That is the empty-channel trap this bead
warned about, arriving through a mechanism the bead did not name.

A TRAP WORTH PROPAGATING, now written into the source: the controls must stamp
:rf.trace/dispatch-id or they measure NOTHING -- push-to-ring! retains only
(when (and dispatch-id frame-id)). The prior-art ei-emit-render! works for EPOCH but would not have
reached the RING, so anyone copying it into a ring-based check gets a silent empty pass.

title: ci: jvm-repo-source-walks skips six walks behind the first failure (no step if:), and on a prose-only PR that lane is the only place they run
description:
`test.yml`'s `jvm-repo-source-walks` job runs SEVEN independent repo-wide walks as seven
steps, and NOT ONE of them carries an `if:`. GitHub's default step condition is `success()`,
so the first walk that fails SKIPS THE SIX BEHIND IT. The seven walks are independent of one
another -- they share only a JDK and a Maven cache -- so there is no ordering reason for this.

=== MEASURED AT SOURCE, trunk 974ff9ed45, by the mayor (fact, not inference) ===

  .github/workflows/test.yml
    line 3153   jvm-repo-source-walks:          job block runs to 3206
    steps found 10 (3 setup + 7 walks)
    `if:` guards in the whole job block: 0

  the seven walks, by line:
    3186  Absence-repair floor lint for :rf/default (implementation/** + tools/**)
    3189  Egress-chokepoint conformance (every implementation/ src root)
    3192  Error-catalogue channel conformance (every implementation/ src root)
    3195  Warn-once-clear governance (file-seq over implementation/)
    3198  Production-gate naming drift (every artefact's test/ tree)
    3201  Late-bind directory drift (every implementation/ src root)
    3204  Observation render-law drift (every tracked prose file, git ls-files)

=== WHY IT MATTERS HERE SPECIFICALLY, AND THIS IS THE HALF WORTH KEEPING ===

This lane exists to schedule these walks when `jvm-core` does not. Measured in the same file:

    line 1414   jvm-core:  if: needs.detect_changed_surfaces.outputs.implementation_jvm == 'true'
    jvm-repo-source-walks:  NO job-level `if:` at all

So on a PROSE-ONLY PR -- where `implementation_jvm` is false and `jvm-core` never runs --
`jvm-repo-source-walks` is the ONLY place those six later walks execute. If the first one
fails there, they do not run anywhere, on any lane, for that PR.

**THE DANGER IS NOT THAT IT ADMITS A MERGE.** The job goes red, so merge clause 2 blocks it
honestly. What fails open is the INFERENCE every reader makes next: "the job is red because
of step 1; fix step 1 and this lane is clean." The six behind it were never EVALUATED, so a
green after the re-run is the FIRST time they have run at all -- and that green looks
identical to a green that had been passing all along.

That is not hypothetical. It is exactly what happened on the incident that produced
rf2-ep7u: a StackOverflowError in the FIRST walk (the `:rf/default` floor lint) took the lane
down, and the six behind it were silently skipped while everyone read the failure as being
about the one step named in the log.

=== THE REPAIR, AND ITS ONE JUDGEMENT ===

Give each of the seven walk steps a condition that survives a failed predecessor -- the
conventional spelling is `if: ${{ !cancelled() }}`, which runs the step unless the workflow
was cancelled, rather than `always()`, which also runs it after a cancellation and is the
wrong default for a lane nobody wants to keep burning after a cancel.

**Do NOT put the guard on the three SETUP steps** (JDK, Clojure CLI, Maven cache). A walk
whose JDK never installed will fail for a reason that has nothing to do with the walk, and
seven such failures is a worse log than one honest one. The guard belongs on the seven walks
and nowhere else -- so this is seven added lines, not ten.

=== A SECOND, SMALLER ITEM IN THE SAME JOB, CLUSTERED HERE DELIBERATELY ===

`test.yml:3143` carries an illustrative comment giving the lane's per-namespace test counts as
"1 / 3 / 27 / 1 / 2 / 8 / 5". Measured today: **3 / 3 / 30 / 1 / 2 / 8 / 5**.

Position 1 moved from 1 to 3 because of the rf2-ep7u repair, which added rows. **Position 3
was ALREADY STALE before that** -- 27 against a true 30 -- so this drifted earlier and nobody
noticed, which is the argument for correcting it rather than deleting it.

Nothing is broken by the staleness: the ENFORCED floor is the runner's own default of 1, and
the comment itself says there is no calibrated number to maintain. So correct the numbers, or
argue in the PR body that an uncalibrated illustrative count should not be maintained at all
and remove it. **Either is acceptable; pick one and say why.** What is NOT acceptable is
leaving a number that is wrong in two positions.

=== HOT ZONE ===

`.github/workflows/**` is hot zone: one toucher at a time, never parallel. Both items are in
one file and one job, which is why they are one bead and must be one PR.

title: instrument: bare `grep -c $'\r'` reads 0 in the Bash tool; only a $() capture reads the truth
description:
A BARE `grep -c $'\r' <file>` IN THE BASH TOOL READS **0** ON A FILE THAT DEMONSTRABLY
CARRIES 156 CARRIAGE RETURNS. The identical command with its output captured by `$( )`
reads **156**. Same file, same shell, same invocation of the same grep binary.

**THE DETERMINANT IS THE INVOCATION FORM, NOT THE FILE.** This matters because it was
first reported as a file-dependent oddity (a worker saw `grep -c $'\r'` read 0 on a file
Python counted 260 CRs in, while the mayor could not reproduce it on `CLAUDE.md`), and the
coordinator explicitly recorded that the determinant was unknown. It is not file-dependent:
measured on BOTH the mayor checkout's `CLAUDE.md` and a worktree copy carrying an extra
3,396 bytes, the bare form reads 0 on both and the `$( )` form reads 156 on both, with
Python reading 156 on both.

=== MEASURED 2026-09-10, worktree hashform-a, base 03d4af871c / f025546df1 ===

    form                                              mayor copy   edited copy
    bare      grep -c $'\r' <file>                        0             0
    bare      grep -c "$(printf '\r')" <file>             0             0
    bare      grep -c $'\r$' <file>                       0             0
    captured  echo "$(grep -c $'\r' <file>)"            156           156
    Python    open(p,'rb').read().count(b'\r')         156           156

The pattern SPELLING is not the determinant either: the `printf` substitution form fails
bare exactly as the ANSI-C-quoted form does, and the ANSI-C-quoted form succeeds once the
grep itself sits inside `$( )`. What moves the answer is whether the grep invocation is
captured.

**IT IS GREP THAT WRITES THE ZERO, NOT THE HARNESS RENDERING IT.** Redirected to a file and
read back with Python, the bare form's output is literally `b'0\n'`. Redirecting to a file
and piping to `cat` both still read 0, so the destination of stdout is not the determinant.
Exit status is 1 (no match), consistent with a genuine zero rather than an error.

**RULED OUT: binary classification.** `grep -a` changes nothing (0 either way), and a
deliberately NUL-bearing scratch file makes grep OVER-count (4 against Python's 3) rather
than read zero, so the "grep decided it was binary" hypothesis does not produce this.
`grep -c .` reads 108 on `CLAUDE.md`, which is exactly its non-blank line count as measured
by Python, so grep is reading every line of the file.

The precise mechanism inside the Bash tool is NOT established here and is deliberately left
open. What is established is the observable, its reproducibility in both directions on one
file, and a working guard.

=== WHY IT IS WORTH CATALOGUING: IT MAKES A STANDING CHECK PASS VACUOUSLY ===

`CLAUDE.md`'s instrument item (e) instructs anyone editing that file to confirm afterwards
that **the total CR count equals the CRLF count**. Run with the bare form, that check reads
`0 == 0` and PASSES — on a file whose CRs it cannot see at all. The check is not merely
wrong, it is wrong in the direction that reports success, and it is prescribed by the file
it is used on, so every future editor of `CLAUDE.md` meets it.

This is the same family as the instrument defects (a) through (r) already catalogue: a
clean-looking answer, exit status consistent with it, nothing on screen to betray it, and
a failure in the reassuring direction.

=== THE GUARD ===

Count carriage returns with Python reading the file in binary, or capture the grep through
`$( )` and never trust a bare one. Prefer Python: it needs no rule about invocation context
and it separates total CR from CRLF pairs from bare CR, which the line-oriented grep count
cannot do at all (`grep -c` counts LINES matching, not CR bytes, so it silently answers a
different question from the one item (e) asks even when it works).

=== SUGGESTED DISPOSITION ===

A new lettered item in the `## Workflow` instrument list of `CLAUDE.md`, and a one-clause
amendment to item (e) naming the instrument its own check must be run with. NOT folded into
item (r) (the `git hash-object` form item, landed under rf2-ymkd) — that is a different
family and mixing them would blunt both. Discovered while verifying rf2-ymkd's own edit to
`CLAUDE.md`, where the bare form's vacuous `0 == 0` was caught only because the same numbers
had been taken with Python first.

THE DETERMINANT IS THE INVOCATION FORM, NOT THE FILE. That correction matters because the finding was first reported as file-dependent and the coordinator recorded the determinant as unknown -- and could not reproduce it, because the $( ) form masks it. I reproduced all three legs in the mayor checkout at 57eb7fb039 before dispatching, so the central claim was mayor-measured rather than inherited.

title: lint.yml cancels its own trunk runs (group keyed on github.ref + cancel-in-progress), making 'Lint required' on main ~94% false positives — copy test.yml's concurrency shape
description:
`lint.yml` cancels its own trunk runs, so the `Lint required` signal on main is ~94% false positives and nobody can read it. This is the DETECTION half of rf2-fa7c and needs no ruling — file separately so it can be fixed while the branch-protection question waits on Mike.

THE BUG, one block:

    # .github/workflows/lint.yml:159-161
    concurrency:
      group: lint-${{ github.ref }}
      cancel-in-progress: true

On main, `github.ref` is the SAME VALUE for every push, so all trunk runs share one concurrency group and each push cancels the one before it. `test.yml:16-18` already has the correct shape and is the model to copy:

    concurrency:
      group: tests-${{ github.event.pull_request.number || github.run_id }}
      cancel-in-progress: ${{ github.event_name == 'pull_request' }}

It keys on the PR number when there is one and falls back to the unique `run_id` otherwise, so trunk runs never share a group; and it only cancels for `pull_request` events, so a push-to-main run is never pre-empted.

MEASURED 2026-09-08, independently of the dossier that found it, over the last 100 main-branch runs of each workflow (`gh run list --workflow <wf> --branch main --limit 100 --json conclusion`):

    lint.yml    46 cancelled
    test.yml     0 cancelled

The `test.yml` zero is the positive control: same command, same branch, same window, same instrument, non-zero-capable — so the 46 is a real difference in behaviour and not a query artefact.

WHY THAT DESTROYS THE SIGNAL. `lint.yml`'s aggregator runs under `if: ${{ always() }}`, so it still reports on a CANCELLED run, and a cancelled dependency is not a success — the aggregate goes red. The result is a required check that is red about half the time on main with only a handful of real failures behind it. A signal with that false-positive rate is unreadable, so it gets ignored, which is exactly what happened: the rf2-fa7c dossier found `lint.yml`'s drift-check DID go failure on 3 of the 4 bad trunk commits, and a manual guard was then built to replace a machine that was already working but unreadable.

THE FIX: adopt `test.yml`'s concurrency shape in `lint.yml`. Two lines. No behaviour change for PRs (they keep cancel-on-new-push); trunk runs stop cancelling each other.

VERIFY BY EFFECT AFTER THE FIX, not by reading the diff: re-run the same `gh run list` census over the following ~50 main pushes and confirm the cancelled count drops toward zero while `test.yml` stays at zero. Then re-check the `Lint required` red rate on main — the point of the fix is that a red becomes informative, so the acceptance test is that the remaining reds are all real.

HOT ZONE: `.github/workflows/*` is a hot-zone path per CLAUDE.md — sequence this against any other workflow-touching bead rather than running it in parallel, and re-measure the check-count band after it lands (this changes no job keys, so the band should not move; confirm rather than assume).

DISCOVERED-FROM rf2-fa7c, whose dossier (ai/decisions/rf2-fa7c.api-manifest-var-count-drift.md, local-only) carries the full analysis including the 47-minutes-of-real-trunk-redness figure and the reconciliation over all 227 trunk commits that ever touched the manifest.
acceptance_criteria: lint.yml uses a run-id/PR-scoped concurrency group and only cancels on pull_request; cancelled trunk runs drop toward zero over the next ~50 main pushes with test.yml as the zero control; remaining Lint reds on main are real.
notes:
--- MAYOR 2026-09-08 19:5x AUSEST — PREMISE VERIFIED AT SOURCE; HELD ONE TICK ON THE HOT-ZONE RULE, NOT ON DOUBT ---
Verified both halves myself on origin/main at 0a6ec61e0f before queuing this, because a workflow change is
the one class where a wrong premise moves the merge criterion itself:
  * .github/workflows/lint.yml — the block is there exactly as filed:
        concurrency:
          group: lint-${{ github.ref }}
          cancel-in-progress: true
  * .github/workflows/test.yml — the model shape is there too, and it is genuinely different in the way
    that matters:
        group: tests-${{ github.event.pull_request.number || github.run_id }}
        cancel-in-progress: ${{ github.event_name == 'pull_request' }}
    Two differences, and BOTH are load-bearing: the group key falls back to github.run_id (unique per run)
    rather than github.ref (identical for every trunk push), and cancellation is gated to pull_request so
    a trunk run is never cancelled at all. Copying only the group key would halve the fix.
WHY IT IS HELD: worker/egress90-a's PR #9491 is open and its file list includes .github/workflows/test.yml
— it added a residue gate to the always-on invariant job. CLAUDE.md's hot-zone list names
`.github/workflows/*` as sequential-never-parallel, and I have enforced that on workers all day. Two
different FILES would not conflict textually, but the rule names the directory for a second reason that
does apply here: a workflow change moves the CHECK SET, which is clause 5 of the merge criterion, and two
concurrent workflow changes make the band ambiguous while both are in flight.
SO THIS GOES THE TICK AFTER #9491 MERGES. The cost is one tick and the rule is not mine to bend for
convenience.
WORTH CARRYING INTO THE BRIEF: #9491's own worker measured the job-key discriminator at 0 added job keys
for its test.yml change (control 1 on 366e4fca79), so it adds a STEP rather than a job and the band does
not move. A concurrency-block change adds no job key either — but measure it rather than assuming, with
the two-space discriminator, because a zero there is the reassuring answer.
close_reason: Delivered by PR #9494, merged as trunk cb703356f1. One file, one hunk. Verified on the merged trunk: lint.yml now reads group: lint-${{ github.event.pull_request.number || github.run_id }} with cancel-in-progress: ${{ github.event_name == 'pull_request' }}. Both differences preserved — the run_id fallback (unique per run, where github.ref is identical for every trunk push) AND the pull_request gate (so a trunk run is never pre-empted). Copying only the group key would have half-fixed it. THE ~94% FIGURE WAS RIGHT BUT MISLABELLED, and the worker found the denominator rather than repeating my number. It is NOT the cancellation rate. It is cancelled / (cancelled + failure) — the share of RED trunk outcomes that are false. Measured over the last 200 main-branch runs of each workflow: lint.yml 76 cancelled (38% of runs), 124 success, ZERO failures; test.yml as the control 0 cancelled, 196 success, 3 failures. So in that window the false-red share is 100%, not 94% — every non-success trunk outcome of lint.yml was a cancellation and there were no real lint findings at all. The claim was if anything understated. THE MECHANISM WAS VERIFIED, NOT INFERRED: cancelled main run 34213407147 has all seven jobs reading 'cancelled' AND 'Lint required' reading 'failure' — a red required check with no lint finding behind it. AND IT IS LOAD-BEARING FOR MERGES, WHICH I CONFIRMED INDEPENDENTLY AFTER THE MERGE. Classic branch protection returns 404 here, so the branch LOOKS unprotected; GitHub models this twice and the answer is in rulesets. The active ruleset requires exactly three status checks: 'All required checks passed', 'Lint required' and 'Docs required'. So a false red on Lint required blocks merges, it does not merely make trunk unreadable. JOB-KEY DISCRIMINATOR EXERCISED IN BOTH DIRECTIONS by the worker and again by me at merge time: 0 added on this branch, 1 on 366e4fca79 which genuinely added a job, and the unindented form reads 0 on BOTH — the reassuring-zero failure reproduced. Rollup came in at 87, the same band as each of the last five merged trunk PRs. Gates: check_workflow_yaml.py 0 (11 files parse), check_workflow_job_timeouts.py 0 (117 jobs), _lint-workflow-policy.test.cjs 0 (4/4), check_gate_scheduling.py 0 (34 gate commands). actionlint is genuinely unavailable on this box, corroborated by the yaml checker's own header rather than assumed. Sabotage proof on an unmatched quote with the match count read as 1 before the run, both yaml gates going red naming the file and line, restore verified by git blob hash. THE ACCEPTANCE IS POST-MERGE BY CONSTRUCTION and I am closing without waiting for it, the same call I made on rf2-amh0: the confirmation is that cancelled trunk runs drop toward zero over the next ~50 main pushes with test.yml as the zero control. Anyone can run it — gh run list --workflow=lint.yml --branch=main --limit 100 and count 'cancelled'. Holding a P2 open for an opportunistic observation of a structurally-verified fix costs a line in every backlog read forever.

title: beads: 210 memory keys vanished from the live store today (1127 -> 938), invisible to bd stats

    (bd-export-from-wrong-cwd-returns-a-different-database) says bd run from the wrong cwd silently
    discovers a different store, and CLAUDE.md repeats it. The two later payloads carry `Total Issues:
    1099` and the two earlier ones carry NO stats block at all, so the payload FORMAT differs and a
    count-to-count comparison across them is not by itself sound.
  * FALSE EXPLANATION 2 RULED OUT — "the payload just did not list them". I asked the LIVE database
    directly rather than trusting a cached payload: `bd memories <key>` returns "No memories matching"
    for concurrency-cap-3-background-agents-not-6-mike, codex-pr-review-cursor and
    merge-band-87-after-8753, while the control 502-on-merge-means-it-may-have-happened IS found. The
    instrument works and the keys are genuinely gone.

WHAT I DO NOT KNOW, stated plainly rather than guessed:
  * WHO deleted them. I ran no `bd forget`. A sibling session (re-frame2-81, idle, started a day ago) and
    the local merged-PR audit harness both write to this database.
  * WHETHER SOME WERE DELETED ON PURPOSE AND CORRECTLY. Several missing keys are things that SHOULD go —
    merge-band-84-after-8775 and merge-band-87-after-8753 are stale band records of exactly the kind
    CLAUDE.md says never to quote, and codex-pr-review-cursor is a cursor. A deliberate cull of stale
    memories would be good hygiene and would look exactly like this. Others do not read that way at all:
    concurrency-cap-3-background-agents-not-6-mike is an operator PREFERENCE, and losing that silently is
    the bad case.
  * WHETHER THEY ARE RECOVERABLE. The store is Dolt, so history should hold them, but `bd dolt` exposes
    no log/sql passthrough — only start/stop/status/commit/push/pull. `bd dolt push` has run many times
    since, so the remote carries the post-loss state too; earlier Dolt commits should still hold the rows.

WHY THIS WAS INVISIBLE, and it is already recorded as a class: `bd stats` reports ISSUES ONLY — it read a
healthy `Total Issues: 1099` across the whole event. An existing memory spells out the reconciliation
that catches it (count the two populations separately and check they sum to the export's row count). That

Merged at band 87 on all five clauses — band re-measured this tick on three settled rollups (#9525/#9524/#9522, unanimous 87): 87 distinct checks, 18 SUCCESS / 69 SKIPPED / **0** failure-or-cancelled, 0 non-terminal, all four workflow runs completed at the full head oid `7dc98158690f84a72a83381750bf2b7a7ac27e6c`, 0 workflow diff lines and 0 new job keys, `git merge-tree` exit 0, 0 `.beads` paths on the branch. Fast-forwarded to `3c0028ce88`, `HEAD == origin/main` re-read after.

## MY OWN CLOSE REASON ON THE SECOND PASS WAS WRONG, AND THE AUDIT DISPROVED IT

I wrote that capturing the baseline oid "immediately after the head copy" meant "the captured oid and the bytes actually compared cannot drift apart — that placement is the substance of the fix." **Adjacency is not identity.** `head_copy()` read `HEAD` in its own body; `BASELINE_COMMIT` resolved `HEAD` again fifteen lines later. Two reads of a moving branch, and a concurrent commit between them makes the guard compare commit A's bytes while printing commit B's sha — a commit that never held the values the operator is told to recover. The printed lookup then exits 0 with an empty value, which is precisely the reassuring failure #9524 set out to remove, reached one step further along. **The tree now carries a comment at `beads-checkpoint.sh:519` recording that reasoning as rejected**, so the next reader does not re-derive it.

## VERIFIED ON TRUNK AFTER THE FAST-FORWARD

  `BASELINE_COMMIT=` resolved at `:534`  — ONCE, and BEFORE the copy
  `head_copy "$TMP_HEAD" "${BASELINE_COMMIT:-HEAD}"` at `:537` — the sha is PASSED IN
  `head_copy()` body now `git show "${2:-HEAD}:$TRACKER"` — it no longer reads HEAD itself
  bare `git show HEAD:` in the .sh = 1 (the unrelated LF comment), `baselineCommit` in the .ps1 = 6,
  8m case references = 32, nonsense control = 0

## THE WORKER PINNED THE AUDIT'S NAMED WRONG FIX AS A SEPARATE RED, WHICH IS THE PART WORTH KEEPING

The audit warned that moving `rev-parse` earlier while leaving the copy on `HEAD` would REVERSE the race rather than close it. The worker planted exactly that and showed it red **with a different signature** — the warning is lost entirely rather than mismatched — so the suite distinguishes "closed" from "reversed" instead of merely detecting breakage. Five plants total, each match-counted at 1 before running and each restored byte-identical by blob hash: the race plant on the `.sh` (exit 1, 138/3, naming the printed reference as the racer's oid against baseline A), the same on the `.ps1` (exit 1, 3 FAILED), the reversed-race fix on both, and one on `check-no-hardcoded-paths.sh` — that last because the gate prints no root, so a red is the only proof it read the worker's worktree at all.

## GATES — CAPTURED EXIT CODES

`test-pre-commit.sh` **0** at 141 passed / 0 failed (135 on base, +6); `beads-checkpoint.ps1 -SelfTest` **0** at 55 PASS / 0 FAIL (T7 +7); `check-no-hardcoded-paths.sh` **0**; `check-ai-tracking-ratchet.sh` **0**; `check_view_lifetime_residue.py` **0**; beads-boundary **0**; attribution **0** on both arms.

## TWO PREMISES OF MINE THE WORKER CHECKED AND FOUND WRONG — I RE-VERIFIED BOTH MYSELF

1. **`git show <sha>:<slashed-path>` does NOT mangle under MSYS, so the guard I put in the brief was inert.** CLAUDE.md item (d) requires the REF **and** the path to carry a slash, and a bare 40-character oid carries none. Four-way matrix measured on trunk: bare-oid:slashed-path **exit 0**; `origin/main`:slashed-path **exit 128** (`fatal: ambiguous argument 'origin\main;.beads\issues.jsonl'`); `origin/main`:plain-path 0; bare-oid:plain-path 0; and the failing case with `MSYS_NO_PATHCONV=1` **exit 0**. So the hazard is real but narrower than I briefed, and it does not touch this fix — whose whole subject is `git show <sha>:.beads/issues.jsonl`.
2. **`git checkout HEAD --` is NOT a restore while the fix is uncommitted — it silently discards the fix and exits 0.** My sabotage boilerplate has been saying "restore with `git checkout HEAD --`" without the precondition that the fix must be COMMITTED first. The worker's first plant discarded its own work this way and only the blob hash caught it, costing one re-apply. `ai/dispatch-blocks.md` records this; my hand-written brief did not — which is the concrete cost of my having skipped that file for this dispatch.

## ONE CHANGE BEYOND THE ASK, AND I ENDORSE IT

The `.ps1` now resolves `git` once to a full path. `Write-HeadCopy` launches via `Process.Start`, whose PATH search appends only `.exe`, while `& git` uses PowerShell's own resolution — so the two halves of the snapshot pair could resolve to two different binaries. That is the same latent defect one level down, it is what lets the `.ps1` race arm grade the two-reads shape at all, and the file already documents the hazard for `bd`. Three lines with a fallback.

## LEFT UNDONE, DELIBERATELY AND STATED

`--pre-pull` still re-resolves `HEAD`, and correctly so — it prints no oid, so there is no pairing to preserve. **No automated gate covers the `.ps1`** (layer 8 is POSIX sh); its `-SelfTest` was run by hand and the worker said so plainly rather than letting a green elsewhere imply coverage. `scripts/*.sh` remains outside the shellcheck roster, which `portability.yml` records as its own cleanup.

title: [tools/xray] Seat the shell frame before manual init applies its target
description:
Surface: tools/xray shell/manual lifecycle. Snapshot 7ffdacf24d797b67864af78a4625b2c1cb3ef8fd; relevant core/mount/router sources unchanged at mayor HEAD 90e9b0008ac96bb59e0e9f6ec03de8e1d650f21d.

Expected: the documented manual startup `(xray/init! {:target-frame :app/main})` accepts the inspected target on a fresh, already-initialized host runtime, without requiring the host to create Xray's private frame or open its UI first. Opening later preserves that explicit choice.

Actual: tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/core.cljs:176-195 installs handlers, collectors, browser exports and keys, then directly dispatches `[:rf.xray/set-target-frame target-frame]` under `:rf/xray`. None of those install calls seats that frame. Unlike core.cljs:254-258's public set-target-frame!, init! never calls mount/ensure-seated!. The manual facade deliberately does not load the preload or start its readiness poll (tools/xray/spec/API.md:282-299). Thus this route cannot rely on eventual preload seating.

Exact fresh-start causal reproduction (source-traced, not executed in CLJS):

1. Require day8.re-frame2-xray.core without the preload. Initialize re-frame with the supported adapter and create host frame :app/main; leave :rf/xray absent.
2. Call `(xray/init! {:target-frame :app/main})` as documented by tools/xray/spec/API.md:173-188 and spec/008-Embedding-Contract.md:363-364.
3. The raw dispatch reaches implementation/core/src/re_frame/router.cljc:4357-4369 with a nil frame record. It emits :rf.error/frame-destroyed and enqueues nothing. This rejection occurs at dispatch, so calling open! immediately afterward cannot rescue the choice.
4. A subsequent first open seats Xray, but its discovery hook has no explicit target to preserve; it selects an available history candidate or remains unselected instead of honoring :app/main.

Impact: a supported manual host integration loses its boot target and emits an error on first startup. The convenience preload often masks it; a host using the advertised manual path sees it deterministically.

Why current tests miss this: tools/xray/test/day8/re_frame2_xray/core_cljs_test.cljs:166-179 calls setup-xray-frame! before init! and redefines dispatch-impl to capture the vector; the other init-options test at181-195 also pre-creates Xray's frame. Neither exercises the real fresh-frame dispatch boundary.

Smallest repair: route init!'s target choice through the existing seated target-setting seam (or factor that tiny shared operation), preserving seat-only semantics and delayed first-open ring harvesting. No new boot protocol or eager opening is required.

Dedupe: searched active and closed manual/init/target/facade records and relevant Xray memories. Read rf2-88f1's full description, audit, repair notes and closed disposition: that issue fixed the standalone setter/Story caller and first-open precedence, not this remaining init route. This is a separate uncorrected supported call site, not a request to redo those fixes. The manual-production placement ruling is unchanged.

Verification limits: source-only exact causal trace. No browser/CLJS compilation or runtime, shared suite or build was run; no implementation fix made.
acceptance_criteria: Fresh runtime with adapter + host frame but no :rf/xray, no preload: real init! {:target-frame :app/main} seats Xray, emits no frame-destroyed error and lands the target after its queue drains. First open preserves it for empty and competing host history. Retain no-opts/no-auto-open/idempotence and existing setter seating controls; do not pre-create :rf/xray or replace dispatch in the regression.
close_reason: PR #9369 merged; verified HEAD == origin/main at d2d8e62f45. The shell frame is now seated before manual init applies its target. THE BRIEF'S GUESS WAS WRONG AND THE WORKER SAID SO: I suggested this and rf2-lffg plausibly shared one mechanism. They do not. One is a dropped option at a mount seam (:frame never read); this one is a missing seat before a dispatch. They share only the word 'frame' — two independent fixes. Delivered in the same PR and covered by the same failing-first evidence (23 reverted-source failures across five new deftests, identical 11311/57107 totals before and after). This bead's own control deftest passed in BOTH runs, which is what distinguishes a real pin from one that merely moved with the change. Spec correction: §Frame roles had attributed the pre-open seat to set-target-frame! alone while the host-config bullet directly above it lists init! {:target-frame ...} and set-target-frame! as peers — they are peers now; before, only one seated.

title: dispatch briefs omit the require-alias canonical dialect, so every new file trips the per-surface ratchet — three PRs in one wave
description:
MEASURED 2026-09-05 by the mayor across one dispatch wave. This is a defect in the MAYOR'S BRIEF TEMPLATE, not in any worker or in the gate.

THE PATTERN. Three PRs from one wave went RED on 'Require-alias dialect ratchet' plus its 'Lint required' aggregator, each for the same reason and each needing a fix round-trip:
  #9264 worker/epoch-a     implementation/adapters 339 vs floor 337 (+2), implementation/epoch 199 vs 196 (+3)
  #9267 worker/ssrhelp-a   (same pair red; diagnosis routed to its author)
  #9270 worker/schemadoc-a implementation/schemas 119 vs floor 112 (+7)
Re-measure these figures rather than quoting them; floors move as the debt is walked down.

THE MECHANISM. scripts/check_require_alias_dialect.py enforces a PER-SURFACE FLOOR, not an absolute count. A surface with baselined debt is green at its floor and red one alias above it. So ANY new file added to such a surface reds the gate unless it uses the canonical rf.* spelling from spec/Conventions.md Require-alias dialect. Nearly every editing dispatch adds a test file. The gate is behaving exactly as designed; what is missing is that the brief never tells the worker the dialect exists.

WHY IT COSTS MORE THAN IT LOOKS. The failure surfaces only in CI, after the worker has reported done and marked the PR ready. Recovering it costs: converting the PR back to draft, a fix dispatch, a rebase, a re-run of the artefact suite (mandatory, because an alias rename that misses one call site fails at RUNTIME rather than at read time), and a second review pass. Three of those in one wave.

THE FIX IS ONE PARAGRAPH IN THE DISPATCH TEMPLATE, and it belongs in the gate-mechanics block that already travels verbatim into every editing brief: name the canonical dialect, name spec/Conventions.md as its authority, say that the ratchet is a per-surface FLOOR so a new file trips it, and tell the worker to run python scripts/check_require_alias_dialect.py --verbose BEFORE opening the PR. That last clause is the whole repair — the gate prints the exact required spelling for every violation, so a worker who runs it once needs no further guidance.

TWO THINGS THE PARAGRAPH MUST ALSO SAY, both learned by getting them wrong. (1) NEVER raise a floor or edit a baseline file to admit the new debt — that inverts the ratchet, and walking the debt down is rf2-7sx1's job. (2) DO NOT fix pre-existing violations in untouched files: implementation/adapters alone carries 337, so a well-meaning sweep is unbounded scope sprawl into another bead's surface.

A THIRD LESSON, ABOUT READING THE LOG RATHER THAN THE FIRST LINE OF IT. On #9264 I quoted a single surface from the CI output into the fix brief. The log had named TWO surfaces over floor, and had the worker fixed only the one I named the gate would have stayed red — it caught this and said so. So the brief must tell the fix worker to run the gate and read its FULL output, never to trust a surface list quoted by the mayor.

SCOPE: this is a change to docs/the-mayor-method/dispatch-prompt-template.md, in the gate-mechanics block. It is the MAYOR'S OWN REPAIR, so per loops.md section 6 it goes through a mayor-occupied worktree rather than the mayor checkout, where the pre-commit hook will refuse it. Check first whether the same class of per-surface ratchet exists for other gates (splint, clj-kondo, api-manifest) and cover the class rather than this one instance if so.
notes:
SECOND DEFECT IN THE SAME BRIEF TEMPLATE, MEASURED THE SAME WAVE — and this one is a rule the template ALREADY carries, which is the more damning shape.

WHAT HAPPENED. The fix dispatch for PR #9263 ended its turn saying it would 'wait for the monitor event rather than continue polling'. That wait can never complete: a Monitor, watch, subscription or background task an agent arms stops when that agent stops, so the worker is the only thing that can read its own exit file and can only do so while its turn is running. The completion event goes to the coordinator instead. The worker was recovered intact by a single status message, which is the documented outcome for every instance of this strand.

THE CAUSE IS MINE AND IT IS SPECIFIC: I wrote that fix brief as a CONDENSED gate-mechanics section instead of pasting the block verbatim. The block already states this rule, already names the class rather than the instances (a Monitor, a watch, a subscription, a background task you expect to wake you), and already refutes the belief that keeps re-arming it — that the harness's own promise to notify survives the end of a turn. None of that reached the worker, because I summarised.

SO THIS BEAD NOW HAS TWO HALVES, and they are different in kind. The first (require-alias dialect) is content MISSING from the template and needs a new paragraph. This second one needs NO new text at all — the text exists and works; what failed is that the mayor did not paste it. dispatch-prompt-template.md says exactly this under Pasting a block: 'no dispatch is small enough to earn a condensed block', and notes the temptation is strongest precisely where the block dwarfs the task, which a two-file alias rename is.

IMPLICATION FOR THE FIX, and it should be stated in whatever lands: adding the require-alias paragraph makes the gate-mechanics block LONGER, which increases the pressure to condense it on small dispatches — the exact pressure that produced this strand. So the repair must not stop at more text. Either the block is pasted mechanically every time by construction (an extraction step the mayor cannot skip), or the fix dispatches keep failing this way while the template gets steadily better and steadily less likely to be used in full.

Recorded here rather than as a separate bead because both defects have one root: the mayor's brief is the scarce output, and both instances are it being degraded on the way to the worker — once by omission, once by summary.
A THIRD GATE OF THIS CLASS, measured 2026-09-05 on PR #9269 — so this bead is about a CLASS of gate, not about the require-alias one.

'No retired view-lifetime vocabulary, repo-wide' (scripts/check_view_lifetime_residue.py) is a repo-wide BANNED-WORD ratchet at a permitted count of ZERO. It fired on PR #9269 for a single word in an explanatory COMMENT — implementation/http/src/re_frame/http/registry.cljc:747, the sentence 'No lock, tombstone, lease or ...' saying what the fix does NOT need. The implementation was correct; the prose used a retired term.

WHY IT BELONGS HERE RATHER THAN AS ITS OWN BEAD: identical shape to the require-alias case. A gate the brief never names, enforcing a project vocabulary a worker cannot infer, surfacing only in CI after the worker has reported done and marked the PR ready, and costing a full recovery round-trip. Three distinct gates now: require-alias dialect (per-surface floor), lease/view-lifetime residue (repo-wide, zero permitted), and the lint.yml aggregator that reports whichever of them failed.

SO THE FIX IS NOT A LIST OF GATES — IT IS A DISCOVERY INSTRUCTION. A list drifts, and this bead would need amending on every fourth gate. What a worker needs is: before opening the PR, run the ratchet/vocabulary gates that cover the paths you touched, and treat the gate's own output as the authority on what it wants. Point at how to find them (scripts/check_*.py plus the lint.yml and test.yml job lists) rather than enumerating them here, for the same reason the method already gives about counts going stale first.

AND NOTE THESE GATES GRADE PROSE, NOT ONLY CODE. That is the non-obvious half: a worker who has carefully gated the code it changed will not think to gate a comment it wrote, and the require-alias case has the same property in reverse — it grades a require form nobody considers part of the change. The paragraph must say the ratchets read the WHOLE tracked file, comments and docstrings included.

WORKER RESULT 2026-09-05 — PR #9274 (https://github.com/day8/re-frame2/pull/9274), one file, 39 insertions, 0 deletions.

RATCHET CLASS IS FAR BROADER THAN THREE. The bead asked whether the per-surface-ratchet class has other members. Census of scripts/ by docstring self-description (ratchet | residue | retired | permitted count | baseline | floor): 18 gates, including check_retired_spellings, check_retired_composition_vocab, check_retired_image_keys, check_inject_cofx_residue, check_failure_corpus_residue, check_ambient_durable_reads, check_thrown_error_messages, check_keyword_catalogue_drift and check-ai-tracking-ratchet.sh, plus the skill-drift family. Only ONE per-surface floor DATA file exists (scripts/require-alias-baseline.edn); the rest are zero-tolerance or scoped-carve-out scans. So the bead's "the fix is NOT a list" ruling is confirmed with a wider margin than the three gates it names — an enumeration would have been stale before it merged.

CORRECTION TO ONE PREMISE IN THE DISPATCH BRIEF (not in this bead): the brief asserted that BOTH named gates "read the whole tracked file, comments and docstrings included". That is true of check_view_lifetime_residue.py, which scans tracked content and paths, but FALSE of check_require_alias_dialect.py, which deliberately strips comments, strings, char literals and #_ discards before grading — precisely so a require form quoted in a docstring does not count. The bead itself is accurate here and was followed instead: the residue gates grade prose, and the alias gate grades "a require form nobody considers part of the change". The landed wording states both halves separately rather than merging them.

SHAPE OF THE FIX. Half one: two paragraphs in the gate-mechanics block, beside the other pre-push obligations. Discovery instruction plus the two non-obvious properties; no markdown link, because the travelling block contains zero links and the page forbids pointing a worker at a section it cannot see. Half two: placed in Pasting a block — mayor-facing prose OUTSIDE the travelling block — so the add-more-text-makes-condensing-likelier tension is not worsened by its own repair; it records the measured case where condensing DID strand a worker (the section previously had only a case where it did not), names which part a condensing mayor drops (the harness mechanics), and states that no wording fixes the pressure because the block only ever grows.

GATES (captured exits): check_doc_slugs.py 0; check_readme_links.py --ci 0; check_require_alias_dialect.py --verbose 0; check_view_lifetime_residue.py --verbose 0. All re-run on the final base after rebase. Non-vacuity: planted broken anchor -> doc-slugs exit 1 naming file/line/anchor; the SAME planted tree left check_readme_links green, which is the finding that check_readme_links excludes DOCS_GATE_ROOTS and does not cover docs/the-mayor-method/ at all. Restore verified by git blob hash (db7c9891...), byte-identical.

Bead left in_progress for the mayor to close on merge; the worker did not close it.
MAYOR-SIDE CORRECTION FROM THE WORKER THAT FIXED THIS BEAD, recorded because the fix brief got a fact wrong that this bead's own text gets right.

I WROTE, in the dispatch brief: 'both named gates read the whole tracked file, comments and docstrings included'. That is TRUE of check_view_lifetime_residue.py and FALSE of check_require_alias_dialect.py, which deliberately STRIPS comments, strings, character literals and #_ discards — precisely so a require form quoted inside a docstring does not count against a surface. The worker checked at source, followed the bead over my brief, and stated the two halves separately in what landed.

THE BEAD WAS ALREADY ACCURATE: its text says residue gates grade prose, and separately that the alias gate grades 'a require form nobody considers part of the change'. Two different non-obvious properties, and I collapsed them into one wrong generalisation. So the corrected statement, for anyone re-reading this bead: a RESIDUE ratchet reads the whole file including comments and commit messages; the ALIAS ratchet reads only real code and catches you on an import edge you did not think of as part of your diff. Both surprise a worker, for opposite reasons.

THE CLASS IS FAR BIGGER THAN THIS BEAD ASSUMED — 18 GATES, not the three it names. Measured by the worker as a docstring census over scripts/ on the markers ratchet | residue | retired | permitted count | baseline | floor: check_retired_spellings, check_retired_composition_vocab, check_retired_image_keys, check_inject_cofx_residue, check_failure_corpus_residue, check_ambient_durable_reads, check-ai-tracking-ratchet.sh, the skill-drift family, and more. Exactly ONE per-surface floor DATA file exists (scripts/require-alias-baseline.edn); every other member is a zero-tolerance or scoped-carve-out scan. That confirms this bead's own 'do not write a list' ruling by a wider margin than the ruling claimed — a list of three would have been wrong within the hour.

ONE MORE PREMISE OF MINE THAT POINTED THE WRONG WAY: I told the worker mkdocs build --strict was not the gate for docs/the-mayor-method/. It IS — exclude_docs lists only tools/playground/, the two codemod trees and design/freehand|hicasso|retirement/, and the-mayor-method sits under docs_dir. The worker skipped it for DIFFERENT and correct reasons (the change adds zero links, --strict does not gate anchors, siblings live) and said so rather than inheriting my wrong reason. It also found check_readme_links.py --ci VACUOUS on this path — it excludes DOCS_GATE_ROOTS — and reported it as vacuous rather than banking its exit 0 as a pass. That is the right handling of a green that inspected nothing.
close_reason:
PR #9274 merged (c974dbfc63). The dispatch-prompt-template now names the two repo-wide ratchet gates, so a brief that omits them is a brief that departed from the template rather than one the template allowed.

Filed after FOUR PRs in one session bounced on ratchets no brief had mentioned: #9264, #9267 and #9270 on check_require_alias_dialect.py, #9269 on check_view_lifetime_residue.py. The two gates are different animals and the template now says which is which — the alias gate is a PER-SURFACE FLOOR baselined in scripts/require-alias-baseline.edn that grades IMPORT EDGES only (it strips comments, strings, char literals and #_ discards); the residue gate is a REPO-WIDE BANNED-WORD scan at permitted count ZERO that DOES read comments, docstrings and commit messages. Briefing them as one thing is how #9269's reworded explanatory comment got missed.

The bead's second half was the stranded fix worker: it ended its turn on a monitor because the brief carried a CONDENSED gate-mechanics section instead of the block, which already names that class. Recovered with one SendMessage. That is the argument for pasting the block rather than summarising it, and it is now in the template's own words.

+39 lines to docs/the-mayor-method/dispatch-prompt-template.md. Final rollup 87 pass / 0 fail / 0 pending.

title: bug(pair-mcp): trace-window and watch-epochs turn operating-frame ambiguity into a false empty epoch ring
description:
Sibling of rf2-q17a on the same axis, found by the census that bead's fix required. rf2-q17a fixed get-path only; these two were left because the bead scoped itself to get-path and its Non-goals forbid widening.

## Mechanism

Both tools emit an implicit-frame read and neither guards the tier-4 nil:

  - tools/re-frame2-pair-mcp/src/re_frame2_pair_mcp/tools/trace_window.cljs
    builds history-call as (rt-call 'epoch-history) when no sticky-frame.
  - tools/re-frame2-pair-mcp/src/re_frame2_pair_mcp/tools/watch_epochs.cljs
    builds epochs-since-call as (rt-call 'epochs-since after) and
    history-call as (rt-call 'epoch-history), same condition.

Runtime epoch-history/1 and epochs-since/1 both default to (current-frame)
(runtime.cljs:1274-1281, 1311-1320), which is nil under two-plus app frames
with no pin. rf/epoch-history nil bottoms out in state/history-for
(implementation/epoch/src/re_frame/epoch/state.cljc:219-222), which returns
[] for an unknown frame. So the tools report :count 0 — 'nothing happened' —
when the truth is 'I could not tell which frame you meant'. watch-epochs
adds a second falsehood: with an empty history the caller's cursor id is
not found, so epochs-since answers :id-aged-out? true, telling the agent its
cursor fell out of the ring.

trace-window's :count-0 advisory cannot catch this: the advisory reads the
same implicit (epoch-history) call, so both sides are empty together.

## Shape

Identical to rf2-q17a's: an implicit-frame read whose runtime callee is
nil-tolerant, so ambiguity is reported as absence rather than refused. The
repair technique is the one rf2-q17a landed — resolve once in the emitted
form via (current-frame <override>), refuse with ambiguous-frame-error when
nil, otherwise read against the resolved id. Reuse the existing envelope;
do not mint new vocabulary.

Extra care these two need that get-path did not: both are cursor-paged and
carry sticky :frame state in the cursor, so the refusal must not clobber or
half-advance a cursor, and the sticky-frame tier must be honoured before the
session pin.

## Census that produced this (controlled)

Ran over every rt-call the pair-mcp tools emit, cross-referenced against the
runtime fns that call ambiguous-frame-error. Control: read-sub!,
sub-cache-info, describe-image, start-recording!, sample-signals all report
the refusal, so the instrument detects the pattern.

Already refusing (no action): read-sub, list-subscriptions, read-dom,
read-ui, describe-image, dispatch, dispatch-dry-run, replay-epoch, record,
watch-until.

Checked and NOT defects: precheck (emits only for an :explicit frame; nil
means 'no precheck, proceed'), replace-app-db (nil frame fails loudly with
:no-such-frame), restore-epoch (nil frame returns false, surfaced as a
structured failure), probe/health (reports the operating frame honestly),
snapshot (deliberately a broad multi-frame mega-op — explicit rf2-q17a
non-goal).

## Acceptance

With two app frames, no pin and no frame arg, trace-window and watch-epochs
each return isError with :reason :ambiguous-frame, :available-frames and the
recovery hint, and do NOT return :count 0 or :id-aged-out? true. Explicit
frame, session pin, sticky cursor frame and sole-app-frame sessions keep
their existing shapes. Witness asserts the error shape, not merely that it
errors.
notes:
PR #9262 audit residual (2026-09-05): resolve-once/refuse-before-read fixes the original ambiguous first call. The existing cursor ownership defect remains at this newly reviewed resolution seam: trace_window.cljs:94,177-183 and watch_epochs.cljs:93,182-194 set sticky-frame from only the input cursor/frame argument and encode that value into next-cursor. For the normal no-frame argument call, a session pin or sole app frame is resolved browser-side to fid, but neither successful eval result carries fid back to the cursor builder. Page 1 therefore stores :frame nil, even though it actually read :stories.

If the session is pinned to :rf/default before page 2, the returned opaque cursor resolves the new pin and queries a different ring. A live :after-id from :stories is then reported cursor-stale/id-aged-out; with overlapping IDs it could silently continue another ring. Similarly, starting with one app frame and registering a second before continuation turns a valid page into ambiguous-frame. The new sticky-frame test manually constructs a cursor with :frame :stories, so it proves consumption of an already-owned cursor but never exercises creation from the default operating-frame path.

title: bug(realworld-http): profile replies can overwrite a newer username route
description:
## Scope

Review surface: `examples/real-apps/**`, specifically the managed-HTTP RealWorld profile page. The resources-based RealWorld variant was compared and is already keyed by canonical resource params; it is not part of the fix.

## Correctness finding

`examples/real-apps/realworld_http/profile.cljs` binds each request URL and request ID to the current `:username`, but every banner/authored/favorites reply target omits that identity and every terminal handler writes the one shared `:profile`, `:profile.articles`, or `:profile.favorites` slice unconditionally. Follow/unfollow similarly captures the route username only in the URL, then applies success or rollback to whichever profile slice is current.

Navigating Alice -> Bob leaves Alice and Bob under distinct request IDs, so managed HTTP may legally deliver both. A late Alice settle can therefore replace Bob data, statuses, errors, timestamps, or following state. It can also corrupt the current state-machine presentation.

## Evidence

- Routes `/profile/:username` and `/profile/:username/favorites` run profile plus list loads on each match: `examples/real-apps/realworld_http/routing.cljs:110-126`.
- The page has shared unkeyed slices initialized once: `examples/real-apps/realworld_http/profile.cljs:39-46,147-153`.
- Banner request ID is `[:profile/load username]`, but targets are `[:profile/loaded]` and `[:profile/load-failed]`; both handlers write unconditionally: `profile.cljs:159-198`.
- Authored requests are keyed by username but their targets omit it and their handlers write unconditionally: `profile.cljs:200-239`. Favorites repeats the defect: `profile.cljs:241-280`.
- Follow/unfollow paths use the current username, while `:profile/followed`, `:profile/unfollowed`, and rollback handlers mutate the shared current profile without issuer identity: `profile.cljs:286-331`.
- The view consumes only those shared slices (`profile.cljs:380-389,438-502`), so stale Alice can be rendered and acted upon under Bob's URL.
- This is not just a cosmetic flash. If late Alice failure arrives while Bob is loading, it can send the data machine to `:error`; a later Bob success writes DB data, but the `:error` state has no `fetch-succeeded` transition (`profile.cljs:86-121`), leaving the page stranded in an error presentation.
- Managed HTTP only supersedes an old request when a new request has the same request ID (`docs/async/http.md:312-316`; `spec/014-HTTPRequests.md:1573-1580`). Alice and Bob IDs differ, so route staleness remains application-owned.
- The local canonical precedent already fixes the equivalent article defect: `examples/real-apps/realworld_http/comments.cljs:152-157,242-284,317-364` carries the slug through targets and rejects replies that do not match the active slug (closed `rf2-iy3d6`).
- The resources variant is immune by construction: identity includes canonical params (`examples/real-apps/realworld_resources/resources.cljs:13-18`), profile/list resources include username/page (`resources.cljs:172-233`), and routes plan those keyed resources (`realworld_resources/routing.cljs:206-245`).
- Existing profile coverage (`implementation/adapters/reagent/test/re_frame/realworld_cljs_test.cljs:2860-2897`) uses immediate canned replies for one username and cannot expose ordering. The same suite's held-request cross-slug tests around lines 1900-2130 provide a suitable pattern.
- History traces this shape to managed-HTTP conversion `36436af528`; the current `origin/main` profile blob is identical to this review worktree's blob.

## Impact

This canonical realistic example teaches programmers and AI that username-keyed request IDs alone provide navigation stale suppression. Under ordinary network reordering it can show or mutate the wrong user's profile, authored/favorited articles, and following state. The machine can remain in an error presentation even after current data succeeds.

## Recommended bounded fix

Use one local correlation convention, mirroring `comments.cljs`:

1. Carry the issuing username in every banner and social terminal target; carry the relevant username/page key (or equivalent generation) in list targets.
2. Record or compare the active logical key and reject stale success, failure, rollback, status, timestamp, and machine writes before mutation.
3. On username identity change, clear or hide prior-user data. Retaining data for a same-key refresh remains valid.
4. Correlate follow/unfollow settlements to their issuing profile. A stable per-profile social request ID may additionally supersede rapid same-profile toggles, but generic framework machinery is unnecessary.

## Non-goals

Do not migrate this page to resources, add a cache framework or generic remote-data abstraction, change the route/HTTP API, redesign the UI, or modify the already identity-keyed resources variant.

## Duplicate review

Searched `.beads/issues.jsonl` and the `origin/main` tracker for cross-profile/cross-username/late-profile/profile-race/wrong-profile terms, every affected handler name, request-id/profile, and out-of-order/profile. Only closed `rf2-iy3d6` matched because its article defect recorded `profile race` as a search term. Generic profile-file/page searches found closed article/comment social work (`rf2-amhpk`, `rf2-84iek`, `rf2-iy3d6`) and unrelated base-href work (`rf2-do50`). Those are precedents, not owners of profile replies. No open or closed duplicate owns this behavior.

## Uncertainty

The review is static by review-pool constraint, but the delivery branch follows directly from the documented same-ID-only suppression and the distinct username IDs. The exact internal key shape, and whether a reply after leaving and returning to the same username should be accepted, are implementation choices. The required invariant is that a settle cannot mutate a different active profile identity.
acceptance_criteria:
1. Add deterministic held-transport CLJS coverage for Alice -> Bob navigation across banner, authored, and favorites requests. Settle Bob first and then Alice success/failure; Alice cannot change Bob data, status, error, timestamps, or machine presentation.
2. Prove non-vacuity: the corresponding current-Bob success/failure is accepted. A late prior-profile failure cannot strand the current machine, and current success can present loaded data.
3. While Bob is pending, previously settled Alice banner/list data is not exposed under Bob's route. Same-identity refresh retention remains allowed.
4. Hold Alice follow/unfollow, navigate to Bob, then settle Alice. Neither success nor rollback mutates Bob; current-profile settlements still work.
5. Production reply vectors carry enough identity for every state-changing terminal path to reject stale work.
6. Demonstrate a red negative control by removing or inverting the correlation guard, then restore it and pass the focused RealWorld CLJS suite and applicable build/type gates.
notes:

Starting unfollowed, :profile/follow optimistically sets true and emits POST success [:profile/followed "alice"]; the now-visible Unfollow button can immediately set false and emit DELETE success [:profile/unfollowed "alice"]. If DELETE settles first and the older POST settles last, both replies match [:profile :username] "alice", so both pass reply-for-current-profile? and the older POST re-seeds the whole banner with :following true. Rollback order can similarly undo a newer accepted intent. No pending flag, operation generation, or request id distinguishes them.

The cross-username fix and its tests remain valid. Bounded follow-up: state and test an explicit same-profile mutation policy. The smallest honest policy is to serialize this one toggle (handler and button refuse/disable a second intent while one is pending, clearing pending on correlated success/failure); if rapid replacement is retained, carry a generation and reconcile server truth rather than treating abort as proof a write did not occur. After Alice -> Bob -> Alice and a truthful followed GET, DELETE was emitted while the earlier POST response remained pending.
