Add a held-transport Alice -> Bob -> Alice witness alongside the immediate-toggle and cross-username controls, including old success/rollback while a newer operation is pending. Keep the one-toggle policy small; dropping old replies alone or treating abort as proof of no server write does not establish serialization. Correct the prose claiming navigation needs no handling. Original criteria and the working cross-username protection remain intact.
Delivery (PR #9284, 2026-09-05): the PR #9260 audit residual is closed. The follow latch moves off the banner slice into a top-level, username-keyed :profile.follow-pending set that :profile/load never touches, so it survives alice -> bob -> alice with the POST still in flight. Each of the three follow settles now splits between two owners, the comments.cljs TWO QUESTIONS shape: the banner write stays gated on reply-for-current-profile?, while the latch release is the mutation's own and therefore unconditional — keying is what makes that safe, since alice's reply can only release alice. (fnil conj #{}) is load-bearing: hydration is :replace-frame-state and the set is deliberately absent from ssr-app-slice-keys, now stated in ssr.cljc. Prose corrected in profile.cljs, schema.cljs and ssr.cljc, including the false 'navigating away needs no handling of its own' claim.

Two CLJS witnesses in implementation/adapters/reagent/test/re_frame/realworld_cljs_test.cljs: profile-follow-latch-survives-a-walk-away-and-back-test (new held-transport alice -> bob -> alice; return GET reports server truth, alice comes back latched, the Unfollow is refused and issues no second request, then the held POST seeds AND releases and the toggle works again) and profile-follow-latch-does-not-leak-to-a-bystander-test (replaces profile-follow-latch-does-not-outlive-its-profile-test, which pinned the behaviour this fixes: bob stays live while alice is out, two profiles latched at once, an older success and an older rollback each release their own username alone under a newer pending operation). Cross-username protection and immediate-toggle serialisation unchanged and still pinned.

Both bead premises verified at source and both HOLD, though the citations had drifted: same-request-id-only supersede is docs/async/http.md:312 and spec/014-HTTPRequests.md:1610 (not :312-316/:1573-1580); the resources variant is immune via [scope resource-id canonical-params] and was not touched. The bead's profile.cljs line ranges are all stale — the file is 774 lines at tip against a largest citation of 502.

The stranded-:error half needs NO further work and no follow-up bead: #9236 already made it unreachable rather than merely unused (no cross-identity :fetch-failed reaches the machine, and every path to :loaded for the current identity passes through :fetch-started first), pinned by profile-cross-username-late-failure-is-refused-test.

Gates (captured exit codes): require-alias dialect 0; view-lifetime residue 0; shadow-cljs compile examples/realworld 0 (0 warnings); node out/node-test.js on the final tree 0 — 11254 tests / 57029 assertions / 0 failures. Planted-fault control: restoring the old latch-dies-with-the-slice line took the suite to exit 1 with 5 failures, all inside the new alice -> bob -> alice witness, at identical test/assertion counts; restore verified by blob hash.

OUTSIDE THE FENCE, for the mayor: main is currently RED on compile-node-test's zero-warning gate. Two :uix.linter/interop-ref-read warnings in implementation/adapters/uix/test/re_frame/adapter/uix_effect_frame_deps_dom_cljs_test.cljs:120 and :139 ('use-ref hook in UIx returns Atom-like ref, use @ instead of .-current'). That file is byte-identical to origin/main in this branch; last touched by 570d07d286 / dc795fb3b5. This fails scripts/test-fast-pr.sh and npm run test:cljs for any diff, not just this one. title: bug(template): prove the optimized release boots for every emitted substrate
description:
## Problem

The generated scaffold gives Reagent and UIx users the same release command and says the resulting resources/public directory is deployable, while the template contract says each substrate is exercised end-to-end and builds an advanced release. The behavioral tier does not enforce that contract: it boots only the development bundle, runs shadow release only for Reagent, and checks the optimized output only for process exit plus a non-empty main.js. UIx's release command is never executed, and neither optimized bundle is loaded in a browser.

## Evidence

- tools/template/resources/day8/re_frame2_template/root/README.md:26-33 tells every generated project to run npm run release and serve resources/public.
- tools/template/resources/day8/re_frame2_template/_shared/package.json maps release to shadow-cljs release app for both substrates.
- tools/template/spec/000-Vision.md:25-30 says the generated SPA can be run, tested, and released.
- tools/template/spec/Principles.md:149-178 says each Reagent/UIx substrate is exercised end-to-end and that the behavioral layer builds the advanced release.
- tools/template/test/day8/re_frame2_template/emitted_test_run_test.clj:351-376 and :457-461 boot the development output before release.
- The release arm at emitted_test_run_test.clj:481-500 asserts only command exit and a non-empty main.js.
- Reagent enables that arm at :516-527; UIx passes an empty option map at :529-539, so its advertised release command never runs.
- The rationale at :424-428 calls the module/export shape substrate-invariant, but the product contract deliberately swaps deps.edn, core.cljs, and views.cljs per substrate (spec/000-Vision.md:33-36), which is source and dependency surface Closure compiles.
- Commit adf2f47322 added the existing Chromium proof after a real emitted page compiled successfully but booted blank under its own CSP. That history demonstrates that compile success is not a page-boot proof. Release currently overwrites the proven dev bundle and the driver is not rerun.
- Closed bead rf2-zq34m acceptance criterion 4 required each substrate to build an advanced release and open the real page. Its implementation note records advanced release on Reagent, matching the residual in current code.

## Impact

A UIx-specific advanced-compilation failure can reach users without CI executing the documented command. For both substrates, a non-empty optimized JavaScript file can still throw at load or paint a blank page, so the deployable release path is materially weaker than the first-run path. This is a narrow scaffold correctness gap, not a request for general production infrastructure.

## Posture fit

The template is the front door to a small SPA and release is one of its three documented commands. Reusing the browser proof already paid for keeps the fix simple and outcome-focused: prove the generated app users deploy, without adding options, policy, or framework machinery.

## Duplicate result

A targeted rg search over .beads/issues.jsonl for template/scaffold with advanced, optimized, release bundle, and npm run release found only closed rf2-zq34m and deferred rf2-8urba. rf2-zq34m is the original contract but was closed after the Reagent-only implementation landed; no open bead owns this residual. rf2-8urba is the future Hicasso substrate and is unrelated. Also checked rf2-pygpw (closed pre-publish generator coordinates), rf2-fo4ng (deferred Maven coordinate rename), and rf2-fgb1 (post-tag documentation flip); each has a distinct center.

## Uncertainty

This review did not execute a UIx optimized build because it was explicitly read-only and prohibited node_modules links. It does not claim today's UIx output is observed broken. The objective defect is the unexercised per-substrate release contract and the absence of a browser verdict for both optimized outputs.
design:
## Bounded fix

- In the existing opt-in behavioral tier, execute shadow-cljs release app for both Reagent and UIx.
- Immediately after each successful release, reuse the existing browser driver against the overwritten resources/public directory and require the same heading, counter 0 to 1, and zero-pageerror verdict. Make driver labels mode-neutral if needed; do not add a second browser harness.
- Keep package-completeness and development-page proof before release because the development build has distinct chunk/eval behavior.
- Keep the existing broken-mount witness as the browser driver's non-vacuity proof.
- Align Principles and test descriptions with the executable per-substrate behavior.

## Non-goals

- No generated API, source, or dependency changes unless the new proof exposes a real fault.
- No new build mode, deployment provider, CSP or hosting policy, performance or bundle-size work, npm-install matrix, substrate selector, or bespoke production driver.
- No expansion into publication-coordinate or repository-split work.
acceptance_criteria:
1. With RF2_TEMPLATE_RUN_EMITTED_TESTS=1, both Reagent and UIx emissions execute shadow release app and assert exit 0 plus a non-empty optimized output.

5. Principles and test prose state the same per-substrate release contract the executable tier enforces.

At runtime: the driver requires typeof goog / typeof cljs to match the mode - object/object in the dev bundle, undefined/undefined under :advanced - so each mode's assertion reads the OPPOSITE way on the other mode's artefact. Both readings are printed per proof. The broken-mount witness stays RED (exit 1) for reagent and the setup-skill leaf and restores index.html byte-for-byte; the broken-click witness stays RED too.

Exactly two - :reagent and :uix - and :hicasso / :reagent-slim / :helix are each refused with :rf.error/template-substrate-must-be-one-of. The gap versus the project's shipped adapters is DELIBERATE and documented in tools/template/spec/001-Substrate-Variants.md 'Future substrates': Hicasso is owned by rf2-8urba (deferred, gated on the repository's first v* tag) and reagent-slim on its first published artefact. Neither was touched.

title: Canonical reply integration/security fixtures pin ledger work keys instead of envelope keys
description:
## Finding

Two contract-support suites build hand-authored maps that they call canonical managed-async reply envelopes, but put work identity on bare `:work/id` / `:work/kind`. Those are the durable work-ledger / verification-payload spellings. A transient reply envelope is single-rooted under `:rf.reply/work-id` / `:rf.reply/work-kind`.

This is not merely prose drift: the tests assert the bare keys and therefore positively pin the wrong record layer.

## Exact evidence

- `implementation/event-conformance/test/re_frame/event_reply_envelope_conformance_cljs_test.cljc:52-59` defines `canonical-reply` with top-level `:work/id` and `:work/kind`. Lines 87-91 call it a canonical uniform envelope; lines 114-124 call these canonical reply facts and assert the bare keys after ordinary event delivery. `rf.reply/valid-reply?` does not expose the mistake because the canonical work fields are conditional/optional to the generic validator and the unknown bare fields are allowed.
- `implementation/security/test/re_frame/security/reply_envelope_egress_security_cljs_test.cljc:52-88` feeds `trace-summary` a reply with bare `:work/id`, then explicitly calls the returned bare key canonical. The same stale spelling recurs in its framed, frameless, generated, suppression, and host-handle reply fixtures (notably lines 97-126, 131-160, 181-201, and 234-252). `trace-summary` projects only wire slots and otherwise preserves the supplied map, so these tests can stay green without ever proving that the canonical namespaced identity survives egress.
- `spec/Managed-Effects.md:92-100` shows live delivery with `:rf.reply/work-id`; lines 122-154 define the reply map, and line 151 explicitly distinguishes namespaced transient-envelope keys from bare durable-ledger / verification / `:current-work` keys. `spec/Spec-Schemas.md:3582-3587` and 3622-3624 carry the same boundary.
- The comparison surface is already correct: `implementation/reply-conformance/test/re_frame/reply_egress_projection_conformance_cljs_test.cljc:91-105,174-176,212,253-254,277-278,370` uses and asserts `:rf.reply/work-id` / `:rf.reply/work-kind`; `reply_vocab_conformance_cljs_test.cljc` also reads family builders through those keys.
- History makes this an evidenced missed migration. Commits `01d9e4ae2f` (production), `084892baa2` / `e5e5a4aa84` (reply tests), and `2b1e536514` (spec) migrated the envelope to `:rf.reply/*` on 2026-07-09 under rf2-l7s7b7. Blame shows the bare fixture keys in both files remain from their 2026-06-17 introductions. Later 2026-09-03 event-conformance cleanup edited the surrounding assertions without correcting this layer mismatch.

## Impact

A regression that drops or reintroduces the wrong work-identity spelling at ordinary reply-event delivery or trace egress can leave these integration/security suites green, even though app handlers and tools consume the namespaced envelope contract for correlation. The fixtures also serve as executable examples, so preserving the ledger spelling here teaches a caller to read a key real family replies do not expose. The production builders currently appear correct; this is a meaningful contract-pin defect, not evidence of a current runtime leak.

## Bounded recommendation

Correct the two suites at the reply-map boundary:

1. Use `:rf.reply/work-id` and `:rf.reply/work-kind` for every top-level reply envelope and corresponding assertion.
2. Keep bare `:work/id` only where it is genuinely correlation/verification/ledger data, such as the carried/current maps passed to `reply/suppress`; do not mechanically rename those nested facts.
3. Add a small explicit tooth at each distinct boundary: ordinary delivered event and trace/suppression summary must retain the namespaced identity and must not grow top-level bare aliases.
4. Keep the existing status, redaction, stale non-delivery, and host-handle assertions intact.

## Non-goals

- No production API or runtime change.
- Do not rename durable work-ledger, verification-payload, entry `:current-work`, or carried/current gate keys.
- Do not tighten the generic reply validator into inferring whether arbitrary data is ledger-backed.
- Do not expand the family matrix, invent a second schema, or duplicate the broader egress suite.

## Posture rationale

This is a small correction at a user/tool-visible contract seam: one fact should have one spelling per record layer. Fixing the executable examples is lower-friction and more valuable than adding machinery. It protects ergonomic SPA continuation handling and debuggable correlation without litigating unrelated reply details.

## Duplicate search

An all-status in-memory scan covered 935 current beads across title, description, notes, design, acceptance criteria, and external ref for `rf.reply/work`, bare `work/id`, cross-record spelling, both fixture names, and work-id spelling. No bead owns this residual. The nearest closed issues are distinct: rf2-6r9j.217 renamed private event/reply roles only; rf2-6r9j.97 replaced a vacuous stale non-delivery row; rf2-6r9j.94 removed a duplicate generic projector row. Historical rf2-l7s7b7 is visible in the migration commits above, but its landed test migration missed these two files.

## Uncertainty

The runtime builders and the dedicated reply-conformance matrix appear canonical today, so the immediate risk is a false-green/misleading-fixture seam rather than a demonstrated production failure. The security file overlaps some projection coverage with reply-conformance, but its adversarial stale/host-handle rows remain independently useful; this issue asks only that their envelope inputs stop modeling the wrong layer.
acceptance_criteria:
1. Every top-level reply envelope constructed in the two named suites uses `:rf.reply/work-id` and, where kind is present, `:rf.reply/work-kind`; bare `:work/id` remains only in genuine ledger/verification/carried-current correlation data.
2. The event integration test proves ordinary delivery preserves the namespaced work id/kind and does not expose top-level bare aliases.
3. The security reply-egress tests prove framed/frameless projection and stale suppression preserve canonical namespaced identity while retaining their existing leak, redaction, non-delivery, and data-only teeth.
4. Focused JVM and consolidated CLJS Node coverage for both suites passes.
5. A temporary focused mutation that removes or replaces the canonical namespaced work-id at each distinct boundary makes the new assertion red; the mutation is restored before handoff.
close_reason: PR #9275. Both suites' top-level reply envelopes now use :rf.reply/work-id / :rf.reply/work-kind; assertions renamed (never loosened to accept both spellings). Bare :work/id kept only on the data-only carried/current stale-gate maps, with a new assertion pinning that they were NOT renamed. New teeth at each distinct boundary (ordinary delivery, stale suppression, framed egress, frameless fail-closed egress, 300-row generated corpus) assert the namespaced identity survives AND that no top-level bare alias grows beside it. Found a live false green in passing: suppress reads its trace work id off :rf.reply/work-id, so the security fixture's ledger spelling left (:rf.reply/work-id trace) nil while the suite stayed green. AC5 mutation control: reverting each envelope construction to the ledger spelling makes event-conformance red (exit 1, 10 failures, both boundaries) and security red (exit 1, 11 failures, all four boundaries); restores verified by sha256 byte-hash. Green: event-conformance 44/194 exit 0 (was 44/186), security 92/725 exit 0 (was 92/717). No production or spec change.

title: hic docs: chapter 20's translation table has no row for rf/reg-view, rf/frame-root or ambient subscribe/dispatch - a re-frame2-native app on the Reagent ADAPTER finds no row that names it
description:
FOUND 2026-09-03 by the rf2-t4jpz PRE-PILOT rehearsal - pilot 2 (LinearLite), a BLINDED
agent reading only the 29 published pages under docs/core/hicasso/, at pin
6e9bb105fc9b1569d63fdebc212b7787a2a023ba. NOT SECTION 13 EVIDENCE: a rehearsal on
:local/root does not satisfy the adoption proof and discharges no artefact gate.

The pilot's own friction-log entry follows verbatim. The 'Bead' field is the PILOT's
recommendation, and it is evidence about the surface rather than a ratified design -
a pilot proposing a framework change is outside its brief by the log protocol's own
rule. The log is at ai/findings/2026-09-03.pilot-b-rehearsal-linearlite.friction-log.md
(local-only) and in the pilot workspace.

----------------------------------------------------------------------

### P2-F01 · outcome 2 · `unresolved` · `docs`

**Trying to** Work out what I am actually migrating *from*. The brief and the
migration chapter both say "Reagent", so I expected to find Reagent components.

**Expected** `defn` components returning Hiccup, `@(rf/subscribe [:q])`,
`#(rf/dispatch [:x])` callbacks — the left-hand column of §2's translation
table in `20-migration-from-reagent.md`.

**Instead** The app's views are `rf/reg-view` forms with *unqualified*
`subscribe` and `dispatch` inside their bodies (`app/src/linearlite/core.cljs`
lines 472–597), mounted with `reagent-adapter/render!` into a
`[rf/frame-root {…}]` wrapper. That is a re-frame2-native view surface that
merely *runs on* the Reagent adapter. The word "Reagent" in the migration
chapter means something narrower than "the thing my app currently is".

**Looked at** `20-migration-from-reagent.md` §2 (translation table, 13 rows);
`00-installation.md` §"Hicasso needs a substrate adapter"; `index.md`
§"When to use another corpus or adapter".

**Resolved by** Nothing yet. The translation table has **no row for
`rf/reg-view`**, none for `rf/frame-root`, and none for the unqualified
`subscribe`/`dispatch` those bodies use. The nearest row, "`defn` component
returning Hiccup → `h/defview`", is a guess by analogy rather than a documented
mapping. I am proceeding on that guess and flagging it here, because a guess
that works leaves no other trace. The guess turned out to be right: every view
in the app ported onto `h/defview` with no surprises, and the ambient
`subscribe`/`dispatch` became `h/sub` and event vectors respectively.

**Bead** Migration chapter §2's table is written against *Reagent's* API
surface. An application on the Reagent **adapter** using re-frame2's own
`reg-view` / `frame-root` / ambient `subscribe` has none of those spellings and
finds no row that names it. Either add the three rows, or say in the chapter's
opening that `reg-view` codebases are a different (and easier) starting point.
The measurement that confirms this is P2-F02: the reporter's own census scored
this codebase at zero Reagent call sites, because it decides by namespace name
and `re-frame.adapter.reagent` is not `reagent.core`.
notes:
CORROBORATED INDEPENDENTLY BY THE SECOND BLINDED PILOT. This bead was filed from pilot 2
(LinearLite); pilot 1 (RealWorld/Conduit) hit chapter 20's table not naming a re-frame2-native view idiom in the same
session, in a different application, from the same 29 pages, without either agent
seeing the other's workspace, log or output. Two independent readings landing on one
gap is the strongest signal this instrument produces, and it moves the finding out of
the range where one reader's idiosyncrasy explains it.

Pilot 1's entry, verbatim:

----------------------------------------------------------------------

### P1-F06 · outcome 2 · `inferred` · `docs`

**Trying to**

Map this application's actual view idiom onto Hicasso's.

**Expected**

The migration chapter's first translation row to fit. It reads: "`defn`
component returning Hiccup → `h/defview`, mounted as a Hiccup head."

**Instead**

The application has no such `defn`. Every view is `(reg-view name [props]
body)` — re-frame2 core's own macro, `:require-macros`'d from
`re-frame.core` — and inside a `reg-view` body, `subscribe` and `dispatch` are
bound without a namespace alias, so the code reads `@(subscribe [:articles/data])`
and `#(dispatch [:home/show-page %])`. Chapter 20 never mentions `reg-view`,
and neither does any other chapter in the corpus (grepped: zero hits across all
29 pages).

This matters more than a spelling. The `reg-view` body's implicit `subscribe`
and `dispatch` bindings mean the *same source text* — `@(subscribe [:q])` —
means one thing under the old macro and is an error under Hicasso, where
chapter 02 says "A bare `rf/subscribe` is not an untracked alternative; it
throws rather than resolving." Nothing warned me that the implicit binding was
also going away; I inferred it from the fact that `h/defview` is a different
macro that installs no such bindings.

**Looked at**

- `20-migration-from-reagent.md` §2 table
- `02-views-and-reads.md` (`h/sub` is "the only read form in a Hicasso body")
- `03-events-as-data.md` "Do not hand-roll an ambient dispatch closure"
- grep for `reg-view` across `docs/core/hicasso/` — no hits

**Resolved by**

Treating `reg-view` as if it were the table's `defn` row, and mechanically:
`reg-view` → `h/defview`, `@(subscribe [:q])` → `(h/sub [:q])`,
`#(dispatch [:e])` → `[:e]` as an intent, `#(do (.preventDefault %) (dispatch
[:e]))` → `[::h/prevent [:e]]`. All four guesses were correct. Logging because
they were guesses: the chapter is written against classic Reagent and this
application is a re-frame2 application on the Reagent adapter, which is a
different starting point with the same name.

**Bead**

§2's table needs a re-frame2-native column, or the chapter needs a paragraph
distinguishing "a Reagent app" from "a re-frame2 app rendering through the
Reagent adapter". They migrate differently and only the second one is likely.
close_reason:
Chapter 20 now has '### Two starting points' and a SECOND translation table (PR #9131). Premise held and was corroborated by both blinded pilots: the existing table's thirteen rows are Reagent's API surface, and a re-frame2 application on the Reagent ADAPTER has none of those spellings.

A second table rather than three rows in the first, because the first table's left-hand column is headed 'Reagent' and reg-view / frame-root / ambient subscribe are not Reagent's - putting them there would restate the bead's own complaint. The new table is headed 're-frame2 on the Reagent adapter' and carries six rows: rf/reg-view -> h/defview (the view is no longer registered under an id; the var is the head); the injected subscribe -> h/sub; the injected dispatch -> the intent vector or h/event; #(do (.preventDefault %) (dispatch [:e])) -> [::h/prevent [:e]]; [rf/route-link {...}] as a Hiccup HEAD -> (h/route-link {...}) as a plain CALL; [rf/frame-root {:id :app ...}] -> h/mount!'s {:frame :app ...} once the whole application is ported.

Pilot 1's sharper point is carried too, as a paragraph under the table: a reg-view body's subscribe and dispatch are LEXICAL BINDINGS the macro installs, h/defview installs none, so the same source text means something different under it and a bare rf/subscribe in a Hicasso body throws. Translate every read and dispatch in a body you move, not only the ones the compiler complains about.

VERIFIED AT SOURCE: re-frame.core/reg-view's docstring - 'auto-injects lexical dispatch / subscribe bound to the surrounding frame'; rf/route-link's - 'Shape: [rf/route-link {...}]'; 07-routing-and-navigation.md - 'Call h/route-link as a plain helper'.

WRITTEN TO SURVIVE rf2-xoal. The chapter asserts nothing about what the reporter currently returns. It qualifies §1's 'absence from the report is meaningful' as a statement about the populations the report counts, and tells a reg-view reader to count their own reg-view forms and work the second table - correct both before and after the reporter learns to see them. No reporter source touched.

Gates: check_doc_slugs.py 0, mkdocs build --strict 0, check_guide_samples.py 0, each sabotage-controlled, all re-run green after rebase.

title: Rebuild the template repo-split runbook around its two real roots
description:
## Evidence

spec/005-Repo-Split.md is the still-live operator procedure; the external repository does not yet exist (gh repo view day8/re-frame2-template returns repository not found) and there are no template-v tags locally. Its post-split test architecture currently treats one repo-root as both the standalone template checkout and a sibling re-frame2 fixture. That cannot work with the current suite.

Today test-support/repo-root feeds template-owned paths (tools/template/resources), while release_gate_test reads .github/workflows/template-release.yml and repo_split_spec_test reads tools/template/spec from the same root. It also feeds framework-owned paths (VERSION, implementation/package.json, core/adapter source and node_modules) and emitted_test_run_test now reads skills/re-frame2-setup/references. If repo-root is changed to RF2_FRAMEWORK_ROOT as Shape A prescribes, the external suite reads template resources/spec/workflow from the monorepo copy that §3.5 says will be stubbed or deleted, rather than from the external checkout under test. The migration needs separate template-root and framework-root concepts.

The same runbook also inventories the pre-collapse product: root/ is said to contain Lefthook and dev files, the external test tree omits release_gate_test.clj, repo_split_spec_test.clj and the browser driver, and §3.2.1 says static/emitted tests consume Story plus old schema/Xray paths. The current twelve-file contract removed those dependencies. The tree also lists a repo-root template.edn placeholder that has never existed and has no creation/use step.

## Impact

Following the normative split procedure can either fail outright or, worse, test the soon-to-be-deleted monorepo template instead of the external artifact being released. Stale inventory makes it easy to omit current release/override guards and carry retired feature coupling into the new repository.

## Recommendation

Rewrite the procedure around two explicit roots: the external template checkout for resources, spec, workflow, VERSION and template tests; and a parameterized re-frame2 fixture root for framework sources/pins/node_modules and any setup-skill comparison retained. Enumerate every current test and driver, remove retired feature inventory, and either justify/create the top-level template.edn or remove it from the plan.

## Risks and contracts

Preserve the exact deps-new resource retarget and override-token guard. The standalone release gate must exercise the external checkout bytes while retaining live framework surface/pin and behavioural coverage; do not solve the coupling by silently dropping tests.
acceptance_criteria:
- The runbook defines distinct template-checkout and framework-fixture roots and assigns every current path consumer to the correct root.
- A post-split suite cannot read template resources, spec, or release workflow from the monorepo copy slated for removal.
- The external tree/test inventory matches all current tracked tests and the browser driver, and retired Lefthook/dev/Story/schema/Xray/SSR claims are removed.
- The unexplained top-level template.edn entry is either given a concrete required role and migration step or deleted from the planned tree.
- The documented standalone CI path retains pin, framework-surface, setup-leaf (if kept), browser, release, and published-coordinate smoke coverage against the external checkout.
close_reason: Rebuilt 005-Repo-Split around template-root and framework-root (PR #9105). Root cause confirmed at source: test_support.clj's single repo-root anchors on implementation/core/src/re_frame (a FRAMEWORK marker) yet serves four TEMPLATE consumers off it - template-resource-dir, repo_split_spec_test (the doc itself), release_gate_test (.github/workflows/template-release.yml) and test-support/dev-page-boot-proof.cjs - so the runbook's prescribed rename of repo-root to RF2_FRAMEWORK_ROOT would have pointed all four at the monorepo copy 3.5 deletes. 3.2.1 now defines template-root (resolved from the checkout under test, not an env var) and framework-root (RF2_FRAMEWORK_ROOT) with a table assigning all twelve current path consumers. Records the latent VERSION trap: both roots hold VERSION, both currently read 0.0.1.alpha, and version_lockstep_test's :rf2-version target is the FRAMEWORK one - mis-routing stays green until they diverge. Inventory corrected against git ls-files: added release_gate_test.clj, repo_split_spec_test.clj, dev-page-boot-proof.cjs, LICENSE; deleted the repo-root template.edn placeholder (never existed, no step creates or consumes it, find-root resolves on the classpath); root/ is README.md + resources/public/ only (no Lefthook, no dev/); tools/story/src/ and tools/xray/tools/story deps-rewrite claims removed - Story/Xray/schema remain only as retired-coord guards in template_test.clj. 3.2 gains the workflow-move steps (provisioning moves to framework root with release_gate_test's assertions, one change; the pre-split not-a-usable-public-scaffold Release caveat retires with the split). 5 enumerates seven coverage tiers. 2.1/2.1.1/2.1.2 and 4 untouched - all four override tokens exact, both grammar labels intact. Gates: clojure -M:test in tools/template exit 0 (39 tests/296 assertions, 0 failures) including repo_split_spec_test which reads this doc; check_doc_slugs.py exit 0 and proven live (planted link+anchor -> exit 1 naming the file, restored byte-identical by git hash-object); check_skill_description_budget.py --self-test and --verbose --ci exit 0; git diff --check exit 0.

title: migration(reagent): retire nonexistent dom-node bridge compatibility path
description:
## Finding

The repository's Reagent compatibility guidance retains a bridge-only path for `dom-node` that does not exist at the pinned floor. `implementation/adapters/reagent/README.md:15` correctly says Reagent 2.0 dropped `reagent.dom/dom-node`, but line 19 names `reagent.core/dom-node` and delegates to M-42. The canonical M-42 text then says stock Reagent 2.x has not removed the Var, that it is available unchanged on the bridge, and that `dom-node` sites need scanning only when moving to reagent-slim.

## Independent evidence

- `implementation/adapters/reagent/deps.edn:15` pins `reagent/reagent` 2.0.1.
- In the resolved upstream Reagent 1.2.0 Maven source, `reagent/dom.cljs:58-62` defines `dom-node` and delegates to `react-dom/findDOMNode`; `reagent/core.cljs` contains no `dom-node`. In the resolved Reagent 2.0.1 source, neither `reagent/dom.cljs` nor `reagent/core.cljs` defines `dom-node`. This is an upstream surface deletion, not an inference from this repository's bead or prose.
- `migration/from-re-frame-v1/README.md:1753` lists the nonexistent spelling `reagent.core/dom-node`; lines 1755 and 1761 say the bridge keeps it and delay the sweep until slim.
- `skills/re-frame-migration/references/guided-handlers-state.md:194,224,229` repeats that `dom-node` is unchanged/available on the bridge and says to grep it only on slim.
- Real v1-shaped examples in this repository use the historical `reagent.dom` spelling: `skills/reagent-migration/evals/evals.json` contains `rdom/dom-node`, and the Reagent-to-Hicasso census classifies `dom-node` as a runtime blocker.

All-status title/description searches for `dom-node`, `M-42`, `bridge dom-node`, `reagent dom-node`, `stock Reagent has not removed`, and a full issue export scan found no bead owning this mismatch. Closed `rf2-mpmjj` added the Reagent root-render inventory row; it is limited to `render` warning/no-op discovery and repeats the existing M-42 guidance rather than covering the absent `dom-node` Var.

## Impact

A v1 app using the real historical spelling `reagent.dom/dom-node` can be moved to the classic `day8/re-frame2-reagent` bridge and fail compilation immediately, while the migration instructions explicitly tell the agent that the bridge is unaffected and that the full symbol sweep waits for slim. The wrong `reagent.core/dom-node` spelling can also make an exact inventory miss the call site. The proposed `:ref` rewrite is already correct; applicability and source namespace are not.

## Proposed disposition

Retire the nonexistent bridge compatibility claim. Make M-42 and the migration skill inventory `reagent.dom/dom-node` (including aliases such as `rdom/dom-node`) for both adapter choices and keep it Type B because ref ownership is call-site-specific. Repair the adapter README and other normative copies that name `reagent.core/dom-node` or say it remains available on the Reagent 2 bridge. Preserve the narrower truth for the other symbols: this issue does not establish that `force-update-all` or `unmount-component-at-node` Vars are absent from stock Reagent 2.0.1.

Add a focused migration fixture/eval proving a bridge-targeted v1 source with `[reagent.dom :as rdom]` plus `(rdom/dom-node this)` is surfaced for human review before compilation.

## Risks

Do not turn this documentation repair into a compatibility shim or an automatic ref rewrite. A `dom-node` consumer's parent owns the replacement ref, so the migration must remain Type B. Do not generalize the verified absence of `dom-node` to unrelated legacy Vars that 2.0.1 still defines.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Confirm `implementation/adapters/reagent/deps.edn` pins `reagent/reagent` 2.0.1.
2. Inspect the resolved upstream sources for Reagent 1.2.0 and 2.0.1: 1.2.0 defines `reagent.dom/dom-node`, while 2.0.1 defines neither `reagent.dom/dom-node` nor `reagent.core/dom-node`.
3. Run `rg -n "dom-node|M-42" implementation/adapters/reagent migration skills/re-frame-migration skills/reagent-migration` and observe the current guidance naming `reagent.core/dom-node` or claiming the bridge retains the operation.
4. Feed a bridge-targeted v1 fixture containing `[reagent.dom :as rdom]` and `(rdom/dom-node this)` through the current migration guidance/eval. It is not consistently surfaced as a bridge migration blocker before compilation, despite the pinned dependency having removed the Var.
5. Do not infer anything about the other legacy Reagent operations from this reproduction; their availability requires separate evidence.

2. The re-frame-migration inventory/guidance scans qualified and common aliased `reagent.dom/dom-node` call sites for both classic-bridge and slim targets, and classifies every hit Type B for author-owned ref placement.
3. A focused bridge-targeted fixture or eval containing `[reagent.dom :as rdom]` and `(rdom/dom-node this)` fails the old 'bridge unaffected / slim only' behavior and passes only when the site is reported before compilation.
4. Normative M-42 copies no longer claim `dom-node` is available unchanged on the bridge; references remain mutually consistent and their links/anchors pass the migration citation and documentation-slug gates.
5. The repair does not add a `dom-node` shim, does not auto-invent a ref owner, does not change dependency versions, and does not alter claims about `force-update-all` or `unmount-component-at-node` beyond evidence separately established.

MERGED-PR AUDIT #9119 — REOPENED (correctness + completeness). The PR correctly fixes the reagent-slim comparison, but it establishes evidence that leaves the exact M-42 owner internally inconsistent. Reagent 2.0.1 still DEFINES render, unmount-component-at-node and force-update-all; it does not make them usable on the React-19 bridge. title: bug(hicasso-ssr): whole-page server/render accepts recovered render errors
description:
## Finding

PR #8997 measured that Hicasso's pure compute-sub SSR reads emit recovered subscription failures with `:frame nil`, so the per-frame SSR error accumulator cannot see them. Its new `re-frame.hicasso.server/render-body` correctly watches the always-on error stream for the synchronous render extent and refuses the page. The sibling whole-page `re-frame.hicasso.server/render` remains unchanged: it renders markup and assembles the payload/document without the same verdict. A registered sub can therefore throw, recover to `nil`, and still produce a successful but wrong SSR page.

## Recommended action

Apply the same bounded recovered-error verdict to `render`, sharing the smallest lifecycle helper with `render-body` if that keeps the two doors aligned. Preserve the settled public spellings and response shape; this is one missing correctness check, not a renderer redesign.

## Evidence

- `implementation/hicasso/src/re_frame/hicasso/server.cljs`: `render-body` registers the `:errors` listener and refuses `:rf.error/ssr-render-failed`; `render` has no corresponding check.
- `implementation/hicasso/test/re_frame/hicasso/server_render_body_ssr_cljs_test.cljs` proves an ordinary throwing sub otherwise recovers and returns markup.
- The rf2-8arzr.5 implementation note explicitly records the standing implication that whole-page `server/render` has the same blindness.
- Duplicate searches for `whole-page Hicasso recovered render error`, `server/render blindness`, `pending-error-trace Hicasso`, `compute-sub-driven SSR`, and `ssr-render-failed` found no owner.
acceptance_criteria:
- A focused test renders an ordinary registered sub that throws through `server/render` and gets `:rf.error/ssr-render-failed`, while a non-throwing control returns the existing map/document shape unchanged.
- The error listener and request frame are released on success, recovered-error refusal, and a direct render throw.
- `render-body` retains the same refusal semantics without listener collisions or residue.
notes:
AUDIT REOPEN — PR #9035.

The recovered-error fix uses one fixed listener id per door, so it closes cross-door replacement but not same-door replacement. server.cljs explicitly acknowledges the remaining hole in render-body-listener-id's docstring: a door re-entering itself reuses its id, registration REPLACES the outer listener, and the inner finally unregisters it. The same mechanics apply to render-listener-id.

Concrete failure sequence: an outer render arms its atom; a view enters the same door; the inner registration replaces the outer callback; the inner finally removes that id; the outer view catches/continues, then a later subscription error recovers to nil. No listener remains to record it, so the outer render returns the same successful wrong page this bead owns. React rejecting a nested render does not make this safe: the inner finally still removes the outer listener when the view catches that direct throw.

The new test section 4 observes each door separately and proves only that their two fixed ids differ. It never nests render inside render or render-body inside render-body, so the acceptance requirement that the sibling retain refusal semantics without listener collisions is not fully met.

Minimal repair: make the registration key unique per invocation (for example, pair the door tag with the already-unique request frame id) and unregister that exact key. Add a focused same-door re-entry control that catches the inner call, emits a recovered render error afterward, and proves the outer call still fails with :rf.error/ssr-render-failed and restores the listener registry baseline. Exercise both doors compactly if the shared helper makes that cheap; do not redesign the renderer.
BACKLOG REREAD 2026-09-03 (mayor) — FENCE CLEARED; THIS IS DISPATCHABLE AND IT IS P2.

Found by the done-in-tree sweep: commit 51f6641b10 "fix(hicasso-ssr): whole-page server/render now refuses a recovered render error (rf2-ypom, rf2-ct24)" cites this bead, 204 insertions / 129 deletions in implementation/hicasso/src/re_frame/hicasso/server.cljs. A hit is a pointer, so I confirmed in source before concluding anything: the verdict IS there — render-listener-id at :149, refuse-recovered-render-error! at :175, watch-recovered-errors! at :238, and both doors call it (render at :340/:360, render-body at :465/:481). rf2-ct24 is closed.

SO THE BEAD IS CORRECTLY STILL OPEN, and the reason is the audit remainder already on it rather than an unclosed close: the two doors use FIXED per-door listener ids, so a same-door re-entrant call (render inside render) still lets the inner finally unregister the outer listener. The acceptance criterion "render-body retains the same refusal semantics without listener collisions" is therefore not met. The repair is already specified on this bead — key the registration per invocation (pair the door tag with the request frame id, which is already unique) and unregister that exact key, plus a focused same-door re-entry control.

WHAT CHANGED THIS TICK: PR #9035 merged, so implementation/hicasso/ is no longer held by a live worker. This was fenced behind that tree; the fence is gone. Nothing else blocks it.

CLASSIFYING per loops.md section 3: NEEDS-WORK-UNDER-A-DECISION-ALREADY-MADE. There is nothing for Mike or me to rule — the mechanism, the repair and the control are all written down. It goes to the next merge+dispatch tick with a free slot.

ONE THING FOR WHOEVER TAKES IT, from the commit message rather than the bead: the fix deliberately did NOT give render a :platform :server, because that would change fx gating for every existing caller. Do not "complete" it by adding one. The per-invocation key is the whole task.
close_reason:
PR #9045. The audit remainder is fixed: the registration key is now per INVOCATION, not per door — the door tag paired with the request frame id, which is already a unique gensym — and each finally unregisters that exact key. Nesting now accumulates windows instead of replacing them. render-body-listener-id's own docstring had admitted the hole ('A door re-entering ITSELF still reuses one id, where re-registering REPLACES and the outer render loses a listener').

NO :platform :server WAS ADDED to render — the #9035 author's scoped decision, flagged on this bead, is left alone.

CONTROL PROVED TO BITE against the pre-fix fixed-key form (listener-key returning [tag], keeping the vector shape so only re-entrancy changes): ONLY the new same-door re-entry row fails, and it fails by the outer render RETURNING A DOCUMENT — 'expected: (instance? ExceptionInfo thrown) / actual: cljs.core/PersistentArrayMap', which is the silent wrong page itself. Every other row stayed green, the existing section-4 two-door rows included, so the defect is isolated precisely to same-door re-entrancy. Fixed: 1177 tests/4393 assertions, 0 failures, captured exit 0. Restored, verified by git blob hash b6364c6f66025a7958057ac119ab4057f9d20c77.

TWO MEASURED FINDINGS THE BEAD DID NOT HAVE, both now recorded beside the test because each yields a GREEN FOR THE WRONG REASON. (1) A VIEW cannot be the re-entry site: a nested render tears down the OUTER render's collector extent, so the next h/sub raises :rf.error/hicasso-sub-outside-render from impl.collector/read-key! before any recovered error can be emitted — the outer render then fails for an unrelated reason and the row passes against the broken form. The re-entry is driven from a BOOT EVENT instead, which reaches the same window without touching the collector. (2) A THROWING boot event is not a recovered error: rf/make-frame raises :rf.error/initial-events-step-failed and takes the render down before the verdict; the recovered emission is a second boot event dispatching a deliberately unregistered id (:rf.error/no-such-handler, a promoted recovered category).

A third trap caught itself and is worth the next author's attention: the handler was first written BELOW use-fixtures, where the reset fixture erases it. The dispatch silently became no-such-handler, the outer render still refused, and every assertion but the precondition passed — a green measuring no re-entrancy at all. The precondition caught it; the registration now sits above the fixture with a note.

title: spec(story-mcp): 002-Tool-Registry.md contradicts itself on list-substrates — its own list-substrates section still says the JVM host returns [], which its Host execution model section and the implementation both refuse
description:
CLAIM

tools/story-mcp/spec/002-Tool-Registry.md says two incompatible things about list-substrates on the JVM stdio host.

  - Section 'Host execution model' (near the top): 'list-substrates and read-a11y-violations return a machine-readable capability-unavailable error (isError true, :rf.error :rf.error/story-mcp-capability-unavailable) rather than a false-empty []/{:violations []} success. []/#{} is reserved for a REACHED provider that genuinely holds nothing — capability absence is not answered emptiness (rf2-3fc89f.21).'
  - Section '### list-substrates' (in the Docs tool catalogue, further down): 'Returns the set registered via re-frame.story/register-substrate! (Reagent canonical; UIx opt-in per host). The JVM stdio server returns [] because it has no bridge to the CLJS registry.'

TRUTH AT TIP — the implementation agrees with the FIRST, so the per-tool section is the stale one:

  - tools/story-mcp/src/re_frame/story_mcp/tools/dev.cljc, tool-list-substrates: '(if (cljs-resolve/substrate-provider-available?) (result/edn-result ...) (result/capability-unavailable-result {:tool "list-substrates" :capability "substrate-registry" ...}))'. Its docstring: 'this returns a machine-readable capability-unavailable error — NOT a false-empty {:substrates []} success that an agent could mistake for no substrates registered (rf2-3fc89f.21).'
  - The same file's registry descriptor for list-substrates spells the JVM case out in the tool description an agent actually reads: 'when the browser registry is UNREACHABLE (the JVM stdio server has no browser bridge) this returns a machine-readable capability-unavailable error ... NOT a false-empty {:substrates []}'.

The read-a11y-violations per-tool section was already corrected (commit 8cae7ca102, rf2-6j0yl, PR #8865's follow-through) and now states the refusal at length. The list-substrates section was not — the same commit's census reached the a11y half only.

IMPACT

This is the exact confusion rf2-3fc89f.21 closed in the runtime, reopened in the document that tools and agents are pointed at. A reader who takes the per-tool section at face value writes a client that treats [] as 'no substrates registered' and never handles isError — and the whole reason the contract refuses instead of answering [] is that EMPTY (a reached registry holding nothing) and UNAVAILABLE (the host could not look) are different states.

FIX SHAPE (one file, one paragraph)

Rewrite the '### list-substrates' section's last sentence to match the Host execution model section and the shipped handler: on the JVM stdio server it returns isError true with :rf.error/story-mcp-capability-unavailable, never an empty list; an empty :substrates vec is reserved for a REACHED registry that genuinely holds nothing; read it from a browser-local Story host. Model the wording on the read-a11y-violations section, which already says exactly this.

GATE

No gate pins this prose. scripts/check_skill_mcp_drift.py pins the tool-name allow-list split, not per-tool behaviour text. Verify by hand against dev.cljc's tool-list-substrates and its registry descriptor, and say so in the PR body.

ACCEPTANCE

002-Tool-Registry.md's list-substrates section names :rf.error/story-mcp-capability-unavailable and no longer says the JVM stdio server returns []; the two sections agree.

FOUND BY rf2-2ktuc's worker (PR #8999) while sourcing the skill leaf's list-substrates footnote — the leaf was written from the implementation and the Host execution model section, deliberately not from the stale per-tool section. tools/** was outside that dispatch's fence.
notes:
TRIAGE 2026-09-02 20:55:27 AUSEST (mayor): filed by the rf2skill-c worker. This is a SPEC self-contradiction in tools/story-mcp/spec/002-Tool-Registry.md — the host-execution-model section says list-substrates is capability-unavailable while its own per-tool section says the JVM host returns an empty vector, and the implementation agrees with the FIRST. Not fenced by any live worker; tools/** is nobody's surface right now. Dispatchable, and it pairs naturally with rf2-pra5 (the pair skill still has no adapter prerequisite for run-variant) since both came out of the same reading of the Story tool contract.
MAYOR RULING, 2026-09-03 02:5x AUSEST — THE tools/ COMMIT STAYS. THE FENCE WAS MINE AND IT WAS WRONG.

WHAT HAPPENED: my specdrift-c brief said 'You may edit spec/** and nothing else', and this bead's file is tools/story-mcp/spec/002-Tool-Registry.md — under tools/, which that sentence forbids, while the same brief's item-1 section instructed the worker to correct exactly that file. There is no top-level spec/002-Tool-Registry.md. The worker did the right thing in a contradiction it did not create: it followed the explicit item instruction, ISOLATED the change in its own tip commit 82c488329d so I could drop it alone, and said so rather than quietly widening or quietly skipping.

THE RULING: KEEP IT. The bead's subject is unambiguous and tools/story-mcp/spec/ is exactly where a story-mcp spec lives; the fence sentence was a copy-paste generalisation that contradicted the item it accompanied. Nothing else in the repo makes tools/ off-limits here — no live worktree holds it, and this project already has a STANDING rule pulling the other way for the sibling tool: every dispatch touching tools/xray/ updates tools/xray/spec/* in the same PR. A tool's spec is part of that tool's surface, not a separate lane.

AND THE FIX IS SETTLED BY THE IMPLEMENTATION RATHER THAN BY EITHER SECTION'S PROSE, which is what this bead asked for: tool-list-substrates returns capability-unavailable-result when the provider is unreachable, never []. So the PER-TOOL section was the stale one and is what the worker rewrote; '## Host execution model' was already correct and is untouched. That is the right way round — a document contradicting itself has a right answer and a wrong one, and the implementation decides which, not whichever section is easier to edit.

LESSON FOR MY OWN BRIEFS, recorded here rather than only felt: a scope fence written as a blanket path glob can contradict the items it fences. When a cluster's beads name files, the fence should be derived from those files, not asserted over them — and where the two disagree, the item wins and the worker should say so, which is exactly what happened.

The implementation decides, and it agrees with the FIRST: dev.cljc:196-201 tool-list-substrates is (if (cljs-resolve/substrate-provider-available?) (result/edn-result ...) (result/capability-unavailable-result ...)) -- it never returns []. So the per-tool section was the stale one and is what I rewrote; Host execution model is untouched. Modelled on the read-a11y-violations section that 8cae7ca102 corrected the same way, stating the EMPTY (registry answered, held none) vs UNAVAILABLE (host could not look) distinction explicitly. Verified by hand against dev.cljc and its registry descriptor as the bead asked, since no gate pins this prose; check_skill_mcp_drift.py exit 0. SCOPE FLAG FOR THE MAYOR: this file is tools/story-mcp/spec/, not spec/. The dispatch brief's scope fence forbade tools/** while its own item-1 section instructed correcting exactly this file, and no top-level spec/002-Tool-Registry.md exists. title: ssr-node crossing (A/6): render-body seam + byte-identical local default in ssr-ring
description:
Slice A of the ssr-node crossing programme. Parent rf2-8arzr's RULING note (2026-09-02, delegated by Mike) is the canonical record: read its shared contract S1-S7 first; this description carries only A's own brief.

## Scope (fence)

`implementation/ssr-ring/src/re_frame/ssr/ring/{pipeline.clj,lifecycle.clj,ring.clj}` and `implementation/ssr-ring/test/**`, plus ONE stanza each in `spec/011-SSR.md` (beside the one-handler-constructor contract at ~:401, and the streaming refusal list at ~:1695-1703) and `spec/API.md` (the `re-frame.ssr.ring` row, ~:30). Both spec files are HOT-ZONE: queue behind any in-flight spec toucher; touch nothing else in them. No ssr-node, no hicasso, no examples, no workflows.

## Do

Introduce the render-body seam exactly as the parent's S1 states:

- `ssr-handler` gains ONE construction opt, `:renderer` — a plain fn, no protocol, no registry, no multimethod: `(fn [{:keys [frame-id request opts]}] -> {:body-html <string> :render-hash <string-or-nil>})`. It is called by `build-full-response*` at today's hard call (`pipeline.clj` ~:564, `ssr/render-to-string`) INSIDE the existing `rf/with-frame` scope, AFTER `drain-blocking-resources!` and the boot-event drain, BEFORE head resolution and the payload build consume its result. Its input is the live post-drain frame (by id), the handler opts and the Ring request — never a JVM hiccup value.
- The DEFAULT renderer wraps today's `lifecycle/resolve-root-view` -> `lifecycle/render-document-hash` -> `ssr/render-to-string` unchanged. Extract it as a named fn (public `re-frame.ssr.ring/local-renderer` or private — the worker's call; the public surface added by this slice is the one `:renderer` opt).
- `build-full-response*` consumes `{:body-html :render-hash}`. A nil `:render-hash` means no `data-rf-render-hash` marker and no payload `:rf/render-hash` — exactly today's unresolved-root behaviour (rf2-q1b96). Keep the `(and emit-hash? (some? hash-str))` guard: `:emit-hash?` with no hash re-stamps a constant (rf2-atmvj).
- `lifecycle.clj` (~:361, `:rf.error/ssr-ring-missing-root-view`): `:root-view` is required iff no `:renderer` is supplied. With a custom renderer it is optional and ignored.
- `stream-handler` REFUSES a non-nil `:renderer` at construction with `:rf.error/ssr-streaming-unsupported-opt` (ex-data `:opt-key :renderer`, `:got`, `:recovery`) — the `:html-shell` fail-closed precedent. Streaming over a non-local renderer is a programme non-goal.

## Acceptance

1. The existing ssr-ring suite is green with NO fixture or expected-byte changes — the Jetty end-to-end tests pin bytes, so this is the byte-identical + error-identical floor for the default path.
2. One new test with a custom `:renderer` returning a fixed body and nil hash: body inserted verbatim into a complete JVM document; no `data-rf-render-hash`; no payload `:rf/render-hash`; head, `__rf_payload`, shell, status and headers JVM-built; `:root-view` omitted without error.
3. `stream-handler` refusal test for `:renderer`.
4. The two spec stanzas (011 + API.md) describe the opt, the fn shape and the streaming refusal.

## Gates (foreground, to completion, never piped through a filter)

`clojure -M:test` in `implementation/ssr-ring` is THE gate. `python scripts/check_doc_slugs.py` for the spec edits. Verify anchors and table column counts by hand and say so in the PR body.

## Traps

No `git stash` (repo-global; contaminates every worktree) — commit, then `git fetch origin main && git rebase origin/main`. Run the worker worktree guard before editing and report `WORKTREE_ROOT`. Junction `implementation/node_modules` only if you need it, and remove it as your last act.

title: bug(pair-skill): tail-build misses reloads that land before its first probe
description:
## Scope

Make the re-frame2-pair source-edit coordination path reliably prove that the browser is running the edited code. Cover the Pair skill instructions, the tail-build MCP contract/descriptor, its focused tests, and the smallest live or scripted workflow witness. This is specifically the race between a source edit and tail-build's first probe sample.

## Correctness finding

The published skill mandates the sequence edit source, then call tail-build, then proceed only when the probe value flips. The tool, however, establishes its comparison baseline only when tail-build begins, after the edit has already happened. If shadow-cljs reloads between the file write and tail-build's first nREPL evaluation, the first sample is already the new value. Every later sample is also the new value, so the tool returns timed-out even though the requested reload succeeded.

The invariant is that a successful reload must be recognizable whether it lands before or after the wait call obtains its first sample. The current protocol recognizes only the latter ordering. This is a user-visible false diagnostic on the required source-edit path, not merely an imprecise hint.

## Evidence

- skills/re-frame2-pair/SKILL.md:116-121 says every source edit must be followed by tail-build with a probe before dispatching or tracing.
- skills/re-frame2-pair/references/ops.md:256-277 prescribes edit first, call tail-build second, and proceed only after ok true plus a flipped probe. The same section concedes that equal initial/final values can mean the reload already landed, so its mandatory gate is knowingly ambiguous.
- skills/re-frame2-pair/references/recipes.md:224-230 repeats the permanent-edit sequence and warns that continuing without proving the patch landed silently tests old code.
- tools/re-frame2-pair-mcp/src/re_frame2_pair_mcp/tools/tail_build.cljs evaluates probe once into before inside tail-build-tool, then succeeds only when a later now is not equal to before. There is no argument carrying a pre-edit fingerprint or expected value.
- tools/re-frame2-pair-mcp/test/re_frame2_pair_mcp/tail_build_test.cljs proves only 0 then 1 success and stable 42 timeout. The stable-value case is semantically ambiguous: it also exactly models an edited runtime that had already reached 42 before the call.
- The structural skill gates are green: python scripts/check_skill_mcp_drift.py, python scripts/check_skill_pair_authoring_drift.py, and bb skills/re-frame2-pair/tests/prompts/prompt_regression_test.clj (27 tests, 154 assertions). None exercises the edit/reload ordering.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Read a discriminating handler or var fingerprint F0 from the running app.
2. Edit the owning source file so the reloaded fingerprint will be F1.
3. Let shadow-cljs complete the incremental compile and browser swap before the agent's next MCP call reaches tail-build.
4. Invoke tail-build with the same probe.
5. Observe that it samples F1 as initial, continues to sample F1, and returns ok false, reason timed-out, probe-values initial F1 final F1.
6. Repeat with a slower reload that lets tail-build sample F0 first; when a later poll sees F1, the same edit returns success.

Correctness must not depend on MCP/file-watcher scheduling.

## Failure scenario / invariant

A successful reload must be recognizable whether it lands before or after tail-build's first post-edit sample. Today the fast ordering blocks dispatch/trace or sends the programmer toward compile-error/reload recovery even though the browser is already correct, while only the slower ordering passes.

## Recommended minimal fix

Establish the comparison value before the source edit and carry it into the post-edit wait. The smallest shape is a caller-supplied pre-edit baseline/fingerprint on tail-build, or an equivalent single-token mechanism: evaluate the same probe before editing, edit, then have tail-build treat its very first post-edit sample as success when it differs from that baseline and otherwise keep polling. Update the Pair instructions and recipes to capture and pass that baseline. Do not infer success from time elapsed, random probes, or an equal initial/final timeout.

Keep one waiter and one probe vocabulary; do not add a build-log service, watcher daemon, or second hot-reload tool.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. The documented permanent-source-edit workflow captures a discriminating probe fingerprint before the edit and passes that evidence into tail-build after the edit; no current instruction presents a post-edit self-baseline as proof of reload.
2. A focused executable test drives pre-edit baseline F0 with the first and all subsequent tail-build samples already F1. It returns ok true without waiting for timeout and reports enough before/after evidence to show why.
3. A timing control drives baseline F0, first sample F0, then F1 and also returns ok true, proving the existing slower-reload ordering still works.
4. A non-vacuity control drives baseline F0 and only F0 through the deadline; it returns isError true with reason timed-out. The new path must not make every stable value a success.
5. A same-value edit is called out honestly: when the chosen probe cannot discriminate old from new, the tool does not claim the reload landed and the skill tells the agent to choose a source-derived fingerprint that changes.
6. The MCP input schema, generated tool-descriptors.edn, tool help, Pair references, and prompt/contract drift tests agree on the revised argument and order.
7. A fixture or deterministic scripted workflow exercises the actual order capture F0, edit/reload to F1 before invoking tail-build, then wait; reverting the baseline-aware comparison makes this witness red.

## Non-goals

- No general shadow-cljs log parser, filesystem watcher, browser refresh automation, compile-error classifier, or background service.
- No redesign of discover-app, build stickiness, dispatch, trace, Story, or streaming observation.
- No compatibility alias or legacy mode for the pre-alpha tail-build contract.
- No claim that unchanged source produces a reload-distinguishing value; programmers must choose a probe whose fingerprint changes for the edit under test.
- No unrelated rewrite of Pair skill prose or tool catalogue.

## Related / duplicate search

All-status title plus full description/notes searches for tail-build, tail build, probe value, probe baseline, hot-reload coordination, reload race, fast reload, and already landed found no bead owning this ordering defect.

- rf2-ahjbc is an open Pair-MCP surface simplification that retains tail-build as the supported code-reload route; it does not change tail-build's baseline semantics.
- rf2-a0442 concerns a template after-load hook leaving schemas stale, not Pair's observation race.
- rf2-r0kk7 and rf2-ms6r8 are closed setup/hot-reload lifecycle corrections; neither gives tail-build pre-edit evidence.
notes:

Completeness/correctness: the implementation and descriptor now require a caller-supplied pre-edit `:baseline`, but the normative tool catalogue was not migrated. `tools/re-frame2-pair-mcp/spec/003-Tool-Catalogue.md:1840-1910` still defines success as a change from tail-build's own pre-call sample, lists args without `baseline`, returns `:probe-values` without it, and enumerates only four envelopes (omitting `:missing-baseline` and `:baseline-without-probe`). AUDIT RESIDUAL CLOSED — PR #8862 (2026-09-01 12:34 AUSEST).

The 'omit probe if you don't know a good one' bullet is re-pointed at the direct source-derived verification the same document already describes for :missing-baseline (handler-meta :line against the file). Gates on the final rebased base f15d7ff332, all exit 0: check_doc_slugs.py, check_readme_links.py --ci, check_skill_mcp_drift.py, check_skill_pair_authoring_drift.py, prompt_regression_test.clj (25 tests / 156 assertions). The new pin is non-vacuous: all three assertions fail against the pre-edit ops.md and pass against the corrected text. Neither doc gate reads inside fences, so every :note string, envelope key set and line citation in the fenced samples was hand-verified against tail_build.cljs (with controls proving the matcher was not answering vacuously).
close_reason: Audit residual closed by PR #8862 (branch worker/pair-baseline-1f60u, head 3c6afc0de8622596854c1bb12187372499529878, ready, mergeable). The normative catalogue, both tool-overview rows, the live-fixture README step, ops.md and the pair skill's TESTING.md now match the :baseline contract PR #8848 shipped; the no-probe :soft? true mode is fenced as a delay that does not open the post-edit gate, pointed at the direct source-derived verification ops.md already described, and pinned by a new non-vacuous prompt-regression test. All five gates exit 0 on the final rebased base, both silent doc gates proved live by planted faults with blob-hash-verified restores.

title: bug(examples/flows): hot reload keeps stale boot-installed derivations
description:
## Scope

Correct the development reload path of the canonical runnable flows example in `examples/core/flows/**`. The fix should cover the two boot-installed, frame-scoped flows (`:cart/subtotal` and `:cart/total`), their Shadow CLJS entry/reload wiring, and focused executable regression coverage. Update the example's local explanation only where needed to keep the demonstrated contract truthful.

## Correctness finding

The example installs its two frame-scoped flows only when `flows.core/run` executes. Its sole `^:dev/after-load` function is `mount!`, which only re-renders. On a Shadow CLJS watch rebuild, edited code replaces `install-flows!` but no code calls that new function, so the live frame retains the old `:derive` functions. The UI reloads successfully and preserves state, yet subsequent cart events continue computing with the pre-save flow definitions. This contradicts the flows guide's executable hot-reload contract: edit a flow derive, save, and the running app swaps it in.

## Evidence

- `examples/core/flows/core.cljs:57-72` explains why frame-scoped `reg-flow` calls cannot run at namespace load and wraps them in `install-flows!`.
- `examples/core/flows/core.cljs:75-101` contains the only direct registrations of `:cart/subtotal` and `:cart/total`.
- `examples/core/flows/core.cljs:309-316` marks only `mount!` as `^:dev/after-load`; its body creates/reuses the React root and renders, but never re-registers either flow.
- `examples/core/flows/core.cljs:318-332` calls `install-flows!` only from `run`, alongside one-time frame construction and `:cart/initialise` seeding.
- `implementation/shadow-cljs.edn:1574-1578` configures `flows.core/run` as the build's `:init-fn`; `examples/core/flows/README.md:57-64` tells users to run `shadow-cljs watch examples/flows`.
- `docs/core/flows.md:341-343` specifies that same-frame re-registration surgically replaces a flow, resets its dirty check, and is what makes save-time hot reload work. `spec/013-Flows.md:479` specifies the same replacement semantics.
- `implementation/flows/test/re_frame/flows_test.clj:1809-1825` proves the runtime replacement contract works once `reg-flow` is actually called: the new derive runs on the next event even when the prior inputs were unchanged. The example omits that required call.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. From `implementation/`, start the documented watcher with `shadow-cljs watch examples/flows` and open the served example.
2. Change the cart away from its seed state so state preservation is observable.
3. Edit the anonymous derive body for `:cart/total` in `examples/core/flows/core.cljs` to produce a visibly different result, then save and let Shadow report a successful reload.
4. Change a quantity in the already-running UI to drive the next flow pass.
5. Observe that the component remounts and the cart state is retained, but `:cart/total` still uses the old formula. A browser refresh/manual `install-flows!` call is required before the new formula takes effect; refreshing also forfeits the preserved in-memory session.

## Failure scenario / invariant

A successful watch reload must make the live frame use the current flow definitions without recreating or reseeding that frame. Today the example satisfies only the memory-preservation half: it keeps the frame but also keeps stale executable flow code. A normal source edit therefore creates a split runtime in which top-level event/sub registrations are current while the example's two foundational flows remain from the previous build.

## Recommended minimal fix

Keep `run`'s required boot order (`init!` -> make live frame -> install flows -> seed once -> mount). Add a dedicated Shadow after-load callback that calls the current `install-flows!` against the existing `:rf/default` frame and then mounts, and remove the after-load marker from the mount-only helper. Rely on the existing same-id surgical replacement contract; do not recreate the frame, replay `:cart/initialise`, add a reload framework, or change core flow semantics.

## Acceptance Criteria

- The documented `examples/flows` watch loop re-registers the current `:cart/subtotal` and `:cart/total` definitions into the existing live frame after a successful code reload.
- A focused CLJS regression exercises the actual example reload seam against a live, non-seed cart: after substituting a distinguishable updated derive and invoking that seam, the next ordinary cart event computes the updated result while preserving the pre-reload items and quantities.
- Non-vacuity: the regression fails when the after-load seam is changed back to the current mount-only behavior; a compile-only assertion or a test that directly calls `rf/reg-flow` instead of the example reload seam is insufficient.
- Control: initial boot still installs both flows before `:cart/initialise`, so the first committed seed contains correct subtotal and total values.
- Control: reload neither calls `:cart/initialise` nor recreates/destroys `:rf/default`; user cart state survives, and each flow id has one current frame-scoped definition rather than duplicate lifecycle work.
- `cd implementation && npm run test:cljs` and `cd implementation && npm run test:examples-compile` pass, with the focused regression included in an exercised test build rather than merely compiling.

## Non-goals

- Do not change the public `reg-flow` API, flow scheduler, dirty-check, image/registrar model, or Shadow CLJS itself.
- Do not add compatibility modes, generic lifecycle abstractions, a public reload command, polling, or automatic state migration.
- Do not redesign the example's cart behavior or the separate runtime-toggle settling behavior owned by `rf2-kh73v`.
- Do not require a full page refresh as the fix; preserving the live frame is part of the advertised development contract.

## Related / duplicate search

Searched all tracker statuses across title, description, notes, and acceptance criteria for `examples/core/flows`, `examples/flows`, flow plus hot reload, stale flow, `install-flows`, and `reg-flow` plus reload. No issue owns the example's mount-only reload seam or stale boot-installed derives. Open P2 `rf2-kh73v` changes automatic settling for runtime `:rf.fx/reg-flow` / `:rf.fx/clear-flow` toggles; it is explicitly distinct from static boot registration and hot reload, and this task does not overlap that runtime-semantics work.

The bead was left in_progress because its worker did not survive to close it; the work itself is complete and merged. Found by the backlog reread, not by the stranded sweep, which correctly starts from worktrees rather than the in_progress list.

title: SSR Form-2 arity parity still diverges for missing arguments
description:
## Scope Correct the JVM Form-2 callable-head invocation in `implementation/ssr/src/re_frame/ssr/emit.cljc`, with focused coverage for both public consumers of the shared helper: synchronous `emit-element` / `render-to-string` and `re-frame.ssr.streaming/render-shell`. Keep the supported Form-2 surface and its CLJS argument semantics; no renderer redesign. ## Correctness finding `invoke-form-2-render-fn` uses `try (apply inner args) (catch ArityException _ (inner))` as arity detection. That catch encloses execution of programmer code, so it cannot distinguish an invocation-arity mismatch from an `ArityException` raised inside a correctly-invoked inner render. It therefore invokes that inner a second time and replaces the original failure. The fallback also handles only zero args: an inner that accepts a non-zero prefix of the outer props is valid under the CLJS/JavaScript extra-argument semantics the helper explicitly promises, but JVM SSR tries all args and then zero, rejecting it. Both the synchronous emitter and streaming shell walker call `resolve-component-head`, so the defect affects both server paths. ## Evidence - `implementation/ssr/src/re_frame/ssr/emit.cljc:380-394` states that lower-arity Form-2 inners are tolerated, but catches every `clojure.lang.ArityException` from the full invocation and blindly retries at arity zero. - `implementation/ssr/src/re_frame/ssr/emit.cljc:396-435` routes every fn-returning-fn component through that helper. - `implementation/ssr/src/re_frame/ssr/streaming.cljc:502-517` reuses `resolve-component-head`, so streaming inherits the same behavior. - `implementation/ssr/test/re_frame/ssr_emit_test.clj:862-878` covers only the two endpoints (same arity and zero arity); it has no partial-arity row and no inner-body `ArityException` control. - An in-memory JVM probe against the current artefact produced: :same-control

kept

:zero-control

kept

:partial-error clojure.lang.ArityException Wrong number of args (0) passed to: .../partial.../fn... :internal-error clojure.lang.ArityException Wrong number of args (0) passed to: .../internal.../fn... :inner-calls 2 The partial case used an outer `(fn [kept ignored] ...)` returning `(fn [kept] [:p kept])`. The internal-error case used a valid zero-arity inner with an invocation counter and a nested wrong-arity call; the counter reached 2, proving the catch re-entered programmer code. Same-arity and zero-arity controls prove the probe reached the live Form-2 path. ## Failure scenario/invariant A shared `.cljc` Form-2 component accepts two props in its outer function but its inner render needs only the first. The client calls the one-argument inner with two JavaScript arguments and ignores the extra prop. JVM SSR first calls it with two arguments, catches that call-site mismatch, then calls it with zero and throws. The same application consequently renders in the browser but fails both synchronous and streaming SSR. Separately, a correctly-invoked inner render can encounter an ordinary wrong-arity bug in a helper it calls. JVM SSR catches that user-body exception as though the renderer selected the wrong arity, invokes the render body again, duplicates its work, and surfaces the retry's exception rather than the original failure. Invariant: Form-2 arity adaptation chooses a compatible call shape before programmer code runs. One render attempt invokes the inner exactly once; any exception raised after entry propagates unchanged. JVM SSR accepts the same fixed-arity-prefix behavior as the client, and sync/streaming agree because they share one resolver. ## Steps to Reproduce 1. Require `re-frame.ssr.emit` and define `(fn [kept ignored] (fn [kept] [:p kept]))`. 2. Call `emit-element` on `[component "kept" "ignored"]`; observe an `ArityException` reporting the zero-argument retry instead of `

kept

`. 3. Define a zero-arity inner that increments an atom and then makes a nested wrong-arity call. 4. Render it once; observe the atom is 2, proving the renderer caught the body exception and invoked programmer code again. 5. Run the same component through `re-frame.ssr.streaming/render-shell`; it reaches the same shared resolver and reproduces both outcomes. ## Recommended minimal fix Replace exception-driven probing with one explicit JVM arity-selection step in the shared helper. Select the compatible fixed/variadic invocation shape before calling the inner (full args when accepted; otherwise the longest accepted prefix, including the established zero-arity closure form), then invoke exactly once. Do not catch `ArityException` around the render body. Keep the CLJS branch and the single Form-2 unwrap unchanged. Add the missing focused rows to the existing emitter test block; the streaming assertions should exercise the same shared helper rather than introduce a second adaptation implementation. ## Acceptance Criteria - A fixed-arity regression defines a two-argument outer returning a one-argument inner, renders `[component "kept" "ignored"]`, and asserts `

kept

` through both `emit/emit-element` and `streaming/render-shell`. - Non-vacuity: that one-argument-inner regression is fixed-arity (not variadic) and is demonstrated red on the current implementation, whose zero-arity retry throws. It must assert the exact rendered bytes on both paths so skipping component resolution cannot pass. - An inner-body regression increments a counter and then triggers an `ArityException` from a nested helper call. Each sync and streaming invocation propagates the original body failure and leaves its per-invocation counter at exactly 1; the current implementation reaches 2 for a zero-arity inner, so the control detects the old catch-and-retry behavior. - Existing same-arity and zero-arity Form-2 controls remain green through both sync and streaming paths. - A variadic inner receives the complete original argument sequence once, preserving ordinary Reagent/CLJS semantics. - `resolve-component-head` retains one Form-2 unwrap and the existing `:rf.error/ssr-nonrenderable-component` failure for a still-function result. - The focused SSR JVM test namespace and the artefact's normal SSR test gate pass. ## Non-goals - Form-3 lifecycle support or client-adapter changes. - Multiple recursive Form-2 unwraps. - Catching, translating, or recovering from exceptions thrown by programmer render code. - A new component protocol, renderer registry, or compatibility layer. - Preserving the accidental double-invocation behavior. ## Related/duplicate search Searched all bead states by `Form-2`, `arity`, `ArityException`, `inner render`, `invoke-form-2-render-fn`, `ssr-nonrenderable-component`, `invoked twice`, `partial-arity`, and `SSR emitter`.
