on node while the JVM raises. That is the same class and the same deliberate divergence, and the contract wording now added to invoke-form-2-render-fn covers it in general terms, so nothing here is undocumented. Pinning further instances is a decision about how much of the class to enumerate, not a defect.

title: surface-review(examples-substrates): make login the runnable three-view-layer comparison
description:
## Scope

Make the existing login feature the canonical runnable comparison of re-frame2's three active browser view languages: Reagent, UIx, and Hicasso. Keep `examples/core/login/` as the Reagent arm and `examples/substrates/uix/login/` as the UIx arm; add one Hicasso arm under `examples/substrates/hicasso/login/` that requires the same substrate-free `login.model` and owns only its view/root code. Add a concise `examples/substrates/README.md` that explains which comparison to read, wire the new arm through the existing example build/runner/compile path, and extend the existing login bundle-isolation proof. Correct only directly coupled catalogue and TESTING prose.

This is one worked-example outcome, not a demo framework or a substrate selector.

## Findings

- The substrate tree has UIx counter/login/dashboard and reagent-slim counter, but no landing page and no human-facing Hicasso example. `examples/README.md` still describes the family as UIx plus reagent-slim even though Hicasso now ships its own canonical view adapter.
- Hicasso already has a complete installation counter in `docs/core/hicasso/00-installation.md` and a Story/Xray-owned counter testbed under `tools/story/testbeds/hicasso_counter/`. Another counter would duplicate the beginner sample or send learners into tool scaffolding; neither shows a realistic model/view boundary.
- Login is already the right comparison seam. Commit `2644f42b72` (`rf2-ppbvav`) extracted roughly 19 schemas/effects/machine/events/subscriptions and `frame-config` into one substrate-free `login.model`, leaving only views and mount code in the Reagent/UIx/Helix entries. Commit `e1f38e5ddf` (`rf2-d6epb`) removed Helix, so that deliberate three-view example became a two-view pair.
- The removal left observable drift: `examples/TESTING.md` still says counter and login "triplet", "three reactive substrates", and "three login examples" although only Reagent and UIx login builds remain. `login.model` also still speaks of "three mounts". Fixing those words alone would be minutiae; supplying the current third view language restores the useful product shape they once described.
- The three small counter files deliberately repeat their tiny event/sub dataflow so each remains readable top to bottom. Extracting a counter model would weaken the smallest-app lesson for little gain. The substantial login model already amortises sharing and has model-level tests.
- Hicasso's native root door is compatible without an API change, but the boot shape must be honest. `h/mount!` accepts only `:frame`, `:initial-events`, and `:identifier-prefix`; the login demo also needs `model/frame-config`'s `:fx-overrides`. The Hicasso entry should therefore install `re-frame.hicasso.substrate/adapter`, create the frame once with the existing config, and mount into that frame. Hot reload should re-render the retained Hicasso root rather than recreate the frame.
- The existing harness already supplies the needed mechanics. A normal `:examples/login-hicasso` build whose init namespace and `index.html` live under `examples/` is discovered by `serve-example.cjs`, staged with `_shared`, and swept by `check-examples-compile.cjs`; no registry or special runner branch is needed.
- Examples are intentionally test-free. The shared login behavior is already exercised outside the tree, while `check-login-bundle-isolation.cjs` proves the shared model does not pull a foreign view runtime. That checker currently has only Reagent and UIx arms even though the general isolation gate already owns live Hicasso sentinels and a positive-control module.

## Recommended Action

Add `examples/substrates/hicasso/login/` as a direct third view over `login.model`. Keep the same fields, messages, test ids, canned success/failure flow, and shared visual assets as the existing pair. Author the view in native Hicasso idioms (`h/defview`, `h/sub`, event vectors where they fit); preserve the password event's classified map payload rather than flattening the secret into a positional intent. Use a small `h/event` callback where constructing that map requires the DOM value.

Declare `:examples/login-hicasso` beside the two current login builds, with the standard `out/examples/login-hicasso` output. Let the existing manifest-derived runner and compile checker enroll it. Add the exact repository-local run command to the new example README, while linking the Hicasso installation chapter for dependency setup and truthfully noting that the Maven coordinate is not published yet.

Make `examples/substrates/README.md` a short decision/comparison surface with two explicit tracks:

1. Same Reagent authoring language, different adapter/package: stock counter versus reagent-slim counter.
2. One substrate-free model, different view language/root: Reagent, UIx, and Hicasso login.

Link directly to the model and three thin entry points so a programmer or coding agent can compare source, not prose excerpts. Point the root catalogue at this page and reconcile the stale parity section in `examples/TESTING.md` and directly coupled login comments/READMEs.

Extend `check-login-bundle-isolation.cjs` and `test:bundle-isolation` to release and inspect the Hicasso login. Reuse the existing Hicasso sentinels and positive control: each login bundle must contain its own view runtime and exclude the other two. Keep compile coverage plus this structural proof; do not add a per-example browser suite.

## Evidence

- `examples/README.md:9,55-61` lists only UIx and reagent-slim under Substrates; `examples/substrates/README.md` does not exist.
- `examples/TESTING.md:82-118` calls two current pairs triplets and claims three login examples while naming only two login bundles.
- `examples/core/login/model.cljs:42-57,722-742` documents the substrate-free owner and shared frame config; only `examples/core/login/core.cljs` and `examples/substrates/uix/login/core.cljs` require it today.
- `implementation/scripts/check-login-bundle-isolation.cjs:3-45,85-103,179-235` explicitly implements a two-bundle Reagent/UIx proof.
- `implementation/package.json:41-42,53` releases only the two login builds for bundle isolation and exposes the existing compile and `dev:example` doors.
- `implementation/shadow-cljs.edn:1611-1644` declares the current login pair; `:examples/hicasso-counter` at lines 1950-1959 points to the tool-owned Story testbed instead of `examples/`.
- `node ../examples/scripts/serve-example.cjs --list` includes `examples/login` and `examples/login-uix` but not the tool-owned Hicasso counter. `node scripts/check-examples-compile.cjs --list` does include that tool build, demonstrating why compile inventory alone is not a human learning catalogue.
- `docs/core/hicasso/index.md:3-6` defines Hicasso as re-frame2's native view layer. `spec/006-ReactiveSubstrate.md:2130-2138` lists Hicasso's own adapter in the canonical shipped inventory.
- `implementation/hicasso/src/re_frame/hicasso.cljc:549-605` and `implementation/hicasso/src/re_frame/hicasso/impl/mount.cljs:115-155` bound `h/mount!` to the three root keys and show that it joins a frame already created through `rf/make-frame`.
- `implementation/scripts/check-bundle-isolation.cjs:300-332,742-746` already defines non-dev Hicasso sentinels (`hicassoBoundary`, `rf.error/hicasso-empty-vector`) and proves them present in a dedicated positive-control module.
- History establishes the sequence: shared login model on 2026-07-11 (`2644f42b72`), Helix removal on 2026-07-22 (`e1f38e5ddf`), Hicasso's own adapter on 2026-08-18 (`4cb9e16951`), and canonical adapter registration on 2026-08-19 (`5d1fd88c3f`). The examples never gained a human Hicasso arm after that change.
- Current tag and installation evidence says the example must stay repository-local for now: `git tag --list 'v*'` is empty and `docs/core/hicasso/00-installation.md:18-40,125` says the coordinate is unpublished and uses `:local/root`.
- Fresh open/closed title and description searches for the exact prefix, Hicasso login, login-hicasso, three-view-layer, cross-substrate, `login.model`, and `examples/substrates/hicasso` found no duplicate. The adjacent launch-command tasks `rf2-iacw2` and `rf2-ujdn0` are distinct and explicitly remain separate.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. `examples/substrates/hicasso/login/` contains a readable Hicasso entry, host page, and concise README. It imports `login.model` and contains no duplicate auth schemas, effects, machine, events, or subscriptions.
2. The Hicasso view uses native `h/defview`/`h/sub`/intent idioms and matches the Reagent/UIx pair's visible login behavior and stable test ids. Email edits remain positional; password edits still dispatch the classified `[:auth.login/edit-password {:value ...}]` shape, and submit/success/failure behavior remains owned by the shared model.
3. Boot installs `re-frame.hicasso.substrate/adapter`, constructs the frame once from `model/frame-config` so the canned HTTP effect override and initial event are honored, mounts Hicasso into that frame, and retains/re-renders one root on hot reload. No expansion or compatibility shim is added to `h/mount!`.
4. `:examples/login-hicasso` emits to the standard example output root and appears automatically in both `npm run dev:example -- --list` and `npm run test:examples-compile` inventory. Its host/shared assets are resolved by the existing staging code with no hard-coded build-to-folder entry.
5. `examples/substrates/README.md` gives the two-track comparison above and links the exact model/view/root files. `examples/README.md`, `examples/TESTING.md`, `login.model`, and the three login READMEs no longer describe deleted Helix arms or incorrect triplet counts.
6. The new README gives one truthful repository-local launch path and points greenfield setup to the Hicasso installation guide; it does not advertise an unresolved Maven version or duplicate a project template.
7. `test:bundle-isolation` releases all three login builds. The existing login checker proves own-runtime presence plus foreign-runtime absence for Reagent, UIx, and Hicasso, using a non-vacuous Hicasso positive control. The Hicasso login carries no Reagent or UIx fingerprint, and the other two carry no Hicasso fingerprint.
8. `npm run test:examples-compile`, `npm run test:bundle-isolation`, the existing example staging/runner tests, and relevant docs-link gates pass. A clean repository-local launch paints the form and exercises one validation failure plus the canned successful login; no new per-example browser gate is introduced.

## Non-goals

- No runtime view-layer switcher, multi-adapter bundle, mode flag, gallery shell, code generator, or new example manifest/framework.
- No extraction of the tiny counter registrations, sharing of view code, or conversion of every example to every view layer.
- No Hicasso variant in `tools/template`, no publication workaround, and no invented compatibility coordinate while the artifact is unpublished.
- No change to Hicasso root/adapter APIs, login business behavior, or the substrate contract.
- No promotion or relocation of the Story/Xray Hicasso counter testbed; tool testbeds remain tool-owned.
- No Hicasso SSR/Node example; `rf2-8arzr` owns that separate path.
- No sweep standardizing existing substrate README launch commands; `rf2-iacw2` and `rf2-ujdn0` own the adjacent catalogue command policy. This task only documents the new arm and follows whichever shared wording lands.
- No per-example browser-test matrix; examples stay human learning surfaces and adapter smokes stay adapter-owned.

## Related beads

- `rf2-8urba` - deferred Hicasso template variant, gated on publication; this task does not scaffold consumers.
- `rf2-8arzr` - native-Hicasso SSR/Node reference path; explicitly outside this browser example.
- `rf2-auiy5` and `rf2-hvr5h` - established Hicasso's canonical native adapter.
- Historical `rf2-ppbvav` / commit `2644f42b72` - created the shared login model and original three-view comparison.
- Historical `rf2-d6epb` / commit `e1f38e5ddf` - removed Helix and its example arms.
- `rf2-5czki` - added Hicasso Story support and the tool-owned testbed; this task supplies the intentionally separate human surface.

description: Found by rf2-skr1c (PR #8787). implementation/ssr-ring/src/re_frame/ssr/ring/pipeline.clj setup-request-frame! builds its per-request make-frame config from :id / :doc / :platform / :initial-events (+ :fx-overrides, :ssr) only — an ssr-handler user has no opt through which to declare (with-base-path history-url-strategy "/realworld") on the request frame. title: surface-review(examples-core): make every documented core run command launch a real page
description:
## Scope

Make the primary examples/core learning path genuinely one-command runnable from the instructions programmers and coding agents actually encounter. Scope is the core catalogue landing copy in examples/README.md, the seven core README carriers (counter, flows, login, managed_http_counter, notebook, todomvc, and seven_guis), and the existing npm run dev:example runner/manifest tests only as needed to pin that documented contract.

The outcome is not a new runner. The repository already has the right one. The outcome is that every default core run recipe invokes it and reaches a real page with the required host assets.

## Findings

The application code is broadly coherent and current: the 12 core builds use the reg-event / reg-sub / reg-view idiom, explicit frame scope, the init! plus lazy frame-root mount shape (with the intentional pre-created-frame exception for frame-local flows), namespaced registrations, and external headless wrappers where behavior needs coverage. test:examples-compile derives every declared :examples/* build and rejects compile errors and warnings.

The first-contact run path is the material gap. examples/README.md says any example runs with shadow-cljs watch BUILD-ID, and every core README repeats a bare shadow-cljs watch examples/... command. Those commands compile to implementation/out/examples/ID but do not stage the colocated index.html, copy _shared, copy per-example assets, or serve that output on a discoverable URL. The core builds also have no matching generic :dev-http roots. Consequently:

- opening a source index.html cannot find its relative main.js;
- opening an output directory has no host page unless the user manually copies it;
- TodoMVC additionally misses base.css and index.css from node_modules;
- managed-http-counter additionally misses api/inc.json, so its headline success request becomes a 404;
- phrases such as "open the served page" and "open index.html against the watch build" describe a page the documented command did not assemble.

This is inconsistent inside the same catalogue. The UIx READMEs already teach npm run dev:example -- examples/ID, which cleans and stages the selected output, starts the watch, serves it on a free loopback port, and prints the URL.

History explains the split. Commit a4636f853f (rf2-pdo5mx) introduced serve-example.cjs, the npm entry point, manifest derivation, staging tests, and migrated the UIx docs. The later concept reorganisation at 210f812fe2 installed the raw-watch sentence in the new catalogue/core READMEs and lost the complete staging-and-serving recipe. Subsequent runner work made the canonical path stronger, not obsolete: 1d62730eb1 added the clean-stage boundary, 8365a4f32e centralised asset exceptions, and the current staging tests explicitly pin TodoMVC CSS and managed-http-counter's JSON fixture.

## Recommended Action

Bless one default command for the core family:

    npm run dev:example -- examples/BUILD-ID

Run it from implementation/. Put one concise explanation on the catalogue landing page: it watches, stages the host/assets, serves on a free port, and prints the URL. Give each core README its exact copy-paste command; the 7GUIs README can show one command and say to substitute the other listed build ids. Use the same runner for the login Story build if it is documented as a default runnable path.

Keep raw shadow-cljs watch only in one clearly labelled advanced/manual note if it still earns a place, and state the full copy/stage/serve obligation there. Do not repeat that troubleshooting ceremony in every example.

Extend the existing listStandaloneExamples staging test just enough to pin that all 12 documented core build ids resolve to a host page. Reuse the existing runner, manifest, and script-policy lane; do not add another wrapper or a per-example browser suite.

## Evidence

- examples/README.md:11 advertises raw watch for every example.
- Bare raw-watch recipes remain in examples/core/counter/README.md:115, flows/README.md:61, login/README.md:84, managed_http_counter/README.md:50, notebook/README.md:159, todomvc/README.md:71, and seven_guis/README.md:59.
- Every core host page loads relative main.js; the build outputs are separately declared under implementation/out/examples/* in implementation/shadow-cljs.edn.
- implementation/package.json already exposes dev:example.
- examples/scripts/serve-example.cjs documents and implements clean, stage, watch, serve, and URL reporting.
- examples/scripts/examples-asset-manifest.cjs records the two core-only staging obligations: TodoMVC CSS and managed-http-counter api/inc.json.
- implementation/scripts/_examples-staging.test.cjs pins clean-before-stage, manifest projection, and those special assets, but its runnable-manifest assertion currently names only the three UIx examples.
- npm run dev:example -- --list currently returns all core ids: counter, flows, login, managed-http-counter, notebook, todomvc, temperature, flight-booker, timer, crud, circle-drawer, and cells.
- examples/TESTING.md confirms compile coverage is not a served-page smoke; examples remain test-free and behavior wrappers live outside the tree.
- Searches across open and closed bead titles/descriptions for serve-example, dev:example, core example run commands, and surface-review(examples-core) found no live duplicate.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. From implementation/, each documented core command uses npm run dev:example -- examples/ID and is copy-pasteable without an unstated copy, staging, or server step.
2. examples/README.md names that command as the default route and explains it once, tersely. Each core README points to the exact build id; all six non-counter 7GUIs ids are discoverable from its README.
3. No bare shadow-cljs watch examples/... remains in the scoped core docs as the default run recipe. Any retained raw-watch form is explicitly advanced/manual and names the missing staging and serving work.
4. The existing staging/runner test suite asserts that all 12 documented core builds appear in listStandaloneExamples() with an existing host page. The assertion has a non-vacuous failure if one core build falls out of the runner.
5. A clean run of the documented counter command serves the current page and main.js on the printed URL; minus and plus update the displayed count.
6. Existing staging tests prove TodoMVC's two CSS assets and managed-http-counter's api/inc.json land under their clean output roots. npm run test:script-policy, the relevant docs link/slug gates, and npm run dev:example -- --list pass.
7. The final change stays documentation-and-existing-runner focused; it does not introduce a second launcher or per-example browser matrix.

## Non-goals

- Rewriting the example applications, their API idioms, or their tutorial narratives.
- Adding a browser smoke for every core example or reversing the test-free-examples policy.
- Turning gallery examples into independent greenfield project templates; tools/template remains that path.
- Abstracting the intentionally visible mount code into a shared helper.
- Sweeping the individual READMEs under capabilities, patterns, real-apps, or substrates in this task, beyond correcting the shared catalogue entry.

## Related beads

- rf2-pdo5mx - introduced the one-command example runner and migrated the UIx learning path.
- rf2-rg2tze - made the runner clean the selected output before staging.
- rf2-cq6va5 / rf2-phpbo8 - pinned and centralised per-example runtime assets.
- rf2-8cevm - established the test-free examples policy; this task preserves it.
- rf2-0vav5.1 - introduced derived compile coverage for declared example builds; compile coverage remains complementary to, not a replacement for, a runnable documented page.

title: RULING: src is 71% prose - docstring = contract plus one sentence of why; the essays move to docs/design/hicasso
description:
src/ is 17,113 lines of which ~12,000 are docstrings and comments (approx: codec.cljs 67%, collector.cljs 74%, controlled.cljs 78%, hicasso.cljc 87%, mount.cljs 76%). impl/ alone: 11,693 lines = 2,788 code + 7,207 docstring + 1,219 comment (72% prose). collector.cljs opens with a 393-line docstring before its first require; controlled.cljs is 688 doc lines for 155 of code; generation.cljs 102 doc lines for 26 of code. Docstrings cross-reference three others, so editing one mechanism means re-reading the essay on all of them, and finding flush! means scrolling ~1,000 lines. This is the shape problem underneath the rest of the review: nothing is short enough to be seen whole, which is why the dead weight survived, and it is why every rename is a multi-file multi-paragraph edit. docs/design/hicasso (146 files) already exists and is where HD-numbered rulings, measurement tables and rejected alternatives belong.

RECOMMENDATION: per file, docstring = what it is/returns, the contract, and one sentence of why (with a link to the design record for the argument); move measurement tables, rejected designs and ruling citations to docs/design/hicasso. Target roughly 1:1 prose:code. Best done per file alongside the cut tasks in this epic so the prose is trimmed once, after the code it describes has settled. This reverses the direction of PR #8736 (which polished the prose in place); that PR is not wasted - the survivors will be the timeless versions - but Mike should rule before a second prose pass starts.

BANNER STRUCK 2026-08-29 15:29:24 AUSEST: ruled.

WHAT THE ADDED REVIEW SAID AND HOW IT WAS WEIGHED. After filing, the dossier gained an independent second review ("Codex Recommendation"). It concurs with A and amends it in five ways. All five are adopted, one with a bound:
(1) A content rule, not a line-count regime: no 1:1 enforcement, no 40-line cap, no docstring-link checker, no migration machinery. Adopted. The bead's "roughly 1:1 prose:code" is the expected OUTCOME of applying the rule, not a threshold a reviewer applies.
(2) Move only durable design reasoning; DELETE duplicated, superseded and journey prose rather than preserving it ceremonially. Adopted, with a bound: the dossier's own sample found about half the essay material already on a design page, so moving it would write it twice; but the PR body still names each deleted essay and where its surviving copy is, so nothing goes silently.
(3) A source comment stays only where it protects nearby code from a plausible-but-wrong edit. The epoch-floor proof beside flush! and the rf2-6c12m.19 counter-example on commit-basis are such proofs and stay; module history, benchmark narrative and repeated cross-module explanation go. Adopted.
(4) A public docstring carries the smallest complete contract a caller needs (inputs, outputs, effects, ordering, failure behaviour) plus an example only where it removes real ambiguity; a private docstring says what the var does and the one non-obvious invariant behind its shape. Adopted - it is the dossier's rule with the public/private line made explicit.
(5) One small cleanup pass over untouched files when the wave is done. Adopted as the follow-up bead.
Its lexical scan read 75.8% prose against the dossier's 72%; the methods differ on ^{:doc} metadata and comment classification, both agree the shape is about three prose lines per line of code, and the ruling does not turn on which figure is right. The one material risk it names - over-trimming caller-facing facts into the unpublished design tree - is why the public-contract clause below is stated in full rather than left to taste.

THE RULE (binding on every PR that edits a docstring or comment under implementation/hicasso/src from now on):
1. A docstring carries: (a) what the var is or returns; (b) the contract - what it takes, returns and promises, its effects, ordering and failure behaviour, in full for a public var; for a private var, what it does plus the one non-obvious invariant behind its shape; (c) one sentence of why; (d) where the argument lives, as a repo-relative path into docs/design/hicasso (docs/design/hicasso/architecture.md, docs/design/hicasso/studio/<page>.md, docs/design/hicasso/decisions.md HD-NNN). An example only where it removes real ambiguity.
2. Links are repo-relative paths, NEVER [[wikilinks]]: 892 [[...]] exist across src/ and nothing resolves them (no codox config; scripts/check_doc_slugs.py scans docs/, spec/, skills/, migration/ and tools/*/spec only - DEFAULT_ROOTS line 94; PR #8736's body says "the doc link gates do not cover source docstrings"). The worker checks each retained path exists while editing and says so in the PR body.
3. A measured figure may stay in a docstring only with its page named beside it (e.g. "2.75 vs 1.42 us/read; docs/design/hicasso/studio/the-cold-read-mount-term.md").
4. A source comment stays only where it protects nearby code from a plausible-but-wrong edit (a local correctness proof). Module history, benchmark narrative, rejected alternatives, HD-ruling derivations and explanations of OTHER namespaces' mechanisms do not.
5. A content rule, not a number: no 40-line cap, no 1:1 enforcement, no docstring-link checker, no migration script.
6. Move vs delete: durable design reasoning with no home in docs/design/hicasso is MOVED there (see WHERE CUT MATERIAL GOES in the next note); prose a design page already carries, superseded prose and change-narration is DELETED. The PR body names, per essay, the path it moved to, or "deleted - duplicated at <path>" / "deleted - superseded".
7. Untouched: retained-inventory's :what strings and the rf2:builder-bypass-ok block (as #8736 left them); impl/slot.cljc until rf2-6c12m.1 retires the freeze gate (implementation/hicasso/scripts/check_freeze.py lines 57 and 799 treat a docstring as code - a changed word reds - for pinned rows, of which slot.cljc is the last).

MEASUREMENTS (scratchpad prose.py against implementation/hicasso/src at HEAD d5a73b28c3; a prose line is one inside a string literal directly following (ns ..., (def... name or (defmacro name, or whose first non-blank character is ';'; the scan misses ^{:doc} metadata docstrings, of which hicasso.cljc has 13, so that file reads 64% here where the bead's 87% is nearer right; everything else agrees with the bead):
- src/ (28 files): 17,085 lines = 10,254 docstring + 1,568 comment + 4,514 code; 72% prose
- impl/ (18 files): 12,474 = 7,499 + 1,285 + 3,174; 73%
- impl/codec.cljs: 3,940 = 2,111 + 570 + 1,085; 71%
- impl/collector.cljs: 2,168 = 1,315 + 298 + 477; 77%
- impl/controlled.cljs: 886 = 678 + 18 + 164; 81%
- impl/mount.cljs: 639 = 436 + 53 + 127; 79%
- impl/generation.cljs: 135 = 102 + 0 + 25; 80%
- 451 docstrings: median 10 lines; 137 at 5 lines or fewer (the bulk already meets the rule); 91 over 30 lines; 17 over 100; 4 over 200
- the 5 longest: collector ns 392 lines, controlled ns 328, intent ns 248, server ns 211, codec ns 198; then native ns 188, overlay ns 187, boundary ns 167, defhost 156, defview 153, forms ns 135, mint-view! 129
- collector.cljs opens with the 392-line ns docstring before its first :require; rstate is at line 427 and flush! at 994
- flush! (9 lines) and with-commit (4 lines) already read as the rule asks; commit-basis (58 lines at HEAD, about 80 once PR #8745 lands) and cold-read! (59 lines) do not

WHAT THE PROSE IS (descending volume): design reasoning (why the shell is 2 hooks, why the commit basis has 3 terms, why the memo is per read); measurement (probe 2.75 vs probe-fresh 1.42 us/read, "4 ms is the SHORTEST delay measured", a Chromium epoch-tie trace inside flush!); rejected alternatives (UIx's 3-hook input wrapper, a run-shared memo, useRef in the shell); cross-references (892 [[wikilinks]], HD-numbered rulings, studio pages, test namespaces).

COSTS THAT DECIDED IT: finding a function means paging past essays; editing one mechanism means re-reading essays on three (the collector, generation and intent docstrings each explain the other two); every rename is a multi-paragraph edit (#8736 needed 27 files, +577/-565, to change vocabulary alone); worker context - codec.cljs and collector.cljs together are about 6,100 lines, roughly 75,000 tokens at 12 tokens a line, before a worker opens a test; the prose half of every diff is the half reviewers cannot check mechanically; the review behind this epic judged "nothing is short enough to be seen whole, which is why the dead weight survived".

BENEFITS, FAIRLY, AND THE AI-FIRST TENSION: the whys are real and many are measured against a named test; an AI pair reading cold-read! learns in one place why the memo is per read and what changing it would cost. No repo convention sets a docstring rule (spec/Principles.md, spec/Conventions.md, CLAUDE.md, AGENTS.md); Principles.md "Low hidden context" favours discoverable reasoning, Conventions.md "annotation is not removal" says a docstring is not where a disposition lives; neither settles it. The tension with the AI-first principle is about PLACEMENT, not existence: an AI pair benefits from context it can reach by a path; it does not benefit from 1,000 lines between a function and its caller, because that is context budget spent before the caller is in view. The rule keeps the reasoning reachable - one path, one authoritative copy - and takes it out of the read path.
RULING rf2-6c12m.4, part 2 of 2 (2026-08-29 15:29:24 AUSEST) - worked examples, destinations, sequencing, acceptance.

WORKED EXAMPLES - the model for every trimming worker (copy the shape, not the words):

A) Namespace docstring - impl/collector.cljs, 392 lines. Current opening:
(ns re-frame.hicasso.impl.collector
  "HICASSO - THE COLLECTOR. The runtime's heart.
  A boundary is a real React function component minted by `defview` ...
  ## The five siblings, and why the grouping is what it is
  | module | what it owns | ...
  ## The shell, and the <=2-hook budget (HD-020)
  ... (386 more lines)
Trimmed to the rule:
(ns re-frame.hicasso.impl.collector
  "The collector: which boundaries a commit must re-run, how a body reaches
  subscription values, and the generation fence that keeps one render pass
  on one commit. React owns everything else about a boundary.

  Owns the render context, the cell table, the commit window (`with-commit`,
  `flush!`), the two read tiers, the read-set entry cache, and the shell and
  mint doors. Those form one dependency cycle, which is why they share a
  namespace; `generation`, `frames`, `roots`, `evidence` and `inventory`
  each hold a one-directional edge out of it.

  2-hook shell, HD-002, HD-020); measurements in docs/design/hicasso/studio/."

That counter-example is a local correctness proof and SURVIVES as the one-sentence why. Trimmed:
(defn commit-basis
  "The number a staged read is judged against: this runtime's flush
  generation + the frame's install epoch (`frame/frame-commit-epoch`) +
  the registry epoch. Monotone within a frame incarnation; install-counting,
  so a value-equal install still advances it (one redundant re-render at
  worst, never a missed one). Pure; allocates nothing.

  Three terms because each sees a movement the other two cannot: the
  generation moves only through a committed cell's watch, the install
  epoch is a plain counter, and only the registry term carries a `reg-sub`
  landing in the render->commit gap. The generation term is load-bearing
  across a same-id reincarnation, where the frame term restarts and can
  tie: any other cell the frame holds is rewired by microtask and that
  flush bumps the generation (staged_reincarnation_basis_cljs_test); a
  frame holding no other cell ties either way, which is Spec 006
  invariant 5's `:node-key` axis, not this number's. Full argument:
  docs/design/hicasso/architecture.md, section The commit basis."
  [frame-kw]
  (+ @!generation (frame/frame-commit-epoch frame-kw) @!registry-epoch))
(The trimming worker WRITES that architecture.md section first - it has no home today; see below.)

C) Private function with a measurement essay - impl/collector.cljs cold-read!, 59 lines. Trimmed:
(defn- cold-read!
  "Read a key no committed cell answers for. Reuses a live sub-cache
  reaction when one exists; otherwise computes pure against one
  frame-state snapshot per body run (the probe on `rstate`), memoised per
  run so a repeated key is a `find`; falls back to `subscribe-once` when
  the frame is missing or destroyed. Runs inside
  `call-with-frame-resolution` so a `reg-sub` from earlier in the tick is
  visible. The memo is per read, not run-shared, because the shared one
  cost more than it saved on the acceptance shape (2.75 vs 1.42 us/read;
  docs/design/hicasso/studio/the-cold-read-mount-term.md)."

WHERE CUT MATERIAL GOES (so workers do not each invent a place). docs/design/hicasso has 146 files in 3 sub-trees. Measurement tables and traces -> studio/ (73 files, "the programme's measured record"). Rulings, rejected alternatives and HD derivations -> decisions.md (2,984 lines, HD-001 to HD-029). - collector.cljs "<=2-hook budget (HD-020)" -> decisions.md line 1357 and architecture.md lines 96 and 196 carry the rule and "never useRef in the shell"; the docstring's 35-line derivation of why no per-instance state is needed is longer than either. PARTLY duplicated: the derivation needs a home in architecture.md, the rest is deleted.

- cold-read!'s figures (probe-fresh, read_profile) appear on 7 design pages including studio/the-cold-read-mount-term.md: delete from source, cite the page.
- The commit-basis argument has NO home: neither architecture.md nor decisions.md mentions the commit basis (grep "commit basis": 0). The worker trimming generation.cljs writes architecture.md section "The commit basis" BEFORE cutting the docstring: the three terms and what each sees; why the registry term lives in the basis and nowhere else (only a staged key reads the basis live, a held key contributes its cell's frozen stamp, so an unrelated reg-sub moves a mounted boundary by zero - a-first-registration-of-an-id-no-cell-holds-disturbs-nothing); install-counting rather than =-counting; the same-id reincarnation tie and the :node-key axis; the rf2-6c12m.19 counter-example (staged_reincarnation_basis_cljs_test, PR #8745).

description:
REQUESTED BY MIKE 2026-08-29 09:57 AUSEST, in chat, verbatim ask: "do a review of hicasso, improving test coverage and quality."

WHAT THIS IS. A review of implementation/hicasso/'s test suite against its actual surfaces, with two deliverables: (1) a findings review of where coverage is thin, weak, or low-quality relative to what the code does; (2) landed improvements for the clear cases, and follow-on beads (filed one at a time, ids appended to this bead's notes) for anything larger, riskier, or needing a ruling.

WHERE TO LOOK. Source surfaces: implementation/hicasso/src/re_frame/hicasso/ — evidence.cljs, forms.cljs, motion.cljs, native.cljc, overlay.cljs, server.cljs, substrate.cljs, tool.cljs, and the impl/ tree. Existing tests: implementation/hicasso/test/re_frame/hicasso/ (40+ files: *_cljs_test, *_dom_cljs_test, *_ssr_* variants), plus test_kit/ and testbed/. Map each source module to the tests that exercise it and find the gaps — surfaces with no adversarial or negative case, behaviours only exercised through the happy path, error/complaint shapes never asserted, SSR/DOM parity holes.

QUALITY BAR, from the method and the stance. A coverage or rigour pass must add at least one adversarial or negative case per surface it strengthens — assertion-count growth alone only exercises the happy path. Quality also means the tests themselves: actionable failure output, no tautological assertions, no tests that pin incidental strings where they should pin behaviour (this repo has a measured history of hollow phrase-matcher guards — see rf2-2iaph/rf2-oflj7 for the shape; do NOT touch those files, see fences). Prefer strengthening a weak existing test over adding a near-duplicate.

GATES. npm run test:cljs (substrate contract), test:hicasso-compile, test:hicasso-invariants, test:hicasso-lint, test:hicasso-controlled, test:hicasso-hmr — all from implementation/. Browser/Chromium gates are heavyweight: run them sequentially, never two at once.

WHAT COUNTS AS DONE. The module-to-test gap map is reported (findings doc in ai/findings/, never committed); clear test improvements merged green via PR with a ## Quality gates section; follow-on beads filed for the remainder with this bead named as owner; the delta between what this bead claims and what the tree holds at dispatch time is reported.

WHAT NOT TO TOUCH.
- implementation/hicasso/test/re_frame/bench/** and alloc_null_floor.cjs anywhere: held under rf2-t78z / rf2-oflj7 / rf2-fc7w awaiting Mike's rulings. Read them if useful; edit nothing.

- Hot-zone files: spec/*, top-level implementation/deps.edn, implementation/shadow-cljs.edn, .github/workflows/*.
- examples/ is test-free by lock (rf2-8cevm): no specs under examples/, ever.
- Testbeds must stay idiomatic re-frame2 (app-db + events + subs); no deliberate bugs or teaching layers.

POSTURE. Pre-alpha masterpiece: elegance, clarity, correctness, good practice. Trust the programmer. No over-engineering, no gold-plating, no nag-diagnostics, no test-count inflation. Reject a finding rather than action minutiae; a short list of sourced, load-bearing improvements beats a long plausible one.

title: hicasso: alloc_null_floor.cjs's section E says 'the clean prefix is three rounds long' where its own table four lines above reads round 2 at 12.3%, and it was two rounds on the 242-cell corpus too
description:
FOUND BY THE POST-REPAIR SWEEP rf2-oflj7's remainder asked for, MEASURED 2026-08-21 at
worker/nullfloor-oflj7. NOT one of rf2-oflj7's seven, and NOT stale-by-fold-in: unlike every
claim on that bead, this one appears to have been WRONG WHEN WRITTEN.

THE CLAIM. Section E, four lines below the round-index table it summarises:

  The clean prefix is three rounds long and `warmups` is 3 in every run. THIS READER HAS NOT
  TESTED WHETHER THOSE ARE THE SAME THREE, and proposes no mechanism for the structure.

WHAT THE SAME RUN PRINTS, four lines above it — rounds carrying mode-2 cells:

  round 0 : 0/22   0.0%
  round 1 : 0/63   0.0%
  round 2 : 7/57  12.3%

So the clean prefix is TWO rounds long, not three. The reader's OWN preceding sentence in the
same section says so in as many words: 'round 0 alone, heavily decimated by certification :
0/22 (0.0%)' sits directly above, and the file's header comment (line ~110) states 'Rounds 0
and 1 carry NONE AT ALL'. Three statements in one file, two of them derived, disagreeing with
the third, which is typed.

AND IT WAS NOT THE PHASE-4 FOLD-IN. On the 242-cell corpus the same table read round 0 at
0.0%, round 1 at 0.0% and round 2 at 6.7% (2 of 30) — the frozen studio page
docs/design/hicasso/studio/the-floor-is-two-populations.md prints exactly those rows at its
section E, and its own prose two lines above the claim says 'Rounds 0 and 1 carry none at
all'. The prefix was two rounds long then as well. This is a published error rather than a
figure the corpus moved out from under.

'CLEAN PREFIX' HAS NO OTHER DEFINITION IN THE REPO. git grep -F 'clean prefix' returns three
hits and they are this one sentence in its three copies (the .cjs header comment, the .cjs
report line, the studio page). The sentence's own follow-on — 'whether those are the SAME
THREE' — pairs it with 'warmups is 3', so 'clean prefix' can only mean the leading rounds
carrying no mode-2 cell. Control: git grep -lF 'warmups' returns 189 files, so the pattern
reaches this corpus and the three is a reading.

THE GUARD IS THE HOLLOW SHAPE THIS FAMILY OF BEADS IS ABOUT. The only check on the sentence is

  ck('the report proposes no mechanism for the round structure',
     /THIS READER HAS NOT\n;; {3}TESTED WHETHER THOSE ARE THE SAME THREE/.test(rep), true);

which asks whether a DIFFERENT CLAUSE of the same sentence is present. It passes whatever the
count says, and has done since the sentence was written.

WHY THIS IS A RULING AND NOT A WORKER'S FIX, which is why it was left rather than folded into
rf2-oflj7's PR. The number is load-bearing on the reader's conclusion: 'three' is what makes
the sentence a COINCIDENCE WORTH NOT EXPLAINING ('warmups is 3 ... has not tested whether
those are the same three'). Correcting it to two dissolves the pairing, and the reader then
either says nothing about warmups or says something new about a two-round prefix against a
three-round warmup — which is a claim about MECHANISM, and this reader's standing position is
that it proposes none. Same class as rf2-oflj7's items 5 and 6.

NOT VERIFIED HERE: whether 'warmups is 3 in every run' holds over the 16 runs. It is unguarded
too — no check reads it — but it was out of the sweep's scope.

THE FROZEN PAGE. docs/design/hicasso/studio/the-floor-is-two-populations.md carries the same
sentence at its section E. That page is explicitly frozen at its 242-cell state by its own
banner ('left exactly as it was published'), so whether a published error inside a frozen
record is corrected in place or annotated is part of the same ruling.
notes:
MAYOR — THE ONE THING THIS BEAD RECORDED AS 'NOT VERIFIED HERE' IS NOW MEASURED, and it changes the shape of the ruling rather than merely filling a gap. 2026-08-22 02:3x AUSEST, tip 86702f3ed7.

THE BEAD SAID: 'NOT VERIFIED HERE: whether warmups is 3 in every run. It is unguarded too — no check reads it — but it was out of the sweep's scope.'

MEASURED NOW, by reading the sixteen committed run files the reader's own CORPORA table names (alloc_null_floor.cjs:165-215): alloc-0gjqi/paired-run{1,2}, alloc-fk6pj/seeded-run{1,2}, alloc-legorder/run{1..8}, alloc-passterm/run{1..4}.

  RESULT: warmups = 3 in ALL SIXTEEN. Uniform, no exceptions.

CONTROLLED IN BOTH DIRECTIONS, because a recursive key search returning one constant across sixteen files is exactly the shape a broken search also produces. Asked for a key that does not exist -> ABSENT. Asked for 'samples' on the same files -> sixteen distinct varying arrays. So the finder discriminates and the uniform 3 is a reading, not an artefact.

*** WHAT THIS DOES TO THE RULING. *** The bead's reasoning for calling this Mike's rather than a worker's was that 'three' makes the sentence A COINCIDENCE WORTH NOT EXPLAINING — 'warmups is 3 ... has not tested whether those are the same three' — so correcting the prefix to two DISSOLVES THE PAIRING and forces the reader to say something new about mechanism.

Measured, the sentence carries EXACTLY ONE falsehood and not two: warmups really is 3 everywhere; the clean prefix really is 2. So the pairing the sentence declines to explain DOES NOT EXIST — the two numbers are simply different.

THAT OPENS AN ARM THE BEAD COULD NOT SEE BEFORE THE MEASUREMENT. The reader can state both derived quantities and record that they are NOT the same number. That proposes NO mechanism — it is two counts, differing — which is precisely this reader's standing position rather than a departure from it. The dilemma as written ('say nothing about warmups, or say something new about mechanism') had no third arm; now it has one, and the third arm preserves the position the first two were trying to protect.

I AM NOT RULING IT, and the reasons the bead gives for it being Mike's are not all dissolved: the frozen studio page docs/design/hicasso/studio/the-floor-is-two-populations.md carries the same sentence under an explicit 'left exactly as it was published' banner, and whether a published error inside a frozen record is corrected in place or annotated is a question about the record, not about the number. That half is untouched by this measurement and stays Mike's.

WHAT I DID NOT DO: I did not run the reader, and I did not re-derive the round-index table's 0.0 / 0.0 / 12.3 figures — this bead already measured those at worker/nullfloor-oflj7 and I took them as given rather than re-deriving. Only the warmups half is mine.
*** AWAITING MIKE — NOT DISPATCHABLE. This bead is its OWN operator call, not one waiting on
rf2-oflj7's. ***

elsewhere, plus a banner. Nothing about the finding itself changes.

say "rf2-t78z is blocked behind rf2-oflj7's ruling", and I repeated that in status reports. The

  "warmups is 3", leaving the reader either silent about warmups or making a NEW claim about
  mechanism — and this reader's standing position is that it proposes none. No third arm.

  THE MEASUREMENT (warmups = 3 in all sixteen committed runs, controlled in both directions)
  SUPPLIED A THIRD ARM: state both derived quantities and record that they are NOT the same
  number. Two counts, differing, no mechanism proposed — which PRESERVES the reader's standing

  So the sentence carries EXACTLY ONE falsehood, not two. The coincidence it declines to explain

WHAT GENUINELY REMAINS MIKE'S, and it is one question rather than the two the description implies:
the same sentence exists in three copies, and one of them is the frozen studio page
docs/design/hicasso/studio/the-floor-is-two-populations.md, carried under an explicit "left exactly
as it was published" banner. Whether a published error inside a frozen record is corrected in place

creates a divergence between the record and the reader — which is the very question being reserved.
The split would decide the reserved question by acting rather than by ruling.

COST OF THE HOLD, priced against a want rather than counted: nothing is queued behind this bead —
no dependants, no edges out. What it costs is that a reader in the tree keeps printing a derived
number that its own table four lines above contradicts, and the only guard on the sentence tests a
DIFFERENT CLAUSE of it, so nothing will ever catch it. That is a live, un-gated falsehood in a

BACKLOG REREAD 2026-08-24 08:12 AUSEST, tip 0bc818e78e. ONE PREMISE ON THIS BEAD IS FALSE. The
conclusion it supports is CORRECT and unchanged; only the evidence for it was wrong.

CORRECTION 1 ABOVE SAYS: "The edge between them is type DISCOVERED-FROM, which is provenance and
carries no force: this bead's dependency_count is 0 and it does not appear in the blocked list."

MEASURED AT SOURCE THIS PASS: this bead's dependency_count is 1, not 0. The single dependency is
rf2-oflj7 with dependency_type "discovered-from". So the count does NOT exclude provenance edges --
it counts them.

WHY THE CONCLUSION SURVIVES ANYWAY, and by a better route: the discriminator is the edge TYPE and
the blocked list, not the count. `bd blocked` at this tip lists exactly two beads -- rf2-hic-064 and
rf2-hic-063 -- and this bead is not one of them. This bead is in `bd ready`. Both measured, not
inferred. So it is genuinely not blocked behind rf2-oflj7, exactly as Correction 1 concluded.

THE GENERAL RULE, because this premise is not local to this bead. dependency_count counts EVERY
dependency record regardless of type, so it is not a test for "blocked". Two beads carry the false
version: rf2-fo4ng states it as a general rule ("a discovered-from edge leaves dependency_count at
0"), and rf2-oflj7 quotes this bead's sentence verbatim. Both reach correct conclusions by other
means; the shared premise is what is wrong.

USE INSTEAD: the dependency_type field for one bead, or `bd blocked` for the board. A count of 0
does prove not-blocked; a count above 0 proves nothing either way.

NOTHING ABOUT THE FINDING OR THE HOLD CHANGES. This bead is still its OWN operator call, still not
downstream of rf2-oflj7's items 5 and 6, and still AWAITING MIKE - NOT DISPATCHABLE.

title: [method] workers open PRs before they are done and the mayor merges them green — use draft PRs as the interlock
description:
THE MERGE LOOP AND THE DISPATCH BRIEF CONTRADICT EACH OTHER, AND THE MAYOR IS THE ONE WHO WROTE BOTH. Twice in one session a PR was merged while its author was still working on it.

THE TWO RULES, both of them mine, both individually right:
  DISPATCH BRIEF: "PUSH AS YOU GO, not at the end — pushed commits are the only durable worker state ... OPEN THE PR as soon as commits exist; a PR is not a claim of green."
  MERGE LOOP: merge on the five-clause criterion the moment it is met, and never block on CI.

Put together they say: workers publish PRs before they are finished, and the mayor merges them the moment CI goes green. **The gap between "CI is green" and "the author is done" is where both incidents happened.**

INCIDENT 1, 2026-08-15 ~11:55. #8323 merged while worker/hicaudit-5zmul was live. GitHub's delete_branch_on_merge removed its branch server-side; the worker's next push recreated it against a main that already carried its commits, producing DUPLICATE PR #8325 with a byte-identical three-file diff. Closed by hand after verifying the duplication rather than assuming it.

INCIDENT 2, 2026-08-16 ~01:33. #8333 merged while worker/w-lane-est was still running gates. Its own words: "#8333 — MERGED by the mayor while gates were still running; full gate table posted as a comment on it." It recovered well — cherry-picked the one wording fix the merge had not carried onto current main as #8339, and re-ran the doc gates on that branch — but that is a whole extra PR and an extra review cycle for work that would have ridden the first one.

NEITHER MERGE VIOLATED THE CRITERION. Both PRs were genuinely green on all five clauses when merged. The criterion is not the defect; the missing coordination is.

*** THE FIX, and it uses a mechanism that already exists rather than inventing a rule to remember. *** Brief workers to open the PR as a DRAFT and mark it ready for review as their last act before reporting done. `gh pr merge` REFUSES a draft, so the interlock is enforced by the host rather than by anyone's memory — which is the property the stash ban and the beads-boundary hook both have and the reason they hold. It preserves everything the push-as-you-go rule buys: commits are still pushed continuously and still survive a worker's death, and the mayor can still read the diff and the gate output at any time.

WHAT TO CHANGE:
  - docs/the-mayor-method/dispatch-prompt-template.md — the push-as-you-go clause gains "open it as a DRAFT; mark it ready as your last act before reporting done."
  - docs/the-mayor-method/loops.md section 1 — the merge criterion gains a line noting a draft PR is not a merge candidate, and WHY: the five clauses test the CHANGE, not whether its author has finished with it.
  - .claude/commands/mayor-merge.md — the same line, concretely: skip drafts in the sweep.

THE ALTERNATIVE, rejected: have the mayor check worker liveness before every merge. It works, but it is a rule that must be remembered on every merge forever, and it re-introduces exactly the worktree-activity sweep the merge loop deliberately does not do. The draft flag costs one command at the end of a worker's run and cannot be forgotten by the mayor at all.

SCOPE FENCE: those three files. HOT ZONE method surface — SOLE TOUCHER, never parallel with another method-file bead. Note rf2-4228y also targets loops.md; SEQUENCE the two, do not run them together.

GATE: python scripts/check_doc_slugs.py plus mkdocs build --strict, which DOES cover docs/the-mayor-method/. Run mkdocs as `python -m mkdocs` — bare `mkdocs` returns exit 127 in Git Bash on this box because it is not on PATH, and 127 is NO VERDICT, not a pass. No fenced code blocks added, so the guide-samples digest gate is untouched; say so in the PR body.
notes:
AUDIT PR #8944: REOPENED exact draft-interlock owner; no duplicate. Completeness: the new finished-draft exception landed only in loops.md. dispatch-prompt-template.md's canonical Publishing the change section still says never flip the flag on an inference, permits only the agent's report or an operator stop, and says that until one arrives the finished change waits stranded. loops.md now gives the opposite executable instruction when the worker's tracker items are closed: verify, publish, and retire. Correctness: the added block also says the earlier third-local-gate worker separates cleanly because it had not reached close, then seven lines later says that same third-gate worker would present with closed items. That contradiction makes the claimed discriminator unclear. Implementation quality: this restores the two-source drift the draft interlock was created to prevent. Minimal completion: state one rule consistently in both method pages (and any surviving concrete merge command); if closed tracker records are the new positive signal, define the required ownership/all-items-closed check in both and preserve the full section-1 merge verification. Replace the contradictory third-gate reference with the actual residual case—an author who closed, then discovered further work. No new liveness system or broader rewrite.
MAYOR, 2026-09-01: PR #8949 opened to answer this audit. Both findings accepted as stated; neither is disputed.

The repair REMOVES what PR #8944 added rather than extending it. #8944 invented 'closed tracker items' as a new positive signal licensing the mayor to set the publish flag. That was unnecessary - dispatch-prompt-template.md already carried a sufficient authorisation, 'the operator's decision to stop that agent, which settles liveness by making it false'. loops.md now routes to that instead, so there is one rule, stated on the template page and deferred to from the loop page. The self-contradiction the audit names (third-gate worker 'separates cleanly' vs 'would present this way too') disappears with the discriminator it belonged to.

What both pages gain is the ORDER, which is where the real error was and which neither page stated: STOP, THEN MERGE. Merging first and stopping second reaches the same end state by the forbidden route, and leaves an identical record afterwards - a merged change beside a stopped agent - so nothing later can tell the two apart. That is why the rule is 'stop, then merge' rather than 'make sure the agent ends up stopped'.

Residual risk restated as the audit asked, and re-attributed: an author who closed its items and then found further work presents identically, and the act that can destroy unpushed work is the STOP, not the merge. Bounded by merging the published head CI graded.

The bead's third file, .claude/commands/mayor-merge.md, no longer exists - that directory has been removed. Nothing to change there; the bead's WHAT TO CHANGE list is stale in that one respect.

title: The beads truncation guard lives only in beads-checkpoint.sh, and the path that actually empties the export does not go through it — second recurrence
description:
Found on the 2026-07-26 method reread, after an empty export reached main earlier the same day.

THE GUARD IS SOUND AND IT WORKS. scripts/beads-checkpoint.sh refuses an empty export outright and refuses any export below 90% of HEAD (line 236: export_rows * 10 < head_rows * 9). It re-exports from Dolt rather than trusting the working file, so a reverted or mid-write file is unreachable. Nothing about it needs changing.

THE PROBLEM IS THAT THE FAILING PATH DOES NOT USE IT. Commit 4d8042d80d — "chore(beads): audit merged PR #7063" — committed .beads/issues.jsonl at ZERO ROWS, a single commit deleting 2573 lines. It was made with a plain git add, not through the checkpoint script, so the floor never ran. Working tree, index and HEAD were all empty afterwards and git status was CLEAN — nothing on screen said anything was wrong.

AND THIS IS A RECURRENCE, NOT A FIRST. The checkpoint script own comment records it: "A git add that catches the JSONL mid-rewrite has landed an empty export on main before (incident 2026-06-10, commit 7aea52459)." Six weeks apart, same mechanism, and the mitigation written after the first incident did not cover the path that caused the second.

THE SHAPE IS THE ONE THIS REPO KEEPS FINDING: sound machinery, and the case it exists to catch arrives by a route it cannot see. Five-plus instances this week — a bijection gate green on all seven planted defects, a conformance projector that had never run over a real record, a checker that accepted a FILE as its scan directory and greened over zero, a CHECK C that could collapse its own population to nothing, and this.

THE FIX, and it should be cheap: PUT THE ROW FLOOR IN THE PRE-COMMIT HOOK, where it protects EVERY path rather than the one that already knows about it. scripts/git-hooks/lib/check-beads-boundary.sh already inspects staged .beads paths — it enforces WHO may commit them (workers may not) but says nothing about CONTENT. Adding "if .beads/issues.jsonl is staged and its row count is 0, or below 90% of HEAD, refuse" reuses the checkpoint script own thresholds in the one place no committer can bypass.

TWO THINGS TO GET RIGHT:
  1. THE HOOK MUST NOT BLOCK A GENUINE MASS DELETE. The checkpoint script answer is "refuse and say so; a genuine mass delete is rare enough to commit by hand" — mirror that, with the escape named in the message.
  2. IT MUST WORK FOR THE AUDIT PROCESS TOO. Hooks live in the primary checkout hooks directory and worktrees share it, but confirm the audit committer actually has hooks installed — scripts/install-git-hooks.sh --check reports whether a checkout is guarded. A hook nobody installed is the same blindness one layer down.

RECOVERY IS NOT PART OF THIS BEAD AND IS ALREADY DONE: the Dolt database was never at risk, bd list worked throughout, and beads-checkpoint.sh regenerated 2576 rows over a HEAD of 0. Record that an empty export is a REGENERATION event, not a data-loss one — restoring an older export from git history would time-travel the tracker, reopening closed beads and vanishing new ones.
notes:

THE CRUX, and the reason the fix could not just be folded into check_beads_boundary: that classifier is gated by `rf2_beads_in_primary_worktree`, so it deliberately no-ops in the MAYOR checkout — which is exactly where 4d8042d80d and 7aea52459 were both made. The new block runs in EVERY worktree, primary included, with no marker file and no worktree derivation.

ONE CONDITION, the same arithmetic as beads-checkpoint.sh:236 (`staged*10 < head*9`), guarded by `head_rows > 0`. With HEAD non-empty a staged 0 is just the extreme of the same shrink, so there is one floor and one spelling of it; only the message branches on the count.

ITEM 2 ANSWERED: `sh scripts/install-git-hooks.sh --check` in the mayor checkout exits 0 — that checkout WAS guarded and current when the empty export landed. So the blindness was not a missing install; it was a hook with no opinion about content. Landing this makes every installed checkout stale by one block, which the existing rf2-zt65l post-merge/post-rewrite advisory reports on the next pull.

ITEM 1 ANSWERED: a genuine mass delete is refused and the message names `git commit --no-verify` (after `bd status`), mirroring the checkpoint script's own "rare enough to commit by hand".

THE RULE IS IN THE MESSAGE: an empty export is a REGENERATION event, not a data-loss one; restoring an older export from git history would TIME-TRAVEL the tracker.

Filed from the senior-developer review wave over Xray (epic rf2-y8doi, tree reviewed at trunk 9555881fe3, 2026-09-17), item C18 of the triage shortlist. Mike's instruction for the wave: "Have an agent with a senior developer persona review the xray codebase. Create beads for any actionable insights. Ensure that the spec is up to date."

## Project stance (verbatim, from CLAUDE.md; paste it into any dispatch preamble unchanged)

> Posture is that we are pre-alpha and focused on elegance, power and a masterpiece.
> But we are not over-engineering or gold plating. Also, we trust the programmer.
> We're trying to facilitate high productivity for them (and the AI they use) via a
> library with excellent ergonomics and low friction. We don't need to litigate every
> last fine detail and drown in the minutiae.

Mike's restatement for this wave (2026-09-17): "The posture is that we are pre-alpha and focused on elegance, power and a masterpiece. But we are not over-engineering or gold plating. Also, we trust the programmer. We're trying to facilitate high productivity for them (and the AI they use) via a minimal, ergonomic API and excellent tools, and low friction. For each review, remember that we don't want to over-engineer. We just want to create a library which has excellent ergonomics for creating SPAs. We don't need to litigate every last, fine detail and drown in the minutiae."

## The item, verbatim from the triage shortlist

### C18. LIVE / RETRO / paused: nothing in the Dynamic chrome says which one you are in  [size: L] [from: rf2-y8doi.5#3, .5#9, .5#10]

- Why it matters: the spine has three states the user must know to read any panel and the only visible difference is whether `»` is disabled — the mode pill (rf2-g9pee) and the head-row pulse/gutter cues (rf2-pjjwh) were each removed on the assumption the other carried the signal; 007:158-163/:489/:1180-1191, 018:107/:249-257/:1132-1133 and DR Lock #14 all describe cues the code no longer paints (`stale?|pulse|"LIVE"|"RETRO"` in shell.cljs: one comment; `event_status_colour.cljc:312-316` still computes `:stale?`/`:paused?`/`:mode` per row and nothing turns them into a class); the Static surface still paints the violet stripe the Dynamic one retired.
- What to do: decide — A: re-add ONE cheap cue — a `data-rf-xray-mode` attribute on the L2 `<ul>` plus a 2 px left rule colour (violet LIVE / cyan RETRO / grey paused) — and rewrite 007/018/DR to that; a morning. B: keep the chrome bare, strike the three spec passages, and drop the Static stripe (static/shell.cljs:322) for symmetry; spec-only. L because Mike removed both prior cues himself. Whichever way: delete `default-tab :event` (.5#9 — dead, names a tab no `reg-l4-tab!` registers) and the five stale root-swap docstrings (.5#10: shell.cljs:1427-1430, :2365-2366, :2907-2913, :3137-3144; resize_handle.cljs:137-139) in the same PR, since this is the only item touching shell.cljs on purpose.
- Files (fence): tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/shell.cljs, tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/static/shell.cljs, tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/resize_handle.cljs (docstring), tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/theme/global_styles.cljs (A only), tools/xray/test/day8/re_frame2_xray/shell_cljs_test.cljs (per .5's roster)
- Tests: A — node lane: `event-list-tree` renders `data-rf-xray-mode="live"` following head, `"retro"` after a row click, `"paused"` after Space. B — none (spec).
- Gates: node lane; browser lane for the shell DOM suites; clj-kondo.
- Re-verified: no — .5's grep with `No events.`/`focused?` as controls is enough.
- Collides with: C4 (shell.cljs:2305), C17 (shell.cljs:3202), C12 (theme/global_styles.cljs under A) — sequence after C4; order against C17/C12 as ruled.

## RULED 2026-09-17 (delegated to a decision agent by Mike): option C, amended — DISPATCHABLE

Build the sticky `↓ N newer events — » to follow` L2 marker that 018-Event-Spine.md:485-491 already specifies, with presence and N derived from the SPINE (the `:head?` predicate `compose-focus` computes), never from the filtered list; drop the Static ribbon stripe; delete the dead `default-tab`; fix the stale docstrings and the skill page. The A/B options in the item above are SUPERSEDED. The IMPLEMENTATION BRIEF note on this bead is the worker's spec (fence, RED tests, gates, what not to do); the RULING and DOSSIER notes carry the reasons and the four recovered historical close reasons (those beads are absent from the live tracker). The "sequence after C4" hold below is discharged: rf2-y8doi.16 merged as PR #9934.

## Source reports (the full evidence: path:line cites, controls, what was run)

- rf2-y8doi.5 (shell-spine): read the description FIELD, never the rendering: bd show rf2-y8doi.5 --json | jq -r '.[0].description'
The triage shortlist itself (every item, the dismissals, the reviewer disagreements) is recorded in full on the epic rf2-y8doi's notes.

## Worker rules

- Every line number above was read at trunk 9555881fe3 on 2026-09-17. Re-verify at the current trunk before editing; this tree churns (about 325 commits touched tools/xray in the prior 30 days).
- The FENCE is the "Files (fence)" line above, spelled as full repo-relative paths. Edit nothing outside it. If the fix genuinely needs another file, say so in the PR body and name it, so the mayor can sequence against any bead sharing it. Seven basenames under tools/xray/src are duplicated (browse_list, events, panel, persistence, shell, subs, view), so never refer to a file by basename anywhere in the PR or the bead.
- Run sh scripts/assert-worker-worktree.sh from your worktree before editing and report WORKTREE_ROOT. Worker branches carry code, spec, docs and tests: never .beads/issues.jsonl or .beads/metadata.json.
- Gates for tools/xray/src: the item's Tests and Gates lines above name the lane. DOM tests (*-dom-cljs-test) run in implementation/'s :browser-test build; node tests (*cljs-test) in :node-test via npm run test:cljs from implementation/; JVM-runnable .cljc tests via clojure -M:test from tools/xray; clj-kondo on changed files. A namespace whose suffix matches no build runs nowhere (rf2-y8doi.10 measured the census at zero orphans; keep it so).
- Write the RED test first where the item names one; the machines, static-catalogue and boot reports each found an existing test pinning a shape the runtime never produces, so derive fixtures from the producer rather than by hand (rf2-y8doi.10 finding 1 is the model).
- No AI attribution trailers in commits or PR bodies (CLAUDE.md § Git Conventions overrides the harness reminder; say so in the report).
- Close this bead with a reason that states what changed, what was verified by which gate, and which sub-items were found to need no change and why.

RULING (delegated by Mike, 2026-09-17 21:22:28 AUSEST, dossier review). Mike delegated this decision on 2026-09-17 with the instruction: read the two reviews, weigh them, decide, record, keep the analysis.
DECISION: C (amended) — build the sticky "↓ N newer events — » to follow" L2 marker that tools/xray/spec/018-Event-Spine.md:485-491 already specifies, with ONE amendment taken from the Codex review: presence and N are derived from the SPINE (the `:head?` predicate `compose-focus` already computes, and the focusable vector it computes it from), never from the filtered list vector `event-list-tree` renders. A is declined; B is not taken; Codex's own preferred option (a conditional "Follow latest" label on the `»` control) is declined. The two triage riders (.5#9, .5#10) and the mayor's static-shell docstring evidence ride in the same PR. The bead stays OPEN and is dispatchable now: C4 (rf2-y8doi.16) merged as PR #9934 at 9dfcfc0fdb, so the "sequence after C4" hold in the description is discharged.
WHY: The dossier's evidence carried on the SHAPE of the cue and Codex's carried on one MECHANISM inside it, and the ruling takes both. Both reviewers agree from line cites that pausing now pins the shown dispatch AND its epoch while collection continues (spine.cljs:747-782, commit 09d53875bd, spine_cljs_test.cljs:945-979) and that App-db consumes that pin (app_db_diff_subs.cljs:127-136) — so the dossier's seat 3 is a debugger reporting a stale epoch as current, with two 21 px chevrons at opacity 1.0 versus 0.4 as the only difference in the Dynamic chrome (Codex is right that the L4 Trace tab's 3 px status bar is a third pixel; that narrows "every pixel" to "every pixel of L2, L3 and the other L4 tabs" and changes nothing). "Trust the programmer" rejects chrome the programmer must decode or that nags while they work; it does not license a wrong result. C is the only option that paints NOTHING while following and nothing when paused-but-current: it appears exactly when the read is stale, states the one fact that makes it stale (how many newer), its click is the existing follow-head, and it is Mike's own unbuilt passage in 018 — so the spec-code gap closes by building rather than by striking. Codex's objection (1) is measured and correct — `event-list-tree` receives `:rf.xray/filtered-event-bundles` (shell.cljs:2407; filters.cljs:333-348, frame scope + pills + mutes) while focus composes from `:rf.xray/event-bundles` (spine.cljs:1066-1072), so index arithmetic over the visible vector can read 0 while the panel is stale — but it is an implementation detail with a one-predicate fix, not a reason against the marker: `compose-focus` (spine.cljs:300-529) derives `:head?` over `focusable-event-bundles` under the same `show-ungrouped?` and frame scope, and in unpaused LIVE the head-tracking branch makes `:head?` always true, so `(not (:head? focus))` is precisely "following is suspended AND something newer exists", and N counted over that same vector agrees with "head" by construction (018:1176-1180). That is cheaper than the dossier's index arithmetic and closes the hole Codex found. Codex's objection (2) — the marker is silent right after Space until an arrival — does not carry: nothing is stale at that instant, Space is the programmer's own deliberate act, and `»` already lights on pause (Codex's own finding, pinned by shell_cljs_test.cljs:1722-1740). Codex's preferred label fails the posture where C passes it: it appears in EVERY RETRO state, which is the routine inspection state, so it is chrome present whenever the user is not following rather than only when something is wrong; it relocates the dropped mode pill into the top ribbon as a verb (Mike's 2026-05-17 instruction offered exactly "relocate into top ribbon OR drop if redundant", and rf2-g9pee dropped it as redundant); it sits in the nowrap left cluster with a documented width constraint (shell.cljs:1309-1326) and would shift layout on every row click; it says nothing about distance; and Codex records no evidence behind it ("no measured usage-frequency evidence or verified visual mockup"). A is declined for the dossier's reasons, which Codex shares: a 2 px left-edge colour is the exact shape Mike reported as spurious on 2026-05-24 (rf2-4yemd, pinned by `chrome-ribbon-has-no-left-edge-stripe`), the named tokens do not exist, and `data-rf-xray-mode` already carries three meanings. B is the cheapest option and would be right if the non-scrolling list were cue enough, but the dossier's seat-3 walk-through shows it is not once the newer rows are below the fold, and Codex's warning against inferring low incidence from four months of silence is accepted. The count stays because 018 specifies it and it is what answers "how far behind am I?"; if Mike finds the number noisy, the same strip without it is the same cost. Two Codex corrections fold into the brief: the AI-facing skill (skills/re-frame2-xray/references/chrome.md:60-62) wrongly says pausing "drops to RETRO" (pause keeps `:mode :live` and sets `:paused?`), and "indistinguishable in every pixel" is narrowed as above.
WHAT CHANGES MY MIND: If Mike says the non-scrolling list plus the lit `»` is cue enough in practice (the dossier's own out), B is right, costs nothing, and 018:485-491 gets struck as rf2-y8doi.45 item 5 already plans. If he wants RETRO and paused to look different from each other, or an always-on "not following" acknowledgment, Codex's label on the `»` control is the cheapest way to add it and can ride on top of the marker; the marker itself would still be built.
