Depends on / feeds: holds three spec beads — rf2-y8doi.36 (007-UX-IA, items 5 and 21), rf2-y8doi.45 (018-Event-Spine, item 4), rf2-y8doi.57 (DESIGN-RATIONALE, item 1) — all `blocks`-edged on this bead. Sequence after C4 (rf2-y8doi.16, shell.cljs). Carries .5#9 and .5#10 whichever way it goes.

## The decision in one sentence

Xray's spine has three states the user must know to read any L4 panel — following the head (LIVE), pinned to an older event (RETRO), frozen by Space (paused) — and after four dated removals the only on-screen difference between them is the opacity of two 21 px chevrons; rule whether to (A) paint one cheap colour cue, (B) stand by the removals and rewrite the three spec documents to promise nothing, or (C, mine) build the sticky "N newer events" marker that 018 already specifies, which shows only when the panel is actually stale.

## The problem, carefully

**What the spine knows.** `spine/compose-focus` returns `{:mode :live|:retro :head? :paused?}` (tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/spine.cljs:20-23, :525-529). Space toggles `:paused?` and is a deliberate no-op in RETRO (spine.cljs:747-753, :773-774); `l`/`»` snap back to LIVE (spine.cljs:734-745); clicking a non-head row pins RETRO, clicking the head row stays LIVE (spine.cljs:562-563).

**What the chrome paints from it.** Exactly two things:
- The nav cluster: `›` disabled when at head, `»` disabled only when `at-head? AND live?` (shell.cljs:919-920, :966-981 — "disabled" is opacity 0.4 on a blue-filled 21 px button, shell.cljs:948-950). `nav-boundary-state` is the only consumer of `:live?` (shell.cljs:1198-1228).
- Auto-scroll: only in LIVE+head+unpaused does the focused row scroll into view (shell.cljs:2242-2244, :1547-1558); RETRO and paused leave the scroll position alone.
The focused row itself is marked by a background wash and a leading `>` caret (shell.cljs:1692-1696, :1873-1883) — the same marking in all three states. Grep `stale\?|pulse|"LIVE"|"RETRO"` over shell.cljs: one comment (:3326), no code; control `No events.` :2276, `focused?` :1683 found (the .5 report's census, re-read here). `panels/event/event_status_colour.cljc:312-316` still derives `:stale?` (focused + RETRO), `:paused?` and `:mode` per row, and `classify-status` maps them to `:stale` / `:paused-by-tool` (:145, :167) — but post rf2-pjjwh that vocabulary has ONE render site, the L4 Trace tab's 3 px status bar (panels/trace.cljs:897-915, `data-rf-xray-status`; the e2e suite's own header says so at panels_e2e/event_status_colour_cross_site_e2e_cljs_test.cljs:31-36). The HCM rules for `stale`/`paused-by-tool` at theme/global_styles.cljs:583-585 match nothing in L2.

**What the three spec documents still promise.** Each names a cue nothing paints:
- 007-UX-IA.md:489 — `- **L2 spine: head row pulses** (LIVE cue; the dedicated Mode pill widget was dropped).` Also :158-163 ("the L2 spine itself indicates LIVE / RETRO via the head-row pulse / pinned-row glyph") and :1180-1182 ("L2 head-row LIVE pulse: 2s gentle 600ms expand-fade on the head row's `●` gutter glyph … Replaces the dropped Mode pill widget as the LIVE/RETRO cue"), :1188-1191.
- 018-Event-Spine.md:252-254 — `LIVE / LIVE-paused / RETRO is a separate SPINE state communicated by the L2 event list itself (the head row's pulse cue indicates LIVE; a pinned row indicates RETRO).` Also :107 (stripe `:accent-violet` / `:cyan` — no such tokens exist; tokens.cljc carries `:magenta` :175 and `:accent` only), :175, :202-203, :1132 (table row "Pulse on head row in LIVE; pinned-row glyph in RETRO"), :1177.
- DESIGN-RATIONALE.md Lock #14 :569-572 — `3. **Motion dampening** — Dynamic ships the LIVE pulse + machine-active pulse + 180ms tab fade`, and :577-582 "The user reads the mode from the chrome shape + stripe colour + motion dampening". Note Lock #14's "mode" is Dynamic/Static; the LIVE pulse is promised there only as a Dynamic motion, and the violet/cyan stripe as the Dynamic/Static signal — both gone (rf2-ad7zx.13 single accent, rf2-4yemd).
The AI-facing skill was already corrected to the truth on 2026-07-11 (f6cc7bed22, rf2-wjl2qo): skills/re-frame2-xray/references/chrome.md:60-66 says "There is **no mode pill and no animated head-row cue** — LIVE vs RETRO is conveyed by the `[◀ ▶ ⏭]` nav cluster plus the focused-row state". So the skill is at option B today; the spec is not.

**The four removals, side by side.** None of the four beads is in the live tracker (identity-select over `.beads/issues.jsonl` at HEAD reads 0 for each against 1749 issue records; control: the epic resolves). Their records were recovered from checkpoint exports at 7b5a851fff, 470584bf43, 47579f1f31 and 44e0238e8b, and the close reasons are quoted here so no worker brief has to cite them (CLAUDE.md's reopened-bead dispatch clause).

| Bead (closed) | What it removed | Its stated reason — the cue assumed to remain |
|---|---|---|
| rf2-g9pee, 2026-05-18, PR #1509 (Mike chat 2026-05-17: "relocate LIVE/RETROSPECTIVE mode pill into top ribbon OR drop if redundant with sticky-selection semantics") | the `● LIVE / ◐ RETRO` mode pill (and the bottom rail) | "mode-pill dropped because state is derivable from **sticky-row selection + nav cluster**, and Space / L / G keybindings preserve toggle access." |
| rf2-4vp5j, 2026-05-22, PR #1972 | re-shaped the two ribbons; re-added a Dynamic/Static `<select>`; moved the nav cluster | Not a LIVE/RETRO change at all — its spec says the 2 px stripe "carries the mode SIGNAL so the control itself recedes" (018:175), where "mode" is Dynamic/Static. That stripe claim was already false once rf2-ad7zx.13 made the accent a single blue. |
| rf2-pjjwh, 2026-05-24, PR #2091 (Mike-dictated) | the row's leading gutter glyph `● ◉` (the pulse's carrier), the trailing lifecycle status stripe (the `:stale`/`:paused-by-tool` colour on the row), badges, dimming | "Surface = the mock": "event-list clean 4-col + active-row bg (gutter/origin glyph/badges/status-stripe/dimming/ungrouped REMOVED)". The Figma mock has no LIVE cue, so none survived. |
| rf2-4yemd, 2026-05-24, PR #2100 (Mike observed live) | the ribbon's 2 px blue left-edge stripe | "rf2-o5f5f.1 mode-signal mechanism left `:border-left '2px solid <accent>'` on chrome ribbon root … the inline-style declaration was never removed" — Mike reported it as a spurious "blue left edge … not in the Figma authority". Pinned by `chrome-ribbon-has-no-left-edge-stripe` (shell_cljs_test.cljs:383-397). |

Read together: g9pee assumed the row position carries the signal; pjjwh then removed every per-row mark except the wash; 4vp5j and 4yemd concern the Dynamic/Static axis, but 4yemd is Mike rejecting exactly the shape option A proposes (a 2 px left-edge colour), and rf2-2sez0 (2026-05-20, cited at 021-Dynamic-Panel-Designs.md:5958-5959) is Mike rejecting a continuous pulse on the machine chart — so the pulse the spec still promises is a genre he has refused. The Static surface, meanwhile, still paints the blue left edge (static/shell.cljs:322, resolving to `:accent` in both modes per :225-241; test static/shell_cljs_test.cljs:325-335 pins it), so the two surfaces disagree about a "signal" that signals nothing.

## Make it tangible

The L2 list shows 8 rows by default (200 px, shell.cljs:2255-2257). Three seats:

1. **LIVE** (mount, or after `»` / `l`). The bottom row carries the wash and the `>` caret; every new event lands at the bottom and the list scrolls to keep it in view; `›` and `»` are dimmed. L4 (Epoch, App-db diff, Views…) re-pivots on every arrival.
2. **RETRO** (clicked any older row, or `j` / `‹`). That row keeps the wash and caret; new events append below it and the list does not scroll; `›` and `»` light up. L4 stays on the pinned epoch. Space does nothing (spine.cljs:773). If the pinned row was second from the bottom, one arrival fills the last slot and every later one goes below the fold — the picture reads "one newer event" whether there is one or five hundred.
3. **Paused** (Space while LIVE, with DOM focus on something inert in the shell — the list background, a header — keybinding.cljs:292-294). The then-head row keeps wash and caret at the bottom edge; the list stops scrolling; `»` lights up. When the next event arrives, `›` lights too, and the new rows sit below the fold. **This picture is pixel-identical to seat 1 except for two chevrons at opacity 1.0 instead of 0.4.** The user reads App-db diff for "the latest event" and it describes one N events ago; nothing on the L2, L3 or L4 surfaces says N, or that there is an N. Seats 2 and 3 are indistinguishable from each other in every pixel.

Under the options, seat 3 after twenty arrivals looks like:
- **A**: the L2 list's left edge is grey (paused) rather than violet (LIVE). The user must know the code; "grey" says nothing about how far behind they are.
- **B**: as today — two lit chevrons.
- **C**: a one-line strip pinned to the bottom of the L2 scroll box: `↓ 20 newer events — » to follow` (click → `:rf.xray/follow-head`). In seat 1 there is no strip; in seat 2 or 3 with nothing newer there is no strip either.

## Options

### A. Re-add one cheap cue (the triage's `data-rf-xray-mode` attribute on the L2 `<ul>` + a 2 px left rule, violet LIVE / cyan RETRO / grey paused) and rewrite 007, 018, DR to it
- What changes: `event-list-tree` (shell.cljs:2219-2303) stamps an attribute from `focus` and paints the rule (inline, or a class in theme/global_styles.cljs); three node tests; the three spec passages rewritten to name the rule.
- Consequences: the programmer gets a permanent colour to decode; tests and testbeds get a machine-readable spine state. Two concrete defects in the form as triaged: (i) the name `data-rf-xray-mode` is already the spec-published axis for mount mode (`overlay`/`inline`/`popout`, mount.cljs:210/:313/:1732), lens mode (`static`, static/shell.cljs:596; shell.cljs:3079-3083) and modal identity (`settings`/`palette`/`segment-inspector`, keybinding.cljs:269 does `.closest` on it) — a fourth meaning on one attribute is a trap, so it would have to be `data-rf-xray-spine`; (ii) there are no violet/cyan tokens (018:107's `:accent-violet`/`:cyan` never existed in tokens.cljc; the nearest, `:magenta`, `:diff-gutter`, `:info`, each already mean something else: COEFFECT/redacted, diff gutter, paused-by-tool). Chrome colour was collapsed to a single accent by rf2-ad7zx.13.
- Cost: a morning. Files: shell.cljs, theme/global_styles.cljs (collides with C12), shell_cljs_test.cljs; spec via S5/S14/S26. No hot-zone files.
- Risk: it re-litigates two of Mike's own calls — a 2 px left-edge colour is the exact shape he reported as spurious on 2026-05-24 (rf2-4yemd), and per-state chrome colour is what single-accent removed. It also does not answer the user's actual question (how far behind am I?).

### B. Stand by the four removals; rewrite 007, 018 and DR to promise no cue; drop the Static stripe for symmetry
- What changes: strike/rewrite 007:158-163, :489, :1180-1191; 018:107 (row 3), :175, :202-203, :249-257, :1132, :1177; DR:569-572 and :577-582 — all to "LIVE/RETRO is read from the focused row's position and the nav cluster; there is no dedicated cue" (the skill's wording, chrome.md:60-66). Delete static/shell.cljs:322's `:border-left`, the `stripe-token-for-mode`/`stripe-hex-for-mode` helpers (:225-248) and their test (static/shell_cljs_test.cljs:322-335); fix the signal lists at static/shell.cljs:50-54 and :127-140.
- Consequences: spec matches code; the tool stays as Mike shaped it in May; the skill needs no edit. Seat 3's wrong-result path stays, undocumented as a hazard unless the spec says "note: a paused spine looks like a live one".
- Cost: spec-only plus one line and one test; the spec edits already ride S5/S14/S26. Half a morning across three PRs that are happening anyway.

## Codex Recommendation

**Recommendation: make the existing follow-head action explicit while inspection is pinned or paused, and correct the specifications.** Prefer a conditional visible “Follow latest” label on that control over either a colour stripe or the proposed counted sticky strip. Keep the existing dispatch and focus model; this needs no new public API, stored state, animation, or counting mechanism.

**Independent findings at `1dbef19ef9ecc3c30ca629b7cb478224b1dcebea` (2026-09-17).** I read the current bead, source, callers, tests, and removal history rather than treating their summaries as authority:

- The current chrome has a real, deliberately tested distinction. `tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/shell.cljs:1215-1228` excludes paused LIVE from `live?`; its existing `»` control is therefore enabled immediately on pause, even before another event arrives (`:919-975`). `tools/xray/test/day8/re_frame2_xray/shell_cljs_test.cljs:1722-1740` exercises precisely this case through the registered pause event. The problem is that this is a subtle action-state cue, not literally an absence of information.
- Pausing now freezes the shown dispatch **and epoch**, while collection continues (`tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/spine.cljs:747-782`). This was repaired on September 13 in `09d53875bd`; the ordinary fresh-LIVE and after-follow-head paths have regression tests at `tools/xray/test/day8/re_frame2_xray/spine_cljs_test.cljs:945-979`. App-db's selected epoch actually consumes that focus (`tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/panels/app_db_diff_subs.cljs:127-136`). Thus forgetting that inspection is paused is a plausible debugger usability problem, although I have not observed a user making that mistake.
- The pulse promises are stale: compare `tools/xray/spec/007-UX-IA.md:158-163,489` and `tools/xray/spec/018-Event-Spine.md:249-257` with the current row/list rendering (`tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/shell.cljs:1680-1700,1873-1886,2219-2303`). The Trace panel does expose paused/stale status in its small bar (`tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/panels/trace.cljs:897-916`), so “indistinguishable in every pixel” is too broad across all panels. Also, the supposedly corrected skill still wrongly says pause drops to RETRO (`skills/re-frame2-xray/references/chrome.md:60-62`); pause keeps `:mode :live`.

**Why I would simplify option C.** Its count is not just an innocent measurement of panel staleness. The list receives filtered bundles (`tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/shell.cljs:2407`), after frame scope, pills, and mutes (`tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/filters.cljs:333-348`). Focus instead composes from `:rf.xray/event-bundles` (`tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/spine.cljs:1066-1072`). Consequently, newer events can exist while the proposed visible-row count is zero, or the pinned event can be absent from that vector altogether. A defined “newer visible events” count could still be useful, but it would not provide the general temporal assurance claimed here. Moreover, C stays silent immediately after Space until another visible event arrives, exactly when acknowledgement of the pause is useful.

The options are therefore:

- **B, truthful documentation only:** defensible minimum cost. Keep the deliberately small controls and accept that users learn their enabled states. Do not describe this as a data-correctness fix, or infer low incidence from the absence of reports.
- **A, three colours:** supplies immediate state but adds a visual code to learn and revisits an explicitly removed stripe. I would decline it.
- **C, counted sticky strip:** provides useful distance information when its counting domain is defined, but adds another surface and leaves ordinary filtered cases unanswered. Defer it until distance, rather than simply resuming following, is a demonstrated need.
- **Preferred, explicit existing action:** show “Follow latest” on the existing follow-head control when `:mode` is RETRO or `:paused?` is true, including when no newer row exists. Its presence says that automatic following is suspended; clicking it uses the existing `:rf.xray/follow-head`, which clears both conditions (`tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/spine.cljs:734-745`). This gives a programmer a directly useful action without asking them to decode colours or another number.

The historical removals support restraint, not a prohibition on improving legibility: `81ea273a18` removed the pill as redundant with selection/navigation; `01b6d7510b` removed row decoration; `9b129fce0d` removed the Dynamic/Static stripe. I checked their commits and identity-selected checkpoint closure records. None establishes that the newer-events counter is required. Correct 007/018/DR and the skill to the chosen actual behavior; assess Static-stripe cleanup separately from this temporal cue.

**Validation limits:** this was source/test inspection and read-only history research; no application tests or browser session were run. The preferred label needs a focused render/click check for LIVE, paused-at-head, and RETRO, plus a narrow-ribbon visual check: the existing nonwrapping cluster already has a documented width constraint (`tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/shell.cljs:1309-1326`). There is no measured usage-frequency evidence or verified visual mockup behind this recommendation.

title: practice: a third of the tracker's findings-path citations are dangling — a close reason must carry its decisive measurement inline, not only a path into the disposable ai/ tree
description:
FOUND BY THE §5 METHOD-REREAD LOOP, 2026-09-16, on the axis that loop says drift lives on: checking a rule the mayor has been ENFORCING against what the tree actually does. It began as two apparent coincidences in one day and was measured rather than left to a third.

## THE MEASUREMENT

A THIRD OF THE EVIDENCE THIS TRACKER CITES NO LONGER EXISTS.

Over all 1,673 issue records in `.beads/issues.jsonl`, counting distinct `findings/...` paths that carry a FILE EXTENSION (so prose fragments cannot inflate the count):

    distinct unambiguous file citations   67
    resolve on disk                       45
    DANGLING                              22   (33%)

Control both ways: the resolving side is real and was sampled (`ai/findings/API-review/codex/README.md`, `.../fable/registration-spellings.md`, `.../fable/registry-introspection.md` all present). A first, looser pass over ALL `findings/` paths read 44 of 124 dangling; it was narrowed on suspicion of over-matching prose — `ai/findings/exit` was the tell — and the narrower instrument agrees at the same rate, which is what makes 33% trustworthy rather than the raw 35%.

THE DANGLING ONES ARE NOT OBSCURE. Ranked by how many distinct beads cite them:

    ai/findings/2026-09-03.pilot-b-rehearsal-realworld.friction.md    12 beads
    ai/findings/2026-09-03.pilot-b-rehearsal-linearlite.friction.md    9 beads
    ai/findings/parity-2026-09/fable/matrix.md                         5 beads
    ai/findings/parity-2026-09/fable/advantage-measured-*.md           5 beads
    ai/findings/parity-2026-09/fable/rerun-2026-09-15.md               4 beads
    ai/findings/xray-ux-design.md                                      3 beads
    ai/findings/re-frame-10x-v2-design.md                              3 beads
    ai/findings/react19.md                                             3 beads

## WHY THIS IS A REAL DEFECT AND NOT JUST UNTIDINESS

**`/ai/` IS GITIGNORED, LOCAL-ONLY AND EXPLICITLY DISPOSABLE.** That is correct and is not the thing to change. What is wrong is that the tracker — whose close reasons this project treats as NORMATIVE RECORDS — cites it as though it were durable. There is no backstop: `.beads/issues.jsonl` lives in git history, so CLAUDE.md can promise complete recovery for an erased `close_reason` or a replaced `notes` field, but a findings doc that has been cleaned up is simply gone, from every checkout, for ever.

**THE FAILURE SHAPE IS ALREADY CATALOGUED, WITH A DIFFERENT CAUSE.** CLAUDE.md's reopen bullet carries a dispatch clause about exactly this: "a brief telling a worker to 'read the bead's close reason' is UNSATISFIABLE on a reopened bead, and the worker reads the absence as its own failure rather than as the tool's — two live workers were briefed that way and had to be messaged mid-flight." A brief saying "read the findings doc at `ai/findings/X`" fails identically, and a third of such citations are now in that state. The remedy written there — restore or do not cite, BEFORE dispatching — has no analogue here because there is nothing to restore.

**AND IT FAILS IN THE REASSURING DIRECTION FOR THE READER WHO MATTERS MOST.** A bead citing a path looks BETTER sourced than one that does not. The citation is the thing that makes a claim feel checked, so the beads carrying dangling paths read as the most rigorous ones on the board.

## THE FIX IS A PRACTICE CLAUSE, NOT A FILE RECOVERY

Do not try to restore the 22. They are gone, most of them deliberately, and hunting them would be the expensive half of a cheap problem.

THE RULE THAT WOULD HAVE PREVENTED ALL 22: **a close reason or ruling must carry its DECISIVE MEASUREMENT INLINE, and may cite a path only as supporting detail.** The path is then a convenience that can rot without taking the finding with it.

This is already the mayor's own practice and is simply not written down — every close reason written this session quotes its figures in the bead (rollup totals, byte counts, exit codes, both-way controls) rather than pointing at a file for them. That is why those closures survive `ai/` being cleared and the older ones do not.

SCOPE, kept deliberately small: one clause, most naturally in CLAUDE.md § Local working files (the `ai/` tree) where the disposability of `/ai/` is already stated, or beside the reopen bullet's existing dispatch clause in § Beads durability. **It should NOT propose deleting or rewriting existing citations**, and it should NOT become a gate — there is nothing to check mechanically that would not also flag every legitimate supporting reference.

## WHAT IS NOT ESTABLISHED

  * WHY they are missing. Deliberate cleanup, a `bd gc`-era compaction, machine moves and ordinary tidying are all plausible; none was investigated. The rate is the finding, not the cause.
  * Whether any of the 22 survives somewhere else (another machine, a PR body, a commit message). Not searched.
  * Whether the same rate holds for citations OUTSIDE `ai/` — tracked paths would mostly resolve, but that was not measured and should not be assumed either way.

The Beads-durability connection is preserved by a cross-reference from inside the new clause; nothing was added to that section.

The deliberately-wide variant (every `findings/` token, 41 of 138) is the inflated one, and its dangling list carries exactly the prose fragments the bead predicted -- `ai/findings/exit`, `ai/findings/X` -- so the extension filter was confirmed by prediction rather than assumed.

AND ONE ROW CORRECTS THE MAYOR'S STATED REASON, WHICH MATTERS MORE THAN THE HEADLINE: **non-`ai/` TRACKED-path citations dangle at 33% (8 of 24)** -- the same rate. The mayor's framing blamed the disposability of `/ai/`; that is the largest bucket but NOT the whole mechanism, because citations into tracked trees rot just as fast when files move or are renamed. The clause as written still covers it, since carrying the measurement inline survives either cause, but the "because ai/ is disposable" reasoning is narrower than the phenomenon it explains.

TWO TRUNCATION ERRORS ON ONE CORPUS IN ONE DAY, BY DIFFERENT MECHANISMS, AND BOTH ARE THE SAME CLASS AS CLAUDE.md INSTRUMENT ITEM (b).

  THE MAYOR'S: this bead's own ranked table named `...friction.md` where the tracker actually cites `...friction-log.md`. The measuring run printed paths into a fixed-width column that truncated at 52 characters and the mayor COMPLETED THE NAME BY HAND when writing the bead. Re-measured: the 12-bead and 9-bead counts belong to the `-log` spellings; the `.md` spellings are cited by one bead each. All four dangle, so the conclusion never moved -- but a table is a claim. Item (b) is written about hand-extending an abbreviated sha; this is the identical act on a path. **A hand-completed identifier is a fabricated identifier whatever its type**, and item (b)'s own companion rule already covers the display half: where you cap a display, write "first N of M".

title: feat(xray): write-reach lint over the optimistic-reconciled trace
description:
An Xray Resources-panel lint that names a mutation instance whose optimistic patch touched a cache key that its invalidation and populate never reached. Tool only: no runtime change, no Spec 016 edit, never a runtime warning. Sequence after the Conduit Xray-mount bead so the lint is visible in the flagship.

Every claim carries its trunk file:line (verified at `f2f9ffd654b7`, 2026-09-15) or the reproducible experiment behind it, so this bead needs nothing outside the checkout. (Provenance: the Resources parity study in the mayor checkout's gitignored `ai/findings/Resources/fable/`, report §4 and §6 L1; a worktree does not carry it, and nothing here depends on it.)

## The bug class, and how to reproduce it

JVM, `re-frame.substrate.plain-atom/adapter` under `re-frame.test-support/make-reset-runtime-fixture`, `:rf.http/managed` overridden with a ledger-appending no-op fx, `:rf.resource/schedule-timers` overridden with a no-op, replies replayed by dispatching the captured `:on-success` vector with `{:status :ok :value data}`. Registrations:

- `:article` — `:scope :rf.scope/global`, `:params-schema [:map [:slug :string]]`, `:tags (fn [{:keys [slug]} _] #{[:article slug]})`.
- `:list` — global, tags `#{[:article-list]}` plus one `[:article slug]` member tag per article in the data.
- `:feed` — `:scope {:from-db <session-resolver>}`, tags `#{[:feed]}` only (no member tags; this is what makes the fault visible).
- A favourite mutation with `:optimistic-tags` returning two descriptors — `{:scope :rf.scope/global :tags #{[:article slug]} :patch …}` and `{:scope {:from-db <session-resolver>} :tags #{[:feed]} :patch …}` — `:populates` the article from the reply, and an `:invalidates` that names the article tag and `[:article-list]` **but forgets the feed descriptor**.

Load all three, execute the mutation, reply ok. Observed: the article is populated from the reply, exactly one refetch is issued (`[:get "/api/articles"]`), and the feed keeps the optimistic guess — `[:loaded <rev> nil]`, not marked stale, never refetched. With the feed descriptor present, two refetches are issued (list and feed). Nothing says so:

- The runtime's dev tripwire `:rf.warning/mutation-scope-mismatch` (`spec/016-Resources.md:878`; `implementation/resources/src/re_frame/resources/mutation_events.cljc:916`) fires for a descriptor that resolved the wrong scope, not for one that is missing.
- The instance row's `:affected-keys` carries the settlement reach only — populated, patched, removed and stale-marked keys (016 line 863) — so for the faulty write it lists the article and the list and omits the feed the optimistic patch touched.

No comparator in the study's set (TanStack Query, RTK Query, SWR, Apollo) can name this bug class either; their devtools show cache state, not cause.

## The data is already emitted

The `:rf.mutation/optimistic-reconciled` trace op records `:optimistic-keys`, `:committed` and `:reconciliation-refetches` per settled instance (`mutation_events.cljc:539-543`, `:1403`, `:1803-1804`), and the row carries `:affected-keys`. The lint is a set difference: optimistic keys that are in none of committed, affected or reconciliation-refetches. One row per instance naming the instance id, the mutation id and the missing key(s).

## Where and how

- `tools/xray`, beside the existing Resources-panel lints (scope-audit, orphaned-owner) per `tools/xray/spec/024-Resources-Panel.md`. Not a hot zone.
- Informational and dedupe-keyed like the scope-mismatch tripwire. A value deliberately left optimistic is a legitimate authoring choice, so the row says what was not reconciled and does not call it a defect.
- Do not duplicate the scope-mismatch case: a wrong-scope descriptor already has its warning.

## Gate, size, acceptance

- Gate: Xray unit tests and the feature-matrix gate (`npm run test:xray-feature-gate`), PR-smoke tier.
- Size: S–M. Not gold-plating: the set difference is the whole computation, over records that exist.
- Acceptance: with the forgets-the-feed mutation above loaded and settled, exactly one lint row names the instance and the feed key; with the correct favourite (all three descriptors), no row; a wrong-scope descriptor produces the existing `:rf.warning/mutation-scope-mismatch` and no second row from this lint.
- Removes: a class of "stale after my own write" bug reports that today are found by reading `mutations.cljs` by hand.

title: docs(story): every open-in-editor :dev-http port 404s at / (only /index.html answers), so the /#/stories URLs in shadow-cljs.edn comments and chapter 08 do not open; chapter 08's 8041 URL also names a variant that build lacks
description:
Discovered while verifying rf2-ot2xp's chapter 01 URL (worker/storytutorial-a). Docs and dev tooling; S.

MEASURED 2026-09-14 on Windows, shadow-cljs 3.4.10, from a worker worktree with `npx shadow-cljs server` (and separately `npx shadow-cljs watch :examples/login-form`): every `:dev-http` port that carries `:handler re-frame.testbed.open-in-editor-server/handler` answers `/` with that handler's own 404 (body `not found`, 9 bytes) and answers `/index.html` with the page. Probed: 8043 `/` 404, `/index.html` 200 (228 bytes), `/main.js` 200; 8042 `/` 404, `/index.html` 200; 8030 `/` 404, `/index.html` 200; 8041 `/` 404. The hand-written `index.html` exists in each port's first root.

Mechanism, read at source and not yet proven on another OS: `tools/testbed-support/src/re_frame/testbed/open_in_editor_server.clj` `handler` is the `:dev-http` fallback and returns 404 for every uri other than its endpoint, so a request for `/` that the roots do not resolve to a file never reaches an index fallback. It may be that a custom `:handler` replaces shadow's push-state index fallback on every platform, which would make this general rather than Windows-only; check on Linux before choosing the fix.

WHAT IT BREAKS:
1. The comments in `implementation/shadow-cljs.edn` (Story showcases block, around :583-:599 and :620-:625) promise `http://localhost:804x/#/stories` and say "the hand-written index.html resolves at `/`". HOT ZONE: sequence the edit.
2. `docs/story/08-snapshot-identity-and-sharing.md:47` shows `http://localhost:8041/?variant=story.login%2Ferror#/stories`. Besides requesting `/`, port 8041 serves `examples/core/login`, whose `:story.login` registers empty / filled / submitting / invalid-credentials / auth-error / locked-out / success and NO `/error` variant, so the example URL names a variant that build does not have. The five-state tutorial testbed is 8043 (`:story.login-form/error`).

rf2-ot2xp worked around (1) for chapter 01 only, printing `http://localhost:8043/index.html#/stories`.

FIX OPTIONS (pick one; do not do both): (a) make the handler fall through to the root's `index.html` for `/`, which restores every `/#/stories` URL as written; or (b) correct the URLs to the `index.html` form. (a) is the smaller surface if the mechanism holds. Then correct chapter 08's port/variant pair and re-probe by effect with curl.

GATES: none of the doc link gates execute a URL; the control is a curl probe of `/` and `/index.html` on a running dev server, red before the fix and green after.

== MAYOR PREMISE CHECK (2026-09-14, trunk ef257944af, before dispatch to worker/devhttpindex-a) ==
VERIFIED AT SOURCE:

CHAPTER 08: pair changed from 8041 + `story.login%2Ferror` to 8043 + `story.login-form%2Ferror`. Evidence:

title: Incomplete: replay fallback still adopts a foreign epoch when its own trace is suppressed
description:
Merged-PR audit #9785 (456dc1459d4cdfed3792729072c8c5eb7d99bf4d), discovered from closed rf2-k0nr. The new arming-thread filter fixes ordinary traced replay, but the own-dispatch result claim remains incomplete through the unchanged fallback. Preserve the source closure.

Location: implementation/epoch/src/re_frame/epoch/state.cljc, note-commit! (around 411-413) unconditionally fills :fallback-epoch-id from the first same-frame commit; take-observed-commit! (around 364-367) returns it whenever no :dispatch-id was observed from the arming thread. The PR explicitly names this remainder. It is reachable in a development build, not only when the whole trace/epoch subsystem is elided.

Deterministic public-runtime reproducer:
1. Initialize plain-atom plus epoch capture, depth 10. Register :audit/add and :audit/other with the same db counter handler. Make :audit/replay and dispatch [:audit/add 1], retaining source epoch 1.
2. Re-register :audit/add with public handler metadata {:rf.trace/no-emit? true}, leaving :audit/other traced. This models replay after changing a handler's tracing policy; no trace producer is stubbed.
3. Replay source epoch 1 on a future. Wrap the real arm-commit-observation! only to park that thread immediately AFTER real arming with CountDownLatch.
4. On another thread dispatch [:audit/other 100] into the same frame, then release replay.
5. Both events execute, db is {:n 102}; retained history is [[:audit/add 1] [:audit/other 100]], because the replay emits no new epoch. Actual result is {:ok? true :source-epoch-id 1 :event-id :audit/add :epoch-id 2}; epoch 2 resolves to the foreign [:audit/other 100]. Expected :epoch-id nil: no epoch belonging to replay was committed.
6. Control: replay the same quiet handler without a foreign dispatch. It returns :epoch-id nil, history is unchanged, db becomes {:n 103}.

Independent evidence: C:/Users/miket/.codex/tmp/audit-re-frame2-pr9785-quiet-replay-probe-1.clj/.log/.exit, exit 0; actual loaded state.cljc resource URL printed, only latch scheduling wrapped, every child ended. The source correction itself is independently confirmed by its exact replay namespace: old state overlay exits 1 (18 tests/136 assertions, 3 failures), landed state exits 0 at 18/136. Thus this is the separately uncovered fallback, not a claim that the normal traced fix failed.

Required correction: prevent commits from another dispatch/thread from becoming replay's fallback evidence. A replay that produces no epoch must return nil even while unrelated same-frame history grows. Constrain or remove the uncorrelated fallback using existing observation/dispatch machinery, preserving ordinary traced replay, same-thread listener nesting, queued-child retention/eviction, and failed-dispatch cleanup. Do not broaden public API or invent new tracing diagnostics.

Impact P3: uncommon but supported tracing-policy change plus JVM concurrency returns false causal evidence from a dev tool. It does not prevent either event from executing. No mayor notification or acknowledgment is inferred from this issue or its forward pointer.
acceptance_criteria: A deterministic JVM public replay regression records an event, suppresses that handler with :rf.trace/no-emit? metadata, interleaves an unrelated traced same-frame dispatch after real observation arming, and proves both events execute while replay returns :epoch-id nil instead of the retained foreign epoch. A no-interleave control returns nil. Existing normal replay/thread-isolation, same-handler nested listener, queued-child retained/evicted and cleanup tests remain green.
notes:
VERDICT (rf2-c74lr), 2026-09-13 19:38:47 AUSEST: fixed in PR #9791.

PREMISE VERIFIED AT SOURCE (trunk e36dbae85a). `note-commit!` filled `:fallback-epoch-id` from the frame's first commit, whatever that commit's `:dispatch-id`. `take-observed-commit!` returned it whenever no dispatch id had been observed from the arming thread.

CORRECTION TAKEN: the fallback is REMOVED, not constrained. The comment kept it for "the no-dispatch-id posture". That posture has no epochs either: capture is a trace stage, and the ring stays empty under the production gate. So the fallback only ever fired in dev, when the replayed dispatch itself emitted nothing. That is a handler registered with `:rf.trace/no-emit?`, which commits no epoch. Every commit the fallback could adopt was another dispatch's. Every router dispatch path gates on `emit-dispatched-trace!`, so a dispatch that runs without emitting `:rf.event/dispatched` is exactly one whose handler opted out.

WHY NOT A THREAD CONSTRAINT: the same defect is reachable on ONE thread. A quiet replayed parent's traced queued child also rode the fallback, because the child's enqueue emit is suppressed under the parent's no-emit handler scope. Confining the fallback to the arming thread would have left that case returning the child's epoch.

SCOPE:
- `implementation/epoch/src/re_frame/epoch/state.cljc`: the fallback is removed from `note-commit!` and `take-observed-commit!`, and the comment is rewritten.
- `tool_pair.cljc`: the `perform-replay!` docstring now says `:epoch-id` is also nil when the replay committed none.
- `implementation/epoch/test/re_frame/epoch_replay_cljs_test.cljc`: the new tests.

- `quiet-replay-alone-reports-nil` (JVM and CLJS): the bead's step 6 control.

The pre-existing neighbours still pin ordinary traced replay, same-thread listener nesting, rf2-k0nr thread isolation, queued-child retention/eviction and failed-dispatch cleanup.

title: mcp-base: preserve list and vector kinds through dedup pooling
description:
Make dedup pooling preserve EDN collection kind, including kinds nested inside pooled parent values. Lists and vectors with equal elements currently pool into one cache slot and both decode as whichever kind was visited first. This is the independently actionable split of rf2-fzbj.9 finding 3; its remediation fence remains in force until Mike rules who owns remediation.

Ownership and revision: tools_mcp_base, tools/mcp-base/src/re_frame/mcp_base/dedup.cljc, baseline 9e8ca973767f4ecff455421e48e1765d59783261. Revalidated at 4df6a3303c68c77ced1f84ce92178bed1d7f7879; owned paths unchanged from baseline. SOURCE_ROOT=C:/Users/miket/code/re-frame2; WORKTREE_ROOT=(none; read-only review).

Source: count-cacheable-element! lines 411-423, repeated-cacheable? 437-445 and check-in-cache 456-470 pool by hash and Clojure = alone. Equal lists/vectors have equal hashes. The exact-inverse promise is at 482-487 and spec/dedup.md; test/re_frame/mcp_base/dedup_test.cljc:425-449 expressly pins collection-kind preservation but never puts equal lists and vectors together.

Reproducer (real JVM Clojure 1.12.0):

```clojure
(require '[re-frame.mcp-base.dedup :as d])
(d/expand (d/de-dupe-eq (array-map :list '(1 2 3) :vector [1 2 3])))
;; => {:list (1 2 3), :vector (1 2 3)}
(d/expand (d/de-dupe-eq (array-map :vector [1 2 3] :list '(1 2 3))))
;; => {:vector [1 2 3], :list [1 2 3]}
```

Expected: the list remains a list and the vector remains a vector in either insertion order. Actual: both use the first visited kind. The fresh public dedup-value probe asserts a real multi-slot wrapper for both cases, proves equality still passes, and asserts type predicates fail. A nested counterexample, {:list {:child '(1 2 3)} :vector {:child [1 2 3]}}, also loses the vector kind because the containing maps pool as equal. A same-kind repeated-vector control compresses and round-trips correctly.

Impact: the agent receives different printed EDN and different list?/vector? semantics, affecting code copied or reconstructed from inspected state. This is P3 fidelity loss; no JSON-value corruption is claimed, since JSON maps both kinds to arrays. Story tools/wire_pipeline.cljc:127-161 reprints dedup output into its EDN text slot, demonstrating the relevant consumer seam without claiming complete integration execution.

Repair: use one wire-shape-aware equivalence consistently in counting, repeat detection and cache lookup. It must distinguish vector from list/seq recursively, including children of containing maps, rather than adding only a top-level kind tag. Retain equality pooling within a wire kind and the deliberately lossy sorted-to-unsorted policy. Do not switch to identity pooling or introduce another wire format.

Acceptance: cross-host .cljc tests cover equal list/vector values in both insertion orders and assert list?/vector? after expansion in addition to equality. Cover equal containing maps with differently shaped child sequences. Require real wrappers and retain same-kind compression plus disabled passthrough controls.

Validation: ai/surface-review-20260913/tools_mcp_base/probe-tools_mcp_base-1.clj ran unmodified absolute-path sources using cached Clojure 1.12.0/spec jars and Java; .log records the source URL, both insertion orders and nested counterexample; .exit is 0 because these current defects and controls were observed. No build, install, source edit, server or Git mutation. CLJS, full MCP transport and broad suites were not executed; this is not a passing correctness gate.

Deduplication: current all-status dedup title and MCP list/vector description searches found no independently actionable dedicated owner. rf2-fzbj.9 is the aggregate; rf2-fzbj.31 expressly points to it. Current reads and bounded newest-first history preserve closed rf2-kjv05 literal-escaping and rf2-7wwp comparator-lowering decisions. Closed rf2-ntbd1 rejects relocating the diff codec; no relocation is proposed. Preserve prior issue statuses/notes and the remediation fence. This is review work only.
notes:
=== VERDICT (worker mcpbase-a, 2026-09-13): ALL THREE FINDINGS FIXED IN PR #9752 ===

Re-verified at tip before fixing. The rf2-fzbj.9 review probe was copied to scratch and run against this branch's own sources at 6186726167. It reproduced all three counterexamples exactly as filed. tools/mcp-base had not changed since the review baseline.

WHAT LANDED. Only tools/mcp-base changed. The wire shape is unchanged: the :rf.mcp/dedup-table envelope, the reference grammar, the de-dupe.cache/cache-N slot spelling and the allocation order are all as before.
- rf2-gwye.30 (finding 1): de-dupe-eq now threads each slot id through the substitution walk as a return value. Metadata is never read. A unique map carrying caller :cache-id metadata passes through verbatim.
- rf2-gwye.31 (finding 2): a new rebuild-record is used by both the forward walk and expand. It rebuilds every entry first, dissocs each original key whose spelling changed, then writes. A respelled extension key no longer survives beside its replacement, and an entry whose new spelling is another entry's old one cannot overwrite that entry before it is read.
- rf2-gwye.32 (finding 3): counting, the repeat check and slot lookup all use wire=. That is = refined by same-kinds?, which separates vector from list/seq at every depth, including map keys and set elements. Pooling within a kind is plain equality as before, and sorted collections still lower to unsorted.
- tools/mcp-base/spec/dedup.md gains two paragraphs recording the three rules.

REGRESSION TESTS, RED THEN GREEN. Six cross-host deftests are in tools/mcp-base/test/re_frame/mcp_base/dedup_test.cljc:

- caller-cache-id-metadata-beside-a-real-repeat-expands-exactly
- record-extension-keys-are-replaced-not-duplicated
- equal-lists-and-vectors-keep-their-kind

They were committed ahead of the fix (f3fe037d05) and run against the unmodified codec:

- CLJS: 55 / 332, 15 failures, exit 1.
Every new test was red at least once and every control passed. After the fix (9136625872) both hosts read 0 failures on the same counts.

The fix lives entirely in the codec, whose cross-host tests pin it, and the pin would sit outside the dispatched tools/mcp-base surface.

NOT TOUCHED.

== AUDIT'S "NO RUNTIME DEFECT ALLEGED" PREMISE STANDS AS WRITTEN.

new harness, no per-control matrix -- the bounds this item set were held.

      number the migration landed.

=== THE FINDING WORTH KEEPING: L3 AND THEME ARE NOT INTERCHANGEABLE, AND THE ITEM SAID THEY WERE.

This item's own description offers "an actual L3 or theme control", and my brief repeated it. THE
THEME TOGGLE CANNOT CARRY A FRAME-ROUTING WITNESS AT ALL. Its read
`[:rf.xray/setting :theme nil]` falls through `settings/subs.cljs` to `config/get-setting`, which is
a PROCESS-GLOBAL ATOM rather than any frame's app-db. Two shells at two frames therefore see ONE
theme, so a theme click can witness that a handler was reached and NOTHING about where the write
landed -- which is precisely the half this item exists to establish.

The worker used the L3 tab instead and recorded the reason in the file, so the next author does not
spend an afternoon rediscovering it. That is the right place for it.

GENERALISE IT RATHER THAN FILING IT AGAIN: a control backed by process-global state cannot witness
frame routing, whatever it is wired to. When a witness needs to prove WHERE a write landed, check
that the thing being read is per-frame before building the row around it.

AND NOTE HOW THE NEGATIVE CONTROL WAS MADE HONEST: the second live frame was loaded with a distinct
non-default tab BEFORE the mount. Held at the `:epoch` default, a misrouted write of `:epoch` would
have been indistinguishable from no write at all -- the row would have passed on a broken
dispatcher.

=== A PRECEDENT EXISTED AT TIP AND MY BRIEF DID NOT MENTION IT. MY MISS, RECORDED SO IT STOPS.

`static/routes/panel_fresco_boundary_dom_cljs_test.cljs` already carries this exact pair for a
Static panel -- residue via `quiesced!`, plus a click-into-named-frame row -- and the static shell
suite already has a `click!` helper and a release/reopen W4. The worker reused those instrument
shapes rather than inventing, and did not copy the suites.

My own dispatch preamble carries the rule that produced this: "the cheapest guard is the tree, not
the item -- before you brief or build X, check whether X ALREADY EXISTS AT TIP." That is twice in
one session I have briefed without running it.

=== SCOPE DECISIONS THE WORKER MADE THAT I ENDORSE

  * WHOLE-COLLECTOR CENSUS over enumerating the seven boundaries' reads. Enumerating is the
    per-control matrix this item forbids, and it would go stale the first time a region gains a
    read.
  * SABOTAGE STAYED INSIDE THE TEST FILE. "Misroute the dispatcher" most directly means editing
    `shell.cljs`, which was fenced to another worker; both faults were simulated in the test and
    both still reddened and named the fault. Correct call -- the fence held and the evidence is
    still real.

BOTH COLOURS, since a witness that has never gone red is not yet evidence:
  W3 plant (dispatcher misrouted to the second frame) -> 4 reds, the cross-frame control naming
     where it went: `(not (= :machines :trace))`.
  W4 plant (release skipped; container detached, root never unmounted) -> 8 reds, and the reopen
     caught the accumulation exactly: cell-refs 16->32, boundaries 7->14, edges 16->32.
  All 12 failures inside the two new rows, no other namespace reddened, counts identical to the
  control (939/5215) -- so neither plant crashed the lane or silenced a neighbour. Restore verified
  by blob hash in the DEFAULT filtered form, then green again: green -> red -> green.

=== THE FEATURE GATE WAS CONSIDERED AND DECLINED, MEASURED RATHER THAN ASSUMED

16 scenarios, 5 smoke. `feature matrix shell and panel handoff` does walk every L3 tab, so it

and NO scenario measures collector state at all (`residue`, `cell-readers`, `reader-edges` all read
0 across `scenarios.cjs`). So it is not the gate for this surface, and saying so is better than
running it for form.

Its read falls through settings/subs.cljs to config/get-setting, a PROCESS-GLOBAL ATOM rather than any frame's app-db, so two shells at two frames see ONE theme -- a theme click can witness that a handler was reached and nothing about where the write landed, which is the entire half this item exists to establish. title: docs/EP/EP-template.md missed the corpus census: 8 escaped continuations + 2 markers rendering as text
description:
`docs/EP/EP-template.md` was INVISIBLE to the corpus census that drove PR #9628, and it carries two independent list-rendering defects. Neither is on any existing list. === FINDING 1: 8 ESCAPED CONTINUATION LINES -- speccont-a's measurement, RELAYED, NOT REPRODUCED === Reported by worker `speccont-a` while completing rf2-fwlj Group 2 (PR #9633, merged ce57e7a337). Labelled as its measurement because I did NOT reproduce it, and the reason is structural rather than lazy: the only instrument for this class is a probe the workers are FORBIDDEN to commit, because committing one would settle rf2-jzv2's undecided gate half by the back door. So the number cannot currently be re-derived without rebuilding the probe. Rebuild it before acting. WHY THE FILE WAS MISSED, which is the part that generalises: it was UNMEASURABLE to the census (reported `unclosed `) until `8bea22404f` (#9625) escaped its placeholders at 19:37. #9628 merged at 19:57 from a branch cut BEFORE that, so its census never saw the file at all. A file can therefore enter the corpus between a census and the sweep that census authorised, and nothing about the sweep's own green says so. THE ARITHMETIC CLOSES EXACTLY, which is the corroboration: 268 + 8 - 22 = 254, being 241 mayor-method (repaired by #9632), 5 `spec/Design-TransducerRouter.md` (deliberately NOT repairable by reindentation, left alone), and these 8. After #9632 and #9633 the standing corpus should be 5 + 8 = 13. RE-MEASURE that; it is the cheapest check that this bead is still live. === FINDING 2: 2 LIST MARKERS RENDER AS LITERAL TEXT -- my own measurement === Measured at trunk ce57e7a337 by rendering the file with python-markdown (extensions=[extra]) and asking, for each source marker, whether its text lands inside an `
  • ` or a `

    `: :46 "* standards-track - changes the fr..." renders in

    :52 "* process - rules about how the pr..." renders in

    This is the SAME class as rf2-n5as (a marker directly beneath a paragraph line with no blank line is a lazy continuation), and it is evidence that the class is CORPUS-WIDE rather than confined to `docs/the-mayor-method/`. A third instance was found and fixed in `spec/009-Instrumentation.md` by #9633, where the five-surfaces list rendered as a one-item `

      `. === THESE ARE TWO DIFFERENT CLASSES AND MUST NOT BE CONFLATED === Finding 1 is a CONTINUATION line escaping its owning list item. Finding 2 is a MARKER that never becomes a list item at all. They have different instruments and different fixes -- reindentation for the first, an inserted blank line for the second -- and #9633 measured that on 009 the two interact: reindent alone bought nothing (1 `
        `/1 `
      1. `), blank lines alone fragmented the list (3/5), and only both together rendered it as authored (1/5). So do not assume fixing one fixes the other, and measure the rendering after each. === SCOPE NOTE === `docs/EP/` is a template tree. Check whether the strict docs build even reaches it before nominating `mkdocs build --strict` as a gate: `mkdocs.yml`'s `exclude_docs` block keeps several trees out of the site, and a page outside `docs_dir` was never a candidate for exclusion in the first place. Neither of the two link gates inspects fenced blocks, and NOTHING validates markdown list rendering anywhere in this repo -- which is why both findings survived to be found by hand.
notes:
== BOTH FINDINGS REFUTED, 2026-09-10 (worker listrender-a, alongside PR #9637) == `docs/EP/EP-template.md` NEEDS NO CHANGE, and PR #9637 does not touch it. One fact accounts for both findings: SOURCE LINES 7-92 ARE A SINGLE HTML COMMENT -- the authoring guidance an EP author is told to delete before opening the PR (`` at :92). Every line either finding cites is inside it. FINDING 2 ("2 list markers render as literal text", :46 and :52) -- REFUTED TWO WAYS. 1. They do not render as literal text; they do not render AT ALL. Verified in the BUILT page, not only in a probe: in `site/EP/EP-template/index.html` after `python -m mkdocs build --strict`, the nearest preceding `` (offset 13633), so the text is inside a comment and invisible to the reader. 2. There is no lazy continuation there to repair anyway. The class-1 fix is an inserted blank line, and SOURCE LINES 45 AND 51 ARE ALREADY BLANK. Nothing about the source shape is wrong. The probe reports these two as "no text node" rather than "outside every li" -- python-markdown emits the whole block as a raw comment, so no TEXT node carries the sentinel at all. A probe that searched the HTML as a STRING instead of walking text nodes would find the marker present and not inside an `
  • `, which is exactly the reading that produced this finding. FINDING 1 ("8 escaped continuation lines", relayed from speccont-a) -- REFUTED, and the 8 looks like a CANDIDATE count read as an ESCAPE count. The file has exactly 8 candidate continuation lines (:47-:50 and :53-:56) and 0 escapes. The eight are the continuation lines of the two commented-out bullets above, so they are inside the same comment: all eight report "no text node". THE INSTRUMENT WAS REBUILT FROM SCRATCH AND SELF-TESTED BOTH WAYS BEFORE BEING TRUSTED, as the brief required. Union rule as specified -- rendered li-depth < the owner marker's own rendered li-depth, OR outside every `
  • `. Over the nine `docs/api` files as they stood at 8cb22c0de5^ (pre-#9620) it reads 84, per file 27/26/18/4/3/2/2/1/1, matching #9620's own census exactly; over the same nine files as #9620 merged them it reads 0. CORPUS ARITHMETIC DOES NOT CLOSE AT 13. Measured over the gate's own 291-file corpus at 34c25ebd83 and again at 806c4f12af: the standing escaped-continuation corpus is 5, all in `spec/Design-TransducerRouter.md`, which #9628 deliberately left because they are not repairable by reindentation. The 8 was stale. WHAT IS TRUE AND IS NOT ON EITHER BEAD: the class-1 defect is corpus-wide -- 205 markers across 29 files after PR #9637. Filed as rf2-2brt. Two of that 205 are these two, and should be subtracted before anyone counts a repair complete. == MAYOR CORRECTION, 2026-09-10: FINDING 2 IS REFUTED. FINDING 1 STANDS. == FINDING 2 — "2 list markers render as literal text" at :46 and :52 — IS NOT A DEFECT, and the finding was mine. rf2-2brt measured it at the renderer and in the BUILT page: both markers sit inside the HTML COMMENT spanning source lines 7-92, so they render as NOTHING AT ALL rather than as literal text. There is nothing to repair and nothing for a reader to see. HOW I GOT IT WRONG, twice over, and both are recorded on rf2-n5as in full: * My probe asked whether each marker's text lands in an `
  • ` or a `

    `. That reading reports healthy LOOSE list items as broken, because a continuation block makes a list loose and python-markdown then wraps every item's text in a `

    `. The correct question is which `

  • ` INSTANCE the marker landed in. * I rendered with `extensions=['extra']` rather than the eleven extensions mkdocs' own config loader produces. Neither error is what caught THIS one, though: a marker inside an HTML comment would have fooled a correct reading of my kind too, because I never asked whether the source line was inside a comment at all. The lesson is the narrower one — ASK WHETHER THE SOURCE IS EVEN RENDERED before asking how it renders. FINDING 1 STANDS AND IS STILL THE POINT OF THIS BEAD: the 8 ESCAPED CONTINUATION LINES, which are a DIFFERENT CLASS (reindentation, not blank lines) and were reported by worker `speccont-a`. title: docs: 458 escaped continuation lines remain corpus-wide, and NO gate detects the class
description:
THE ESCAPED-CONTINUATION CLASS IS NOT GATE-PROTECTED, AND A CLOSED BEAD SAID IT WAS.

458 escaped continuation lines remain corpus-wide after PR #9620 took `docs/api` from 84 to 0
(542 at that base). Measured by the continuation probe rebuilt under rf2-6ml6 -- a sentinel
injected into each candidate continuation line, asking whether it landed inside an `<li>` --
with pipe-bearing lines excluded from injection, which is what made the three previously
"refused" files measurable.

=== WHY THIS IS ITS OWN BEAD: THE GATE DOES NOT SEE THIS CLASS ===

rf2-luch's close reason asserted "the remainder is gate-enforced from now on, so it cannot
grow". THAT IS REFUTED and has been corrected on that bead. `scripts/check_flattened_lists.py`
gates flattened NESTING, not escaped CONTINUATIONS: `_pair_defect` requires
`cur_at.root == prev_at.root` (line 435; the rule statement at line 56 says "two
document-consecutive items SHARING A ROOT LIST"), and an escaped continuation SPLITS the root
list, so the pair is never compared.

MAYOR-VERIFIED with a control taken both ways, at trunk 8cb22c0de5:
  - gate on trunk, this class present  -> exit 0
  - flattened list planted in a TRACKED file -> exit 1   (the gate is live)
  - restored to a byte-identical hash  -> exit 0
A FIRST CONTROL OF MINE WAS INVALID and is recorded because the failure is reusable: I planted
into an UNTRACKED file and read exit 0, concluding the gate was dead. `_tracked_markdown`
enumerates with `git ls-files`, so an untracked file is invisible to it. A probe file must be
tracked, or the instrument never sees it.

So this class can grow silently. Nothing reports it.

=== WHERE IT IS, LARGEST FIRST ===

    docs/the-mayor-method/loops.md                    166
    docs/EP/EP-0012                                    81
    docs/the-mayor-method/dispatch-prompt-template.md  75
    spec/, 8 files                                     31
    plus 19 further indented TABLE blocks under list items outside docs/api

1. THE REPAIR. `docs/api` proved it is mechanical and safe: 211/211, `git diff -w` EMPTY, no
   prose touched. The same should hold elsewhere. But the two largest carriers are
   `docs/the-mayor-method/` pages, which are held to a STRICTER rule than the rest of the
   corpus -- their fences are pasteable deliverables and a doc link inside a fence is itself
   reported -- so that tree wants its own pass and its own care, not a corpus-wide sweep.

2. WHETHER TO EXTEND THE GATE to this class at all. That is a NEW PERMANENT OBLIGATION and gets
   its own decision rather than riding on a repair, exactly as rf2-7ntc reasons about the SSR
   roster. Note the argument is stronger here than usual: the defect is the most reader-facing
   markdown fault measured in this corpus (the bullet list VISIBLY splits in two with body prose
   stranded between the halves), it is silent, and the instrument already exists and is proven.
   The cost is that the probe is a renderer round-trip, which is slower than the current gate's
   line walk.

decided about the gate.

title: xray: mount-app-db-diff! cannot name an instance, so two standalone mounts in one frame still collide
description:
`panels/mount-app-db-diff!` passes `Panel-bridge` to `render-panel!`, which mounts
`[panel-view]` with **NO props** — so two STANDALONE mounts sharing a `:frame` opt still
cannot be told apart, even though rf2-t3fz gave the Panel an `:instance-id` prop and both
the Fresco and Reagent doors carry it today.

=== WHAT rf2-t3fz DID AND DID NOT CLOSE ===

rf2-t3fz (PR #9605, merged 7886452fd0) added an optional `:instance-id` prop to `Panel`,
threaded `panel-tree` -> `state-body` -> the section renderers -> `value-body`, so that
naming an instance qualifies BOTH the edn-inspector `:mount-id` AND the expansion/zoom
`:site-id`. That closes the case where a CALLER can pass props.

**This bead is the case where it cannot.** The mount entry point takes opts, not props, and
nothing in those opts reaches the Panel as an `:instance-id`. So the affordance exists and
one door does not open onto it.

=== WHY IT WAS NOT DONE IN rf2-t3fz, AND THIS IS THE PART TO PRESERVE ===

The change is an `:instance-id` key on `mount-app-db-diff!`'s opts in
`tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/panels.cljs` — and `panels.cljs` is SHARED across panel
slices. Its own rule, recorded on rf2-k97c.3, is narrow and worth quoting rather than
paraphrasing: *a panel slice that changes its own `mount-*!` caller line collides with any
other slice that does; a slice that does not, does not.*

The rf2-t3fz worker stopped at that boundary rather than crossing it, and was right to.
A citation is not permission.

=== SEQUENCING ===

`panels.cljs` is the collision surface, so this wants to be the ONLY thing touching a
`mount-*!` caller line while it is in flight. It is small — one opts key, its threading into
the `render-panel!` call, and a row proving two standalone mounts with different
`:instance-id` values get distinct `mount-id` and `site-id`.

=== EVIDENCE STANDARD ===

The same one rf2-t3fz met, and it is not optional here because the failure is invisible:
assert on what the two mounts actually RECEIVE, not on what was passed. rf2-t3fz's own
sabotage signature is the model — restoring the shared identity produced
`(contains? nil :ref)` for the survivor after the other detached, which is the bug rather
than a proxy for it. A row that asserts an opts key was threaded is a hollow gate; delete
the signal and keep the fault.

Report the `^{:key ...}`-on-a-call-form census for whatever panels you read, INCLUDING zero,
per the standing direction on rf2-k97c.3 — and take a live control so a zero means absence
rather than a broken instrument.
notes:

The mayor confirmed the sequencing constraint before filing: panels.cljs is shared across panel slices and its narrow rule -- only a slice changing its own mount-*! caller line collides -- is recorded on rf2-k97c.3.

title: gate: check_flattened_lists.py - render markdown and fail on a flattened nested list
description:
rf2-3bq6 asked whether a GATE is wanted for the flattened-nested-list class. The
answer measured while fixing it is YES, and the evidence is direct.

=== NOTHING CATCHES IT, MEASURED RATHER THAN ASSUMED ===

On a tree carrying one deliberately re-flattened list item (a four-space child pushed
back to two), on the repaired branch:

    scripts/check_doc_slugs.py --verbose      exit 0
    python -m mkdocs build --strict           exit 0

Both green over a real defect. The whole 42-script check suite is green over it too;
none of them look at list structure. A flattened list is valid markup, so there is no
warning for `--strict` to promote. That is why 205 sites accumulated.

=== THE RULE IS EXPRESSIBLE WITHOUT AN ALLOWLIST ===

Measured over the 488 tracked markdown files under docs/, spec/ and migration/, the
rendering detector produced ZERO false positives that needed excusing. Its output is
205 defects across 49 files, every one of which is a genuine flattening. There is no
per-file allowlist and no tolerance list. Contrast the indentation heuristic in
rf2-3bq6, which read 209 across 45 with 23 false positives - the difference is
entirely that one reasons about spaces and the other about rendering.

One file cannot be measured and the detector says so rather than guessing:
docs/EP/EP-template.md renders a `<Title>` placeholder as an unclosed HTML tag, which
derails the HTML walker. It has zero defects by both instruments and its two candidate
list lines sit inside an HTML comment, so nothing is lost - but a gate needs an
explicit UNMEASURABLE verdict rather than a silent pass.

=== THE INSTRUMENT, WHICH ALREADY EXISTS AND WAS EXERCISED BOTH WAYS ===

Built for rf2-3bq6 and run over the whole corpus; not committed, because a gate is its
proper home. The method, in enough detail to rebuild it:

  1. Load the extension list and config through `mkdocs.config.load_config`, not by
     transcribing `markdown_extensions` from mkdocs.yml. MkDocs adds `toc`, `tables`
     and `fenced_code` as builtins, so the real list is eleven extensions where the
     yaml declares nine, and rf2-3bq6's own description names only four.
  2. Enumerate list-item lines in the source, skipping fenced blocks.
  3. Inject a unique sentinel into each item's content and render.
  4. VALIDATE the injection: the sentinel render with sentinels removed must equal the
     baseline render. Otherwise report UNMEASURABLE.
  5. Walk the HTML; per sentinel record enclosing `ul`/`ol` count, whether it is inside
     an `li`, and its root list element. Handle `handle_comment` separately - text in
     an HTML comment is never rendered, so a flat list there is not a defect.
  6. DEFECT: document-consecutive items sharing a root list where the source indents
     deeper but the rendered depth does not increase.

Exercised in both directions, which is the property that makes its all-clear worth
anything: the four-space sample reports no defect, the two-space sample reports one,
a six-space grandchild of a four-space child reports one, and list-shaped lines inside
a fence are skipped. 34 such checks, all passing.

=== SHAPE ===

`scripts/check_flattened_lists.py`, with `--self-test`, matching the repo idiom. Its
natural home is `test.yml`'s `verify-readme-links` job, which already runs
`check_doc_slugs.py` and `check_readme_links.py` unguarded on every PR and is the
existing home for markdown-structure checks. Roots: docs/, spec/, migration/ - the
trees the strict build renders, spec/ and migration/ because `mkdocs_hooks.py`'s
`on_pre_build` stages them into `docs_dir`.

COST: rendering 488 files twice each takes a few minutes locally, which is more than
the seconds `check_doc_slugs.py` costs. Worth measuring whether to render only files
the PR touches; the detector is per-file and has no cross-file state, so a
changed-files scope is sound.

DEPENDENCY: do not arm it until the sweep is complete, or it fails on arrival. 4 sites
remain in docs/ and 70 in spec/ + migration/ - see the sibling beads.

title: release: nothing guards Story's reagent-slim exclusion against deletion (clojure -Stree and both preflights are blind to the collision)
description:
PR #9542 (rf2-qvyr) added an exclusion of `day8/reagent-slim` from Story's Xray edge in
`tools/story/deps.edn`. It is load-bearing: without it a published Story consumer resolves TWO
providers of `re-frame.adapter.reagent`, and which one wins flips on the consumer's own unrelated
dependency choices. **Nothing in the tree would catch its deletion.**

WHY THE OBVIOUS GATES CANNOT: measured under rf2-qvyr. `clojure -Stree` exits 0 and prints a healthy
tree over the colliding graph in BOTH consumer shapes, and a complete pom is equally consistent with
it. Worse, the two release preflights actively REQUIRE both providers into the poms —
`preflight-xray-package.sh` derives its required set from every `:local/root`, which includes slim.
So the instruments that look authoritative here are precisely the ones blind to it. The discriminator
that DID work was runtime `:kind` self-identification off a real classpath.

THE PROPOSED SHAPE, from the rf2-qvyr worker, which deliberately did not implement it under that
bead's authority: roughly ten lines in `preflight-story-package.sh`, which already parses the Story
pom — assert the emitted `<exclusions>` carries `day8/reagent-slim` on the Xray edge. No new gate, no
new workflow, no new job: the assertion goes inside a preflight that already runs.

WHY IT IS WORTH TEN LINES RATHER THAN NOTHING: the exclusion looks like tidy-up to anyone who meets
it cold, so the deletion is plausible rather than exotic; and the failure it prevents is silent at
build time and surfaces only as a wrong adapter in a consumer's app. Set against the standing
posture — trust the programmer, do not build machinery — ten lines inside an existing parser is the
cheap end, and no wrapper, registry or new subsystem is authorised here.

OUT OF SCOPE: the pre-existing case where a consumer pins `day8/reagent-slim` DIRECTLY alongside
Story and still gets two providers. Story's direct `day8/re-frame2-reagent` dep is irreducible, and
settling that is the adapter re-architecture rf2-qvyr explicitly rules out. Do not widen into it.

SEQUENCE: before the tools-tier tag (rf2-pv7p / rf2-kmqx3), since the guard's whole value is holding
the exclusion in place across a release. Isolated surface — one script.
close_reason:
SHIPPED in PR #9554 (`808b6eeb11` on trunk after fast-forward), merged at band 87 on all five clauses.

Grading, re-measured this tick rather than quoted: band 87 confirmed across the five previously
merged PRs (#9552, #9551, #9549, #9548, #9547, all 87); #9554's own rollup 87 distinct; 0
failure-or-cancelled; 0 non-terminal; all four workflow runs (portability, lint, docs, tests)
completed at the full 40-character head oid 503cd68e4f64913f0c13673ada68fd1341707754; workflow
diff against merge-base 6a73a16a7d = 0 lines and 0 job keys, so the check set was unchanged
against trunk; `git merge-tree --write-tree` rc=0, mergeable being a separate fact from green.

Story's release preflight now asserts the load-bearing `day8/reagent-slim` exclusion on its
`day8/re-frame2-xray` pom edge, and the guard is proved to bite rather than merely to exist.

TWO THINGS THE WORKER GOT RIGHT THAT THE BRIEF HAD WRONG, both recorded because they change how
the next release-gate bead should be briefed:

1. The deletion test AS SPECIFIED IS IMPOSSIBLE in-tree. `clein pom` skips `:local/root`
   coordinates, so a preflight run over the unrewritten `deps.edn` reds for five MISSING
   dependencies and the exclusion assertion never gets to speak. The worker built the real
   release chain instead — the real `rewrite-local-root-coord.sh` over all five roots, stub
   `day8/*` artefacts in a local Maven repo at a probe version, then the real preflight with a
   real `clein pom` — which is what makes the red genuinely attributable to the deletion.

2. The load-bearing premise had never been verified anywhere: nothing had shown `clein pom`
   emits an exclusions element at all. It does (verified on a throwaway project first, then on
   the real Story pom), and `rewrite-local-root-coord.sh` preserves the `:exclusions` key.
