load-bearing and aborting before deploy; restore verified by git BLOB hash
8b328f2bb78e67b6404b0424afcb9093c36273a5, byte-identical. A second independent plant (disarming
assertion 4 in the script, blob ff0333f4ce83847b24fc37ee416045708c44a1d5) turns the mirror test
red on exactly the two new cases and no others — which is also the proof the gate read the
worker's own worktree.

The mirror test needed a change in the same commit, correctly: it pins script output, and its
rewritten-pom fixture carried no exclusions element, so the existing passing case would have
gone red on its own.

One gate exit 1 in the worker's own table is honest and not this change: the post-rebase failure
was `_preflight-xray-package.test.cjs`, a file it never touched, dying on `python3: Resource
temporarily unavailable` under machine contention. It passes 15/15 in isolation and CI's
equivalent job is green — and CI, not a local run, is what the merge criterion grades.

Size ran to 33 executable lines rather than the brief's estimate of roughly ten; flagged by the
worker rather than absorbed, and well short of the stop signal.

AI-attribution trailers were declined on both the commit and the PR body.

title: hygiene: three FOREIGN-harness worktrees (~/.grok/) frozen 45 days hold no work, but no record says so
description:
`git worktree list` in this repo shows THREE worktrees belonging to a different harness, not to the
mayor's dispatch system. They have been frozen since 2026-07-26 and hold no work, but nothing records
that, so every hygiene sweep re-derives it from scratch — the same gap [[rf2-bipw]] exists to close for
orphan branches.

**THE THREE** (all under `C:/Users/miket/.grok/worktrees/code-re-frame2/`, named `subagent-<uuid>`):

    subagent-019f98e1-5e3a-75b0-ade5-52ed5083fdde
    subagent-019f98e1-5e3d-7fa0-9bd0-4e93e77df56b
    subagent-019f98e1-5e3d-7fa0-9bd0-4eaa8708b745

**MEASURED 2026-09-09 AUSEST, and the finding is that they hold NOTHING:**

  * All three are **detached HEAD at `0f6fa33cb7`** ("chore(beads): audit merged PR 6963",
    2026-07-25) — no branch is checked out in any of them (`branch refs/heads/` count: 0).
  * `0f6fa33cb7` **is an ancestor of `origin/main`**, so the commit they sit on is already trunk.
  * **10,753 commits behind** `origin/main`.
  * **0 stash entries** in each.
  * Each has **exactly ONE dirty file, and it is `.beads/issues.jsonl`** — which is precisely what
    `CLAUDE.md` § Beads durability says happens: "`bd` rewrites it in **every** checkout, so each
    worker worktree carries a snapshot of the tracker as it stood when that worktree was created."
    A July snapshot is the *last* thing anyone would want to keep; committing it time-travels the
    tracker.
  * Index write clocks frozen at **2026-07-26 02:43:2x**, i.e. ~45 days.

**So there is no work to lose.** No branch, no stash, no commit that is not already on trunk, and the
only modification is a stale tracker export that must never be committed anyway.

**WHY I DID NOT REMOVE THEM.** Two reasons, and the first is the binding one:

  1. **They are not mine.** The §5 reap test reads the AGENT'S OWN COMPLETION REPORT, and no report
     exists or can exist for another harness's subagents. "A frozen tip + frozen write clock is
     AMBIGUOUS, not death" — 45 days is strong evidence and still not the test. Movement proves life;
     stillness proves nothing.
  2. `scripts/remove-worker-worktree.sh` derives the worktree parent as the `re-frame2-worktrees`
     sibling of the mayor checkout. These live under `~/.grok/worktrees/`, **outside that parent**, so
     the script refuses them without an `RF2_WORKTREE_PARENT` override.

**THE JUNCTION HAZARD DOES NOT APPLY HERE — I checked, because it is the reason the bare command is
banned.** None of the three has `implementation/node_modules` at all (`exists=no`, `[ -L ]` no), so
there is no junction for a recursive delete to follow into the mayor's real tree. Mayor canary
concurrently healthy at **103 immediate entries with `.bin` present holding 27 executables**, counted
with `find -mindepth 1 -maxdepth 1` rather than bare `ls`, which omits dotfiles and would have been
blind to `.bin` (instrument item (i)).

**WHAT I WANT — one line.** Either "they are dead, remove them", in which case a plain
`git worktree remove --force` is safe HERE specifically because the junction check above came back
clean, followed by `git worktree prune`; or "leave them", in which case that reason gets recorded and
no future sweep re-opens it.

**NOTHING HAS BEEN DONE.** No worktree removed, no file touched, no prune run.
notes:
## INVESTIGATION 2026-09-09 (gitspace) — the description's finding is CONFIRMED independently. This note is the record it asked for.

Measured 2026-09-09 ~15:30 AUSEST, READ-ONLY: no worktree removed, no prune run, no file touched. I
re-derived every claim from scratch rather than reading them off the bead, because the bead's whole point
is that nothing records this and so each sweep re-derives it. It now needs deriving once more only if
somebody doubts the numbers below.

### The four questions, per worktree — all three answer identically

| Question | `subagent-…52ed5083fdde` | `subagent-…4e93e77df56b` | `subagent-…4eaa8708b745` |
|---|---|---|---|
| (a) git checkout, pointing where? | YES, registered; **detached** at `0f6fa33cb7` | same | same |
| (b) any commit not on `origin/main`? | **NO** | **NO** | **NO** |
| (c) uncommitted work? | 1 entry, `.beads/issues.jsonl`, and it is **STAGED** (`M ` in column 1) | same | same |
| (d) junction into shared deps? | **absent** — no `implementation/node_modules` at all | same | same |
| immediate entries | 34 | 34 | 34 |
| stash entries | 0 | 0 | 0 |

### Why (b) is a firm NO rather than an inference from HEAD alone

Checking HEAD by itself would not settle it — a worktree can hold objects reachable only from its own refs
or reflog. So I checked all three routes:

* `git merge-base --is-ancestor 0f6fa33cb7 origin/main` → **YES, ancestor**. The commit is
  `chore(beads): audit merged PR 6963`, 2026-07-25 20:44:13 +1000.
* **Worktree-local refs: 0.** `find <git-dir>/refs -type f` reads 0 in each (their git-dirs are
  `.git/worktrees/subagent-…` under the mayor checkout).
* **HEAD reflog entries: 0** in each, so there is no dangling tip a detached checkout might otherwise
  have left behind.

**Correction to one figure, and it is the expected kind:** the bead recorded 10,753 commits behind; today
it reads **10,791**. Trunk moved. Nothing else in the description needed correcting.

### The one dirty file is the same object in all three, and it is already in the object store

The staged blob for `.beads/issues.jsonl` is `36c019fd7dc03c57fbffe048a914e0eeb43938f8` — **identical
across all three worktrees**. Because it is staged rather than merely modified, git has already written it
as an object, so even that stale July export is recoverable and nothing is lost by discarding the working
state. It is exactly what CLAUDE.md § Beads durability predicts: a July snapshot of a full-database export,
which must never be committed because committing it time-travels the tracker.

### So the finding stands: THERE IS NO WORK TO LOSE.

No branch, no worktree-local ref, no reflog entry, no stash, no off-trunk commit, and the sole modification
is a stale tracker export already present as a git object.

### Proposed disposition: REMOVE — but the reasoning that blocked it before is still sound, so this is a call for the operator, not a fait accompli

The bead declined to remove on two grounds. The first — "they are not mine; the reap test reads the agent's
own completion report, and no report exists or can exist for another harness's subagents" — I cannot
discharge from inside this repo, and I want to be plain about that: **whether a foreign harness still
considers these live cannot be determined from here.** Stillness is not death. What I *can* now say is that
the question has been made cheap, because the answer no longer matters much: even if that harness came back
to them tomorrow, it would find a detached checkout 10,791 commits stale whose only content is a July
tracker export it must not commit. There is nothing for it to resume.

The second ground — that `scripts/remove-worker-worktree.sh` derives the worktree parent as the
`re-frame2-worktrees` sibling and so refuses these — I confirm: they live under `~/.grok/worktrees/`,
outside that parent. **Do not reach for `RF2_WORKTREE_PARENT` to force that script onto them.** It is not
needed: the script's whole reason for existing is the junction unlink, and there is no junction here.

**If the call is "remove":** `git worktree remove --force <path>` for each, then `git worktree prune`. That
is safe HERE specifically because `find -type l` reads 0 and `implementation/node_modules` is absent in all
three — re-check that immediately before removing rather than citing this note, since it is a fact measured
on one day. Reclaims very little space; the value is that `git worktree list` stops carrying three rows
every hygiene sweep must re-adjudicate.

**If the call is "leave":** that is defensible on the "not ours to reap" ground alone, and this note is then
the record that stops the next sweep re-deriving it. Either way the deliverable the bead asked for — a
durable record that they hold nothing — now exists on the bead.

### Gates

No tracked file was changed, so no gate applies and there is no PR.
--- MAYOR RULING 2026-09-09 19:0x AUSEST: REMOVE. Blocked at execution by a permission classifier; the command is below for the operator. ---

THE CALL IS "REMOVE", not "leave". Reasons, in order of weight:
1. They hold nothing. Re-verified at source this session, not cited from the note below: all three detached at `0f6fa33cb7`, which `git merge-base --is-ancestor HEAD origin/main` confirms IS an ancestor of trunk; 0 stash entries each; the ONLY dirty file in each is `.beads/issues.jsonl`, which is a regenerable whole-database export and the last thing anyone would want to keep from July; `find -type l` reads 0 in each (the junction hazard is absent); `implementation/node_modules` is absent in all three.
2. The cost of leaving them is recurring and the cost of removing them is one-off. Every hygiene sweep re-adjudicates three rows in `git worktree list`, which is exactly what this bead was filed to stop.
3. "Not ours to reap" is the honest counter-argument and it loses: they are registered in THIS repository's worktree list, so they are this repository's liability whoever created them.

ONE CORRECTION TO MY OWN INSTRUMENT, recorded because it read plausibly and was wrong. I probed "branches" with `git for-each-ref refs/heads | wc -l` and got 32 for each worktree. That is the repository's SHARED ref set — worktrees share `refs/heads` — not the branches checked out in the worktree. The note below is right and my probe was measuring something else; `git worktree list` shows all three as `(detached HEAD)`, which is the fact that matters. Anyone re-deriving this should read the detachment from `git worktree list`, not from a ref count.

EXECUTION IS BLOCKED, NOT DEFERRED. The mayor attempted the removal and Claude Code's auto-mode permission classifier refused the recursive delete. This is a harness boundary, not a change of mind. The commands, for an operator or a session with the permission:

    git worktree remove --force C:/Users/miket/.grok/worktrees/code-re-frame2/subagent-019f98e1-5e3a-75b0-ade5-52ed5083fdde
    git worktree remove --force C:/Users/miket/.grok/worktrees/code-re-frame2/subagent-019f98e1-5e3d-7fa0-9bd0-4e93e77df56b
    git worktree remove --force C:/Users/miket/.grok/worktrees/code-re-frame2/subagent-019f98e1-5e3d-7fa0-9bd0-4eaa8708b745
    git worktree prune

`scripts/remove-worker-worktree.sh` is correctly NOT the tool here, as the note below establishes: these live outside the worktree parent, and that script exists for the junction unlink, of which there is none here. Do not reach for `RF2_WORKTREE_PARENT` to force it onto them.

RE-CHECK BEFORE REMOVING rather than citing this ruling: `find <path> -type l | wc -l` must read 0 and `implementation/node_modules` must be absent. Both were measured on 2026-09-09 and both are facts about one day.

This bead stays OPEN until the removal lands, because the durable-record half it originally asked for is already delivered and the only thing outstanding is the act.
RETRY 2026-09-09 22:4x AUSEST, merge+dispatch tick. REFUSED AGAIN — the block is persistent, not a one-off.

Safety pre-checks re-run first and all five targets PASSED: symlinks 0, implementation/node_modules absent, on every path. So the refusal is the classifier, not a condition of the trees.

The exact call refused: `git worktree remove --force <path>` for the three ~/.grok worktrees, in Bash, auto mode. I did NOT retry through PowerShell or any other shell. Re-running the same recursive delete through a different shell would be working around the intent of the denial rather than using a different tool for the same benign act, and a 3.78 GB recursive delete is precisely what such a gate exists to hold. Recorded and surfaced to Mike instead.

WHAT UNBLOCKS IT: Mike runs the commands himself, or grants a Bash permission rule for them. Nothing else about either bead has changed; the rulings, the salvage verdicts and the re-check instructions all stand.
close_reason:
DONE 2026-09-09, on Mike's explicit permission after two classifier refusals.

Safety pre-checks re-run immediately before, on all three: `find <path> -type l | wc -l` read 0 and `implementation/node_modules` was absent — so the junction hazard the removal script exists for did not apply, exactly as this bead's earlier note ruled.

  git worktree remove --force .../subagent-019f98e1-5e3a-75b0-ade5-52ed5083fdde   exit 0
  git worktree remove --force .../subagent-019f98e1-5e3d-7fa0-9bd0-4e93e77df56b   exit 0
  git worktree remove --force .../subagent-019f98e1-5e3d-7fa0-9bd0-4eaa8708b745   exit 0

Nothing was salvaged because there was nothing to salvage — all three were detached HEAD, frozen 45 days, holding no work, which this bead established and re-confirmed from `git worktree list` rather than from a ref count.

title: beads: reopening a bead ERASES its close_reason — record it in CLAUDE.md beside the --notes trap
description:
`bd` clears `close_reason` and `closed_at` when a bead is reopened. The loss is silent, total, and lands precisely on the beads that matter most — this project treats close reasons as NORMATIVE RECORDS (a ruling is often the close reason of a closed dependency, which is why `bd gc`'s decay phase is banned and why the backlog-reread loop tells you to read there), and an audit reopening is the system working, so every audit reopening destroys the account of what the reopened change actually did.

MEASURED 2026-09-09 on rf2-dokz and rf2-z5lv, both closed by the mayor and reopened by the merged-PR audit within the hour: `close_reason_len=0`, `closed_at=null`, and a grep for a distinctive phrase from each close reason read 0 in `notes` — the text is not moved anywhere, it is gone. Control on a still-closed bead: `close_reason_len=5159`.

DETECTION IS NOT AVAILABLE THE OBVIOUS WAY, and that is worth stating because it is the probe a careful reader reaches for first: you CANNOT find reverted closures by listing non-terminal beads that still carry a `close_reason`. That reads 0 across the whole backlog even when reopenings have happened, because the reopen removes its own evidence.

RECOVERY IS COMPLETE AND CHEAP, BY TWO INDEPENDENT ROUTES, and both were exercised:
  1. `.beads/issues.jsonl` in git history. `scripts/beads-checkpoint.sh` exports the full record, so any checkpoint commit made while the bead was closed carries the text:
     `git show <commit>:.beads/issues.jsonl | jq -r --arg i <id> 'select(._type=="issue" and .id==$i) | (.close_reason // "" | length)'`
     The window can be narrow — for rf2-dokz exactly ONE of the last twelve checkpoints carried it.
  2. `bd history <id> --json`, whose nested `.Issue` snapshots carry it (4 entries did for rf2-dokz).
Restore with `bd update <id> --append-notes` (never `--notes`, which replaces), under a heading naming it a RESTORED CLOSE REASON and citing the commit, so nobody reads it as newer than the audit note below it.

## The deliverable

ONE bullet in `CLAUDE.md` § Beads durability, beside the existing `--notes` REPLACES bullet — same class (a silent field-level loss with a cheap git-history recovery), same section, and it should say so rather than repeat the recovery mechanics in full.

It must carry: the erasure itself; that it is silent and not copied to notes; WHY it bites here (close reasons are normative and reopenings are routine); that the obvious detection probe cannot work; both recovery routes with the `jq` identity-select form (NOT a bare grep — a bead id appears in other beads' prose, which is CLAUDE.md instrument item (f)); and the `--append-notes` restore.

ONE MORE CLAUSE, because it cost a real cycle: a dispatch brief that says "read the bead's CLOSE REASON" is UNSATISFIABLE on a reopened bead, and the worker reads the absence as its own failure. Two live workers were briefed that way on 2026-09-09 and had to be messaged mid-flight. So either restore the reason before dispatching, or do not cite it.

## Not in scope

No change to `bd`, no wrapper, no gate. This is a durable note about a tool's behaviour, and the stance says record it rather than build machinery against it.

## Gates

`CLAUDE.md` is repo-root markdown: `scripts/check_readme_links.py --ci` is the link gate; `scripts/check_doc_slugs.py` does NOT reach it and exits 0 on a broken link there; `mkdocs build --strict` does not cover it (`docs_dir` is `docs`). Nothing grades its prose. `CLAUDE.md` is a ONE-TOUCHER — sequence behind any live dispatch holding it.

Already recorded as the memory `reopening-a-bead-erases-its-close-reason`; this bead is for the tracked half.
notes:
NOT DISPATCHED ON FILING (mayor, 2026-09-09 01:1x AUSEST). Four workers are live and this is a durable
note about a tool's behaviour, not a red: nothing is broken on trunk, and the finding is already safe in
the memory `reopening-a-bead-erases-its-close-reason` and in the two restored notes on rf2-dokz and
rf2-z5lv. It goes out as soon as a slot frees.
`CLAUDE.md` was measured FREE at filing time — no live worktree's diff carries it — but it is a
one-toucher, so re-measure at dispatch rather than trusting this line.
close_reason:
Landed in PR #9516, merged at band 87 on all five clauses (0 non-terminal, 4 workflow runs completed at the full head oid `134c51008c`, no new job keys, merge-tree clean). One file, one line. **Verified on trunk after the fast-forward**: the bullet is present and `CLAUDE.md` is 142 lines, up from 141.

**THE WORKER REPRODUCED THE ERASURE ON ITS OWN THROWAWAY BEAD RATHER THAN TAKING MINE**, which is what makes the bullet a measurement instead of a relay. Bead `rf2-i834`, created and disposed of (closed again) at the end of the run, no other bead's status touched:

  after close  -> `close_reason` **419**, `closed_at` a timestamp, sentinel present **1**
  after reopen -> `close_reason` **0**,   `closed_at` **null**,      sentinel across the WHOLE stringified record **0**

`notes` read 0 before and after, and `bd` printed its ordinary success line on the reopen. The sentinel probe over the whole record — not merely `notes` — is the part that upgrades "not copied into notes" from an assumption to a finding.

BOTH RECOVERY ROUTES WERE EXERCISED, and one hazard was reproduced deliberately:
  * Route 2, `bd history rf2-i834 --json`, read `[0,419,0]` newest-first — exactly one snapshot carrying the sentinel.
  * Route 1, identity-select over checkpoints, found `rf2-dokz`'s 5181-character reason in **exactly 1 of the last 14** checkpoints — the narrow window, confirmed independently of my own measurement of 1-in-12.
  * **The bare-grep hazard was reproduced rather than described**: on checkpoint `4cbaba034c`, five records MENTION `rf2-dokz` and exactly one IS it, and `grep '"rf2-dokz"' | head -1 | jq` duly reported a `close_reason` length of **0** on the very checkpoint carrying 5181 characters of it. That is CLAUDE.md instrument item (f) failing in the reassuring direction, on the exact operation the bullet prescribes.
  * **The detection-probe premise was verified WITH A LIVE CONTROL**, which is what makes "the obvious probe cannot work" a claim rather than a shrug: 0 of 33 non-terminal beads carry a `close_reason`, against 1084 of 1085 closed ones that do. The probe is live; it simply cannot see this.

ONE CORRECTION THE WORKER MADE TO MY BRIEF: `MSYS_NO_PATHCONV=1` is NOT needed for `git show <sha>:.beads/issues.jsonl`, because a bare sha carries no slash — item (d) bites only when the REF and the PATH both do. It was left out of the bullet's command, correctly, since item (d) already covers the general case. (My own earlier measurement of trunk rows hit exactly that trap using `origin/main:` and read a false 0.)

GATES: `check_readme_links.py --ci` 0 — that is the gate for repo-root markdown; `check_doc_slugs.py` 0, run only to prove the split; `check_retired_composition_vocab.py` 0; `check-no-hardcoded-paths.sh` 0; attribution 0 on both the commit and the PR-body arms. `mkdocs build --strict` was NOT nominated, with the reason stated: `docs_dir` is `docs`, so repo-root markdown was never a candidate for `exclude_docs`, and absence from that block is not evidence of coverage.

SABOTAGE OF THE GATE SPLIT: a broken link planted mid-line into the new line 79 (match count 1, and mid-line rather than at line end so the CRLF trap could not silently no-op it). `check_doc_slugs.py` exit **0**, its log not mentioning the planted target at all; `check_readme_links.py --ci` exit **1**, naming `CLAUDE.md:79 -> docs/nonexistent-closereason-a-probe.md`. Restored and verified by blob hash `53845fec28a87e286ae17c712e6f44b75f60d135`.

**THE SECOND LIVENESS PLANT IS THE ONE WORTH KEEPING, because the worker caught a suppressor in its OWN text before trusting a green.** It read `check_retired_composition_vocab.py` first and found that on root-support markdown the architecture-prose family is what reads bare prose — and that its `_REMOVED_CONTEXT_RE` includes a bare `\bno\b`. The new bullet contains "no wrapper … no gate", so a plant there would have been SUPPRESSED and come back green: a fact about the plant, not about the gate. It planted after the last line instead, whose window carries no suppressor — match count 1, exit **1** naming `CLAUDE.md:144`. Restored, blob hash equal again.

CRLF WITH DIFF-STAT RECONCILIATION: before 68829 bytes / 141 CRLF / 0 bare LF / 0 bare CR; after 72659 / 142 / 0 / 0. Delta 3830 = 3828 bytes of bullet plus one CRLF, exact. `git diff --numstat` read `1 0 CLAUDE.md` — a CR-stripping rewrite would have shown 142 changed lines.

A HAZARD THE WORKER FLAGGED IN PASSING AND I THEN DISCHARGED: three `.grok/worktrees/code-re-frame2/subagent-*` harness worktrees each carry a STAGED `.beads/issues.jsonl`. Measured, committing one would resurrect ~1069 issues and destroy ~704 memories. **It is already guarded** — I verified empirically that `rf2_beads_in_primary_worktree` exits 1 from a `.grok` worktree (linked, so refused) and 0 from the mayor checkout, that `rf2_beads_is_permitted_path ".beads/issues.jsonl"` exits 1 against a `.beads/PRIME.md` control exiting 0, and that `git -C <grok-worktree> rev-parse --git-path hooks` resolves to the mayor's `.git/hooks` with `pre-commit` present and `core.hooksPath` unset. The guard holds for a harness nobody designed for because it derives the primary as the FIRST entry of `git worktree list --porcelain` rather than by the `re-frame2-worktrees` sibling convention. Recorded as the memory `grok-subagent-worktrees-staged-beads-already-guarded`.

title: gate(errors): check_thrown_error_messages.py has no notion of where-sym — 21 diagnostics still name symbols that do not resolve
notes:
Close the DEFECT CLASS behind rf2-z67m and rf2-0v23: a thrown error's `where-sym` can name a symbol that
does not resolve, sending an author who reads the message to a door that is not there. Eight sites have
been fixed one at a time; a check would stop the ninth being written.

MEASURED 2026-09-08 by the rf2-0v23 worker, with the extractor's own caveats recorded: a controlled sweep
of quoted `'rf/...` in where-sym argument position across implementation/**/src found 138 candidates, of
which 115 resolve and **21 DO NOT**. Named clusters: interceptor_registry.cljc x4 (resolve-interceptor-ref,
resolve-chain), adapters/test-react x4 (local-test-only), three `rf/render` (substrate/plain_atom.cljc:103,
substrate/spine.cljs:1233, ssr/substrate.cljc:53), plus reg-classification, conformance-eval x2, set-db,
register-handler, replace-container!, invoke-handler x2, poll-until, route-resource-plan.
The extractor is a HEURISTIC — bare quoted `'rf/x` on its own line, or inline after throw-error! /
thrown-ex-info — so every site needs reading before acting. The 21 is a worklist, not a verdict.

THE ORACLE QUESTION, AND MY EARLIER ANSWER WAS WRONG. rf2-z67m's close reason (mine) endorses
`spec/api-manifest.edn` as the resolution oracle. IT IS NOT SUFFICIENT, and I verified the refutation
myself at source: the manifest lists DOCUMENTED publics, so a `^:no-doc` facade public is fully
resolvable and carries no row. Measured on trunk — `reset-frame!` and `reload-images!` each read ZERO
manifest rows while appearing 6 and 8 times in implementation/core/src/re_frame/core.cljc, and that file
carries `no-doc` 25 times. Control: `reg-flow` reads 2 rows. A manifest-only check reported 23
non-resolving sites where the live public set reports 21, falsely flagging exactly those two.
THE ORACLE SHOULD BE `ns-publics` OF THE FACADE, or the union of the manifest with the no-doc publics.

WHERE IT BELONGS: scripts/check_thrown_error_messages.py, the existing whole-tree scan over framework
ex-info / throw-error! calls. It already parses those calls and resolves let-bindings, and it already has
a `--self-test` fixture tree — but it has NO notion of where-sym at all (measured 0 against an ex-info
control of 85). What it needs is to extract the second positional argument and check it against the oracle
above. Estimated ~1 day done properly with fixtures, against ~1 hour for a narrow in-process pin that
would go stale exactly like the thing it pins.

TWO THINGS TO GET RIGHT, both learned from the sites already fixed:
  * THE RULE IS NOT "always fully qualify". core.cljc's own not-queryable-kinds map at :1848-1850 spells a
    symbol with `rf/` IF AND ONLY IF the facade exports it, and with the owning namespace otherwise — it
    writes re-frame.flows/flows beside rf/frame-ids in the same map. The check should assert RESOLVABILITY,
    not a spelling.
  * THE PUBLIC SET WAS MEASURED ON THE JVM. A CLJS build could differ under reader conditionals, so the
    check needs to say which runtime it is asserting about, or assert about both.

GATES: the script's own --self-test plus its live scan (333 files under implementation at last run), and
implementation/core clojure -M:test for the thrown-error-message conformance ns. No public name moves, so
the manifest and its two sidecars stay untouched.
MERGED-PR AUDIT #9501 (2026-09-08; merge 837a2d3fc7a464a977a21c827a184baf8a3c37e2): reopening this exact gate owner for two reproduced false-green paths. The existing public-var rule, baseline debt decisions and all prior notes remain intact. No product API change or new defect-convention ruling is requested.

1. P2: Inactive definitions become public exports in the static oracle. At scripts/check_thrown_error_messages.py:1072, comment is treated as a transparent def wrapper; _top_level_forms at 1078 also walks through reader discard/quote prefixes. For a tracked namespace re-frame.audit-fixture with a real known function and an active builder call naming 're-frame.audit-fixture/ghost, the default CLI correctly exits 1 when ghost is absent. Adding ONLY (comment (defn ghost [] nil)), #_(defn ghost [] nil), or '(defn ghost [] nil) makes the same CLI exit 0, reporting zero unresolved names. title: bench: bench/* reaches no CI gate at all — the five stale hicasso/mount! callers are ALREADY FIXED; only the nightly-sweep operator call remains
description:
Five bench arm apps under `bench/hicasso/` still call `rf.hicasso/mount!`, which no longer exists as a public name. Nothing catches it because `bench/*` is classified to no PR gate (ruling rf2-6c12m.1), so these files are never compiled by CI.

FOUND 2026-09-08 by the rf2-kuky.58 dossier worker, independently re-verified before filing.

THE FIVE CALL SITES (`grep -rn 'hicasso/mount!' bench/`):
  bench/hicasso/src/re_frame/bench/hicasso/amp_merge_clock_app.cljs:690
  bench/hicasso/src/re_frame/bench/hicasso/direct_return_clock_app.cljs:219
  bench/hicasso/src/re_frame/bench/hicasso/ledger_frame_clock_app.cljs:955   (plus prose at :933)
  bench/hicasso/src/re_frame/bench/hicasso/slice_broad_clock_app.cljs:991    (plus prose at :939)
  bench/hicasso/src/re_frame/bench/hicasso/slice_echo_clock_app.cljs:834     (plus prose at :174)
All five `(:require [re-frame.hicasso :as rf.hicasso])` and call the form as `(rf.hicasso/mount! container {...} ...)`.

WHY `mount!` IS GONE. The root door is now `h/render!` plus `h/frame-root` (the rf2-kuky.58 line of work). The replacement shape is spelled out verbatim in `h/render!`'s own docstring at `implementation/hicasso/src/re_frame/hicasso.cljc:679`:

    (defonce app-root (h/client-root))
    (defn ^:dev/after-load mount! []
      (h/render! app-root
                 [h/frame-root {:id :rf/default
                                :initial-events [[:counter/initialise]]}
                  ...]))

so the migration is mechanical: `client-root` once, then `render!` a `[h/frame-root {...} ...]` tree. Note the `mount!` in that snippet is the APPLICATION defining its own function — it is not a re-frame2 export.

HOW THE ABSENCE WAS ESTABLISHED, because a naive grep gets this wrong in both directions. A source grep for `defn mount!` under `implementation/hicasso/src/` returns nothing, but that alone is not evidence — a positive control on the same instrument (`defn hydrate!` / `defn frame-root`) ALSO returned nothing, so the instrument was not discriminating and its zero proved nothing. The authoritative check is the generated API manifest: `grep -o 'hicasso/[a-z!-]*mount[a-z!-]*' spec/api-manifest*.edn` returns NOTHING, against a control of `frame-root` returning 7 rows in `api-manifest-metadata.edn` and 4 in `api-manifest.edn`. A manifest miss with a passing control is real: `mount!` is not a public name. Separately, `hicasso.cljc:679` and `:728` DO contain the string `defn ... mount!` — both inside DOCSTRINGS — which is exactly how a source-grep census reaches the opposite, wrong conclusion.

WHY NOTHING CAUGHT IT. `bench/*` reaches no PR gate by ruling rf2-6c12m.1, and `implementation/scripts/check-examples-compile.cjs` reads its roster from `implementation/shadow-cljs.edn` (`:examples/*` and `:testbeds/*` build ids) — bench arms are not in that roster. Confirmed: `grep -rn 'bench' .github/workflows/*.yml` returns nothing. So these files can reference a deleted var indefinitely without any red.

WHAT IS WANTED: migrate the five call sites to `client-root` + `render!` + `frame-root`, and update the three prose blocks that describe the old door (`ledger_frame_clock_app.cljs:933`, `slice_broad_clock_app.cljs:939`, `slice_echo_clock_app.cljs:174`) so they do not teach a deleted API.

THEN THE REAL QUESTION, which is worth more than the fix: SHOULD `bench/*` COMPILE ANYWHERE? Today nothing proves a bench arm still builds, so the next deletion breaks them again silently and the breakage is only discovered when someone tries to run a benchmark. Options: add bench build ids to the `check-examples-compile.cjs` roster (cheap, but bench arms may be heavy and the ruling deliberately kept `bench/*` off PR gates); add a nightly-only bench compile sweep in `expensive-tests.yml` (matches the "expensive, not per-PR" posture that rf2-6c12m.1 was protecting); or accept the drift explicitly and say so in `bench/README.md` so the next person is not surprised. RECOMMEND the nightly sweep — it honours the no-PR-gate ruling while ending the silent-rot class. That half is an operator call and should not be actioned without it.

VERIFY BEFORE FIXING: re-run the grep — a mayor loop is merging continuously and some of these may have been repaired since this bead was filed.
acceptance_criteria: The five call sites use client-root + render! + frame-root; the three stale prose blocks updated; and a recorded decision on whether bench/* gets a nightly compile sweep or documented drift.

title: [tools/re-frame2-pair-mcp] Do not claim a cache hit for payloads withheld by the wire cap
description:
Surface: tools/re-frame2-pair-mcp response-cache/wire boundary. Source snapshot 7ffdacf24d797b67864af78a4625b2c1cb3ef8fd, relevant source unchanged at mayor HEAD 90e9b0008ac96bb59e0e9f6ec03de8e1d650f21d.

Expected: a :rf.mcp/cache-hit telling the caller to reuse a byte-identical prior payload is issued only after that payload was actually delivered to the caller. A result replaced by :rf.mcp/overflow was not delivered and cannot establish that reuse premise. This is the explicit contract in tools/re-frame2-pair-mcp/spec/003-Tool-Catalogue.md:302-309 and src/re_frame2_pair_mcp/cache.cljs:252-259.

Actual: src/re_frame2_pair_mcp/tools.cljs:253-267 and298-309 runs apply-cache BEFORE apply-cap. On a cache miss cache.cljs:321-334 stores the full response hash and :sent-at timestamp immediately. apply-cap can then replace the response with an overflow marker. The next identical opt-in cache:true read matches that stored full-response hash, returns cache-hit, and skips the cap step, falsely claiming the client received the original bytes.

Exact existing focused witness (source inspected, not run): test/re_frame2_pair_mcp/invoke_test.cljs:387-412, cache-hit-bypasses-cap-walk, drives actual tools/invoke/cache/cap with only snapshot-tool replaced by a deterministic 8000-character result. Same args {:cache "true" "max-tokens" 200} both calls. It explicitly asserts first response = overflow; second response = cache-hit. The test therefore pins the defect; it is not evidence that the delivery contract is met. No collision or app-state race is needed. A real cacheable snapshot/get-path producing a post-projection result above the requested cap follows exactly this pipeline. Raising max-tokens is a different cache key and can recover, but retrying the same read must not erase the overflow diagnosis in favor of a nonexistent prior payload.

Impact: an agent using the documented optional cache is told to reuse content it never received and loses the actionable size-limit response on repeats. Narrow P3: cache is opt-in and default-off; this is response honesty/recoverability, not data corruption.

Smallest repair: preserve the fast hit-before-cap optimization for genuinely delivered responses, but commit cache identity only after the cap allows the payload through (or equivalently do not retain the candidate hash when the payload is withheld). Do not cache overflow markers as if they were the source payload. No new cache protocol or retained payload store is needed.

Dedupe: active+closed cache/cache-hit/overflow/wire/apply-cap searches and relevant memories checked; no matching actionable owner found. Referenced historical rf2-3rt1f no longer resolves in the tracker; its full surviving cache ruling in Principles.md:724-860 says the prior payload was emitted and does not authorize reuse of withheld data. The current test/contract tension is explicit above.

Limits: source-only exact existing test and causal pipeline trace; no CLJS compilation, live MCP/nREPL call, shared suite or implementation change.
acceptance_criteria: At actual invoke boundary, two identical cache:true oversized reads both preserve an honest overflow outcome, never claim prior full payload delivery. A delivered under-cap payload followed by an identical read still gets the fast cache-hit marker. Changed payload and errors retain current correct behavior. Replace the current overflow-then-cache-hit assertion with delivery-aware coverage.
close_reason: PR #9380 (worker/mcp-a). apply-cap-step now withdraws the cache entry apply-cache just recorded whenever the cap withholds the payload (cache/withhold! over a new cache/forget!), so a :rf.mcp/cache-hit is only ever claimed for bytes that were actually delivered. The :precheck-hash goes with the entry — retaining it would reopen the same false claim through the pre-eval door. Delivered payloads are untouched: cap/apply-cap returns the identical object under the cap, so the fast hit-before-cap path costs nothing and keeps its entry. invoke_test's cache-hit-bypasses-cap-walk asserted the overflow-then-cache-hit sequence outright — it pinned the defect, exactly as the bead said — and is replaced by delivery-aware arms: withheld-payload-never-claims-a-cache-hit (both oversized reads stay honest overflow, the read is genuinely re-run), delivered-payload-still-gets-the-fast-cache-hit, and raising-the-cap-after-a-withheld-read-delivers-the-payload. Failing-first inside the same red/green pair as rf2-olqo: RED exit 1 / 12 failures, GREEN exit 0 at 1170 tests / 4277 assertions. Catalogue §cache contract updated.

title: [implementation/core/lifecycle] JVM reload can leave late-bind cache permanently serving the old function
description:
## Problem

On the JVM, a hook lookup overlapping namespace reload can permanently repopulate the late-bind cache with the superseded function after `set-fn!` has published its replacement. Later dispatches keep invoking the old function until another explicit invalidation or publication. This breaks the existing reload contract without any malformed application input.

## Source evidence and supported usage

Reviewed source: `7ffdacf24d797b67864af78a4625b2c1cb3ef8fd`. Compared the relevant files with mayor HEAD `584dd853856fad0a97106737d59d5fc4eff61e94`; no relevant source diff.

- `implementation/core/src/re_frame/late_bind.cljc:84-85`: `set-fn!` first updates `hooks`, then removes the cache slot through `invalidate-cache!`.
- `implementation/core/src/re_frame/late_bind.cljc:131-134`: a cache miss reads the function from `hooks`, then independently calls `(swap! fn-cache assoc hook-key resolved)` without checking whether that publication is still current.
- `implementation/core/src/re_frame/router.cljc:1782`: the event commit path obtains `:flows/run-flows-on-db` through this cache. `implementation/flows/src/re_frame/flows.cljc:486` republishes the function at namespace load. A JVM event running while the developer reloads that namespace can therefore keep the old flow runner on later events. The schema validator lookup at `router.cljc:827`, republished at `implementation/schemas/src/re_frame/schemas.cljc:113`, is another concrete consumer.
- `implementation/core/test/re_frame/late_bind_cache_test.clj:132` already tests the advertised next-lookup reload behavior, but only with sequential calls. The file explicitly identifies stale cached functions as a correctness bug. `implementation/core/test/re_frame/live_frame_teardown_hook_reload_jvm_test.clj:43` documents and exercises the supported JVM `(require ... :reload)` path.

## Deterministic reproduction

An isolated Babashka process loaded the actual `re-frame.late-bind` source using the checkout's `implementation/core/src` classpath. The probe used a synthetic hook, the real `set-fn!` and `get-fn-cached`, and an intercept around `swap!` solely to pause the reader immediately before its cache insertion. Both promise waits were bounded to three seconds; the process exited 0. No framework build, shared runtime, or suite ran.

1. Publish `old-fn` with `set-fn!`; the cache slot is empty.
2. Start a reader and pause after it reads `old-fn` from `hooks`, before it inserts into `fn-cache`.
3. On the other thread, call `set-fn!` with `new-fn` and let its invalidation finish.
4. Resume the reader; it inserts and returns `old-fn`.
5. Make three further cached lookups after both operations have completed.

Observed output:

```text
published-before-reader-resumes: :new
racing-reader: :old
subsequent-cached-lookups: [:old :old :old]
uncached-lookup: :new
explicit-invalidation-control: :new
```

The racing call returning the old function is not itself the defect; all subsequent calls remaining stale after completed publication is. The control shows that the replacement was present and that a later invalidation repairs the stuck cache.

## Impact and smallest repair

P3: a bounded development hot reload failure, not a claim about normal single-threaded CLJS startup or production registration. A developer can successfully reload an implementation namespace yet continue executing its old hook implementation on every event, with uncached inspection disagreeing with runtime behavior.

Coordinate cache insertion with hook publication so a reader holding a superseded value cannot restore it after the replacement's invalidation. Keep the existing API and nil-resolution behavior; this does not call for new validation, public lifecycle verbs, or general reload machinery.

## Acceptance

- Add one deterministic JVM interleaving test using the actual lookup/publication functions: pause an old cache miss, complete replacement publication, resume, then assert later lookups return the replacement.
- Cover the ordinary sequential replacement and unpublished-then-published controls with the existing focused late-bind cache tests.
- Preserve the intended behavior that an already-running invocation may finish using its captured function; only persistent stale cache publication must be prevented.

## Dedupe and limits

Searched open and closed titles for late-bind, construction, and teardown; searched all-status descriptions for `get-fn-cached`, `late_bind.cljc`, `fn-cache`, and cache invalidation, and relevant late-bind/review-posture memories. Matches concern unrelated emitter, feature-inventory, and API migrations. Existing boot work `rf2-kuky.1`, `.2`, `.74`-`.77` does not address this cache algorithm. No implementation edits or full JVM/CLJS integration run were made; evidence is the bounded actual-source probe plus consumer inspection.
notes: Repair posture: late_bind.cljc:46 already says the JVM performance gain is bounded. Compare a JVM uncached lookup with a coherent cache/publication state; prefer the smallest repair. Do not add a new generation or locking framework solely to retain this optimization.
close_reason: Fixed in PR #9384: every late-bind cache invalidation now bumps a generation counter carried IN the fn-cache map and the memo insert is conditional on it, so a reader that resolved before a publication cannot restore the superseded fn afterwards. Deterministic JVM interleaving test added to late_bind_cache_test (parks the reader at the memo-insert seam through the real set-fn!/get-fn-cached): red with the bead's [:old :old :old], green after. No new atom, no locking - the counter is in the map so an invalidation always yields a distinct value.

title: spec(006): subscribe 'raises' :rf.error/frame-destroyed at :1210 contradicts :1166 in the same document
description:
Found 2026-09-06 by worker ssrframe-a while landing rf2-t6yr (PR #9333), reported rather than actioned because it sat outside that dispatch's fence. NOT yet verified by the mayor — treat the line numbers as a claim and re-measure.

THE CLAIM: spec/006-ReactiveSubstrate.md:1210 says subscribe RAISES :rf.error/frame-destroyed, while :1166 in the same document correctly says it does NOT throw. One document, two clauses, opposite answers about the same call.

WHY IT IS CREDIBLE AND WHY IT IS SMALL: rf2-t6yr just established, at source, that the ONLY live throwing surface for this id anywhere in the tree is the SSR precondition require-live-frame! in implementation/ssr/src/re_frame/ssr/render_state.cljc — measured by two independent censuses over 971 tracked source files, each run three ways. subscribe is not that surface, so :1166 is the correct clause and :1210 is the defect. The fix is almost certainly one sentence.

READ rf2-t6yr's CLOSE REASON BEFORE TOUCHING THIS. It carries the whole-category correction that landed in spec/009-Instrumentation.md and the reason the SSR arm is special (throw-error! throws and does not also emit, so that arm produces no record at all). Whatever :1210 becomes should agree with the 009 row as it now stands rather than re-deriving the story.

ONE INSTRUMENT WARNING INHERITED FROM THAT WORK, because it would defeat a casual check here too: the throw site is written across TWO LINES, so a line-oriented search for it returns a clean zero. rf2-t6yr's census read zero line-oriented against a control returning 10+. Run any confirming search whitespace-flattened as well.

spec/006-ReactiveSubstrate.md is a hot-zone file — sequence it, do not parallel it.
notes:
MAYOR SEQUENCING 2026-09-06 23:5x AUSEST: DISPATCHABLE BUT DELIBERATELY HELD, and the reason is the holding rather than the work.

This bead is genuinely ready — spec/006-ReactiveSubstrate.md is free right now, no live worker and no open PR holds it, and the fix is one sentence. I nearly dispatched it on that basis.

WHY I DID NOT. spec/006 is a hot-zone file, so whoever takes it holds it until their PR merges. FOUR P2 beads are queued on that same file — rf2-kuky.56, .57, .58 and .59, the views cluster (UIx and Hicasso publishing client-root / render! / unmount!, the one value-hook name, and the ENSURE/SCOPE spelling). Every one of them is blocked today only because it ALSO needs implementation/hicasso or implementation/adapters, both currently held by worker aliasdebt-a. When aliasdebt-a lands, all four become dispatchable at once and they want spec/006 together.

Taking the spec/006 holding now, for a P3 one-sentence correction, would put four P2s behind a trivial change for a whole PR cycle. Held instead, this bead costs nothing and rides along with whichever of those four takes the file first — it is a single sentence in a document that dispatch will already have open.

SO THE RELEASE CONDITION IS: dispatch this WITH the first spec/006 bead that becomes dispatchable, as a rider, rather than on its own. If spec/006 is still free when the views cluster unblocks, the cluster takes it and this rides. If for some reason those four stay blocked for a long stretch, dispatch this alone rather than let it rot — the hold is an optimisation, not a fence, and nothing about the fix depends on them.

NOTHING ABOUT THE FINDING IS IN DOUBT — see the description for the evidence and rf2-t6yr's close reason for the census that establishes the SSR precondition is the only throwing surface. The hold is purely about which worker carries it.
--- FIXED 2026-09-07, worker views-a, rode along with rf2-kuky.56 in PR #9340
    (open, ready for review). BEAD STAYS OPEN pending merge. ---

The hold's release condition was met exactly as written: spec/006 was opened for the
views cluster, and this rode along as a rider.

PREMISE RE-MEASURED AND HELD, but the LINE NUMBERS HAD MOVED — the bead said to treat
them as a claim, and that was right. At tip the pair is:

* `spec/006-ReactiveSubstrate.md:1233` (the bead's ":1210") — §Lifetime contract —
  frame disposal, guarantee 2 "No stale reads": "After `destroy-frame!`, attempts to
  subscribe to `F` raise `:rf.error/frame-destroyed`." THE DEFECT.
* `spec/006-ReactiveSubstrate.md:1189` (the bead's ":1166") — the `subscribe-once`
  contract MUST: returns nil, emits the always-on error, "it does NOT throw." CORRECT.

THE FIX, one sentence, replacing guarantee 2's first sentence: a `subscribe` against a
destroyed frame returns nil and emits the always-on, production-survivable
`:rf.error/frame-destroyed` (recovery `:replaced-with-default`), cross-referencing
009 §Error event catalogue and 002 §Destroy and pointing at the `subscribe-once` clause
as the same answer. The "no path returns a value from a destroyed frame's cache" half
is untouched — that guarantee was never in doubt and is what the section is for.

behaviour IN THE dispatch / dispatch-sync / subscribe REALMS, and names
`re-frame.ssr.render-state`'s `require-live-frame!` as a separate, deliberately-throwing
arm that emits no record at all. My sentence is consistent with that split and adds no
new claim about the SSR arm.

title: dispatch-prompt-template: the two-axis search rule needs a third comment-stripped axis — measured zero on both existing axes
description:
The gate-mechanics block in docs/the-mayor-method/dispatch-prompt-template.md tells every worker to run a search on TWO axes:

  "Run the search twice — once line-oriented, once over the text with whitespace collapsed — because neither result is a superset of the other."

MEASURED 2026-09-05 (schemas-a worker, rf2-fxp5 / PR #9295): TWO AXES ARE NOT ENOUGH, and the case that defeats them is common in this repo rather than exotic.

Searching spec/Spec-Schemas.md for the phrase "FOUR live emitters" returned ZERO on the line-oriented axis AND ZERO on the whitespace-collapsed axis. title: mcp-conformance: confirm the hermetic orchestrator's watchdogs fit a COLD Windows runner (rf2-hhw6 follow-up)
description:
PR #9276 added the repo's first Windows CI leg (expensive-tests.yml job mcp-live-windows), which runs the mcp-conformance live hermetic suite twice. It is the first exercise of makeShadowTreeReaper's real (non-inert) path.

Those were sized against Linux runners. A cold-cache Windows runner resolving five :local/root artefacts plus Reagent/Malli may not fit.

PR #9276 mitigates within its own fence — two pre-warm steps (clojure -P and the fixture npm install) move the cold resolve OUT of both watchdogs, and the Maven/gitlibs/deps.clj cache keeps later nights warm. It could not do more: those constants live in tools/mcp-conformance/, outside that PR's fence.

ACTION: read the first two nightly runs after PR #9276 merges. If mcp-live-windows reds with 'boot failed: nREPL port not found' or the orchestrator's watchdog exit 2, the remedy is a platform-aware bound in run-re-frame2-pair-live-hermetic-suite.cjs, NOT a wider pre-warm. If both nights are green, close this as not-needed.

Also unverified there: deps.clj's COLD tools download from download.clojure.org (the local measurement had a warm tools dir). It has its own named step, 'Verify the Clojure CLI answers', so a failure in it is legible as itself.

inverts this bead's emphasis. Calibration caveat, stated plainly: a windows-latest
runner is 4 vCPU against this box's 24, so the local figure is a LOWER BOUND and not
the runner's number. On a largely serial JVM + CLJS compile the realistic gap is 2-4x,
which lands a cold CI run near 170-350 s against the 540 s cap: inside, but the margin
is real rather than luxurious. The nightly remains the actual test.

FOUR STRUCTURAL FACTS, read from the source rather than measured. They refine what
signature to expect from the nightly, and they are the reason no change is proposed.

1. The whole-run watchdog is armed at MODULE LOAD (the setTimeout sits at file scope),
   while main() is only invoked further down under the require.main guard. The 540 s
   therefore covers everything: setup, boot, preload, inner tests and teardown.

2. waitUntil recomputes `const deadline = Date.now() + timeoutMs` PER CALL, and the
   boot phase makes FOUR separate calls each passing SHADOW_BOOT_TIMEOUT_MS (port
   file, nREPL TCP, fixture http, bundle-ready). That is 4 x 360 = 1440 s of nominal
   budget inside a 540 s outer cap, so SHADOW_BOOT_TIMEOUT_MS can only actually fire
   on the FIRST probe, and only when setup was fast. CONSEQUENCE FOR READING THE
   NIGHTLY: a slow cold COMPILE is the FOURTH probe, so it will surface as the outer
   watchdog's `watchdog timeout (540000ms) - bailing` exit 2, NOT as this bead's
   predicted "boot failed: nREPL port not found". Do not read the absence of the
   predicted string as the absence of the predicted cause.

   names the probe that was pending. The failure is self-diagnosing, so the case for a
   platform-aware bound or an extra diagnostic is not made.

timing constants in the file with no env override — every HERMETIC_CLEANUP_* and
HERMETIC_SETUP_TIMEOUT_MS has one. That asymmetry is worth knowing, not worth
pre-emptively fixing.

I enumerated both runs through the jobs API, confirmed the job name matches, confirmed the conclusion is success on each, and additionally counted SKIPPED STEPS within the job: zero on both. So the job ran and its steps ran.

CLOSED AHEAD OF ITS defer_until, DELIBERATELY. The defer was set to 2026-09-07T00:00:00Z, still about eight hours away. That date was never the condition — this bead's own text sets it as an ESTIMATE of when the two nightlies would have fired ("DEFER UNTIL 2026-09-07T00:00:00Z = after the first TWO nightlies at 15:17 UTC"), and names the real close condition separately: "mcp-live-windows has completed two nightly runs and the hermetic orchestrator did not hit a watchdog". Both runs are in and neither breached. Waiting out the calendar would hold a satisfied bead for eight hours on a proxy for a thing already measured.

WHAT THIS SETTLES. The substantive question — do the hermetic orchestrator's watchdogs fit a COLD Windows CI runner — is answered YES on real 4-core runners across two independent nights. Worker mcpcold-a's decision to change NOTHING was correct: it measured a 6.3x margin locally (cold-compile worst case 85.8s against HERMETIC_TIMEOUT_MS 540s) and a 19.7x margin on the slowest boot probe (18.3s against SHADOW_BOOT_TIMEOUT_MS 360s) on a 24-core box, and declined to widen a timeout on intuition — reasoning that a timeout widened without evidence is indistinguishable from one that was already fine and hides the next real hang. CI has now confirmed the margins survive a runner roughly six times smaller.

NOT CHANGED, AND CORRECTLY SO: HERMETIC_TIMEOUT_MS stays 540s and SHADOW_BOOT_TIMEOUT_MS stays 360s. No code, config or workflow change was made by this bead at any point — its whole deliverable was a measurement and a decision not to act.

FOR ANYONE WHO SEES THIS BREACH LATER: read the failure correctly. waitUntil recomputes its deadline per call and the boot phase makes FOUR calls each passing SHADOW_BOOT_TIMEOUT_MS (4 x 360 = 1440s of nominal budget inside a 540s outer cap), so a slow cold compile surfaces as "watchdog timeout (540000ms) — bailing" exit 2, NOT as the "nREPL port not found" string this bead originally predicted. Do not read the missing string as a missing cause. bail() calls flushDiagnostics() first, so the failure names the pending probe and is self-diagnosing.

ONE READING TRAP RECORDED ON THIS BEAD EARLIER AND WORTH KEEPING: bd displays the defer as "Deferred: 2026-09-07" with no timezone, and on an Australian clock that reads as expired for most of the day it is not — the underlying value is UTC, i.e. 10:00 AUSEST. Convert before concluding a defer has lapsed.

title: hic: every outward link in the app README the manifest copies is dead in the workspace (12/12 resolve outside the pilot root) and most aim into spec/, which the read fence bars
description:
FOUND 2026-09-03 ~18:1x AUSEST by the rf2-t4jpz PRE-PILOT rehearsal, from the
operator's chair, at pin 6e9bb105fc9b1569d63fdebc212b7787a2a023ba.

workspace.md step 2 copies each application's README.md into the pilot's app/
verbatim, and workspace.md's own section "On the app's own README" invites the
pilot to read it: "That is the pilot's own codebase and a real adopter would
have exactly this." Both briefs repeat the invitation - "Its README explains
what the application does and which patterns it is built from - read it freely."

BUT THE README'S LINKS ARE WRITTEN FOR ITS POSITION IN THE REPOSITORY, and the
copy sits somewhere else entirely. Measured on the assembled pilot 1 workspace:
of the 31 links in app/README.md that leave app/, there are 12 unique ../
targets, and ALL TWELVE resolve OUTSIDE the pilot root and NONE of them exists.
They land in the directory ABOVE the pilot root - the parent folder the pilot
was never told about - because the README's paths count levels from
examples/real-apps/realworld_http/ and the copy is two levels shallower. Pilot 2
is the same shape at a different depth: 14 leaving links, targets computed from
examples/capabilities/resources/linearlite/.

So a pilot reading its own README as instructed meets a document with dozens of
references it cannot follow, and no explanation, in the FIRST hour, in the one
file it has been told is unambiguously its own.

AND THE DEAD ONES POINT AT THE FORBIDDEN TREES. Ten of pilot 1's and two of
pilot 2's aim into spec/ - spec/014-HTTPRequests.md, spec/005-StateMachines.md,
spec/012-Routing.md, spec/016-Resources.md and more - which the read fence bars
by name ("Reading spec/, docs/design/, or any other example under examples/"),
and others aim at sibling examples (../../core/flows/, ../resources/,
../infinite_feed/), barred by the same row. The briefs do cover this ("Any file
your app's README links to outside app/. The README is yours; the things it
point at are not"), so the blinding holds - but the package is handing the pilot
a 35 KB document whose every outward reference is simultaneously dead and
forbidden. A pilot that tries one, finds nothing, and tries a second is spending
its attention on the instrument rather than on Hicasso.

WHY IT IS NOT MERELY COSMETIC. The friction log's "Looked at" field is the
blinding evidence, and its rule is that "an entry citing anything that is not a
published page is a recorded leak". A README full of paths INTO spec/ is the
single most likely way an honest pilot generates a leak row it did not mean to,
and the audit rf2-hic-069 consumes cannot tell "followed a link and read the
spec" from "tried a link and found nothing" unless the pilot happens to say so.

CHEAPEST HONEST FIXES, in increasing order of work: (a) step 2 strips or
de-links the outward references when it copies the README, which is one sed in
the manifest and makes the copy self-consistent; (b) the copy keeps them but
step 2 appends one line saying the references point into the framework's own
repository and are not part of this project; (c) leave it and accept the noise.
(a) is the only one that leaves the pilot with a document that is true about
where it now lives.
close_reason: Fixed by PR #9138. PREMISE RE-MEASURED AND IT HOLDS, with one clarification: the 12/12 is a count of unique FILE targets, not of links. Pilot 1's README carries 31 relative links across 12 distinct files; all 12 land above <pilot-root> (two levels, not one) and none exists. Pilot 2 has 14 relative links, 12 landing above <pilot-root> and two inside it at paths that do not exist. Two genuinely different instruments were used - a Python link parser and grep -oE over the raw bytes - each run line-oriented and whitespace-collapsed, agreeing at 33 and 14 inline links; no target begins with '/', so the MSYS pattern-mangling trap does not bite here (']( /' reads 0 against a '](../' control reading 14 lines). No link sits inside a fenced block. THE FIX IS NOT A BLANKET DELETION, because the fence and the targets disagree. REPAIRED, 29 links: every docs/ target either README names is under a tree the site builds - docs/core/glossary.md, docs/machines/glossary.md, docs/machines/concepts.md, docs/resources/glossary.md, docs/EP/EP-0019-optimistic-mutation-rollback.md, none under an exclude_docs prefix - which the read fence ALREADY ADMITS since rf2-lpfz, so stripping them would deny the pilot something it is allowed to read. They are repointed at ../re-frame2/docs/ and all 29 resolve from app/ afterwards with every anchor present, verified by assembling a workspace and resolving each link. DE-LINKED, 16 links: 11 for pilot 1 (10 into spec/, one sibling example) and 5 for pilot 2 (2 into spec/, three sibling examples) - the trees the fence bars by name. Link text stays, so no prose is lost. EXPLAINED: readme-note.md joins the package and step 2b prepends it to the copy, one paragraph saying where the framework's documentation now lives and why the named spec/ files and sibling examples do not resolve here; it names no bead, no experiment and no repository path, so blinding is untouched. That is the bead's option (a) and (b) together, applied per link. The mechanism is three sed/cat commands in workspace.md step 2b, identical for both pilots and depth-agnostic, and they were run verbatim in an assembled workspace rather than reasoned about, because neither link gate reads inside a fenced block. ONE ADJACENT DEFECT FIXED IN THE SAME PASS: workspace.md's 'On the app's own README' said 'Its links into spec/ AND docs/ ... following one is a logged leak', which has contradicted the fence's own documentation row since rf2-lpfz amended it; the paragraph now matches the table. The two app READMEs under examples/ are NOT edited - the repair happens at copy time. Gates: check_doc_slugs.py 0, check_provenance_pins.py 0, check_readme_links.py --ci 0, each with a planted-fault control that went red, restores verified by git blob hash, all re-run post-rebase.

title: TESTING.md's surface-signal table does not know about test_react_jvm (rf2-6r9j.87 follow-up)
description:
PR #9125 (rf2-6r9j.87) added a `test_react_jvm` output to .github/scripts/report-changed-surfaces.sh and carved implementation/adapters/test-react/** out of the generic shipped-adapter arm. TESTING.md is the canonical surface-signal table (CLAUDE.md names it as such) and was outside that dispatch's fence, so it now carries a falsehood plus an omission.

WHAT IS WRONG, precisely, at TESTING.md as of PR #9125:

1. Line 193, the `adapter_diagnostic` row. Its TRIGGER column reads 'an adapter artefact changes (and implementation/core/**, which every adapter resolves by :local/root)'. That is now false for one of the four adapters: a change under implementation/adapters/test-react/ no longer sets adapter_diagnostic at all. The row's GATES column is still correct -- jvm-adapters-test-react IS still gated on adapter_diagnostic, because the job condition is now a DISJUNCTION and adapter_diagnostic is the reverse edge from core, which the fixture depends on. So the fix is to the trigger clause, not the gates clause.

2. There is no row for the new `test_react_jvm` output. It should read roughly: trigger = implementation/adapters/test-react/{src,test}/** or its deps.edn; gates = jvm-adapters-test-react. Note the asymmetry worth stating in the row: src/test also arm cljs_node_test (the fixture is CLJC so it runs under BOTH hosts, which is the point of it), while deps.edn arms the JVM lane only, because shadow reads its source paths from implementation/shadow-cljs.edn and its deps from implementation/deps.edn and so cannot see this artefact's own deps.edn. A prose-only README edit arms NOTHING executable -- its markdown links and inventory are still covered by the always-on verify-readme-links job.

3. Line 241, the 'Adapter JVM classpath probes' row, says 'Two siblings on the same adapter_diagnostic gate' and names jvm-reagent-slim and jvm-adapters-test-react. After #9125 jvm-adapters-test-react is no longer on the SAME gate -- it is on a superset. The substance of the row (it is real coverage, 35 deftests, not a skip-ok probe) is unchanged and worth keeping.

WHY IT WAS NOT DONE IN #9125: the dispatch fence was report-changed-surfaces.sh + its mirror + test.yml + test-fast-pr.sh, plus implementation/adapters/test-react/**. TESTING.md is none of those. It is not on CLAUDE.md's hot-zone list either, so this should be a low-conflict single-file edit for whoever picks it up.

VERIFY AFTER EDITING: no gate validates TESTING.md's prose or its table semantics. Its markdown links and heading anchors are covered by scripts/check_readme_links.py --ci (repo-root markdown is that gate's surface, NOT check_doc_slugs.py's -- nominate by path, not by job name), which runs in test.yml's always-on verify-readme-links job. Column counts and the truth of the trigger clauses have to be checked by hand and said so in the PR body.
close_reason: Fixed in PR #9133 (branch worker/tierpin-a). All three defects corrected in TESTING.md. (1) The adapter_diagnostic row's TRIGGER no longer claims 'an adapter artefact changes' unqualified -- it names the implementation/adapters/test-react/** carve-out and routes the reader to the new output, and it now also explains why jvm-adapters-test-react still appears in the GATES column: adapter_diagnostic is the REVERSE edge (the fixture depends on core), so the job reads a disjunction rather than either output alone. (2) A test_react_jvm row was added, stating the asymmetry the bead asked for: src/** and test/** also arm cljs_node_test because the fixture is .cljc and runs under both hosts, while deps.edn arms the JVM lane ONLY, since shadow takes its source paths from implementation/shadow-cljs.edn and its deps from implementation/deps.edn and cannot see this artefact's own deps.edn; a prose-only README edit arms nothing executable and is still covered by the always-on verify-readme-links job. (3) The skip-ok table's 'Two siblings on the same adapter_diagnostic gate' is reworded -- jvm-reagent-slim is on adapter_diagnostic alone while jvm-adapters-test-react is on the superset -- and the row's substance (real coverage, not a probe) is kept. MEASURED, not read off the script: every trigger claim was exercised against the classifier using the real tracked paths, controls firing. test-react src/test/deps/README all return adapter_diagnostic=false, while reagent-slim src and core src both return adapter_diagnostic=true with test_react_jvm=false. The superset claim was checked against the job's actual if: condition in test.yml. HAND-VERIFIED because no gate covers it: column counts across all eight TESTING.md tables are uniform. That check caught a real defect before it landed -- a draft of the skip-ok row wrote the gate as a code span containing two pipe characters, and GitHub splits table rows on a pipe even inside a code span, taking that row to 5 pipes against the table's 3; reworded as prose. GATES: check_readme_links.py --ci captured exit 0 (the correct gate by path -- check_doc_slugs.py does not cover repo-root markdown), and a planted broken link in TESTING.md prose returned captured exit 1 naming TESTING.md:242, proving the gate read this worktree. Restore verified by git blob hash.

title: Fix angle-bracket placeholder in pair-retro skill description
description:
## Finding

The public frontmatter description in `skills/re-frame2-pair-retro/SKILL.md` uses
the angle-bracket placeholder `<kw>` in the post-error examples (lines 16 and
34). The skill-creator validator rejects angle brackets in descriptions, so the

## Ambiguity cost

`<kw>` is a terse placeholder whose role is not obvious to readers scanning a
trigger description, and it makes the package fail the validator before trigger
fixtures or runtime behavior can be trusted.

## Compatibility and Phase-1 exclusions

This is a frontmatter wording-only correction. Preserve the public skill name,
directory, frontmatter fields, trigger vocabulary and boundaries, allowed-tools,
routing, references, package metadata, and all runtime behavior. Do not rename
the skill or alter its explicit-pull/post-error activation semantics. Do not
touch any Phase-1 target or public/wire identifier.

## Acceptance criteria

- Replace the angle-bracket placeholder with an explicit non-angle-bracket role
  such as `reason-keyword` in every affected frontmatter/example occurrence.
- The description remains semantically equivalent and keeps the same trigger
  terms and post-error boundary.
- `quick_validate.py skills/re-frame2-pair-retro` exits 0.
- Package reference, docs/link, eval-doc, description-budget, and duplicate
  search gates remain green.
acceptance_criteria: Replace every angle-bracket placeholder in the public description/examples with the concrete keyword placeholder :error-kind; retain a user-supplied recap wording (without 'of one'); preserve skill name, frontmatter, trigger vocabulary, routing, references, IDs, paths, and behavior; quick_validate, description-budget, package-reference, docs/link, eval-doc, and duplicate-search gates all exit 0.

title: Clarify private testbed editor process-stream lifecycle locals
description:
## Finding

The private process/stream lifecycle code in `tools/testbed-support/src/re_frame/testbed/open_in_editor_server.clj` uses short locals at the concurrency boundary. `drain-stream` (around lines 208-227) binds `sb` for the retained diagnostic builder, `buf` for the read buffer, `cap` for the retained-character limit, `r` for the UTF-8 reader, and `n` for each read count. `launch!` (around lines 254-296) binds `pb` for the process builder, `proc` for the child process, and `err-drain` for the concurrent stderr future. These names are private but sit beside timeout, pipe-draining, and bounded-diagnostic behavior where each value has a distinct lifecycle role.

## Ambiguity cost

A maintainer changing the deadlock/timeout protection must infer whether `cap` bounds the stream or only retained text, whether `n` is bytes or characters, and whether `err-drain` is a stream or a future. The generic builder/process names also obscure which object owns stdout redirection versus stderr draining. That raises the chance of accidentally stopping the drain, changing UTF-8 character accounting, or dereferencing the wrong lifecycle value while preserving green ordinary tests.

## Phase-1 exclusions and compatibility

This is a private/local naming-only slice. Do not rename `launch!`, `drain-stream`, endpoint paths, query flags (`file`, `line`, `column`, `editor`), error tokens, exit codes, JSON keys, editor command vocabulary, public handler vars, test filenames/namespaces, or any Phase-1 vestigial/removal target. Preserve subprocess argv order, stdout/stderr redirection, timeout and termination behavior, UTF-8 decoding, retained diagnostic cap, response bodies/statuses, fixtures, and all browser/JVM contracts. Risky public terminology or CLI migrations remain open and are excluded.

## Acceptance criteria

- `drain-stream` uses explicit names for the diagnostic builder, character buffer, retained-character cap, reader, and read count; `launch!` uses explicit names for the process builder, child process, and stderr-drain future.
- No behavior or output changes: the full focused JVM suite and testbed-support CLJS/browser proportionate gates remain green.
- The private process/stream code contains no bindings named `sb`, `buf`, `cap`, `n`, `r`, `pb`, `proc`, or `err-drain` for these roles; public keys, flags, paths, IDs, and error text remain byte-for-byte unchanged.
- Diff is limited to safe local names/comments in `open_in_editor_server.clj`.
acceptance_criteria: Explicit process/stream lifecycle locals; unchanged subprocess, timeout, diagnostics, and response contracts; focused JVM and testbed-support gates pass; diff limited to private names/comments.
close_reason: CLI/contention duplicate of canonical implemented bead rf2-6r9j.243; no separate work remains.

title: Clarify private locals in reply vocabulary conformance matrices
description:
## Finding
The reply vocabulary conformance suite uses one-letter or abbreviated private lexical bindings in its EDN helper, family matrix loops, correlation helper, and time-pair loops.

## Evidence
implementation/reply-conformance/test/re_frame/reply_vocab_conformance_cljs_test.cljc:51 defines edn-roundtrip [x]; lines 467, 492, 619, 849, 862 bind family specs as :as f; lines 619-622 and 849-864 bind descriptor keys as with-k/no-k; lines 746-804 bind projected replies as out in correlation helpers and stale-row loops. These names are lexical only and do not alter vocabulary keys.

## Impact
The suite has a large cross-product of reply families and situations. Abbreviated bindings make it harder to distinguish family descriptors, key names, and projected outcomes while reviewing conformance failures, increasing maintenance and review ambiguity.

## Recommendation
Rename only lexical bindings to role-revealing names (value, family-spec, with-key/no-key, outcome or equivalent), updating local references mechanically. Keep all descriptor map keys, test names, statuses, payloads, and control-flow predicates byte-for-byte semantic equivalents.

## Compatibility and exclusions
No public API, namespace, file, operation keyword, wire/storage key, or behavior change. Do not change the matrix predicates or coverage owned by rf2-6r9j.88/.90, nor stale descriptor/inventory/path targets owned by rf2-6r9j.91 (including :error-work-status and the phantom filename); docs and files outside this bounded surface are excluded.

## Acceptance Criteria
1. All identified abbreviated locals at lines 51, 467, 492, 619-622, 746-804, and 849-864 are renamed consistently with no missed references.
2. Matrix cardinality, predicate semantics, test names, reply keys, statuses, and assertion counts remain unchanged.
3. Focused CLJS/JVM test and lint gates pass, and git diff --check is clean.
notes: Detailed scope: exact evidence is implementation/reply-conformance/test/re_frame/reply_vocab_conformance_cljs_test.cljc lines 51 ([x] in edn-roundtrip), 467 and 492 (:as f family descriptor aliases), 619-622 (with-k/no-k descriptor key locals), 746-804 (out projected outcome helper/control locals), and 849-864 (with-k/no-k time-pair controls). Ambiguity cost is reviewer inference across a large family x situation matrix. Rename lexical bindings only to value, family-spec, with-key/no-key, outcome; preserve all descriptor map keys, test names, statuses, payloads, predicates, cardinality, and assertion counts. Explicitly exclude semantic matrix predicates and coverage in rf2-6r9j.88/.90 and stale :error-work-status, phantom filename, inventory/docs targets in rf2-6r9j.91. Acceptance is a lexical-only diff, no public/wire/storage change, green focused CLJS/JVM/kondo and git diff --check.
close_reason: Implemented and verified in commit 584bd9fd4d: private vocabulary helper/family/key/outcome bindings clarified; JVM, CLJS, kondo, negative-control, and diff-check gates green.

title: Name API.md projection parser locals by role
description:
## Finding
The API manifest's API.md projection parser uses compressed locals at the boundary between Markdown cells, line numbers, namespace context, and manifest indexes. title: Replace one-letter Hicasso test lookup helpers with domain names
description:
## Evidence
- Nineteen tracked Hicasso tests/examples define a file-private helper named only `k` or `q`; `k` constructs the runtime cell key `[frame-id query-v]`, while `q` performs a DOM selector lookup. Two ledger examples add `q*` for querySelectorAll, and `tool_reads_cljs_test.cljs` adds `bk` for the exported boundary-read identity.
- Several of these helpers have 10–39 call sites, so their one-letter names recur throughout long concurrency, read-extent, SSR, portal, keyboard, and tool evidence tests.

## Actionable insight
Rename private `k` helpers to `sub-key`, `q` to `query-node`, `q*` to `query-nodes`, and the distinct exported-key helper `bk` to `boundary-read-key`, updating each file's references and explanatory links.

## Ambiguity cost
The current names conceal the key distinction tests are proving (raw runtime key versus privacy-projected boundary key) and make long DOM tests read as algebra rather than interactions with selected nodes.

## Risks / migration
Test-local only. Do not rename public APIs, selectors, fixture IDs, test names, namespaces/files, or the public example translation function `t`. Preserve test expressions exactly aside from symbol spelling.

## Acceptance criteria
1. Every private Hicasso test helper whose complete name is `k`, `q`, `q*`, or `bk` states its runtime/DOM role.
2. Exact old-definition searches are empty, with the intentional public `t` untouched.
3. Affected node/browser suites or their closest focused build gates pass, plus lint/diff checks.

description:

title: ssr-node protocol validation: name boundary values by role
description:
## Coverage and evidence

`implementation/ssr-node/src/protocol.cjs` is the fail-closed module/request grammar. Its internal validation names obscure the values being adjudicated: `validateAllowlist(where, id, entry, { allowlist, keys })` uses `keys` for the human partition label (`app-db`/`runtime-db`), not keys; `validateModule(mod, where)` hides that `where` is a diagnostic module label; `validatePartition(req, entry, entryId, ...)` then uses `k`, `v`, and `bytes` at the security boundary; `validateRequest(req, tables)` names the two validation results `state` and `runtime` even though each is `{partition, bytes}`, and `why` is the deliberate-refusal explanation. These names date to initial commit b2b35bf6e9; 9a42302f7a added the second partition without resolving the role ambiguity.

The ambiguity makes review of the most security-sensitive path need repeated lookups: `keys` sounds like a collection, `entry` alternates between an ID and a config, and `state`/`runtime` sometimes mean maps and sometimes validation results.

## Recommendation

Keep the public/exported validator names and every field/refusal spelling unchanged.

This is identifier-only: JavaScript parameter names and private locals are not call contracts. Preserve exported `validateModule`/`validateRequest`, `PARTITIONS`, `CODE`, all serialized request/detail keys, and the `STATE_KEY_NOT_ALLOWED` wire member. Do not touch `chunkFrame`, `KEY_TEXT`/`refuse` exports, or other residue owned by rf2-6r9j.74/.84.
