title: Routing matcher: name both sides of the pattern-intersection automaton explicitly
description:
Partition: implementation/routing route-pattern parsing, matching, and equal-rank intersection automaton (`re-frame.routing.match`).

Evidence:
- `implementation/routing/src/re_frame/routing/match.cljc:503-619` used single-letter or compressed automaton names (`ts`, `t`, `eps`, `eps-closure`, `ta`/`tb`, `na`/`nb`, `sa`/`sb`, `la`/`lb`, `succs`) while simultaneously walking two token streams and two NFAs.
- `match-against` at the same namespace's decode boundary used `m`, `g`, `d`, `n`, and `v` for the regex result, captured group, decoded value, parameter name, and parameter value.
- The namespace's public behavior is `patterns-intersect?` and `match-against`; the compressed names are private functions or lexical bindings. Repo-wide exact searches found no consumers of private `eps-closure`; `patterns-intersect?` call sites and all route-pattern IDs remain unchanged.
- Targeted history shows two earlier routing naming passes (`2df2d88a37`, `eed266f99a`) fixed nearby cryptic locals but did not cover the later product-automaton code. All-status bead searches by `eps-closure`, `labels-compatible`, `tokens->nfa`, and `product-automaton` found no existing naming owner.

Ambiguity cost:
The old A/B names make it easy to cross an edge label, state, or NFA from the wrong pattern when maintaining the equal-score shadow detector. `eps` also forces readers to decode an abbreviation that the docstring already spells out as epsilon. At the decode boundary, `g`/`d` hide the fail-closed distinction between a raw regex capture and a decoded value.

Recommendation:
Use role-bearing names throughout this private algorithm: `remaining-tokens`, `token`, `epsilon-edges`, `epsilon-closure`, `tokens-a`/`tokens-b`, `nfa-a`/`nfa-b`, `state-a`/`state-b`, `label-a`/`label-b`, `next-state-a`/`next-state-b`, `successors`, and explicit match/decode names. Keep the serialized/public route vocabulary and all public function names unchanged.

Risks/contracts:
This is internal lexical/private vocabulary. Preserve the NFA data shape within the private producer/consumer pair and prove the full shadow-intersection behavior on both JVM and CLJS. Do not rename `patterns-intersect?`, warning IDs, route patterns, or public matcher functions.
acceptance_criteria:
- The product-automaton and match decode path use role-bearing names with no remaining `eps-closure` or listed single-letter A/B automaton bindings.
- Every producer/consumer reference to the private epsilon-edge field is updated together.
- Exact old-name searches are clean except intentional public/data vocabulary.
- Focused route-shadow/matching JVM tests and the relevant CLJS routing gate pass; clj-kondo and git diff --check pass.
- No public var, route/event/fx ID, serialized key outside the private NFA map, or matching behavior changes.

Public matcher vars, route vocabulary, IDs, and behavior are unchanged. title: Name schemas validation callbacks, outcomes, and trace paths by role
description:
Partition: implementation/schemas validation pipeline.

Locations and evidence:
- implementation/schemas/src/re_frame/schemas/validate.cljc:321-322 abbreviates the humanizer callback as `hum-fn`.
- validate.cljc:378-382, 457-504, and 656-704 use `vf`, `result`, `ex`, and `base` around a three-way validator outcome (`true`, `false`, or `[:malformed throwable]`). The short names make the security-sensitive malformed-schema branch harder to audit.
- validate.cljc:665-670 abbreviates the registered path/value as `reg-path` and `reg-slice`.
- validate.cljc:843-848 calls the path selected for trace emission `path-in` and then `leaf-path`, even though it may contain redaction sentinels and is specifically the trace-safe path.

Ambiguity cost:
The validator's return value is not an ordinary boolean, and the two path forms have different privacy guarantees. Generic abbreviations obscure when code is handling a callback versus its tagged outcome, a raw Malli `:in` path versus its sanitized trace representation, and a registered root versus the value read from app-db. That increases review cost precisely on fail-closed and redaction branches.

Proposed names:
- `hum-fn` -> `humanize-fn`
- `vf` -> `validate-fn`
- `result` -> `validation-result`; `ex` -> `validator-error`; `base` -> `base-tags`
- `reg-path` -> `registered-path`; `reg-slice` -> `registered-value`; `schema-meta` -> `registration-metadata`
- `path-in` -> `trace-in-path`; `leaf-path` -> `trace-path`

Compatibility and migration risk:
Change lexical bindings only. Preserve public validate-* arglists, private function names, schema and trace operation IDs, serialized tags/reasons, recovery values, validation order, continuation semantics, and late-bind hooks. Do not touch `walk-schema?`, which is owned by the existing vestigial-code bead rf2-6r9j.45.
acceptance_criteria: Validation locals clearly distinguish callbacks, tagged outcomes, validator errors, registration roots/values, and trace-safe paths; emitted maps and public arglists remain unchanged; rf2-6r9j.45-owned code is untouched; exact searches, focused JVM/CLJS tests, lint, and diff checks pass.

title: mcp-conformance: remove the stale descriptor exemption from the indicator gate
description:
Evidence
- indicator_field_test.clj's no-inline-indicator-slot-emit-outside-the-helper skips every file in inline-emit-whitelist before reading and applying fx/strip-comments-and-strings.
- The whitelist includes tools/re-frame2-pair-mcp/src/re_frame2_pair_mcp/tools/descriptors.cljs solely because its descriptor docstrings mention :dropped-sensitive and :elided-large.
- Commit efd0c8dbf32 changed this gate to strip comments, docstrings, and strings before matching specifically so descriptor prose no longer needs exclusion.
- Executing the gate's actual stripper and variant-regex against descriptors.cljs returns false for both indicator literals. Therefore removing that path from the whitelist is green today.
- Because the pre-read whitelist bypasses the whole file, any future real code emission of either slot in descriptors.cljs would also be skipped and the conformance gate would falsely pass. wire.cljs is different: it is the deliberate central helper location and remains a valid exception.

Impact
A compatibility exemption outlived the false-positive it addressed and now forms a whole-file blind spot in a MUST-level single-emit-path gate. The current source is conformant, but a later inline emission in descriptors.cljs would evade CI.

Recommendation
Remove descriptors.cljs from inline-emit-whitelist and update the surrounding comments/docstring to describe only the central wire.cljs helper exception. Continue stripping strings before the scan so user-facing descriptor prose remains permitted.

Risks and contracts
Do not remove the wire.cljs exception or forbid indicator names in descriptor documentation. Preserve keyword-boundary matching, filesystem source discovery, and the central with-indicators contract. This change tightens only test coverage; it does not alter an MCP tool/schema/protocol surface.
acceptance_criteria:
- descriptors.cljs is scanned by no-inline-indicator-slot-emit-outside-the-helper after comments/docstrings/strings are stripped.
- wire.cljs remains the explicit central-helper exception.
- The current wire-vocab Clojure suite passes.
- A temporary real-code occurrence such as (assoc envelope :dropped-sensitive 1) in descriptors.cljs makes the focused test fail, while existing descriptor prose does not.
- Comments no longer describe descriptors.cljs as whitelisted.
close_reason: PR #9086 (head 79b2ee56a6). descriptors.cljs removed from inline-emit-whitelist; wire.cljs remains the sole central-helper exception; the surrounding comment and docstring no longer describe descriptors.cljs as whitelisted, and the docstring now records WHY prose needs no row (the gate strips comments/docstrings/strings first, per efd0c8dbf32) and that a row is strictly stronger because it skips the file whole. PREMISE DRIFT worth recording: the bead says the whitelist exists because descriptor docstrings mention :dropped-sensitive and :elided-large — on the current tree descriptors.cljs contains NEITHER literal in any form (grep over tools/re-frame2-pair-mcp/src returns only descriptors_data.cljs, wire.cljs and wire_pipeline.cljs). descriptors_data.cljs is NOT whitelisted and passes purely on the strip, which is the working proof that the strip suffices. So the exemption was doubly stale and the recommendation held. Gate liveness proved directly, both directions: planting (assoc envelope :dropped-sensitive 1) in descriptors.cljs turned no-inline-indicator-slot-emit-outside-the-helper RED naming the file and the literal (exit 1, 119 assertions); with the same fault in place, temporarily restoring the old whitelist row turned it GREEN (exit 0, 117 assertions) — the whole-file blind spot reproduced exactly as the bead describes. Both temporary edits reverted; descriptors.cljs verified byte-identical by blob hash 6cbd4df82d18a212c4b69ecd1ce4f211aa06a349 and carries no diff in the PR. title: Remove retired CSP/SSR remnants from the template browser proof
description:
## Evidence

The emitted browser driver still describes and diagnoses the retired CSP/SSR scaffold. tools/template/test-support/dev-page-boot-proof.cjs says the emitted index.html carries a Content-Security-Policy meta tag, contrasts itself with a synthetic SSR page, and has two diagnose() branches dedicated to CSP refusal and unsafe-eval errors. The current root/resources/public/index.html has no CSP. template_test.clj explicitly bans the Content-Security-Policy string, and skills/re-frame2-setup/tests/setup_drift_test.clj locks the default route as CSP-free. The driver server deliberately emits no CSP response header, so those two branches have no policy source in any current positive or mutation run.

The same pre-collapse story remains in .github/workflows/test.yml, .github/workflows/expensive-tests.yml, and .github/workflows/template-release.yml: comments say this tier contains two Chromium proofs including an SSR DOM-adoption proof. The current emitted_test_run_test.clj contains only the generic emitted-page driver, used for Reagent, UIx, the setup-skill leaf, and its mount/click witnesses; no SSR fixture remains.

History shows the CSP and SSR scaffold disappeared in the rf2-zq34m reduction while this driver and CI narrative were not fully reconciled.

## Impact

Dead diagnostic code and false CI descriptions make a generic boot test look like it still validates a retired security/SSR feature. This obscures the actual teeth: mount, live click, package declaration completeness, pageerror cleanliness, and red witnesses.

## Recommendation

Delete the unreachable CSP-only diagnose branches and rewrite the driver plus CI comments around the current SPA proof. Keep the useful missing-bundle diagnostic and all functional proof/witness behavior.

## Risks and contracts

Do not remove browser provisioning, CI-hard browser launch failure, static-server containment, the mount/click/pageerror checks, or either red witness. A future CSP recipe should have its own policy-bearing fixture rather than dormant diagnostics in a CSP-free scaffold.
acceptance_criteria:

title: Delete unreachable schemas conformance load-error skip branch
description:
## Finding

`implementation/schemas/test/re_frame/schemas_conformance_test.clj` retains a `(:fixture/load-error fixture)` skip branch even though its loader can no longer return that datum. The branch became unreachable when fixture parsing was changed to throw on every load failure.

## Evidence

- `read-one-form` (currently lines 118-144) throws for an empty fixture, malformed EDN, or more than one top-level form. Its docstring explicitly says it throws rather than returning `:fixture/load-error` because the runner classifies that shape as a skip.
- `load-fixture` (currently lines 146-156) has no catch and returns only the parsed EDN form; `all-schemas-fixtures` invokes it directly before entering the test result loop.
- Nevertheless `run-schemas-conformance-corpus` (currently lines 508-514) still tests `(:fixture/load-error fixture)` and appends a `{:skipped? true :reason "load error" ...}` result. No loader output reaches this arm. The skipped-summary fallback `(:error s)` exists only for this retired result shape.
- Commit `b6e26366a8` removed every loader catch and `{:fixture/load-error ...}` producer specifically because a parse failure must fail the suite rather than disappear as a skip, but it left this consumer branch behind. The follow-up PushbackReader implementation (`f2b899cc497`) preserves the throwing contract.
- All-status title/description searches for `fixture/load-error`, `load error`, and `schemas conformance` found no owning issue. Closed `rf2-98ni` owns the exactly-one-form loader fix; it does not remove this unreachable runner residue.

## Impact

The dead arm preserves and documents precisely the failure policy the loader migration retired: malformed fixtures represented as skips. It makes the runner harder to audit and invites a future loader change to reuse the stale shape, silently weakening the conformance gate. The extra `:error` summary fallback similarly suggests skipped parse failures remain supported.

## Proposed disposition

Delete the `:fixture/load-error` condition/result arm and its error-only skipped-summary rendering from the schemas conformance runner. Keep spec-version and out-of-capability skips intact. Load/parse errors must continue to escape before the result loop and fail the test process.

## Risks

Do not convert thrown fixture errors into ordinary failed or skipped corpus records. The security property of `rf2-98ni` is that malformed/trailing fixtures abort the gate. Preserve the non-empty runnable floor, capability filtering, and ordinary runtime `run-fixture` exception reporting.
acceptance_criteria:
- `rg -n ":fixture/load-error|reason +\"load error\"" implementation/schemas/test/re_frame/schemas_conformance_test.clj` finds only explanatory historical text if retained, and no executable branch/result construction.
- A malformed, empty, and two-form selected schemas fixture each makes the focused conformance invocation exit nonzero before results are summarized; none is counted as skipped.
- The five current selected fixtures still load and execute, and the runnable-floor assertions remain non-vacuous.
- Spec-version and unsupported-capability fixtures, when exercised, retain their current explicit skip behavior.
- The schemas JVM suite passes; a planted trailing-form negative control turns the focused gate red and restoring the fixture turns it green.
close_reason: PR #9113 (head 6711fbafe1). Deleted the (:fixture/load-error fixture) cond arm and its skip-result construction from run-schemas-conformance-corpus, plus the (:error s) slot in the skipped-summary that existed only to render that retired shape. A comment in its place records why there is no such arm. Unreachability proven by execution probe, not census alone: a marker in the load-error arm fired 0 times while the same marker in the live :else arm fired 5, matching the five selected fixtures exactly. title: vestige(reagent-adapter): remove ten redundant test imports
description:
## Finding

The Reagent adapter test surface retains ten imports/refers that have no live use:

- `:require-macros [re-frame.core :refer [reg-view]]` is unused in seven namespaces: `reg_view_devtools_cljs_test.cljs`, `source_coord_dom_cljs_test.cljs`, `source_coord_warn_once_cljs_test.cljs`, `view_rendered_op_cljs_test.cljs`, `view_id_attr_cljs_test.cljs`, `view_render_trigger_handler_cljs_test.cljs`, and `view_side_capture_cljs_test.cljs`.
- `[re-frame.trace :as trace]` is unused in `render_key_cljs_test.cljs` and `view_render_trigger_handler_cljs_test.cljs`.
- `testing` is referred but unused in `views_synthetic_event_frame_dom_cljs_test.cljs`.

## Evidence

`clj-kondo --lint implementation/adapters/reagent --cache false` reports each of these exact clauses as referred/required but never used. Repo-wide lexical inspection confirms there are no unqualified `reg-view` calls in the seven listed namespaces: they use `rf/reg-view`, or only the plain function `rf/reg-view*`. `implementation/core/src/re_frame/core.cljc` lines 170-188 explicitly self-requires its macros and states that `(:require [re-frame.core :as rf])` is the only import CLJS callers need; many neighboring Reagent tests compile with `rf/reg-view` and no explicit macro refer. The two trace aliases have no `trace/` reference; each namespace already requires `re-frame.core`, which itself requires `re-frame.trace`, and their recorder macro comes from `re-frame.test-support`, which requires `re-frame.trace.tooling`. The synthetic-event test contains no `(testing ...)` form.

All-status bead searches for `reagent unused`, `reagent require`, `unused require`, `macro import`, `test imports`, plus description scans for `require-macros`, `dead import`, and every affected file name found no existing owner. `rf2-6r9j.12` is limited to dead imports in pair-mcp tests and is a different slice.

## Impact

The clauses add lint noise and falsely suggest that qualified `rf/reg-view` needs a second macro import, or that these tests directly exercise the trace namespace. That makes dependency intent harder to audit. Runtime impact is otherwise negligible.

## Proposed disposition

Remove only the ten proven-unused imports/refers. Keep every bare-macro import that has an unqualified call and keep side-effect-only namespace loads that are not proven redundant. Do not change test behavior or production code.

## Risks

ClojureScript macro loading is sensitive to namespace declarations. The `reg-view` removals are supported by core's self-macro contract, but the normal node/browser compilation lanes must remain the authority. Removing whole require clauses instead of the specific unused entries could accidentally remove a load dependency.
acceptance_criteria:
1. The seven unused `re-frame.core/reg-view` macro refers, two unused `re-frame.trace` aliases, and one unused `cljs.test/testing` refer listed in the description are removed, with no unrelated import cleanup.
2. A focused `clj-kondo --lint implementation/adapters/reagent --cache false` run no longer reports those ten warnings; unrelated pre-existing diagnostics need not be resolved in this bead.
3. The Reagent node test build and browser test build compile and pass, proving qualified `rf/reg-view`, trace capture, and the real-DOM synthetic-event test still work.
4. A source check confirms namespaces containing a bare `(reg-view ...)` still retain the required macro refer.
5. No production source, public API, test discovery regex, or dependency coordinate changes.
close_reason: Re-counted at tip: ten is right. EIGHT landed in PR #9161 (seven :require-macros [re-frame.core :refer [reg-view]] clauses and one unused testing refer); the TWO [re-frame.trace :as trace] requires are split to rf2-b38y because removing them takes implementation/adapters from 339 to 337 against a floor of 339 and check_require_alias_dialect.py fails from below, so the removal and the baseline lowering must land in one commit against a file this dispatch was fenced from. Each removal established unused in ITS OWN file, namespace included: the seven reach the macro as rf/reg-view or the function rf/reg-view*, and rf is [re-frame.core :as rf] in all seven, which core.cljc's self-:require-macros covers. AC4 holds: the six sibling namespaces calling reg-view bare keep their refer, and they are the census control (3,2,1,1,3,1 vs 0 on all seven). Gates on the final base, captured exits: CLJS compile 0 (0 warnings), suite 0 (11174 tests / 55752 assertions, 0 failures), examples-compile 0 (58 builds), alias ratchet 0. A planted load-bearing refer removal in auto_inject_form2_cljs_test.cljs reddened the compile at exit 1 with :undeclared-var at the exact line, which is the control for the seven made.

title: Retire the orphaned route-link prefetch hook trio
description:
## Problem

Routing still publishes three optional-artifact hooks for a substrate-neutral `:prefetch :intent` route-link integration, but no current code reads any of them. Their original view-artifact consumer was retired, and the shipped replacement view explicitly declines this integration. The hook directory nevertheless says Hicasso consumes all three, so the integration catalogue describes reachability that does not exist.

## Evidence

- Repo-wide fixed-string searches find `:routing/prefetch-payload`, `:routing/prefetch-on-intent!`, and `:routing/prefetch-intent-keys` only at their `late-bind/set-fn!` publications in `implementation/routing/src/re_frame/routing.cljc:572-580`, their catalogue rows in `implementation/core/src/re_frame/late_bind/directory.cljc:540-551`, and prose/comments. There is no `late-bind/get-fn`, `require-fn!`, wrapper, or other reader for any key.
- The shipped Hicasso route-link consumes only `:routing/link-model` and `:routing/activate-link!` (`implementation/hicasso/src/re_frame/hicasso/impl/route_link.cljs`). Its namespace contract explicitly says the prefetch trio is "Not wired in v0", and `control-keys` merely prevents `:prefetch` leaking into HTML. `docs/core/hicasso/07-routing-and-navigation.md:144-163` likewise teaches authors to dispatch `:rf.route/prefetch` themselves and states that `h/route-link` installs none of routing's prefetch handlers.
- The ordinary Reagent `rf/route-link` is still a live consumer of `link/prefetch-payload`, `link/prefetch-on-intent!`, and `link/prefetch-intent-keys`, but calls them directly inside the routing artifact. It does not traverse these hooks, so deleting only the publications does not remove route-link prefetch.
- History confirms the lost-consumer path: commit `fa3bc36bae4` introduced the first two hooks for `ui/Freehand consumers`; commit `4da020a5af2` added the intent-key hook and changed `implementation/freehand/src/re_frame/freehand/route_link_seam.cljc`. Those view artifacts are retired. Commit `c07b9f84674` later rewrote the directory prose to name Hicasso, but today's Hicasso implementation never adopted the hooks.
- Bead searches for each exact hook name, `substrate-neutral prefetch`, and `Hicasso prefetch` found no existing issue covering the orphaned trio.

## Impact

Every routing load installs three unread global hook-table entries, including one host-conditional operation and a thunk whose only purpose was cross-artifact sharing. More importantly, the authoritative late-bind directory falsely promises a supported Hicasso integration, making drift checks green while maintainers reason from an imaginary consumer.

## Proposed disposition

Remove the three `late-bind/set-fn!` publications and their directory rows, and update the nearby routing comments that describe them as seams. Keep the underlying `re-frame.routing.link` functions/data and the documented `rf/route-link :prefetch :intent` behavior unchanged because those are directly consumed. If a non-Reagent route-link is intentionally being changed to support prefetch, land that real reader first and keep only the keys it actually needs rather than preserving speculative hooks.

## Risks

The directory may be consumed by generic drift tooling, so publisher and catalogue changes must land together. Recheck any concurrent Hicasso work before removal because recent design notes discuss a possible future acceptance even though current runtime and user guide explicitly decline it. Do not delete or change the underlying prefetch event, resource warm-plan, or Reagent route-link behavior.
acceptance_criteria:
1. `:routing/prefetch-payload`, `:routing/prefetch-on-intent!`, and `:routing/prefetch-intent-keys` are either removed from both publisher and late-bind directory, or each retained key has a shipped, tested `get-fn`/`require-fn!` consumer; catalogue prose names only real consumers.
2. `rf/route-link {:prefetch :intent}` still validates on both hosts and installs its CLJS hover/focus/touch behavior through the live direct `re-frame.routing.link` functions.
3. Hicasso route-link tests and documentation agree on whether `:prefetch` is supported; no key is silently stripped under a catalogue claim that it is consumed.
4. Routing tests plus core late-bind directory drift/coverage tests pass, and repo-wide fixed-string searches show no orphaned reader or publisher.
close_reason: PR #9165. The three prefetch late-bind publications and their three directory rows removed together; verified at tip that no get-fn/require-fn!/wrapper read any of them, with :routing/link-model as a control that DOES have real readers. rf/route-link's :prefetch :intent is untouched (it calls re-frame.routing.link directly), and :prefetch stays in Hicasso's control-keys so it still never reaches the anchor. Hicasso's route-link contract corrected: it claimed routing published a trio it no longer does. Gates: late-bind drift JVM 8 tests/683 assertions exit 0 (pins both directions), routing JVM 553 tests/3451 assertions exit 0, CLJS 11175/55753 exit 0, browser 783/4253 exit 0. Deletion run backwards: re-adding one publication without its directory row turned the drift test exit 1 with exactly one failure naming :routing/prefetch-payload. NOTE the bead's file list was stale in two ways: the implementation/freehand/ path it cites is retirement HISTORY (rf2-0yp7w / PR #8322, git ls-files returns zero) and needed no work, and three docstrings in re-frame.routing.link still call these functions late-bind seams - out of this fence, follow-up filed.

title: the audit process emits bead ids that do not exist — rf2-wyvf2 is cited by rf2-l1hh's own audit note AND its acceptance criteria
notes:
FILED 2026-09-03 02:4x AUSEST by the mayor, on evidence returned by the records-a worker (PR #9041).

THE FINDING. Three bead ids cited in this repo resolve to nothing:
  - rf2-mxkq7 — cited in tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/views/view_walker.cljs:8 and in commit fe4ff001b9 subject. Tracked as rf2-rn3u.
  - rf2-k0rbk — cited in the bench/hicasso ambient_refusal test as the bead a PROVISIONAL marker is pending on. Tracked as rf2-fgwf.
  - rf2-wyvf2 — and this one is the reason this bead exists.

Each was verified absent with `bd show` returning "no issue found" (exit 1) against a control that resolves, AND against the full id list in the export.

WHY rf2-wyvf2 IS DIFFERENT, AND WHY THIS IS ITS OWN CLASS. The first two are TREE-side: a source comment or a test marker cites a dead id. That is rf2-fgwf and rf2-rn3u, both filed, both narrow, both P4-ish docstring work. rf2-wyvf2 is TRACKER-side: it is cited by rf2-l1hh own audit NOTE and, worse, by rf2-l1hh ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA. So a worker dispatched on rf2-l1hh is told to satisfy a criterion that points at nothing, and the pointer was written by the audit process itself rather than by a human typing from memory.

THAT IS THE CLASS: the audit process emits bead ids that were never created. Every other instance of this shape in the repo is a HISTORICAL id — something that existed once, or a commit-subject artefact from a renaming. These are different: they are forward references that never landed. An acceptance criterion citing one cannot be satisfied and cannot be checked, and it reads as authoritative because acceptance criteria are where a worker looks for the definition of done.

WHAT THIS BEAD IS FOR, and it is NOT for fixing the three citations — those have their own beads.
  1. Establish the MECHANISM. Where do these ids come from? A plausible hypothesis, unverified: an audit drafts a follow-up bead id in prose, the create never runs (or fails), and the prose ships anyway. Another: an id is invented as a placeholder. Find out which, because the remedies differ completely.
  2. MEASURE THE POPULATION. How many cited-but-nonexistent ids are there across bead descriptions, notes and acceptance criteria? Note the trap that sank an earlier attempt at this: a census over the whole TREE returned 4,997 of 5,179 cited ids "absent", which is absurd on its face — the tracker holds ~520 issues and the repo deliberately keeps historical citations as provenance. The real class is much narrower: a LIVE CONDITIONAL GATED ON NOTHING (an acceptance criterion, a PROVISIONAL marker, a dependency edge), not a citation to a bead that once existed. Draw the boundary before counting, and state it.
  3. Only then decide whether anything mechanical is worth building. Under the stance this may well end as "record the rule and move on" — do not gold-plate a linter for three instances.

DO NOT close the three citation beads from here; they stand on their own.
MORE CARRIERS, 2026-09-03, from the xray-b worker while fixing rf2-rn3u. The phantom count in ONE FILE is now four, not one.

tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/views/view_walker.cljs cites rf2-mxkq7 (already known), and ALSO rf2-01il5, rf2-ztxnm8 and rf2-nr7vf2 — all verified absent by bd (exit 1) and against all 477 ids in the export, with a control that resolves. rf2-rn3u had flagged rf2-01il5 as unchecked and suspected; it is confirmed, and it brought two more with it.

WHAT THAT DOES TO THIS BEAD MEASUREMENT STEP. Four phantom ids in a single docstring block is not a scattering of typos — it is a pattern with a source, and it sharpens the hypothesis: these read like ids DRAFTED in prose whose create never ran. Whoever measures the population should start by asking whether all four trace to one authoring event, because if they do, the mechanism is one broken habit rather than a class of drift, and the remedy is correspondingly small.

Note the asymmetry that keeps this bead narrow: these four are TREE-side and inert — a reader follows them nowhere. rf2-wyvf2 is TRACKER-side, in an ACCEPTANCE CRITERION, where it gates a definition of done. Same defect, different blast radius.
PREMISE REFUTED, 2026-09-03, by the phantom-a worker. Measured, with controls in both directions.

THIS BEAD'S CENTRAL CLAIM IS FALSE. The title says "the audit process emits bead ids that do not exist" and the body says "they are forward references that never landed". Neither holds. EVERY id this bead names was a REAL bead that was CREATED, CLOSED, and later GARBAGE-COLLECTED out of the tracker.

METHOD. Absence from the CURRENT export proves nothing, because the tracker has been GC'd hard. Sampled 13 historical snapshots of .beads/issues.jsonl across the whole life of the export (11,413 commits, 2026-05-06..2026-09-03) and unioned their ids: 14,551 distinct ids ever exported, against 539 live today. Row counts show the collection directly - 10,444 rows on 2026-07-11, 2,149 on 2026-07-19, 533 today.

CONTROLS. rf2-2rtt6 (a large real programme, absent today) FOUND in history -> the instrument sees GC'd beads. rf2-fgwf (live) FOUND. rf2-zzzzznotanid NOT found -> no false positives.

THE SIX "PHANTOMS", ALL REAL, ALL CLOSED BEFORE GC:
  rf2-k0rbk  "rf2-2rtt6.122 follow-up: confirm or rename the provisional error id" - closed 2026-08-06, close_reason "ambient-frame-refused stands... Remaining touch: the provisional stamps' removal is a one-line comment/docs touch". That is EXACTLY the rf2-fgwf edit. The marker was correct when written and became stale when the bead was DISCHARGED - the mayor's own "third case", not a phantom.
  rf2-e28wl  "spec 009: the ambient-frame-refused row enumerates :operation as (:dispatch / :subscribe)..." - closed 2026-08-05, fixed in PR #7533.
  rf2-wyvf2  "feat(causa): Reactive panel - rebuild + rename L3 tab 'Views' -> 'Reactive'" - closed 2026-05-20, landed in #1741. So the rf2-l1hh acceptance-criteria citation is HISTORICAL PROVENANCE naming the PR that did the removal - it gates nothing. The "worst case" that motivated this bead is out of class by this bead's own boundary.
  rf2-mxkq7 / rf2-01il5 / rf2-ztxnm8 / rf2-nr7vf2 - all present in sampled history.

POPULATION, boundary stated first. Counted: a forward-looking marker (PROVISIONAL / pending / blocked on / to sequence with / awaiting / revisit / tracked as / see bead / deferred to / future work) in the SAME SENTENCE as an rf2- id absent from the live tracker; word-boundary matched excluding identifier context; over tracked files only. Result: 292 sites, 204 distinct absent ids, 172 files. Of those 204: 200 verified as real-then-GC'd; the remaining 4 (rf2-hic, rf2-ssr, rf2-abort, rf2-ede1h.3) are the census regex truncating longer tokens (rf2-hic-065, rf2-ssr-streaming-, the test name rf2-abort-vs-decode, and rf2-ede1h which IS in history). NET: ZERO ids that were never created.

ONE GENUINE INSTANCE FOUND, AND IT IS A DIFFERENT MECHANISM. spec/conformance/README.md:605 read "Tracked as future work - see bead `` for context" - an EMPTY citation slot. Traced to commit 2d64e1f7c2 (2026-05-27), "docs(spec): strip bead refs + historical commentary", which replaced the real id rf2-j9yf INSIDE the backticks and left the sentence standing. Its commit message reports mkdocs, check_doc_slugs and test-fast-pr all green, because no gate looks at this. Fixed in this PR.

MECHANISM, ESTABLISHED: not a failed `create`. Two real mechanisms - (1) tracker garbage collection removing closed beads out from under prose that cites them, and (2) a bulk bead-ref stripping sweep that emptied a citation slot without removing its sentence.

JUDGEMENT: NO TOOLING. A linter here would flag 292 sites whose ids were all legitimately created and legitimately collected; the signal is zero and the noise is the whole corpus. THE RULE WORTH RECORDING: absence of a bead id from the tracker is NOT evidence it never existed - the tracker is a working set, not an archive, and git history of .beads/issues.jsonl is the archive. Resolve a suspect id against that history before calling it a phantom.
close_reason:
CLOSED ON A REFUTED PREMISE, with the measurement this bead asked for delivered. PR #9052 (https://github.com/day8/re-frame2/pull/9052). Full method and evidence in the PREMISE REFUTED note above.

THE BEAD'S CENTRAL CLAIM IS FALSE. "The audit process emits bead ids that were never created" does not hold: every id this bead names was a REAL bead that was created, CLOSED, and later garbage-collected. rf2-k0rbk ("confirm or rename the provisional error id", closed 2026-08-06 with "the id stands"), rf2-e28wl (closed 2026-08-05, PR #7533), rf2-wyvf2 ("Causa Reactive panel rebuild", closed 2026-05-20, PR #1741), plus rf2-mxkq7 / rf2-01il5 / rf2-ztxnm8 / rf2-nr7vf2, all present in sampled history.

SO THE MOTIVATING "WORST CASE" IS OUT OF CLASS BY THIS BEAD'S OWN BOUNDARY. rf2-wyvf2 in rf2-l1hh's acceptance criteria reads "deliberately removed by the Reactive-panel rebuild in PR #1741/rf2-wyvf2" - a HISTORICAL citation naming the PR that did the removal. It gates no definition of done; it records why something is absent, which this bead itself calls normal and harmless.

1. MECHANISM - ESTABLISHED, and it is NEITHER hypothesis on the bead. Not a failed `create` and not an invented placeholder. Two real mechanisms: (a) TRACKER GARBAGE COLLECTION removing closed beads out from under prose that cites them - 10,444 rows on 2026-07-11, 2,149 on 2026-07-19, 539 today, against 14,551 distinct ids ever exported; and (b) a BULK BEAD-REF STRIPPING SWEEP - commit 2d64e1f7c2 (2026-05-27, "strip bead refs + historical commentary") replaced the real id rf2-j9yf INSIDE the backticks in spec/conformance/README.md and left the sentence standing, yielding "Tracked as future work - see bead `` for context". Its commit message reports mkdocs, check_doc_slugs and test-fast-pr all green, because no gate looks at this. Fixed in PR #9052.

2. POPULATION - MEASURED, boundary stated first (a live conditional gated on nothing, NOT a citation to a dead bead). Dependency edges to an absent id: 0, fully decidable. acceptance_criteria citing an absent id: 2, both historical provenance. Empty citation slots: 1, fixed. Tree sites with a forward-looking marker in the same sentence as an absent id: 292 sites / 204 distinct ids / 172 files - of which 200 are verified real-then-GC'd and the remaining 4 are the census regex truncating longer tokens (rf2-hic-065, rf2-ssr-streaming-, the test name rf2-abort-vs-decode, and rf2-ede1h which IS in history). NET COUNT OF IDS THAT WERE NEVER CREATED: ZERO.

3. JUDGEMENT - NO TOOLING, which this bead anticipated as the likely answer. A linter would flag 292 sites whose ids were all legitimately created and legitimately collected: signal zero, noise the whole corpus. THE RULE, recorded here and in the note above: absence of a bead id from the tracker is NOT evidence that it never existed. The tracker is a WORKING SET, not an archive; .beads/issues.jsonl in git history IS the archive. Resolve a suspect id against that history before calling it a phantom - one `git show <rev>:.beads/issues.jsonl` would have prevented this bead's framing, and would have retitled rf2-fgwf and rf2-rn3u from "phantom" to "discharged promise", which is a different fix.

INSTRUMENT WARNING WORTH KEEPING. On this grep build (GNU grep 3.0) `-F` combined with `-i` silently returns ZERO - `grep -ri PROVISIONAL spec/` reads 25, `grep -rFi` reads 0, no error, ordinary no-match exit. And `bd --json | jq` emits CRLF. Every census here carried a control needle through the same pipeline with the same flags; the first tree-wide attempt was DISCARDED because its positive controls read zero.

DID NOT touch rf2-rn3u or rf2-fgwf from here, per this bead's instruction. rf2-fgwf stays OPEN: its bench half landed in PR #9052, its docs/design/hicasso/ half was outside that dispatch's write surface.

title: check_keyword_catalogue_drift.py checks source-to-catalogue only, never catalogue-to-source — three ids exist in spec/ and nowhere else
description:
Found by the rf2-dxuzp/rf2-k91an worker while reading the 009 catalogue arm by arm. Reported, not actioned — out of that bead scope.

THE FINDING, measured at ef495cfdc7: NO .clj / .cljc / .cljs file outside spec/ names :rf.error/ui-dispatch-unwired, :rf.error/ui-test-bad-selector, or :rf.error/ui-test-frame-collision. The catalogue documents three error ids that NOTHING EMITS.

AND THE GATE IS GREEN, which is the actual defect: check_keyword_catalogue_drift.py evidently checks SOURCE -> CATALOGUE only — every emitted id has a row — and never asks CATALOGUE -> SOURCE, whether every row has an emitter. So a row for an id that no longer exists is invisible to it forever.

WHY THIS IS THE SAME FAMILY AS EVERYTHING ELSE FOUND THIS WEEK: it is gate blindness — sound machinery, one direction it cannot see. Five-plus instances have been found in this repo in the last few days, including the 009 ratchet pinning the Channel column but not Tags, a bijection gate green on all seven planted defects, and a conformance fixture whose projector had never run over a real record.

WHY IT MATTERS BEYOND TIDINESS: a documented error id with no emitter is a promise to consumers that the framework can produce a diagnostic it cannot. A consumer or an AI reading the catalogue to write a handler for :rf.error/ui-test-bad-selector writes dead code. That is the same class as the reg-route example that throws and the "not IFn" prose — documented claims the code does not keep.

TWO THINGS TO ESTABLISH BEFORE FIXING: (1) are these three DONOR-tier ids? All three carry ui in the name, and rf2-drpa3.57 deletes implementation/ui wholesale — if they retire with the donor, the honest fix is to record that rather than to add a reverse check for rows about to vanish. (2) If a reverse arm IS built, it needs a NON-VACUITY PROOF against these three, and it must be able to distinguish a row whose emitter was deliberately retired from one whose emitter was never written. Without that distinction the arm becomes a nag.

DO NOT build this as a general catalogue-completeness framework. One arm, or a recorded decision that the three rows go.

title: DECLINED (2026-09-08): hicasso capability receipts are NOT built, in any form — only the docs reversal of the Adopt row remains; still carries the standing KEEP for worker/receipts-hic081
description:
DECIDED 2026-09-08 — DECLINED. Capability receipts are NOT built, in any of the five-field, reduced or deferred forms. Do not file an implementation bead; do not pick up the scope list preserved below. The full ruling and its file:line evidence are in this bead's NOTES.

THE DECISION IN ONE LINE: the five-field receipt is refused because its headline field does not measure what it is named for, its load-bearing premise is false on main, and its own tap would corrupt the ranking it exists to inform — so the 'Adopt (counts only)' row at docs/design/hicasso/product/specification.md:361 is REVERSED to an explicit non-adoption. That reversal is the ONLY remaining work and it is a docs PR, filed separately (see the discovered-from child of this bead). The self-time refusal SURVIVES the reversal untouched — Spec 028 depends on it.

CONSEQUENCE FOR THE BRANCH: reversing that row discharges release condition (b) below, after which worker/receipts-hic081 becomes deletable as bookkeeping. The deletion is the operator's, not a worker's, and it happens AFTER the reversal merges — never before, and never as a way of implying the reversal.

THIS BEAD REMAINS A HOLDING RECORD, NOT AN IMPLEMENTATION BEAD. It stays open until the reversal lands and the branch is dealt with. The 2026-09-04 ruling on rf2-7ngc that REJECTED filing an implementation bead for capability receipts stands, and today's ruling reaches the same place from the product side: there is nothing to implement.

WHY IT EXISTS AT ALL — the data half of rf2-94l1. The standing KEEP for worker/receipts-hic081 lives on rf2-lafmr, rf2-hic-081 and rf2-fuuqd, ALL THREE of which have been compacted out of the live tracker (bd show returns 'no issue found' for each; their text survives inside rf2-7ngc's notes and in .beads/issues.jsonl history). So 'bd search receipts-hic081' returned only the hygiene bead re-asking the question. rf2-94l1 fixes the procedure side by adding --status closed to the sweep; this bead fixes the data side by putting the ruling back on an OPEN row. A fourth re-filing needs both to fail.

=== THE STANDING RULING ON THE BRANCH (unchanged; do not re-litigate) ===
worker/receipts-hic081, tip ae14841ab3ac1401ddb2803e8ab4a86bc08ea15c, 3 commits from 2026-08-11, 381 insertions across impl/receipt.cljs (new, 162 lines), test/receipt_spike_cljs_test.cljs (new, 199 lines) and a tap in impl/collector.cljs.

KEEP. No PR, and there never will be one — that IS the design. rf2-hic-081 ('Spike: capability receipts') closed with verdict SPLIT and the close reason ends verbatim: 'Spike commits are pushed on worker/receipts-hic081 and retained as the experiment's record; nothing from them lands on main.' Re-affirmed by rf2-lafmr (mayor ruling 2026-08-21) and again by rf2-7ngc (delegated ruling 2026-09-04, two independent reviewers concurring).

RELEASE CONDITION (rf2-lafmr's, restated so it is findable): delete the branch when EITHER (a) counts-only capability receipts are implemented on main with the owed witnesses discharged, OR (b) the design is EXPLICITLY abandoned — which means reversing the 'Adopt (counts only)' row at docs/design/hicasso/product/specification.md:361, not letting a branch deletion imply it.

TAG-THEN-DELETE WAS CONSIDERED AND REJECTED, twice, and a third proposal to tag it was made on 2026-09-07. Recording the reasoning so it stops recurring: rf2-7ngc ruled 'introduces a naming convention the repo does not use, for no durability the existing ref lacks' — the tree agreed, no such tags exist. A tag and a branch are both refs; refs are what protect objects from gc, so a tag is not more durable than the branch, only differently named. Recording SHAs in a bead IS strictly weaker (unreferenced objects are collectable) and must not be treated as preservation — that error was made and withdrawn on 2026-09-07.

=== THE GAP THIS BEAD RECORDS, WHICH IS REAL ===
Provenance is not ownership. rf2-eoo9 (PR #7898, commit c34090a044, 2026-08-11) landed the design, and specification.md:361 reads 'Capability receipts | Adopt (counts only)'. decision-brief.md:141 lists them under Adopt. So the DECISION is recorded and owned. NOBODY OWNS THE REMAINING IMPLEMENTATION, and no bead tracked it before this one.

SCOPE THAT WAS PROPOSED — ALL SEVEN ITEMS REFUSED 2026-09-08. Preserved verbatim as the record of what was considered and declined, NOT as a worklist. Nobody is to pick these up; the reasons each was refused are in this bead's notes.
  1. A bounded counts-only implementation: five derived fields (body runs, read calls, unique reads, cache hits, codec nodes), self time REFUSED per the adopted row.
  2. Abrupt outcomes. specification.md:361 requires an attempt be counted FROM BODY ENTRY, so a throw, a thrown Suspense promise and a failed lowering are each recorded attempts whose codec-node count reads 'unknown' rather than zero. THE SPIKE FAILS THIS: its tap runs only after codec/as-element returns, so those three leave no receipt at all. rf2-eoo9 ruled the tap into run-once's finally; the spike predates that.
  3. Witness one, the load-bearing one: mutate a cell mid-body and assert the DERIVED cache-hit count still equals the live one. left-field-ideas.md:39 says this is argued from the fence invariant and from the cold path retaining nothing, and was never witnessed adversarially. REFUTED 2026-09-08 — this witness tests the RECEIPT's derivation, not a runtime invariant, so it is NOT worth running once the receipt is declined. See notes.
  4. Witness two: drive a throwing body and a Suspense-throwing body; assert each leaves a recorded attempt whose read facts match the completed case and whose codec-node count reads 'unknown'.
  5. Attached-only allocation: detached must be one deref and one nil test, with nothing built that would be handed to a receipt.
  6. Production erasure. The spike's first cut FAILED 'npm run build:hicasso-release' — 'DEV SURFACE LEAKED: evidence projection' — and the fix was to require no schema. Any implementation re-faces that gate; the rule that failure established belongs with the erasure gate (rf2-nkr3, PR #7878) and is ALREADY PRESERVED THERE on main, independently of this decision.
  7. Browser-path overhead, explicitly UNMEASURED: every number behind the adopted verdict came from the Node lane or the release gate. Moot under the decline.

PRIORITY STAYS P4. The decision is made, so nothing here is urgent; what remains is one small docs PR tracked on the child bead. Do not raise this bead's priority to chase the reversal — chase the child.

DO NOT dispatch this bead to a worker as implementation work, and DO NOT re-litigate the ruling. The reopen trigger, and the only shape a future receipt may take, are stated at the end of the notes.
notes:
Filed 2026-09-07 09:2x AUSEST as part of the rf2-jojz ruling. The scope list above is owed to a third-party review that correctly widened it from 'two witnesses' and correctly objected to a reflexive P2; the branch disposition in it is the standing ruling, which that review did not have in front of it.

=== RULING 2026-09-08 23:27 AUSEST — DECLINED (decision closeout; dossier weighed against Codex Recommendation) ===
Verified against main @ 432a93da1545593fcb3d403eaa99c42e7e49a471.

--- 1. THE DECISION ---
CAPABILITY RECEIPTS ARE DECLINED. Not built in the five-field form, not built in a reduced form, not deferred behind a trigger. No impl/receipt.cljs, no fifth evidence read, no advisor axis. The "Adopt (counts only)" row at docs/design/hicasso/product/specification.md:361 is REVERSED to an explicit non-adoption, and decision-brief.md:141's Adopt list is corrected to match. Because nothing is emitted, NOTHING CONSUMES A RECEIPT — that is the finding, not an omission. The self-time refusal is NOT reversed with it: it survives verbatim, because tools/xray/spec/028-Hicasso-Advisor.md, hicasso_advisor.cljc:28 and hicasso_reads.cljs:100 all cite it as normative upstream for the empty Hiccup-lowering row.

No public name is created, so spec/API.md, spec/api-manifest-metadata.edn and the generated spec/api-manifest.edn are NOT in play and no manifest regeneration is owed. The whole remaining footprint is docs/design/hicasso/.

--- 2. WHY, AND WHO WON ---
CODEX WINS, comprehensively. The original dossier recommended Option A (build, sequenced, P3, witnesses first) and rested it on two pillars. Codex refuted both from source, and I re-verified both against main before ruling. A third defect — the tap corrupting the very ranking it exists to inform — is fatal on its own under the design's OWN stated kill rule. The dossier's central persuasive artefact, its worked specimen, is arithmetically wrong. Where Codex itself hedged (landing on "defer at P4 pending a useful diagnostic witness", with full abandonment named as also reasonable), I go further and DECLINE outright: deferral is what produced four rounds of this conversation, and the dossier is right that it has a track record of not holding here — its own Option C note calls deferral "the option most likely to produce a fifth round".

--- 3. THE LOAD-BEARING ANALYSIS ---

(a) THE HEADLINE FIELD DOES NOT MEASURE WHAT IT IS NAMED FOR. Verified at implementation/hicasso/src/re_frame/hicasso/impl/codec.cljs, in as-element's case over child-kind: the :react-element branch is literally "x" — an already-built React element is returned UNCHANGED, doing no lowering at all. The spike's receipt.cljs:100 nevertheless walks props.children recursively. So a body returning a prebuilt 1000-child element earns a 1000-node receipt for zero lowering work, while a body constructing equivalent hiccup earns a similar count for real work. The direct-return escape is not hypothetical: implementation/hicasso/test/re_frame/hicasso/direct_return_cljs_test.cljs:386 probes the codec entry and establishes it. Compounding this, a functional child's eventual output is not present in the element the parent returns at all. codec-nodes therefore describes RETURNED STRUCTURE, not lowering cost, and cannot fill Spec 028's Hiccup-lowering row. The dossier's pillar 2 — "the only instrument anyone has proposed for a hole a shipped surface documents" — is false, and the name codec-nodes actively overpromises.

(b) THE LOAD-BEARING PREMISE IS FALSE ON MAIN, AND ITS FAILURE INDICTS THE RECEIPT, NOT THE RUNTIME. The derivation removes the per-read counter by claiming an end-of-attempt recheck returns the answer each read actually got, argued from the fence invariant plus a retention-free cold path. Verified in impl/collector.cljs: render-body (circa line 1127) captures basis-before, calls run-once, and compares commit-basis ONLY AFTER run-once RETURNS. That constrains the ACCEPTED pass; it says nothing about the read history of a pass still in flight. And invalidate-cell! (circa line 344) does (set! (.-reaction cell) nil) SYNCHRONOUSLY, deferring only the re-wire and mark-dirty! to a queueMicrotask. So the adversarial sequence is: read a warm key, re-register that subscription mid-body, finish the body. The reaction is nil'd synchronously, no commit has landed, the fence does not re-run — and the end-of-attempt recheck scores an earlier WARM read as COLD. hmr_registry_cljs_test.cljs:224 already exercises that synchronous drop and later repair. Neither Codex nor I executed the new mid-body composition; the structure is confirmed at source and that is enough to rule.
CRITICAL CONSEQUENCE: this kills the dossier's pillar 1, its single strongest argument — that witness one is "worth running whatever you decide" because it tests a claim the RUNTIME makes about itself, so specification.md:361 and Spec 028 would be wrong on main today if it failed. They would not. The fence's claim is about the ACCEPTED render; the receipt's claim is about EVERY ATTEMPTED pass. Only the latter is at risk, so with the receipt declined there is NO standalone reason to commission witness one. Do not resurrect it as a cheap, high-information experiment; it is neither.

(c) THE TAP CORRUPTS THE RANKING IT EXISTS TO INFORM — and this trips the design's own kill rule. Verified in impl/collector.cljs circa line 1235: the boundary component is (fn hicasso-boundary [js-props] (rf.performance/mark-and-measure :render view-name (shell body-fn js-props))). shell reaches render-body reaches run-once, so a tap in run-once's finally sits INSIDE the User-Timing :render bracket. Attached, that tap allocates a set, pushes every read key for dedup, rechecks every key against the cell table, and walks every node of the returned element — work proportional to read count and output size, charged to the render measure that the hot-view advisor's TIME axis ranks on. left-field-ideas.md's own rule is "Kill the idea if instrumentation changes rankings or requires production retention." It does. The spike's cheapness evidence covers only the DETACHED path (one deref, one nil test); its witness proves no table survives detachment, which does not measure attached transient allocation. The 8.9 ns/child figure quoted in support is child DISPATCH cost from docs/design/hicasso/studio/our-walk-against-reagents.md:284, not the cost of lowering a child.

(d) "CACHE HITS" IS A MISNOMER THAT WOULD MISLEAD. Verified in impl/collector.cljs cold-read! (circa 568-600): it reuses a substrate reaction via (:reaction (get @(:sub-cache frame-record) query-v)) even when NO collector cell is warm, and it memoizes repeated cold reads within an attempt in the probe's vals map — the code's own comment notes that a memoised nil "is a HIT". cold_probe_cljs_test.cljs:239 and :305 already distinguish these cases. So the derived number means COMMITTED COLLECTOR-CELL HITS, not avoided computation and not all cache reuse. A low reading sends a programmer hunting work that never ran. Under this project's posture that is a nag-diagnostic that lies, which is worse than no diagnostic.

(e) NO CONSUMER, AND THE TRANSPORT IS NOT FREE. Verified: re-frame.hicasso.evidence (implementation/hicasso/src/re_frame/hicasso/evidence.cljs:39) is a CLOSED set of four — #{:mounted-boundaries :read-attribution :intents :explain-render} — its docstring reading "The four read operations", and envelope throws outside it. Pair exposes THREE reads, not the four the dossier claimed: tools/re-frame2-pair-mcp/src/re_frame2_pair_mcp/tools/hicasso_tool.cljs tier-reads is ["read-mounted-boundaries" "read-read-attribution" "explain-render"], and consumed-evidence-schema just below it pins :re-frame.hicasso.evidence/v3 as a deliberately CONSUMER-OWNED literal whose docstring says a projection stamped a schema this build does not understand is reported as a typed mismatch, never forwarded. So the dossier's "a fifth would need no new transport" is wrong: a fifth read means editing the closed set and its docstring, answering the v3-to-v4 question against a schema whose own docstring says there is no compatibility path, and TEACHING Pair. The dossier itself found no code on main waiting for a receipt — every downstream citation of the design section is for what it KILLED (self time), never for what it adopted — and I did not disturb that finding. Nothing breaks without receipts.

(f) THE DOSSIER'S WORKED SPECIMEN IS ARITHMETICALLY WRONG, and it was the document's most persuasive page. It reads 1310 read-calls against 31 unique-reads as "a 42x duplication ratio ... re-reading the same subscriptions inside a loop". But 1310 calls over 42 attempts is 31.19 calls per attempt against 31 distinct keys per attempt — roughly EIGHT duplicate calls across the whole window, about 1.006 per distinct read occurrence. It compared a cross-attempt aggregate against a per-attempt distinct count. The one headline finding the specimen was drawn to demonstrate is an artefact of that error. Its second reading is unsound too: 420 attempts cannot establish 420 upstream notifications, since props, context, fence retries and dev-mode React double-invocation all produce attempts.

(g) THE SPIKE IS DEAD AS A PATCH REGARDLESS, on the dossier's own verified evidence: evidence/projection no longer exists (it is envelope, v3, folding scope/basis into complete?/loss); set-lowering-owner! is gone from the package (0 hits, against an as-element control of 36 across 8 files); collector.cljs restructured by roughly 550 lines. Three drifts in four weeks. It stays valuable only as the record of the reasoning, which is exactly what the standing KEEP says it is for.

(h) INTERNAL VS AUTHOR-FACING COST, for the record: receipts would have been WHOLLY INTERNAL — no app author passes, threads, names or remembers anything. That is the cheapest category of API cost and the strongest thing that could be said for the proposal. It is not enough, because the emitted number is unsound (a, d), the derivation is unsound (b), the emission perturbs the measurement (c), and nothing reads it (e).

--- 4. DELIBERATELY OUT OF SCOPE — DO NOT ADD THESE LATER "TO FINISH THE JOB" ---
REFUSED, each by name: (i) impl/receipt.cljs in any form, including a reduced attempts-plus-read-calls-only version landed now; (ii) a fifth member of evidence/reads and any v3-to-v4 schema bump undertaken for it; (iii) any Pair MCP descriptor or tier-reads change for receipts; (iv) a fifth ranking axis on the Hicasso advisor, and any tools/xray/spec/028 amendment beyond leaving its lowering row honestly empty; (v) witness one (mid-body cell mutation) as standalone work — see 3(b), it is not a runtime-invariant test; (vi) witness two (throwing and Suspense-throwing bodies) as receipt work; (vii) a browser-path overhead measurement for a tap that will not exist; (viii) any new spec paragraph, Spec-Schemas entry, lint rule, api-manifest entry or backfill; (ix) re-opening the tag-then-delete question for worker/receipts-hic081, already rejected three times. Self time remains refused as it always was — that refusal is load-bearing downstream and must SURVIVE the reversal, not be reversed alongside it.

--- 5. NEXT STEPS ---
Exactly one piece of work remains, filed as a discovered-from child of this bead: the docs reversal PR. Four files, and its whole risk is surgical precision — reverse specification.md:361 to an explicit non-adoption citing this ruling; correct decision-brief.md:141's Adopt list; rewrite the left-field-ideas.md Capability receipts section so it reads as a CLOSED investigation rather than a live design, KEEPING the self-time kill intact and correcting its now-stale sentence about the finally clause needing a "lowering-owner clear" (that clear is gone from the package; the finally on main is the frame reset only); and check the result against tools/xray/spec/028-Hicasso-Advisor.md, hicasso_advisor.cljc:28 and hicasso_reads.cljs:100 before merge, since all three cite that section for the self-time refusal. Note for whoever takes it: docs/design/** is excluded from the mkdocs strict build via exclude_docs, so that is NOT the gate for this diff.

AFTER it merges, release condition (b) is discharged and worker/receipts-hic081 becomes deletable — the operator's action, after the merge, never as a substitute for it. This bead then has no work left in it; the close is left to the operator.

REOPEN TRIGGER, recorded so it is not re-asked, and NOT as a live proposal: a real diagnosis in which the advisor's ranking points at read topology and the true owner turns out to be tree size. Codex named the concrete reproduction — implementation/hicasso/test/re_frame/hicasso/examples/grid/scaling_dom_cljs_test.cljs:26, where fine reads and coarse-reads-with-scalar-props both run two bodies while the coarse parent still constructs and compares many children. If that ever bites in earnest, the ONLY shape to reconsider is per-boundary ATTEMPT counts (attempts, read-calls, sum of per-attempt distinct reads), grouped by frame and declared view, stated as view aggregates rather than instance identities, WITH a real Xray or Pair consumer in the same PR. title: hygiene: three orphan worker branches carry unmerged commits with no PR and no bead — decide keep-or-drop (naming-tools-story x2 net-zero, receipts-hic081 spike)
description:
Found by the §5 hygiene loop, 2026-09-06 18:4x AUSEST. All three survive the cherry test as "+" (not patch-present on main), so §5 correctly KEEPS them — "+" is absence of proof of merge, not evidence of unmerged work. But none has a PR, none has a bead, and one is 26 days old. Recording them so they are a decision rather than sediment.

MEASURED at origin/main a36196ced4 (git cherry origin/main <branch>; git diff --name-only origin/main...<branch>; gh pr list --head <name> --state all):

1. worker/naming-tools-story-20260903 — cherry +1. One commit, 2026-09-03 14:29:48: "docs(story): correct Story build count", touching tools/story/README.md. No PR, ever.

2. worker/naming-tools-story-20260903-r1 — cherry +2, but its NET DIFF VS MAIN IS EMPTY. It carries the same commit as (1) plus "revert(docs): leave Story build count outside naming scope" at 14:32:36 — three minutes later. So somebody made the change, judged it outside the naming campaign scope, and reverted it in place. THE BRANCH CONTRIBUTES NOTHING: git diff --name-only origin/main...<branch> returns zero files. This is the case where the cherry test and the net-content test disagree, and the net-content test is the one that matters for "would deleting this lose work" — it would not. I did not delete it, because §5 binds on cherry and the decision is cheap to leave; but it is safe to drop whenever anyone wants to.

3. worker/receipts-hic081 — cherry +3, from 2026-08-11 (26 days before this sweep). Three SPIKE commits: "capability receipts derived from the runtime own leavings", "the receipt witness, green on the hicasso node lane", "split the projection out of the runtime, as the erasure gate demanded". Touches implementation/hicasso/src/re_frame/hicasso/impl/collector.cljs, a NEW file impl/receipt.cljs, and test/re_frame/hicasso/receipt_spike_cljs_test.cljs. THIS IS THE ONE THAT MATTERS: real exploratory work, a named erasure-gate motivation, its own green test lane, and no tracker record of any kind. The Mayor Method README warns in terms that work written outside the tracked record gets lost — "two audits were lost that way here". A spike is allowed to die, but it should die with its reasoning recorded rather than by nobody noticing.

WHAT IS WANTED, and it is small: for (3), someone who knows the hicasso erasure-gate context decides whether the receipt idea is live (promote to a bead with the spike branch cited), superseded (record what replaced it and drop), or abandoned (record why and drop). For (1) and (2), confirm the 2026-09-03 revert stands — if the Story build count in tools/story/README.md is in fact WRONG on main, that is a separate one-line bug worth its own bead; the revert only said the fix was out of scope for the naming campaign, NOT that the count was right. Nobody has checked which.

NOT URGENT, and deliberately P4. Branches cost nothing to keep and the cherry test protects them from this loop. The point of this bead is that they stop being invisible.
notes:
MAYOR 2026-09-07 02:2x AUSEST: ALL THREE BRANCHES ANALYSED AT SOURCE SO THIS BECOMES A ONE-LINE DECISION. I have deleted nothing — see the cherry result, which is the reason.

BRANCH 1 — worker/naming-tools-story-20260903. ONE commit, 0b508e744e, "docs(story): correct Story build count". Its entire content is a single line in tools/story/README.md: "Four Story-enabled builds are wired into the top-level :dev-http map" -> "Five".
ITS INTENDED END STATE IS ALREADY ON MAIN. tools/story/README.md:142 today reads "Five Story-enabled builds are wired into the top-level `:dev-http` map" — matched byte-for-byte with grep -cF, count 1. So the correction this branch carries was made by some other route and the branch's work is moot.

BRANCH 2 — worker/naming-tools-story-20260903-r1. TWO commits: the same 0b508e744e, plus ce02cf3cec "revert(docs): leave Story build count outside naming scope". Its NET DIFF AGAINST THE MERGE BASE IS EMPTY — git diff --name-only returns nothing and --shortstat returns nothing. The branch applies a change and reverts it, so it contains no content at all. Its one piece of information is the revert's own message: an author deciding the build-count fix was out of that dispatch's naming scope. That decision is now moot too, since the fix landed anyway.

BRANCH 3 — worker/receipts-hic081. THREE commits from 2026-08-11, 381 insertions across 3 files:
  implementation/hicasso/src/re_frame/hicasso/impl/receipt.cljs             (new)
  implementation/hicasso/test/re_frame/hicasso/receipt_spike_cljs_test.cljs (new)
  implementation/hicasso/src/re_frame/hicasso/impl/collector.cljs           (edited)
Commit subjects: "capability receipts derived from the runtime's own leavings", "the receipt witness, green on the hicasso node lane", "split the projection out of the runtime, as the erasure gate demanded".
THIS ONE IS NOT SUPERSEDED. Both new files are ABSENT from main, and 'receipt' returns just 1 hit across all of implementation/hicasso. Every commit calls itself a SPIKE. So it is genuine unmerged exploratory work, four weeks old, and nothing has replaced it.

WHY I DELETED NOTHING, AND THIS IS THE PART WORTH KEEPING. Per loops.md §5 the authority for deleting a branch is git cherry patch-equivalence, and only a '-' authorises it. All three branches read '+' on EVERY commit:
  worker/naming-tools-story-20260903      + 0b508e744e
  worker/naming-tools-story-20260903-r1   + 0b508e744e, + ce02cf3cec
  worker/receipts-hic081                  + fece72f80a, + 418312d680, + ae14841ab3
Branch 1 is the instructive case: its END STATE is on main byte-for-byte, and cherry still says '+'. That is not a contradiction — cherry compares PATCHES, and a patch that produces the same line from different context, in a different commit, is not patch-equivalent. So "the outcome is already on main" and "the branch is provably contained in main" are DIFFERENT claims, and only the second licenses deletion. A reader who saw the matching line and deleted on that basis would be discarding a branch on the wrong test, and would be right by luck.

MY RECOMMENDATION, for a one-line answer:
  DROP branch 1 — its outcome is already on main; nothing is lost.
  DROP branch 2 — it contains nothing; its net diff is empty.
  For branch 3, KEEP or FILE-AND-DROP. A branch costs nothing to keep, so the cheap default is keep. If you would rather the roster were clean, the alternative is that I file a bead capturing the receipts idea with these three commit ids in it, and then the branch is droppable without losing the thought.
On your word I will delete whichever you name, using the merge-verified path rather than cherry (which cannot authorise these), i.e. an explicit decision recorded here first.
MAYOR HYGIENE 2026-09-07 06:5x AUSEST: THE `git cherry` TEST IS NOW PROVEN TO DISCRIMINATE ON THIS BOX, so the `+` these three branches keep returning is real evidence rather than a possible instrument failure. That was an open question I had flagged twice without resolving; it is closed.

WHY IT NEEDED PROVING. §5 authorises deleting a branch only on a `-` from `git cherry` — patch-equivalence with something already on the trunk — and treats `+` as absence of proof rather than proof of absence. All three of these branches have read `+` on every check across this session. But I had never seen this box's `git cherry` emit a `-` at all, so "always +" was equally consistent with a broken instrument, under which the rule would hold the branches forever for no reason.

THE CONTROL, and the first two I tried were vacuous. Pointing cherry at a branch one commit BEHIND main returns 0 and 0 — nothing ahead to classify, so it says nothing about whether `-` is reachable. What works is a commit that is patch-equivalent to a trunk commit but carries a DIFFERENT sha, which is exactly the shape a merged-then-rebased branch has. Synthesised with plumbing rather than a checkout:
    tree=$(git rev-parse 'origin/main~1^{tree}')
    parent=$(git rev-parse 'origin/main~2')
    ctl=$(git commit-tree "$tree" -p "$parent" -m "control")
That commit has main~1's tree on main~2's parent — same patch, new identity. `git cherry origin/main <it>` returns:
    - ecc64e0c89474f0989909509c10a21fb982dbaed
minus=1, plus=0. The instrument emits `-` when a `-` is warranted.

MEASURED THE SAME TICK, against current main:
    worker/naming-tools-story-20260903      minus=0  plus=1
    worker/naming-tools-story-20260903-r1   minus=0  plus=2
    worker/receipts-hic081                  minus=0  plus=3
So §5 does not authorise deleting any of them, and that verdict now rests on a test known to be capable of the opposite answer.

WHAT THIS DOES AND DOES NOT SETTLE. It does NOT contradict the earlier finding that branch 1's END STATE is already on main byte-for-byte, or that branch 2's net diff is EMPTY. Cherry compares PATCHES commit by commit, so a branch whose cumulative effect landed by a different route — squashed, re-authored, or arrived at through several other PRs — still reads `+` on every commit. Both things are true at once: the content is present, and the commits are not patch-equivalent to anything on the trunk. That is precisely why this stays an operator call rather than a mechanical one.

MY RECOMMENDATION IS UNCHANGED from the earlier analysis: drop 1 and 2, and either keep 3 or file its content and drop it (381 insertions, the hicasso receipts spike, not superseded by anything on main). Nothing here is urgent — three unreferenced branches cost nothing but a line each in the remote listing.
close_reason:
RULED AND EXECUTED 2026-09-07 09:1x-09:2x AUSEST. Two branches deleted, one kept under a standing ruling, two follow-ups filed. Verified at origin/main b3a3c41537.

=== 1. worker/naming-tools-story-20260903 — DELETED (remote and local) ===
Remote tip was 221efbb4323c0c14c926b22384215e8e66589e31; local ref was 0b508e744e02488032aa1c690353e3627e7580f8. THE GUARD CAUGHT THAT DIVERGENCE and it is worth recording: the two are the SAME one-line change on different bases, 32 seconds apart, stable patch-id 6f6bf4df0fc1e90622db92e2eb14683d36241b89 on both, one file, +1/-1. Two attempts at the same fix, not two changes. Nothing lost. Had the local ref been deleted on the remote's expected sha without checking, the mismatch would have gone unseen; the sha-guarded loop refused it and the comparison was then cheap.

ITS OUTCOME IS ON MAIN AND IS CORRECT — this closes the open question the description left ('Nobody has checked which'). tools/story/README.md:142 reads 'Five Story-enabled builds are wired into the top-level :dev-http map'. Five is RIGHT: the README table lists five story builds (8040 nine-states, 8041 login, 8042 counter-with-stories, 8043 login-form, 8045 hicasso-counter) and implementation/shadow-cljs.edn's :dev-http map has exactly those five story-rooted ports (8044 is linearlite, not a story build). SO NO BUILD-COUNT BUG BEAD IS OWED. The 2026-09-03 revert stands and was only ever a scope judgement.

Tip ae14841ab3ac1401ddb2803e8ab4a86bc08ea15c, verified unmoved after the deletions.

THIS BEAD'S CENTRAL PREMISE WAS FALSE. The description says the spike has 'no tracker record of any kind' and a mayor note added 'THIS ONE IS NOT SUPERSEDED'. Both are wrong, and rf2-jojz is the THIRD re-filing of a question settled three times:
  rf2-hic-081 closed with verdict SPLIT, close reason ending verbatim: 'Spike commits are pushed on worker/receipts-hic081 and retained as the experiment's record; nothing from them lands on main.' The absence of a PR IS the design.
  rf2-lafmr (mayor ruling 2026-08-21) — KEEP with an explicit release condition.
  rf2-7ngc (delegated ruling 2026-09-04, two independent reviewers concurring) — re-verified at source, KEEP re-affirmed.
  bd memory 'worker-receipts-hic081-is-a-retained-spike-record': 'do not delete it, and do not re-file it as hygiene residue.'
  bd memory 'hygiene-cannot-tell-a-strand-from-a-retained-record': 'A future hygiene pass that rescues it would re-litigate a closed decision.' That is this bead.

The findings ARE on main, and the census that missed them was scoped to implementation/hicasso only — a single-axis census, the trap CLAUDE.md names. They landed via rf2-eoo9 (PR #7898, commit c34090a044, 2026-08-11): specification.md:361 'Capability receipts | Adopt (counts only)', decision-brief.md:141 under Adopt, and lanes/left-field-ideas.md:27-39 carrying the derivation, the attempt-vs-commit seam decision and the two owed witnesses. left-field-ideas.md:31 says in terms: 'The rf2-hic-081 spike decided this row and retained no code'.

TWO PROPOSALS REJECTED, both already rejected on the record and re-proposed on 2026-09-07:

  TAG-THEN-DELETE: rejected by rf2-7ngc — 'introduces a naming convention the repo does not use, for no durability the existing ref lacks', tree agreed, no such tags exist.
