title: Decide how far the api-manifest roster-completeness gate should widen: 243 namespaces sit under trees it does not cover
description:
PR #9040 restored the roster-completeness gate (orphaned since the freehand retirement c951808b47) and enrolled two source trees. This bead is the OPEN QUESTION it deliberately did not answer, recorded so the narrow scope is a decision rather than an omission.

MEASURED at 375d5dd899: 276 namespaces under implementation/ are absent from jvm-namespaces. #9040's two roots account for 33 of them (25 ssr, 8 ssr-ring), all now classified internal. The remaining 243 are in trees the gate does not read:

  core 84 · machines 33 · routing 28 · hicasso 25 · resources 23 · http 17
  adapters/reagent-slim 9 · schemas 7 · epoch 5 · test-quiet 5 · flows 3
  spec-resource 1 · adapters/{reagent,test-react,uix} 1 each

A namespace in an uncovered tree is still UNSCANNED in exactly the sense rf2-8arzr.7 described: absent from the roster is not unclassified, and every manifest-derived gate is blind to it at once. That class produced re-frame.resources (rf2-ivuun), two freehand namespaces (rf2-h0b0l, rf2-cfhuv) and the three ssr-node ones.

THE COST IS THE DECISION. Enrolling a tree obliges a human classification for every namespace under it, recorded in internal-namespaces with a reason. That is real editorial work — 84 for core alone — and rf2-o8xev's original write-up made the same call for the same reason: 'Widening it to the other artefacts is a separate decision with a separate cost, not a free generalisation.'

The mechanism no longer argues against it, which is what changed: roster-covered-roots is data, so a tree is a root plus its classifications and never another mechanism. Options: (a) widen tree by tree as each is touched, cheapest and never blocks anyone; (b) one sweep, expensive but ends the class; (c) leave it at the SSR trees and accept the rest stay unscanned. Not urgent, and (a) is the de facto status quo.
notes:
MAYOR RULING 2026-09-03 06:1x AUSEST. WIDEN IT, BUT ONE TREE PER DISPATCH AND HIGHEST-RISK FIRST. Do not enrol all thirteen, and do not leave it where it is.

WHY NOT LEAVE IT. The class this gate catches is not hypothetical and the bead names its victims: re-frame.resources (rf2-ivuun), two freehand namespaces (rf2-h0b0l, rf2-cfhuv), and the three ssr-node ones. That is SIX namespaces that shipped unscanned, found one at a time, each by somebody noticing. And rf2-3ne8 added a seventh finding on top of it - of the 26 under implementation/hicasso/src, FIVE turned out to be PUBLIC AUTHORING SURFACES with no documentation page at all, which nobody had spotted because the manifest could not see them. The gate does not merely record a roster; it is the only instrument that turns "we forgot" into "the build refuses".

WHY NOT ALL THIRTEEN AT ONCE. The cost is real and it is EDITORIAL, not mechanical: every namespace under an enrolled root needs a human classification with a reason. 84 for core alone. A dispatch that tries to classify 243 namespaces will either time out or produce 243 rubber-stamped entries, and a rubber-stamped classification is worse than none because it looks like a decision.

THE ORDER, and the ordering principle is BLAST RADIUS OF A MISS rather than count:
  1. hicasso (25) - ALREADY DONE by rf2-3ne8. Proof the per-tree shape works, and the tree that yielded five undocumented public surfaces.
  2. routing (28) and resources (23) - the two trees whose namespaces are most likely to carry PUBLIC authoring surfaces an app requires directly. The route-link P0 came out of routing this session; a public surface there being invisible to every manifest gate is the same shape of exposure.
  3. http (17), machines (33), schemas (7), flows (3), epoch (5) - feature artefacts with public API.
  4. core (84) LAST, not first. It is the biggest and the most tempting, and it is also the tree whose namespaces are best known and most likely to be genuinely internal - so it has the worst work-to-finding ratio, and doing it first would exhaust the appetite for the rest.
  5. adapters/* (3), reagent-slim (9), test-quiet (5), spec-resource (1) - small tails, fold into whichever dispatch has room.

FILE ONE BEAD PER TREE as you go rather than tracking it here, each carrying its own namespace count and its own classification. This bead stays open as the parent question until the last tree lands, and it should record which trees are done.

WHAT I AM NOT RULING: whether every root eventually gets enrolled. Stop and re-ask after step 2 - if routing and resources yield nothing but internal classifications, that is evidence the remaining trees are not worth the editorial cost, and the honest answer then is to stop and record why. THE MEASUREMENT DECIDES THE TAIL, not this ruling.

AND THE STANCE POINT, because it cuts both ways here: enrolling a tree is not gold plating - it is the gate refusing to let a public surface ship unrecorded, which is exactly the ergonomics-and-low-friction goal. But rubber-stamping 243 entries to reach a green IS gold plating, of the worst kind: effort spent producing the appearance of coverage.
STEP 2 MEASURED AND REPORTED (rf2-hjj4, PR #9063, 2026-09-03). Trees done: hicasso (rf2-3ne8), routing + resources (rf2-hjj4). roster-covered-roots is now five roots.

THE MEASUREMENT THE RULING ASKED FOR: 51 unaccounted namespaces (routing 28, resources 23), ALL 51 CLASSIFIED INTERNAL. Zero public authoring surfaces, zero new manifest rows (528 -> 528), zero new docs/api pages, zero nav entries. That is the ruling's own stop signal.

BUT THE REASON MATTERS MORE THAN THE ARITHMETIC, and it should govern the tail rather than the schedule does. Routing and resources are FACADE artefacts: one enrolled door re-exports everything an app may call (27 rows and 21 rows respectively), and the siblings are the concerns it composes - handler bodies, *-meta registration maps, cofx constructors, *-sub-fn bodies, host-side caches. Hicasso is the OPPOSITE shape: its five modules are separately requirable BECAUSE they are opt-in, so its door structurally could not re-export them, which is why five surfaces could hide there. THE PREDICTOR IS NOT TREE SIZE - it is whether the artefact has a single re-exporting door.

By that test the ruling's remaining steps 3-5 look like routing/resources rather than hicasso: machines, http, schemas, flows, epoch and core each publish ONE facade namespace already in jvm-namespaces. WORKER RECOMMENDATION (not a decision taken; this bead stays open as the parent question): stop enrolling trees on a schedule, and instead enrol a tree WHEN IT ACQUIRES A SECOND REQUIRABLE DOOR - the condition that actually produces findings. The reasoning is written into gen.clj's own section header so it is met where the decision is made.

TWO CAVEATS. (1) The gate still earns its keep on the two trees enrolled: it now REFUSES a new unclassified namespace under either, which is the 'we forgot' -> 'the build refuses' conversion this bead wanted, worth the 51 lines regardless of today's zero findings. (2) adapters/* is the one part of the tail NOT covered by the facade argument - adapters are requirable by definition, so if any tree is enrolled next, that is where to look first, ahead of core.

ONE THING FOR A RULING, raised by rf2-hjj4 rather than settled by it: the four .tooling / .test-support siblings. skills/re-frame2/references/tooling/routing.md:180 tells app authors to write (:require [re-frame.routing.test-support]) - a documented direct require, the hicasso signature - yet the require is for its LOAD EFFECT and the consumer-facing names are an event id and a late-bind hook, not the one public var each namespace holds. They were classified internal on that ground, so the roster now says 'not a supported surface' about a namespace the skills tell people to require. The manifest is one row per public VAR and neither var is one, so there is nothing to row; inventing a require-for-effect vocabulary would be over-engineering. If that reads wrong, the fix is a tier on those two, not a change to the gate.
MAYOR RULING 2026-09-03 07:3x AUSEST — I AM REPLACING MY OWN ORDERING RULE WITH THE WORKER STRUCTURAL ONE. STOP THE SCHEDULED WIDENING.

WHAT STEP 2 MEASURED (rf2-hjj4, PR #9063): routing 29 namespaces / 28 unaccounted, resources 24 / 23 - and 51 of 51 classified INTERNAL. ZERO public authoring surfaces. No manifest row (528 -> 528), no docs/api page, no nav entry. That is the exact opposite of hicasso, where five of twenty-six were public surfaces with no documentation page.

MY ORDERING RULE WAS "BLAST RADIUS, NOT COUNT" AND IT WAS THE WRONG AXIS. I put routing and resources first because routing produced the route-link P0 and both looked likely to carry public surfaces. They carry none, and the worker found the reason, which is structural rather than statistical: ROUTING AND RESOURCES ARE FACADE ARTEFACTS - ONE DOOR RE-EXPORTS EVERYTHING AN APP MAY CALL. Hicasso is the opposite: its modules are SEPARATELY REQUIRABLE BECAUSE THEY ARE OPT-IN, which is precisely why five surfaces could hide behind an unenrolled root. Nothing can hide behind a single re-exporting door, because the door is already rowed.

THE RULE I AM ADOPTING, in the worker words: THE PREDICTOR IS NOT TREE SIZE BUT WHETHER THE ARTEFACT HAS A SINGLE RE-EXPORTING DOOR. Enrol a tree WHEN IT ACQUIRES A SECOND REQUIRABLE DOOR, not on a schedule. machines, http, schemas, flows, epoch and core all match the routing/resources shape, so the remaining 190-odd namespaces under them are not worth the editorial cost on present evidence - and rubber-stamping them would be the gold plating I warned against when I ruled step 2.

THE ONE EXCEPTION WORTH LOOKING AT: adapters/*. Adapters are REQUIRABLE BY DEFINITION - an app requires the adapter it uses - so they have the hicasso shape rather than the facade shape, at 3 namespaces total. That is cheap enough to be worth doing on its own evidence rather than on a schedule, and it is the only tree I would enrol next.

THIS BEAD STAYS OPEN as the standing question, now with a decision procedure rather than a queue: when an artefact gains a second requirable door, enrol it then. The recommendation is also written into gen.clj section header by PR #9063, so the rule lives beside the mechanism rather than only in the tracker.

AND THE MEASUREMENT DECIDED THE TAIL EXACTLY AS THE RULING SAID IT WOULD. I wrote "if routing and resources yield nothing but internal classifications, that is evidence the remaining trees are not worth the editorial cost, and the honest answer is to stop and record why." They did. This is that.
THE "adapters/*, THREE NAMESPACES" EXCEPTION DOES NOT HOLD AS STATED. Measured 2026-09-03 07:5x AUSEST by the mayor, at the point of filing it as the next slice, which is why it was checked rather than inherited.

THE COUNT IS 15, NOT 3. `find implementation/adapters -path '*/src/*' -name '*.clj*'` returns fifteen namespace files:
  reagent/src           1  (re-frame.adapter.reagent)

Enrolling `implementation/adapters/*/src` in roster-covered-roots obliges a classification for every namespace beneath the root — gen.clj:248-252 says so in terms — so the real bill is eleven rubber-stamp entries for somebody else's library internals. THAT IS PRECISELY THE EDITORIAL COST THIS BEAD'S OWN RULING SAID TO REFUSE, and the ruling recommended it because the count made it look free.

WHAT SURVIVES, AND IT IS SMALL. reagent/src and uix/src are one namespace each, both already public doors, both already rowed. Enrolling just those two roots is genuinely cheap — but the VALUE of enrolling a root is that it catches a NEW namespace appearing beneath it unclassified, and beneath a root holding one door that is close to zero. So the cheap version is also the version that buys least.

MY CALL: DO NOT FILE THE SLICE. Not now and not as ruled. This is minutiae, and the stance says so — enrolling two roots to protect against a namespace nobody is adding is gold plating with a governance costume on. The DECISION PROCEDURE this bead adopted is the durable part and it is unaffected: enrol a tree when it acquires a second requirable door. reagent-slim already HAS a second door in the sense that matters (reagent2.core is requirable), which is an argument for enrolling it and immediately an argument against, because the eleven behind it are a fork rather than a surface.

description:

Preserve action-only candidates when enumerating the leaf's :on events, provide a clear targetless row label, and retain the existing event-input/step flow. Flat action-only events also list. Regression coverage retains ordinary targeted events, region-prefixed paths, and the intentional exclusion of ancestor/root :on fallbacks. The UI does not invent a target.

The SURFACE fence releases on MERGE, never on the worker's report. description:
Two one-line prose staleness follow-ups, both created by PR #10168 (rf2-fn0kx.3, merged as 9b1212ef4850ab8818a7af4c46070253fd00ef88) and both deliberately held out of that branch's fence by its worker rather than made silently. They are UNBLOCKED as of that merge.

Each is a one-toucher in a different tree, so they are one dispatch and one PR.

## 1. `spec/Construction-Prompts.md` — the CP-3 row names a renamed fx id

The CP-3 row reads that Flight Booker "shows a custom `:notify` fx". PR #10168 finding 2 renamed that id to `:flight/notify`, because `:notify` was the one example breaking the prefix-every-registered-id-with-your-own-stem convention that `examples/TESTING.md` sets out — and it did so in the very example a reader is sent to for "how to register an fx". So the table cell now names an id that no longer exists.

The row wants `:flight/notify`.

## 2. `docs/core/how-to/boot-and-mount-an-app.md` — describes a listener the file does not contain

The page says `todomvc/core.cljs` "adds URL routing, a `hashchange` listener, and `:url-bound? true`". That is finding 7's other half: `core.cljs` installs no such listener. `:url-bound? true` plus the hash `:url-strategy` is what causes the frame to install it — as the file's own comment already says.

Replacement text suggested by #10168's worker, carried here verbatim from the PR body so it does not evaporate with it:

  "adds URL routing via `:url-bound? true` and a hash `:url-strategy` (the frame installs the `hashchange` listener)"

Treat that as a starting point rather than as dictated text: re-read the surrounding sentence and make it read well.

## Explicitly NOT part of this

`docs/core/subscriptions.md:234-237` needed NO change. #10168's finding 1 made its existing sentence TRUE rather than false — the cells dedup now actually saves a render on the propagation path the sentence describes. Do not "fix" it.

## Verification

Both targets are prose in markdown. Re-verify each quoted string at trunk before editing — #10168 has merged since these were written, and this repo's review waves have repeatedly found premises that moved.

Neither link gate validates prose or table text, so the substance here is hand-verified. `spec/Construction-Prompts.md` is on `check_doc_slugs.py`'s surface (root `spec/`) and `docs/core/how-to/boot-and-mount-an-app.md` is on it too (root `docs/`), but only for link targets and heading anchors — and if your edit changes no link and no anchor, a green from either gate is vacuous with respect to what you changed. Say so rather than citing it as coverage.

Neither file is a hot-zone file.

title: story: xray-preset :panel arm dispatches :rf.xray/select-panel, which Xray no longer registers (select-tab) — silent no-op
description:

CLAIM (tools/story/spec/001-Authoring.md §Xray preset slot, lines ~601-604 and ~626): a story/variant `:xray {:panel <panel-kw>}` preset auto-selects that Xray panel on mount by dispatching `:rf.xray/select-panel`.

- tools/story/src/re_frame/story/xray_preset.cljc:395-402 — the preset's `:panel` arm does `(safe-call! ":rf.xray/select-panel" rf/dispatch [:rf.xray/select-panel panel] {:frame :rf/xray})`, and its docstring says "Xray's registry registers this event handler".
- tools/xray/src — `rg 'reg-event :rf.xray/select-panel'` reads 0. The only tab/panel selection handler Xray registers is `(rf/reg-event :rf.xray/select-tab …)` at tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/registry.cljs:918. tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/panels/cancellation_cascade_events.cljs:90-91 says in terms: "The legacy `:rf.xray/select-panel` slot is no longer read by the 4-layer shell (rf2-qy0nu)".

- Story's only test of the arm, tools/story/test/re_frame/story/xray_preset_cljs_test.cljs:548, asserts that the dispatch HAPPENED, not that a panel changed — which is how the drift stayed green.

notes:
## REVIEW REPORT — slice `adapters` (rf2-3x7nj.6), 2026-09-23 22:19:16 AUSEST

### Tree

Frozen review tree `C:/Users/miket/code/re-frame2-worktrees/review-sep23` at `034d0c8fc87a0331e8803ff3f82d6f3b15e9b914`. I confirmed the tree was clean after my probe: the only ignored entries are pre-existing `.cpcache` dirs, timestamped 21:48 and 21:56, before this review ran any probe.

### Method

- I read every adapter source file against the Spec 006 substrate contract, with particular weight on render and unmount cleanup, Reaction disposal (the stock exactly-once guard and slim's snapshot-and-clear), frame-provider and `contextType` propagation, the slim scheduler and commit boundary, the slim static-markup serializer, and the smoke-manifest gate.

### Findings

| bead | P | title |
|---|---|---|
| rf2-3x7nj.6.1 | P1 | reagent-slim `render-to-static-markup` emits attacker-controlled attribute/tag names raw and misses `oncommand` (the XSS vectors `re-frame.ssr` closed) |
| rf2-3x7nj.6.2 | P2 | reagent-slim `render-to-static-markup` entity-escapes `<style>`/`<script>` bodies (corrupts inline CSS/JS) and drops pre/textarea leading-LF compensation |
| rf2-3x7nj.6.3 | P3 | ratom-family class render subscribes during render; a pass React discards (Suspense or error boundary on mount) leaks its Reaction, pins the sub and forceUpdates a never-mounted instance on every change. Decision (a/b/c) on the bead. |

rf2-3x7nj.6.1 and .6.2 share one fence (`reagent2/dom/server.cljs`), so sequence them.

Not refiled, because they are already open: rf2-3x7nj.2.2 (UIx `destroy-adapter!` with a mounted spine `use-sub`) and rf2-3x7nj.3.1 (render-owned claims retain disposed reactions on a live owner).

### Considered and rejected

1. **Stock Reagent exactly-once dispose guard.** It is correct. Stock `dispose!` captures `on-dispose-arr` before iterating, so the marker-first callback works. It is pinned in both orders plus the shutdown interleave by `adapter_reaction_dispose_exactly_once_cljs_test`.
2. **A guarded Reaction re-deref'd after disposal cannot be explicitly re-disposed.** Stock auto-dispose on last-watch removal still cleans it, so there is no persistent leak.
3. **The ratom hydrate path ignores render opts (no `onRecoverableError`).** This is by design: the hiccup tier verifies via the render-tree hash (Spec 011). The UIx `render!` line "no UIx-only keys" is slightly overstated, which is not worth a bead.
4. **reagent2 `_try-capture`/`_run` check mode.** The state clobber was fixed (rf2-ee38b.15), and an error state recovers on the next source change, the same as stock.
5. **Slim `activate!` re-runs a Reaction whose body reads nothing.** This is perf-only and negligible.
6. **Slim `flush-render!` does a single component pass.** Render-induced cascades land on the next microtask. This is documented in the docstring and matches stock `r/flush`.
7. **Slim `:f>` bodies are not reactive and have no current-component.** Deliberate (IMPL-SPEC §4.7 and §7.1).
8. **Form-2 reg-views bypass the frame-aware wrapper after the first render.** The core-reactive reviewer already rejected this as tooling-only, and it is identical to stock.
9. **`reagent2.impl.template/*source-coord*` is never bound by production code**, although its docstring says `reg-view*` binds it. This is dead mechanism plus comment drift. Coordinates come from the views-layer walk, so no user is misled.
10. **The compile-time `:reagent2/form` tag lands on the user fn, not on the wrapper slim classifies.** The hot-path fold never fires. This is perf-only, and the runtime classification is correct.
11. **Static markup does not model React's form special forms** (`:default-value`, `:default-checked`, textarea/select `:value`). `re-frame.ssr` does not model them either, so this is minutiae.
12. **Static markup emits a `:children` prop as an attribute.** Cosmetic. It was fixed in SSR as rf2-dgyi.
13. **A test-react update-render failure logs `:forced-teardown`, not `:will-unmount`.** This is the deliberate observation contract per its docstring.
14. **Test-react re-renders re-mount children without reconciliation.** The test owns the clock and the body.
15. **Test-react and plain-atom derived values are not `IWatchable`.** That follows from the headless recompute-on-read design, which is core scope.
16. **UIx `flush-views!` with `f` and no `act()` skips `f`.** This is a documented test-only no-op, in spine scope.
17. **The smoke manifest covers reagent and uix only.** The slim smoke is a separate `smoke.cjs` runner by design, and the reconcile guard is sound.
18. **The publication transform.** Its fail-loud invariants and post-conditions are sound, it rewrites only the ns form, and the adapter has no self-reference to the `-slim` ns.
19. **A ratom sub auto-disposes before the owner's release.** Known and ruled (rf2-ty246, Spec 006 §Which lifetime governs a ratom adapter).
20. **The RAtom validator uses `assert`, so it is elided in prod.** Stock parity.
21. **Prop-name and tag caches grow with distinct dynamic keys.** Stock parity. It is pathological only for data-driven keys.

### Could not verify

- Every slim and Reagent behaviour above is inspected rather than executed, because the code is CLJS-only and shadow-cljs and browsers are out of bounds.
- For findings 1 and 2, the slim side is a short context-free trace. The reference side was executed on the JVM:
  - `re-frame.ssr` strips `:oncommand`.
  - It throws `:rf.error/ssr-invalid-attribute-name` on the hostile key.
  - It emits `<style>` text verbatim.
- For finding 3, React's discard of uncommitted class instances is reasoned from React's documented contract and source, not measured. Its regression test has to be a real Suspense or error-boundary DOM test in the browser lane.

No tracked file was edited and no git write was made.

title: False delivered-reply claim: Xray links a silenced HTTP failure to a later reused-ID reply
description:
Merged-PR audit of #10276 (a24d7b2321417752f91ad26a8a4213e1b9cbbe49; merged 2026-09-23T06:07:03Z), discovered from closed rf2-6ooch. The new HTTP record claims its reply link identifies the delivery of that particular completion, and that undelivered outcomes have no link. This claim is false for ordinary supported reply silencing plus sequential request-id reuse.

Reproduction, using the real managed HTTP effect and JVM java.net.http transport, with trace.projection/group-by-event and the shipped Xray http-join-context/event-bundle->managed-fx-records:
1. Issue a named request with :request-id :audit/reused, :on-success [:audit/done :first], :on-failure nil. Server responds 500. Its canonical :rf.http/replied row exists but no reply event is delivered (Spec 014 Reply addressing / Silenced expressly permits this).
2. After completion, issue another request under :audit/reused and respond 200; deliver [:audit/done :second ...]. The runtime legitimately reuses the full work-id [:rf.work/http :audit/reused 1 1] after eviction.
3. Both projected records now carry exactly the successor's reply-link. Measured links were [{:dispatch-id 7 :frame :rf/default} {:dispatch-id 7 :frame :rf/default}], while actual deliveries contained only [:audit/done :second]. The earlier ERROR record advertises a reply it never delivered and its button focuses unrelated later work.

Cause: managed_fx_helpers.cljc:802-811 reply-link-for searches the first delivery with matching frame/full work-id and trace id greater than the terminal row, with no completion-specific boundary. joined-fields:891-896 assumes every non-stale status was delivered; :on-failure nil and :reply-to nil are counterexamples. Both a silenced reply and a later delivered reply can share the same work-id.

Required correction: associate reply links with the particular completion they actually delivered, rather than an unbounded later delivery under a reusable work-id. Leave the link absent when that completion has no observed delivery; preserve separate links when both requests really deliver. Keep the existing programmer-facing API and runtime request-id reuse semantics. Add a producer-derived regression, not a hand-built trace-only fixture. Consider the fully silenced :reply-to nil spelling under the same correction.

Independent evidence: guarded audit-sep23-monitor worktree, ai/probe-http-reply-link-audit-sep23-monitor.clj and ai/gate-http-reply-link-audit-sep23-monitor-1.log/.exit. Two tests / 16 assertions: 1 failure, 0 errors, exit 1, exactly the silenced predecessor link. The positive control delivers both replies and correctly produces distinct links (dispatch 2 and 4). Existing managed-fx-helper and reply-envelope JVM suites passed 52 tests / 466 assertions, exit 0 (gate-xray-http-helpers-audit-sep23-monitor-1). No source code changed. No inference about mayor notification or acknowledgement.

The delivered/delivered control still yields two distinct correct links. ## Correctness review report: ssr-ring (rf2-3x7nj.14), 2026-09-23 22:51 AUSEST

### Tree
Frozen review tree C:/Users/miket/code/re-frame2-worktrees/review-sep23 at 034d0c8fc87a0331e8803ff3f82d6f3b15e9b914. All path:line cites are against it.

### Scope read
Primary source, all read IN FULL (3,831 lines):
- implementation/ssr-ring/src/re_frame/ssr/ring.clj (379)
- .../ring/lifecycle.clj (492), pipeline.clj (809), streaming.clj (841), node.clj (485)
- .../ring/headers.clj (139), cookie.clj (195), payload.clj (93), shell.clj (170), trust.clj (103)
- implementation/ssr-ring/deps.edn (125)

Supporting evidence, read in part: ring_test.clj (trusted-shell nil case 1780-1840, default-head title 2030-2080, route-head 925-1010), test_support.clj (reset fixture, thread detector), concurrency_stress_test.clj (harness + echo isolation), streaming_robustness_test.clj and ring_draintime_error_view_test.clj (test rosters). Spec 011: Server flow, Request storage substrate, HTTP response contract (fx guards, CRLF, redirect precedence, cookie shape, status defaults, materialiser backstop), Trusted shell hook contract, Head/meta (default flow, default head), Server error projection (sanitisation, drain-time classification, substrate, view-time exceptions, on-error vs error-view), Streaming SSR (failure semantics, pre-commit rule, chunk order, html-shell/renderer refusal, fn-form invocation count, writer concurrency, payload liveness), Per-request frame teardown. Spec 016 SSR and hydration. Core consumers traced at source: ssr/error_listener.cljc (apply-error-projection!, project-render-exception!, flush-response-result!, pending-error-trace?, the non-projection set), ssr/request.cljc (slots + on-frame-destroyed!), ssr.cljc drain-blocking-resources!, ssr/head/registry.cljc (default-head, head-model), ssr/streaming.cljc project-delta, ssr/html_helpers.cljc (escape-attr, attr-string), resources/ssr.cljc (blocking drain), ssr/response.cljc redirect-fx. ring-core 1.12.1 and 1.15.3 sources (ring.middleware.head, ring.middleware.not-modified) from the local Maven repo.

### Method
Read every production namespace top to bottom, tracing each public entry (ssr-handler, ssr-middleware, stream-handler, node/renderer, cookie->set-cookie-header, default-html-shell, the streaming prefix/suffix) through setup, drain-time classification, render seam, head, payload, shell, materialisation and teardown, against Spec 011. Checked every exit path of both handlers for frame teardown and request-slot clearing; checked per-request isolation (gensym ids, frame-address-keyed side channels, explicit with-frame on the writer thread, explicit-frame payload projection). Confirmed suspected defects with four bounded process-local JVM probes: classpath computed once with `clojure -Spath -M:test`, then `java -Dre-frame.debug=false -cp <cp> clojure.main <probe>.clj` from implementation/ssr-ring, scripts and logs in the reviewer scratch dir (probe1..4 .clj/.log/.exit), each exit 0. Probe 3's first attempt exited 1 before exercising anything (harness called register-listener! with :errors, which is not a stream); the listener was removed and the rerun is the evidence. Tracker duplicate search: `bd search` title queries, plus a full-field search (title/description/notes/close_reason) over a stdout `bd export` redirected to scratch, with controls (PipedInputStream 2 hits, default-head 4 hits, attr-string 12 hits).

### Findings

| Bead | P | Title |
|---|---|---|
| rf2-3x7nj.14.1 | P2 | stream-handler leaks its writer thread, request frame and side-channel slots for ever when middleware drops the body unread (Ring wrap-head / HEAD) on a page over 16 KiB |
| rf2-3x7nj.14.2 | P3 | stream-handler renders the document prefix on the writer thread after commit, so a head-model attr the shell rejects ships a blank 200 where ssr-handler answers the projected 500 |
| rf2-3x7nj.14.3 | P3 | explicit nil :script-src / :app-element-id (spec: 'use the default') drops the bootstrap script and renders `<div id="">`; :html-shell nil 500s every request |
| rf2-3x7nj.14.4 | P3 | pages whose route declares no :head ship `<title>ssr-ring per-request frame</title>` (hard-coded frame :doc feeds default-head) |

All four EXECUTED with controls both ways (see each bead's Evidence). Decisions needed: 14.1 (stall bound vs documented rule), 14.3 (explicit opt-out spelling for the bootstrap script), 14.4 (no default title vs caller opt).

### Considered and rejected (so nobody re-litigates)
- Setup short-circuit returns without destroying the frame (ring.clj:302-303, streaming.clj:763-764): correct. make-frame owns the failed incarnation's exact-token rollback; a bare-id reap is the rf2-c6lp3 hazard; the catch clears the request slot (pipeline.clj:349).
- Post-render projected 5xx is checked before a redirect (pipeline.clj:691): harmless, the materialiser takes its :redirect arm first (pipeline.clj:202), so redirect precedence still holds.
- The projected-error arm keeps the app's Content-Type: per Spec 011 Status defaults ("unless user code has set a different one").
- drain-blocking-resources! result, including :route-blocking-failure, is discarded (pipeline.clj:620, streaming.clj:185): the timed-out entries themselves settle to a structured :error with :reason :ssr-blocking-timeout, which is what a renderer reads; nothing consumes the record. Not worth a bead.
- A custom :error-view renders with :doctype? false and no shell (pipeline.clj:495-497), so a custom error page ships without `<!DOCTYPE html>` (quirks mode) and the comment "the error body is the inner shell body" is wrong. A one-line fix (:doctype? true is harmless for a fragment), but cosmetic, so below the bar. Noted for anyone passing.
- :ssr-blocking-timeout-ms works through opts passthrough but is not in the handler docstring: a docs gap, not a defect.
- Cookie :value URL-encoding (`=` becomes %3D): documented, and Ring's wrap-cookies decodes it.
- Streaming re-resolves a fn :root-view on the writer thread when continuations exist: this is the Spec 011 fn-form invocation-count contract.
- A continuation that blocks, or a slow-loris client: the spec gives the in-flight ceiling to the host server (rf2-fzbj.24 left it unverified). 14.1 is different because there the HTTP request has already completed, so the host knob cannot bound it.
- Redirect status fallback `(or redirect-status status)` (pipeline.clj:214): redirect-fx always defaults :status to 302.
- Node renderer: the rf2-fzbj.24 body-deadline repair is present (sendAsync + bounded get + cancel), the classification order (connect-timeout, then HttpTimeout, then IO) is right, interruption restores the flag, and build-skew equality includes an absent header. No defect.
- pr-str of the payload honours `*print-length*`: only if a host alters its root binding. Trust the programmer.
- The error-view pending-trace heuristic (pipeline.clj:502) could misfire if an async reply errors on the frame mid-error-render: speculative, and the async side is core-owned.
- The post-shell redirect comment (streaming.clj:801-808) says it cannot happen in v1, but a blocking-resource reply could set one. The code handles it, so this is comment drift only.
- HEAD is not matched by ssr-middleware's default :match? (GET only): configurable, and the request falls through.
- Per-request isolation (the P1 axis): no leak between concurrent requests found. Frame ids are gensym-unique; request/response/pending slots are keyed by frame address and cleared by the destroy hook; every handler exit path destroys the frame (by VALUE); the writer thread pins with-frame at each step; payload and delta projection take the explicit frame id.

### Could not verify
- No real Node sidecar crossing was run (needs Node). The node.clj review is by inspection plus the existing rf2-fzbj.24 regression.
- Jetty/http-kit/Aleph handling of HEAD with no middleware was not measured. Ring's servlet copies an InputStream body inside with-open, so Jetty closes it (inspected).
- Compojure's HEAD body-drop is not measured (no jar in the local repo).
- The client-side consequence of `id=""` or a missing bootstrap script (14.3) is inferred from the hydrator contract, not executed in a browser.
- No full test suites or CLJS/shadow-cljs lanes were run; only the four bounded probes.

### Hygiene
No edits to tracked files and no git writes. The probe classpath computation created implementation/ssr-ring/.cpcache/ (gitignored) in the frozen tree even though CLJ_CACHE pointed at scratch. I removed it after the probes; the frozen tree's ssr-ring directory is back to deps.edn/src/test only, and git status is clean. Other artefacts' .cpcache dirs in that tree are not mine and were left alone.

- rf2-3x7nj.14.1 (P2): stream-handler leaks its writer thread, the request frame and its side-channel slots permanently when middleware drops the body without reading it (Ring wrap-head on a HEAD request) and the page is larger than 16 KiB. title: core-frames: JVM same-id re-make-frame hides the live frame from other threads; a drain in the window strands its async queue for good (:scheduled? stuck true)
description:
## Defect

On the JVM, a same-id `rf/make-frame` against a LIVE frame (the surgical update / hot-reload path) stages the existing record as a `:provisional` revision, and the registry visibility predicate hides every provisional row from any actor other than the construction owner on the owning thread. So for the duration of the re-registration (trace-policy publication, the `:rf.frame/re-registered` emit, the registration hook), the live frame does not exist for every other thread: `(rf/frame id)` answers nil, a dispatch from another thread is silently dropped, and — the worse half — an async drain already scheduled for that frame that runs in the window finds `frame-incarnation-live?` false, drops `:drain-lock` but leaves the router's `:scheduled?` flag true. `ensure-drain-scheduled!` only arms a drain when it flips `:scheduled?` from false to true, so from then on every async dispatch to that frame is enqueued and never drained: the frame's async queue is stranded permanently (until something happens to call `dispatch-sync` on it, or the frame is destroyed). This contradicts spec 002's surgical-update promise that the router queue and in-flight events are preserved across re-registration.

JVM-only: on CLJS the host-holder is constant and the construction is synchronous, so no foreign actor can run inside the window.

## Where

All cites at `034d0c8fc8` (frozen tree `re-frame2-worktrees/review-sep23`).

- `implementation/core/src/re_frame/frame.cljc:3508-3531` — re-registration swaps the live record to `:construction (provisional-construction owner policy-token)`, preserving `:drain-lock`, app-db and queue.
- `implementation/core/src/re_frame/frame.cljc:3539-3556` — the provisional window: `publish-trace-policy!`, `rf.trace/emit! :rf.frame/re-registered`, `fire-frame-registered-hook!`, then `finalize-frame-construction!`.
- `implementation/core/src/re_frame/frame.cljc:1366-1379` — `frame-record-visible-to-current-actor?`: a provisional row is visible only when `*frame-transaction-owner*` is the record's owner AND `owner-holds-frame-id?`, which compares the owner's `:holder` against `(Thread/currentThread)` (`frame.cljc:259-268`). No distinction between a first construction and a re-registration of a live frame.
- `implementation/core/src/re_frame/frame.cljc:1381-1398` (`frame`), `1400-1419` (`frame-incarnation-token` = `(some-> (frame id) :drain-lock)`), `1421-1431` (`frame-incarnation-live?`) — all visibility-gated, so the live incarnation reads as dead to a foreign thread.
- `implementation/core/src/re_frame/router.cljc:4068-4101` — `ensure-drain-scheduled!` fences the enqueue on `frame-incarnation-live?` (foreign dispatch in the window: not enqueued) and schedules `drain-try!` only when it flips `:scheduled?`.
- `implementation/core/src/re_frame/router.cljc:3959-3969` — `drain-try!` not-live branch: `(reset! drain-lock false)` with `:scheduled?` left true (the branch was written for an obsolete incarnation, where that is harmless).
- Public entry points: `rf/make-frame` with an already-registered `:id` on one thread; `rf/dispatch` / any async drain (`next-tick` executor thread, `:dispatch-later` timer thread) on another.

## Failure scenario

1. A JVM process (REPL session, JVM-hosted app, server) has a live frame `:app` receiving async `rf/dispatch` traffic; the drain runs on the single-thread `next-tick` executor.
2. `(rf/make-frame {:id :app ...})` is re-evaluated (hot reload / REPL re-eval of the frame's form) on the REPL thread.
3. While the revision is provisional: (a) any `rf/dispatch [...] {:frame :app}` issued from another thread returns normally and the event is gone — no exception, nothing on stderr; (b) if a `drain-try!` for `:app` runs in the window, it releases the lock and leaves `:scheduled? true` with the queue non-empty.
4. After the re-registration finalizes, every further `rf/dispatch` to `:app` enqueues (queue grows) and nothing ever drains it. app-db stops moving. The window is short (policy publish + trace emit + registration hook), but any registration hook or synchronous trace listener widens it, and the consequence of hitting it once is permanent rather than transient.

## Evidence

EXECUTED — a bounded JVM probe from a scratch project (`deps.edn` with `day8/re-frame2 {:local/root "<frozen tree>/implementation/core"}`, so `.cpcache` landed in scratch; frozen tree `git status --porcelain` read 0 lines afterwards). It uses the frame ns's own `*upsert-policy-probe*` test seam to act inside the provisional window. Output, verbatim:

```
P1 control: foreign-thread lookup BEFORE re-registration -> true
P1 during re-registration -> {:owner-thread-sees? true, :foreign-thread-sees? false, :foreign-dispatch-result :returned}
P1 app-db after the foreign dispatch issued in the window -> {}
P2 after dispatch, before re-registration -> {:scheduled? true, :queue-count 1} app-db {}
P2 after re-registration settled -> {:scheduled? true, :queue-count 1} app-db {}
P2 after a SECOND dispatch + 500ms -> {:scheduled? true, :queue-count 2} app-db {}
CONTROL (no re-registration) -> {:scheduled? false, :queue-count 0} app-db {:n 1}
```

P1: the same foreign-thread lookup reads true before the re-registration and false inside it; the owner thread sees the frame; a foreign `[:inc]` dispatch in the window returned normally and never reached app-db. P2: the `next-tick` executor was parked, `[:inc]` dispatched to `:app2` (queue 1, scheduled), the executor released inside the provisional window; after settle the queue is still 1 with `:scheduled? true`, and a second dispatch 500 ms later leaves queue 2, app-db untouched. The CONTROL runs the identical park/dispatch/release sequence without a re-registration and drains normally (`{:n 1}`, `:scheduled? false`).

Tests: `implementation/core/test/re_frame/frame_upsert_linearization_jvm_test.clj` and `frame_construction_transaction_jvm_test.clj` pin foreign invisibility and rollback for FIRST construction; neither exercises a foreign thread's view of a live frame during re-registration.

Tracker: a scan of all 2109 beads (live `bd list --all --json`) for re-registration + foreign/provisional/invisible, `:scheduled?` stuck/strand, and `drain-try!` + scheduled/not-live found nothing on point (control: the same scanner found 9 beads citing `rf2-1frc`).

## Smallest fix

Direction: a re-registration of a LIVE frame should not hide it from foreign actors — only a FIRST construction's provisional row needs owner-only visibility. E.g. mark the construction record with its kind and let `frame-record-visible-to-current-actor?` treat a re-registration's staged row as process-visible (foreign readers see either the prior or the staged config; runtime state is the same object either way). Belt-and-braces, independent of the spec choice: `drain-try!`'s not-live branch should not leave `:scheduled?` true for a record that is still the registry's raw row (clear it, or re-arm).

Fence: `implementation/core/src/re_frame/frame.cljc` (visibility predicate / `provisional-construction`); optionally `implementation/core/src/re_frame/router.cljc` (drain-try!, outside this review slice). HOT ZONE: `spec/002-Frames.md` §Construction transaction (line 626 states provisional-row owner-only visibility without carving out re-registration; lines 831-850 promise queue / in-flight events survive) — the two statements conflict for this case and one must be reworded.

## Gates

JVM lane: `implementation/core` (`clojure -M:test`), extending `frame_upsert_linearization_jvm_test.clj` with a foreign-thread lookup + dispatch + scheduled-drain case during a re-registration (the probe above is the test shape). No CLJS branch involved.

## Decision needed

Yes, one line: during a re-registration's provisional window, should a foreign thread see (a) the frame with its PRIOR config, (b) the frame with the STAGED config, or (c) nothing (today) with the router made tolerant of it? (a) or (b) are both fine for correctness; (c) loses events by design and needs the spec's "in-flight events preserved" softened.

== RULING (delegated by Mike; mayor-dispatched ruling agent, 2026-09-23 23:07:20 AUSEST) ==

RULING: Option (b). While a LIVE frame is being re-registered under the same id (a surgical update), every actor sees the frame with its STAGED config. That includes foreign JVM threads.
- Owner-only visibility of a :provisional row stays, but ONLY for a FIRST construction.
- Admission does not change: a same-id constructor or destroyer still loses at the per-id reservation.
- This needs an edit to spec/002-Frames.md (HOT ZONE) at ~:626 and ~:833.

WHY
- The dossier and the independent Codex review both recommend (b), and both reject (a) and (c) for the same reasons.
- Why (a) loses. (a) would show foreign threads the prior config.
  - It needs a two-version read path inside `frame`, which runs on every dispatch and subscribe. The table in frame.cljc's comment near :1338 counts about 125 calls to the visibility predicate per event.
  - That path would have to be reconciled with set-generation!, the legitimate generation-only writer, the same way restore-provisional-frame! (frame.cljc:3069-3099) already has to.
  - It would isolate only config reads; the runtime containers are shared anyway. With no demonstrated need, that is gold-plating.
- Why (c) loses. (c) would keep hiding the frame and make the router tolerate it.
  - C2 (a foreign dispatch is dropped) would stay lost BY DESIGN, so 002:831 and 002:850 ("router queue, in-flight events all remain") would have to be softened.
  - C1 would still need run-one-pass! to tell "provisional" apart from "destroyed". That moves the visibility exception into the hottest router path.
- 002:626's own rationale decides the question. Owner-only visibility exists so "unrelated callers cannot observe a live-looking half-construction", and a re-registering frame is not half-built.
  - The re-register swap (frame.cljc:3508-3531) assocs only :config, :generation, :trace-policy-token and :construction onto the LIVE record.
  - It keeps :drain-lock, the router, the frame-state container and the sub-cache by identity.
  - 002:856 already says the metadata swap "is visible to subsequent dispatches" by the time :rf.frame/re-registered fires.
- Codex's framing is adopted: these are destruction mechanisms getting the wrong answer from frame visibility. A stable incarnation briefly fails its own liveness check.

THE DEFECT, VERIFIED AT TRUNK 5d74c334bb (frame.cljc and router.cljc are unchanged since 4b627ee9e2)
- The predicate, frame.cljc:1366-1379 frame-record-visible-to-current-actor?:
  - A :provisional row is visible only when *frame-transaction-owner* is the row's owner AND owner-holds-frame-id? holds, meaning the owner's :holder is identical to (Thread/currentThread) (:260-269).
  - It makes no distinction between first construction and re-registration.

title: ssr-ring: stream-handler renders the document prefix on the writer thread after commit, so a head-model attr the shell rejects ships a blank 200 where ssr-handler answers the projected 500
description:
## Defect

`stream-handler` renders the shell BODY on the request thread (so its failures fail closed pre-commit), but it renders the document PREFIX — `<html>`/`<body>` attribute bags from the head model, `<head>` with the head fragment, the app-root `<div>` — on the detached writer thread, AFTER the response head (status 200) has been selected and returned. The prefix can throw on content: the shared `attr-string` serialiser rejects an attribute name outside the HTML5 grammar with `:rf.error/ssr-invalid-attribute-name` (the rf2-vl8ir XSS gate), and `html-attr-bag` throws on a non-map bag (inspected, not probed). When it does, the writer truncates-and-closes and the client receives a 200 with an EMPTY body. The non-streaming `ssr-handler` renders the same prefix inside its render try and answers the projected 500 error page. This breaks the streaming pre-commit rule (Spec 011: a shell-render failure must fail closed to the non-streamed projected-error arm, "no partial-state shell") and the handler's own docstring claim that the writer's failure surface is "never the shell, whose status was fixed on the request thread".

## Where

- `implementation/ssr-ring/src/re_frame/ssr/ring/streaming.clj:312-314` — `default-streaming-prefix` rendered on the writer thread (phase `:shell-prefix`).
- `implementation/ssr-ring/src/re_frame/ssr/ring/streaming.clj:182-208` — `render-streaming-shell!` (request thread) resolves the head bag and renders `shell-html` but not the prefix string.
- `implementation/ssr-ring/src/re_frame/ssr/ring/shell.clj:152-186` — `document-prefix` calls `attr-string` on `:html-attrs` / `:body-attrs`.
- `implementation/ssr-ring/src/re_frame/ssr/ring/streaming.clj:696-699` (docstring claim) and `spec/011-SSR.md:1737` (pre-commit rule).
- Public entry: `re-frame.ssr.ring/stream-handler` with a route whose registered `reg-head` returns an `:html-attrs` / `:body-attrs` key such as `:data-user.id`.

## Failure scenario

`(rf/reg-head :probe/head (fn [_ _] {:title "T" :html-attrs {:data-user.id "42"}}))` on the active route. `ssr-handler` -> status 500, projected "Something went wrong" error page. `stream-handler` -> status 200, body 0 bytes (headers only), no error page; only the post-commit `:rf.error/ssr-streaming-writer-failed` record says anything went wrong.

## Evidence

EXECUTED — bounded JVM probe (`probe3_prefix_throw.clj`, reviewer scratch dir), real handlers, `-Dre-frame.debug=false`, frozen tree `034d0c8fc8`:

- CONTROL (valid key `:data-user-id`): ssr 200 with `data-user-id="42"`; stream 200, 476 bytes, with `data-user-id="42"`.
- CASE (invalid key `:data-user.id`): ssr status 500, body begins `<!DOCTYPE html><html><head><meta charset="utf-8"><title>Something went wrong</title>`; stream status 200, body-bytes 0; zero live writer threads afterwards (cleanup itself is fine).

Tracker search (all fields) for default-streaming-prefix / shell-prefix: 0 hits.

## Smallest fix

Compute the prefix string on the request thread: move `(default-streaming-prefix head-html shell-opts)` into `render-streaming-shell!` (inside `render-shell-or-projected-error`'s try, so a throw takes the existing projected-error arm) and hand the finished string to the writer, which then only writes it. Fence: `implementation/ssr-ring/src/re_frame/ssr/ring/streaming.clj` plus a regression in `streaming_robustness_test.clj` or `ring_streaming_test.clj`. No hot-zone file.

## Gates

JVM: `clojure -M:test` from `implementation/ssr-ring`. No CLJS lane involved.

## Decision needed

No.

title: xray-data-layer: spine/registry frame re-seeds write the RAW epoch ring into :epoch-history, bypassing epoch/redact-history - sensitive records reach every epoch-history panel after a frame-picker change or cross-frame click
description:
## Defect

Xray's privacy gate on `:epoch-history` is `epoch/redact-history`. Under the default `:rf.egress/local-redacted` profile it drops every epoch record whose `:rf.epoch/sensitive?` rollup is true, or that carries a suppressed trace event. Spec 013 calls it the one ingress gate for that slot, and `epoch.cljs` calls it "the one seam every `:epoch-history` write passes through". That is not true. Five spine and registry handlers re-seed the slot straight from the framework's RAW epoch ring (`(vec (rf/epoch-history frame))`) and never call `redact-history`:

- `:rf.xray/set-frame` (the frame picker);
- `:rf.xray/focus-event` (an L2 row click);
- `:rf.xray/focus-event-prev` and `-next` (`j`/`k` and the ribbon chevrons);
- `:rf.xray/focus-epoch` (the parent-epoch chip);
- `:rf.xray/select-dispatch-id`.

After any of these gestures, sensitive records sit in `:epoch-history` with their raw `:trigger-event`, `:trace-events`, `:sub-runs`, `:renders` and `:db-*`. Every panel that reads the slot can then render them. The leak lasts until the next `:rf.xray/epoch-recorded` for that frame rewrites the slot through the gate.

This is the same undercount rf2-y8doi.13 recorded in its own close reason. It found three writers where the bead named two, and gated them in `epoch.cljs`. The re-seed writers in `spine.cljs` and `registry.cljs` were never counted.

## Where

At `034d0c8fc8`:

- Gated writers, for contrast: `tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/epoch.cljs:201`, `:268`, `:271`, `:317`. `redact-history` is at `:75-124`.
- Ungated reducers:
  - `tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/spine.cljs:916-923` (`set-frame-reducer`, `:epoch-history (vec epoch-history-for-frame)`);
  - `spine.cljs:992-1008` (`reseed-epoch-history-for-frame`, the same bare `vec` at `:1008`).
- Handlers that feed those reducers the raw ring:
  - `spine.cljs:1181` (`:rf.xray/focus-event`);
  - `spine.cljs:1200` and `:1210` (`focus-event-prev` / `-next`);
  - `spine.cljs:1235` (`:rf.xray/focus-epoch`);
  - `spine.cljs:1293` (`:rf.xray/set-frame`);
  - `tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/registry.cljs:858-861` (`:rf.xray/select-dispatch-id`).
- `spine.cljs:1329-1331` (`:rf.xray/preview-event`) also resolves the previewed epoch-id against the raw ring. It writes only an id, but it should use the gated history too.
- Public entry points:
  - `frame_switcher.cljs:626` (`:rf.xray/select-frame` dispatches `:rf.xray/set-frame`, including for the frame already selected);
  - `shell.cljs:1838` (row click);
  - `keybinding.cljs:308` and `:312` (`j`/`k`);
  - `panels/epoch/view.cljs:2261` (parent-epoch chip);
  - `focus.cljc:216` and `palette/events.cljs:385` / `:399` (embedding and palette focus).
- Contract: `tools/xray/spec/013-Trace-Consumer.md:239-270`, §One policy, three ingress paths. Its text: "The epoch path — `epoch/redact-history` gates every framework epoch record on its way into Xray's `:epoch-history` slot". Also `013:201-209`, which says the Trace panel's printed rows are gated only by that epoch path.

## Failure scenario

1. The host frame `:app` registers `:auth/login` with its args classified `:sensitive` and dispatches `[:auth/login {:password "hunter2"}]`. The raw ring keeps replay material, so the record carries `:rf.epoch/sensitive? true`, the raw `:trigger-event`, and `:trace-events` all stamped `:sensitive? true`. Under the default profile, `:rf.xray/epoch-recorded` writes the slot through `redact-history`, so the record is absent. Correct so far.
2. The operator picks `:app` in the ribbon's frame picker. This fires `:rf.xray/select-frame` then `:rf.xray/set-frame`, and `set-frame-reducer` writes `(vec (rf/epoch-history :app))`. The login record is now in `:epoch-history`. A cross-frame L2 click, a `j`/`k` step onto another frame's row, or `select-dispatch-id` does the same through `reseed-epoch-history-for-frame` whenever the frame differs from `:target-frame`.
3. Any `:epoch-history` reader now sees the record. For example, a child event the login handler dispatched offers its parent-epoch chip, whose `:rf.xray/focus-epoch` now resolves. The Epoch panel then renders the login cascade, and the Trace panel prints its `:sensitive? true` events as rows. No per-event `suppress-sensitive?` check exists downstream of this slot: across `tools/xray/src`, the only callers are `epoch.cljs` and `trace_collector.cljs`.
4. The same happens with no sensitive event at all, once a handler returns `:sensitive [[:auth :token]]` with a non-nil token. The rollup is then true for every later record of that frame, and `redact-history` drops them all "by the intended price". After step 2 they are all back, with ordinary visible L2 rows that the operator can click.

## Evidence

Inspected only. `spine.cljs` and `epoch.cljs` are CLJS, so no JVM probe is possible.

- I read every `:epoch-history` writer in `tools/xray/src`: all `assoc`/`update` sites on that key, found by searching for `:epoch-history`. Only the four `epoch.cljs` sites call `redact-history`: `:rf.xray/set-target-frame`, the two arms of `:rf.xray/epoch-recorded`, and `:rf.xray/sync-epoch-history`. The other writers are the two spine reducers above and the test-only `:rf.xray/set-epoch-history-for-test` (`panels/machine_inspector.cljs:1583-1587`).
- Controls:
  - The same file set shows `redact-history` at 4 call sites in `epoch.cljs`, so the search does find the gate where it exists.
  - `tools/xray/test/day8/re_frame2_xray/sensitive_trace_cljs_test.cljc` is the only test naming `redact-history` or `:rf.epoch/sensitive`. It contains no `set-frame`, `focus-event` or `reseed`, so nothing pins the re-seed paths.
- Framework semantics: the rollup is `sensitive-rollup` in `implementation/epoch/src/re_frame/epoch/assembly.cljc:160-180` (a sensitive event OR a non-nil declared-sensitive leaf). `re-frame.epoch/replay-epoch!` documents that the ring keeps the raw argument-bearing `:trigger-event`.
- Tracker: rf2-y8doi.13's close reason records the writer undercount and lists the three gated files. No open or closed bead mentions `reseed-epoch-history` or `set-frame-reducer` with redaction.

## Smallest fix

Route every `:epoch-history` write through the gate:

- Have `set-frame-reducer` and `reseed-epoch-history-for-frame` store `(epoch/redact-history epoch-history-for-frame)` rather than the bare `vec`. `spine` can require `day8.re-frame2-xray.epoch` with no cycle.
- Or wrap each handler's `(rf/epoch-history f)`, including `registry.cljs:861` and the `preview-event` read.

Add one node-lane test: a sensitive record in the framework ring stays out of `:epoch-history` after `:rf.xray/set-frame` and after a cross-frame `:rf.xray/focus-event`.

Fence: `tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/spine.cljs`, `tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/registry.cljs`, and one test under `tools/xray/test/`. No hot-zone file.

## Gates

`npm run test:cljs`. `spine.cljs`, `registry.cljs` and `epoch.cljs` are CLJS-only, so no JVM artefact compiles them, and a JVM green says nothing about this change.

## Decision needed

No.

title: ssr: the hydration payload (and streaming deltas) carry JVM-only numbers (Long > 2^53, BigDecimal, BigInt, Ratio) that the browser reads back as different values - the manifest and render-state wires refuse exactly these, the payload wire does not
description:
## Defect

On a JVM host, the hydration payload carries JVM-only numbers onto the wire without complaint, and the browser reads them back as DIFFERENT values. This applies to both `:rf/app-db` and `:rf/runtime-db`, and to the per-boundary streaming deltas. The affected values are:

- a `Long` wider than 2^53, for example a 64-bit database or snowflake id
- a `BigDecimal`, which is `next.jdbc`'s default for NUMERIC/DECIMAL columns
- a `BigInt`
- a `Ratio`

Spec 011 states this failure for the root-manifest wire. There, `9007199254740993N` reads back as `9007199254740992` and `1/3` as `0.333…`, "it *succeeds*, with a different value", and "Rejecting rather than coercing is the rule". The same artefact enforces that crossing rule on TWO wires, the root manifest and the ssr-node render-state wire. The render-state wire carries the very same `{:rf/app-db … :rf/runtime-db …}` envelope, and its docstring says a JVM-only number "fails AT PROJECTION … never … discovered at the far end".

The hydration payload is the largest of the three wires and has no such check. Nothing in Spec 011 or Spec-Schemas (`[:rf/app-db :any]`) warns that the JVM's numeric types narrow silently on this wire, so a programmer has no reason to expect it.

## Where

Cites are at `034d0c8fc8`.

- `implementation/ssr/src/re_frame/ssr/payload_policy.cljc:715-789` `build-payload` assembles `:rf/app-db` and `:rf/runtime-db` with no domain check. Both SSR paths share it: `implementation/ssr-ring/src/re_frame/ssr/ring/payload.clj:26-93` for non-streaming, and `implementation/ssr/src/re_frame/ssr/streaming.cljc:728-841` `build-final-payload` for streaming.
- `implementation/ssr/src/re_frame/ssr/streaming.cljc:192-263` `subtree-delta`/`project-delta` do the same for the delta scripts.
- The wire is `pr-str`'d at `implementation/ssr-ring/src/re_frame/ssr/ring/streaming.clj:438` and via `shell.clj:39-169`, and read by `cljs.reader/read-string` at `implementation/ssr/src/re_frame/ssr/boot.cljc:88`.
- **Contrast.** `implementation/ssr/src/re_frame/ssr/manifest.cljc:239-332` has `wire-number?` and `edn-carryable?`, with the reader table at 255-265. `implementation/ssr/src/re_frame/ssr/render_state.cljc:70-81` has the docstring, and 272-279 applies `edn-carryable?` to every key and value. The spec text is `spec/011-SSR.md:546-567`.

## Failure scenario

On ssr-ring, a boot event loads `{:order/id 9007199254740993 :price 10.50M}` into an allowlisted app-db key. The payload ships `{:order/id 9007199254740993, :price 10.50M}`.

The browser's reader yields `{:order/id 9007199254740992 :price 10.5}`, a double. The client's `[:cancel-order id]` then targets a different order, or client-side money arithmetic runs on doubles.

The render-hash catches only the cases where the value is printed into the tree differently. An id carried only into an event, or a price the view formats identically, passes every check.

## Evidence

**Executed.** I ran a bounded JVM probe (`probe3.clj`) from `implementation/ssr` in the frozen tree, with output sent to scratch. `git status --porcelain` read 0 before and after.

- `(payload-policy/build-payload nil {:price 10.50M :order-id 9007199254740993 :share 1/3 :big 9007199254740993N} nil {})` returned the map unchanged. Its `pr-str` is `{:price 10.50M, :order-id 9007199254740993, :share 1/3, :big 9007199254740993N}`.
- **Control, same artefact.** `manifest/edn-carryable?` is `false` for each of those four values.
- **Control the other way.** It is `true` for the in-domain twins `10.5`, `9007199254740991`, `0.3333333333333333` and `"10.50"`.
- **The browser half is not executed here** (it needs the CLJS reader). It is the behaviour Spec 011:546-551 and the `manifest.cljc:255-265` table record as measured.

**Tracker.** A search of the export for `bigint|2^53` with `hydration payload|build-payload`, and for `edn-carryable|wire-number`, finds only rf2-8arzr.3 and rf2-8arzr.6. Those introduced the render-state wire's reuse of the domain and say nothing about the hydration payload.

## Smallest fix

In `build-payload` and `project-delta`, reject (throw, naming the partition and the key path) any number outside `manifest/wire-number?`, walking the projected slices.

Do NOT reuse `edn-carryable?` wholesale. `#inst` and `#uuid` read back fine through `cljs.reader` and are presumably carried in app-db today. Only the silently-narrowing numbers need refusing, and records already fail loudly at the reader.

The fence is `payload_policy.cljc`, `streaming.cljc`, tests, and one paragraph in Spec 011 §The hydration payload. No hot-zone file is involved. Spec-Schemas is hot-zone and only needs touching if the schema is narrowed.

## Gates

`cd implementation/ssr && clojure -M:test` (JVM; the code is `.cljc` with no `:cljs`-only branch). ssr-ring's payload tests (`cd implementation/ssr-ring && clojure -M:test`) exercise the shared builder.

## Decision needed

Should the hydration payload enforce the same numeric crossing rule as the manifest and render-state wires? The cost is a walk of the projected slices per request, possibly dev-only. The alternative is to rule the payload domain `:any` deliberate and say in Spec 011 that JVM-only numbers narrow silently on this wire.

== DOSSIER WRITTEN 2026-09-23 23:31:51 AUSEST (analysis only — no status change, no dispatch, no edit) ==

Dossier: ai/decisions/rf2-3x7nj.13.3.payload-numeric-crossing.md (ai/ is local-only and gitignored, so this path is a convenience that can rot; the decisive findings are restated below).
Read at trunk 950a0cba74 (= origin/main). git diff --stat 034d0c8fc8 HEAD over implementation/ssr/src, ssr-ring/src, fresco server.cljs, spec/011, spec/Spec-Schemas, spec/009 and docs/ssr is EMPTY, so every cite on this bead holds at trunk.

- WHAT: a #?(:clj ...) walk over the projected :rf/app-db and :rf/runtime-db in build-payload (payload_policy.cljc:715) and over each delta in project-delta (streaming.cljc:241). It reuses the manifest's own predicate, wire-number? (manifest.cljc:239, private today), VERBATIM and checks numbers only: NOT edn-carryable? wholesale, because #inst/#uuid read back fine through cljs.reader (boot.cljc:88).
- THE ERROR: one new catalogued error naming :partition, :path and the value's class. Always on.

   - The render-state wire refuses exactly these values at projection: render_state.cljc:70-81 says so and :268 check-wire-domain! enforces it. That wire carries the SAME {:rf/app-db :rf/runtime-db} envelope. Spec 011:546-567 states the rule ("it succeeds, with a different value"; "Rejecting rather than coercing is the rule").
   - The payload, by contrast, is Spec-Schemas.md:3932 [:rf/app-db :any].
   - docs/ssr/concepts.md:637-638 already claims the render-state policies "project the same EDN wire domain the hydration payload already uses". That is false today.
2. MEASURED AT TRUNK (bounded JVM probe from implementation/ssr).
   - build-payload returns {:price 10.50M, :order-id 9007199254740993, :share 1/3, :big 9007199254740993N} untouched. wire-number? is false on those four and on (float 0.1), and true on 9007199254740991 and 10.5.
   - Walk cost against the pr-str every request already pays (warmed, median of 31): 0.655 vs 3.130 ms for 2,559 leaves; 1.405 vs 16.192 ms for 25,509; 8.672 vs 86.320 ms for 255,009. That is 0.09 to 0.21 of pr-str.
   - The walk named the path [:orders 37 :lines 2 :unit-price] for a planted 3.25M.
3. CORRECTION TO THE BEAD. "No hot-zone file" holds only if an existing error id is reused, and none fits: malformed-hydration-payload is the client's parse failure, and ssr-render-state-invalid is the ssr-node wire. A new id needs a spec/009-Instrumentation.md row (hot-zone), because check_keyword_catalogue_drift.py CHECK A requires one. Spec-Schemas stays untouched.

Other points:
- Keep the walk JVM-only: on CLJS, including Fresco's Node door (fresco server.cljs:416), every number except NaN already crosses.
- What a throw does. Non-streaming: it goes through the pipeline's render-throw projection (pipeline.clj:799-809). Streaming: it lands in the writer catch (ssr-ring streaming.clj:442-466, :truncate-and-close).
Interactions: rf2-3x7nj.13.1 also touches streaming.cljc (walk-dom-tag), so sequence the two. Sequence the spec/009 row behind rf2-986kg and any other spec/009 holder.
Lanes: cd implementation/ssr && clojure -M:test, plus ssr-ring; the new forms sit in a #?(:clj) branch, so the JVM lanes grade them.
== RULING (delegated by Mike; mayor-dispatched ruling agent, 2026-09-24 00:19:58 AUSEST) ==

RULING: FAIL CLOSED, ALWAYS ON, JVM ONLY. `build-payload` (both partitions) and `project-delta` walk every number in the projected structure, map KEYS included. On the first number outside the portable subset they throw a new catalogued error, `:rf.error/ssr-hydration-payload-invalid`, naming the partition, the path and the class. The portable subset is the manifest's JVM crossing rule: no Ratio, BigDecimal, BigInt/BigInteger or Float; integers only within ±(2^53−1); every double admitted. It does NOT take the manifest's `##NaN` exclusion, so NaN rides. The new id needs a spec/009 row, which is HOT-ZONE, so the mayor must sequence it.

Verified at trunk f6bb999d6e (= origin/main after `git fetch origin main`, exit 0). The cited paths are unchanged since the review tree 034d0c8fc8: the diff over them is empty, and the unfiltered control reads 31 files.

--- WHY ---

1. The rule already exists; this makes one artefact say one thing.
   - spec/011-SSR.md:546-567 states the crossing for the manifest: "`9007199254740993N` prints, and the browser's reader reconstructs `9007199254740992` … it *succeeds*, with a different value". It also says: "Rejecting rather than coercing is the rule".
   - The ssr-node render-state wire enforces that rule at projection on the SAME {:rf/app-db :rf/runtime-db} envelope (render_state.cljc:70-81; `check-wire-domain!` about :268).
   - Today the same data gets two verdicts: it fails closed on one wire and narrows silently on the other.
   - docs/ssr/concepts.md:637-638 already claims the payload uses the same domain.
2. "Trust the programmer" trusts choices the programmer made and can see. Neither holds here:
   - next.jdbc picked the BigDecimal (JDBC NUMERIC/DECIMAL; Postgres `sum` over bigint and `avg` return numeric). That is stated from JDBC/Postgres behaviour, not measured here;
   - the EDN reader picked the double;
   - the server reads its own value back perfectly, same-host tests pass, and the render hash agrees whenever the view prints the value identically or carries it only into an event (an id in `[:order/cancel id]`).
   The failure is an order id that changes identity, or money that becomes a double.
3. Option B (debug-gated) LOSES. The failure is DATA-dependent, so a production build with `-Dre-frame.debug=false` (interop.clj:287-293) reopens it exactly where a wrong id costs money. Both reviewers rejected it.
4. Option C (document :any) LOSES. It leaves every next.jdbc user to learn from prose; it leaves three wires with two rules; and the docs currently promise the opposite.
5. Option D (coerce) is ruled out by 011:565. Option E (tagged decimals plus a client decimal type) is gold-plating.

Where the dossier and Codex AGREED: fail closed; always on; JVM only; numbers only, NOT `edn-carryable?` wholesale, because `#inst`/`#uuid` read back fine through `cljs.reader` and must keep riding; the walk covers both final-payload partitions and every streaming delta.

Where they DIFFERED, and what decided each point:
(a) NaN. The dossier said reuse `wire-number?` VERBATIM and accept NaN refusal "for one rule"; Codex said keep NaN riding. The deciding fact is what each wire's property IS:
    - the manifest's predicate is round-trip `=` (manifest.cljc:239 docstring: "NaN is not `=` to itself, so no NaN can satisfy a round-trip-EQUALITY test"; 011 says the same);
    - the payload's property is 011:52, "the client … computes the same view the server rendered";
    - NaN reads back as NaN. Codex executed the real ClojureScript 1.12.145 reader on bytes from the current JVM builder: `##NaN` came back NaN, and `##Inf`, `#inst` and `#uuid` were preserved.
    Refusing NaN would be a new framework refusal with no transport damage behind it. RULED: share the JVM type/range logic, not the NaN clause.
(b) "NaN is the only false positive". This was the dossier's claim; Codex refuted it. The predicate also refuses values whose mathematical value crosses intact: `10.50M`, `1/2`, `1N`, `(float 1.5)` and the integer `9007199254740992`. RULED: keep the conservative TYPE/RANGE rule anyway, and acknowledge the friction honestly. 011's own reason is TYPE, not value: a bigint arriving as a plain number "changes the value's type between server and client". In Clojure, `(= 10.50M 10.5)` is false, and `(str 10.50M)` is "10.50" on the server where the client prints "10.5", so value-preserved is not behaviour-preserved. A predictable portable subset beats a clever per-value exactness test. The author narrows deliberately: ids to strings, money to a string, a double or integer cents.
(c) Cost. The dossier measured the walk against the `pr-str` every request already pays (warmed, median of 31):
    - 2,559 leaves: 0.655 vs 3.130 ms;
    - 25,509 leaves: 1.405 vs 16.192 ms;
    - 255,009 leaves: 8.672 vs 86.320 ms.
    That is 0.09-0.21 of `pr-str`. Codex declined to treat that as a latency measurement. RULED: always on needs no benchmark to justify it. A dev-only check leaves the data-dependent failure unguarded, and the walk inspects only data that is leaving the server anyway. Build the path lazily (only on failure) if convenient.
(d) Codex's DUPLICATE-KEY finding. `{1 :integer, 1.0 :double}` passed the scalar predicate, but the CLJS reader rejects it as a duplicate key. That failure is LOUD at the far end (`:rf.error/malformed-hydration-payload`), so it is OUT OF SCOPE. Do not advertise a general "lossless payload" guarantee; this ruling is bounded to SILENT numeric narrowing.
(e) Streaming availability. Codex noted that a refusal on the streaming path cannot become a tidy error page. RULED: accepted and documented. On the streaming path the throw lands post-commit in the writer catch (ssr-ring streaming.clj:442-466): one always-on `:rf.error/ssr-streaming-writer-failed`, `:recovery :truncate-and-close`. On the non-streaming path it goes through the pipeline's render-throw projection (pipeline.clj `project-render-throw->ring-response`, :703, :809) to the projected error page. The final payload is built after the whole body has streamed, from a db that changed during streaming, so no pre-commit check is possible there. Pin both outcomes with one focused integration check each.

--- WHAT TO BUILD (trunk f6bb999d6e) ---

1. `implementation/ssr/src/re_frame/ssr/manifest.cljc`: factor the JVM arm of the private `wire-number?` (:239-292) into one shared predicate, e.g. `portable-number?`:
   - JVM: false for `ratio?`/`decimal?`/BigInt/BigInteger/Float; integers only within ±`max-safe-integer`; any double INCLUDING NaN and ±Inf;
   - CLJS: true.
   Then make `wire-number?` = `(and (portable-number? v) (not NaN))`. Manifest and render-state behaviour stay BYTE-IDENTICAL, and their existing suites are the control. Keep ONE copy of the rule; make `portable-number?` public, or expose a small public walker from manifest.cljc (the worker's choice). No wider public API.
2. `implementation/ssr/src/re_frame/ssr/payload_policy.cljc` `build-payload` (:715-789): a `#?(:clj …)` walk over the `db-slice` (partition `:rf/app-db`) and, when non-nil, the `runtime-db` slice (partition `:rf/runtime-db`), BEFORE assembly.
   - `build-payload` is shared verbatim by both SSR paths: ssr-ring payload.clj:26-74 (non-streaming) and streaming.cljc `build-final-payload` (about :728). So one site covers both final payloads.
   - Fresco's Node door (fresco server.cljs about :416, CLJS) passes through untouched. Every CLJS number already crosses, and NaN rides under this ruling.
3. `implementation/ssr/src/re_frame/ssr/streaming.cljc` `project-delta` (:241-263): the same walk over the projected delta (partition `:rf/app-db`) before it returns. It runs on the writer thread (ssr-ring streaming.clj about :380-391).
4. THE WALK: map KEYS as well as values, since an app-db keyed by entity id, `{9007199254740993 {…}}`, narrows silently too. Also sets, vectors, lists and seqs. Records are left to the reader, which fails LOUD.
5. THE ERROR, via `rf.error/throw-error!`:
   - id `:rf.error/ssr-hydration-payload-invalid`;
   - `:recovery :narrow-the-value-or-drop-the-key`, reusing render-state's keyword because it means the same thing;
   - `:extra {:partition … :path … :class …}`. The path runs from the partition root. For a map KEY or a set member, it names the containing collection, and a key carries `:half :key` (mirroring render-state).
   - THE MESSAGE MUST NAME the partition, the path and the class. On the streaming path only the message survives: the writer-failed record carries `:exception` (the message) and `:ex-class`, not ex-data.
6. `spec/009-Instrumentation.md` is HOT-ZONE and needs one row for the new id. `scripts/check_keyword_catalogue_drift.py` CHECK A requires a row for every emitted `:rf.error/*` literal. No existing id fits:
   - `:rf.error/malformed-hydration-payload` (009:1962) is the CLIENT's parse failure;
   - `:rf.error/ssr-render-state-invalid` (009:2386) is the ssr-node wire.
   SEQUENCE this row behind rf2-986kg (in progress; it amends two spec/009 rows) and any other spec/009 holder.
7. `spec/011-SSR.md`, §Payload scope (canonical boundary) or the hydration-payload text, gets one paragraph (011 is NOT hot-zone). It must say:
   - on a JVM host the payload obeys the manifest's numeric crossing rule, except `##NaN`, and why;
   - a violation fails closed with the new id, always on;
   - `#inst`/`#uuid` ride;

title: xray-epoch-panel: L2 Duration column is always blank — event-bundle-duration-ms reads [:handler :tags :duration-ms], which :rf.event/run-end never carries (it stamps :rf.event/elapsed-ms)
description:
## Defect

The L2 event list's Duration column is blank on every row. Spec 018's row anatomy lists it as `1.2 ms`, right-aligned.

`l2-timeline/event-bundle-duration-ms` reads `[:handler :tags :duration-ms]`. The bundle's `:handler` slot holds the `:rf.event/run-end` trace, and the producer never stamps `:duration-ms` on that trace. It stamps `:rf.event/elapsed-ms`. So the reader returns nil for every real event, and the cell renders empty. The column looks like a feature that is present but has nothing to measure.

`event-status-colour/event-bundle-outcome` reads the same absent key for its `:duration-ms` field, which is therefore always nil. No live renderer reads that field today; the trace status bar uses only `:outcome`. So it is latent rather than visible, but it has the same root cause and the same fix.

The Epoch panel's own HANDLER step already made this repair (rf2-slnce). It reads `:rf.event/elapsed-ms` and shows the right number. The two sibling readers were left on the retired key.

The tests stay green because their fixtures stamp the key the producer never emits:

- `l2_timeline_cljs_test.cljc:108-120` (`cascade-with-duration`)
- `shell_cljs_test.cljs:993-1003` (`run-end-trace-ev`)

## Where

Frozen tree `034d0c8fc8`:

- `tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/panels/l2_timeline.cljc`
  - `:128-137`: `event-bundle-duration-ms`.
  - `:154-159`: `event-bundle-duration-label`.
- `tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/panels/event/event_status_colour.cljc:260-274`: `event-bundle-outcome`, where `:duration-ms (get-in handler [:tags :duration-ms])`.
- Consumer: `tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/shell.cljs:835-864`. `duration-cell` renders the label, and is called at `:2058`. That file is the xray-shell-views slice and needs no change.
- Producer: `implementation/core/src/re_frame/router.cljc:2899-2906`. `:rf.event/run-end` carries `(assoc :rf.event/elapsed-ms handler-elapsed-ms)`.
- Spec: `tools/xray/spec/018-Event-Spine.md:391`, the row-anatomy line "Duration │ ≥60px │ 1.2 ms (right-aligned)".
- Fixture drift:
  - `tools/xray/test/day8/re_frame2_xray/panels/l2_timeline_cljs_test.cljc:108-120`.
  - `tools/xray/test/day8/re_frame2_xray/shell_cljs_test.cljs:993-1003`.

## Failure scenario

A programmer opens Xray on any app to find the slow event in a list of dispatches. Every row's Duration cell is empty, with no explanation. The cue the column exists to give is missing. And because the cell is deliberately allowed to be blank ("an event-bundle with no measured handler time"), the programmer can reasonably read the blank as "not measured in this build". In fact it is measured and then misread.

## Evidence

EXECUTED as a bounded JVM probe, from the scratch dir against the frozen tree's `tools/xray` as a `:local/root`, with no writes into the tree (`probe2.clj` section P5). The probe dispatched one real event and grouped its trace into the bundle Xray builds:

```
run-end tag keys: (:frame :rf.event/elapsed-ms :rf.event/v :rf.trace/dispatch-id :rf.trace/event-id :rf.trace/phase)
run-end :rf.event/elapsed-ms = 8
run-end :duration-ms         = nil
bundle :handler is run-end?   true
l2/event-bundle-duration-ms  = nil
l2/event-bundle-duration-label = nil
esc/event-bundle-outcome :duration-ms = nil
epoch-panel HANDLER :duration-ms (control) = 8
```

The control is the Epoch panel's HANDLER step, which reads 8 off the same event. So a duration is measured, the bundle's `:handler` slot is the right event, and only the key is wrong.

Census: `rf.event/elapsed-ms` appears 0 times in `l2_timeline.cljc` and `event_status_colour.cljc`, against 2 in `epoch/projection.cljc`.

What was INSPECTED rather than executed: that `event-bundle-outcome`'s `:duration-ms` has no live reader. `trace.cljs:929-948` (`event-bundle-status-bar`) and `event-bundle->state` (`event_status_colour.cljc:300-323`) read only `:outcome`.

Tracker search for `event-bundle-duration`, `elapsed-ms`, `duration column` and `rf2-slnce`: no existing bead for these two readers.

## Smallest fix

Read `(or (get-in b [:handler :tags :rf.event/elapsed-ms]) (get-in b [:handler :tags :duration-ms]))` in both readers. Keep the legacy key only as a fallback, mirroring `handler-row`'s rf2-slnce repair.

Move the two fixtures onto `:rf.event/elapsed-ms` so they pin the producer's real shape. A fixture stamping the legacy key could stay alongside as the fallback case.

Fence:

- `panels/l2_timeline.cljc`
- `panels/event/event_status_colour.cljc`
- `l2_timeline_cljs_test.cljc`
- `shell_cljs_test.cljs` (fixture only)

No hot-zone file.

## Gates

- JVM lane from `tools/xray` (`clojure -M:test`). It runs `l2_timeline_cljs_test.cljc` and `event_status_colour_cljs_test.cljc`.
- `npm run test:cljs` for `shell_cljs_test.cljs`, which is a `.cljs` node-lane namespace that no JVM artefact compiles.

No.
