title: ssr-node: a render callback that throws null/undefined crashes the whole sidecar (isolate.cjs:200 reads err.message unguarded)
description:
## Defect

`Isolate.start()` registers one `worker.on('error')` handler for the worker's whole life, and it ends with `reject(new Refusal(CODE.MALFORMED_MODULE, err.message, { stack: err.stack }))`. The `reject` is a no-op after boot, but its ARGUMENTS are evaluated on every `'error'` event in every phase. When a render module's scheduled callback throws a nullish value (`throw null` / `throw undefined`, which CLJS emits for `(throw nil)`, e.g. `(throw (:error resp))` with the key missing), Node delivers that value to the parent as `err === null` / `undefined`, `err.message` throws a `TypeError` inside the listener, and that becomes an uncaught exception in the MAIN thread. The whole sidecar process exits. Every in-flight render on every isolate is lost, not only the faulting one. This is the one hole in the fault containment the package otherwise states: an application fault stays in one isolate, and the pool replaces that isolate. Compare rf2-gwye.22, where one bad request line taking the sidecar down was treated as P1.

## Where

- `implementation/ssr-node/src/isolate.cjs:161`: `worker.on('error', (err) => { ... })`, registered in `Isolate.start()`
- `implementation/ssr-node/src/isolate.cjs:200`: `reject(new Refusal(CODE.MALFORMED_MODULE, err.message, { stack: err.stack }));`. The crash site, and the probe's stack trace names it (`isolate.cjs:200:55`).
- `isolate.cjs:186` (`reportIsolateFault`) and `:187-192` (`_failPendingRender`) already tolerate a nullish `err`. Only line 200 does not.
- Public entry points: `createService` (`src/service.cjs:233`) boots every isolate through `Pool.start()` -> `Isolate.start()`. The fault then fires from any render: `service.renderFrames` / `renderToString`, or HTTP `POST /render` (`src/http.cjs:302`). Because line 200 runs whatever the phase, it also fires when the callback lands after the render completed, i.e. while the isolate is idle.

## Failure scenario

A pool of 2. Request A renders an entry whose module does `setImmediate(() => { throw null; })`. Request B renders a well-behaved entry on the sibling isolate at the same moment. Result: the parent prints `[rf.ssr-node] isolate 0 died mid-render: null`, then `TypeError: Cannot read properties of null (reading 'message') at Worker.<anonymous> (...isolate.cjs:200:55)`, and the process exits 1. A never receives its `:rf.ssr-node/isolate-lost` refusal. B, which was innocent, never completes. Under `bin/serve.cjs` the JVM sees `:rf.error/ssr-node-unreachable` for every in-flight and following request until a supervisor restarts the sidecar and its isolates re-boot.

Expected, as for any other escaping throw: A is refused `:rf.ssr-node/isolate-lost` with service-owned detail, B is served, and the pool replaces the one dead isolate.

## Evidence

EXECUTED: a bounded Node probe, process-local, reading the frozen tree's `src/` and writing nothing into the tree (`scratchpad/review-wave/ssr-node/probe-throw-nullish.cjs` plus the probe module `late-throw-module.cjs`, Node v24.13.0 at `034d0c8fc8`). Each entry's render emits one chunk, schedules the throw with `setImmediate`, and returns a promise that never settles. A sibling `app/ok` render runs concurrently on the second isolate.

- `app/throw-null`: exit 1. stderr carries the TypeError at `isolate.cjs:200:55`. No stdout line: neither the faulting request's outcome nor the sibling's was ever reported.
- `app/throw-undef`: exit 1, the same TypeError (`reading 'message'` of `undefined`), same line.
- CONTROL, `app/throw-string` (a non-nullish primitive through the same path): exit 0. The request was refused `isolate-lost` with detail `{"isolate":0,"threadId":1,"afterChunks":1}`, the sibling was served (`sibling ok`), `replacements` went to 1, and stderr carried `[rf.ssr-node] isolate 0 died mid-render: a string`. So the path works, and only nullish values break it.
- CONTROL, `app/reject-null` (an unhandled `Promise.reject(null)`): exit 0, handled. Node wraps a non-Error rejection reason in `UnhandledPromiseRejection` before raising it. So the trigger is specifically a literal nullish `throw` from a callback, not a rejection.

INSPECTED: the idle-phase variant, a callback that throws nullish after the render has completed. Line 200 is unconditional, so it reaches the same crash. That variant was not separately executed.

Tracker: `bd export` scanned over all 71 ssr-node-mentioning records for `throw null|throw undefined|nullish|Cannot read properties of (null|undefined)`: 0 hits. The pattern's control, `postMessage`, hit 4 (rf2-kirm, rf2-ey07, rf2-2hmg, rf2-6r9j.177). Not previously filed or ruled.

## Smallest fix

Read `err` nullish-safely at line 200, e.g. `err?.message ?? String(err)` and `err?.stack`. The same guard can also go in `worker.cjs:120-121`, the boot `catch`: today it reads `err.code` / `err.message` directly, so a module that throws nullish at boot gets an operator refusal reading `Cannot read properties of null (reading 'code')` instead of anything about the module. That one does not crash anything. Add one row to `test/egress.test.cjs` beside the existing `throws-async` rows (`:736-910`), with an entry in `test/fixtures/throws-async.cjs` that throws `null` from `setImmediate`, and assert `isolate-lost` plus a live service afterwards.

Adjacent, and NOT this bead's scope: this is the same handler that rf2-pk4i6.5 finding #3 names, the isolate dying while idle, which was dismissed on 2026-09-16 with "take the `onDeath` + `dead`-skip when ssr-node is next touched". A fix here counts as touching ssr-node.

Fence: `implementation/ssr-node/src/isolate.cjs`, optionally `src/worker.cjs`, `test/egress.test.cjs`, `test/fixtures/throws-async.cjs`. No hot-zone file.

## Gates

`node implementation/ssr-node/test/run.cjs` (same as `npm run test:ssr-node` from `implementation/`), i.e. CI's `node-ssr-node` job. Plain Node with no shadow-cljs, and neither the CLJS lanes nor the JVM lanes compile these files.

## Decision needed

No.

title: pair-mcp: every elision marker ships :digest nil - off-box-tool enables digests against spec 009:3041 and the browser-side digest is nil against the :string schema
description:
## Defect

Every `:rf.size/large-elided` marker pair-mcp ships carries `:digest nil`. There are two causes, and they point in opposite directions.

1. **Spec conflict.** pair-mcp projects every surface through the `:rf.egress/off-box-tool` profile, and that profile turns `:rf.egress/include-digests?` ON. But spec/009-Instrumentation.md:3041 is a MUST: "the re-frame2-pair-mcp / Xray-MCP / story-mcp servers ... MUST default `:rf.egress/include-large?` to `false` and `:rf.egress/include-digests?` to `false`". Its reason, given at :3025, is that a digest "forces a full walk of the elided value, which negates the elision's cost-saving". EP-0015 §10 (docs/EP/EP-0015-frame-owned-egress-policy.md:783), spec/015-Data-Classification.md:264 and tools/mcp-base/spec/egress.md:42 say the opposite: off-box-tool "include[s] structural indicators / digests". So the specs contradict each other, and the code follows EP-0015.
2. **The digest does not exist on the host where pair-mcp projects.** pair-mcp runs `project-egress` inside the *browser* runtime, which is CLJS. There `re-frame.elision/sha256-hex` is `#?(:cljs nil)`. `->marker` still does `(assoc :digest (sha256-hex v))`, so the marker ships `:digest nil`. Spec-Schemas.md:3649 types the slot `[:digest {:optional true} :string]`: optional means absent or a string, and `nil` is neither. So on pair-mcp's host the "structural indicator" that justifies overriding 009:3041 carries no information, and every marker fails the normative `:rf/elision-marker` schema.

## Where

At `034d0c8fc8`:

- `implementation/core/src/re_frame/projection.cljc:123-142`: `profile->size-opts`, whose docstring says "All six off-box / on-box-redacted boundaries fail closed (... no digests)" and then that off-box-tool "additionally turns on `:rf.egress/include-digests?`", with the off-box-tool row at `:139-142`.
- `implementation/core/src/re_frame/elision.cljc:641-650` (`sha256-hex`: a `:clj` MessageDigest branch, and `:cljs` returns `nil`) and `:658-676` (`->marker`: `include-digests? (assoc :digest (sha256-hex v))`).
- `tools/re-frame2-pair-mcp/src/re_frame2_pair_mcp/tools/elision.cljs:107-161` and `tools/epoch_egress.cljs:140-199` (every pair egress form names `:rf.egress/off-box-tool`). The docstrings at `epoch_egress.cljs:71`, `:90`, `:153-157` and `:335`, and at `elision.cljs:87`, promise "the structural digest a tool needs".
- The contract: spec/009-Instrumentation.md:3025 and :3041, spec/Spec-Schemas.md:3649 and :3660, spec/015-Data-Classification.md:264.

Entry point: any pair tool that returns a marker (`get-path`, `snapshot`, `read-sub`, `trace-window`, ...).

## Failure scenario

`get-path {:path "[:blob]"}` over a frame declaring `{:large [[:blob :payload]]}` returns `{:payload {:rf.size/large-elided {:path [:blob :payload] :bytes 50000 :type :string :reason :effect :hint nil :handle [...] :digest nil}}}`. An agent comparing digests across turns to detect change-without-fetch, which is the use case spec/009:3025 gives, sees `nil = nil` and concludes that nothing changed, however the value moved. A validator holding the marker to Spec-Schemas `:rf/elision-marker` rejects every marker pair-mcp emits.

## Evidence

**Executed** (JVM half): a bounded probe of `rf/project-egress` against the frozen `implementation/core`, run from the scratch dir with no tree writes. Under off-box-tool the marker `contains? :digest` is true, with value `"sha256:2c6847..."` on the JVM. Under off-box-observability, `contains? :digest` is false. So the profile does enable digests, as the JVM test `implementation/core/test/re_frame/core_epoch_egress_profile_test.clj:140` pins.

**Inspected** (CLJS half, the one pair-mcp runs): `sha256-hex`'s `:cljs` branch is literally `nil`, and `->marker` assocs the result unconditionally once `include-digests?` is true. Per CLAUDE.md, a `#?(:cljs ...)` branch is compiled only by the CLJS lane, so no JVM probe can execute it. A Grep for `:digest` over `tools/re-frame2-pair-mcp` finds 1 hit, a docstring, so no pair test pins the digest's value. As a control, the same Grep over `implementation/core/test` finds the JVM `string?` / `contains?` assertions (`elision_test.clj:349`, `core_epoch_egress_profile_test.clj`), so the Grep does find what exists. None of those run in the browser host.

Tracker: rf2-kuky.6, rf2-kuky.9, rf2-kuky.88, rf2-kuky.93 and rf2-bv1p (all closed) built the profile vocabulary. None rules on 009:3041 against off-box-tool, or on the CLJS nil. rf2-3x7nj.3.4 (open) concerns resource-handle hash digests, which is a different mechanism.

## Smallest fix

Per the decision below.

- (a) **Digests on, made real.** In `->marker`, assoc `:digest` only when `sha256-hex` returns a string. On CLJS, either compute one (SubtleCrypto is async, so a synchronous FNV or similar is the practical choice) or accept that the slot is absent there. Then amend spec/009-Instrumentation.md:3041 (**hot zone**) to exempt off-box-tool.
- (b) **Digests off.** Set off-box-tool's `include-digests?` to false in `projection.cljc`, and correct spec/015:264, EP-0015 §10, `tools/mcp-base/spec/egress.md:42`, the `epoch_egress.cljs` docstrings and the JVM profile test.

Either way, `->marker` should never assoc a nil `:digest`. That one-line guard is uncontroversial and fixes the schema violation on its own.

## Gates

`elision.cljc` is `.cljc`, and the change sits in the `#?(:cljs ...)`-dependent path, so the CLJS lane `npm run test:cljs` in `implementation` is the grading lane. `clojure -M:test` in `implementation/core` covers the JVM half (`core_epoch_egress_profile_test`, `elision_test`). The pair-mcp `npm test` confirms the tool side. The spec edits need `mkdocs build --strict` and `scripts/check_doc_slugs.py`.

## Decision needed

Yes. Should off-box-tool carry digests? (a) Keep them, emit `:digest` only when one can be computed, and amend spec/009:3041. (b) Turn them off and correct spec/015, EP-0015 and the mcp-base egress spec. Either way, stop shipping `:digest nil`.
notes:
== DOSSIER WRITTEN 2026-09-24 01:51:52 AUSEST (analysis only — no status change, no dispatch, no edit) ==
Dossier: ai/decisions/rf2-3x7nj.32.6.off-box-tool-digests-on-or-off.md in the mayor checkout. The ai/ tree is local-only and gitignored, so this path is a convenience that can rot. The findings below stand on their own.

Read at trunk 28b89b9308 (= origin/main). Probe ran at dafe7ade2d (no relevant diff).

RECOMMENDATION: option (b) plus the guard. Set :rf.egress/off-box-tool's :rf.egress/include-digests? to false (implementation/core/src/re_frame/projection.cljc:142). Guard ->marker (elision.cljc:681) to assoc :digest only when sha256-hex returns a string. spec/009-Instrumentation.md:3041 then stays exactly as written, so rf2-c5ggd's item 3 (narrow :3041) must be DROPPED. Fix spec/015-Data-Classification.md:264, tools/mcp-base/spec/egress.md:42 and the spec/Tool-Pair.md:896 parenthetical (hot zone) instead. EP-0015 needs no edit.

DECISIVE FINDINGS:
1. Nothing consumes a digest. Pair descriptors, knobs and skill references mention it 0 times. No source passes include-digests? true; the off-box-tool row is the only thing in the tree that turns digests on. No CLJS test asserts a marker digest. The JVM tests pin presence only (core_epoch_egress_profile_test.clj:140/178/252, epoch_privacy_test.clj:875/938). Change detection is already served by watch-epochs :touches-path and trace-window's per-epoch diff encoding.
2. Same profile, two wire shapes. sha256-hex is #?(:cljs nil) (elision.cljc:647-656), so pair-MCP (browser host) ships :digest nil on every marker, while story-MCP (JVM -main, server.cljc:433) ships a real sha256. Probe with the verbatim Spec-Schemas ElisionMarkerBody (:3649): :digest nil validates false, absent validates true, string validates true. Two different same-size values with nil digests give EQUAL markers, a false "unchanged".
3. Bead corrections. EP-0015 section 10 (EP-0015:783) says only "include structural indicators/counters", never "digests"; the digest gloss came with f3169be2e2 (rf2-yjbr1w) and spec/015:264. The bead's "SubtleCrypto async, so FNV" is wrong: a synchronous goog.crypt.Sha256 path already exists (implementation/schemas/src/re_frame/schemas/digest.cljc:55-66). But computing it on CLJS pulls goog.crypt into core and hashes multi-MB values on every read, which is the cost 009:3025 names.
Relation to rf2-3x7nj.3.4 (ruled keyed HMAC for resource handles): a different role. A handle is an identity over sensitive params; a marker digest is change detection over non-sensitive content (009:3053: sensitive values never get markers). That keying ruling does not transfer.
Lanes: implementation/core + implementation/epoch clojure -M:test (JVM pins); the guard sits behind #?(:cljs nil), so only npm run test:cljs grades it.
== RULING (delegated by Mike; mayor-dispatched ruling agent, 2026-09-24 05:00:30 AUSEST) ==

RULING: option (b) PLUS THE GUARD. `:rf.egress/off-box-tool` stops turning digests on (its `:rf.egress/include-digests?` floor becomes `false`, like every other profile), and `->marker` never emits `:digest nil` — it associates `:digest` only when a digest string was actually computed, whatever the profile or override. spec/009-Instrumentation.md :3041's MUST ("the re-frame2-pair-mcp / Xray-MCP / story-mcp servers ... MUST default ... `:rf.egress/include-digests?` to `false`") is therefore RIGHT AS WRITTEN and stays; spec 015 :264, the mcp-base egress page, spec/Tool-Pair.md :896's parenthetical and the docstrings that promise a digest are corrected instead. The explicit per-call `:rf.egress/include-digests? true` override is kept: on the JVM it still yields a `sha256:` string; the browser build computes none and now omits the slot. This bead (rf2-3x7nj.32.6) is the implementation carrier; it is NOT a pair-MCP change despite its surface label — the code is in implementation/core.

THIS SUPERSEDES ONE PASSING OBSERVATION IN rf2-ealv5's RULING, explicitly. rf2-ealv5's "NOTICED IN PASSING (i)" said 009 :3041's digest clause is "stale for the MCP-server clause" because "015 and the code agree", and routed "narrow :3041 to the forwarders" into rf2-c5ggd item 3. That observation was not part of rf2-ealv5's decision (its ruling is about the `:large` subtree and un-gating the size override, both untouched here), and it was wrong on four counts, each checked at source for this ruling: (1) the code agrees only on the JVM — on the browser host where pair-MCP runs `project-egress`, `sha256-hex` is `#?(:cljs nil)`, so the flagship MCP server has never shipped a digest, and every marker it ships is `:digest nil`, which the normative marker schema rejects (C6 below); (2) spec 015's "structural indicators / digests" does not come from EP-0015: EP-0015 §10's off-box-tool row (docs/EP/EP-0015-frame-owned-egress-policy.md :783) reads only "include structural indicators/counters" — the word "digests" arrived with the implementation commit f3169be2e2 (2026-06-11, rf2-yjbr1w) and was copied into 015 by 6ebe277e7c (2026-06-22, rf2-5fqlz1; pickaxe on "indicators / digests"); (3) nothing reads a marker digest (census below); (4) rf2-kuky.88's own RULING chose `:rf.egress/off-box-observability` over `off-box-tool` for Xray's clipboard precisely BECAUSE the latter "turns `:rf.size/include-digests?` ON" — the record already treated digests-on as a policy change to avoid, not a wanted default. A note recording the supersession is appended to rf2-ealv5, and rf2-c5ggd item 3 is replaced (note appended there).

WHY
- Measurements, re-run by this ruling at trunk 6b787c338b (JVM probe through the PUBLIC `rf/project-egress` door, `:large [[:blob :payload] ...]`, 50,000-char values; verbatim Spec-Schemas `ElisionMarkerBody`; exit 0, 0 bytes stderr, mayor checkout 0 porcelain lines after):
  C1 off-box-tool marker `:digest` → "sha256:2c68470035a1..." (JVM)
  C2 CONTROL off-box-observability → no `:digest` key
  C3 50,000 x "X" vs 50,000 x "Y": markers EQUAL once `:digest` is removed
  C4 ... their JVM digests differ → a digest WOULD detect a same-size change
  C5 schema, marker as emitted on the JVM (string digest) → valid
  C6 schema, the same marker with `:digest nil` (what the browser host emits) → INVALID
  C7 schema, the same marker with `:digest` absent → valid
  C8 two nil-digest markers over different values → equal: the browser's `nil` is a false "unchanged"
- Same profile, two wire shapes, chosen by host: `re-frame.elision/sha256-hex` (implementation/core/src/re_frame/elision.cljc:647) is a MessageDigest on `:clj` and literally `nil` on `:cljs`, and `->marker` (:664) does `include-digests? (assoc :digest (sha256-hex v))` unconditionally (:681). Pair-MCP projects in the browser → `:digest nil` on every marker; story-MCP is in-process `.cljc` with a JVM `-main` → a real digest when it runs on the JVM.
- Nothing consumes it. `git grep -n include-digests -- 'implementation/*/src/**' 'tools/*/src/**' 'skills/*/preload/**'`: the profile table (projection.cljc :130-162), the walker plumbing (elision.cljc :669/:681/:699/:1110/:1182) and docstrings — ZERO sources pass `:rf.egress/include-digests? true`; the off-box-tool row (projection.cljc:142) is the only thing in the tree that turns digests on. Pair descriptors, knobs and skill references mention `digest` 0 times (case-insensitive line counts: descriptors_data.cljs 0, descriptors_knobs.cljs 0, skills/re-frame2-pair/references/*.md 0 — controls on the same files: `handle` 44, 2 and 71); Xray mentions the slot in one docstring (views/edn_inspector.cljs:534). No CLJS test asserts a marker digest, which is how the `nil` survived; the JVM tests pin PRESENCE only.
- EP-0015's "structural indicators/counters" are already delivered without a digest: the marker's `:path`, `:bytes`, `:type`, `:handle`, and the tools' `:elided-large` / `:elided-count` counts.
- The "cost" half of spec 009 :3025's rationale is overstated (Codex, verified): `pr-str-bytes` (elision.cljc:589) already serialises the whole elided value to compute `:bytes`, so the digest does not "force a full walk" that was otherwise avoided — it adds a SECOND `pr-str` (sha256-hex re-prints `v`) plus a SHA-256 per marker on the JVM. The conclusion (default off) stands; the sentence is corrected via rf2-c5ggd.
- (a1) keep digests on, accept the browser omits them: LOSES — a profile promise one of its two hosts can never keep, a hot-zone amendment of 009 :3041 plus Tool-Pair :896 reworded to "on hosts that can compute one", for a feature nobody reads. (a2) compute one in the browser: LOSES — the bead's "SubtleCrypto is async, so a synchronous FNV" premise is wrong (a synchronous `goog.crypt.Sha256` path already exists in implementation/schemas/src/re_frame/schemas/digest.cljc:56-69, and an FNV value would not be the `sha256:<hex>` the schema types), but using it pulls `goog.crypt` into core's `re-frame.elision`, which compiles into every browser build, and runs pure-JS SHA-256 over the full printed value of every large marker on every read — cost with no reader. Defer until a concrete workflow needs browser-side content identity.

WHERE THE TWO RECOMMENDATIONS AGREED / DIFFERED, AND HOW RESOLVED
Both chose (b) plus the guard, both keep callers NAMING `:rf.egress/off-box-tool` even though its size floor now equals off-box-observability's (the profile names the boundary — EP-0015's point; local-redacted, ssr-hydration and public-error already share that floor), and both leave EP-0015 unedited. Codex corrected the dossier twice; both accepted, neither changes the ruling:
1. The dossier claimed change detection "is already served by the epoch stream". FALSE: `trace-window`/`watch-epochs` project each page app-side (trace_window.cljs ~:144-155 `project-page-src`) and the wire pipeline then diff-encodes the ALREADY-PROJECTED records (tools/re-frame2-pair-mcp/src/re_frame2_pair_mcp/tools/wire_pipeline.cljs:180, strip-sensitive → diff-encode → dedup), so a same-size change inside a large slot yields equal markers (C3) and NO patch — Codex measured zero patches for X vs Y, one patch with a real digest. And `watch-epochs`' `:touches-path` tests non-nil PRESENCE at the path in `:db-before` or `:db-after` (skills/re-frame2-pair/preload/re_frame2_pair/pure.cljc:234), not whether the value changed. So (b) genuinely costs JVM-host consumers (story-MCP) a default content-change signal. Accepted: nothing reads it, pair has never had it, and the explicit override remains for a JVM caller who wants it. The honest consequence is written down: absent a digest, equal markers say NOTHING about whether the content is equal (one clause in spec 009 via rf2-c5ggd, one in the pair skill's marker bullet via rf2-ealv5's PR).
2. The dossier's file list missed a CLJS pin: implementation/core/test/re_frame/projection_cljs_test.cljc:95 asserts `(true? (:rf.egress/include-digests? o))` for off-box-tool ("off-box-tool includes structural indicators (§10)") — it flips.
Relation to rf2-3x7nj.3.4 (ruled keyed HMAC-SHA-256 for opaque resource handles): a different mechanism with a different role — a resource handle is an IDENTITY over sensitive scope/params that must be one-way; a marker digest is change detection over NON-sensitive content (a value matching a sensitive declaration never becomes a marker, and a whole-output marker carries no digest under any profile, tool_pair.cljc ~:2192-2196). That keying ruling does not transfer; nothing here touches resource-handle hashing.

WHAT TO BUILD (carrier: this bead; re-verified at trunk 6b787c338b)
1. implementation/core/src/re_frame/projection.cljc:142 — off-box-tool `:rf.egress/include-digests?   true` → `false`. Rewrite the `profile->size-opts` docstring (:123-133): all six non-raw boundaries fail closed with no digests; off-box-tool differs from off-box-observability by the boundary it NAMES, not its size floor; digests are an explicit per-call override only.
2. implementation/core/src/re_frame/elision.cljc:681 — compute the digest once and associate it only when it is a string, e.g. `(let [d (when include-digests? (sha256-hex v))] (cond-> body d (assoc :digest d)))`. Give `sha256-hex` (:647) a docstring saying the browser build returns nil and the slot is then omitted. No new dependency, so no bundle growth (nothing for the perf-bundle gate to see).

title: machines-viz: SCXML import decodes foreign ids and event lists with the export codec - hyphens become namespaces, _hh becomes a control char, 'a b' becomes one event
description:
## Defect

`scxml->spec` decodes EVERY `id`, `initial`, `target`, `event` and `cond` string with machines-viz's own injective export codec. That codec treats the first bare `-` as a keyword namespace boundary and every `_` followed by two hex digits as an escaped character. It is correct for documents this library emitted, but it is applied just the same to third-party SCXML, which the API and the parser advertise as a use case. As a result, ordinary external documents import silently renamed:
- `id="logged-out"` becomes `:logged/out`;
- `event="login-ok"` becomes `:login/ok`;
- `id="step_1a"` becomes a keyword ending in the control character U+001A;
- a W3C space-separated event list, `event="logout session.expired"`, becomes ONE keyword containing a space. SCXML §3.5 defines `event` as "a space-separated list of event descriptors", so the imported transition can never fire.

The import-postcondition (`grammar/valid-definition?`) passes all of this, so the caller gets a confident, well-formed machine whose event names and states differ from the document.

## Where

At `034d0c8fc8`:
- `tools/machines-viz/src/day8/re_frame2_machines_viz/scxml.cljc:319-334`, `id-string->keyword`: splits on the first `-` and unescapes `_hh` for any string.
- `scxml.cljc:264-274`: `unescape-id-segment`.
- `scxml.cljc:962-988`: `unescape-id-string`.
- `scxml.cljc:1241`: `:on` keys decode via `id-string->keyword`, one keyword per `event` attribute.
- `scxml.cljc:880-888`: the parser says it "consumes the common SCXML shapes external tools emit".
- The contract: `tools/machines-viz/spec/API.md:2222-2226` (SCXML "lets re-frame2 machines be shared with non-CLJS tooling — external workflow systems, Erlang gen_statem-derived tools, Stately's importers, the xstate-visualizer").
- Entry point: `scxml/scxml->spec` (:1571).

## Failure scenario

```xml
<scxml xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2005/07/scxml" version="1.0" initial="logged-out">
  <state id="logged-out"><transition event="login-ok" target="step_1a"/></state>
  <state id="step_1a"><transition event="logout session.expired" target="logged-out"/></state>
</scxml>
```

This imports as `{:initial :logged/out :states {:logged/out {:on {:login/ok :step<U+001A>}} :step<U+001A> {:on {:logout session.expired :logged/out}}}}`, and `valid-definition?` returns true. A host dispatching `[:login-ok]` or `[:logout]` never moves the machine.

## Evidence

Executed with a bounded JVM probe (`p3.clj`, frozen tree, scratch `deps.edn`). It printed the imported map, the state-name code points `[115 116 101 112 26]` for `step_1a`, and the event keys as `[pr-str namespace name]` triples: `[:login/ok login ok]` and `[:logout session.expired nil logout session.expired]`, i.e. one un-namespaced keyword whose name contains a space. Control: machines-viz's own exports round-trip exactly (the existing `round-trip-property-pinned-on-supported-subset` fixtures), so the codec is sound for its own output and the defect is only its application to foreign strings. Tracker: rf2-qy8p (closed) hardened foreign CHILD ELEMENTS and kept "the id codec" explicitly out of scope, so there is no ruling on foreign ids. No other bead matched "scxml" plus hyphen, space-separated or external ids.

## Smallest fix

Have `spec->scxml` stamp its documents (for example a `data_rf_codec="1"` attribute on `<scxml>`, the same carrier posture as `data_rf_error_final`). `scxml->spec` then applies the codec only when the stamp is present. Otherwise it maps foreign ids and event names verbatim (`(keyword s)`, splitting nothing), and splits a whitespace-separated `event` list into one `:on` entry per descriptor. The alternative is to declare the importer round-trip-only and refuse unstamped documents loudly. Fence: `scxml.cljc`, `spec/API.md` (§SCXML), `scxml_cljs_test.cljc`. No hot-zone file.

## Gates

`tools/machines-viz`: `clojure -M:test` (JVM; `scxml_cljs_test.cljc`).

## Decision needed

Yes, one line. Is third-party SCXML import in scope (decode foreign ids verbatim and split event lists), or is `scxml->spec` round-trip-only (then say so in API.md and refuse unstamped documents)?

== DOSSIER WRITTEN 2026-09-24 01:33:31 AUSEST (analysis only — no status change, no dispatch, no edit) ==

Dossier: ai/decisions/rf2-3x7nj.33.5.scxml-import-foreign-or-round-trip-only.md. The ai/ tree is local-only and gitignored, so that path is a convenience that can rot; the findings below stand on their own.

Read at trunk 4fe0cbe915 (local HEAD, one checkpoint ahead of origin/main 805612eef6). `git log 034d0c8fc8..HEAD -- tools/machines-viz/` returns 0 commits against 44 over the whole range, so every review-tree line citation still holds.

RECOMMENDATION: Option A — keep third-party import in scope at its small size. spec->scxml stamps its <scxml> root with a data_rf_codec-style carrier, following the data_rf_error_final precedent. scxml->spec applies the export codec only when the stamp is present, reads unstamped ids, events and guards verbatim with (keyword s), and splits every `event` attribute on whitespace. That split is safe for stamped documents too, because the codec never emits a space. The fix is roughly 30-40 source lines in scxml.cljc plus one tool API.md paragraph, and touches no hot-zone file. Cross-level targets in nested foreign documents stay a documented limitation that fails loudly (W3C ID-reference resolution is option A+, deferred).

Decisive findings:
1. There is no earlier ruling, and no spec names an import source. Tool API.md:2222-2227 names only export consumers ("Stately's importers, the xstate-visualizer"); scxml.cljc:1574 says "Inverse of spec->scxml"; tool 000-Vision.md:811 says "the SCXML subset we emit". But scxml.cljc:882-883 says the parser "consumes the common SCXML shapes external tools emit", and rf2-qy8p (closed, PR #9289) hardened foreign <onentry>/<invoke> input on exactly that premise while keeping "the id codec" out of scope.
2. The export carries no marker, so foreign input cannot be told apart today. The flat root, emitted at scxml.cljc:650-651, is only xmlns/version/initial, and the probe found `data_rf` absent from a flat export. A stamp is therefore needed under either answer (A, or round-trip-only B), and B's refusal saves no code: it forces rewriting all 8 rf2-qy8p foreign fixtures (scxml_cljs_test.cljc:1558-1822), where A touches one (:1641, which uses exporter-style outer___one ids).
3. All decoding funnels through two primitives: id-string->keyword (scxml.cljc:319-334, 7 call sites) and id-string->abs-path/unescape-id-string (:962-997, 7 call sites). Probe executed at trunk: the reviewer's document imports as :logged/out and :step+U+001A, with ONE event keyword named "logout session.expired", and valid-definition? returns true. Control: the same names authored in re-frame2 round-trip equal. A nested foreign document with a cross-level target THROWS :scxml/invalid-spec, so that failure is loud, not silent.

Under A, .33.4's "every emitted target is a declared id" test stays the only export guard, because stamped documents keep decoding targets by codec.
== RULING (delegated by Mike; mayor-dispatched ruling agent, 2026-09-24 05:02:32 AUSEST) ==

RULING: Option B, round-trip-only. `scxml->spec` reads only documents written by this library's own `spec->scxml`. The exporter marks every document it writes, and the importer refuses any document without that exact marker, with one documented error, before it applies any export convention. Keep export-for-sharing exactly as it is. Keep the rf2-qy8p hardening, because a marked document can still be hand-edited. No hot-zone file moves.

WHY B, AND WHY A LOSES

The dossier recommended A (import third-party SCXML verbatim when unstamped and split `event` lists on whitespace, about 30-40 lines). The independent Codex review recommended B. The decider is whether A actually yields a correct machine for a third-party document. It does not, and I re-verified that by reading the source at trunk 7fc78b7b72. `git log 034d0c8fc8..origin/main -- tools/machines-viz/` returns 0 commits (control: 11 commits touch spec/ over the same range), so every line cite below is also the review-tree line.

A fixes the NAMES. It leaves at least four places where a foreign document still imports as a confident, valid, different machine. That is the same failure class as the defect, only quieter:
1. Transition type. W3C SCXML defaults a transition's `type` to `external`. The importer sets `:reenter? true` only for an explicit `type="external"` (scxml.cljc:1181, `reenter? (and target (= type-s "external"))`). So an omitted type imports as re-frame2's internal default, and a foreign self-transition silently stops re-running exit and entry. Our exporter always writes `type` explicitly on target-bearing transitions (scxml.cljc:419-467), so this is invisible on our own documents. The comment at :1178, "(incl. the SCXML default `internal`)", is itself wrong: the W3C default is `external`.
2. `after.*` and `done.state.*`. These are this library's conventions. The importer checks `(str/starts-with? event "after.")` and `"done.state."` BEFORE ordinary event decoding (scxml.cljc:1216/1227, and the parallel-root twin at :1514/:1517). Our codec escapes a literal `.`, so our own user events can never collide. A foreign `event="after.500"` becomes an `:after {500 …}` TIMER. Codex executed that on a bounded JVM probe, and got the identical timer with verbatim decoding substituted, so A does not change it.
3. Event descriptor matching. A W3C descriptor matches by token prefix: `error` matches `error.communication`. re-frame2 prefix-matches on the keyword namespace (`/`, Spec 005 §partial-match tier), so a verbatim `:error` never matches `:error.communication`. Splitting on whitespace does not make foreign events behave as W3C says.
4. Targets. W3C `target` values are document-wide id references, but the importer derives a state's path from its id string (`id-string->abs-path`), which works only for our fully-qualified ids. The dossier's probe found that a cross-level target in a nested foreign document THROWS `:scxml/invalid-spec`. That failure is loud, but the fix for it (option A+) was a further 60-100 lines.

So a faithful foreign import is a translator project with its own corpus. It is not a codec switch, and A would advertise it while still being wrong. B is the smallest design that is correct and loud. The documentation already draws that boundary: `scxml->spec`'s docstring (:1574) says "Inverse of `spec->scxml`", and tool 000-Vision.md:810 says "string-based for the SCXML subset we emit". The tool API.md intro names only export CONSUMERS (Stately's importers, the xstate-visualizer). The pull the other way came from two places: one parser comment (:882-888, "consumes the common SCXML shapes external tools emit"), and rf2-qy8p hardening foreign child elements on that comment's premise. rf2-qy8p's own scope says "Preserve … the id codec", so no earlier ruling put foreign ids in scope. The dossier's `bd search scxml` found no Mike ruling, and my own export search found none either.

Nobody loses anything real. Nothing outside machines-viz's own tests calls `scxml->spec`: across the tree it occurs in 7 files, and the only one outside machines-viz is Spec 005 prose. ai_generate's use is a round-trip test. There is no paste UI.

The dossier said B costs as much as A. That is true, and it does not decide between them: B's cost is fixture churn, while A's real cost is the list above.

The reason sentence should say that `scxml->spec` reads only documents `spec->scxml` wrote, and that the fix is to re-export from the re-frame2 definition. title: core-pipeline: a machine handler's :dispatch-later inherits :rf.machine/internal? and front-inserts when it fires, contrary to spec 002/005 (timer events go to the back)
description:
## Defect

A `:dispatch-later` emitted by a MACHINE handler inherits the `:rf.machine/internal?` front-of-queue flag, so when its timer fires the delayed event FRONT-inserts ahead of external events already waiting in the queue.

The specs say a timer-delivered event goes to the back:

- Spec 005 Level 4 lists "a timer/promise/websocket callback" among the ordinary back-of-queue origins.
- Spec 005 §Delayed `:after` says the timer event "arrives at the back of the runtime FIFO, no different from any other `:dispatch-later`".
- Spec 002's drain pseudocode copies the flag in `do-fx :dispatch` and deliberately does NOT copy it in `do-fx :dispatch-later`.

The code's shared `child-dispatch-opts` copies the flag for both. The front-of-queue rule exists so a machine settles its macrostep before the next external event. A delayed message fires long after that macrostep ended, so leap-frogging events the user queued meanwhile reorders them for no reason the spec gives.

## Where

- `implementation/core/src/re_frame/fx.cljc:611-662`, `child-dispatch-opts`. It runs `(assoc :rf.machine/internal? true)` whenever the parent envelope carries it (656), with no regard to `:ms`.
- `fx.cljc:664-721`, `child-dispatch!`. A numeric `:ms` routes to `arm-dispatch-later!` with those same opts (716-717).
- `fx.cljc:882-888`, the `:dispatch-later` reserved body.
- `implementation/core/src/re_frame/router.cljc:2999-3001`. This stamps the flag on every machine-handler envelope. The comment at 2991-2993 asserts the `:dispatch-later` copy is intended, which contradicts the spec.
- `router.cljc:4313`: `insert-envelope`, which front-inserts via `front-insert-machine-internal` (4238-4259).
- Spec:
  - `spec/002-Frames.md:2279-2285`: `do-fx :dispatch-later` carries no flag copy.
  - `spec/005-StateMachines.md:1282`: timer callbacks go to the back.
  - `spec/005-StateMachines.md:2490`.
- Public entry point: a `reg-machine` action returning `{:fx [[:dispatch-later {:ms n :event ev}]]}` (the explicit-timeout idiom as opposed to `:after`).

## Failure scenario

Executed (probe p3, JVM, frozen tree plus the machines artefact).

- Setup: machine `:p/m`, whose entry action returns `{:fx [[:dispatch-later {:ms 100 :event [:p/timer]}]]}`.
- Step 1: `dispatch-sync! [:p/m [:go]]`.
- Step 2: immediately async-dispatch `[:p/slow]`, whose handler sleeps 400ms, then `[:p/ext]`. The timer fires while `:p/ext` is still queued behind the running `:p/slow`.
- Result: the log is `[:slow :timer :ext]`. The timer event jumped ahead of `:p/ext`, which arrived first.
- Control: the identical `:dispatch-later` from a plain non-machine handler logs `[:slow :ext :timer]`, which is arrival order, as the spec requires for every timer callback.

## Evidence

- Executed: `review-wave/core-pipeline/probe3/p3.clj`, output `p3.out`, both lines quoted above. The frozen tree read `git status --porcelain` 0 lines afterwards.
- Inspected:
  - `take-event!` pops before processing (`router.cljc:3773`), so the front insert lands ahead of the waiting external events and not ahead of the running one.
  - Spec 005 `:after` timers do not go through this path (they arm via `re-frame.managed-timer`), so `:after` ordering is unaffected. Only an explicit `:dispatch-later` from a machine action is.
- Not pinned by any test:
  - `machines/test/re_frame/substrate_source_machine_test.clj` pins only the `:source :machine-action` stamp.
  - `core/test/re_frame/router_front_of_queue_cljs_test.cljc` exercises `:rf.machine/internal?` only on direct `dispatch!`.
  - Of the 27 files under `implementation/**/test/**` that mention `dispatch-later`, 0 mention `machine/internal`. The control is the same per-file count on two known files, which read 2 and 7.
- Tracker:
  - `bd search dispatch-later` returned 0. As a control, `stranded` returns 3.
  - A full-text scan of the 2109 exported issues for dispatch-later-near-`internal?` found 0.
  - The rulings the code comments cite (rf2-j20a7, rf2-c3990, rf2-lud4af) are not in the database (`bd show` answers "no issue found"), so no recorded ruling makes the front insert deliberate.

## Smallest fix

In `child-dispatch!` (`fx.cljc`), drop the flag on the delayed path: when `(number? ms)`, `dissoc :rf.machine/internal?` from `opts` before `arm-dispatch-later!`. Keep `:source :machine-action`. Also correct the comment at `router.cljc:2991-2993`.

Fence: `implementation/core/src/re_frame/fx.cljc` and `router.cljc` (comment only), plus one test. No hot-zone file.

If Mike instead rules that the code is right, the spec side is `spec/002-Frames.md` and `spec/005-StateMachines.md`, which are BOTH hot-zone files.

## Gates

- `clojure -M:test` in `implementation/core`, plus `implementation/machines` for a machine-level ordering test.
- `fx.cljc` is shared `.cljc` outside any reader conditional; `npm run test:cljs` covers the CLJS compile.

## Decision needed

Yes, which side is stale:

- Timer-delivered machine messages go to the back, as spec 002 and 005 say today (fix the code).
- Or they front-insert, as the code comment says (edit two hot-zone specs).

- The fix: in fx.cljc child-dispatch!, drop :rf.machine/internal? from the opts on the numeric-:ms branch, before calling arm-dispatch-later!.

WHY

    - So the spec is the deliberate side. Even so, "never chosen" cannot be proved: the implementation's comments do mention delayed children, and the beads they cite (rf2-j20a7, rf2-c3990, rf2-lud4af) have been pruned from the tracker.
    - The decisive reasons are therefore the contract as it reads today, and the fact that a callback which fires after the macrostep has ended has no macrostep rationale for jumping the queue.
  - (2) The browser example in the dossier (a timer firing mid-render) is really a JVM interleaving. In a browser, a timer cannot interrupt a synchronous handler.

title: xray-domain-panels-a: Cancellation cascade counts every actor-destroy HTTP abort twice (aborted-on-actor-destroy plus its :rf.http/aborted :actor-destroyed echo)
description:
## Defect

The Cancellation-cascade visualiser counts every actor-destroy HTTP abort TWICE. When an actor with an in-flight managed request is destroyed, the runtime emits two trace rows for that one request, both in the destroying drain:

1. `:rf.http/aborted-on-actor-destroy`, from the registry, which then calls the request's abort-fn with `:actor-destroyed`.
2. `:rf.http/aborted`, from the transport's abort choke, with `:reason :actor-destroyed` and the same `:actor-id`.

The cascade's abort set contains both operations. Its gatherer dedups by trace `:id` only, so both rows survive. As a result:

- the waterfall draws two ABORT rows for one request;
- the teardown row reads "2 in-flight fxs";
- the summary reads "1 child destroyed · 2 effects aborted".

The helper's own docstring expects `:rf.http/aborted` in a cascade to be "rarer". In fact it accompanies every actor-destroy abort, by construction.

## Where

At `034d0c8fc8`:

- `tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/panels/cancellation_cascade_helpers.cljc`
  - `:136-156`: `abort-operations` holds both `:rf.http/aborted-on-actor-destroy` and `:rf.http/aborted`. The docstring at `:140-141` calls the latter "rarer".
  - `:220-224`: `abort-event?`.
  - `:401-461`: `gather-related-aborts` collects same-dispatch-id aborts and dedups by `(:id ev)` only (`:450-459`).
  - `:463-522`: `gather-related-teardowns`. `counts-by-actor` counts each abort row per `:actor-id`, which becomes `:inflight-count`.
  - `:617-639`: `cascade-summary`.
- **Runtime, one request, one destroy:**
  - `implementation/http/src/re_frame/http/registry.cljc:908-915` emits `:rf.http/aborted-on-actor-destroy` `{:request-id :actor-id :url}`, then `((:abort-fn handle) :actor-destroyed)`. This is the only `:actor-destroyed` abort-fn call site in `implementation/http/src`.
  - `implementation/http/src/re_frame/http/transport.cljc:764-775` handles that abort-fn by emitting `:rf.http/aborted` with the failure map `{:kind :rf.http/aborted :reason :actor-destroyed :actor-id …}`.
  - Both emits sit under the same `rf.interop/debug-enabled?` gate.
- **Entry points:**
  - the Machines-tab side panel (`:rf.xray/cancellation-cascade-for-focused-machine`, `cancellation_cascade_subs.cljs:51-56`);
  - the Trace popover (`:rf.xray/cancellation-cascade-for-focused-event`, `:66-84`).
  - Both are rendered by `cancellation_cascade.cljs` (`header` `:253-271`, `teardown-row` `:308-342`, `body` `:455-508`).

## Failure scenario

1. A machine `:app/cancel` has an `:authenticating` state that `:spawn`s the `:rf.http/managed` wrapper against a slow endpoint.
2. Dispatch `[:app/cancel [:login]]`. Then, while the request is in flight, dispatch `[:app/cancel [:cancel]]`, which destroys the wrapper actor.
3. Open the cascade. It shows:
   - TEARDOWN `:rf.http/managed#1 · 2 in-flight fxs · :explicit`;
   - two ABORT rows, both `:actor-destroyed`;
   - the header "1 child destroyed · 2 effects aborted".

Exactly one request was in flight. The doubled count also halves the effective collapse threshold (`default-collapse-threshold` 10, `:641-644`).

## Evidence

**Executed.** A bounded JVM probe (`probe_cascade.clj`, reviewer scratch dir) ran the real runtime on the plain-atom substrate: core, machines and http from the frozen tree, plus a local `HttpServer` that holds the request open. It then ran the frozen tree's `extract-cascade` over the captured buffer with `{:frame :rf/default}`.

The one `[:cancel]` dispatch emitted:

| id | Operation | frame | dispatch-id | actor | reason |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 64 | `:rf.http/aborted-on-actor-destroy` | `:rf/default` | 3 | `:rf.http/managed#1` | |
| 65 | `:rf.http/aborted` | same | same | same | `:actor-destroyed` |
| 67 | `:rf.machine/destroyed` | | | | `:explicit` |

`extract-cascade` then returned:

- `child-teardowns [{:child-id :rf.http/managed#1 :reason :explicit :inflight-count 2}]`;
- `effect-aborts` 2, with trace-ids 64 and 65, both `:cancel-cause :actor-destroyed`;
- summary "1 child destroyed · 2 effects aborted · 5ms elapsed".

In-flight requests actually aborted: 1.

**Why the tests miss it.** The fixtures at `tools/xray/test/day8/re_frame2_xray/panels/cancellation_cascade_helpers_cljs_test.cljc:87-105` model only the `aborted-on-actor-destroy` row, so no test sees the pair.

**Tracker.** A full-text export search hits 0 beads for `inflight-count`. `aborted-on-actor-destroy` hits rf2-y8doi.12, whose cascade item was the cross-FRAME fold, since fixed by rf2-y8doi.15, along with unrelated managed-fx beads. None raises the double count.

## Smallest fix

In `gather-related-aborts`, drop an `:rf.http/aborted` whose `:reason` is `:actor-destroyed` when the gathered set also holds an `:rf.http/aborted-on-actor-destroy` for the same `:actor-id` in the same drain. Both rows carry the actor and dispatch-id; the `:request-id`, when present, can refine the match.

The simpler alternative is to stop treating `:rf.http/aborted` with `:reason :actor-destroyed` as an abort row at all. It is always the transport-side echo of a registry row. Keep `:rf.http/aborted` for its other reasons, and correct the "rarer" docstring.

Add one fixture carrying the real pair.

**Fence:** `cancellation_cascade_helpers.cljc` and its test. No hot-zone file.

## Gates

The tools/xray JVM suite (`clojure -M:test` from `tools/xray`) and `npm run test:cljs` (`cancellation_cascade_helpers_cljs_test.cljc`).

## Decision needed

No.

title: template: classifier never schedules the template job for Story/Xray changes, though every scaffold's dev build compiles Story+Xray since rf2-1bkoc (stale rf2-6r9j.108 premise + negative controls)
description:
## Defect

Every generated app has compiled Story, and through Story it compiles Xray, since rf2-1bkoc (PR #9821, 2026-09-14). But the changed-surface classifier still skips the template job for Story and Xray changes, on a premise that became false that day. Its `tools/story/*|tools/xray/*` arm deliberately leaves `template_expensive` off. The comment justifying that says "no emitted file names either tool" and "`template_test.clj` FORBIDS `day8/re-frame2-xray` / `day8/re-frame2-story` in deps.edn plus ... `include-story?`", and it ends with the rule "Re-add an arm only WITH a real emitted dependency and a fixture that compiles it". Both of those now exist:

- the emitted `deps.edn` `:dev` alias carries `day8/re-frame2-story`;
- `stories.cljs` requires `re-frame.story`;
- the `:app` build's `:dev` override boots `stories/init`;
- `emitted_test_run_test.clj` compiles exactly that with `-M:shadow:dev`.

The mirror test still pins the old premise as negative controls ("Story src change does NOT arm template_expensive — the with-story variant is gone"). So a Story or Xray PR that breaks the scaffold's dev compile, or its load-time Story registration, merges green at PR time. It is caught only by the nightly `template-emitted-app` job. That breakage could be a deps-graph omission masked by the monorepo's global `:source-paths` (the rf2-r8trk class, which only a consumer-shaped compile like the scaffold's can see), a `tools/story/deps.edn` or `tools/xray/deps.edn` edit, or a Story API change that `stories.cljs` calls. This contradicts the template contract `tools/template/spec/Principles.md:210-212`: "a change that breaks the manifest, drifts the framework surface, breaks the pin lockstep, or breaks the emitted compile / boot / release fails the build".

## Where

- `.github/scripts/report-changed-surfaces.sh:2312-2330`: the `*)` sub-arm of `tools/story/*|tools/xray/*`, "rf2-6r9j.108 — deliberately NO template_expensive arm", with the stale premise and the re-add rule. The same stale premise appears at `:447` (the macros.clj note) and `:1226-1240` (the per-feature artefacts, whose rationale says the emission "requires core, the selected adapter and the view library only").
- `implementation/scripts/_changed-surfaces.test.cjs:2043-2080`: the negative controls pinning the old premise ("Xray src change does NOT arm template_expensive — not in the reduced scaffold", "Story src change does NOT arm template_expensive — the with-story variant is gone").
- Evidence that the premise is gone:
  - `tools/template/resources/day8/re_frame2_template/_reagent/stories.cljs:6` and `_uix/stories.cljs:7` require `re-frame.story`.
  - `_shared/shadow-cljs.edn:22` is the `:dev` override booting `stories/init`.
  - `_reagent/deps.edn:20` and `_uix/deps.edn:22` carry the `:dev` Story coordinate.
  - `tools/template/test/day8/re_frame2_template/template_test.clj:181-185` asserts that coordinate positively, and `:72-73` says Story is deliberately NOT in `retired-coords`.
  - `tools/story/src/re_frame/story.cljc:173` requires `re-frame.story.ui.shell` for CLJS, `tools/story/src/re_frame/story/ui/shell.cljs:64` requires `xray-embed`, and `xray_embed.cljs:57-58` requires `day8.re-frame2-xray.*`. So every scaffold dev compile compiles Xray.
- Entry point: any PR whose diff is confined to `tools/story/**` or `tools/xray/**` (non-spec), including their `deps.edn`.

## Failure scenario

A PR adds a CLJS `:require` in `tools/xray/src` of a namespace from an artefact that is on the monorepo shadow-cljs `:source-paths` but not in `tools/xray/deps.edn`, or it edits `tools/story/deps.edn`. All of Story's and Xray's own lanes compile through `implementation/shadow-cljs.edn`'s global source paths, so they stay green. The classifier reads `template_expensive=false`, so `jvm-tools-template` is not scheduled. The PR merges, and the next `clojure -M:shadow:dev ... compile app` of a freshly generated app fails, as would a newcomer's `npx shadow-cljs watch app`. The only signal is the next nightly run.

## Evidence

Executed, against the frozen tree at `034d0c8fc8`, running `bash .github/scripts/report-changed-surfaces.sh <path>` with paths (not revisions, per the CLAUDE.md classifier trap) and reading the `template_expensive` line:

- `tools/story/src/re_frame/story.cljc` → false
- `tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/core.cljs` → false
- `tools/story/deps.edn` → false
- `tools/xray/deps.edn` → false
- `implementation/fresco/src/re_frame/fresco.cljc` → false (fresco is on Xray's `:deps`)
- controls: `tools/template/src/day8/re_frame2_template/hooks.clj` → true, `implementation/core/src/re_frame/core.cljc` → true

Inspected: the rf2-6r9j.108 close reason (PR #9091) removed these arms on the premise that "today's twelve-file emission requires core, the selected adapter and the view library only" and stated "Re-add fan-out only with a real emitted dependency and a fixture proving it". The rf2-1bkoc close reason (PR #9821) re-added exactly that dependency and fixture but touched neither classifier file.

I also executed a namespace-graph check over tools/story, tools/xray and tools/machines-viz. It found that every `re-frame.*`/`day8.*` require resolves inside Story's declared deps graph today: 1393 requires, 0 missing. As a control, `implementation/ssr` measured against the same graph reported 25 missing, so the check can bite. **So nothing is broken on trunk right now.** The defect is that the one consumer-shaped Story compile is not scheduled when Story or Xray changes.

## Smallest fix

Re-add `template_expensive=true` for non-spec `tools/story/*` and `tools/xray/*` changes, which covers src, deps.edn and EDN. The arm's own rule is now satisfied. Flip the two negative controls at `_changed-surfaces.test.cjs:2063-2080` to positives, and correct the stale rationale comments at `report-changed-surfaces.sh:447`, `:1226-1240` and `:2312-2330`. The transitive artefacts Xray pulls (epoch, machines, schemas, fresco, flows, routing, resources, tools/machines-viz) have the same stale "not in the scaffold" controls. Decide whether they join, or whether their own lanes are judged enough. Files: `.github/scripts/report-changed-surfaces.sh` and `implementation/scripts/_changed-surfaces.test.cjs`. Both are **HOT ZONE**, the one-toucher pair, and they change in ONE commit.

## Gates

`node --test implementation/scripts/_changed-surfaces.test.cjs` (the mirror). Controls: run the classifier by path on a Story src file (expect true) and on a Story spec `.md` (expect false).

## Decision needed

Yes. The fix costs a ~30-minute `jvm-tools-template` run (npm ci plus Playwright) on every Story or Xray PR, and those are high-churn trees. The options are:

- (a) re-arm, as the classifier's own re-add rule says;
- (b) keep nightly-only coverage, but correct the stale comments, the negative controls and Principles P7's "fails the build" claim;
- (c) add a cheap compile-only arm: the scaffold `:app` dev compile, with no Chromium.
notes:
== DOSSIER WRITTEN 2026-09-24 04:16:31 AUSEST (analysis only — no status change, no dispatch, no edit) ==

Dossier: ai/decisions/rf2-3x7nj.37.1.template-job-for-story-xray-prs.md (ai/ is local-only and gitignored, so this path is a convenience that can rot; the findings below stand on their own). Read at trunk a3d19d9826 (= origin/main); 0 of the 62 commits since 034d0c8fc8 touch any cited path.

RECOMMENDATION: (a) re-arm template_expensive in the tools/story/*|tools/xray/* `*)` sub-arm of .github/scripts/report-changed-surfaces.sh (:2312-2330), flip the two negative controls at implementation/scripts/_changed-surfaces.test.cjs:2063 and :2072 to positives, correct the stale rationale (:447, :1226-1240, :2312-2330) and the wrong "~30-minute" figure (:1236, :2326, test :2053) — one commit, hot-zone one-toucher pair. Do not arm the transitive artefacts; say the nightly covers them.

DECISIVE FINDINGS:
1. The bead's cost basis is wrong. jvm-tools-template (test.yml:5355) measured over the last 105 completed test.yml runs: n=25 successes, median 404 s, mean 390 s, max 440 s — not ~30 minutes. On run 35879727586 the test step was 378 s of 413 s; npm ci 2 s, Playwright install 14 s. The classifier itself already records "jvm-tools-template's 5m38s" at report-changed-surfaces.sh:2245.
2. Zero wall-clock cost. Five sampled Story/Xray PR runs (#10270-#10277) spanned 1417-1497 s with "CLJS (compile every standalone example build)" at 1095-1180 s as the critical path; the template job would run beside it. Repo is public, so standard runner minutes are unbilled. 3. Premise re-verified at trunk: classifier by path reads template_expensive=false for tools/story/src/re_frame/story.cljc, tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/core.cljs, both deps.edn, and fresco.cljc (controls true: tools/template hooks.clj, core.cljc, reagent adapter). The scaffold compiles Story under :dev (_reagent/deps.edn:20, _reagent/stories.cljs:6, _shared/shadow-cljs.edn:22) and Story compiles Xray (story.cljc:173 -> shell.cljs:64 -> xray_embed.cljs:57-58). Under nightly-only a break surfaces 0-24 h after merge (cron 17 15 * * * UTC; Template emitted-app smoke green 10/10 nights since 09-14) with ~19 candidate PRs per day to bisect; the post-merge push run uses the same classifier, so it does not catch it either.

Interaction: rf2-fo4ng (P1 rename campaign) also edits the classifier pair — sequence them. rf2-3x7nj.37.2 (template README :dev) is independent.
== RULING (delegated by Mike; mayor-dispatched ruling agent, 2026-09-24 05:03:27 AUSEST) ==

RULING: (a), NARROWED. Re-arm `template_expensive=true` for exactly the paths a generated app's dev compile reads from the two tools: `tools/story/src/**`, `tools/story/deps.edn`, `tools/xray/src/**` and `tools/xray/deps.edn`. Test-only, testbed-only, spec and README changes stay off. The edit is to the hot-zone one-toucher pair `.github/scripts/report-changed-surfaces.sh` + `implementation/scripts/_changed-surfaces.test.cjs`, in ONE commit. NO workflow edit is needed: `.github/workflows/test.yml` job `jvm-tools-template` (:5355) is already gated on `needs.detect_changed_surfaces.outputs.template_expensive == 'true'` (:5358). The job key does not change, so the check-count band does not move; a skipped job is still a row.

Decision needed (the description's three options): answered, (a) narrowed. (b) nightly-only and (c) a new compile-only arm are rejected.

--- WHY ---

1. The classifier's own re-add rule is now met. Its `*)` sub-arm of `tools/story/*|tools/xray/*` (report-changed-surfaces.sh :2312-2330 at trunk 7fc78b7b72) says "Re-add an arm only WITH a real emitted dependency and a fixture that compiles it". Both exist since rf2-1bkoc (PR #9821, 2026-09-14), verified at trunk:
   - the emitted `:dev` alias carries Story: tools/template/resources/day8/re_frame2_template/_reagent/deps.edn:20, _uix/deps.edn:22;
   - the emitted stories.cljs requires `re-frame.story`: _reagent/stories.cljs:6, _uix/stories.cljs:7;
   - the `:app` dev build boots it: _shared/shadow-cljs.edn:22 `:dev {:modules {:main {:init-fn {{namespace}}.stories/init}}}`;
   - Story compiles Xray: tools/story/src/re_frame/story.cljc:173 (`#?(:cljs [re-frame.story.ui.shell ...])`), then ui/shell.cljs:64 (`re-frame.story.ui.xray-embed`), then xray_embed.cljs requiring `day8.re-frame2-xray.*`;
   - the fixture: tools/template/test/day8/re_frame2_template/emitted_test_run_test.clj:617 and :1012 run `clojure -M:shadow:dev -m shadow.cljs.devtools.cli ... compile`.
   History (Codex): the Sept 3 removal (rf2-6r9j.108, PR #9091) predates both the Story emission and its Sept 14 compile-test update, and neither later commit touched the classifier pair. It is a stale classifier, not a deliberate later trade-off.
2. It is the only consumer-shaped compile. Story's and Xray's own lanes compile through implementation/shadow-cljs.edn's global `:source-paths`, so they cannot see a namespace missing from `tools/story/deps.edn` / `tools/xray/deps.edn` (the rf2-r8trk class) or a Story API change the emitted stories.cljs calls. Only the scaffold resolves through the declared deps graph. Under nightly-only such a break merges green and surfaces 0-24 h later (cron `17 15 * * *` UTC), with about 19 Story/Xray PRs a day to bisect. The post-merge push run uses the same classifier, so it skips too. The template contract (tools/template/spec/Principles.md:210-212, "breaks the emitted compile / boot / release fails the build") holds today only at the nightly.
3. The cost basis in the bead is wrong. The job is not "~30 minutes": two independent samples agree, the dossier's n=25 successes over the last 105 test.yml runs (median 404 s, mean 390 s, max 440 s) and Codex's n=9 from 40 runs on 2026-09-23 (330-438 s, median 394 s). Setup is small: on run 35879727586 npm ci took 2 s and the Playwright install 14 s of 413 s. The classifier itself already records "jvm-tools-template's 5m38s" (:2245). The job runs beside the Story/Xray critical path, "CLJS (compile every standalone example build)", 1095-1180 s in the dossier's five sampled PR runs and 18m15s / 19m59s in Codex's two. So the expected wall-clock cost is near zero; Codex rightly notes "zero" is stronger than the evidence (queueing, cache misses and one more failure opportunity are real). Runner minutes: the repo is public, so standard hosted minutes are unbilled; it adds about 10% runner time to a Story/Xray PR.
4. Why narrowed (the dossier's full arm versus Codex's narrow one; the tree decides it). Both tool artefacts declare `:paths ["src"]` (tools/story/deps.edn:14 and tools/xray/deps.edn:20, at trunk), so the ONLY files under those trees a generated app can compile are `src/**` plus the two deps.edn files. A `test/`, `testbeds/`, `spec/` or README change cannot reach the scaffold by construction. The dossier measured the difference as 272 extra runs over 14 days for the full arm against 232 for the narrow one; the 40 saved are pure cost. The narrow arm is also the classifier's own principle: arm a lane by the generated app's ACTUAL inputs.
5. Why not (b): the edit is the same size as (a) (the same pair must be touched to correct the stale rationale and controls, plus a Principles.md rewording), and it buys only the late, bisect-heavy failure mode. Why not (c): a new classifier output plus a new test.yml job (hot zone, and it moves the merge band) to save minutes that do not sit on the critical path. Codex adds a fair qualification: the job body also runs node tests, browser interaction and advanced release builds, so a compile-only tier could save more than the 16 s of setup, but those savings are unmeasured, and the existing job's boot check catches failures a compiler cannot.

title: mcp-base: overflow replacement drops isError, so an over-cap FAILED tool call reads as a non-error overflow (both server adapters)
description:
## Defect

When a tool call FAILS and its error result is over the token cap, the overflow replacement drops the MCP `isError` flag. The agent receives an overflow marker that is byte-for-byte the shape it gets for an over-cap SUCCESS. It cannot tell that the call failed, and the marker's hint ("Re-call with narrower args, or raise `max-tokens`") invites a re-call. For a write or dispatch tool, that reads as "it worked, the reply was just big" and re-runs the side effect.

mcp-base's shared `apply-cap` hands the original result to the adapter, and the `ResultIO` docstring says why ("`original-result` is provided for implementations that need to preserve sibling slots (e.g. `:isError` flags)"). But BOTH shipped server adapters ignore it. The shared convention text, cap.md and TOKEN-BUDGETS.md, says overflow is never an error, which was written with successful calls in mind. That makes the convention mcp-base's, even though the two lines that drop the flag live in the servers.

## Where

Frozen tree `034d0c8fc8`.

The drop, one site per server:

- story-mcp: `tools/story-mcp/src/re_frame/story_mcp/tools/wire_pipeline.cljc:117-119`, where `(build-overflow-result [_ marker _original] {:content [...] :structuredContent marker})` never reads `_original`. The error path reaches it on purpose (`wire_pipeline.cljc:316-317`: "The cap applies to error results too").
- re-frame2-pair-mcp: `tools/re-frame2-pair-mcp/src/re_frame2_pair_mcp/tools/cap.cljs:140-145`, where `(build-overflow-result [_ marker _original] (wire/result marker false))` passes a literal `false`. Its own docstring (`cap.cljs:180-194`) says `apply-cap` "wraps an `:isError` result in `:rf.mcp/overflow` like any other payload" and cites deep CLJS stack traces as the reason an error can be over budget.

The shared layer that forwards the original and licenses dropping it:

- `tools/mcp-base/src/re_frame/mcp_base/cap.cljc:109-118` (protocol docstring) and `:388` (`(build-overflow-result io marker result)`, which passes the original through).
- `tools/mcp-base/spec/cap.md:127-129`: "Overflow is a budget/retry signal, not a tool-execution failure: the shipped adapters return `isError: false` or omit it."
- `tools/mcp-conformance/TOKEN-BUDGETS.md:62`: "Overflow is a successful budget signal, so `isError` remains false."

Contract text on `isError`:

- `tools/story-mcp/spec/Principles.md:163`: "`isError: true` on a tool result signals 'the tool ran and the call failed for a documented reason'".
- `tools/story-mcp/spec/001-Wire-Protocol.md:347-349` says answering `isError: true` "is what MCP §Error Handling asks for: the agent shows the failure to the LLM instead of aborting the conversation".
- `tools/re-frame2-pair-mcp/spec/003-Tool-Catalogue.md:398`: "Every `:ok? false` response is `isError: true`."

Public entry: every `tools/call` on either server whose error result exceeds the per-call cap (the default is 5000 tokens, and a caller may pass a smaller `max-tokens`).

## Failure scenario

An agent calls a story-mcp tool with a bad id and `:max-tokens 1`, or any error whose body is over the cap: a pair-mcp stack trace, a large ex-data relay. Uncapped, the reply is `isError: true`. Capped, the reply is `{:content [...] :structuredContent {:rf.mcp/overflow {...}}}` with no `isError`. That is exactly what an over-cap successful `list-stories` returns, so nothing on the wire separates the failure from a success.

## Evidence

EXECUTED: a bounded JVM probe of story-mcp end to end (`re-frame.story-mcp.tools.wire-pipeline/invoke-tool`, classpath from `tools/story-mcp` in the frozen tree, run from the scratch dir):

```
get-variant unknown id, :max-tokens 0 (CONTROL, no cap)    isError=true  overflow-marker?=false
get-variant unknown id, :max-tokens 1 (error OVER cap)     isError=nil   overflow-marker?=true
list-stories, :max-tokens 1 (success OVER cap)             isError=nil   overflow-marker?=true
```

This isolates the layer. The same mcp-base `apply-cap` over a 30,000-character `isError: true` result gives `isError=nil` with story's real `result-io` (taken from the private var). It gives `isError=true` with a control adapter that only reads `original`. So mcp-base forwards the flag and the adapter drops it.

pair-mcp: INSPECTED, not executed (CLJS; no shadow-cljs by rule). The literal `false` at `cap.cljs:145` is unconditional, and `wire/result` (`wire.cljs:170-187`) emits `:isError true` only when its second argument is truthy.

Tracker: no bead rules on over-cap FAILED calls. The live pair overflow test (`live-re-frame2-pair-overflow.cjs:192-199`) asserts `isError` false for an over-cap SUCCESS only. The story-mcp review (rf2-3x7nj.34) recorded this item and deferred it here as a shared convention. Pair's response cache is unaffected, because the cache step runs before the cap and already bypasses `isError` results.

## Smallest fix

Carry the original flag across the replacement in both adapters:

- story: `(cond-> {...} (true? (:isError original)) (assoc :isError true))`.
- pair: `(wire/result marker (true? (j/get original :isError)))`.

Then correct the convention sentence in `tools/mcp-base/spec/cap.md:127-129` and `tools/mcp-conformance/TOKEN-BUDGETS.md:62` to read that overflow of a SUCCESS stays non-error and overflow of a FAILURE keeps `isError: true`. Tighten the `cap.cljc:109-118` docstring to say adapters MUST carry `isError` across. The marker body is unchanged, and `assertIsErrorMatchesOk` is unaffected because the marker has no `:ok?`.

Fence:

- `tools/story-mcp/src/re_frame/story_mcp/tools/wire_pipeline.cljc`
- `tools/re-frame2-pair-mcp/src/re_frame2_pair_mcp/tools/cap.cljs`
- `tools/mcp-base/src/re_frame/mcp_base/cap.cljc` (docstring only)
- `tools/mcp-base/spec/cap.md`
- `tools/mcp-conformance/TOKEN-BUDGETS.md`
- one regression test per server

No hot-zone file.

## Gates

- story half: `clojure -M:test` in `tools/story-mcp` (JVM; add an over-cap error case beside the existing overflow cases in `tools_test.clj`).
- pair half: `cap.cljs` is CLJS, graded only by the shadow-cljs lane (pair-mcp's CLJS tests, e.g. `wire_cap_test.cljs`; machine-wide exclusive). A JVM green says nothing about it, so declare reliance on CI or take the lane.
- mcp-base: docstring and spec only; no behaviour change there.

## Decision needed

No, if TOKEN-BUDGETS.md's "isError remains false" is read as covering over-cap SUCCESSES (the recommended reading). If Mike reads it as deliberately covering failed calls too, the alternative is to keep `isError` false and add an error indicator inside the marker body instead.

title: xray-shell-views: edn-inspector zoom into a list/seq element (or a stale path) shows the whole root under breadcrumbs that claim the zoom
description:
## Defect

When the zoom path cannot be resolved, the EDN inspector renders the WHOLE root value under breadcrumbs that still claim the zoom. Two ways reach that state. The ordinary one is zooming into any container that is an element of a list or lazy seq. `children-of` keys those children by integer index, but `resolve-zoom-into` walks the stored path with `get-in`, and `get` on a CLJS `List`, `IndexedSeq` or `LazySeq` answers not-found. The other is the documented stale-path fallback, where the zoomed key is dissoc'ed while zoomed. In both cases `render-inspector` keeps `zoom-active?` true, keeps `zoom-path-prefix` as the unresolvable path, and paints the breadcrumb row, `data-rf-zoomed "1"` and `data-rf-zoom-path` above a body that is the un-zoomed root. Every further double-click in that body then dispatches `(into zoom-path-prefix path)`, which is a meaningless absolute path, so the breadcrumb keeps growing while the body never moves.

## Where

Frozen tree `034d0c8fc8`:

- `tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/views/edn_inspector.cljs:505-520`: `resolve-zoom-into` uses `(get-in value path ::no-resolve)` and falls back to the whole value.
- `…/edn_inspector.cljs:1537-1538`: list and seq children are keyed `[i x]`, which is the zoom path segment.
- `…/edn_inspector.cljs:3358-3365`: every non-root, non-empty container gets `zoom-trigger-attrs` with `:absolute-path (into zoom-path-prefix path)`.
- `…/edn_inspector.cljs:4865-4883`: `zoom-active?` depends only on the stored path being non-empty, never on whether it resolved. `zoom-path-prefix` stays the stored path.
- `…/edn_inspector.cljs:4947-4954` (breadcrumbs), `:4999-5001` and `:5048-5050` (`data-rf-zoomed` / `data-rf-zoom-path`).
- Public entry: App-DB mounts with `:zoomable? true` (`panels/app_db_diff_state.cljs:408`), and so does Epoch (`panels/epoch/view.cljs:2149`, `:4357`, `:4664`).
- Contract: `tools/xray/spec/021-Dynamic-Panel-Designs.md:4974` says "Every non-empty non-root container is a double-click / Enter zoom target". `:5091-5093` says "the zoom IS the new root". `:5085-5086` says a stale path "falls back to the full value", which is silent on the breadcrumbs.

## Failure scenario

The app-db is `{:todos (list {:id 1 :title "a"} {:id 2 :title "b"})}`, as produced by `conj` onto a list, `sort-by`, `map` or `filter`. In App-DB, double-click the second todo map. The zoom slot stores `[:todos 1]`. The next render shows the breadcrumb `<header> › :todos › 1` with the whole app-db root beneath it. Double-clicking `:todos` in that body stores `[:todos 1 :todos]`, and the breadcrumb reads `› :todos › 1 › :todos` over the same root. The same shape appears when a zoomed-into key is removed by a later event.

## Evidence

title: mcp-conformance: live replace-app-db two-arity arm re-injects the one-arity payload verbatim, so a frame-targeted call that commits nothing still passes
description:
## Defect

The frame-targeted (two-arity) arm of the live `replace-app-db` gate injects the byte-identical payload that the one-arity arm has already committed. It reads back the same two slots, and nothing resets app-db between the arms. A second call that commits nothing therefore still reads back `[inc 41]` and `js/window`, the first arm's values, and the arm passes. The source says the opposite. The comment above the second payload reads "A DIFFERENT expression on the second arm, so a stale read of the one-arity injection cannot pass for the frame-targeted one", and the expression it introduces is identical. It has been identical since the file landed (`e051e9f493`). A `pr-str` regression on the two-arity path would still be caught, because it would overwrite the slots with `42` and `#object[Window]`. What the arm cannot see is a two-arity call that answers `:ok? true` without writing to the operating frame. The arm also never reads the `:frame` the tool reports back.

## Where

Frozen tree `034d0c8fc8`, `tools/mcp-conformance/test/live-re-frame2-pair-replace-app-db.cjs`:

- `:104-105`: `PAYLOAD_DB = '{:count 5 ' + EXPR_KEY + ' (inc 41) ' + SYM_KEY + ' js/window}'`
- `:280-283`: the "A DIFFERENT expression" comment, then `frameDb` spelled identically.
- `:284-308`: the two-arity call, then `get-path` on the same `EXPR_KEY` / `SYM_KEY` with the same assertions. There is no reset or clear between `:255` and `:284`.
- The server side is `tools/re-frame2-pair-mcp/src/re_frame2_pair_mcp/tools/replace_app_db.cljs:110-112`, where the two arities split: `(ef/rt-call 'app-db-reset! (ef/rt-quote new-db) frame)`.

Public entry: the hermetic live suite (`scripts/live-test-inventory.cjs` row 7), which runs in the per-PR `mcp-conformance-re-frame2-pair` job in `.github/workflows/test.yml` (surface `mcp_live`), in the nightly `mcp-live` jobs in `expensive-tests.yml`, and under `npm --prefix implementation run test:mcp-conformance -- --live`.

## Failure scenario

1. A regression in the frame-targeted path makes `replace-app-db {db frame}` return success without committing to the frame that `get-path` reads. For example, `args/->frame-keyword` coerces the id to a different keyword, or the runtime's two-arity `app-db-reset!` resets some other frame and returns `{:ok? true :frame <other>}`. Frame-arg coercion is exactly the class the pair slice is reporting (rf2-3x7nj.32.2).
2. Arm 1 has already left `:rf2-olqo/expr [inc 41]` and `:rf2-olqo/who js/window` in the operating frame.
3. Arm 2's `callOrThrow` sees no `isError`. `get-path` returns arm 1's values, `assertQuotedDatumSurvived` and `assertQuotedSymbolSurvived` pass, and the test prints `...survives as DATA (not 42) — two-arity` and its GREEN sentinel.
4. The frame-targeted write path is certified with no evidence that it wrote anything. The rf2-olqo close reason relies on this arm for its "holds ... on BOTH arities" claim.

## Evidence

EXECUTED: a read-only Node probe (scratch, no `require` of the test) evaluated both expressions exactly as the source spells them. Both are `"{:count 5 :rf2-olqo/expr (inc 41) :rf2-olqo/who js/window}"`, `identical = true`. Control: the same probe reports `EXPR_KEY === SYM_KEY` as `false`, so it can see a difference. It also confirms the "A DIFFERENT expression on the second arm" comment is present.

INSPECTED: `git log -S"const frameDb"` shows the payload identical from the file's first commit, `e051e9f493`. The rf2-olqo notes and close reason have no ruling on this; their records for "frameDb" and "DIFFERENT" both read 0.

## Smallest fix

Give arm 2 values that arm 1 cannot have left behind, for example `(inc 99)` beside a different symbol such as `js/document`. Assert those, keeping the `:value 100` negative as the evaluation control. Alternatively, restore `FIXTURE_BOOT_DB` between the arms so that a no-op two-arity call reads back an absent slot. Optionally also assert that the tool's returned `:frame` equals `frameId`.

Fence: `tools/mcp-conformance/test/live-re-frame2-pair-replace-app-db.cjs` only. No hot-zone file.

## Gates

The hermetic live suite only. It enters the shadow-cljs build lane (machine-wide exclusive) plus Chromium: `npm --prefix implementation run test:mcp-conformance -- --live`, or rely on CI's per-PR `mcp-conformance-re-frame2-pair` job (armed by the `mcp_live` surface). No unit lane covers this file, because it SKIPs without `SHADOW_CLJS_NREPL_PORT`.

## Decision needed

No.

Completeness: Raw get-variant guidance, accepted registration slots/predicate exception/tags, real hermetic verdict coverage, and distinct frame-targeted replace-app-db payload all match the three sources.
