title: xray-domain-panels-b: reactive flow graph keys nodes by registration id, so list instances share React keys and every edge lands on the last instance
description:
## Defect

The Reactive panel's flow graph identifies nodes by REGISTRATION id, but it is fed one row per INSTANCE. `project-record` emits:

- one sub row per concrete run, so `[:todo/by-id 1]`, `[:todo/by-id 2]` and `[:todo/by-id 3]` are three rows that all carry `:sub-id :todo/by-id`;
- one view row per `:rf.view/rendered` op, so three `:app/todo-row` instances are three rows.

`layout` then builds each node's `:slug`, which is also its React `:key`, from the id alone, and it indexes nodes for edge routing with `(into {} (map (juxt :id identity)) ...)`. That keeps only the LAST node per id. In the canonical list shape, where N instances of one view each read their own cell of one parametric sub:

- the graph renders N sibling `<g>` elements with the SAME React key;
- every sub-to-view edge, and every input-to-Level-2 edge, lands on the last instance's box;
- the other N-1 view nodes float with no incoming edge;
- which sub instance drove which view instance, which is the graph's whole purpose, is lost.

The panel's own Subs-skipped slice already keys identity by concrete `:query-v` (rf2-cj2yx). The graph was never brought into line.

## Where

All cites are at `034d0c8fc8`.

- `tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/panels/reactive_flow_graph.cljc`:
  - lines 88-91: `slug`;
  - lines 102-126: `col-nodes`, where `:id sid` and `:slug (slug sid)` come from `(:sub-id row)`;
  - lines 127-150: `view-nodes`, where `:slug (slug vid)` comes from `(:view-id row)`;
  - lines 207-208: `sub-by-id` and `view-by-id` are `(into {} (map (juxt :id identity)) ...)`;
  - lines 221-240: the `sub-sub-edges` and `sub-view-edges` lookups.
- `tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/panels/reactive_panel_view.cljs`: lines 325-336 (`sub-node`, `:key slug` at 336) and 361-390 (`view-node`, `:key slug` at 390).
- `tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/panels/reactive_panel_subs.cljs`:
  - lines 576-632: `project-record`, where `ran` is every `:sub-runs` row, not de-duplicated;
  - lines 446-500: `partition-subs-by-level`, one row per run;
  - lines 233-290: `view-rows`, one row per `:rf.view/rendered` op, which carries `:render-key` but `layout` never reads it.
- Public entry: the Reactive panel's REACTIVE FLOW graph, on any epoch that re-renders a list of one view over a parametric sub.

## Failure scenario

1. A todo list renders `[:app/todo-row id]` for ids 1-3, and each row derefs `[:todo/by-id id]`.
2. The list's first load mounts all three rows, or `[:todos/toggle-all]` changes every cell. Either way, all three row instances render in one epoch.
3. The epoch carries three `:sub-runs` rows for `:todo/by-id` (one per query-v) and three `:rf.view/rendered` rows for `:app/todo-row`.
4. The graph draws three `:todo/by-id` nodes and three `:app/todo-row` nodes, labelled identically.
5. All three sub-to-view edges terminate on the THIRD view box. Views 1 and 2 have no incoming edge, so they read as re-rendered for no reason.
6. React receives three siblings keyed `_app_todo_row` and three keyed `_todo_by_id`.

The single-toggle case (only row 1 re-renders) still draws three identically keyed sub nodes, all wired into the one view box. The edges do not depend on the `changed?` flags, which the probe below sets to one true and two false.

## Evidence

`layout` (`.cljc`) was **executed** in a bounded JVM probe with the row shape above:

```
l1 node slugs (React keys): [_todo_by_id _todo_by_id _todo_by_id]
view node slugs (React keys): [_app_todo_row _app_todo_row _app_todo_row]
view node y positions: [16.0 70.0 124.0]
sub->view edges (to-id, target y2, changed?): [[:app/todo-row 144.0 true] [:app/todo-row 144.0 false] [:app/todo-row 144.0 false]]
view nodes receiving an edge (by centre y): #{144.0}
distinct view-node centres: [36.0 90.0 144.0]
--- control: distinct view ids route one edge each
slugs: [_v_one _v_two] edges to: [[:v/one 36.0] [:v/two 90.0]]
```

The following were **inspected**, not executed, because the CLJS lanes are out of bounds for this review:

- `project-record`, `partition-subs-by-level` and `view-rows` really do produce one row per instance (read at the lines above; `.cljs`);
- what React does with duplicate sibling keys (a dev console warning, and possible reuse of the wrong child on reorder).

Spec: `tools/xray/spec/021-Dynamic-Panel-Designs.md` §3.2 (lines 552-567) says "**Views** ... each tagged re-rendered + *why*" and "a sub with edges to two or more views is shared; the topology (two edges) carries the 'one sub drives N views' fact". With the collapse, the topology is wrong.

## Smallest fix

Give each node an instance identity. That is:

- `(or (:query-v row) [(:sub-id row)])` for sub nodes;
- `(or (:render-key row) [view-id i])` for view nodes.

Use it for `:slug`/`:key` and for the `*-by-id` indexes. Route edges by instance: a sub instance goes to the views whose `:rf.view/deref-subs` contain its query-v, falling back to the registration id only when the query-v is absent. Labels can carry the query-v arg so instances are distinguishable.

- Fence: `reactive_flow_graph.cljc`, `reactive_panel_view.cljs` (keys only), and possibly the `sub-readers` shape in `reactive_panel_subs.cljs`, plus tests.
- No hot-zone file.

## Gates

- `reactive_flow_graph.cljc` has no reader conditional at these lines, so the `tools/xray` JVM suite grades it (`clojure -M:test`, `scripts/test-jvm-tools.sh`).
- The `.cljs` key and readers changes are graded only by `npm run test:cljs`, plus the browser lane for any dom test on the graph.

## Decision needed

No.
notes:
## Fixed in PR #10332 (worker xpanels-3x7nj, 2026-09-24)

Reproduced at trunk 982fb2ce41 (JVM probe on layout): three :todo/by-id instances and three :app/todo-row instances all keyed _todo_by_id / _app_todo_row; all three sub->view edges ended at y 144.0 (the last view box).

Fix: reactive_flow_graph.cljc gives every node an :instance identity (query-v for a sub, render-key or [view-id i] for a view); the React :key is that identity (a repeat gets an occurrence suffix, so sibling keys are unique by construction). Edges route per instance: a sub instance goes to the view instances whose own :deref-subs hold its query-v; a Level-2 input edge starts at the instance its declared input query-v names; a row with no query-v falls back to the registration-level :readers. :id / :slug / testids stay registration-based (existing selectors unchanged); an instance with args is labelled by its query-v. reactive_panel_subs.cljs carries :query-v on sub rows, :input-query-vs on :static L2 rows and :deref-subs on view rows; reactive_panel_view.cljs changes only the :key attribute. Spec 021 §3.2 updated. After the fix the probe reads keys [[:todo/by-id 1] ...] and edges ending at 36.0 / 90.0 / 144.0, one per box.

Control: with the fix removed, layout-instances-carry-distinct-keys, layout-routes-each-sub-instance-to-its-own-view-instance and layout-level-2-edge-starts-at-the-declared-input-instance went red (JVM). The producer-derived project-record -> layout test and the view key test are CLJS, graded by CI only.
Merged-PR audit #10332 (78e6cc1baf60796452734b92ebc638b7a1e688a2; merged 2026-09-24T01:24:15Z). Completeness: All four domain-panel fixes match their sources: before-only whole instances/areas/top removals survive projection and use the inspector removed-root marker; graph keys/edges carry concrete query/render identities; severity stage follows namespaced stage or preceding non-severity chronology; equal rebuilt leaves produce no modified row. Both spec pages align. Correctness: Accepted JVM Xray 1413 tests/6945 assertions, 30 planted-control failures, node 12717/64074 with exactly the new 14 tests/63 assertions, and CI 38 successes. Read projection-to-view wiring and focused removed-ghost/key/edge/stage/equality regressions. No rerun or concrete residual found. Implementation quality: Reuses the shared inspector absence marker and diff engine; instance identity travels through existing rows rather than adding a new graph abstraction. Stage calculation remains a small fire-order fold; structural sharing short-circuits before leaf value comparison. Actionable findings: none. Existing finding updates: none.

title: examples-real-apps: realworld_resources README:13 pitch calls [:article-list] 'global' — the viewer-scoped wording rf2-m16m2 corrected in the skill leaf, missed by its census
description:
## Defect

The resources example's opening pitch, its most-read sentence, teaches the invalidation scope the example exists to warn against: "One favourite makes `[:article slug]`, the global `[:article-list]`, and `[:feed]` (your private, personalised feed) stale."

In the code, the `[:article-list]` tag rides the VIEWER-scoped list reads, and the favourite invalidates it under `{:from-db :realworld/viewer}`. Nothing about it is global. `[:article-list]` is also not only the Global Feed: the tag-filtered lists carry the same tag.

rf2-m16m2 corrected this exact wording in the shipped skill leaf ("stales global article tags", changed to "stales the viewer-scoped article tags", `skills/re-frame2/patterns/resources-mutations.md:197`). Its close reason records a census "for the false claim elsewhere: not repeated anywhere". That census missed this sentence.

The README's own scope table (`:30-42`) defines "global" as the scope column's `:rf.scope/global`, reserved for the popular tags alone. So a reader moving from `:13` to the table reads a contradiction.

## Where

- `examples/real-apps/realworld_resources/README.md:13`.
- Code:
  - `examples/real-apps/realworld_resources/resources.cljs:124` (`:scope {:from-db :realworld/viewer}` on `:realworld/articles`) and `:128-131` (its `:tags` fn adds `[:article-list]`);
  - `examples/real-apps/realworld_resources/mutations.cljs:156-161` (`fav-invalidates`, `{:scope {:from-db :realworld/viewer} :tags #{[:article slug] [:article-list] ...}}`).
- README contrast: `:39` (only `:realworld/tags` is **global**) and `:42` ("Only the popular tags are truly the same for everyone (global)"). Also `:56`, the favourite row: "invalidates the viewer-scoped article tags".

## Failure scenario

INSPECTED. A reader copies the pitch's shape and declares the article lists `:rf.scope/global`. That is the leak boundary the README's scope section (`:42`, `:99`) and the skill leaf's callout say not to cross: the lists carry the viewer-relative `favorited` flag.

## Evidence

- A census of `global` in `realworld_resources/README.md` finds 9 lines. `:13` is the only one that attaches "global" to an article or list cache tag. `:39`, `:42`, `:99` and `:165` use it for the tags read or the scope term, and `:145` and `:217` for the UI's "global list" (Global Feed) with no tag named.
- The rf2-m16m2 close reason is quoted above.

## Smallest fix

`README.md:13`: "the global `[:article-list]`" becomes "the viewer-scoped `[:article-list]`" (or "every list's `[:article-list]`"). One word in one file. No hot-zone file.

## Gates

None that grades it. The README carries links on other lines, but this edit changes no link or anchor. `check_readme_links.py --ci` and `check_doc_slugs.py` inspect targets and anchors only, so a green from either says nothing about this sentence. The worker verifies by reading and says so in the PR body.

## Decision needed

No. Already ruled under rf2-m16m2 for the identical wording in the skill leaf.

title: ssr: the hydration payload is the egress projection, so :rf/hydrate installs :large size markers (data destroyed) and :rf/redacted into live client state; spec 015's promised SSR allow-through door does not exist
description:
## Defect

The SSR hydration payload is built with the egress projection (the one meant for off-box tools), and `:rf/hydrate` installs that projection into the client's LIVE app-db. So any app that server-renders a classified field gets a projection artefact as live client state:

- `:large` fields are DESTROYED. A `[1 2 3]` list arrives in the client as a `#:rf.size{:large-elided ...}` marker map instead of the data. The SSR projection sets `include-large? false` (`implementation/ssr/src/.../projection.cljc:154-157`). Size elision exists to protect tool token budgets, not the hydration wire, yet here it removes data the page needs.
- `:sensitive` fields become the keyword `:rf/redacted` in live state. That covers a password the browser types, and a server-held CSRF token the client needs to send back.
- On the hiccup tier the server renders the RAW value into the HTML while the payload carries `:rf/redacted`. So the client's first render hashes differently, and a hydration mismatch is reported on a correct app. On the Fresco tier both halves print "redacted", so nothing is reported. That is how the Fresco login example (rf2-3x7nj.43.1) shipped unnoticed.
- `hydrate!` runs its mismatch check immediately after `:rf/hydrate` (`boot.cljc:163-172`). So on the hiccup tier there is nowhere to run Spec 011's own advice ("apps that want client-only seeded state run it after the hydration event", spec/011-SSR.md:1874) before the check fires.

The spec text does not match the code either:
- spec/015 at line 404, EP-0015 §14 and the how-to guide promise a way for SSR policy to let a classified field through. No such door exists: `include-sensitive` / `include-large` match 0 times across the ssr, ssr-ring and fresco sources, against 17 matches for `project-app-db-egress` there.
- spec/011 says the payload carries elision declarations; the code leaves them out.
- spec/015 and Privacy.md teach an `:include-app-db` spelling that exists nowhere in the code.

## Evidence

EXECUTED at trunk a3d19d9826: two bounded JVM probes by the rf2-3x7nj.43.1 dossier agent (scratchpad `decisions-sep23/rf2-3x7nj.43.1-probe/`, out.txt and out2.txt). Probe 1, the real payload build and `:rf/hydrate`:

    SERVER-LIVE-DB       {:auth {:draft {:email "", :password ""}}, :session {:csrf "csrf-abc-123", :user "alice"}, :catalog {:items [1 2 3], :title "Shop"}}
    CLIENT-POST-HYDRATE  {:auth {:draft {:email "", :password :rf/redacted}}, :session {:csrf :rf/redacted, :user "alice"}, :catalog {:items #:rf.size{:large-elided {... :bytes 7, :type :vector ...}}, :title "Shop"}}
    ITEMS-COUNT-OR-NIL   nil
    UNCLASSIFIED-SIBLING "alice" "Shop"                <- control: unclassified leaves survive intact

Probe 2, the hiccup tier:

    SERVER-HTML   ... <input type="hidden" name="csrf" value="csrf-abc-123"> ...
    CLIENT-RESOLVED ... [:input {:type "hidden", :name "csrf", :value :rf/redacted}] ...
    SERVER-HASH 6a1aa453   CLIENT-HASH 68e5f961   HASHES-EQUAL false

## Where

- implementation/ssr/src (payload build through the egress projection; `projection.cljc:154-157` profile with `include-large? false`)
- implementation/ssr boot `hydrate!` (`boot.cljc:163-172`, mismatch check immediately after `:rf/hydrate`)
- spec/011-SSR.md (hydration payload contract), spec/015-Data-Classification.md:404, EP-0015 §14, Privacy.md

## Smallest fix

The `:large` half looks like a plain bug: the hydration payload should not apply size elision at all, since the wire to your own client is not a tool budget. The `:sensitive` half and the promised allow-through door are the decision below. The example-local fix for the Fresco login (rf2-3x7nj.43.1, option a) stands whatever is ruled here.

## Gates

`implementation/ssr` JVM tests. Add a RED case, a `:large` vector surviving hydration intact, with an unclassified sibling as the control. `npm run test:cljs` for any `#?(:cljs …)` hydrate path. Several hot-zone files would move: spec/011 is not hot-zone, but spec/Spec-Schemas.md (payload schema) and spec/009 (egress profile table) may be. Sequence behind rf2-3x7nj.13.3, which edits `build-payload`, and rf2-3x7nj.32.6, which edits the same egress profile table.

## Decision needed

Yes, one choice for the `:sensitive` half. (A) Implement the allow-through door that spec 015:404 and EP-0015 §14 promise: SSR policy names classified fields the hydrating client may receive raw, for example a CSRF token. (B) Remove the promise, rule that `:sensitive` never crosses the hydration wire, and document that the client must re-seed such fields after hydration. Under (B), also give `hydrate!` a seam that runs before its mismatch check, or the hiccup tier cannot follow that advice. The `:large` half and the spec-text drift need no decision.

Discovered from rf2-3x7nj.43.1 (its dossier ai/decisions/rf2-3x7nj.43.1.hydrated-sentinel-example-or-framework.md, local-only, recommends this as a separate bead). Related: rf2-3x7nj.40.1, a sibling SSR example that ships raw runtime-db.

== RULING (mayor's ruling agent, 2026-09-24 13:19:33 AUSEST, under the project stance; dossier + Codex Recommendation weighed) ==

Read at trunk 4c70b35a41 (= origin/main). Codex reviewed at 42c7524b9c; the only SSR-area commit since is d5d985706f (rf2-w1hd8, hiccup javascript: URLs), which touches none of the sites cited here.

QUESTION: may a :sensitive app-db value reach the hydrating browser raw? (A) build the promised per-path SSR permit, or (B) withdraw the promise so :sensitive never crosses and the client re-seeds. The :large half and the spec drift need no decision.

OPTIONS AND SIZES
- (A) Permit list. One optional host opt beside :payload, naming concrete app-db paths whose raw value may cross. The default stays redact. Size: a ~15-line helper in payload_policy.cljc, threaded through five call sites. Prose goes in spec/011, spec/015, Privacy.md and two docs pages, plus one clause in spec/009 (hot-zone). No walker change, no API.md row.
- (B) Withdraw. Drop "unless SSR policy explicitly permits it" (spec/015:404, how-to :343) and document the re-seed. Server-originated values the client needs (a CSRF token for fetch calls, the user's own email) then have NO framework route: out-of-band <meta> plus a cofx, or a refetch. It cannot make the hiccup tier agree for a rendered server-originated value (measured below). A new seam would move the spec/API.md hydrate! row, or API.md plus both manifest files (all hot-zone).
- (C) Flip include-sensitive? on the :rf.egress/ssr-hydration row. Least code, but it silently reopens the nested-server-secret leak f3e8ca1953 (rf2-bt9kct) closed. It contradicts spec/011 "no fail-OPEN default at a security boundary", and flips the conformance fixture and ~16 pinned files. A whole-host boolean is (C) scoped to one host, with the same silent-leak property. A dev warning when a sentinel is installed would nag correct apps (also rejected in rf2-3x7nj.43.1's ruling).

RULING: (A). Land the :large fix FIRST as its own commit, and fix the spec drift alongside. Five specifics settle what the reviews left open:
1. A permit restores the raw value at its exact path, and NEVER pierces a classified ancestor (semantics (a)-(f) in the brief).
2. The permit covers app-db only. Route :query and machine :data stay projected.
3. There is one shared rule: a 3-arity project-app-db-egress. Every hydration call site AND the sidecar render-state pass the same host permit.
4. No new hydrate! seam. Document the existing split.
5. The in-heap render tiers are NOT a separate defect (see ALSO RULED).

WHY
- Both reviews chose (A), and I agree. Classification ("keep it out of Datadog and the tools") and browser entitlement ("may this user's browser hold it") are different decisions. Only the app knows the second, and it knows it at the host, which already makes the privacy decision.
  - A CSRF synchronizer token is the counterexample to "sensitive means server-only". Codex cites OWASP: the server generates it, delivers it in HTML or JSON, and the client returns it in a form or AJAX call, while it stays out of logs.
  - The redact default keeps the one real threat closed: a server secret nested inside an allowlisted top-level key. :payload takes top-level keys only (select-keys).
- (B) makes classification and SSR mutually exclusive for user-owned data, and cannot repair the hiccup tier (measured). The stance's "low friction" argues against it. (C) fails open silently.
- AGREED WITH CODEX, OVERRULING THE DOSSIER:
  - (i) The splice is not an unconditional assoc-in. Its edges must be defined.
  - (ii) The sequencing behind rf2-3x7nj.13.3 and .32.6 is stale; both are CLOSED. 13.3 merged as PR #10298, and check-portable-numbers! is live in build-payload. 32.6 merged as PR #10308, and 0d9c23f154 is in projection.cljc's history.

The direct Fresco server render (fresco/server.cljs) renders the LIVE frame (element + renderToString, ~:400-408), then projects the payload separately (:417-428). So the permit must reach both the payload and the render-state.
- OVERRULING CODEX: "reconstruct only an explicitly permitted branch where necessary". I rule it is never necessary: a permit does not pierce a classified ancestor.

  - It would have to tell a classified-ancestor sentinel apart from the fail-closed dead-frame whole-slice sentinel, which must stay closed.

description:
## Gap (stale claims in `spec/005-StateMachines.md` at trunk `fe8de195bd`, measured against `xstate@6.0.0-alpha.59`)

Four claims are stale, three of them wrong about what XState v6 now does and one a dated re-validation stamp. Four more are v5 spellings that v6 renamed; they are listed at the end as optional refreshes and are NOT counted in the title.

1. **Line 2178** (§DIVERGENCE from XState — a Clojure set, NOT an array). Says: "XState v6's `internalEvents` is an **array** … alpha-drift-confirmed against XState v6 alpha.3". Measured: since `6.0.0-alpha.42` the canonical declaration is `schemas.internalEvents`, a **map** keyed by event type with a payload schema per key and wildcard keys allowed (`'progress.*'`); the alpha.1 top-level array "remains supported for migration" and the v6 docs (`xstate-v5-to-v6.md` §12, glossary "Internal event") call it deprecated. Probe `xs/D-2-semantics.mjs` §B: a map with `tick` and `'progress.*'` — an external `progress.chunk` and an external `tick` are both rejected (`reason: 'internalEvent'`), an internal raise of `progress.chunk` is handled. Corrected wording: "XState v6 declares internal events as a `schemas.internalEvents` **map** keyed by event type (a payload schema per key; wildcard keys such as `'progress.*'` are accepted; the alpha.1 top-level array survives only as a deprecated migration form). re-frame2 declares them as a Clojure **set** — `:internal-events #{:tick}` …". Keep the rest of the paragraph; the boundary semantics below it (refuse, no state change, error trace) match v6's alpha.50 reject-and-report exactly (probe `xs/D-2-semantics.mjs` §A vs `jvm/D/D-j1-dispatch.clj` §a).

2. **Line 4661** (§Parity re-validation). Says: "Re-validated 2026-09-07 against `6.0.0-alpha.52` … `latest` = `5.32.6` … the v6 line has 52 alphas". Measured 2026-09-24 with `npm view xstate dist-tags` from the scratch install: `latest` = `5.33.2`, `beta` = `5.0.0-beta.54`, `alpha` = `6.0.0-alpha.59`; the `next`-branch changelog carries `## 6.0.0-alpha.0` through `## 6.0.0-alpha.59` (60 entries) and no stable v6. Corrected: re-stamp the paragraph to alpha.59 / 5.33.2 and add one sentence recording that this re-validation was EXECUTED (the package installed and driven through `transition` / `getMicrosteps` / `createActor`, paired with JVM probes) rather than read off the changelog — the four numbered points below it were all re-confirmed by execution (point 1: `xs/D-4b-entry-order.mjs` pure effect list; point 2: spec text unchanged, `alpha.17` still the correction; point 3: `xs/D-2-semantics.mjs` §D/§D2 guard-blocked exact falls to `mouse.*`; point 4: §D4 unhandled event stays `active`).

3. **Line 457** (§Guards, "No combinator data form (divergence from XState v5)"). Says: "XState ships higher-order guard combinators — `and([...])`, `or([...])`, `not(...)`, `stateIn(...)` (from `xstate/guards`)". Measured: v6 REMOVED all four at `6.0.0-alpha.1` ("the guard creators `and`, `or`, `not`, `stateIn`" in the removed-exports list; `xstate-v5-to-v6.md` §2 and §16), composition is plain JS inside the transition function, and `checkStateIn(snapshot, …)` is the exported replacement for `stateIn`. The paragraph presents as a divergence what is now a convergence. Corrected heading and first sentence: "**No combinator data form (divergence from XState v5; convergence with v6).** XState v5 shipped higher-order guard combinators … ; v6 removed them — composition is plain code inside one function, which is exactly re-frame2's rule, and v5's `stateIn` became the `checkStateIn(snapshot, …)` helper."

4. **Line 1790** (§Cross-region coordination — tags as `stateIn`). Says: "`stateIn(stateValue)` (XState v5, from `xstate/guards`; v4 `in: '#someState'`)". Measured: v6 spells it `checkStateIn(self.getSnapshot(), 'a.b')` (exported from `xstate`; `xstate-v5-to-v6.md` §2, cheatsheet §Guards). Corrected: add "; v6 `checkStateIn(snapshot, …)`" to the parenthetical so a v6 reader recognises the primitive.

Optional v5-spelling refreshes (not counted; do them if the file is open anyway): line 308 "XState v5's partial (prefix) event descriptor `mouse.*`" — v6 keeps it (`'pointer.*'`; probe `xs/D-2-semantics.mjs` §D3 shows `a.*` still matches `a.b.c`), so "XState's (v5 and v6)"; line 782 "XState-v5 parity — no `assign` to reorder" — v6 removed `assign` outright, context is the function's return, so the property holds there by construction; line 2035 "XState v5 **throws** on a non-converging eventless / `raise` cycle" — still true in v6 and now measured: `Error: Microstep count exceeded 1000` thrown from `createActor(...).start()` (probe `xs/D-2b-unbounded-loop.mjs`) against re-frame2's `:rf.error/machine-always-depth-exceeded` at depth 16 (`jvm/D/D-j1-dispatch.clj` §d); line 3129 "XState v5's `const ref = spawn(child)` captured into `context`" — v6 spells it `enq.spawn(...)` returning a ref that can be returned inside `context`. The five "verified against `xstate@6.0.0-alpha.52`" stamps (lines 780, 1560, 1732, 1769, 2021) can all move to alpha.59: each was re-executed (lines 1560/2021: `xs/D-2-semantics.mjs` §D, §E — always settles before the raise, microsteps `b → c → fromC`; line 780: `xs/D-4b-entry-order.mjs`).

title: story: a recorded timer child's replay wait can come out 1ms short of its scheduled delay ([:wait 79] for an 80ms timer), flaking the node lane
description:
## Defect

A recorded replay script can wait LESS than the timer it replays, so the replay checks app-db before the timer child has run. The result is an intermittent `:fail`, which makes the node lane flaky for EVERY PR.

**Observed** (worker ptcore2-tv5ac, CI on PR #10368, job `CLJS (shadow-cljs :node-test)`; that PR changes only comments in implementation/core and cannot reach this path):
- Failing test: `recorded-dispatch-later-child-runs-once-on-replay` in `tools/story/test/re_frame/story/recorder_timer_child_cljs_test.cljs`. It was 1 failure of 12,784 tests.
- The test's child timer fires 80ms after the root event.
- The exported replay script recorded the gap as `[:wait 79]`, so the replay's check ran 1ms before the child could have fired.
- The replay returned `:fail` where the test expects `:pass`.

**Where it comes from:** the recorder's timer-child wait computation, last changed today by rf2-mcjdg: PR #10349, trunk `52119f573f`, "a recorded timer child's wait runs from where the replay has reached, so a short-gap event cannot shorten it". A measured wall-clock gap can come out one millisecond under the scheduled delay, through truncation or through where the two timestamps are taken.

## Required correction

The recorded wait for a timer child must never be shorter than the delay the child was scheduled with.
- Prefer deriving it from the scheduled delay the recorder already knows (the `:dispatch-later` `:ms`), minus what the replay has already covered, over a measured wall-clock gap.
- If a measured gap must stay, round it UP, never down.
- Pick whichever is simpler in the recorder as it stands. Do not reopen rf2-mcjdg's "runs from where the replay has reached" semantics; this is only the lower bound.

## Gates

- A DETERMINISTIC regression: it must reproduce the short wait without relying on the scheduler's luck. For example, drive the recorder's clock or timestamps directly so the measured gap lands one millisecond under the scheduled delay.
  - Show it RED with the fix removed, then restore and hash-check.
- The existing `recorder_timer_child_cljs_test.cljs` tests stay green.
- Story JVM: `cd tools/story && clojure -M:test`.
- clj-kondo, plain.
- The node lane via CI. The shadow-cljs lane is machine-wide exclusive; ask the mayor for it.
notes:

Fix. The recorder's trace listener already recognised a fired :dispatch-later child by its :rf.event/source-detail {:ms …} stamp, but it dropped the delay. The :event/timer-child marker now keeps that delay as :ms (tools/story/src/re_frame/story/recorder.cljc: record-timer-child! and append-timer-child).

The export's timer-child wait is now max(catch-up gap, :ms), rounded up (tools/story/src/re_frame/story/recorder/play_export.cljc). The catch-up gap is unchanged: it still runs to the child's recorded :t from where the replay has reached (the rf2-mcjdg rule). The replay clock (covered-t) advances by the wait actually emitted, and a marker without :ms behaves exactly as before.

Why the delay runs from the current replay point. The marker does not identify the step that armed the timer. The step just replayed, or the timer child before it, may be the arming point; a timer that re-arms itself is the obvious case. So the whole delay, measured from where the replay has reached, is the only bound that is safe without knowing the arming step. The cost is an over-wait when the root sits before other waited steps: safe, just slower.

title: xstate-parity: transition-spec bare keys are not vocabulary-checked (a :targt typo is a silent forbidden block) and root-only keys are accepted inert on non-root nodes, while state-node keys are closed
description:
## Gap

This is NOT an XState-parity gap in the row-7 sense (XState is equally silent — see below); it is an internal asymmetry in re-frame2's own fail-loud grammar that dimension D handed to E for grading, and it is small enough to close. re-frame2 closes the BARE-key vocabulary of a STATE NODE (`validation.cljc:1457-1480` `known-state-node-keys`; a bogus bare key is `:rf.error/machine-unknown-node-key`, namespaced keys are the open extension carve-out) but (a) does not apply the same rule to a TRANSITION SPEC, so `{:targt :b}` registers `:ok` and then behaves as the FORBIDDEN block (the child opt-out: the event is consumed with no transition, no action, and no `:rf.machine.event/unhandled-no-op` — only `:rf.machine/event-received`), and (b) lists the ROOT-ONLY keys `:initial :states :data :schemas :internal-events :guards :actions` in that same node set ("root-only, but harmless on the set"), so a per-state `:data`, `:schemas`, `:internal-events`, `:guards` or `:actions` map is accepted and silently inert (a per-state `:guards` is worse than inert: the state's own `:guard :ok?` then fails with `:rf.error/machine-unresolved-guard`, which at least is loud).

XState v6 at alpha.59 is silent on all of it: a `{ targt: 'b' }` transition is accepted (the event does nothing), an unknown transition key beside a valid target is accepted, unknown state-node keys and root-only keys (`context`, `guards`, `actions`) on a nested node are accepted and ignored. So the CLASS is MATCH (both silent); re-frame2 already leads on node keys and can lead on the rest at the cost of one more closed set.

## XState evidence

Executed: `xs/E-7b-handoffs.mjs` -> `E-7b-handoffs.out`: `transition typo { targt: "b" } | accepted, value="a"`; `transition unknown key + target | accepted, value="b"`; `nested node with root-only keys | accepted, value="b"`; `state node unknown key | accepted, value="a"`. Also `xs/E-7-validation.out`: `unknown top-level key | NEVER`, `unknown state-node key | NEVER`, `leftover v5 types key | NEVER` (the alpha.59 changelog line 47-56 makes `types` a COMPILE error in TypeScript only).

## re-frame2 evidence

An author sees `event-received` and nothing else. The node-key rule exists precisely so a typo dies at registration with the valid vocabulary in the message; a transition typo is at least as common (there are many more transition maps than state nodes) and is currently the only bare-key typo in the grammar that survives. Per-state `:schemas` deserves a mention because XState v6 legitimately HAS per-state `schemas` (alpha.51), so a reader coming from v6 will write one expecting refinement and get silence.

3. Leave as is (trust the programmer). Defensible under the stance, but inconsistent with the rule re-frame2 already enforces one level up.

## Recommendation

title: xstate-parity: explicit [:rf.machine/destroy <parent>] orphans the parent's declarative :spawn children and leaves their registry slot (XState stops children; spec/005 contradicts itself)
description:
## Gap

XState v6: stopping a parent stops its children — `actor.stop()` "Stops the actor, its children and its timers" (`xs-docs/create-actor.md`), and alpha.59 extended the same guarantee to a parent that ERRORS. Measured: after `parent.stop()` the invoked child reads `status stopped` and leaves `snapshot.children`.

re-frame2: an explicit `[:rf.machine/destroy <parent-id>]` on a parent sitting in a `:spawn`-bearing state runs the parent's AUTHORED `:exit` (measured) but NOT the desugared auto-destroy of its declarative child. The child survives at its address, still stamped `:rf/parent-id` of a parent that no longer exists, and its registry slot `[:rf.runtime/machines :spawned <parent> <invoke-id>]` lingers under the dead parent's id. The spec promises the opposite in three places (§Declarative `:spawn` 2977: "when the machine leaves the state (by any transition, including a parent-level cascade), the child is destroyed"; §Composition 3188-3189: "On exit: the user's `:exit` action runs, then the auto-destroy fx is emitted"; §Top-level boot-time spawn 2916: "destroy — Internally: run :exit action, dissoc the snapshot") while §Declarative `:spawn` 3054-3058 asserts the reverse for a spawner's descendants ("outlive their spawner exactly as they outlive an explicit `[:rf.machine/destroy <actor-id>]`") and §Generated address 3068-3070 already anticipates "a parent destroyed and respawned at the same address begins counting from zero beside its own still-live orphans". The spec contradicts itself; the code takes the orphaning side; the gold standard takes the other.

## XState evidence

- Executed: `xs/C-4.mjs` → `xs/C-4.out`: `after parent stop: parent stopped kid status stopped log []`.
- Executed: `xs/C-2.mjs` → `xs/C-2.out` e): `after parent error: parent error kid status stopped` (alpha.59, CHANGELOG-next line 7).
- Docs: `xs-docs/create-actor.md` §Actor members (`stop()`), `xs-docs/lifecycle-and-errors.md` ("Stopping a parent also stops its children").

## re-frame2 evidence

- Executed: `jvm/C/c4.clj` → `jvm/C/c4.out` #4 (fixed-id child): `4 parent destroyed: parent nil | declarative child survives? {:state :running, :data {… :rf/parent-id :c/login4 …} :rf/machine-type :c/auth} | log [:parent-auth-exit]`; ops carry ONE `:rf.machine/destroyed` (the parent) and no destroy for `:c/auth-4`.
- Executed: `jvm/C/c8.clj` → `jvm/C/c8.out` (generated-id child): `C destroyed: live (… :c/wc#1) | C's child orphaned? true | registry #:c{… :pc {[:busy] :c/wc#1}}` — the slot under the destroyed parent `:c/pc` remains.
- Control (parent TRANSITION, not destroy): `jvm/C/c4.out` #3 — leaving the state via `[:cancel]` destroys the child and runs its `:exit` (`:rf.machine/destroyed {:actor-id :c/auth-3 :reason :explicit …}`), as pinned by `implementation/machines/test/re_frame/destroy_exit_cascade_test.clj` (`exit-fires-on-invoke-exit-cascade-destroy`).
- Mechanism (read, fe8de195bd): `lifecycle_fx/destroy.cljc:181-262` `teardown-live-actor!` step 1 calls `lifecycle_fx/exit_cascade.cljc:64-142` `run-child-exit!`, which resolves the spec via `lifecycle_fx/resolver.cljc:150-166` `spec-from-id-or-snapshot` → the registrar's `:rf/machine` projection, i.e. the USER-WRITTEN spec (spec/005:3182 "the registrar stores the user-supplied map verbatim"). The `:spawn` → `:entry`/`:exit` desugar lives in `make-machine-handler`'s runtime spec, so the destroy-time cascade never sees the composed `:rf.machine.spawn/destroy-<state>` action. The frame-destroy path is unaffected: it walks every live actor (`frame_destroy_cascade_test.clj`).
- No test pins the explicit-parent-destroy case in either direction (searched `implementation/machines/test` for parent-destroy scenarios; `lifecycle_composed_corners_test.clj` covers frame destroy and stale timers only).

## Why it matters

A parent machine that owns a `:spawn` child and is torn down explicitly — a feature unmounting, a session ending, a `:final?`-less flow being reset by `[:rf.machine/destroy]` — leaks a live child: its in-flight `:rf.http/managed` requests keep running (the abort hook fires per DESTROYED actor only), its `:after` timers stay armed, and its completion carrier will be minted into a dead parent and stale-suppressed. The programmer wrote `:spawn` precisely so as not to remember this teardown (spec/005:3259 "the parent does not have to remember to destroy the child"). A porter from XState assumes the tree dies with its root.

## Options

1. **Reap tracked children on parent destroy (runtime, small).** In `teardown-live-actor!`, after the exit cascade, walk `[:rf.runtime/machines :spawned <actor-id>]` and destroy every tracked child (single `:spawn` keyword slot and `:spawn-all` `:children` map) through the ordinary destroy path, clearing the slot — the same work the parent's state-exit cascade does today. Hand-emitted children (no slot) stay explicit, so the "Teardown is explicit in v1" rule for un-owned actors is untouched. Spec: make §Declarative `:spawn` say "including an explicit destroy of the parent" and re-word 3054-3058 to name hand-emitted descendants only. Breaks no machine that does not rely on orphaning.
2. **Run the destroy-time exit cascade against the DESUGARED spec (runtime).** Resolve the runtime spec the handler closes over (or re-desugar at destroy time) so the composed auto-destroy actions fire. Same observable result as 1, larger blast radius (`hydrate.cljc` and `finalize.cljc` share the resolver).
3. **Declare orphaning by design (spec-only).** Re-word §Declarative `:spawn` 2977 / §Composition 3188 / §Top-level 2916 to say an explicit destroy of the parent does NOT cascade to declarative children, and add the "destroy your children in `:exit`" idiom. Cheapest, but it keeps a lingering registry slot under a dead id, contradicts the gold standard, and moves the burden `:spawn` exists to remove back onto the author.

## Recommendation

Option 1: it is the reading two of the three spec sentences already give, it is what the parent's own state exit does, it matches XState, and the registry slot makes it a bounded walk with nothing new to track.

## Fence

- `implementation/machines/src/re_frame/machines/lifecycle_fx/destroy.cljc` (`teardown-live-actor!`), `lifecycle_fx/exit_cascade.cljc` (if option 2), `lifecycle_fx/teardown.cljc` (slot pruning)
- `spec/005-StateMachines.md` (HOT ZONE — §Spawning 2656, §Declarative `:spawn` 2977 / 3054-3062 / 3188-3189, §Top-level boot-time spawn 2916)
- `spec/009-Instrumentation.md` (HOT ZONE) only if a new `:reason` is minted for the cascaded child destroy (recommend reusing `:explicit`, so no edit)
- new test beside `implementation/machines/test/re_frame/destroy_exit_cascade_test.clj`; `frame_destroy_cascade_test.clj` as the control that frame destroy is unchanged

## Gates

- `clojure -M:test` in `implementation/machines`; `npm run test:cljs` (the destroy path is `.cljc`, and the CLJS class of destroy tests — `destroy_silent_idempotent_cljs_test.cljc`, `machine_exit_cascade_incarnation_fence_cljs_test.cljc` — must stay green); `spec/conformance` corpus if a fixture asserts child survival (none found).

## Decision needed

Yes. Does an explicit `[:rf.machine/destroy <parent>]` reap the parent's DECLARATIVE `:spawn` / `:spawn-all` children (XState parity; the reading §Declarative `:spawn` gives) — or is orphaning the v1 contract, in which case §Declarative `:spawn` 2977 / 3188 and §Top-level 2916 are re-worded and the lingering registry slot is pruned on destroy?

== RULING (mayor's ruling agent, 2026-09-24 21:09:19 AUSEST, under the project stance; dossier + Codex Recommendation weighed) ==

QUESTION: Does an explicit `[:rf.machine/destroy <parent>]` reap the children the parent's `:spawn` / `:spawn-all` slots TRACK, as XState's `stop()` does? Or is orphaning them the v1 contract?

OPTIONS AND SIZES
- 1. Reap tracked children inside the shared teardown pipeline. Size S-M runtime (one fenced step plus tests), about six spec/005 sentences, three pinned tests re-based, and four doc lines.
- 2. Compute a pseudo-transition to `[]` at destroy time and run `build-destroy-fx` over it. Size M-L. It reaches the same observable through a heavier door. RULED OUT by the stance, as both reviews say.
- 3. Declare orphaning by design. Size S. It re-words spec/005:2977/:3259/:3696/:3188-3189/:2979/:3182, documents the author-side `:exit` idiom, and adds two hygiene fixes: prune `[:spawned <actor>]` on the actor's own destroy, and make a keyword destroy of a tracked child prune its slot.

RULING: OPTION 1. An explicit destroy of an actor reaps every child that one of its `:spawn` / `:spawn-all` slots tracks, through the ordinary tracked-destroy entries, after the actor's own `:exit` cascade.
- One step in `teardown-live-actor!` covers every destroy cause that routes through it: explicit keyword destroy, replacement onto an occupied `:fixed-actor-id`, the frame-destroy walker, and a tracked or join child's own teardown. That last case makes reaping recursive for nested children.
- Hand-emitted actors (no slot) are untouched. "Teardown is explicit in v1" keeps its full meaning for actors nothing tracks.
- Why:
  - The author already declared the child's lifetime by putting it on a state. The spec promises that lifetime at :2977 and :3259 ("the parent does not have to remember to destroy the child … on every code path out of the state").
  - The runtime already records that ownership (`[:rf.runtime/machines :spawned <parent> <invoke-id>]`) and already acts on it at every transition exit, `:after` and join resolution.
  - The explicit-destroy door is the one place the recorded relation is ignored.
  - Option 3 moves a teardown the sugar exists to remove back onto every author, including every XState porter, who will not write it.
- This is completing an existing abstraction, not a new subsystem: no ownership API, option, warning or registry.

THIS NARROWS AN EARLIER RULING — READ BEFORE REVERSING. It narrows the "No descendant reaping / implicit ownership cascade" fence in rf2-dokz (ruled 2026-09-08 23:08 AUSEST) and the "'destroy the orphans' is not on the table" line in rf2-1sip (closed 2026-09-09). The operator delegated this ruling; Mike may reverse it.

  - Both lean on the 2026-05 resolved decision (:2656 dated 2026-05-19, :4645). Its subject is an opt-in `:owned-by` relation for actors IN GENERAL. Its premise, "ports do not need to model an ownership graph", does not describe declarative children, whose ownership graph the runtime already keeps.
- So this is the first MERITS ruling on declarative children.
- rf2-dokz's substance is untouched: an occupant is destroyed cleanly and then the new one installed; `:reason :explicit`; no warning; no registry.

The handler did execute and can have returned a :db value that was discarded by frame destruction. Correction: represent :halted-destroy as an interrupted lifecycle cascade, preserving that the handler ran and distinguishing discarded/uncommitted output from "returned no :db". Carry the existing blocked/lifecycle meaning rather than declaring an exception or falsely stamping the handler "did not run". Resolve the wording/presentation choice here, then add a real self-destroying-handler projection/view regression plus ordinary and depth-halt controls. title: resources: a load-more / refetch-sweep page success clears a stale mark the infinite feed already had
description:
Residual left open by rf2-3x7nj.10.1 (PR #10293, merged), flagged unmeasured in that item's ruling and confirmed still open by the implementing worker: a load-more success on an infinite feed clears a stale mark the feed ALREADY had before that page's attempt started, and a later refetch-sweep page clears a mark kept by an earlier page the same way. 10.1 made a success keep a stale mark stamped with its own attempt; these paths clear marks stamped by a DIFFERENT (earlier) attempt or by none. Measure first at trunk; if it reproduces, a page settle should clear only a mark stamped with its own attempt, as 10.1's rule already does for the ordinary settle.

## Decision needed

No — extend 10.1's own rule to the infinite-feed page settles.
notes:
Merged-PR audit #10293 at 14d784af9f725c043e5f1ddb448cde084fd6d6b4: confirmed both recorded residuals through public resource events, using the merged JVM sources and capturing transport. Case 1: accumulate 3 pages, release owner, invalidate feed tag, load-more page 3; original three pages remain unchanged but :invalidated-at becomes nil. Case 2: owner-free refetch-all sweep; invalidate during page 0, settle page 0 (mark correctly survives), then settle page 1; page 0 still contains its pre-invalidation result but the feed mark becomes nil. Two targeted tests: 8 control assertions pass, 2 required-staleness assertions fail, 0 errors, runner exit 1. Root and all relevant merged resource paths verified. Evidence in guarded audit-sep23-monitor ai/repro-10293-audit-sep23-monitor-2.clj and gate-10293-audit-sep23-monitor-2.log/.exit. Existing six focused suites passed 91 tests/550 assertions. Correction must preserve whole-feed staleness until the invalidation is actually covered; a page append or a later sweep leg cannot certify the older pages fresh. Reuse of this exact open finding; no status/criteria/closure changes.
WORKER VERDICT (2026-09-24, PR #10337, commits 625b883a8c + 5569349aee on branch worker/resources-3x7nj): FIXED.

Reproduced at trunk 61b41468b3 through public events (JVM, plain-atom, capturing transport), both audit cases: (1) 3 pages, owner released, feed tag invalidated, load-more page 3 -> :invalidated-at nil after the append; (2) refetch-all sweep invalidated during page 0 -> page 0 keeps the mark (10.1), the page-1 leg clears it. A third case of the same class also reproduced: an ensure of an invalidated feed (10.3 path) cleared the mark at page 0's settle before the tail legs ran, so a leg failure left pages 1-2 pre-invalidation and the feed reading fresh.

Where the item and this fix differ: the description's literal prescription ("a page settle should clear only a mark stamped with its own attempt, as 10.1's rule already does") is inverted - 10.1 KEEPS a mark stamped with its own attempt and clears others, which is exactly the defect. Followed the audit note instead: preserve whole-feed staleness until the invalidation is actually covered.

Rule (state/settle-page-invalidation): a mark written during this attempt survives it (10.1); page 0 covers a mark that predates it - at once when no sweep follows (window-preserving default unchanged), otherwise the sweep carries it (:sweep-covers-invalidation?) and its last leg clears it; a load-more append keeps it; entry-invalidate drops the claim so a mid-sweep mark outlives the sweep; clear-refetch-sweep drops it too. settle-invalidations now reads definite? off the pre-settle entry, else a kept older mark fires the owned follow-up refetch and restarts the sweep in a loop (plant F reproduced exactly that, also reddening the existing 10.3 test). Spec 016 Refetch-and-invalidation bullet carries one sentence stating the rule.

Controls: the 5 new deftests read 13 failures on unfixed code. Plants on committed code went red only in their own tests: A (append clears) -> load-more test; B (last leg clears uncarried mark) -> later-leg test; C (page 0 clears despite a following sweep) -> sweep-coverage test; F -> owned-sweep assertion + 10.3 test. Counts held at 39 tests / 241 assertions in the namespace; each restore verified by blob hash. resources JVM 922 tests / 8061 assertions exit 0 (baseline 917 / 8026). CLJS node lane left to CI.
Merged-PR audit #10337 (8a0088d422c5b16239ec393133fa0a92ffb5926f; merged 2026-09-24T02:14:42Z). Completeness: All three claims are covered: append and sweep invalidation coverage, authoritative writes dropping abandoned sweeps, and both catalogue clauses for addressed inline spawns. The prior audit finding w5p2p is corrected; its owner already closed it, so no status or finding update. Correctness: Traced the pre-settle attempt identity, page-zero coverage claim, last-leg clearing, mid-sweep invalidation and failure cancellation, and patch/populate late-reply suppression. The definite-follow-up change avoids repeatedly restarting an owned sweep. No actionable defect found. Accepted the author reported resources 922 tests/8061 assertions, focused negative controls, dependent suites and successful CI; no tests rerun. Implementation quality: One private state helper centralizes page coverage; writers reuse clear-refetch-sweep. The extra carry flag expresses the minimum information needed to distinguish a sweep covering an old mark from one predating a new mark. Public-event regressions exercise the races and preserved defaults. No unnecessary API or machinery. Actionable findings: none. Existing finding updates: none.
Audit-update recovery 2026-09-25: prior audit findings have separate new open records. Historical resolutions are explicit; existing statuses and closure metadata are preserved. Forward pointers below identify the recovery records. This records ledger delivery, not mayor notification or acknowledgement.

title: xstate-parity: a parallel REGION BODY silently accepts :entry/:exit/:tags/:spawn - apply the root rule (honour entry/exit/tags, refuse the rest)
description:
## What

Worker xroot-51 reported this while fixing the machine root (rf2-2n6uv.5.1, PR #10407, merged at trunk abc2be08ce). In a parallel machine, a REGION BODY's own `:entry`, `:exit`, `:tags` and `:spawn` (and other state-node keys) are accepted at registration and never run or read. That is the same silent swallow the root had, and spec/Conventions.md forbids it (a MUST). The root ruling deliberately left region bodies alone. Re-verify at your trunk.

## RULING (mayor, 2026-09-25, under the stance): a region body follows the ROOT rule. One rule for every tree root is the elegant reading, and it matches XState, where a parallel region is a state node with its own entry/exit.
- A region body HONOURS `:entry`, `:exit` and `:tags`:
  - region `:entry` runs when the region is entered, after the parallel root's `:entry` and before the region's initial leaf cascade;
  - region `:exit` runs when the region is exited, after its leaf-to-region exit cascade and before the parallel root's `:exit`;
  - region `:tags` join the snapshot's tag union while the machine is in that region.
- A region body REFUSES every other key the runtime never reads for a region, `:spawn` included, with the existing `:rf.error/machine-root-slot-not-supported` (it names the region path in `:path`). Derive the refused set by reading every place that reads these keys, as PR #10407 did for the root. Do not copy the root's list blindly: a region may legitimately carry keys the root may not, and vice versa.
- Transitions still never run a region body's `:entry`/`:exit` unless they genuinely enter or exit that region. In this engine a region is entered at birth and exited at teardown, so check for any transition that re-enters a region; if one exists, follow the node semantics exactly.

title: INCOMPLETE: persisted machine install loses per-actor privacy classification in the documented save/load loop
description:
Merged-PR audit #10455 at 15c2cd34e42f7bd689c494a5f07c8208678d3dab; correctness/completeness finding from rf2-2n6uv.2.5.

The production persistence loop restores machine data but does not restore its machine-owned classification claims. docs/machines/coming-from-xstate.md:240 saves only :rf.runtime/machines from runtime-db. The lowered :sensitive / :large claims live in the separate :rf.runtime/elision subtree and are therefore omitted. events.cljc:1317-1356 merges the supplied subtrees over the fresh frame and requests only the timer re-arm fx. machines/hydrate.cljc:314-340 enumerates timer declarations, cancels and arms handles; it does not reconstruct classification.

This matters for a normal registered machine such as {:sensitive [[:data :token]], :data {:token "saved-secret"}, :initial :idle, :states {:idle ...}}. Run it in the source frame, save using the new guide, and install into a fresh frame. The token returns, but its per-actor sensitive claim does not. machines/classification.cljc:152-184 lowers those declarations only at spawn/singleton first-boot. lifecycle_fx/registration.cljc:1139-1164 guards lowering with needs-bootstrap? and NOT existing-snap?, so an already-installed snapshot does not repair the missing claim on an ordinary event either. core/classification.cljc:953-980 reads only the destination frame registry for machine snapshot classification (also reused by machines SSR projection); with no claim, the restored token is no longer protected by that declaration at egress. Spawned actors have the same gap.

Required correction: make the supported persisted-machine install preserve or reconstruct machine-owned classification for restored singleton and spawned actors before they become observable through normal projections, while preserving unrelated destination claims and avoiding entry/action replay. This is a real privacy defect, so it keeps P1. The documented save/load loop brings back a secret without the claim that redacts it. That is exactly what the classification machinery exists to prevent.

The rule: install RECONSTRUCTS machine-owned classification from the DESTINATION's registered machine definitions. It does not carry claims in the payload.

- Destination claims owned by anything else are preserved untouched, and claims owned by a restored actor are replaced, not duplicated.
- No entry or action replay, no new error id, and no new mechanism beyond calling the existing lowering.
- The payload shape does not change. Selecting only `:rf.runtime/machines` stays the supported save, and the guide example at `docs/machines/coming-from-xstate.md:240` stays valid. So `:rf/install-frame-state` and `:rf/hydrate` now restore machine privacy claims, including on server frames. Re-verify each item at your trunk.

1. **PRIVACY LEAK (the reason this is P1).** The `:rf/install-frame-state` event's OWN traces carry the whole saved state unredacted. The worker measured that after projection, **4 of 6** install traces still contained `"saved-secret"` in `:rf.event/v`. So restoring the machine claims (#10462) protects the snapshot in app-db, while the event that installed it still leaks the same secret through the trace stream.
2. **Stale descriptions of the rearm fx, which now also restores classification:**

   - the spec/015 subsystem table row that reads "actor spawn / first-boot" for machine claim lowering.

## Ruling (mayor, 2026-09-26, under the stance)

- **Item 1.** The install payload IS app state, so a trace of it must be classified as the state would be. Declare the install event's payload SENSITIVE as a whole, fail-closed, through the EXISTING event-meta classification mechanism. The worker's pointer is `install-frame-state-standard-meta` in `events.cljc`, next to how other framework events declare sensitive args.
  - Whole-payload redaction on the install trace is correct and enough. A public field in the saved state does not need to survive in the TRACE of the install, because it is readable in app-db after the install.
  - No per-path derivation, and no new mechanism.
  - Check `:rf/hydrate` for the same leak. If its payload rides a trace unredacted, it gets the same one-line declaration.

- **Item 2.** Present-tense prose: say the rearm step re-arms timers AND restores machine classification claims. Keep the comment's spawn-order-cache point.

title: Reserve :rf/install-frame-state as a reserved event id
description:
MAYOR RULING (2026-09-26): option 1. Add :rf/install-frame-state to reserved-event-ids (events.cljc), so a public reg-event over it is refused like :rf/set-db and :rf/settle-flows. It is a framework-write-authority event and spec/Conventions.md reserves :rf/*. Add a test, and update docs/api/re-frame.core.md's Standard events intro.

From GitHub issue #10501 (closed into this bead). Original text:

**Type:** decision → task · **Priority:** P3 · **Surface:** `implementation/core/src/re_frame/events.cljc`

## Description
`reserved-event-ids` is `#{:rf/set-db :rf/settle-flows}` (`events.cljc:889-913`). `:rf/install-frame-state` is a framework-standard event with framework-write authority (`events.cljc:1253-1391`), but a public `reg-event` over it is not refused, even though `spec/Conventions.md` reserves the `:rf/*` namespace.

## Options
1. Add `:rf/install-frame-state` to `reserved-event-ids`, with a test, and update the `docs/api/re-frame.core.md` Standard events intro, which currently names only `:rf/set-db`.
2. Keep it re-registrable on purpose, and record why in the source.

## Acceptance
- A ruling is recorded, and code, tests and docs follow it.

title: [:rf/machine id] :rf.sub/run trace carries a machine's :sensitive :data unredacted
description:
A machine's :sensitive :data leaks, unredacted, through the :rf.sub/run trace of the framework subscription [:rf/machine id]. Found by the docs/machines correctness review (rf2-ahrss, step 2), measured on the JVM at trunk eb53174c3d.

Measured: a machine registered with {:sensitive [[:data :token]]} gets the :token slot redacted in every machine trace. But the :rf.sub/run trace for [:rf/machine <id>] carries the snapshot in :rf.sub/value with the token in clear.

Why it is a defect, not user error: spec/009-Instrumentation.md (~:259) says a subscription does not inherit its inputs' classification. For user subs the fix is to classify the sub. [:rf/machine id] is a framework subscription, though, and the user cannot classify it, so no user code closes the leak.

Fix direction (for the owner to decide): have [:rf/machine id] inherit the machine's :sensitive classification, or redact its :rf.sub/value by the machine's declared paths. The docs/machines guide now scopes its :sensitive sentence to what holds, and states this gap.
notes:
== FIX (PR #10511, branch worker/machsub-rgm64, commits b84d31e9df + d2c7b64992 on trunk 8da978bd95)

Reproduced at 8da978bd95 on the JVM before any source change: a machine registered with {:sensitive [[:data :token]] :large [[:data :blob]]}, subscribed as [:rf/machine id], put the token in clear in the :rf.sub/run trace's :rf.sub/value AND :rf.sub/prev-value, and left the blob unelided. The same leak held for an off-box direct read naming the sub by :query-v (rf.elision/elide-wire-value, the door Pair MCP read-sub / list-subscriptions :include-values / snapshot :sub-cache use). The new namespace re-frame.machine-sub-classification-test read 10 failures of 21 assertions, exit 1.

Fix, per the mayor's ruling (the framework sub classifies its value by the machine's declared classification, reusing the machine-trace redaction):
- implementation/core/src/re_frame/classification.cljc: the class project-machine-tags already computed (frame-snapshot-classification over the lowered :source :machine claims, unioned with any author :event classification) is extracted as machine-classification. project-sub-tags, where a user-classified sub is redacted, unions it into its one redact-with-paths walk when the sub id is :rf/machine, keyed by (second :rf.sub/query-v). Spawned <type>#n actors are covered by their own lowered claims.
- implementation/core/src/re_frame/elision.cljc: elide-wire-value's :query-v re-seed (the route read subs' existing direct-read door) also walks a [:rf/machine id] value from [:rf.runtime/machines :snapshots id], so the registry's absolute machine claims match. The snapshot prefix moved there as core's single definition (machine-snapshot-prefix); classification reads it.
- implementation/core/src/re_frame/subs/memo.cljc: docstrings/comments only (the route subs are no longer "the one" narrow addition).
- :large paths become the :rf.size/large-elided marker exactly as on machine traces. The in-process @(subscribe [:rf/machine id]) stays raw. Both registry reads are untracked snapshots, so the reaction gains no dependency.
- spec/005 §Privacy and spec/009's :rf.sub/run paragraph each gained one sentence stating that the framework machine sub carries its machine's declared classification.

Control: with the :rf/machine match removed from both halves, the regression read 10 failures of 21 assertions, exit 1 (7 in the trace test, 3 in the direct-read test; the non-sensitive-slot assertions stayed green). The restore was verified by blob hash against the committed objects.

Gates on the branch tree: machines JVM 1519/6474 -> 1523/6495 (+4 tests/+21 assertions, the new namespace), 0 failures; core JVM 2404/12602 before and after; full implementation JVM sweep PASS, exit 0; routing prod gate 571/3267 exit 0; core prod gate 2102/9180 exit 0; clj-kondo on the changed core files identical before/after (only pre-existing warnings), new test 0/0; require-alias ratchet exit 0; check_doc_slugs exit 0 (a planted anchor in the new 009 sentence went red). CLJS lanes and mkdocs --strict are relied on from CI.

Docs follow-up (not edited, another session's page): docs/machines/concepts.md at trunk d260199251, lines 452-453, still reads "The `:rf.sub/run` trace of a `[:rf/machine id]` subscription is not a machine trace, and it carries the value unredacted." Once this lands, that sentence is false.
Forward pointer from merged-PR audit #10511: rf2-85rta is a new OPEN finding. Current-main JVM probe confirms a classified spawned actor leaks its retained snapshot through :rf.sub/prev-value after destroy removes its classification. See the new bead for reproduction and acceptance; original status/content preserved.
close_reason:
Fixed by PR #10511, merged 2026-09-26T07:06:14Z at trunk 6fe05f1f5e, per the ruling that the framework sub classifies by the machine's declared paths, and that there is no second mechanism.
- Reproduced on the JVM at 8da978bd95: a machine declaring {:sensitive [[:data :token]] :large [[:data :blob]]}, subscribed as [:rf/machine id], put the token in clear on :rf.sub/value and :rf.sub/prev-value and did not size-mark the blob. An off-box direct read by :query-v (the MCP read-sub path) leaked the same way.
- Fix: classification.cljc extracts the class the machine traces already compute as machine-classification, and the sub-run chokepoint applies it to a [:rf/machine <id>] value. elision.cljc's :query-v re-seed walks a machine sub's value from [:rf.runtime/machines :snapshots <id>]. :large paths get the size marker. In-process reads still return real values. subs/memo.cljc changed in docstrings only. One sentence each in spec/005 §Privacy and spec/009's :rf.sub/run paragraph.
- Regression: implementation/machines/test/re_frame/machine_sub_classification_test.clj, which covers the value, prev-value, size marker, undeclared slots kept, the direct read, and a sibling machine riding raw. With the fix removed: 10 failures / 21 assertions. The restores match the committed blobs.
- Gates: machines JVM 1519/6474 -> 1523/6495; core 2404/12602 unchanged; all implementation JVM artefacts, the routing and core prod gates, and check_doc_slugs (planted anchor went red) all pass. PR CI read 88/88.
The docs/machines/concepts.md sentence (about :452-453) saying the sub trace carries the value unredacted is now false. It is filed as its own bead.

title: Route read subs leak declared-sensitive route params in :rf.sub/prev-value when navigating to a route that declares no classification
description:
Found by rf2-85rta's worker (PR #10598, merged at trunk 36e406aec4) while looking for siblings of the machine-teardown leak. It is the same class of leak: a previous value is redacted against the CURRENT classification, and the classification that governed it has already been replaced. The worker reports it leaks at base; it is a CLAIM, so reproduce it first.

Reproduction as reported:
1. Register a route declaring `:sensitive [[:params :secret]]`, and a second route declaring nothing.
2. Hold `[:rf/route]` and `[:rf.route/params]`.
3. Navigate from the first route (with a secret param) to the second.
4. Capture `:rf.sub/run` traces.

Both subs' `:rf.sub/prev-value` carry the secret in the clear. No other trace carries it.

Why #10598's fix does not reach it: that fix hands the `:rf/machine` sub the runtime-db it last read, under a private `:re-frame.classification/prev-inputs` tag, so its previous value is redacted against the claims that applied when it was computed (see `project-sub-tags` in implementation/core/src/re_frame/classification.cljc, and implementation/core/src/re_frame/subs/memo.cljc). `:rf.route/params` sits DOWNSTREAM of `[:rf/route]` rather than reading the runtime-db, so it has no prev runtime-db to hand over. The fix needs `implementation/routing/**` and probably the route-sub projection in classification.cljc (`project-route-sub-slot`).

Constraints, as for rf2-85rta:
- reuse the existing projection mechanism;
- keep no stale registry state indefinitely;
- do NOT redact the in-process value.

A regression goes red at base: both subs, both directions (sensitive to plain, and plain to sensitive as a control).
notes: Audit follow-up from PR #10602: rf2-li9em tracks a reproduced prior-value leak after the leaving route is re-registered. Separate open bead; the original closure is unchanged.
close_reason:
FIXED in PR #10602 (branch worker/routeleak-kuyza, rebased onto trunk 094d614760). ## The decisive measurement, inline The reproduction is a real navigation with the subs held, capturing the traces. `:route/secret` declares `{:sensitive [[:params :secret] [:query :token]]}`, and the test navigates from "/secret/

?token=" to "/plain" with [:rf/route], [:rf.route/params] and [:rf.route/query] held. - **At base:** 11 failures of 37 assertions. The :rf.sub/run prev-value of all three subs carried both secrets raw, and a `[]` whole-projection route leaked the same way. - **With the fix:** 0 of 38. In every prior slice the declared slots read :rf/redacted, while the unclassified :route-id rides verbatim. - **Sabotage, core half removed** (the prev slot no longer hands ::prev-inputs to the projector): 9 failures of 38. - **Sabotage, routing half removed** (the prior route is never found): 9 failures of 38. - **Restore:** both plants were restored and verified by blob hash (default form equal to the committed blob). - **Control, the reverse direction (plain to sensitive):** green at base and fix. The prior value is the plain slice, and the new value is redacted by the registry the entering route installed. - **Census:** with no sub held, the sensitive-to-plain navigation emits no trace carrying either secret, so the prev-value slot was the whole leak. ## The fix It extends #10598's ::prev-inputs mechanism. The registry keeps no entry for the leaving route, and in-process reads stay raw. - **Core:** project-sub-tags passes ::prev-inputs to the existing project-route-sub-slot path for the prev slot. - **Routing:** project-route-sub-egress gains a four-argument arity. A prior value belongs to the route its slice names: the value itself for :rf/route, and the prior [:rf/route] input for the params/query leaves. - **Why routing, not the registry:** the leaves are layer-2 subs with no prior runtime-db to read. - **Classification:** routing.classification/classification-at re-roots that route's declaration (the same validate+extract activation lowers from) onto the sub's value. Those claims are unioned into the walk ahead of the unchanged registry pass. - **Directory:** late_bind/directory.cljc gained one sentence documenting the four-argument arity. The mayor granted that fence extension; no key was added. ## Gates, base -> branch (captured exits) - **core JVM:** 2163/12193/0 -> 2163/12193/0. - **core prod gate:** 1889/8870/0 -> same. - **routing JVM:** 574/3688/0 -> 577/3726/0, exactly +3/+38 from the new namespace. - **routing prod gate:** 44 ns 576/3289 -> 45 ns 579/3300. - **machines JVM:** 1323/6217/0 -> same. #10598's namespace, run alone, gives 7/67/0. - **late-bind-drift-test:** 8/632/0. - **clj-kondo (plain form):** 0 errors / 1 pre-existing warning, identical at base. - **Static ratchets:** 24 green. - **CLJS:** relies on CI's node lane, which this diff arms. ## Sibling findings - **Different cause, not fixed here:** a secret path param appears raw in the URL string of the :rf.route/handle-url-change event vector on the event traces, and in :rf.route/planned's :url, where the query is redacted but the path segment is not. That is the URL-carrier surface, which plan-trace-tags documents as ambient on the drain. - **rf2-ajpcr:** not made trivially answerable. The route derivation is routing-owned and does not reach resource or mutation subs.

title: Check whether resource and mutation read subs classify their values on :rf.sub/run traces: project-sub-tags handles only machine and route subs
description:
A LEAD, not a measurement. rf2-85rta's worker (PR #10598, merged at trunk 36e406aec4) noticed it and did not measure it.

`project-sub-tags` in implementation/core/src/re_frame/classification.cljc special-cases machine subs (the snapshot classification) and route subs (the route egress projection). It has no equivalent for resources. So a resource or mutation read sub whose slot is declared `:sensitive` may emit its value raw on `:rf.sub/run` traces, in both `:rf.sub/value` and `:rf.sub/prev-value`.

First establish whether it leaks at all: declare a sensitive resource slot, hold its read sub, and capture the trace. If it does not leak, close this with the measurement as the finding. If it does, fix it the way machine and route subs are handled, with a regression shown red at base.

SEQUENCING: the route-sub leak bead edits the same function, so this depends on it in the tracker. Take classification.cljc only on a trunk carrying that fix.
notes:
== CORRECTION TO THE CLOSE REASON (2026-09-29, before PR #10611 merged): the projector moved namespace

The close reason above names the projector re-frame.resources.sub-egress/project-read-sub-egress, and says the branch was rebased onto trunk 98facb7f83. Both are superseded:

- The projector is now re-frame.resources.trace-egress/project-read-sub-egress. The namespace re-frame.resources.sub-egress no longer exists. CI's "Public-API manifest drift-check" refused it as an unaccounted source namespace. Classifying a new namespace means editing implementation/scripts/api-manifest, which was outside the fence, so the code moved into the already-classified trace-egress namespace instead. project-trace-scoped-key stays private, since the projector now sits beside it. The hook key :resources/project-resource-sub-egress and its directory row are unchanged.
- The api-manifest job's seven steps, run locally on the moved tree, each exit 0. late_bind_drift_test reads 8/638/0.
- Re-measured AFTER the move, with the hook unpublished at its publication site in re-frame.resources: resources-read-sub-egress-cljs-test read 25 failures of 6 tests / 69 assertions, the same count as before the move. After the restore it read 0 failures, and the default-form blob hash equals the committed blob.
- The branch is rebased onto trunk b712ee8269. Trunk changed implementation/http/src (rf2-ksdtl), which is on the core and resources test classpaths, so those lanes were re-run on the rebased tree. The counts are unchanged: core 2163/12199/0, core production gate 209 ns 1889/8876, resources 932/8170/0.

Behaviour, the measurement at base, the controls and the siblings are as the close reason states.
Audit PR #10611 follow-up: rf2-lafas — Claim incomplete: resource/mutation prior-value redaction forgets historical declarations. Evidence and required correction are in the new open finding.
Audit PR #10611 follow-up: rf2-cudar — Claim incomplete: infinite-feed merged item traces leak owner-declared sensitive fields. Evidence and required correction are in the new open finding.
close_reason:
FIXED in PR #10611 (branch worker/subprivacy-2p7fo, commit "fix(resources): resource and mutation read subs redact their owner's declared slots on :rf.sub/run", rebased onto trunk 98facb7f83). It LEAKED, so this is a fix rather than a no-leak finding.

## The decisive measurement, inline

Measured on JVM with debug on, capturing the :rf.sub/run traces through a trace listener.

Resource :acct/profile declares :sensitive [[:data :ssn]]. At base 6c698873a3, with [:rf/resource q] and [:rf.resource/data q] held, the registry carried [:rf.runtime/resources :entries <kid> :data :ssn], yet:
- :rf.sub/value carried {:name "Ann" :ssn <secret>} raw on both subs;
- :rf.sub/prev-value carried the prior secret raw across a :rf.resource/refetch;
- after :rf.resource/remove it still carried the secret raw, with the registry claims already empty.

Mutation :m/secret declares :sensitive [[:data :token]]. [:rf/mutation {:instance :i1}] :result and [:rf.mutation/result {:instance :i1}] carried {:token <secret>} raw, and after :rf.mutation/clear the prev-value carried it raw, with the claims gone.

The regression is resources-read-sub-egress-cljs-test, 6 tests / 69 assertions:
- at base: 25 failures;
- core half removed (project-resource-sub-slot passes through): 25 failures;
- resources half removed (hook unpublished): 25 failures;
- with the fix: 0 failures.

Controls: a resource declaring nothing rides verbatim (green in every run), and in-process reads stay raw. Both plants were restored and verified by blob hash (default form equal to the committed blob).

## Where the classification now happens

project-sub-tags in implementation/core/src/re_frame/classification.cljc runs these subs' value and prev-value through the late-bound :resources/project-resource-sub-egress projector. The projector is re-frame.resources.sub-egress/project-read-sub-egress, published by the re-frame.resources facade.

It classifies from the OWNER SPEC's declaration, re-rooted onto the sub's value (the classification-at approach #10602 used for prior route values), so no registry state is kept:
- data under :data / :previous-data / :items / :pages / :result, or the whole value, walked index-free;
- a coarse :sensitive? / :large? resource claim covers the whole data projection;
- :previous-key and :affected-keys go through the family's trace-row key projection.

A mutation sub's owner is read off its instance: in the live runtime-db (an untracked read) for the current value, and in the prior inputs for the prior value. The mayor granted the fence extension for the one new directory.cljc row.

## Gates, base -> final

JVM lanes (tests/assertions/failures):
- core: 2163/12193/0 -> 2163/12199/0. The +6 is late_bind_drift_test, 8/632 -> 8/638/0.
- core production gate: 1889/8870 -> 1889/8876.
- resources: 926/8101/0 -> 932/8170/0, exactly +6/+69 from the new namespace.
- machines: 1323/6217/0, unchanged. #10598's namespace is 7/67/0.

Other gates:
- clj-kondo (pinned 2026.04.15, plain form): 0 errors; the only warnings are pre-existing and identical at base.
- CLJS: relies on CI's node lane, which the diff arms.

## Siblings (not fixed)

- A resource sub's :rf.sub/query-v carries its payload :params, declared ones included. Spec 015 documents this as a fail-open ("a subscription's query vector is identity").
- The re-frame.subs.memo validate-and-trace docstring still names only the machine and route subs. It is outside this fence.

description:
