title: Xray inline panel: shell content overflows its host (page-level horizontal scroll moves app + Xray); shared testbeds hard-code host width so the resizer can't resize
description:
Reported by Mike while using the deep_machine testbed: Xray's inline-panel resizer does nothing, and the page's horizontal scrollbar scrolls BOTH the app and Xray. It should scroll only the app.

Measured 2026-09-29 with headless Playwright at a 1280x800 viewport, against compiled builds at trunk cfa994bbe3.

1. RESIZER. The shared testbeds' host CSS hard-codes `[data-rf-xray-host] { flex: 0 0 420px }` rather than the documented `flex: 0 0 var(--rf-xray-inline-width, …)`. Xray's drag writes --rf-xray-inline-width, which nothing reads, so the panel cannot resize.
   - deep_machine: dragging 150px left gave width 420 -> 420.
   - Control, the counter example, whose host reads the var: 560 -> 713, var set to 713px.
   - The hard-coded pages are 12 shared testbeds (tenant_switcher, ssr_multi_frame, ssr_hydration_mismatch, schema_violation, non_trivial_app_db, multi_frame, long_flow_w_failure, large_dispatcher, http_toggle, drain_depth_trigger, deliberate_throw, deep_machine). Xray's own testbeds and the examples use the var.
2. PAGE-LEVEL HORIZONTAL SCROLL. Xray's shell content overflows its host horizontally, and nothing clips it, so the document's scrollWidth grows past the viewport. The page's horizontal scrollbar then moves the app AND the panel.
   - deep_machine: docScrollWidth 1749 vs viewport 1280. The L3 tab-bar buttons extend to x=1749 inside a 420px host, and EDN inspector rows overflow too; 45 elements in all.
   - counter: docScrollWidth 1610 at the default 560px width, so it is not specific to the hard-coded testbeds.
   - The fix belongs in Xray: the shell must never widen its host. The tab strip and panel bodies scroll within the panel.
notes:
== FIX COMMITTED (2026-09-29 14:45:35 AUSEST) == Commit 464eaa4c6d is on worker/xray-host-overflow-20260929 (worktree xrayrun, cut from trunk 0cdc51f202). It changes three things. First, shell.cljs tab-bar-tree: the label and tabs move into a rf-xray-tab-bar-scroller (overflow-x auto, min-width 0, thin scrollbar), and Reset sits outside it; the bar uses min-height instead of height. Second, the 12 shared testbeds' host rules become flex: 0 0 var(--rf-xray-inline-width, 420px). Third, spec 007 §L3 gains one sentence, and the shell's DOM suite gains row W6. Local verification awaits a shadow-cljs lane grant from the mayor.
== APPROACH CHANGED: host layout, not Xray internals (2026-09-29)

Mike redirected the fix to how the Xray aside is laid out: the app and Xray must not share a scrollbar, the app gets its own horizontal scrollbar, and the splitter must drag. The tab-strip commit d30ec2535b was dropped. PR #10616 now carries 2e235dcabb: the shell row is height 100vh, #app is overflow auto, and the host is overflow hidden with flex-basis var(--rf-xray-inline-width, ...). This covers the config.cljc snippet, spec 011, docs, README, tutorial, skills, examples/_shared/css/structure.css and all 18 testbed host pages.

Measured with a Playwright probe at 1280x800 (drag 150px, widen the app's content, scroll it):
- deep_machine: before, every check failed (splitter 420 -> 420); after, every check passed (420 -> 713).
- counter: before, the page was 3032 wide and shared one scrollbar, but the splitter worked (560 -> 713); after, every check passed and the page is 1280 wide.
Doc gates all exit 0: check_doc_slugs, check_readme_links --ci, check_retired_spellings, check_readme_inventories, mkdocs --strict.
Audit PR #10616 follow-up: rf2-d9aum tracks the new app scroll container bypassing routing scroll-to-top and Back/Forward capture/restore. Independent-scroll layout retained; correction and evidence are in the new open finding.
close_reason:
Fixed by PR #10616, merged 2026-09-29T05:23:09Z (trunk 5c997a5e37; commits 2e235dcabb + bb1d91af4f, 88/88 checks green).

Inline Xray is now a pinned side pane in every host layout. The shell row is height: 100vh, so the page never scrolls. #app has overflow: auto, so the app has its own scrollbars. The [data-rf-xray-host] aside has overflow: hidden, so nothing in Xray can widen the page. Its flex-basis reads var(--rf-xray-inline-width, <px>), so Xray's drag handle resizes it.

title: Claim incomplete: callable feed replies bypass declared large-field elision
description:
Merged-PR audit #10631, merge c323e3ed3ebfe50736fd912dc6fe201f41ba89e4, run 7c8a9165-023d-421f-98ce-3e92f6303aef.

The feed-reply correction translates the :large axis for keyword accessors, but a callable accessor leaves the original page-relative path in place after the page envelope has been removed. Declared large payloads therefore ship raw in the off-box continuation echo.

Reproduction: register :infinite true, :page->items (fn [pg] (:items pg)), and :large [[:data :items :blob]], then settle {:items [{:blob "probe-large" :name "public"}]}. BOTH projected reply :value slots contain the original :blob string. Control: the identical envelope and declaration with keyword :page->items :items returns :rf.size/large-elided at :blob. This declaration elides even a small marker; a real declared large blob is equally left unclassified.

Cause: trace_egress.cljc:857 gives callable accessors a whole-value fallback for :sensitive, while :858 always passes false for :large. title: re-frame-migration skill: floor-gate Check 1 treats React peer-range admission as compatibility evidence (gh-10786)
description:
GitHub issue #10786: https://github.com/day8/re-frame2/issues/10786 (opened 2026-10-03T05:47:30Z under mike-thompson-day8). The body below is the issue's, verbatim. Mike's standing rule (2026-10-03): the worker that does this bead also closes issue #10786 as its last act, with a comment naming the PR.

---

## Problem

[floor-gate.md Check 1](https://github.com/day8/re-frame2/blob/412f86be3d07009cc45927ed495673f454b37f23/skills/re-frame-migration/references/floor-gate.md#check-1--downstream-react-lib-compatibility-audit) classifies a library as already compatible, with no action, when its peer range admits React 19.

A permissive historical peer declaration does not establish compatibility with APIs or component semantics removed in React 19. This classification can suppress the evidence check the migration actually needs.

## Concrete counterexample

[npm's exact react-toastify 9.1.3 metadata](https://registry.npmjs.org/react-toastify/9.1.3) declares React and React DOM >=16. That range admits 19. Its [immutable ToastContainer source](https://github.com/fkhadra/react-toastify/blob/94a36ff04e1cc8de6b2aa588e207a47ba1188d39/src/components/ToastContainer.tsx) is a forwardRef component whose defaults, including closeOnClick and draggable, live on ToastContainer.defaultProps.

[React's upgrade guide](https://react.dev/blog/2024/04/25/react-19-upgrade-guide#removed-proptypes-and-defaultprops-for-functions) removes function defaults while retaining class defaults. The important qualification is how the element is constructed.

A small SSR probe on React/DOM 19.2.0, using a defaulted function, forwardRef and class with omitted props, produced:

| Component | legacy createElement | JSX runtime |
| --- | --- | --- |
| function | default retained | default absent |
| forwardRef | default retained | default absent |
| class | default retained | default retained |

The probe's captured exit was 0. This is not a claim that every Toastify 9 integration fails: a caller using legacy createElement can retain these defaults. It proves that peer admission cannot settle compatibility on its own, and that blanket claims about function defaults also need the factory distinction.

## Proposed correction

Classify peer admission separately from verified support. Check explicit target-major release evidence, relevant removed-API/source usage and the application's actual element factory and rendering paths. For unverified component libraries, reuse the existing author-approved empirical-verification path. Preserve class defaults and record behavior changes before choosing an upgrade; avoid unconditional bumps solely because a generic scan found defaultProps.

Acceptance: an open-ended peer declaration alone never yields the no-action compatibility verdict, and the audit records its supporting evidence and targeted runtime scope.

Open and closed issue searches for peer/React, defaultProps, Toastify and the floor gate found no duplicate.
close_reason: Fixed by PR #10790 (GitHub issue #10786), commit "docs(skill): stop floor-gate Check 1 treating React peer-range admission as compatibility". Check 1 now treats a peer range that admits 19 as admission, not evidence. "Already React-19-compatible" now requires a React-19 release or changelog for the installed version, or a source read for React-19-removed API on the paths the app renders, and the evidence and the paths it covers are recorded. A library with only a peer range goes through Check 2's existing option 4, an empirically-verified GO naming the screens tested. A new paragraph covers the element factory. React 19.2.0's ReactJSXElement.js createElement resolves type.defaultProps unconditionally (lines 649-650), while jsxProd resolves none, and classes are resolved in ReactFiberClassComponent.js line 1201. Reagent's :> reaches react/createElement (template.cljs at f23875aac2, lines 306 -> 250 -> 143). So bumps are chosen from recorded behaviour changes, not from a defaultProps scan hit. Counterexample verified: npm react-toastify 9.1.3 declares peerDependencies react >=16 and react-dom >=16 (gitHead 94a36ff04e). Its ToastContainer.tsx is forwardRef at line 13, with ToastContainer.defaultProps at line 86. CI is green with 88 checks, and all repo check_*.py and check-*.sh ratchets passed locally.

title: Live Fresco examples in the Fresco guide (docs/core/fresco/)
description:
## This section

`docs/core/fresco/` is the 24-page Fresco guide plus its cookbook, troubleshooting, escape-ladder and glossary pages. It has static code only, because until now no cell could run Fresco. It is the section that gains the most.

Pages to work through, with what a live cell could show:
- `01-getting-started`, `02-views-and-reads`: an `h/defview` reading `h/sub`; a view that re-renders when its subscription changes.
- `03-events-as-data`: intent vectors, key maps (`{"Enter" [...]}`), `::h/prevent`, `h/event`.
- `04-controlled-inputs`: `:on-input [:x/edit ::h/value]` round-trips, `::h/checked`, selects.
- `05-forms`: `re-frame.fresco.forms`.
- `06-lists-and-collections`: keyed lists that update.
- `07-routing-and-navigation`: `h/route-link` with an **in-memory** routing frame only; never `:url-bound? true`.
- `08-async-resources`: views over stubbed `:rf.http/managed` and `reg-resource`.
- `09-interop`: `h/as-element` / `h/as-component` only. `h/defhost` is unavailable, so its examples stay static.
- `11-ephemeral-state`: `h/reg-state`.
- `12-motion-and-presence`: `re-frame.fresco.motion/presence`.
- `13-overlays-and-focus`: `re-frame.fresco.overlay` popover and modal.
- `17-errors`: `h/error-boundary` with a view that throws, and the fallback rendering.
- `20-migration-from-reagent`: a reagent2 cell and a Fresco cell side by side, rendering the same thing.
- `cookbook`: the recipes that are interactive.

Leave these static:
- `00-installation`, `10-native-tier` (`re-frame.fresco.native` is not bundled), `15-testing` (the test kit is not bundled), `18-ssr-and-hydration` (`re-frame.fresco.server` is not bundled), `19-performance` and `21-code-splitting`.
- Any `h/render!` / `h/client-root` boot code. A cell's last form is mounted for you, so a cell ends with the tree, e.g. `[h/frame-root {:id :todo} [todo-list {}]]`.

The Fresco pages use the `h` alias; keep it.

## Start after

PR #10791 (Playground: Fresco and every optional artefact in cljs-rf2 cells) must be merged first. Check with `gh pr view 10791 --json state`. Until it merges, the engine on `main` cannot run the cells this bead asks for.

## The new capability

The docs' live ` ```cljs-rf2 ` cells run on `docs/cljs/playground-rf2.js`, built from `docs/tools/playground/sci`. That engine now bundles:

- re-frame2 core and reagent2 (reagent-slim), as before;
- **Fresco**: `re-frame.fresco` and its `forms`, `overlay` and `motion` modules;
- **every optional artefact**:
  - machines, flows and schemas (as before);
  - **HTTP**: `re-frame.http.managed`, plus `re-frame.http.test-support` for stubs;
  - **resources**, **routing**, **epoch** and **SSR**.

Before PR #10791, a cell could use only core, reagent2, machines, flows and schemas. So pages teaching Fresco, HTTP, resources, routing, epoch history or SSR could only show static code. Now a reader can run those examples, edit them, and see the result.

## How to write a live cell

The fence is ` ```cljs-rf2 `; there is no separate Fresco fence. A cell runs when the page loads, and again on Mod-Enter after an edit. Its last form is rendered.

- **Which renderer.** The last form renders through **Fresco** when it contains:
  - a Fresco view (`h/defview`), or `h/frame-root` / `h/frame-provider`; or
  - a handler written as data, such as `:on-click [:inc]`.

  Otherwise it renders through **reagent2**. Plain hiccup looks the same either way. One page can mix reagent2 and Fresco cells, but one tree cannot. A plain fn or `reg-view` head inside a Fresco tree raises `:rf.error/fresco-bad-head`.
- **What a cell can require.**
  - `re-frame.core`, which includes `reg-view`, `reg-machine`, `reg-flow`, `reg-app-schema`, `reg-resource`, `reg-route`, `epoch-history` and `restore-epoch!`
  - `re-frame.fresco`, `.forms`, `.overlay` and `.motion`
  - `reagent2.*`
  - `re-frame.schemas`
  - `re-frame.http.managed` and `re-frame.http.test-support`
  - `re-frame.resources`, `re-frame.routing`, `re-frame.epoch` and `re-frame.ssr`
- **Not available:**
  - `h/defhost`, since a cell has no foreign React component to wrap
  - `re-frame.fresco.native`, `re-frame.fresco.server` and the Fresco test kit
  - Story, Xray, and the Ring/Node SSR hosts
- **Frames.** A cell that creates no frame uses `:rf/default`. A cell that wraps its tree in `frame-root` uses that frame, as a real app does.
- **Shared page state.** All cells on a page share the registrar and the frames, so a later cell can render a view an earlier cell registered. Leaving the page unmounts everything, destroys frames and removes the page's registrations.
- **HTTP without a network.** Stub `:rf.http/managed` and route the frame to the stub:

  ```clojure
  (require '[re-frame.core :as rf]
           '[re-frame.http.managed]
           '[re-frame.http.test-support :as http-test-support])

  (http-test-support/install-managed-request-stubs!
    {[:get "https://api.example.com/articles/intro"] {:reply {:ok {:title "Welcome"}}}})

  ;; ... events, subs and a view ...

  [rf/frame-root {:id :demo :fx-overrides {:rf.http/managed :rf.http/managed-test-stub}}
   [article-view]]
  ```

  - Key each stub on the exact `[method url]` the request sends. A miss reaches `:on-failure` with `no stub matched`.
  - Use `{:reply {:failure {...}}}` to demo errors.
  - Install stubs and never uninstall them: the stub stack is global.
  - Real requests also work, but only to `https` endpoints that allow CORS, and they depend on the network. Prefer stubs.
- **Never create a `:url-bound? true` frame.** It would take over the docs site's address bar. Routing works on in-memory frames.
- **Working examples to copy:**
  - The cells in `docs/tools/playground/test/smoke.test.mjs` cover a Fresco view, a data-handler cell, a stubbed HTTP request, a `reg-resource` load, `reg-route` and `render-to-string`; all of them pass in CI.
  - `docs/tools/playground/README.md` has the full rules and a troubleshooting table.

## What to do

1. Read `docs/AUTHORING.md` and follow it. Examples must be real, use the actual API, and be self-contained; keep the page's continuing example domain.
2. Go through each page in this section and find the examples where **running** the code would teach something reading it cannot. Good candidates are behaviour that changes on a click, a request moving through loading, success and failure, data flowing into a view, and a rendered result. Introduce running examples there: convert a static block to ` ```cljs-rf2 `, or add a cell next to it.
3. Do not convert every block. Keep code static when it is:
   - a fragment, an `ns` form or configuration;
   - server-side, or needs the unavailable pieces listed above;
   - or the live version would need setup that buries the point.

   A page with one well-chosen live example beats a page where every block runs. If a page gains nothing, leave it.
4. Within one page, give each cell's registrations distinct ids unless a later cell is meant to reuse an earlier one's. Cells share the registrar.
5. Fix stale prose you touch, but keep the diff to this section.

## How to verify

Nothing in CI runs the docs' cells, so clicking them yourself is the only check. Say what you clicked in the PR body.

- Build the engine: `cd docs/tools/playground && npm install && npm run build`. `npm run build:rf2` enters shadow-cljs, so it uses the machine-wide build lane; ask the coordinator for it first (`AGENTS.md`).
- Run `mkdocs serve` from the repo root. Open every page you changed and use every cell: it renders, its buttons and inputs work, and no cell shows `ERROR`. Then navigate to another page and back.
- Run `mkdocs build --strict` and `python scripts/check_doc_slugs.py`.
notes:
== Findings from rf2-oph8k.1 (live Fresco cells), for anyone writing docs cells ==
1. Material instant navigation claims any IN-SITE link click without checking defaultPrevented (its link filter returns early only for a target attribute or a modifier key). A cell anchor with href "#" and an ::h/prevent intent therefore re-fetched the page on its first click, which re-ran every cell and reset their state; later clicks pushState the "#". Workaround used in docs/core/fresco/03-events-as-data.md: the cell's anchors carry :target "_self", which Material skips, with a comment saying an application leaves it out. h/route-link hrefs such as "/active" sit outside the site's /re-frame2/ base, so Material ignores them. A playground-level fix (for example stopping propagation of clicks whose default a cell already prevented) would remove the need; not filed, per the dispatch.
2. A misspelled event id or subscription id does not reach a cell's result area: the dispatch or read fails quietly (the subscription reads nil, the click does nothing) and no console.error was observed either. Only a misspelled symbol (SCI "Unable to resolve symbol") or a throw during the synchronous Fresco render shows ERROR. Plant controls must use a misspelled symbol.

title: re-frame-migration: audit Form-3 update-hook dependencies before extracting a subscribing child (GH #10839)
description:
GitHub #10839. skills/re-frame-migration/references/guided-views-m11.md, Form-3 route 1 (extract the subscribing content into a reg-view child, preferred) does not first check whether the class's update hooks (component-did-update, after-render sizing or scrolling) depend on the reactive changes being moved. Once the read lives in the child, a child-only update no longer runs the parent class's componentDidUpdate, so DOM synchronization keyed to that update silently stops. The same leaf already documents passing reactive values from a registered outer view as plain props into an imperative class; the missing step is choosing update ownership deliberately before route 1.

Ask: a short lifecycle-dependency audit before route 1. If the class's update hooks depend on the subscribed value, keep update ownership by passing the value as a prop into the class (or a guarded post-commit callback from the updated child); keep per-mount handles, cleanup and repeat-commit/StrictMode behaviour explicit; no unconditional render-time DOM mutation as the replacement. The existing long-lived imperative-subscription exception stays a separate choice.

Issue acceptance asks for a worked example plus a browser regression (child-only value change with stable parent props, post-commit scroll or size verified, unmount cleanup, no duplicated imperative work on repeated commits). Proportionate reading: the worked example is the deliverable; cite React's componentDidUpdate contract for the claim; an executed check is welcome where a cheap runner exists, but do not add a browser suite to the skill for a docs correction.

Mayor triage 2026-10-04: valid, action it. The cited passage was re-read at trunk ef050b81af (after PR #10833 landed) and still reads as the issue says. Proportionate fix in the skill's existing voice: the GitHub issue closes when the PR merges (PR body carries `Fixes #N`); the mayor closes this bead at merge and verifies the issue reads CLOSED. Executed checks live in the worker's scratch and the PR body, not as new committed suites, unless an existing skill check already pins the passage.

title: core.cljc dispatch-impl comment and spec 008 recorder heading overstate what they do
description:
Found while implementing rf2-3vl7y (PR #10862). Two prose inaccuracies outside that PR's fence (implementation/** and spec/**). Neither changes behaviour.

1. implementation/core/src/re_frame/core.cljc, the comment above dispatch-impl, says "a SINGLE `with-redefs` on one of these (or the CLJS value-alias, which aliases the SAME var) intercepts every real dispatch". The parenthetical is false on CLJS. The Convention-A alias `(def dispatch dispatch-impl)` COPIES the value at load time: a shadow-cljs :node-test output carries `re_frame.core.dispatch = re_frame.core.dispatch_impl;`. CLJS with-redefs is a `set!` of `re_frame.core.dispatch`, and macro call sites compile to `re_frame.core.dispatch_impl...`, so a redef of the value alias cannot reach a macro call site. GH #10859 measured exactly that miss. The same holds for dispatch-sync and subscribe. Fix: drop the parenthetical, or say that the value alias reaches only value-position callers.

2. spec/008-Testing.md has the heading "### Recording dispatched events without firing handlers", but its example interceptor only records and returns ctx, so the handler still runs. A JVM control in rf2-3vl7y recorded [[:demo/clicked 1]] through a frame :interceptors recorder, and app-db showed that the real handler had written :clicks [1]. Fix: retitle it "Recording dispatched events", or show how to stub the handler as well.

title: re-frame-migration: one consistent first-compile contract across setup, inventory, sequencing, orchestration and SKILL.md (GH #10909)
description:
GitHub #10909 (filed by Mike). The migration references disagree about which rewrites may precede the first compile and whether that compile must succeed, so a planned migration can read as a requirement to compile a tree whose known blockers have not been removed.

Verified by the mayor at trunk e357364f22: skills/re-frame-migration/references/setup.md opens 'apply the coord swap; then verify the project compiles; then sweep for breakage' and closes 'Stop after M-0. Do not start sweeping for other M-rules until you've tried a compile and seen what - if anything - breaks.' The issue cites, at 8730e375bd: inventory-and-plan.md 'What the plan unblocks' (requires the planned forced PATCH/DROP/CONVERT sweep before compiling); sequencing.md (about L46, clears known compile blockers so the post-M0 gate is reachable); orchestrating-a-large-migration.md section 5 (first real whole-tree compile after all waves; the earlier failed diagnostic attempt vs the successful aggregate gate is not distinguished); SKILL.md Phase 0a and Phase 3 (inventory before any compile; the planned sweep applies whether or not the post-M0 compile succeeded).

Ask: make the first-compile contract consistent. (1) Distinguish read-only inventory searches from source rewrites; Phase 0a stays before dependency edits and compilation. (2) Name the prerequisite edits that may precede the post-M0 diagnostic attempt - classpath preparation and the inventory's approved forced blocker fixes - and explain how that diagnostic attempt relates to the large migration's consolidated acceptance compile. (3) State consistently that an attempted diagnostic compile need not pass before unrelated authorised Type A work proceeds. Keep real Type B holds and the full final compile/test/runtime/release acceptance bar.

Acceptance (from the issue): walk a small generic app and a large partitioned app whose retained add-on requires a removed framework namespace. Both produce their inventory without building; planned prerequisite repairs and the first diagnostic attempt have one unambiguous order; a failed attempt does not hold independent Type A sites; the large case distinguishes that attempt from its later consolidated gate and does not require repeated per-file compiles. Prior art: closed #10819 (M0 exclusion authority), closed #10855 (final verification-gate order) - keep both intact.

title: A registered Reagent view rejects more than ~20 positional arguments (Invalid arity: 30), because its frame-aware head is a cljs MetaFn; preserve keyword-variadic forwarding (GH #10967)
description:
GitHub #10967, filed by Mike. A registered Reagent view (rf/reg-view) whose caller passes more than about 20 positional arguments fails at mount with "Invalid arity: 30". This hits any keyword-variadic legacy view, for example [& {:keys [label]}] called with 15 key/value pairs. The consumer reproduced it in a real mounted native-click run, attributed to cljs.core.MetaFn.call / .apply under reagent.impl.component.wrap_render.
Mayor verified the cause in source at trunk b62df0e31e: implementation/core/src/re_frame/views.cljs build-frame-aware-view (about L553) returns (with-meta (fn frame-aware-view [& args] ...) {:contextType frame-context}) (about L641). The docstring at about L480-489 says with-meta on a fn yields a MetaFn, an IFn object, not a JS function. The issue reports that in the compiled ClojureScript, MetaFn.call switches on arguments.length - 1 over cases 0 to 21 and then throws, and MetaFn.apply calls it with the original array. So 30 arguments fail before the registered render wrapper runs.
skills/re-frame-migration/references/guided-views-m11.md (about L48) tells the migration to keep the original symbol and argument vector, and describes the reg-view* outer callable route for Form-2/Form-3. So the frame wrapper must preserve the consumer's argument forwarding rather than force a one-map ABI.

Ask:
- Make the registered Reagent head forward any number of arguments, while keeping the React contextType / frame context, the displayName stamp, tracing, source-coord annotation and lifecycle behaviour, and the UIx/React-hook componentize hook that wraps the MetaFn for non-Reagent substrates.
- Add real mounted keyword-variadic regressions with more than 21 scalar arguments: a Form-1 view, a Form-2 inner callable, and the applicable reg-view* path. Check the boundary counts (20, 21, 22) separately.
- Audit the M11 recipe against the corrected surface, and describe any remaining restriction with a preserving alternative.
- Never rewrite consumer calls into a one-map ABI to get green.

Mayor triage 2026-10-06 at trunk b62df0e31e: valid, filed by Mike; actioned. Read the issue in full (`gh issue view 10967 --json body,comments`). The PR carries 'Fixes #10967' on its own line; the mayor closes this bead at merge and verifies the issue reads CLOSED.
notes:
== RESULT (worker, 2026-10-06) — PR #10970, Fixes #10967

CAUSE, verified at source. build-frame-aware-view returned (with-meta (fn frame-aware-view [& args] ...) {:contextType frame-context}); with-meta on a fn yields cljs.core/MetaFn, an IFn object. shadow-cljs replaces cljs.core/add-ifn-methods (shadow/build/cljs_hacks.cljc, shadow-cljs 3.4.10): a deftype's .call switches on arguments.length - 1 over the defined -invoke arities 0..21 and throws "Invalid arity: N" otherwise, and .apply hands it the original array. Arity 21 is MetaFn's [a..t rest] method, so a 21st argument is read as a rest seq and 22+ throws. (Vanilla CLJS 1.12.145's .apply slices to 20 + rest and would forward correctly; the defect is under shadow-cljs, which this project builds with.) Stock Reagent 2.0.1 wrap-render calls the render fn with .call up to 4 args and (.apply f c (.slice (into-array argv) 1)) beyond; reagent-slim calls (apply render-fn args), and cljs.core/apply on an IFn object falls back to .apply past 20. A second site: when reagent-slim is on the compile classpath the reg-view expansion stamps {:reagent2/form ...} onto the (fn ...) form, the CLJS analyzer wraps a fn form carrying non-reader meta in with-meta, so the registered render-fn is itself a MetaFn and the head's (apply render-fn args) failed the same way (base CI stack: frame_aware_view__delegate -> cljs.core/apply -> apply_to_simple -> MetaFn.apply -> .call -> "Invalid arity: 23" for 21 args).

FIX (implementation/core/src/re_frame/views.cljs only, plus test prose). The head is the JS fn itself with IMeta specify!'d onto it, (specify! (fn frame-aware-view [& args] ...) IMeta (-meta [_] head-meta)) where head-meta is {:contextType frame-context}, so (meta head) still answers what Reagent's fn-to-class and reagent-slim read, and .apply is the platform's own. The head calls its render-fn through a new private unwrapped-fn, which returns the fn a MetaFn wraps (.-afn) or the value itself. displayName stamp, tracing, source-coord annotation, lifecycle, componentize hook and the head cache are unchanged. No adapter src, no public API name, no manifest change.

CONTROL. New tests: implementation/adapters/reagent/test/re_frame/reg_view_variadic_args_dom_cljs_test.cljs (Form-1 kw-variadic 15 pairs / 30 scalars: label, provider frame in head and in a registered child, mounted displayName; Form-2 outer+inner; reg-view* outer-callable Form-3; boundary 20, 21, 22 each a row; head-* rows on both lanes: head is a JS fn reached by .apply at 20/21/22/30, head meta :contextType is the frame context) and a reagent-slim twin. Tests-only commit CI: :browser-test 1101 tests / 6196 assertions, 24 failures 1 error, all 25 in the new namespaces (Invalid arity: 30 / 22, and 23 for 21 args; boundary 20 green); :node-test 10070 / 56079, 1 failure 1 error, both in the head-* row. Fix commit CI: :browser-test 1101 / 6198 and :node-test 10070 / 56081, 0 failures 0 errors each (+2 assertions per lane = the head-* row's assertions the base error cut short). Plant (render-fn unwrapping removed only; force-pushed away): :browser-test 1101 / 6197, 20 failures 1 error, every reg-view-macro row with 21+ args red (boundary 21 rendered "23|0"), reg-view* Form-3 and boundary 20 green; restore verified by blob hash (views.cljs default-form git hash-object equals the fix commit's blob) and git diff --quiet 0. Final head after rebase onto trunk 23b684d80c (docs/beads-only commits between): 64317f838b, same views.cljs blob; CI :browser-test 1101 / 6198 and :node-test 10070 / 56081, 0 failures 0 errors, All required checks passed green.

FENCE NOTE. The UIx boot-order row in adapters/uix/test/.../uix_reg_view_direct_mount_dom_cljs_test.cljs asserted (not (instance? js/Function head-at-registration)), which the fix makes false by design; its premise now asserts what the row depends on, that the reg-time head carries no UIx component marker (plus the docstring/comment sentences naming the MetaFn). Stale MetaFn prose left for a follow-up, comments only: core substrate/spine.cljs (~L2480, ~L2498, ~L3807), adapters/uix/src/re_frame/adapter/uix.cljs (~L285), tools/xray/test/.../managed_fx_template_cljs_test.cljs (~L639).

M11 AUDIT. No change needed. guided-views-m11.md L48's "same symbol and arg-vector" holds for any argument count, keyword-variadic included, for Form-1 and Form-2 reg-view and for the reg-view* outer-callable route (its examples are positional and register any callable). No framework restriction remains.

GATES. core JVM clojure -M:test baseline and final exit 0, 1705 tests / 10108 assertions both (no JVM delta). scripts/test-core-prod-gate.sh exit 0, 1473 tests / 7203 assertions (floor 1437). clj-kondo v2026.04.15 on the 5 changed files: 0 errors, 1 warning (pre-existing unused private var in views_adapter_switch_head_cljs_test.cljs, present at base). All scripts/check_*.py and check-*.sh exit 0.

Under shadow-cljs 3.4.10, which replaces cljs.core/add-ifn-methods (shadow/build/cljs_hacks.cljc), MetaFn .call handles up to 21 arguments and .apply passes the array straight through, so a 21st argument is read as a rest seq and 22 or more throws Invalid arity. title: Anonymous :rf.mutation/execute rows (generated instance ids) are never retired after settle
description:
## Bug

`:rf.mutation/execute` without `:instance` mints a generated instance id, and the settled row is never retired. Each anonymous execution leaves a terminal instance row (params, result, scope, timestamps) plus a work-ledger row in runtime-db. They accumulate for the frame's life, ride every epoch snapshot, and leave only through an explicit clear. The only clear the app can write without first capturing the generated id is `[:rf.mutation/clear {:mutation id}]`, and that also wipes the mutation's named instances, such as a form's error state.

## Evidence

Code at 475bdcaacf:
- `implementation/resources/src/re_frame/resources/mutation_events.cljc:111-123`: `mint-instance-id` returns `[:rf.mutation/instance mutation-id generation]` when no `:instance` is supplied.
- `implementation/resources/src/re_frame/resources/mutation_runtime.cljc:105-110`: a terminal instance is cleared only by explicit `:rf.mutation/clear` or by registration teardown.
- `mutation_events.cljc:1621-1690` (the clear handler): `{:instance id}` clears one row, and `{:mutation id}` clears every row of that mutation id, named or generated.
- `implementation/resources/src/re_frame/resources/work_ledger.cljc:542-599`: ledger tails are bounded per instance, not across instances.

Repro (*probed*: JVM, plain-atom substrate, a capturing `:rf.http/managed` stub, run at 989a1c6d53, whose resources tree is identical to 475bdcaacf):

```clojure
(rf/reg-mutation :m/like {:scope :rf.scope/global :params-schema [:map [:slug :string]]}
  (fn [{:keys [slug]} _] {:request {:method :post :url (str "/api/like/" slug)}}))
(dotimes [i 20]
  (rf/dispatch-sync [:rf.mutation/execute {:mutation :m/like :params {:slug (str "a" i)}}])
  (rf/dispatch-sync (conj (:on-success @last-args) {:status :ok :value {:liked (str "a" i)}})))
;; then one named execute (:instance :form/like) settles, then [:rf.mutation/clear {:mutation :m/like}]
```

Observed:

```
after 20 anonymous executes, each settled :success:
  instance rows: 20  statuses: {:success 20}
  sample instance keys: (affected-keys cause current-work error generation id id params patch-summary result scope settled-at started-at status)
  work-ledger rows (top-level keys): 20
after [:rf.mutation/clear {:mutation :m/like}]: instance rows: 0 (the named :form/like row is cleared too)
```

Contract:
- Spec 016 §Mutations (`spec/016-Resources.md:870`) allows a generated instance id, and makes `:rf.mutation/clear` the causal reset (`:874`).
- No clause gives a generated-id row a retirement rule. The failure-state lifetime the clear exists for, keeping a form's error until the user resets it, has no reader for a row whose id the caller never held.

## Expected

An anonymous execution leaves no row behind once it has settled and its continuation, if any, has been delivered. Named instances keep their form state until cleared or re-executed.

## Fix direction

- Retire generated-id instances, and their ledger rows, after accepted settlement and continuation delivery, reusing the clear handler's drop machinery.
- Concurrent pending anonymous attempts must still suppress late replies, and the `:rf.mutation/succeeded` / `:rf.mutation/failed` traces keep the instance id.
- A smaller alternative, Mike's call if preferred: require `:instance` on every execute.

## Acceptance

- New JVM test, failing before the fix (it reads 20 and 20 today): twenty anonymous executes, each settled, leave zero instance rows and zero `[:rf.mutation …]` ledger rows.
- A named instance that settles `:error` keeps its row until `[:rf.mutation/clear {:instance …}]`.
- Two concurrent anonymous executes, settled in reverse order, each deliver their own `:reply-to` exactly once.
- A late reply for a retired anonymous instance is suppressed.

## Notes

- Origin: Sol review (Sol 15 §5, independent). The Opus review adopted it (resources decision 13).
- Prior art: rf2-3x7nj.10 / rf2-3x7nj.11 ("Considered and rejected") called this the spec's failure-state lifetime, and pointed to the `{:mutation id}` clear. The probe shows that clear also wipes named form state.
- Latent today: every shipped example names its instances.
- Hot zones: none.
- Supporting detail: `ai/findings/advisarial-review/opus/resources.md` decision 13 and action 9; `ai/findings/advisarial-review/sol/15-resources.md` §5.
notes:
== FIXED ON BRANCH worker/resources-review, PR #11064 (worker, 2026-10-10 AUSEST) ==
Reproduced at base 72c951f102. Fix commit 947395b596.

Fix (the mayor's chosen direction, reusing the clear handler): mutation_events.cljc succeeded-handler and failed-handler, on an ACCEPTED reply for a generated instance id ([:rf.mutation/instance <id> <gen>]; the :rf.mutation/* head is reserved, so a caller-supplied id never has it), append [:dispatch [:rf.mutation/clear {:instance id}]] as the LAST fx, after the :reply-to continuation. The continuation therefore still reads the settled row (Spec 016 phase order), and the clear drops the instance row and every [:rf.mutation id] ledger row. Caller-supplied instances are untouched. :instance stays optional. A stale reply goes down the suppressed path, which already writes no row: settle-terminal and update-record do nothing for a dropped ledger row.

Spec 016: the Mutations invariant on instance ids says a generated-id instance is retired. Ledger-retention clause 3 says the same. Phase order gains step 7, Retirement.

Tests (resources_mutation_cljs_test.cljc, new section on generated-id retirement): 20 anonymous executes, alternating success and error, leave 0 instance rows and 0 mutation ledger rows. A supplied :instance that settles :error keeps its row and 1 ledger row until [:rf.mutation/clear {:instance ...}]. Two concurrent anonymous executes, settled in reverse order, each deliver their own :reply-to exactly once, each continuation reads its own row as :success, and both then retire. A late reply for a retired instance emits only :rf.mutation/stale-suppressed, fires no continuation, and recreates no row.

- green: exit 0, 58 / 186.

title: Spec 011 says a malformed reserved :rf.server/* fx still renders the page in dev; dev and release both return 500
description:
## Bug

Spec 011 and two SSR source comments say that in a dev build with the schemas artefact, a malformed reserved `:rf.server/*` fx is skipped and "the page still renders". It does not: in dev the Malli failure is buffered by the SSR error listener and the default projector maps it to a 500, exactly as in release. Only the diagnostic differs between builds. A reader (or an AI pair) predicting dev behaviour from the spec gets the wrong answer.

## Evidence

- `spec/011-SSR.md:1038` (trunk 475bdcaacf): "In dev with the schemas artefact present the Malli boundary gets there first: the effect is `:skipped`, the programmer gets `:rf.error/schema-validation-failure :where :fx-args` naming the failing path, and the page still renders. In a release build ... it fails closed instead."
- Same claim in code comments: `implementation/ssr/src/re_frame/ssr/response.cljc:128-131` ("dev-with-schemas gets the Malli step-5 skip ... and the page still renders") and `implementation/ssr/src/re_frame/ssr/server_fx_schemas.cljc:57-61` ("the fx is `:skipped`, siblings continue, the page still renders").
- Why it is a 500 in dev: `validate-fx!` emits the frame-tagged `:rf.error/schema-validation-failure` with `:where :fx-args`; the dev trace listener the SSR façade installs (`implementation/ssr/src/re_frame/ssr.cljc:407-421`) buffers it; `default-error-projector-fn` sends anything but `:where :event` to the generic 500 (`implementation/ssr/src/re_frame/ssr/error_projector.cljc:221-231`).
- Repro, *probed* (JVM, `implementation/ssr` with `day8/re-frame2-schemas` on the classpath; default projector; dev, then `-Dre-frame.debug=false`):
  ```clojure
  (rf/reg-event ::attempt
    (fn [_ _] {:fx [[:rf.server/set-status "not-an-int"]
                    [:rf.server/append-header {:name "X-Sibling" :value "ran"}]]}))
  ;; server frame, dispatch-sync [::attempt], then (rf.ssr/flush-response-result! f)
  ```
  ```
  dev:     {:response-status 500, :public-error {:status 500 :code :internal-error ...}, :sibling-ran? true, :always-on-records []}
  release: {:response-status 500, :public-error {:status 500 :code :internal-error ...}, :sibling-ran? true, :always-on-records [:rf.error/fx-handler-exception]}
  ```
  Both postures take the error arm; the sibling fx runs in both.

## Expected

Spec 011 and the comments describe what the runtime does: one malformed reserved fx sends the request to the 500 error arm in every build, with a different diagnostic in dev (`:rf.error/schema-validation-failure :where :fx-args`) and release (`:rf.error/fx-handler-exception` on the always-on axis).

## Fix direction

Correct the prose to match the behaviour, which both reviews consider right (an honest 500 beats a silently dropped `Set-Cookie`): rewrite 011:1038 so dev and release both "take the error arm", differing only in diagnostic, and fix the two comments the same way. No code change. If Mike instead wants dev to skip-and-render, that is a behaviour change to the SSR listener or projector, and this becomes that bead.

## Acceptance

- `spec/011-SSR.md`, `response.cljc` and `server_fx_schemas.cljc` no longer claim the page renders in dev after a malformed reserved fx.
- Optional, cheap: a JVM test running the repro above asserts `:public-error` status 500 and the sibling header present, so the two-posture claim is pinned (it passes today; it fails if someone makes the prose true by accident).
- `mkdocs build --strict` and `scripts/check_doc_slugs.py` pass.

## Notes

- Origin: Sol review (SSR rendering §6) predicted it by reading; Opus's cross-review probed both postures and withdrew its own earlier "dev 200 / release 500" claim (ssr decision 6, conflict C1). Re-probed at trunk during bead drafting.
- Related: rf2-6c25z (open) lists a neighbouring stale comment in `ssr.cljc:407-414` about schema-validation failure being dev-only; the two are easy to fix in one pass.
- Hot zones: none (`spec/011-SSR.md` is not on the list).
- Supporting detail: `ai/findings/advisarial-review/opus/ssr.md` decision 6 item 1; `ai/findings/advisarial-review/sol/27-ssr-rendering.md` §6.

The prose was the fault, so only the prose changed:

title: Make run-to-completion true: two per-frame lanes (internal/external) replace machine-origin queue priority; ships in one PR with rf2-mn2ht.20
description:
## Bug

Spec 002's run-to-completion headline contradicts the detailed rules in the same spec and in Spec 005:
- The headline: everything an event dispatches drains before any further external event.
- The detailed rules: a plain handler's child goes to the back of the queue, behind external events already waiting, and only machine-originated children jump ahead.

The code follows the detailed rules. So a reader, human or AI, who trusts the headline predicts the wrong order. A synchronous decide-then-commit chain can also be interleaved by an external event queued behind it. One origin-independent rule has to be chosen.

## Evidence

**The contradiction (trunk 475bdcaacf):**
- **Headline:** `spec/002-Frames.md:1820`: "every event dispatched (synchronously) during its handler — and every event those handlers dispatch in turn — drains to fixed point before any further external event is processed *for this frame*". `spec/Runtime-Architecture.md:163` restates it.
- **Against it:**
  - `spec/002-Frames.md:1855` (Rule 2) limits the guarantee to *actor messages*.
  - `spec/002-Frames.md:1843` and `:2335` (edge case #3): `:dispatch` "from a plain handler … lands at the back (FIFO); from a *machine* handler it leap-frogs to the front".
  - `spec/005-StateMachines.md:1299-1305` (§Level 4): "FIFO by default with one exception … for a *non-machine* handler, `:fx [[:dispatch :ev-X]]` emitted during event Y lands at the back".
  - `spec/002-Frames.md:1876`: "Domain events from outside the frame wait until the current drain settles". Yet an external event queued while a drain runs is processed inside that drain.
- **Code:**
  - `implementation/core/src/re_frame/router.cljc:4364-4368` (`insert-envelope`): the flow settle goes to the head, a machine-internal envelope is spliced to the front, and everything else is `conj`ed to the back.
  - `router.cljc:3018-3025`: a plain handler clears an inherited `:rf.machine/internal?`, so its children go to the back. Trunk commit 69c8e0e89c added this after the flag had leaked onto plain handlers' children.

**Repro (*probed*):** JVM, `clojure -M` from `implementation/core`, plain-atom adapter. Run at HEAD 9b20bf0093, whose `implementation/core` is byte-identical to 475bdcaacf.

```clojure
(rf/reg-event :probe/block2  (fn [_ _] (swap! log conj :block) (deliver started2 true) @gate2 nil))
(rf/reg-event :probe/a       (fn [_ _] (swap! log conj :a) {:fx [[:dispatch [:probe/a-child]]]}))
(rf/reg-event :probe/a-child (fn [_ _] (swap! log conj :a-child) nil))
(rf/reg-event :probe/b       (fn [_ _] (swap! log conj :b) nil))
(rf/dispatch [:probe/block2] {:frame :probe/h})
(rf/dispatch [:probe/a] {:frame :probe/h})   ; external: main thread, outside any handler
(rf/dispatch [:probe/b] {:frame :probe/h})   ; external
(deliver gate2 true)
;; order => [:block :a :b :a-child]   (the headline promises [:block :a :a-child :b])
```

On CLJS a click callback doing `(dispatch [:a]) (dispatch [:b])` builds the same queue (read).

A handler that itself dispatches `[:a]` and `[:b]` gives `[:a :b :a-child]`. That is correct breadth-first sibling order (005:1371), so it is not evidence of a violation. Only externally queued events show the contradiction.

Inferred, not reproduced: routing's queued link-A then navigate-B can interleave its decide/commit pairs and end with route A and URL B.

## Expected

Spec 002, Spec 005 and Runtime-Architecture state one ordering rule that does not depend on the dispatch's origin, and the router implements exactly that rule.

## Fix direction — Mike chooses one

All three options are deterministic.

- **(a) Two lanes per frame (recommended by the Opus review; Sol 04 §3 leans the same way).**
  - *Internal* lane: everything enqueued while that frame's event is in flight, FIFO, with the flow settle at its head.
  - *External* lane: everything else, including timer fires and async replies, FIFO.
  - The drain always empties the internal lane first.
  - Effects: the headline becomes true and sibling order is kept. `:rf.machine/internal?`, `front-insert-machine-internal` and its O(n) queue rebuild are deleted, and rf2-mn2ht.20 gets its family boundary for free.
  - Cost: an observable ordering change, and conformance fixtures move.
- **(b) Uniform FIFO, headline narrowed** (the machines review's D8).
  - Every dispatch appends, and machine priority goes. `:raise` stays the intra-macrostep tool.
  - Keeps v1's "dispatch appends".
- **(c) Today's hybrid, headline narrowed** to match Rule 2 and 005 §Level 4.
  - Spec-only.
  - Keeps the origin flag, which has already leaked once.

Only (a) shields synchronous chains from queued external events.

## Acceptance

- **Any option:** `spec/002-Frames.md:1820`, `:1855`, `:1876`, the drain pseudocode, `spec/005-StateMachines.md` §Level 4 and `spec/Runtime-Architecture.md:163` state the one chosen rule. A test pins the external probe's order under that rule.
- **For (a):**
  - The probe gives `[:block :a :a-child :b]`.
  - The handler-dispatched sibling shape stays `[:a :b :a-child]`.
  - The flow settle still precedes queued continuations.
  - `dispatch-sync` still runs its seed's family first.
  - `:rf.machine/internal?` greps to zero in `implementation/`.

## Notes

- Origin: Opus review (core-event-pipeline D1; probe corrected after Sol 04 §3 showed the first probe was mis-specified).
- Related: rf2-mn2ht.20 (its per-cascade budget is simplest under (a)). Sequence rf2-mn2ht.20 after this ruling, because both edit `spec/002-Frames.md` and the router's queue and drain code. rf2-3x7nj.1.2 (closed) fixed a `:dispatch-later` child inheriting the machine flag.
- Hot zones: `spec/002-Frames.md`, `spec/005-StateMachines.md`. Under (a), also `router.cljc` (not a hot-zone file) and conformance fixtures.
- Supporting detail: `ai/findings/advisarial-review/opus/core-event-pipeline.md` D1, action 3 and open question 1; `ai/findings/advisarial-review/sol/04-core-events-effects.md` §3.
notes:
== RULING (delegated by Mike; decided 2026-10-10 23:52:00 AUSEST at HEAD 57b1acab35) ==

DECISION: Option (a), two lanes per frame, classified CAUSALLY, shipped in ONE PR together with rf2-mn2ht.20's per-family budget.
- A dispatch made synchronously from within the target frame's in-flight event goes to that frame's INTERNAL lane. "Within the event" covers its handler (plain or machine), its interceptors, its :fx walk, imperative rf/dispatch calls in the handler body, machine continuations, same-frame spawn starts and completion carriers.
- Every other dispatch goes to the EXTERNAL lane. That covers UI callbacks, timers (including a machine's :dispatch-later at 0 ms), HTTP and socket replies, other frames, other threads, the REPL and after-render work.
- Both lanes are FIFO. The drain always dequeues from the internal lane first. The framework-private flow settle goes to the head of the internal lane.
- dispatch-sync's seed runs first, and the seed's whole family settles before any external input that was already queued.
- Machine-origin queue priority is deleted outright: the :rf.machine/internal? flag, front-insert-machine-internal and the plain-handler clearing branch all go. The :source :machine-action trace stamp stays, derived from the emitting handler's kind rather than from anything the queue reads.
- The spec's existing headline (002:1820), Rule 2, 002:1876, migration M-3 and the skill all become true as written. Spec 005 Level 4 is rewritten as that one origin-independent rule.

WHY:
- It makes the words everyone already believes true, instead of retracting them. Humans and AI pairs are taught "one outside dispatch settles before the next starts" in the 002 headline, in Runtime-Architecture:163, in migration M-3:144 and in the shipped skill (event-state-cycle.md:45, :121). Making those true is the lowest-friction outcome. It also leaves the hot migration guide untouched, which (b) and (c) cannot do.
- It is ONE rule with no origin flag: "what an event dispatches settles before the next outside event." Today, whether a dispatch jumps the queue depends on whether the emitter is a machine, which is invisible at the call site. That flag has leaked twice (rf2-3x7nj.1.2; commit 69c8e0e89c), every new dispatch site has to remember to dissoc it, and it costs an O(n) queue rebuild per insert. Deleting it is elegance by subtraction.
- It keeps Mike's 2026-05-22 Level-4 intent and generalises it (commit 903e2b8d0a: "a machine completes its macrostep to quiescence before the next external event"). A machine still settles before external input; now every handler does. A plain relay no longer loses priority (S3), and a machine child no longer overtakes an earlier sibling from its own cascade (S4).
- It shields decide-then-commit chains split across events from unrelated queued input. That is the bug class rf2-mn2ht.5 hit in routing (since fixed locally by committing in one event); it stays open for app code under (b) and (c).
- rf2-mn2ht.20's family boundary falls out for free: the internal lane IS the current family. No cascade-root stamp is needed.
- The latency cost is smaller than it looks. On CLJS a drain runs until both lanes are empty, so an external event queued before the drain still runs in the SAME drain, before the next render; only its position changes. Paint latency is unchanged. On the JVM, external input arriving mid-family waits for that family, bounded by the budget. Note that this bounds events admitted, not elapsed time.
- Pre-alpha is the time to change an ordering rule. Every reviewer recommends (a), and nobody split on values, so this did not need to go back to Mike.

REJECTED:
- (b) Uniform FIFO, headline narrowed. It is the simplest code and matches v1's "dispatch appends". But it retracts the guarantee everywhere: the hot migration guide, the skill, Runtime-Architecture and the 002 headline. It reverses Mike's Level-4 rule, leaves decide/commit pairs and two-machine handshakes exposed to queued input (:raise only helps inside one machine), and makes .20 need a root stamp on every envelope. It trades a stronger contract for a slightly smaller diff, the wrong trade under the stance.
- (c) Keep the hybrid, narrow the headline. It is the cheapest now and the most expensive to keep. Ordering stays dependent on an origin flag nobody can see, which has leaked twice. The O(n) splice stays, the interleaving bug class stays, and .20 needs the root stamp.
- "Change nothing" is not an option: the spec contradicts itself, and the shipped skill teaches the false half.

WHERE THE REVIEWS AGREED / DISAGREED:
- All three opinions chose (a): the bead (Opus review, with Sol 04 §3 leaning the same way), the dossier author and Codex. All three rank (b) as the coherent alternative and (c) last.
- Dossier author vs Codex on the classifier. The dossier proposed the thread-bound *event-owner* (frame.cljc, current-event-envelope) as the existing causal test. Codex showed it is not sufficient, and I re-probed at HEAD and agree with Codex (S7 below). Clojure conveys dynamic bindings into futures, and a captured bound-fn still sees the envelope after the event returned. *event-owner* carries no host-thread identity and no liveness check; current-event-envelope compares only the frame id. SETTLED: classify by "the target frame is executing an event on THIS host thread right now", a private execution-scope check that goes inactive when the event returns. The router's :scheduled?/busy flag is not enough either, because it is true for the whole drain, including while another thread enqueues (S5).
- Sequencing. The dossier says .20 lands "in the same change, or strictly back to back"; Codex says "one delivered change". SETTLED: one PR closing both, with a fallback below.
- The default budget. The dossier says raise it to about 1,000; Codex says that is "a separate sizing choice". SETTLED: 1,000, as .20's own fix direction proposes. A 151-event fan-out family cannot fit 100 under any lane rule, and .20's acceptance needs it to.
- SCXML framing. Codex corrected the dossier's "SCXML-aligned" rationale. SCXML's internal queue is :raise (005 Level 3), and SCXML C.1 sends inter-session messages to the receiver's EXTERNAL queue. So frame-wide internal priority is a deliberate re-frame2 composition guarantee, not an SCXML requirement, and the spec must say it that way. Agreed.
- The bead's acceptance clause "dispatch-sync still runs its seed's family first" is false today; only the seed runs first (S6). Under (a) the clause becomes true, so read it as "now runs".

EVIDENCE (probe at HEAD 9b51da3393; every cited source, spec, test, fixture and skill file is byte-unchanged through 57b1acab35, the only intervening edits being unrelated Spec 009 handled-events rows):
- Command: cd implementation/core && java -cp "$(clojure -Spath -M:test)" clojure.main probe_head.clj. Exit 0, empty stderr. Real registered handlers on the plain-atom adapter. "External" means dispatched from the main thread, outside any handler, while a blocker event holds the drain.
  - S1 externals a, b queued behind a busy event; a dispatches a-child: [:block :a :b :a-child]. Under (a): [:block :a :a-child :b].
  - S2 one event kick dispatches a, b; a dispatches a-child: [:kick :a :b :a-child]. Unchanged under every option (breadth-first siblings, 005:1371).
  - S3 externals machine m, then b; m dispatches plain m-child, which dispatches m-grandchild: [:block :m :m-child :b :m-grandchild]. Under (a): [:block :m :m-child :m-grandchild :b].
  - S4 kick dispatches machine m, then sib; m dispatches m-child: [:kick :m :m-child :sib]. Under (a): [:kick :m :sib :m-child].
  - S5 x dispatched from thread "main" while a runs on "pool-1-thread-1"; a then dispatches a-child: [:a :x :a-child], with x running inside the same drain. Under (a): [:a :a-child :x].
  - S6 drain held (next-tick captured with with-redefs), q1 and q2 queued, then dispatch-sync seed, which dispatches seed-child: [:seed :q1 :q2 :seed-child]. Under (a): [:seed :seed-child :q1 :q2].
  - S7 inside a real handler: {:in-future {:has-envelope? true, :same-thread? false}, :in-handler true, :bound-fn-after-return true, :outside-any-handler false}.
  - D1 one handler fans out 150 children: ran 99, error {:depth 100 :queue-size 51}.
  - D2 150 external events plus :other behind a busy event: ran 99, :other did not run, {:depth 100 :queue-size 52}.
  - D3 runaway self-dispatch loop with :other queued behind it: loop ran 98, :other DID run, {:depth 100 :queue-size 1}. :other survives only because FIFO interleaves it, so (a) without .20 would starve and then drop it.
- The contradiction at HEAD:
  - 002:1820 (headline): "every event dispatched (synchronously) during its handler — and every event those handlers dispatch in turn — drains to fixed point before any further external event is processed for this frame".
  - 002:1855 Rule 2 covers actor messages only.
  - 002:1924: "From a plain (non-machine) handler they append to the back (FIFO); from a machine handler they are inserted at the front".
  - 005:1299: "FIFO by default with one exception".
  - 002:1876: "Domain events from outside the frame wait until the current drain settles", which S5 refutes.
- Code at HEAD:
  - router.cljc:4361-4364 insert-envelope holds the three clauses: the settle goes to the head, a flagged envelope goes through the splice, everything else is conj.
  - router.cljc:4288-4309 is front-insert-machine-internal: split-with, then a rebuild.
  - router.cljc:3014-3021 sets the flag when the handler carries :rf/machine? and dissocs it otherwise.
  - fx.cljc:674 copies the flag onto :dispatch children; fx.cljc:742 drops it for :dispatch-later; fx.cljc:913 and :968 derive :source :machine-action from it.
  - Spawn drops it by hand at machines spawn.cljc:1552 and spawn_error.cljc:112.
  - router/diagnostics.cljc:153 lists it as a known dispatch opt.
  - frame.cljc:3704-3713 defines *event-owner* as a plain dynamic var with no thread field; 3738-3752 is current-event-envelope.
  - router.cljc:4382-4392 is a PRECEDENT for the fix: *frame-destroy-cascade* already pairs its binding with (identical? owner (Thread/currentThread)), because "JVM bound-fn may convey dynamic bindings to an executor".

IMPLEMENTATION GUIDANCE (one worker, one PR, closing rf2-mn2ht.21 AND rf2-mn2ht.20; see the RULED UNDER note on .20 for the budget semantics):
- Router, implementation/core/src/re_frame/router.cljc:
  - Two lanes in the router atom. Keep :queue as the EXTERNAL lane's name: the xray CLJS tests and frame.cljc read (:queue @router) for external dispatches. Add an :internal lane.
  - insert-envelope (4359-4364) chooses the lane by the causal check. Both enqueue paths already route through it (enqueue-envelope! and ensure-drain-scheduled!). head-insert stays, for the settle at the head of the internal lane. Delete front-insert-machine-internal (4288-4309).
  - The dequeue (take-event!) pops internal first.
  - Delete the tag/clear cond in process-event! (3014-3021).
  - The causal scope: around each event's processing (handler + interceptors + fx walk), record the executing host thread for the frame, and clear it in a finally. An enqueue is internal iff that slot names Thread/currentThread on the JVM, or iff the slot is set on CLJS. Do NOT use *event-owner* or current-event-envelope alone (S7), and do NOT use :scheduled? (S5). No new public dispatch opt.
  - dispatch-sync seed-push (4733-4739): the seed must run first and its children land internal. Do not cons it onto a mixed queue.
  - Remove the flag from the build-envelope opts plumbing (around 357-456) and from the dispatch! docstring (4395-4410).

Re-key :source :machine-action (around 900-968) on whether the EMITTING handler is a machine (its :rf/machine? registration meta), threaded through a private seam that insert-envelope never reads. :source is not inherited by children (009:141).

title: Production error coords ship a classpath-relative :file (omitted when only an absolute path is known); fix Privacy.md items 1-2
description:
## Bug

Every production (`:advanced`, `goog.DEBUG=false`) bundle embeds the build machine's absolute source paths as string literals, one per macro-driven registration: `/home/<user>/…`, `/Users/<user>/…`, `C:/Users/<user>/…`. Anyone who can fetch the app's JS can read the builder's directory layout and username.

This is the documented contract today, not an accident. But the reason given for absolutising the path is a dev-tool one, editor-URI resolution, while production only needs to name a source line for error reports. So the contract deserves a decision rather than a fix.

## Evidence

- `implementation/core/src/re_frame/source_coords.cljc:738-768` — `prod-coords-form`, the production branch of every `reg-*` macro's coords (`core_reg_macros.cljc:66, 531`; `core_reg_view_macro.cljc:137`), runs `(absolutise-file chosen-file)` (`:765`) at macro-expansion time and emits `{:ns … :file <absolute path> :line …}`.
- `source_coords.cljc:595-604` — "PRODUCTION KEEPS THIS PATH … A release bundle therefore carries the BUILDING MACHINE's directory layout, once per macro-driven registration. That is the contract rather than an oversight".
- `source_coords.cljc:566-593` — the stated reason to absolutise: "`:project-root` plus the classpath-relative tail produces the wrong on-disk path", which breaks Story and Xray's `open-in-editor` chip. That is a dev tool.
- `spec/Privacy.md:53-59` (§What the production bundle itself discloses) — the always-on error-coord registry keeps coords in production "so that Sentry / Honeybadger / Rollbar reports keep source-line information". The `:file` "is absolutised deliberately so the editor-URI builder resolves regardless of the host's `:project-root`". The remedy offered is to "build in a neutral working directory".
- *Read*, not re-measured here. The commit that wrote the Privacy.md section (`554a7dad87`) records measuring the paths in a real `:advanced` release bundle.

## Expected

Production bundles carry only what the always-on error record needs to name a source line, or the current disclosure stays as an explicit, re-affirmed choice.

## Fix direction

Mike's call:

- **A. Keep** the contract as documented, and close this bead with the ruling recorded.
- **B. Drop `:file`** from `prod-coords-form`. `:ns` plus `:line` locate the line for Sentry-style reports. The dev form keeps the absolute `:file` for editor URIs. This is the Opus observability review's recommendation (TWEAK, small contract change).
- **C. Emit the classpath-relative `:file`** in production (no `absolutise-file` on the prod branch), keeping a file hint without the builder's layout.

B and C change the production error record's `:source-coord` shape, so off-box consumers that read `:file` would change. They also touch Spec 001 §Production elision contract, `spec/Privacy.md` §What the production bundle itself discloses, and Spec-Schemas `:rf/source-coord-meta`. Under B or C, decide too whether compiled-declaration manifest site coords (Privacy.md item 2) follow the same rule.

## Acceptance

- **A:** the ruling is recorded on the bead.
- **B or C:**
  - a JVM macro-expansion test asserts the prod coords form carries no absolute path (no leading `/`, drive letter or `file:`), while the dev form still does;
  - the elision probe or bundle check, run against an `:advanced` release bundle, finds no build-machine path prefix;
  - the Spec 001 and Privacy.md text matches.

## Notes

- Origin: Opus review (core observability §11); Sol confirmed it in source after reading the Opus report.
- Related: none open.
- Hot-zone files:
  - option A touches none;
  - options B and C touch `spec/Spec-Schemas.md` (hot) for `:rf/source-coord-meta`, if its shape note changes;
  - `spec/001-Registration.md` and `spec/Privacy.md` are not hot.
- Supporting detail: `ai/findings/advisarial-review/opus/core-observability.md` §11.
notes:
== RULING (delegated by Mike; decided 2026-10-10 23:44:49 AUSEST at HEAD 9b51da3393) ==

DECISION: Option C, tightened to a "relative-or-absent" rule. In production (the `prod-coords-form` arm that survives `:advanced` + `goog.DEBUG=false`, and JVM SSR under `-Dre-frame.debug=false`), the error coordinate's `:file` is the classpath-relative path the reader supplied, emitted verbatim; when the only path available is absolute (`rf.source-coords.editor-uri/absolute-path?` true: leading `/`, drive letter, backslash or `file:`), `:file` is OMITTED and the coordinate ships `{:ns :line}`. `:ns` and `:line` are unchanged. The dev arm (`coords-form`, with `:column`) stays absolute for the editor-URI tools. No knob. Privacy.md item 1 is rewritten to match (its "neutral working directory" remedy and its stale "that registry" wording both go), and Privacy.md item 2 (the Freehand compiled-manifest leftover) is deleted.

WHY:
- The absolute production path was never chosen. Commit `69f191c8a1` (which introduced `absolutise-file`) fixed the dev open-in-editor chip and hooked `prod-coords-form` along with `coords-form` and `form-coords`; its message reasons only about the editor URI. Commit `554a7dad87` (which wrote the Privacy.md section) explicitly left relativising "open ... to the operator". No ruling ever picked it.
- Nothing in production consumes the absolute form. `:ns` is the only load-bearing key (image selection reads it off the live `*pending-coords*` binding, `source_store.cljc:232-244`, EP-0023); `:file` is transported to error sinks and read by people and AI pairs, for whom a checkout-independent path is MORE useful than the builder's laptop path.
- The leak is real and the remedy offered today does not cover it: a git dependency resolves to a `file:` URL under `~/.gitlibs/...`, so its registrations ship that absolute path even from a CI build in a "neutral" directory. And bundle bytes depend on the build directory (content hashes / SRI differ for no semantic reason).
- Under the stance: one tiny rule in one function, the published record keeps its keys whenever a portable path exists, the schema already allows it, no configuration, and production output becomes uniform (jar-sourced registrations already ship a classpath-relative `:file` today, because `absolutise-file` returns non-`file:` URLs unchanged, `source_coords.cljc:712-714`).
- The "or absent" half is what makes C actually true rather than true-for-shadow-only (see EVIDENCE: the native ClojureScript compiler hands the reader an absolute path, so merely deleting the `absolutise-file` call would still ship builder paths for cljs.main / figwheel-main builds). Omitting is the simplest honest answer for that case: such builds degrade to option B's shape, which every reviewer agreed is adequate.

REJECTED:
- A (keep, re-affirm): every shipped app keeps disclosing the builder's username and layout for a benefit only dev tools use, and dev already has its own absolute form. Nobody recommended it.
- B (drop `:file` in production always; the Opus review's recommendation carried in this bead's description): sound and simple, but it throws away a useful hint (the real file and its `.cljs` / `.cljc` extension) in the common shadow-cljs case to save about 30 bytes per registration, which gzip mostly erases (measured: 51 bytes saved on a 318,717-byte gzipped probe bundle by relativising all 24 path literals). The relative-or-absent rule gives B's privacy outcome exactly where C alone would fail, and keeps the hint everywhere else.
- C as a bare one-line deletion (the dossier author's literal proposal): correct for shadow-cljs, but passes already-absolute reader metadata straight through (native CLJS compiler, JVM `load-file`), so the leak survives for those builds.
- A build-time knob (absolute vs relative): configuration nobody needs.
- Deriving a relative path from an absolute one (e.g. matching the munged `:ns` against the path's tail, or searching source roots): not wanted. Small, but it is speculative machinery for a minority build path whose `{:ns :line}` fallback is already enough.

WHERE THE REVIEWS AGREED / DISAGREED:
- Both the dossier author and the Codex reviewer recommended C; both rejected A; both rated B acceptable but inferior. The bead description carries the Opus review's B. Ruled C over B for the reasons above.
- Disagreement 1, on the fix's sufficiency. Dossier: delete the `absolutise-file` call at `source_coords.cljc:809`, done. Codex: the native ClojureScript compiler supplies an absolute filename to the reader, so the deletion alone still ships absolute paths; rule should be "relative when available, otherwise omit". SETTLED FOR CODEX by reading the compiler source and by a JVM probe (EVIDENCE below).
- Disagreement 2, on an existing test. Dossier: `source_coords_test.clj` `registration-file-is-absolute` "runs with debug on, so it stays green". Codex: its absolute assertion is unconditional; only its public-meta comparison is debug-gated. SETTLED FOR CODEX: at HEAD the test (lines 125-138) asserts `(rf.source-coords.editor-uri/absolute-path? f)` outside any posture guard, and the namespace runs in the JVM production-gate lane too (it is not on `scripts/test-core-prod-gate.sh`'s `known_red` roster, and that lane runs every namespace outside the roster under `-Dre-frame.debug=false`). On the JVM the prod arm reads `*file*`, which under `require` is classpath-relative (`re_frame/source_coords_test.clj`), so after the fix that assertion goes red in the `jvm-core-prod-gate` CI job unless it is posture-split.
- Both reviews agree, and I confirmed, that Privacy.md item 2 is a Freehand leftover: `{:compiled true}` / `v/manifest` / "compiled declaration" appear in no tracked file under `spec/` or `implementation/` other than Privacy.md (hits remain only in `docs/design/freehand/**`, `docs/EP/EP-0036-...`, the `skills/reagent-fresco-migration/spec/**` design inputs, and untracked `implementation/out/` build artefacts). This also settles the bead's sub-question "do compiled-declaration manifest site coords follow the same rule": moot, there are none.

EVIDENCE:
- `implementation/core/src/re_frame/source_coords.cljc` at HEAD 9b51da3393 (unchanged since the dossier's read at 5eef8e1e2c):
  - `prod-coords-form` is `:781-812`; the absolutise call is `:808-809`: `(let [chosen-file (resolve-file form-meta file) chosen-file (when chosen-file (absolutise-file chosen-file))] ...)`.
  - `coords-form` (dev arm) is `:723-779`; its absolutise is `:770-772`.
  - `resolve-file` `:592-608` picks `(:file form-meta)`, else `*file*`, rejecting the `"NO_SOURCE_PATH"` sentinel; it never relativises.
  - `absolutise-file` `:671-721` passes through anything `absolute-path?`, unresolvable, or a non-`file:` URL.
  - The "PRODUCTION KEEPS THIS PATH ... That is the contract rather than an oversight" comment is `:639-650`; the rationale block (multi-source-root editor-URI failure) is `:610-637`.
- Emission sites, all wrap `(if re-frame.interop/debug-enabled? <coords-form> <prod-coords-form>)`: `core_reg_macros.cljc:63-66` (`with-coords-form`, every `defreg-macro` surface), `core_reg_macros.cljc:528-531` (`expand-reg-machine`), `core_reg_view_macro.cljc:135-137` (`reg-view`). `prod-coords-form` is the single production carrier; every other coordinate (public `handler-meta` coords via `merge-coords`, machine element coords, call-site coords, `:rf.handler/source`, Fresco `defview`/`defhost` coords) is dev-gated and DCE'd.
- Runtime path: `registrar.cljc:643-645` attaches the bound map to the descriptor; `error_emit.cljc:393-414` reads it into the error record's `:source-coord`. `spec/015-Data-Classification.md:305` makes `:source-coord` a summary slot ("build metadata, not runtime data") that passes every egress profile including `:rf.egress/public-error` — so no runtime privacy profile can remove the literal; only the macro can.
- Native ClojureScript compiler (the version on this repo's classpath, `org.clojure/clojurescript 1.12.145`, read from the jar in `~/.m2`): `cljs/compiler.cljc:1651` reads forms with `(ana/forms-seq* rdr (util/path src))`, and `cljs/util.cljc:172-174` defines `path` as `(file? x) (.getAbsolutePath ^File x)`. So under cljs.main / figwheel-main, `(:file (meta &form))` is ABSOLUTE. Codex separately read shadow-cljs 3.4.10's `shadow/build/compiler.clj:414-421`, which supplies the classpath-relative `resource-name` to the indexing reader.
- JVM probe of the rule (mine). Command: `cd implementation/core && clojure -M -i <scratch>/probe_rule.clj`; exit 0. The probe calls the real `prod-coords-form`, `resolve-file` and `editor-uri/absolute-path?` and builds the ruled shape with `(cond-> {:ns ...} (and chosen (not (absolute-path? chosen))) (assoc :file chosen) ...)`. Output:

- Who hits the leak today: any app shipping a CLJS bundle exposes `C:/Users/<name>/clients/<client>/<project>/src/...` (or `/Users/<name>/...`). CI builds leak less (`/home/runner/work/<repo>/<repo>/...`) but git dependencies resolve to `file:` URLs under `~/.gitlibs/...`, so their registrations are absolute even on CI — the "neutral working directory" remedy never covered them. Severity: a low-grade information leak; no user data, no crash, no wrong answer; P3 is right.
- Reproducibility: the same commit built in two directories produced different bytes, so content-hashed module names and SRI hashes differed for no semantic reason. The rule removes this source of path dependence; it does not by itself prove a whole build reproducible.
- Readers of off-box error records (Sentry dashboards, AI pairs) get a path valid in every checkout, which the dev-server open endpoint (`POST /__rf-open-in-editor?file=...`) resolves against live source-paths; the `editor://` fallback ("production-mode inspection") joins it to the reader's own `:project-root`, which is right for single-source-root projects, whereas a builder's absolute path was wrong on every other machine.
- What still ships is the source-tree path, which `:ns` already discloses; versus B, the only extra disclosure is the file extension. That is intentional diagnostic information, not a promise to conceal the application's structure.
- Under the rule, production output is uniform across source kinds: classpath directories, `:local/root` and git deps (all relative via shadow's `resource-name`), and jars (already relative today). Builds whose reader supplies absolute paths (native CLJS compiler; JVM `load-file`) ship `{:ns :line}`.

- Dev tools are unaffected under every option: the dev form keeps the absolute path. - Bundle size is not a deciding factor (51 bytes gzipped across 24 literals on the probe bundle).
