title: reset fixture leaves error listeners and observability sinks registered, contrary to Spec 009 and API.md
description:
## Bug

The standard reset fixture (`re-frame.test-support/make-reset-runtime-fixture`) clears trace and event-emit listeners between tests, but it never clears error-emit listeners. Spec 009 and API.md both say it does. It also leaves observability sinks, the observability process default and trace-disabled frames in place. So an error listener or sink that one test leaves behind keeps receiving records in every later test of the same JVM lane or node bundle. Any leftover listener also silences the unowned-error dev fallback for those later tests.

## Evidence

All file:line references are at trunk 475bdcaacf (unchanged at b375cd0e42).

- **Contract.**
  - `spec/009-Instrumentation.md:669-674`: "`re-frame.test-support/make-reset-runtime-fixture` restores a clean listener registry between tests via the lower-level sinks (`re-frame.trace.tooling/clear-listeners!` and its :epoch sibling, plus the implementation-tier `re-frame.event-emit` / `re-frame.error-emit` clears)."
  - `spec/API.md:657`: "`re-frame.test-support`'s reset clears the registries through the lower-level sinks directly (… `re-frame.event-emit/clear-event-listeners!`, `re-frame.error-emit/clear-error-listeners!`, …)".
- **Code** (*read*).
  - `implementation/core/src/re_frame/test_support.cljc` `reset-runtime!` (`:538-570`) calls `rf.trace.tooling/clear-listeners!` (`:559`) and `rf.event-emit/clear-event-listeners!` (`:560`) only.
  - These clear functions exist and have no caller in `test_support.cljc`:
    - `re-frame.error-emit/clear-error-listeners!` (`error_emit.cljc:91-94`, docstring "Test-isolation only");
    - `re-frame.observability/clear-observability-sinks!` (`observability.cljc:136`) and `clear-observability-default!` (`:208`);
    - `re-frame.trace/clear-frame-no-emit!` (`trace.cljc:396`).
  - The reset-hook table (`:335-473`) has no row for any of them.
- Repro (*probed*, JVM, from `implementation/core`):

  ```clojure
  (re-frame.error-emit/register-error-listener! ::leaked-error-listener (fn [_] nil))
  (re-frame.event-emit/register-event-listener! ::leaked-event-listener (fn [_] nil))
  (re-frame.observability/register-observability-sink! ::leaked-sink (fn [_] nil))
  ((re-frame.test-support/make-reset-runtime-fixture {:adapter re-frame.substrate.plain-atom/adapter})
   (fn [] (prn (keys @@#'re-frame.error-emit/listeners)
               (keys @@#'re-frame.event-emit/listeners)
               (keys @@#'re-frame.observability/sinks))))
  ;; inside the next test:
  ;;   error listeners #{:user/leaked-error-listener}   event listeners #{}   sinks #{:user/leaked-sink}
  ```

- **Why the code differs from the spec.** `re-frame.ssr` registers a process-global `::error-projection` error listener when its namespace loads (`implementation/ssr/src/re_frame/ssr.cljc:404-405`). A blanket clear with nothing to reinstate it would break every later SSR test.
- **Second effect.** Arm (a) of `report-unowned-error!` (`error_emit.cljc:234-273`) suppresses the dev console fallback whenever any error listener is registered, so a leaked listener changes later tests' observable behaviour too.

## Expected

After the fixture's reset, the error-listener and observability-sink registries hold only what framework namespaces install at load time, such as SSR's projection listener. That is what Spec 009 and API.md describe.

## Fix direction

- In `reset-runtime!`, also call `clear-error-listeners!`, `clear-observability-sinks!` and `clear-observability-default!`.
- Add a post-dispose row to `reset-hook-table`, for example `:ssr/reinstall-error-projection!`, registered by `re-frame.ssr` through the existing late-bind pattern, so SSR's listener comes back after the clear.
- Expect some suites to have relied on a listener registered outside a test surviving the reset; move those registrations into the test or its fixture.
- Alternative: correct Spec 009:669-674 and API.md:657 to say error listeners persist. That edits two hot-zone files and keeps the leak, so the code fix is preferred.

## Acceptance

- Add a JVM regression with two tests run under the fixture:
  - test A registers an error listener and an observability sink;
  - test B emits an error and asserts that neither of A's callbacks fired.
- The test fails before the fix and passes after.
- The SSR suite stays green, with its projection listener present after reset.
- Core and SSR JVM lanes and the CLJS node lane stay green.

## Notes

- **Origin:** Opus core-observability review (Insight 10, action 14). Sol (surface 09) independently noted that `reset-runtime!` has no error-listener, sink or default reset.
- **Related:** none open.
- **Hot-zone files:** none for the code fix (`implementation/core/src/re_frame/test_support.cljc`, `implementation/ssr/src/re_frame/ssr.cljc`). The spec-only alternative would touch `spec/009-Instrumentation.md` and `spec/API.md`, both hot-zone.
- **Supporting detail:** `ai/findings/advisarial-review/opus/core-observability.md` Insight 10; `ai/findings/advisarial-review/sol/09-core-errors.md` (dev fallback recommendation).

Delete both once #11093 has merged. No gate pins either.

Tests (implementation/core/test/re_frame/test_support_test.clj, JVM `clojure -M:test -n re-frame.test-support-test`):

B's listener and sink are the control and both receive :rf.error/handler-exception.

Note: set-frame-no-emit! on :rf/default does NOT leak at base, because ensure-default-frame! re-registers :rf/default and resets its flag, so the test uses another id.
- with the fix: exit 0. Src reverted alone (test_support.cljc, directory.cljc, ssr.cljc): exit 1, the same 5 failures; restored by blob hash.
- plant removing only the ssr set-fn!: exit 1, the SSR-presence test alone fails; restored by sha256.
Census: a search for top-level registrations, :once fixtures and fixtures composed outside the reset, across the 73 test files that both register a listener / sink / default / no-emit frame and use a reset fixture, found none relying on survival, so no suite registration moved. JVM lanes green after the change: core 1242 tests / 3673 assertions, ssr 439 / 2150, prod gate 1061 / 2469 (205 namespaces), and machines, routing, flows, http, ssr-ring, epoch, resources, schemas and event-conformance all exit 0. The CLJS node and browser lanes are CI's. Many suites' :init-fn still call clear-error-listeners! / clear-observability-sinks!; now redundant, left alone.
After the rebase onto 7462046f5a this bead's commit is bc64995837 (the id in the note above is pre-rebase). No spec/009 edit was needed.
close_reason: Delivered by PR #11117 (merged f1400d7091), the code fix as described. reset-runtime! (and so make-reset-runtime-fixture) now also clears error-emit listeners, observability sinks, the observability process default and trace-disabled frames; a new post-dispose reset hook :ssr/reinstall-error-projection!, registered by re-frame.ssr through the late-bind pattern, puts SSR's process-global projection listener back after the clear. Two-test JVM regression: red at base (5 failures), green, red again with the source reverted (same 5). A separate planted fault (dropping only SSR's hook registration) turns the SSR-presence test red. The trace-disabled case uses a non-default frame id because the fixture re-creates :rf/default. Suites whose :init-fn still clear listeners by hand are now redundant but harmless; left alone deliberately.

title: unsubscribe takes the reaction subscribe returned: (rf/unsubscribe r), identity-guarded; drop both address forms (one PR, also delivers rf2-mn2ht.37)
description:
DECISION FOR MIKE: should re-frame.core/unsubscribe accept subscribe's [query-v opts] shape?

THE RULING IN FORCE. Commit 87b3eec977 (rf2-bfadc6, 2026-07-03) gave subscribe-once the public {:frame f} opts form, shape-discriminated on the first argument (a query vector first is the public form; a frame first is internal plumbing). It records "Per Mike's ruling (Option A), unsubscribe deliberately stays frame-first and does NOT gain an opts-map form — pure teardown, never a hot in-view call." Spec 006 says "No opts-map form (deliberate)". A later review finding proposing a guard (rf2-pk4i6.4 #4) was dismissed as "can be noted on that ruling if it bites".

IT HAS BITTEN (measured by rf2-tpmsl's worker, PR #11018). On the JVM, after (rf/subscribe [:v] {:frame f}), the call (rf/unsubscribe [:v] {:frame f}) returns nil and the cache entry stays at {[:v] 1}: a silent leak. DECISION: Option H — release by handle. The public release becomes `(rf/unsubscribe r) → nil`, where `r` is the reaction `subscribe` returned. It returns ONE counted share of `r` through the existing atomic identity guard, so a release whose reaction no longer occupies its slot (evicted by re-registration, `clear-sub-cache!`, hot reload, or a destroyed-and-recreated frame of the same id) is a silent no-op and never touches a successor. `nil` and never-cached reactions are no-ops. A vector argument (the retired address forms) throws a new typed error naming the handle form. Both address forms, `(unsubscribe query-v)` and `(unsubscribe frame-id query-v)`, leave the public surface; in-tree holders that already know their address release through the existing internal `unsubscribe-if-reaction`. This one change resolves rf2-xkog1 AND rf2-mn2ht.37: one PR delivers and closes both.

WHY:
- The leak is real and recurring. Today's 2-arity reads its first argument as a frame, so `(rf/unsubscribe [:v] {:frame f})` — the shape every other frame-targeting fn uses — looks up a frame named `[:v]`, misses, returns nil, releases nothing and reports nothing. 19 xray test sites write exactly that, every one intending to release (five carry the comment "Release the imperative probe explicitly"). The July ruling's premise, "unsubscribe footgun is weak (pure teardown, never a hot in-view call)", is refuted by that measurement.
- The hazard is real. Address release decrements whatever entry sits at the key, so after any eviction a late release disposes the successor another holder built. Every long-lived holder inside core already avoids this through `unsubscribe-if-reaction`; the public door — which Spec 006 teaches to tests, REPL sessions and tools, and which the Form-3 recipe uses in apps — is the one release in the codebase that is not guarded.
- H answers both with one rule: give back what you got. One argument, nothing to retype, no argument order, no frame to resolve. It cannot be miscopied from the `subscribe` row because there is no frame position to get wrong. It is correct across hot reload BY CONSTRUCTION, not opt-in. It needs no ambient frame, so teardown from a lifecycle hook or a Fresco body (where ambient resolution fails or is refused) just works. title: Move re-frame.ssr's error-projection capture off the :errors and :trace listener registries onto late-bind hooks, so loading SSR stops silencing the dev prints (after PR #11123)
description:
FOUND by the err-print worker implementing rf2-mn2ht.24 (PR #11123), a CLAIM to re-check at tip once #11123 merges.

rf2-mn2ht.24's ruling makes an unrouted dev error print one line on every host, and makes the eight no-silent-swallow warnings print one line while no :trace listener is registered. Its PRESERVED ANALYSIS says: "A JVM SSR dev server will now print, for example, a malformed reserved :rf.server fx on every request where no sink is declared. Intended."

That does not hold. Loading `re-frame.ssr` registers, at namespace load, an always-on `:errors` listener (the error-projection listener the reset fixture reinstalls through `:ssr/reinstall-error-projection!`) and a `:trace` listener (implementation/ssr/src/re_frame/ssr.cljc, around lines 403-420 at 789d56d004). Under the unchanged two-arm ownership predicate, the `:errors` listener owns every promoted error record, and the `:trace` listener is "a listener" for the warning print. So in ANY process that loads re-frame.ssr, a JVM SSR dev server or a REPL with SSR on the classpath, neither print ever fires. The core test for .24 has to clear error listeners in its fixture to stay order-independent for exactly this reason.

QUESTION FOR A RULING (small): should SSR's framework-internal listeners stop counting as ownership for the two dev prints, so an SSR dev server prints as the .24 ruling intended? Candidate directions, for the ruler to weigh, not decided here:
(a) accept as is: an SSR process routes errors into the response by design, so a print would duplicate; record the limit in Spec 009's fallback paragraph;
(b) mark SSR's two load-time listeners as framework-internal (one registration flag or a separate internal registry), and have the ownership test and the warning snapshot skip them;
(c) narrow SSR's listeners so they only take request-scoped records (records carrying an SSR request context), leaving everything else unowned.
Posture: trust the programmer, low friction, no knob.

Touches: implementation/ssr/src/re_frame/ssr.cljc, core error_emit.cljc and trace/tooling.cljc (the ownership and snapshot checks), and possibly spec/009's fallback paragraph (hot). Dispatch only after PR #11123 merges.
notes:
== RULING (delegated by Mike; decided 2026-10-11 04:20:12 AUSEST at HEAD a29639c01d) ==
DECISION: Option (b), done the way epoch already does it. `re-frame.ssr` stops registering on the `:errors` and `:trace` listener registries. Its two capture paths become late-bind hooks that the delivery code calls beside the listener fan-out:
- core's error-emit fan-out calls an always-on SSR hook for every promoted record;
- the dev trace delivery calls a dev-only SSR hook for every trace event.
Neither hook is a listener, so neither owns either dev print. The ownership predicate (rf2-kuky.18's two arms) and PR #11123's print code stay exactly as they are, and SSR projection behaves the same in dev and production. The general rule: a listener registration means somebody is watching, whether an app, a tool, a test, or a framework capture site for the length of one synchronous call. A framework namespace never registers a permanent (load-time) listener. A permanent framework consumer rides a late-bind hook instead, as `:epoch/capture-event` already does.

WHY:
- The bead's claim holds, measured against #11123's code (probe under EVIDENCE). With `re-frame.ssr` loaded, a typo'd dispatch, a throwing handler and a misspelt `configure!` key each print 0 characters. Unregister SSR's two listeners and each prints its one line.
- SSR's listeners own records they never touch. Both already ignore every record that is not on a `:platform :server` frame. The dev trace listener also ignores every non-`:error` op, so all eight no-silent-swallow warnings are simply dropped. Under the rule that registration is ownership, that is pure silencing.
- It is not only a JVM SSR problem (established by reading). A hydrating browser client requires `re-frame.ssr` to get `:rf/hydrate` (`examples/real-apps/realworld_http/core.cljs:50-54`), and `ssr.cljc` installs its error listener at top level on CLJS too. So at HEAD the browser's existing unowned-error console fallback (rf2-fu75) is already dead on every hydrating page. After #11123 the warning print would be dead there too.
- Core's own documentation already defines arm (a) as "an IMPLEMENTATION-tier door — the framework's own synchronous-window capture sites and tests" (`error_emit.cljc:131-138`). SSR's permanent load-time registration is the one consumer that does not fit that description. Fixing the consumer rather than the predicate keeps the predicate's meaning and needs no new concept.
- The hook route has a precedent, and it removes machinery rather than adding it. Epoch's capture deliberately rides `:epoch/capture-event` "rather than registering as a listener via `register-listener!` ... [so] the user-facing `clear-listeners!` call does NOT wipe the internal capture path" (`epoch/capture.cljc:179-183`, `trace.cljc:533-548`). SSR sitting on the listener registries is the reason two pieces of machinery exist, and both go:
  - the `:ssr/reinstall-error-projection!` hook (test_support reset row, directory row);
  - #11123's new test fixture's `:init-fn rf.error-emit/clear-error-listeners!`.
- Printing server-frame errors is intended (rf2-mn2ht.24 PRESERVED ANALYSIS), and it is right. The projection hands the browser the locked, sanitised public-error shape. The server console line is the developer's readable cause: category, message, event id, frame, and `ns:line`. It is the dev log line any web stack prints for a 500. Production prints nothing (the JVM gate is false, per `spec/Security.md` §Production gates), and an app with a sink owns the record.

REJECTED:
- (a) Accept and document. The duplication premise applies only to server-frame records, and even there it is wrong: the browser gets a sanitised response, the server log gets a readable line, and those are two audiences. For everything else SSR routes nothing: client frames, REPL frames, hydrating browser pages, and all eight warnings. Documenting it would mean Spec 009 telling users that loading SSR, even on the client just to hydrate, turns off the dev diagnostics.
- (c) Narrow SSR's listeners to request-scoped records. Under the unchanged predicate, registration owns whatever the listener does with a record (`error_emit.cljc:136`: "even if that listener ignores this category"). SSR's listeners are already as narrow as they can be, server frames only, and they still silence everything. Making (c) work needs one of two things, and both fail:
  - per-record ownership, which rf2-fu75 and rf2-kuky.18 rejected as per-category ownership;
  - per-request registration. A busy dev server would hold a registration nearly all the time, it would suppress the intended server-frame line, and it adds lifecycle bookkeeping.
- (b) as a non-owning flag on the listener registries. It works, but it adds a registration option and changes two predicates (#11123's error arm and its trace-snapshot test). It also leaves SSR exposed to listener clears, so the reinstall hook stays and the trace side would need one too. The hook route needs none of that.
- Deleting the dev trace listener instead of moving it. It is not dead. It buffers every `:rf.error/*` trace event on a server frame, including dev-only categories that have no always-on record, so deleting it would change a dev SSR server's wire status for those. That is SSR projection policy, outside this bead. (Its stated reason, in the code and in Spec 011, is stale: see probe D.)
- Changing the transient framework windows: the `frame.cljc` setup-step watch (~:2840), the on-destroy watch (~:4007) and the Fresco server's one-render window (`fresco/server.cljs:259-298`). These are the users arm (a) was designed for. Each lasts one synchronous call, and each re-raises, throws or re-emits what it captured (Fresco's docstring says so at :295-298). An unrelated record landing inside such a window is silenced for that window. Accepted; it is not worth new machinery.

WHERE THE OPINIONS AGREED / DISAGREED:
- There is no dossier and no Codex section. The opinions in play are:
  - the bead's three candidate directions, posed without a recommendation by the err-print worker, under the posture "trust the programmer, low friction, no knob";
  - .24's PRESERVED ANALYSIS: "A JVM SSR dev server will now print ... Intended."
- The bead's rationale for (a), "an SSR process routes errors into the response by design, so a print would duplicate", is settled against it. The probe shows SSR routes only server-frame records and no warnings, and the records it does route go to a sanitised response.
- The bead's (b) offered "one registration flag or a separate internal registry". Ruled: neither. Each capture path gets one late-bind hook, the existing shape for an internal consumer (epoch). It is closest to the "separate internal registry", but needs no registry.
- The bead's evidence is confirmed in every particular. Lines 403-422 are the same at 789d56d004 and at a29639c01d.
- Facts beyond the bead:
  - the reach into hydrating browsers;
  - `make-reset-runtime-fixture` clears SSR's trace listener (`test_support.cljc:584`) and never reinstalls it. However, 48 of the 86 files under `implementation/ssr/test` use SSR's own fixture, which reloads `re-frame.ssr` before every test (`ssr/test/re_frame/ssr/test_fixture.clj:38`), so most of the SSR suite runs with both listeners present;
  - the no-such-route claim is stale.

EVIDENCE:
- PROBE. Setup:
  - Base: HEAD 789d56d004, which is PR #11123's base. SSR, core and test-support source are unchanged through a29639c01d.
  - #11123's head 272ce475a6 `error_emit.cljc` and `trace/tooling.cljc` overlaid ahead of core src on SSR's `:test` classpath.
  - Plain-atom adapter, no reset fixture (a real process), each call run with Clojure `*err*` and `System.err` captured.
  - Command, from `implementation/ssr`: `java -cp "<overlay>;$(clojure -A:test -Spath)" clojure.main <scratch>/probe.clj`. Exit 0.
  - Output, abridged:
  ```
  PR-overlay present? true debug-enabled? true
  == A: re-frame.ssr NOT loaded
    error-emit listeners: []   trace listeners: []
    dispatch-sync typo'd id (client frame)        lines=1 "[re-frame2] :rf.error/no-such-handler (event :p/typo, frame :p/client)"
    dispatch-sync throwing handler (client frame) lines=1 "[re-frame2] :rf.error/handler-exception — kaboom (event :p/throws, frame :p/client, at probe.b6g2u:37)"
    configure! misspelt key                       lines=1 "[re-frame2] :rf.warning/unknown-configure-key — rf/configure! was given unrecognised top-level key [:epoch-histroy]. ..."
  == B: re-frame.ssr loaded (no test reset)
    error-emit listeners: [:re-frame.ssr/error-projection]   trace listeners: [:re-frame.ssr/error-projection]
    dispatch-sync typo'd id (client frame)        lines=0 chars=0
    dispatch-sync throwing handler (client frame) lines=0 chars=0
    configure! misspelt key                       lines=0 chars=0
    server frame: throwing handler                lines=0 chars=0
    SSR buffered it for projection? true   flush-response-result! status: 500
  == C: re-frame.ssr loaded, its two listeners unregistered
    (the three client-frame rows print exactly as in A)
    server frame: throwing handler                lines=1 "[re-frame2] :rf.error/handler-exception — server kaboom (event :p/srv-throws, frame :p/server, at probe.b6g2u:61)"
    SSR buffered it for projection? false
  == D: route-url miss inside a server-frame handler
    :error trace ops seen [operation ex-data-id]: [[:rf.error/handler-exception :rf.error/no-such-route]]
  ```
  - B is the bead's claim.
  - C shows that removing SSR's two registrations restores all four lines, and that the projection then captures nothing. So the hooks must REPLACE the registrations, not merely drop them.
  - D shows that `:rf.error/no-such-route` never reaches a listener as an `:operation`. `route-url` THROWS it (`routing/registry.cljc:2052-2056`, through `route-error` → `rf.error/thrown-ex-info`, which emits nothing). So a miss inside a handler projects as `:rf.error/handler-exception`, which maps to 500.
- Census of listener registrations under `implementation/**/src` and `tools/**/src` (Grep for `register-listener!|register-error-listener!`: 26 files, each call site read):
  - Load-time registrations exist ONLY in `re-frame.ssr`: the error listener at `ssr.cljc:403-407` plus the reinstall hook at :443, and the trace listener at :421-422.
  - Epoch captures through `:epoch/capture-event`, not a listener.
  - The transient framework windows (`frame.cljc` setup-step and on-destroy watches, the `fresco/server.cljs` render window) all unregister in a `finally`.
  - Tools register on an explicit install or for a scoped extent: Xray at `install.cljs:53` and :168; Story in recorder, play, trace_buffer and error.cljc. These are watchers and correctly own.
  - `routing.cljc:14`'s ns docstring lists `register-error-listener!` among its load-time registrations, but the file makes no such call.
- SSR's capture predicates:
  - The always-on `error-emit-projection-listener` buffers only when `(rf.ssr.error-projector/server-frame? (:frame record))` (`error_listener.cljc:474-476`).
  - The dev `error-projection-listener` buffers only for `:op-type :error` with a server frame in `[:tags :frame]` (:401-412, :38-50).
  - `server-frame?` is `(= :server (:platform (frame-meta id)))` (`error_projector.cljc:449-453`).
- The reset fixture:
  - `make-reset-runtime-fixture` clears error listeners (`test_support.cljc:579`), runs the post-dispose hooks including `:ssr/reinstall-error-projection!` (:491), then clears trace listeners (:584).
  - `core/test/re_frame/test_support_test.clj:187-193` pins the reinstall.
- Spec:
  - `spec/011-SSR.md:1411`: "installs onto the always-on error-emit substrate, through its framework-internal listener registry".
  - `spec/011-SSR.md:1417-1421`, about no-such-route: "For dev parity it is routed through the projector via a secondary `register-listener!` install."
  - `spec/API.md:638` lists "the SSR error projector" among the error-emit registry's framework-internal consumers.

IMPLEMENTATION GUIDANCE (the base is PR #11123 merged; dispatch only after it merges):
- Core, error side (`implementation/core/src/re_frame/error_emit.cljc`):
  - There are two corpus fan-out sites, in `dispatch-on-error!` and `dispatch-error-record*`. Each is currently `((:fan-out registry) record rf.trace/continuation-live?)`. Add one private helper and use it at both. The helper:
    - runs the registry fan-out;
    - then, while `(rf.trace/continuation-live?)` holds, calls the SSR hook, resolved with `rf.late-bind/get-fn-cached` (suggested key `:ssr/capture-error-record`);

title: Hydrating a root topped by h/frame-root silently duplicates the page: React keeps the server DOM and appends the client
description:
## Bug `h/frame-root` renders nothing on its first pass; its children arrive on a second pass after a layout effect ensures the frame. When it sits at the top of a hydrating root (`h/render! … {:hydrate? true}`), React 19 is handed an empty tree where the server's markup is. React does not report a mismatch at the root level. It leaves the server DOM in place, and the layout-phase second pass then mounts the client tree beside it. The page shows its content twice, the first copy inert, with no error and no `:rf.ssr/hydration-mismatch`. The Fresco guide warns against this composition but says React "would report a mismatch" and the markup "is replaced". That is not what happens, so the commonest SSR boot mistake fails silently. ## Evidence Trunk 475bdcaacf. - `implementation/core/src/re_frame/views/frame_boundary.cljs:298-366`: `frame-root-fc` returns nil until its `useLayoutEffect` flips `ready?` (`:361-366`, "PASS 1 / SSR / pre-commit: emit no descendant subtree"). This holds even when the frame is already live. - `implementation/fresco/src/re_frame/fresco/impl/frame_boundary.cljs:108-136`: `h/frame-root` delegates to that two-pass component and has no check for an adopting root. - `implementation/fresco/src/re_frame/fresco/impl/mount.cljs:361-401`: `hydrate-root!` builds the tree, a Fragment of the window closer (which renders nil) and the app, and calls `hydrateRoot` without any ENSURE refusal. `roots/adopting-here?` exists (`impl/roots.cljs:122`) but only presence reads it. - React DOM 19.3.0, `implementation/node_modules/react-dom/cjs/react-dom-client.development.js:5661-5690` (the guard at `:5667`): `popHydrationState` skips the unclaimed-tail mismatch check for `HostRoot` (tag 3) and `HostSingleton` (tag 27). Leftover server nodes directly under the root are neither reported nor cleared. Repro (*probed*: React 19.3.0 dev build in headless Chromium through Playwright, using a stand-in component with `frame-root-fc`'s exact shape: `useState(false)`, a `useLayoutEffect` that sets it true, and nil until ready. Server markup `

hello

` in the container, hydrated with `hydrateRoot` and an `onRecoverableError` logger): | Client tree | Container after hydration | Errors | |---|---|---| | control: `Fragment(Closer,

)` | `

hello

` (1 copy) | none | | two-pass at the root: `Fragment(Closer, TwoPass(

))` | `

hello

hello

` (2 copies) | **none**: no `onRecoverableError`, no `console.error` | | two-pass nested under a host element: `
TwoPass(

)

` | `

hello

` | `onRecoverableError: Hydration failed because the server rendered HTML didn't match the client…` (regenerated) | So the nested case is reported and replaced, as the guide describes. The root case, which is the one the guide warns about, duplicates silently. Contract contrast: - `docs/core/fresco/18-ssr-and-hydration.md:158-160`: "React would be handed an empty tree where the server's markup is and report a mismatch". - `docs/core/fresco/18-ssr-and-hydration.md:379` (troubleshooting): "Hydration reports a mismatch and the server markup is replaced". - Spec 011 §Hydration-mismatch detection promises the adoption tier surfaces structural divergences through `onRecoverableError`. This one never reaches it. ## Expected ENSURE inside an adopting root fails loudly with a named error pointing at `h/frame-provider`, before React sees the tree. At minimum it must never silently duplicate the page. ## Fix direction In Fresco's `frame-root` lowering, refuse when `roots/adopting-here?` is true, with a typed error naming the supported recipe: `rf/make-frame`, `ssr/hydrate!`, then `[h/frame-provider {:frame …}]`. A nested `frame-root` inside an adopting tree never carries server markup either, since the server emitted nothing for it, so refusing there too costs nothing real. Correct the two guide sentences to describe the real outcome, or point them at the new error. `rf/frame-root` on UIx and Reagent shares `frame-root-fc`, so their hydrate paths likely have the same root-level shape. That was not traced here; check it while fixing. ## Acceptance - A DOM test: `h/render!` with `{:hydrate? true}` over a container holding server markup, with a tree topped by `h/frame-root`, raises the named error, and the container keeps exactly one copy of the server markup. Today it ends with two copies and no error. - The supported recipe (`make-frame`, `ssr/hydrate!`, then `frame-provider`) still hydrates cleanly with no recoverable error. - A non-hydrating `h/render!` under `h/frame-root` is unchanged. ## Notes - Origin: Opus fresco review (decision 9, action 5). Sol report 23 §4 source-checked it (an Opus-derived claim) and added the nested case. The duplicate-content outcome and the React root-level skip were found while verifying this bead. - Related: rf2-kuky.58 (closed) recorded the "shape argument" for using SCOPE when hydrating. The guide text that came out of it says React reports the mismatch, which the probe above contradicts for the root case. - Hot zones: `spec/002-Frames.md`, but only if its frame-root contract text gains the refusal. The code fix plus the Fresco guide page touch no hot file. - Probe script: `scratchpad/bugbeads/views-work/probe_root_null_hydrate.cjs` (session scratch, not durable). - Supporting detail: `ai/findings/advisarial-review/opus/fresco.md` decision 9; `ai/findings/advisarial-review/sol/23-fresco-react-runtime.md` §4.

== FENCE (mayor, 2026-10-10 AUSEST): wait for PR #11072 (adapters-hydrate) to merge ==
The fix mints a new typed :rf.error/* id. scripts/check_keyword_catalogue_drift.py CHECK A requires a spec/009-Instrumentation.md catalogue row for every emitted error id, and spec/009 is a hot zone that the adapters-hydrate worker is editing (PR #11072, which also touches spec/011, spec/004C and the Reagent hydrate paths). Dispatch this bead once #11072 merges. Released by: PR #11072 merged.
== WORKER RESULT (spec009-cluster, PR #11092, 2026-10-10 AUSEST) ==
FIXED in the Fresco commit "fix(fresco): h/frame-root refuses a hydrating root's tree instead of duplicating the page".

What changed: impl.mount/hydrate-root! lowers its tree with roots/*adopting-walk?* bound; frame-root's lowering (impl/frame_boundary.cljs) refuses inside that walk with the new :rf.error/fresco-frame-root-adopting, naming the boot that adopts (rf/make-frame, ssr/hydrate!, then [h/frame-provider {:frame ...}]). The refusal lands before hydrateRoot runs, so the container keeps the server markup and the client-root handle stays empty. Spec 009 gains the catalogue row (CHECK B needed no Conventions change: :rf.error/* is reserved). docs/core/fresco/18-ssr-and-hydration.md: the "report a mismatch" sentence and the troubleshooting row now describe the real outcome and name the new error.

Evidence (DOM test client_root_lifecycle_dom_cljs_test W4, a-hydrating-first-render-refuses-frame-root):
- RED at base: the test alone pushed as 738d1e605f; CI browser lane job 114209267484 ran 969 tests / 5056 assertions, 5 failures all in the new row: no error, (= 1 2) copies of .panel, second copy not server nodes, a root made.
- GREEN: fc50b9919b, browser lane job 114211960287, 969 / 5056, 0 failures (same count, so the row ran in both).
- RED AGAIN with src reverted alone: the 738d1e605f tree is exactly that state.
- The supported recipe's clean hydration is the existing W5 row (frame-provider adopt, no mismatch); the non-hydrating frame-root rows (frame_boundary_heads W1 etc.) are unchanged and green.

RESIDUAL (not refused): a frame-root reached only through a view body is lowered during React's render, outside the hydrating walk. A render-time refusal needs a hiccup-conditional hook call or a wrapper fiber on every frame-root, and a throw during hydration makes React retry as a client render that clears the container. Not taken; worth a bead only if that shape shows up.

REAGENT / UIX TRACE (by reading, not probed): same root-level shape. UIx hydrate (re-frame.substrate.spine mount-client-root!) wraps the tree as Fragment(sentinel, closer, tree); the ratom path wraps it as [:r> adoption-window-closer props tree] under Reagent's root component. No host element sits between the container and frame-root-fc, whose first pass renders nil, so an adopting root topped by rf/frame-root should duplicate silently the same way. A fix in core views/frame_boundary.cljs alone is not possible: frame-root-fc has no adoption signal (the spine's adoption flag is root-local and reaches only the closer), so a core refusal needs spine plumbing and would throw during hydration rather than before it. Not done here (adapters fenced; rf2-mn2ht.68 is the UIx hydrate parity bead).

SUGGESTED spec/002 sentence for the frame-root section (file held by the contract-truth worker): "A hydrating root cannot adopt a frame-root. Its empty first render leaves React nothing to claim the server's markup with, and React keeps an unclaimed server node directly under a root, so the client tree would mount beside the server's copy. An adopting root makes its frame, installs the payload, and scopes it with frame-provider; Fresco's hydrating root door refuses a frame-root in its own tree with :rf.error/fresco-frame-root-adopting."
Merged-PR audit #11092: follow-up rf2-5a1d9 — Fresco frame-root returned from a view bypasses hydration refusal and duplicates the page. This is a separate open finding; the source status and ruling are preserved.
close_reason: Fixed in PR #11092, merged at 200a67df2d (2026-10-10 AUSEST). A hydrating h/render! now lowers its tree with roots/*adopting-walk?* bound, and h/frame-root refuses inside that walk with the new :rf.error/fresco-frame-root-adopting before hydrateRoot runs. The container therefore keeps exactly one copy of the server markup and no root is made. The spec/009 row was added, and the two docs/core/fresco/18-ssr-and-hydration.md sentences are corrected. The DOM test was red at base in the browser lane (5 failures: no error, two copies, a root made) and green after (969 tests / 5056 assertions); the test-only run is the red-again. ACCEPTED LIMIT: a frame-root reached only through a view body is lowered during React's render, outside the walk, so it is not refused. Catching it needs a conditional hook or a wrapper on every frame-root, and a throw during hydration makes React clear the container. The Reagent/UIx rf/frame-root shape (which duplicates the same way, read not probed) is filed separately. CI 88/88.

## The problem, carefully

**What the example does today.** Every navigation in `examples/capabilities/routing/routing/core.cljs` is an `rf/route-link` anchor — four call sites, `core.cljs:115`, `:125`, `:142`, `:151` — and the file's own docstring says so at `core.cljs:18-19`: "`route-link` — renders links that drive navigation" / "`:rf.route/url-requested` — the event a user clicking an anchor fires".     [:div
     [:h1 "Not found"]

title: RealWorld HTTP (ruled A): latch the favourite heart and the article-page Follow on the one-at-a-time in-flight pattern the profile follow already has; share :profile.follow-pending across pages
description:
RULED A on 2026-09-22 (delegated ruling; see the RULING note and the "## IMPLEMENTATION BRIEF" note below — the brief is the dispatch contract). One PR, size M (about 40 lines of example code plus one RED-first test block), fence `examples/real-apps/realworld_http/**` plus ONE adapter test file outside it.

WORK: In the RealWorld HTTP flagship, give the favourite heart and the article-page Follow/Unfollow the one-at-a-time in-flight latch the profile page's follow already has (profile.cljs, SERIALISING THE TOGGLE). (1) `:article/toggle-favorite` (favorites.cljs:157-186) refuses while its slug is in a new top-level `:favorite-pending` set, acquires the slug on issue, and `:article/favorite-synced` / `:article/favorite-rollback` release it UNCONDITIONALLY; a `:article/favorite-pending?` sub disables both heart buttons (articles.cljs:466-469, comments.cljs:808-817). (2) `:article/toggle-follow-author` (comments.cljs:556-603) consults and acquires the EXISTING username-keyed `:profile.follow-pending` set; its two settles release the username unconditionally while keeping the slug-gated author write; the byline button (comments.cljs:760-765) disables on it — closing the profile-to-article hole where a second mutation on the same author goes out while the first is in flight. schema.cljs gains `[:favorite-pending] [:maybe [:set :string]]`; ssr.cljc names it as the second deliberate absentee; README.md:44 gains a clause and :46's app-db path count is truthed (23 after this entry); the favorites.cljs:133-155 rationale block gets one paragraph saying the race policy is now ONE policy. One RED-first test block in implementation/adapters/reagent/test/re_frame/realworld_cljs_test.cljs, mirroring the profile latch tests at :3676-3894 but shorter.

WHY, in one line: both reviewers measured the defect (a fast second click issues an opposite POST/DELETE pair with no latch; a reordered reply pair — and a pair of failures — leaves the heart lying against the server), the app already argues and implements the policy for the profile follow, and the article-page follow bypasses that very latch one page away; copying about forty lines is cheaper than the rationale B would have to write. No framework concurrency abstraction; no `:request-id` on writes (option C rejected by both reviewers).

SEQUENCE with rf2-3bf01 (ruled B; same files favorites.cljs, articles.cljs and README.md): whichever is dispatched first, the second rebases; README:46 reads 23 after both. rf2-67vjf (origin-root) shares no file — parallel-safe. Examples are test-free (rf2-8cevm); the test lives in the adapter test file. Gates: `node implementation/scripts/check-examples-compile.cjs` AND `npm run test:cljs` (both take the shadow-cljs lane the mayor grants), clj-kondo without `--fail-level error`, `scripts/check_readme_links.py --ci`.

Depends on / feeds: audit follow-on of closed rf2-fn0kx.7 (finding 3) and merged PR #10149 (`b609c2700f`, merged 2026-09-21T16:52:20Z). Siblings from the same PR, each with its own dossier by another writer: rf2-3bf01 (the unused `:articles/cancel` / `:feed/cancel` events; touches `favorites.cljs:87-93` and `README.md:21`) and rf2-67vjf (`<base href>` vs `with-base-path`; touches `index.html`, `routing.cljs`, `core.cljs`). This bead owns both the ruling and its bounded example correction (bead description, last sentence).

## The decision in one sentence

The flagship serialises its profile Follow/Unfollow on a username-keyed in-flight set and argues for fifty lines that a toggle MUST be serialised, while its favourite heart (the README's headline optimistic example) and its article-page Follow issue overlapping opposite requests with no latch and no explanation: (A) give those two the same one-at-a-time latch, or (B) keep them unlatched and write down why the race policy differs.

## The problem, carefully

**What is true today (all lines re-verified at trunk `155ff6871c`; `favorites.cljs` last moved `a02f272809` on 2026-09-13, `comments.cljs` and `profile.cljs` in `b609c2700f`, so the review's cites hold positionally for `favorites.cljs` and shifted by ~20 lines in `profile.cljs`).**

1. The profile latch. `examples/real-apps/realworld_http/profile.cljs:475-524` (block titled SERIALISING THE TOGGLE) states the law:

   > Starting unfollowed: Follow flips `:following` true and issues the POST; the button now reads "Unfollow", so a second click issues the DELETE. Let the DELETE settle first and the older POST settle last, and `:profile/followed` re-seeds the whole banner from the STALE reply … Arrival order is not intent order, and nothing in a username-keyed gate can tell these two apart. So the toggle is SERIALISED rather than superseded. (`:487`)

   Mechanism: `:profile/follow` (`:526-556`) refuses when `(follow-pending-for? db username)` (`:544-545`, returning `{}`), otherwise flips the flag and `conj`s the username into `:profile.follow-pending` (`:548-550`); `:profile/followed` / `:profile/unfollowed` / `:profile/follow-rollback` each `disj` it UNCONDITIONALLY while gating the data write on `reply-for-current-profile?` (`:569-572`, `:600-603`, `:613-616` — "two owners, two questions"); the `:profile/follow-pending?` sub (`:626-637`) disables the button (`profile-loaded` reads it as `follow-busy?`, `:802`). The set is initialised at `:profile/initialise` (`:244`), has its own schema entry `[:profile.follow-pending] [:maybe [:set :string]]` (`schema.cljs:321`), is deliberately absent from the SSR payload (`ssr.cljc:28-33`), and is pinned by tests at `implementation/adapters/reagent/test/re_frame/realworld_cljs_test.cljs:3654-3859`.

2. The favourite toggle, unlatched. `favorites.cljs:157-186` (`:article/toggle-favorite`): auth-gate, `find-article`, snapshot `prior {:favorited :favoritesCount}`, flip everywhere via `patch-article-everywhere`, then `:rf.http/managed` with `(if favorited? :delete :post)` to `/articles/<slug>/favorite`, `:on-success [:article/favorite-synced slug]`, `:on-failure [:article/favorite-rollback slug prior]`. No pending set, no `:request-id`. `:article/favorite-synced` (`:188-197`) replaces the article WHOLESALE from `(:article value)` on every success. Two buttons dispatch it: the card heart (`articles.cljs:466-469`, reused by the profile lists) and the detail-page button (`comments.cljs:808-817`).

3. The article-page follow, unlatched. `comments.cljs:556-581` (`:article/toggle-follow-author`): auth-gate, read `following?` off `[:article :data :author]`, flip it, POST/DELETE `/profiles/<username>/follow`, replies carry the slug and are correlation-gated (`:583-603`). It never consults `:profile.follow-pending` — the search tool reads 0 hits for `follow-pending` in `comments.cljs` against 22 across `profile.cljs`, `schema.cljs` and `ssr.cljc`.

4. The rationale block that explains the ROLLBACKS differ (`favorites.cljs:133-155`: "why the three optimistic-with-rollback flows don't share one rollback helper") says nothing about why the RACE policy differs; `README.md:44` presents "Favorite toggle, comment delete, and follow/unfollow" as one shape.

**A second hole, mine, found while re-verifying: the existing latch is bypassable from the article page.** The profile block's own navigation argument (`profile.cljs:495-505`: "the latch belongs to the MUTATION, not to the screen … keyed by username, it latches alice and nobody else, and outlives every walk away and back") is violated by (3): open `/profile/alice`, click Follow (POST issued, alice latched), click through to one of her articles, and the byline's Follow/Unfollow button is live — a second mutation on alice goes out while the first is in flight, which is exactly the pair the latch exists to prevent. Measured by reading: the handler at `comments.cljs:566-581` has no `contains?` on the set and no `conj`. So B is not merely "leave favourites alone" — it leaves the profile's fifty-line argument partly untrue on the same username one page away.

**Who it affects.** A reader copying the flagship (the README's first "try it" step is "favourite an article", `README.md:94`). Not the demo tour: the demo backend replies through the canned fx with `:after-ms reply-delay-ms` (`realworld_shared/demo_backend.cljs:62-65`, `:577-581`), which rides `:dispatch-later` (`:39-42`), so replies land FIFO in issue order and the reordering cannot happen offline. It can against the hosted API the README points readers at (`README.md:101`).

**Measured versus asserted.** The race is established by reading the handlers (above) and by the profile block's own argument; nobody has reproduced it in a browser, and this dossier does not claim to. What IS measured: the demo's FIFO reply path; the absence of any latch read in `comments.cljs`; the test coverage (both `:article/toggle-follow-author` tests settle between clicks — `realworld_cljs_test.cljs:3096-3111` settles the POST before the second toggle, `:3205` toggles once — and `favorite-synced-success-test` at `:3154-3182` toggles once, so option A changes no existing expectation).

**Side finding, not this bead's.** `README.md:46` says `reg-app-schemas` registers "all 20 app-db paths"; `schema.cljs:301-343` carries **22** entries at trunk (counted by hand: `[:auth]` … `[:editor]` = 20, plus `[:settings.saves-in-flight]` and `[:settings.saves-answered]` at `:336`, `:343`). It read 20 at `b609c2700f`, where #10149 corrected the sentence from 19; `dc172448c8` (rf2-bq1fy, 2026-09-22) added the two ledger entries and left the sentence. Whoever next touches that sentence fixes it; under A it becomes 23.

## What the library already provides (so the options are priced against the API)

- **`:request-id` supersession** — `spec/014-HTTPRequests.md:150`, `:648-666`; implemented at `implementation/http/src/re_frame/http/registry.cljc:581-607` (`supersede!`: look up the frame's in-flight handle under the id, clear the slot, call its `:abort-fn` with `:request-id-superseded`). A fresh request with the same id ABORTS the prior one and SUPPRESSES its reply (`spec/014:666`, `docs/async/http.md:313`: "the cure for the search-box race"). The app already uses it for READS (`:feed/load` at `favorites.cljs:83`, `README.md:21`) and DECLINES it for every WRITE on purpose: `profile.cljs:468-473` — "supersede aborts the request as well as suppressing the reply, and abort-mid-write is a decision a POST deserves to have made about it on purpose: an aborted request is no proof the server declined to perform the write." That is the only place in the tree the argument is made (search: `no proof|not proof|abort-mid-write` over `*.{md,cljs,cljc,clj}` hits `profile.cljs:471-472,492` and nothing in `spec/` or `docs/` about HTTP writes).
- **The four registry-driven stale-suppression triggers** (`spec/014:1494-1499`): same-id supersede, actor destroy, epoch restore, frame destroy. None is "the same intent issued twice"; the runtime has no notion of a toggle.
- **No app-facing in-flight read in the HTTP artefact.** `in-flight-snapshot` is a TEST helper (`spec/014:1093-1100`); `:rf.http/in-flight` in `spec/Derivations.md:761` is the host-transient handle ADDRESS, not a subscription (control: the search for `:rf.http/(in-flight|pending|requests|busy)` over `spec/`, `implementation/http/src` and `docs/` finds only that address family). So "is a favourite in flight for this slug?" is app state in the HTTP twin, whichever option wins — which is why the bead says "do not introduce a framework concurrency abstraction".
- **Resources DOES provide it, and the resources twin uses it.** `spec/016-Resources.md:864-869`: `[:rf/mutation {:instance …}]` returns `{:pending? :optimistic? …}` per instance, and "a superseded reply (a re-execute under the same instance …) NEVER overwrites a newer instance". `realworld_resources/views.cljs:107-129` keys `[:favorite slug]` / `[:follow username]` and DELIBERATELY does not disable on `:pending?` (`:280-286`, `:612-618`: "the optimistic value is the truth on screen until it settles"). So the twin's policy is latest-intent-wins, enforced by the runtime, with no latch; the HTTP twin is by design the hand-rolled path (`spec/016:29`).
- **The spec's own optimistic pattern is unlatched.** `spec/Pattern-RemoteData.md:203-222` (`:article/toggle-like`) is prior-capture plus rollback, no pending state — so an unlatched favourite is not heresy against the spec; it is the profile page that went further, and said why.

## Make it tangible

One user, one article `hello`, starts unfavourited (count 0), real network. Two clicks on the heart 150 ms apart.

**Today (`favorites.cljs:157-203`).**

| step | dispatched | app-db | wire / server |
|---|---|---|---|
| click 1 | `[:article/toggle-favorite "hello"]` | flipped: favorited `true`, count 1; `prior₁` = `{false 0}` | POST `/articles/hello/favorite` (no `:request-id`, so no ledger entry to supersede) |
| click 2 | same event; `find-article` reads the FLIPPED article, so `favorited?` is `true` | flipped back: `false`, 0; `prior₂` = `{true 1}` | DELETE `/articles/hello/favorite` — both requests in flight |
| server | processes POST then DELETE (demo: `conj` then `disj` on `:favorites`, `demo_backend.cljs:497`) | | server truth: unfavourited |
| replies, in intent order | DELETE's `favorite-synced` re-seeds `false/0`; then POST's re-seeds… | **`true/1`** while the server says unfavourited | heart lit, count 1 — wrong until the next list load re-seeds the row (`:feed/loaded` writes `[:feed :data]` wholesale, `favorites.cljs:108-111`) |
| replies, arrival reordered | POST's then DELETE's | `false/0` | correct by luck of arrival |

Offline this never shows: both canned replies are queued through `:dispatch-later` with the same 20 ms and land FIFO. Failure variants mostly self-correct (a DELETE 500 rolls back to `prior₂ = {true 1}` while the POST did land, so both say favourited) — the out-of-order SUCCESS pair is the case that lies.

**Under A (slug-keyed `:favorite-pending`, mirroring `profile.cljs:544-550`).**

| step | dispatched | app-db | wire |
|---|---|---|---|
| click 1 | toggle | flipped `true/1`; `:favorite-pending #{"hello"}` | POST |
| click 2 | toggle → `(contains? (:favorite-pending db) "hello")` → `{}` | unchanged; the heart is `:disabled` on a `:article/favorite-pending? slug` sub, so in the browser the click usually never fires | nothing |
| POST reply | `favorite-synced` re-seeds `true/1` AND `disj`s `"hello"` (unconditionally; rollback does the same) | `true/1`, set `#{}` | one request, one reply, agreement at every settle |
| the user still wants to unfavourite | clicks again after the settle | `false/0`, latched | DELETE |

Cost to the user: a fast second click is DROPPED, not queued — they re-click after the round trip. That is the trade the profile page already made (`profile.cljs:541-543`: "a refused click, not a queued one").

The article-page follow under A: `:article/toggle-follow-author` refuses on `(contains? (:profile.follow-pending db) username)`, `conj`s on issue, and its two settles `disj` unconditionally while keeping the `reply-for-current-slug?` gate on the data write — the same two-owner split at `profile.cljs:569-572`. No namespace cycle: neither `comments.cljs` nor `profile.cljs` requires the other (search over `realworld-http.(profile|comments|favorites)`: only `core.cljs:65-68` requires them), and the key is a plain app-db path, so no require is needed at all. The profile → article walk above then finds alice's button disabled on both pages.

**Under B.** Behaviour unchanged. The `favorites.cljs:133-155` block gains a paragraph of the shape: "favourites are NOT serialised: the heart stays live, a double-click issues an opposite pair, and the last reply to ARRIVE wins the row until the next list load re-seeds it from the server; we accept that because the reply carries the whole article and every list load overwrites it, so the disagreement is bounded by one refetch — whereas `:profile/followed` re-seeds a banner nothing refetches until the next visit". `comments.cljs:548-554` needs a matching sentence for the follow, and it will have to say that the profile latch is not consulted here — the sentence that reads badly next to `profile.cljs:495-505`. `README.md:44` gains a clause ("…the profile follow additionally serialises itself").

**Under C (mine, not the bead's): `:request-id [:favorite slug]` and `[:follow username]` on the three write handlers.** Two lines each, and the runtime does the rest (`registry.cljc:581-607`). Click 2 aborts the POST and suppresses its reply; the DELETE's reply re-seeds the row, so on success the UI agrees with the server without any app state. But: the aborted POST may or may not have been applied (`profile.cljs:471-473`), and if the DELETE then FAILS the rollback restores `prior₂ = {true 1}` against an unknown server state — and adopting it means rewriting the profile block's stated reason for declining `:request-id` on writes, and re-litigating it on the profile page too (where the banner is not refetched). Cheaper than A, not clearly better, and it contradicts the app's own written law; listed so the "why not one line?" question is answered.

## Options

### A. Reuse the existing one-at-a-time pattern (bead's A; reviewer leans here)
- What changes: `favorites.cljs` — a `:favorite-pending` set (init beside `:feed/initialise` at `:54-56` or in `:articles/initialise`), `contains?`-refuse in `:article/toggle-favorite`, `conj` on issue, unconditional `disj` in `favorite-synced` and `favorite-rollback`, one sub `:article/favorite-pending?` taking a slug; `articles.cljs:466-469` and `comments.cljs:808-817` add `:disabled`; `comments.cljs:556-603` reuses `:profile.follow-pending` keyed by author username with the two-owner split, `comments.cljs:760-765` adds `:disabled`; `schema.cljs` one entry `[:favorite-pending] [:maybe [:set :string]]` with the same `:maybe`-is-hydration comment as `:321`; `ssr.cljc:28-33` names a second deliberate absentee; `README.md:46` count → 23 (fixing the rf2-bq1fy drift in passing); a sentence in the `favorites.cljs:133-155` block saying the race policy is now one policy.
- Consequences: programmer/AI copying the flagship gets ONE concurrency law for all three optimistic writes, already argued in one place (`profile.cljs:475-524`), referenced from two. Tools: nothing. Production: n/a (example). Spec: none. Existing tests keep passing (both toggle tests settle between clicks; the latch's `:maybe` covers frames that never ran the initialiser via `(fnil conj #{})`).
- Cost: one worker-morning; 6 files, all inside `examples/real-apps/realworld_http/**`; no hot-zone file. ~40 lines of code and ~15 of comment. Gates: `node implementation/scripts/check-examples-compile.cjs` AND `npm run test:cljs` (the node lane requires the example's production source — the #10149 close reason's own correction, `realworld_cljs_test.cljs:3086-3111` among the cases that run it). An optional latch test mirroring `:3654-3859` lives in `implementation/adapters/reagent/test/` — outside the fence, so a follow-on if wanted; examples themselves stay test-free (rf2-8cevm).
- Risk: low. The one thing to get right is the split (release unconditional, write gated); the profile handlers are the template. A dropped fast second click is a UX choice, already made on the profile page.

### B. Deliberately retain the different race policy and explain it (bead's B)
- What changes: comment paragraphs at `favorites.cljs:133-155` and `comments.cljs:548-554`; one clause at `README.md:44`. No behaviour.
- Consequences: the flagship teaches two policies for one gesture and has to justify the article-page follow's bypass of a latch keyed by the very username it mutates — the justification does not exist yet, and the honest version of it ("we did not extend it here") is not a rationale. The favourite half of B is defensible on its own (bounded by one refetch; the spec's own pattern is unlatched; the Resources twin also never disables).
- Cost: under half a morning; 3 files, no hot-zone; the compile sweep alone (comment-only).
- Risk: the hole in (3) stays; a copier who lifts the article-page follow lifts an unlatched mutation into an app whose profile page promises it is latched.

### C. `:request-id` on the writes (mine, for completeness; not recommended)

title: fix(story): Test-mode promotion cannot capture a variant whose :script has no dispatch step (the flagship login_form testbed's shape) — variant-play-events keeps script dispatches only, result->artifact returns nil, the Test pane hides the promote row; and promote-run-artifact! accepts a nil artifact and registers a hollow variant
description:
== CONTEXT ==
rf2-5vmog (merged as PR #9804) made a promoted regression fail for the reason its source failed: artifact->variant-body now carries the source's terminal :assertions/:checks (promotion.cljc:110 source-expectations) and replaces a dispatch-only capture with the source's full step program (promotion.cljc:145 retained-program). The Story-parity research re-executed the whole journey at trunk 8b876b5466 — failing variant -> promote -> promoted FAILS with its source's assertion count -> fix the app -> PASSES -> restore the fault -> FAILS — on BOTH promotion routes and SEVEN source shapes (ai/findings/Story/fable/evidence.md section P6; scripts ai/findings/Story/fable/probes/probe6c.clj and probe6d.clj, run from tools/story with `clojure -Sdeps '{:deps {day8/re-frame2-epoch {:local/root "../../implementation/epoch"}}}' -M -i <probe>`). The fix holds for every shape whose :script carries at least one dispatch: 7 of 7 on the spec/017 API route, 5 of 7 on the Test-dialog route. The two dialog-route failures are this bead.

== THE MEASUREMENT ==
Shape -> dialog route -> API route (want [[:fail 1] [:pass 1] [:fail 1]]):
- declarative :assertions beside a :script dispatch -> holds -> holds
- in-script [:assert ...] checkpoint after a dispatch -> holds -> holds
- dispatched :rf.assert/* event -> holds -> holds
- tutorial shape, :setup event + :script [[:dispatch-sync [:rf.assert/...]]] -> holds -> holds
- mixed, :setup + :script dispatch + :assertions -> holds -> holds
- :setup event + declarative :assertions, NO script -> [[:pass 0] [:pass 0] [:pass 0]] -> holds
- TESTBED shape, :setup event + :script [[:assert ...]] only -> variant-play-events=[] ; result->artifact nil -> holds

== MECHANISM, AT SOURCE ==
1. tools/story/src/re_frame/story/play.cljc:279 `variant-play-events` returns "one per :dispatch / :dispatch-sync step. Other step types have no event-vector representation and are skipped" — it walks the SCRIPT's stepped program; :setup events are not play events and an [:assert ...] step is not a dispatch. For the two failing shapes it returns [].
2. tools/story/src/re_frame/story/ui/promotion.cljc:110 `result->artifact` returns nil when the result has no :run-artifact back-link AND play-events are empty ("promotion needs a replayable program"). Nothing about the source — not its id, not its program, not its :assertions — reaches the promotion, so the merged fix's `source-variant-id` ([:result :variant/id]) and `retained-program` are never consulted.
3. tools/story/src/re_frame/story/ui/test_mode/view.cljs:605 gates the promotion row on `(some? (result->artifact result play-events))`, so in the BROWSER the affordance is simply absent for these variants. That is a workflow gap, not a hollow variant.
4. tools/story/src/re_frame/story/promotion.cljc:448 `promote-run-artifact!` throws `story-promote-no-id` on a missing id but accepts a NIL artifact and registers a body of (:doc :extends :run-artifact :tags) — on the JVM that variant runs :pass with 0 assertions (probe6d, "dialog body keys=(:doc :extends :run-artifact :tags) ... [[:pass 0] [:pass 0] [:pass 0]]").

== WHO IS AFFECTED ==
All five flagship variants in tools/story/testbeds/login_form/stories.cljs:120-232 are `:setup [[:login/flow ...]]` + `:script [[:assert [:rf.assert/state-is ...]]]` — the exact failing shape — so the demo the tutorial points at (docs/story/04-the-variant-is-a-test.md, docs/story/02) cannot be promoted from Test mode with intent preserved. Any setup-only variant with declarative :assertions is affected the same way. The tutorial's own first variant (a :dispatch-sync of an assert) is not. tools/story/spec/018-Story-UI-North-Star.md section 3.1 sells "generated failures promote to curated variants"; today that is true only for dispatch-bearing scripts.

== FIX, TWO SHAPES (choose A; B is the fallback if A is not small) ==
A. CAPTURE THE PROGRAM THE API ROUTE ALREADY HAS. When play-events are empty but the run result carries a :variant/id whose plan compiles, synthesize the artifact from the compiled plan — the same fold `re-frame.story.determinism/->artifact` applies to a variant plan ([:world :setup] ++ :script -> :event-program, :fx-overrides -> :fx-decisions, :network carried) — and attach `:result` so `source-variant-id` resolves and `source-expectations` fire. One branch, either in `result->artifact` (it already prefers a back-link, then play-events; add "then the source plan") or in the Test pane's slot builder. The merged fix's `retained-program` then does the rest. Keep it pure data -> data; the dialog's default draft (:setup-count 0, :extends source, #{:test}) is unchanged.
B. REFUSE HONESTLY. Keep the gate but render why ("nothing to capture: this variant's script has no dispatch step; promote from the API, or add a dispatch"). Cheaper, but it leaves the flagship demo unpromotable from the UI and contradicts 018 section 3.1 — NOT preferred.
REGARDLESS: `promote-run-artifact!` must refuse a nil or non-artifact with an ex-info (e.g. `story-promote-no-artifact`) exactly as it refuses a missing id, so the JVM can never register a hollow body. Mirror in `materialize-variant-plan` if it has the same hole.

== ACCEPTANCE ==
- Extend the rf2-5vmog block of tools/story/test/re_frame/story/promotion_cljs_test.cljc (lines 430-560; helper `assert-promotions-fail-pass-fail`, routes `dialog-promote!` and `api-promote!`) with the two failing shapes (setup-only + :assertions; setup + [:assert]-only script): both routes run fail / pass / fail with the source's one assertion. Show the new cases RED before the fix.
- A unit test that `promote-run-artifact!` throws on a nil artifact and registers nothing.
- A DOM test (tools/story's *_dom_cljs_test.cljs pattern) that after a Test-mode run of :story.login-form/idle the promotion row is present (shape A) — or, under shape B, that the refusal text is rendered and names the reason.
- Re-run ai/findings/Story/fable/probes/probe6d.clj: every "dialog fault/fix/fault" line reads [[:fail 1] [:pass 1] [:fail 1]] and "result->artifact nil?" reads false.
GATES: tools/story JVM (`clojure -M:test` from tools/story), the story CLJS suite, the DOM cljs tests for test_mode. Not a hot zone.

== DO NOT ==
Change ordinary :extends inheritance (terminal assertions are child-only on purpose); add a generalized inheritance-removal or merge API; add a second capture store; make the Test pane run anything it did not run. rf2-yt6ak (fidelity upgrades retain pins from composed fragments — the #9803 audit finding) is the same "intent survives every projection" class but a different file (ui/view_state.cljc) and is held separately; do not fold it in.

title: Incomplete: resource and mutation introspection omit frame-value normalization
description:
The documented frame-target contract is incomplete in the resources introspection doors: rf/resource-state and rf/mutation-state accept an explicit live frame value but return nil for existing rows, whereas the same read by frame ID returns the row. Complete the existing one-way target normalization in these two functions. This is one shared target-resolution defect across the paired introspection API, not a new API or validation requirement.

Discovered during merged-PR audit #9766 at c198de34a5e7ec7d0f097c8009a4b16132c363d0. That PR correctly repairs the example caller by passing fid; its three example repairs remain valid. Its body flags the resource-state library inconsistency but a routing note is not a separately tracked correction. Closed source rf2-gwye.44 supplies the discovery chain; rf2-fzbj.7 is the resources implementation owner. Neither closed source is reopened or has its prior verdict/closure rewritten.

Contract and source:
- spec/002-Frames.md, opening principles: a public operation accepts the ID keyword or live frame value and normalizes the latter to its ID; teardown has its own incarnation rule.
- docs/core/frames.md, lexical scoping section: every read/write surface accepts either the value returned by make-frame or the ID interchangeably.
- implementation/core/src/re_frame/frame.cljc:208, frame-target->id is the existing pure normalization seam.
- implementation/resources/src/re_frame/resources.cljc:144-182 resource-state forwards the raw frame target into both frame-app-db-value (scope resolution) and frame-runtime-db-value (entry lookup).
- Same file:184-217 mutation-state forwards the raw target into frame-runtime-db-value.
These internal readers key the ID registry directly. A frame value is not that key, so the result falsely represents a live entry as absent. This is observable in the intended tool/test/SSR projection lane, including callers holding an anonymous make-frame result; callers should not need a value-to-ID accessor.

Fresh actual-source JVM witness (runner exit 0 means successful defect reproduction): initialize plain-atom, register a global resource and a mutation, hold managed HTTP through a registered no-op effect override, and create :audit/frame with resource ensure and mutation execute as initial-events. ID-target reads report :loading and :pending respectively; frame-value-target reads both report nil. rf/frame-state-value f equals the ID-target state, proving the value is the correct live target. Other-frame absent-row controls return nil; explicit nil controls retain :rf.error/no-frame-context. Finally destroy both frames and shut down the process. No external HTTP was issued.
Evidence: C:/Users/miket/.codex/tmp/audit-re-frame2-pr9766-frame-target-probe-1.clj, .log, .exit. The log names the actual resources source URL in this checkout. Resource production and frame producer source were verified unchanged from the audited merge before/after the probe. CLJS was inspected, not freshly compiled for this probe; the faulty implementation is shared CLJC.

Required correction: normalize an explicit frame value through the existing frame-target->id before both app-db scope resolution and runtime-db entry/instance lookup. Preserve explicit-nil refusal, unknown/destroyed-ID nil behavior, and normal ID reads. Keep this in the two public target boundaries; do not broaden unrelated internal registry readers, add an accessor, or alter the repaired example back.

Deduplication: all 32 literal-open Beads inspected; none explicitly records this defect and correction. Shared resources ownership is not an exact duplicate. No mayor notification or acknowledgment is inferred from this finding or its forward pointers.
acceptance_criteria: CLJC regression using actual public registration/dispatch and a live make-frame value: resource-state and mutation-state equal corresponding ID reads for present rows; a from-db resource scope resolves against the same app-db; another frame remains isolated; missing/nil target refusal and unknown/destroyed-ID nil controls remain unchanged. Verify in focused JVM and CLJS resources tests. Existing #9766 example ID fix remains valid.
notes:
VERDICT (rf2-ym12) — FIXED in PR #9781, commit 7f31df0333 on worker/frametarget-a (base 84328e4c1c).

Premise verified at source at 84328e4c1c: `resource-state` and `mutation-state` in implementation/resources/src/re_frame/resources.cljc forwarded the raw `:frame` target into the id-keyed `rf.frame/frame-app-db-value` / `frame-runtime-db-value`; `frame-target->id` had drifted to implementation/core/src/re_frame/frame.cljc:211 (the description says :208).

Fix: both public functions normalize an explicit target through the existing `rf.frame/frame-target->id` before the app-db scope resolution and the runtime-db lookup. Two call sites, nothing else. Explicit-nil / missing `:frame` refusal (`:rf.error/no-frame-context`), nil for unknown/destroyed ids, and ordinary id reads are unchanged. No internal registry reader broadened, no accessor added, implementation/core untouched, the #9766 example id fix untouched.

A second symptom the red run surfaced, beyond the silent nil: a `{:from-db}` resource read by frame VALUE THREW `:rf.error/resource-sub-unresolved-scope`, because the named resolver ran against the nil app-db a value read produced — a misleading diagnostic naming the resolver rather than the target. The same normalization fixes it.

Regression: new implementation/resources/test/re_frame/resources_frame_value_target_cljs_test.cljc (dual JVM + CLJS; public reg/dispatch, live `make-frame` values). It pairs every value read with the id read of the same frame for present resource rows and mutation instances; checks that a `{:from-db}` scope resolves from each frame's own app-db; checks isolation of a second frame by value in both directions; checks that a destroyed frame reads nil by retained value and by id; covers an anonymous `make-frame` value; and keeps the missing/nil/unknown/ordinary-id controls.

Evidence (captured exit codes):
- RED against the pre-fix source, focused JVM: exit 1 — 3 tests, 17 assertions, 3 failures (value reads nil where id reads found the row) + 1 error (the `{:from-db}` value read throwing resource-sub-unresolved-scope); the controls test passed.
- GREEN focused JVM: exit 0 — 3 tests, 32 assertions.
- `JVM resources (clojure -M:test)` lane (test.yml `jvm-resources`): exit 0 — 872 tests, 7763 assertions, 0 failures.
- `CLJS (shadow-cljs :node-test)` lane (`npm run test:cljs`): exit 0 — 12068 tests, 60175 assertions, 0 failures; the new namespace run alone from the same bundle: exit 0, 3 tests, 32 assertions.
- Ratchets grading these paths (lane bijection, thrown-error messages, retired spellings, require-alias dialect, keyword catalogue, architecture census, ambient durable reads, failure-corpus residue, retired image keys, inject-cofx residue): all exit 0.

Declined, per the stance: no docstring rewrite (neither docstring claims an id-only target; the inline comment at each call site records why), no change to the `:frame <frame-id>` recovery hint in the refusal message, no broadening to other id-keyed readers.

`valid-scope-policy?` (`implementation/resources/src/re_frame/resources/registry.cljc:75–114` at 6d513ba07f; `resolve-scope-for-event` arms at `:841–861`) admits FIVE policy shapes. The corpus — 14 `reg-resource` registrations across 5 apps + 1 testbed — uses exactly two: `:rf.scope/global` ×6 and `{:from-db <id>}` ×8 (`git grep -n -E '^\s*:scope\s' -- examples testbeds` shows only those two spellings). Zero app/testbed consumers of:

- **B3** `:scope :rf.scope/from-caller` — "every ensure / refetch / sub MUST pass `:scope`"; missing → `:rf.error/resource-scope-required-from-caller` (`registry.cljc:846–855`). It alone drags the ~140-line dev heuristic `:rf.warning/resource-sub-scope-mismatch` (`subs.cljc:121–260`; fires for THIS policy only, `:238`) — compensation for the policy's own ergonomics. The skill's "current user" snippet (`skills/re-frame2/patterns/resources.md:163–166`) teaches this zero-consumer policy — the AI footgun.
- **B4** `:scope (fn [] …)` fn-of-nothing — arm 3d, `registry.cljc:857–858`; 1 test line.
- **B5** `:scope <literal EDN>` at registration — arm 3e, `registry.cljc:861`. A constant at registration partitions the cache exactly as `:rf.scope/global` does — it is global under another label; a tenant that is state is `{:from-db}`.

At `reg-resource`, `:scope` ∈ { `:rf.scope/global` , `{:from-db <id>}` }. Nothing else. Use-site `:scope` on an event payload or a sub query stays an OPTIONAL OVERRIDE taking a concrete scope or `{:from-db …}` — never required (this preserves the explicit-selection case: the tenant-switcher testbed's `cache-witness` reads two tenants' caches at once via explicit sub `:scope`s, and must keep working).
