title: api(boot): configure! emits dev-gated :rf.warning/unknown-configure-key for an unrecognised bare top-level key
description:
_Filed 2026-09-05 12:37:46 AUSEST by the API-review wave-3 coordinator from boot.md (ref boot.2); parent epic rf2-kuky. Local-only dossiers: ai/findings/API-review/{fable,codex}/ (gitignored; may be deleted)._

## Problem

`rf/configure!` (`implementation/core/src/re_frame/core.cljc:2554-2605`) reads three bare keys — `:epoch-history`, `:trace-buffer`, `:elision` — and drops every other key without a signal: `(rf/configure! {:epoch-histroy {:depth 100}})` returns `nil`, applies nothing, says nothing. The docstring (`:2578`), `implementation/core/test/re_frame/configure_test.clj:221` `configure-unknown-key-is-silent-no-op` (rf2-mmlci) and `spec/API.md:873` / `:930` §Fixed-and-additive pin the swallow as intended. That contradicts `spec/Conventions.md:1149-1160` §No silent swallow, which names this exact shape — "a bare or framework-namespaced key the runtime does not recognise … reads as a typo of a real key and MUST signal" — and reserves silence for user-namespaced extension keys. API.md:930's rationale ("user code that wraps configure can pass a composed config value straight through") is the namespaced-key case and survives; the bare-key silence is a tested violation.

A live instance in the tree: `tools/re-frame2-pair-mcp/src/re_frame2_pair_mcp/tools/discover_app.cljs:248` tells the AI to run `(rf/configure! {:source-coords {:annotate-dom? true}})`. `:source-coords` is not a `configure!` key anywhere (`git grep -n -F ':source-coords' implementation/core/src/re_frame/core.cljc` hits only the machine `:states`-tree usage at `:655-694`; `annotate-dom?` appears nowhere else in the repo), so the advice no-ops silently today.

## Evidence (tip 3fbd3a9ede)

- `core.cljc:2594-2605` — the three `when-let` delegations; nothing else is read.
- `configure_test.clj:221-245`; `spec/API.md:873`, `:895-897`, `:930`; `spec/Conventions.md:1149-1171` (the instances table at `:1171` lists `:rf.warning/unknown-dispatch-opt` as the dispatch case).
- The emission convention to reuse: `re-frame.router.diagnostics/emit-unknown-dispatch-opts-warning!` (`core/src/re_frame/router/diagnostics.cljc:318-372`) — body gated on `rf.interop/debug-enabled?` so it DCEs, `rf.trace/emit! :warning :rf.warning/<id> {…}`, one warning per call naming every bad key and the known set, observational never refusal.
- The per-subsystem sibling already shipped: `:rf.warning/trace-buffer-unrecognised-opts` (`core/src/re_frame/trace/tooling.cljc:625`; `spec/009-Instrumentation.md:2072`, recovery `:ignored`).
- `core.cljc` already requires `re-frame.trace :as rf.trace` (`:52`) and `re-frame.interop :as rf.interop` (`:41`).

## Target API

```clojure
(rf/configure! {:epoch-history {:depth 100}})   ; unchanged
(rf/configure! {:epoch-histroy {:depth 100}})   ; dev builds: :rf.warning/unknown-configure-key
                                                ;   {:unknown-keys [:epoch-histroy]
                                                ;    :known-keys   [:elision :epoch-history :trace-buffer]
                                                ;    :reason "…"}
                                                ; the call still returns nil and applies nothing
(rf/configure! {:rf.foo/bar 1})                 ; framework-namespaced unknown → same warning
(rf/configure! {:myapp/thing 1})                ; user-namespaced → silent (the extension-key carve-out)
```

Sketch, in `configure!` after the three delegations:

```clojure
(def ^:private known-configure-keys #{:epoch-history :trace-buffer :elision})

(defn- unknown-configure-keys [m]
  (into []
        (remove (fn [k]
                  (or (contains? known-configure-keys k)
                      (and (keyword? k) (some? (namespace k))
                           (not (re-find #"^rf(\.|$)" (namespace k)))))))
        (keys m)))

;; inside configure!, gated so the whole surface DCEs under :advanced + goog.DEBUG=false
(when rf.interop/debug-enabled?
  (when-let [unknown (seq (unknown-configure-keys config-map))]
    (rf.trace/emit! :warning :rf.warning/unknown-configure-key
                    {:unknown-keys (vec unknown)
                     :known-keys   (vec (sort known-configure-keys))
                     :detected-at  (rf.interop/now-ms)
                     :reason       (str "configure! was given unrecognised top-level key"
                                        (when (next unknown) "s") " " (pr-str (vec unknown))
                                        ". The runtime reads only " (pr-str (vec (sort known-configure-keys)))
                                        " — a bare or rf-namespaced unknown key is ignored, so a typo "
                                        "(e.g. :epoch-histroy) changes nothing. User-namespaced keys "
                                        "pass through silently.")})))
```

Recovery `:ignored` (mirrors `:rf.warning/trace-buffer-unrecognised-opts`). No validation of nested opts — each subsystem keeps its own. Non-map arguments are rf2-xn13's surface, not this bead's.

## Corroboration

One-reviewer (fable boot doc). Codex: "A development warning for unknown bare keys is useful feedback; it should reuse existing diagnostic conventions, not grow a configuration policy framework." This bead reuses the `unknown-dispatch-opt` convention verbatim and adds nothing else.

## Relationship to rf2-xn13 (open, P2, same fn)

rf2-xn13 replaces the `assert` at `core.cljc:2594` with an always-on `throw-error!` for NON-MAP arguments and lists "do not reject unknown top-level keys" as a non-goal. This bead does not reject — the call still no-ops; it warns, dev-only — so the two are compatible. They touch the same fn, docstring, test file and API.md rows: dispatch both to ONE worker, or sequence this bead after rf2-xn13's PR merges; never in parallel. The AMEND below points rf2-xn13's worker here so it does not add a test pinning the swallow harder.

## Deletion list

None (the `:221` test is rewritten, not deleted).

## Consumers to migrate

Every in-repo `configure!` caller uses known keys — Xray `tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/settings/effects.cljs:468,491`; mcp-conformance evals `tools/mcp-conformance/test/live-re-frame2-pair-turn-observation.cjs:95,453`, `live-re-frame2-pair-redaction.cjs:211`; Story / story-mcp tests — so the suites should emit zero warnings (acceptance checks it). One tool string to fix in the same PR: pair-mcp `discover_app.cljs:248` — remove the `:source-coords` `configure!` advice (it is not a key) and point at the real mechanism for `data-rf2-source-coord` annotation, or delete the sentence; with this bead an AI following the old note would finally see the warning that was missing.

## Spec, docs, examples, skills, tests

- `spec/API.md` (HOT-ZONE): `:873` `configure!` row ("unknown top-level key silently no-ops" → "an unknown bare or `rf`-namespaced key warns `:rf.warning/unknown-configure-key` in dev builds and is ignored; user-namespaced keys pass through silently"); `:895-897` §Configure keys intro; `:930` §Fixed-and-additive — keep the composed-value pass-through for namespaced keys, strike "silently ignores unknown top-level keys".
- `spec/Conventions.md` (HOT-ZONE): `:1171` instances table — add "Core configure! | unknown bare top-level key (`:rf.warning/unknown-configure-key`)"; `:1420` bucket-1 prose if it repeats the silent claim.
- `spec/009-Instrumentation.md` (HOT-ZONE): §Error contract warning catalogue — new row beside `:2072`: `:warning`, diagnostic, recovery `:ignored`, data `:unknown-keys` `:known-keys` `:reason`, dev-only (`interop/debug-enabled?`-gated, DCE'd in production).
- `docs/api/re-frame.core.md:864-890` `configure!` entry; `core.cljc:2578-2580` docstring.
- Skills: `git grep -n -i "silently no-op" skills/` beside `configure` — 0 expected; re-measure.
- Tests — `configure_test.clj`: rewrite `:221` as `configure-unknown-bare-key-warns-and-no-ops`: `:strict-subs`, `:totally-made-up`, retired `:sub-cache`, `:rf.nope/x` each produce exactly one `:rf.warning/unknown-configure-key` in `(rf/trace-buffer :rf/default {:flat true})` (the collection idiom of the neighbouring test at `:200-219`), the call returns `nil`, known-key state is unchanged (keep the existing second `testing` block); controls: `{:myapp/thing 1}` and `{:epoch-history {:depth 7}}` produce none. The elision probe (`npm run test:elision`, `implementation/scripts/check-elision.cjs`) pins that `:rf.warning/*` reason strings vanish under `goog.DEBUG=false` — add the new id to its sentinel roster if that roster is enumerated by id (re-measure; do not name-grep).
- `spec/api-manifest.edn`: no row change; run `--check`. Conformance corpus: no `configure!` fixtures; unaffected. Migration README: no v1 name changes.

## Sequencing and hot-zone

`API.md`, `Conventions.md`, `009` → serialise with @boot.1 (`API.md`, `009`), @boot.3 (all three), rf2-xn13 (same fn / test / API.md rows — one worker or after its merge), and any open bead on those files.

## Risks

Low: dev-only, observational, DCE'd; production behaviour unchanged. The `rf` / `rf.*` namespace test is the same line Conventions draws for "framework-namespaced".

Local dossier: ai/findings/API-review/fable/boot-adapter-and-features.md (local-only pointer)

- `npm run test:cljs` and `scripts/test-jvm-tools.sh` logs contain zero `:rf.warning/unknown-configure-key` emissions from in-repo callers.
- `tools/re-frame2-pair-mcp/.../discover_app.cljs:248` no longer advertises a `:source-coords` `configure!` key.

The source report routes this correction only as added notes on implementation Bead rf2-2n6uv.2.1 (the separate :spawn :on-done defect). This new OPEN finding tracks the skill correction separately, as required by the audit instructions; coordinate it with that worker rather than implement twice.
Add parent destruction to the tracked-child lifetime wording and identify transition-reducer lowering with the literal :spawn/:spawn-all maps retained. Preserve the explicit distinction that hand-emitted actors without tracking slots outlive their spawner. No new API or runtime change.

title: CI-log instrument defects: gh refuses a completed job's log while the run is open, and grepping a job log for a test namespace is a vacuous control
description:
Two defects in reading a CI job's result, both measured 2026-09-17 by the worker on rf2-y8doi.14
(PR #9947), each of which cost a wasted call, and the SECOND of which nearly put a false corroboration
into a completion report the mayor would have believed.

## (1) `gh run view --log --job <id>` REFUSES while ANY job in the run is unfinished — even for a job that has COMPLETED

The message is *"run is still in progress; logs will be available when it is complete"*. It is a
statement about the RUN, not about the job you asked for, and not about the logs existing.

**Why it misleads:** you ask for one job's log precisely BECAUSE that job has finished — usually
finished RED — and the refusal reads as "the evidence is not available yet", so the natural move is to
wait. On this repository's matrix a single slow job (`examples_compile` is the usual one) holds the run
open for many minutes after the lane you care about has already failed, so the wait is long and
unnecessary.

**Measured both ways on this box the same day:** the mayor hit the identical refusal on a sibling PR's
failing node lane and concluded the logs were simply not yet written. They were.

**The guard:** `gh api repos/<owner>/<repo>/actions/jobs/<id>/logs` returns the completed job's log
regardless of the run's state. Reach for the API form whenever the CLI form refuses with an
in-progress message and the JOB you named is complete.

## (2) GREPPING A JOB LOG FOR A TEST NAMESPACE NAME IS A VACUOUS CONTROL — a passing `cljs.test` run PRINTS NO NAMESPACE NAMES

This is the dangerous one. Having got a green lane, the natural corroboration is "did my new namespace
actually run?" — so you grep the job log for the namespace. It reads **0**, and 0 looks like "my tests
did not run", or, read the other way by a tired author, gets written up as though the search had
confirmed something.

**It confirms nothing in either direction.** `cljs.test` prints namespace names on FAILURE paths; a
clean run emits totals and nothing else. So the zero is a property of the runner's output format, not
evidence about what was compiled or executed. **The worker nearly reported that zero as corroboration**
and caught it.

**The instrument that actually discriminates is the COUNT DELTA**, derived from the source BEFORE any
log is opened: predict the change in tests and assertions from the diff, then compare against a
baseline taken at YOUR OWN MERGE BASE. On this item the prediction was +10 tests / +40 assertions and
the run matched exactly, which is evidence that CI compiled that branch — where the namespace grep
would have been silent whatever happened.

**This is the vacuity rule reaching CI logs**, one door on from the rule this project already carries
for gates: *a gate cannot fail on a file containing none of what it inspects.* Here a SEARCH cannot
find what the successful path never prints. Both produce a clean-looking zero from an instrument that
was never able to answer.

## Required correction

Add both to CLAUDE.md's instrument-defect catalogue, § "Ways the INSTRUMENTS misreport", as new lettered
items in the existing style: the observable, the measurement, the direction it fails in, and the guard.

**(1) fails CLOSED** — it withholds evidence and costs a wait, so it is catalogued for the cost rather
than for danger. **(2) fails in the REASSURING direction** for the question it is asked, which is the
property that earns it a place: a zero that reads as either "nothing ran" or, worse, as confirmation.

Keep the existing framing conventions: name the guard, state the control both ways, and do not
generalise beyond what was measured — in particular do not assert what OTHER test runners print.

## Scope and sequencing

- Fence: `CLAUDE.md`, the instrument-defect bullet only. No new gate, no script, no wrapper.
- Several beads have edited this file today (`rf2-d3l8g`, `rf2-oitjw`, `rf2-1hh87`, all merged) and
  `rf2-48awk` is open against item (s) in the same bullet — **sequence against it; two workers must
  never hold one file.**
- `CLAUDE.md` is `i/lf w/crlf`: never `sed -i` (item (u)), build replacement text with the Write tool
  rather than a heredoc (item (o)), take the three line-ending numbers with Python on bytes.
- The gate for repo-root markdown is `scripts/check_readme_links.py --ci`, NOT `check_doc_slugs.py` —
  two workers have separately DEMONSTRATED the latter exits 0 on a planted broken link there.
- **Re-measure both defects before writing them up.** They are relayed from one worker's report; the
  catalogue's value is that its entries are measured, and this project has already found one catalogued
  entry (item (s)) to be intermittent when re-tested.

description:

The mayor re-verified the key at tools/template/resources/day8/re_frame2_template/_shared/shadow-cljs.edn:11-12 (`{:deps {:aliases [:shadow]} :source-paths ["src" "test"]}`) and the pin at tools/template/test/day8/re_frame2_template/template_test.clj:178-179.

MEASURED (reviewer, two-file config in a scratch dir, `node implementation/node_modules/shadow-cljs/cli/runner.js compile nope`): with `{:deps {:aliases [:shadow]} :source-paths ["src" "test"]}` the launcher prints the four-line `WARNING: The configured :source-paths in shadow-cljs.edn were ignored! / When using :deps they must be configured in deps.edn` banner before launching the JVM; the control without the key prints none. - tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/static/routes/simulate_url.cljs:1-8 explicitly identifies URL resolution as a Static browse operation; header at 80-125 renders the native text input with data-testid rf-xray-static-routes-sim-input at line 104.

2. Follow its Dynamic Routes row and open that tab; selecting a navigation event or an ordinary event does not reveal a simulator.
Expected: the inventory directs the operator to Static -> Routes for URL ranking, and describes Dynamic Routes as the current-route/epoch-activity/table lens.
Actual: it explicitly promises a Simulate-URL input in Dynamic Routes, where none is rendered. A deeper read partly corrects the location but also teaches a stale set of section names.
Impact: a programmer or AI following the canonical tour searches the wrong mode for a shipped control. There is a working Static route and no data corruption, so P3 is appropriate.

Executable witness:
Babashka read the original forms from absolute tools/xray/src paths and evaluated the Dynamic panel-tree with ALL of its original section/row helper functions, importing the real theme.tokens constants. No rendering helper was replaced by a stub. Two synthetic composites represented an active /orders/42 route, one with no navigation activity and one with an :on-match navigation from :home to :orders. Both returned the three expected section testids and ZERO :input nodes. The original Static simulate-url/header, rank-cell and candidate-row forms returned the real simulator input for /orders/42. Its dispatcher was supplied as a fail-if-called function and was not called during projection.

Probe output (runner exit 0):
{:dynamic-navigation? false, :input-count 0, :sections 3}
{:dynamic-navigation? true, :input-count 0, :sections 3}
{:static-input "rf-xray-static-routes-sim-input", :source-root "C:/Users/miket/code/re-frame2/tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/"}

This is an executed source projection witness with inspected production mount wiring, not a browser/React commit or a full CLJS suite.

Precise repair:
- Remove the Simulate-URL claim from the Dynamic Routes row; describe current route, navigation evidence and the route table.
- Make the family leaf name the actual three sections, retaining the useful distinction that an ordinary event keeps current route/table visible while navigation activity is quiet.
- Keep URL matching/ranking under Static -> Routes. No need to add a duplicate simulator to Dynamic, change APIs, or expand the tour into implementation anatomy.

2. The Dynamic description agrees with the three current section captions, the no-navigation state, and the registered-route table.
3. A focused manual answer check returns the existing Static simulator as the first surface for URL simulation and Dynamic Routes for "what did this navigation event do?". Reuse the existing manual harness if recording it; no new runner or prose-presence test is warranted.
4. Required link/package/doc checks for the eventual prose diff retain their normal project safeguards. Verify prose against the source; an inventory-ID gate alone cannot prove where a control is mounted.

OTHER EXECUTED VALIDATION

A separate Babashka probe loaded the exact valid-panels, panel-aliases, normalize-panel and focus-command->dispatches forms from focus.cljc. Six assertions passed:

DONE. Draft PR #9715, branch worker/storydeps-a, one commit (67bb484529), one file, comments only.

THE CORRECTION. tools/story/deps.edn, the day8/re-frame2-xray :exclusions rationale under
"THE STATED REPLACEMENT (this is a re-point, not a silent drop)". The unqualified sentence
"Xray renders through re-frame.substrate.adapter and the adapter the HOST installs governs the
runtime path, so Xray is fully served by Story's stock-Reagent adapter" is replaced by the split
it describes:

  * THE EMBEDDED PANEL DOOR - panels/render-panel! and panels/mount-shell!, the chokepoint behind
    every mount-<panel>! facade the RHS inspector reaches - still delegates to
    rf.substrate.adapter/render with a hiccup tree, so the adapter the HOST installs does govern
    that path and Story's stock-Reagent adapter does serve it.
  * XRAY'S OWN MOUNT VERBS - mount/open!, mount/open-overlay! and mount/popout!, the last being
    Story's popout escape hatch - paint through re-frame.fresco client roots Xray owns and do not
    consult the host adapter at all (rf2-k97c.3 severed that coupling).

The bead cited lines 86-95; re-derived at this branch's base (f882486af0) that range was exact.
The paragraph now runs 86-107.

PREMISE VERIFIED AT SOURCE rather than taken from the bead, as the brief required.
mount.cljs carries 0 adapter/render sites; panels.cljs carries 2. The zero has a live positive
control on the same census over the same file (fresco reads 9 in mount.cljs), so it means absence
and not a broken instrument. Code was separated from comment before counting: panels.cljs shows six
textual hits and only two are executable - render-panel! spans 246-341 and holds the call at 328,
mount-shell! starts at 793 and holds the call at 855; the other four (84, 311, 529, 834) are
docstring or comment prose. On the Fresco side, mount.cljs owns two rf.fresco/client-root handles
(xray-root 367, xray-popout-root 371), render-shell! (373) paints via rf.fresco/render! (382), and
open! (1010), open-overlay! (1045) and popout! (1641) all reach it - open! and open-overlay!
through mount-shell-into! (385), popout! through render-shell! directly at 1697. The searches ran
through the ripgrep-backed tool, not Bash grep, whose -iF pair aborts at exit 134 on this box.

THE SURVIVING CLAUSE WAS RE-CHECKED TOO. "Xray's src requires neither reagent2.* nor the adapter ns"
still holds: all six hits of reagent2 / re-frame.adapter.reagent / reagent-slim under tools/xray/src
sit in comments or docstrings, none in a :require form.

WHAT DELIBERATELY DID NOT CHANGE, and this is proved rather than asserted. The :exclusions value,
the publication/classpath argument, the "THE :exclusions IS LOAD-BEARING - do not drop it
(rf2-qvyr)" line, the preceding embedded-Xray context and the dependency conclusion all stand
verbatim. The parsed EDN data before and after the edit compares EQUAL under clojure.edn/read-string
(= is true, no differing top-level keys), so no coordinate, exclusion or alias moved. The diff is
17 insertions / 5 deletions, every line a ;; comment. The two in-file references to "line 16" (at
lines 74 and 88) remain correct because nothing above line 86 moved.

RF2-L1JM IS UNTOUCHED. This states today's behaviour and settles nothing about tomorrow's. I
deliberately did NOT add a forward pointer to rf2-l1jm in the file: the coordination clause - if
the embed door later moves, this sentence needs updating again - is already recorded in rf2-l1jm's
own notes, which is where a fresh maintainer working that decision will read it, and putting an
open question into a dependency file's rationale is the kind of thing that goes stale next.

GATES. Every exit code below is the runner's own, captured with the redirect and the echo on one
command line in one shell.

  jvm-tools-story (clojure -M:test from tools/story) .... exit 0, 1914 tests / 7047 assertions,
      0 failures, 0 errors. This is the one gate that genuinely reads this deps.edn; it ran from
      the worker worktree's tools/story with pwd printed on the same command line, so the tree it
      resolved from is known.
  scripts/check_retired_spellings.py .................... exit 0, and PROVED to read this file: the
      retired product name planted in the very comment line being edited took it RED at exit 1
      naming tools/story/deps.edn:101. Restore verified by blob hash against the committed object -
      the default git hash-object form matched (correct for this file's i/lf w/crlf classification)
      - corroborated by a clean git diff --quiet HEAD and a zero residue probe.
  scripts/check_jvm_lane_rosters.py ..................... exit 0 (reads deps.edn presence/aliases).
  scripts/check-no-hardcoded-paths.sh ................... exit 0.
  scripts/check_readme_inventories.py ................... exit 0.

ONE GREEN IS DELIBERATELY NOT CLAIMED AS EVIDENCE. scripts/check_retired_image_keys.py DOES cover
this path - tools/ is in its DEFAULT_SOURCE_DIRS and .edn is in its _CLJ_SUFFIXES - but it grades a
Clojure-family file through _clj_code_lines, i.e. CODE ONLY. A retired image key planted in the
same comment left it GREEN at exit 0. So it is green and its green says nothing whatever about this
diff. Recording the mechanism rather than the colour, because the next comment-only change to a
.clj/.edn file will meet the same false reassurance.

VECTOR: a pair-MCP server NEWER than its app renders `project-egress` on an epoch record into a runtime whose door has no epoch arm, or whose epoch artefact stamps no `:kind` → the door treats the record as a kindless VALUE and bare-walks it from `:path []` → declared-sensitive `:db-*` slots ship RAW. Three guards, each one line, together closing every mixed-version pairing:
- **G1 (new core, recognised kind, no projector)** — `project-egress` throws `:rf.error/epoch-artefact-missing` before returning any payload (item 2).

## Problem

A spawned actor is an event handler whose id is its address (005 §Spawning). Every real parent and child in the tree holds that id (`:rf/spawned` on the parent, `:rf/self-id` / `:rf/parent-id` on the child) and sends with the one verb `[:dispatch [id ev]]` — `examples/patterns/websocket/connection.cljs:99-108`, `messages.cljs:342-344`, `examples/patterns/long_running_work/worker.cljs:56,143`. Beside that, 005 teaches a second addressing mode and heads its example "the common case" (005:2708): a per-frame reverse index `[:rf.runtime/machines :system-ids <name>] → <actor-id>` written at spawn (`spawn.cljc` ~:574), released on every teardown path (D8, 005:3205), read by `re-frame.machines/machine-by-system-id` and sent to by `[:rf.machine/dispatch-to-system [sid ev]]`, with two traces, one error, a conformance axis and a runtime-db slot. Consumers in `examples/`, `testbeds/`, `tools/*/src`: **0**, through two independent counts eight weeks apart (July wave 2, September wave 3); the only hits are machines-viz's closed spawn-key vocabulary and Xray's diff-panel row for the SLOT. `dispatch-to-system-fx` is a silent no-op on an unbound name (`machines.cljc` ~:282; `docs/machines/actors.md:217` teaches that as a feature) — Principles §No silent swallow, verbatim. And the one behaviour that distinguishes `:system-id` from `:fixed-actor-id` — a collision REBINDS the name to the new actor while the old one lives on unnamed (005:2905) — is not XState's: `system._set` THROWS on a duplicate systemId (verified on `main`, 2026-09-06). So the rebind is a divergence kept in parity's name.

`:child-machine` is a spec key with no implementation (API.md:952; 005:4595-4602, :4637) whose own reconsideration trigger — repeated hand-rolled entry/exit spawn boilerplate — has never fired: the tree has 0 hand-emitted `[:rf.machine/spawn]` sites, and the sugar it describes already shipped as `:spawn` (005:4049).

**Ruling A (rf2-kuky.15): delete both.** The address is the id; `:fixed-actor-id` is the one stable-name mechanism. No shim, no deprecation, no park, no "retired key" diagnostic.

## Target — replacement teaching (write it; do not only delete)

1. **Flip 005:2708.** Declarative `:spawn` leads (it IS the common case: 4 declarative sites vs 0 hand-emitted); the hand-emitted `[:rf.machine/spawn]` fx is presented as the desugar target and the only non-state-bound lifetime. The example loses `:system-id`; the :2719 `dispatch-to-system` sentence goes.
2. **Write the rebind difference into 005** (§Declarative `:spawn` or the `:fixed-actor-id` row) as plain sentences, so nobody re-adds a registry to "restore parity": *The name is the address. A re-entered `:fixed-actor-id` child is a new incarnation at the SAME address (`spawn.cljc` ~:1184 — attempts reuse the id; `actor-generation` is 1 for them); the join and lifecycle machinery tells incarnations apart via the `:work-generation` stamp (~:313), but an ordinary application dispatch to `:x` reaches whichever incarnation currently owns `:x`. Two children in one `:spawn-all` batch resolving to one literal are rejected (`:rf.error/machine-spawn-all-duplicate-id`, `spawn-all-address-collisions`). XState's actor system throws on a duplicate systemId; re-frame2 has no separate registry — the id is the only name.*
3. **Complete the imperative-spawn recipe** (Codex; verified at tip: only DECLARATIVE spawns carry a reducer-stamped `:rf/spawned-id`, `spawn.cljc:49-62` — a hand-emitted fx with only `:id-prefix` allocates at fx time and delivers nothing back to the author's snapshot): *An action that hand-emits `[:rf.machine/spawn …]` and must keep the child's id chooses a fresh explicit keyword address from an event value or a recorded coeffect, stores it in ordinary `:data`, and passes it as `:fixed-actor-id`. title: Skill review: skills/re-frame2 - completeness, correctness, organisation, skill best practice
description:
Review the `re-frame2` skill: skills/re-frame2/, meaning SKILL.md and every reference and script under it. Do it in four SERIAL passes, finishing each one, and fixing what it finds, before starting the next:

1. COMPLETENESS. Does the skill cover what its description promises, and what an agent invoking it will need? Look for gaps against the current spec/ and implementation/: features, APIs, workflows and failure modes this skill's audience will meet. Also look for references the SKILL.md points at that are missing or empty.
2. CORRECTNESS. Check every claim against spec/ and implementation/ at trunk: API names, signatures, keywords, reserved namespaces, file paths, commands and code examples. Look for names that no longer exist, behaviour that has changed, dead links, and examples that would not compile or run as written.
3. ORGANISATION AND STRUCTURE. SKILL.md should be a concise entry point. References should be split by topic, sit one level deep, and be linked directly from SKILL.md. Nothing should be duplicated across files, terminology should be consistent, and a reader should find what they need in the order they need it.
4. SKILL BEST PRACTICE (Anthropic's Agent Skills authoring guidance).
   - Frontmatter: `name`, and a `description` in the third person that says what the skill does AND when to use it, with specific trigger terms.
   - A lean SKILL.md body (well under ~500 lines) that uses progressive disclosure into reference files.
   - No time-sensitive or history narrative.
   - Concrete examples, and checklists for workflows where order matters.
   - Scripts for deterministic operations rather than prose instructions.

DELIVERABLE: one PR applying the fixes, whose body summarises what each pass found and changed. Report findings outside skills/re-frame2/ (spec/, implementation/, skills/README.md, another skill) rather than editing them. skills/README.md is shared by every skill, so name any change it needs and do not make it.

POSTURE: fix real defects and improve structure where that pays a reader. Do not rewrite for style. Present-tense convention: no bead ids and no history in the skill text.

title: Unit-test pruning: flows
description:
Apply Mike's pruning prompt to implementation/flows/test recursively in an isolated worker worktree. This is a distinct cluster in rf2-0wcq5. Push a test-only draft PR, babysit all checks until green, then mark ready; do not merge. Report no-op with evidence instead of manufacturing changes.

Simplify the unit tests under implementation/flows/test. Do not change the code under test. LLMs tend to
write too many low-value unit tests, and this suite was largely written by them.

Assume the suite has more tests than it needs, and that many of its tests are longer
than they need to be. Every test costs CI time, reading time and refactoring friction,
and the low-value ones hide the tests that matter. I want a lean suite: each test earns
its place by guarding a behaviour a caller relies on, against a regression that could
plausibly happen and would matter. Each surviving test should be as short as the thing
it proves.

Stay inside implementation/flows/test. Do not edit tests elsewhere. If a deletion relies on a test outside
implementation/flows/test to keep covering something, name that test in your report.

Work in this order:
1. Run the suite and record the result: tests, assertions, failures, lines. Confirm a
   runner actually executes each file in implementation/flows/test; a file nothing runs cannot be pruned on
   evidence, so report it.
2. Read the code under test and list what it promises its callers: normal results, each
   boundary that takes its own path, each promised failure, and any past bug the tests
   refer to.
3. Map every test to the promise it checks. Most of the work shows up in this map:
   promises with five tests, tests with no promise, and tests of something no caller
   relies on.
4. Decide each test: keep, simplify, merge or delete.
5. Run the suite again and prove the pruned suite still guards every promise.

Work in small batches by contract group, and commit as you go. Before each batch,
predict the change in test and assertion counts; after it, confirm the counts moved by
exactly that much. If helper agents are available, use read-only ones for the mapping
step. If implementation/flows/test plainly will not finish in about four hours, stop at a group boundary,
ship what is done, and list the files you did not reach.

Decide each test with two questions:
- If this test were deleted, what bug could ship that no remaining test would catch?
  If you cannot name one, delete it.
- If you can name one: is that bug plausible in this code, would a caller notice it,
  and would nothing else surface it at once (a compile or load error, a boot-time
  validation, most of the suite going red)? If the bug is implausible, harmless, or
  loud anyway, delete the test.

Delete:
- A test another test implies. If A cannot pass while B fails, drop B.
- Extra examples of one behaviour that take the same path through the code.
- Existence and smoke checks: a function exists, a var resolves, something "is
  registered", a result is non-nil, a call "does not throw", when another test
  exercises the same call with a real assertion.
- Change detectors: a test that copies a constant, a data table, a default config, a
  roster or a string out of the source and asserts equality. It fails on every intended
  change and catches no bug. The exception is a value callers depend on exactly, such as
  a public id or a documented default, that nothing else pins: keep one test for it.
- Absence checks for things nothing produces, and negative-input tests for inputs no
  caller passes and the contract does not mention.
- Exhaustive enumeration: one row per enum member, keyword or field when they all take
  one path. Keep one representative plus the members that take a different path.
- Tests of the language, a library or the framework: a constructor sets a field, a
  getter returns it, a map holds the key just put in it.
- Tests that pin how the code works instead of what it does: private helpers already
  exercised through the public path, call order, internal data shapes, greps of the
  implementation's own source, and log, trace or error wording that is not part of the
  contract.
- Tests whose expected value is computed by the same logic as the code under test.
- Assertions that a mock returned what it was told to return, and tests whose mock setup
  is most of the test while the assertion checks the mock.
- Separate per-platform test files asserting the same thing about platform-neutral code.
  A single shared test that runs on both platforms is one test, not two: keep it.
- Tests of test helpers and fixtures.
- Tests of code that has no logic in it, and tests whose only subject is production code
  that no production caller uses.

Simplify every test you keep:
- Assert the whole result with one equality instead of one assertion per field. Drop an
  assertion that a later one in the same test implies.
- Cut setup, fixtures and data to what the assertion needs. Remove unused bindings,
  requires, helpers and fixtures.
- Tests that vary one input become one table-driven test. Keep the boundary rows and
  drop the mid-range ones.
- Tests that repeat the same setup for one assertion each become one test.
- Delete comments and docstrings that restate the code or narrate history. Keep a
  one-line why where a test's purpose is not obvious from its name and body.
- Rename a test only when its name no longer says what it asserts, and first check that
  nothing matches on the name, such as a CI filter, a skip list or a doc that cites it.

Keep, however small:
- The only test of a promise a caller relies on: a normal result, a boundary that takes
  a different path (empty, one, many; zero; the limit and one past it), a promised
  failure.
- A regression test for a bug that actually happened, unless a stronger test now covers
  it.
- The last guard of a security, privacy or redaction promise.
- The last test that keeps a gate able to fail, and the last test holding a published
  doc or spec claim to the code.
When a weak test and a strong test overlap, keep the strong one: the one that would fail
on more bugs.

Do not:
- Weaken an assertion, or swap an exact check for a looser one, to make a merge or a
  simplification easier.
- Delete a test because it fails, is slow or is flaky. Report it.
- Leave unused helpers, fixtures or requires behind.
- Add new tests. If you find a promise with no test, report it.
- Change production code. Dead code and stale docs or spec text go in your report as a
  list, not into your change.
If anything pins test counts or names, such as a count floor or a roster, update it in
the same change. Commit one file or module at a time.

Prove it:
- The suite passes before and after. Report both sets of counts.
- For each group of deletions that rests on a surviving cover, break the code in a place
  the deleted tests guarded and confirm a surviving test fails. Then restore the code and
  confirm it matches the committed file. One plant per group sharing a cover is enough.
  If nothing fails, you removed real coverage: put the tests back.
- A cover must actually run. A skipped test, a fixture the runner never loads, or a test
  on a lane nothing executes covers nothing. Confirm the runner executes a cover before
  resting a deletion on it.
- Run each test file you touched on its own at least once. Deleting a file can break a
  sibling that relied on it loading something first; give such a file its own require.
- A deletion made under the second question needs no plant. Give its one-line reason in
  the report instead.
- A simplification must not change what a test can catch. Where you removed an
  assertion, name the assertion that implies it.

Report:
- Before and after: tests, assertions, lines.
- Deleted tests, grouped by reason. For each, the surviving cover, or the one-line
  reason it was not worth keeping.
- Merges and simplifications: what went into what, and the lines each file lost.
- Notable keeps: tests you considered deleting but kept, and why.
- Plants, and which test caught each.
- Tests outside implementation/flows/test that your deletions rely on.
- Dead code, stale docs or spec text, and gaps (promises with no test). One line each.

If you are unsure whether a promise a caller relies on is still covered, keep the test
and say so. Losing the only guard of a real promise is still the one mistake that matters
more than leaving an extra test in. But being unsure whether a test is worth keeping is
not a reason to keep it. If you cannot say in one line what plausible regression it
catches that a caller would notice, delete it.

title: Spec names three slots for :rf.runtime/resources, but the GC window fix adds :last-gc-window
description:
The fix for rf2-21u8l adds a fourth slot to the resources runtime-db child: `[:rf.runtime/resources :last-gc-window]`, an int holding the id of the last GC window the frame opened. `open-gc-window` in implementation/resources/src/re_frame/resources/events.cljc draws every entry's `:gc-window` from it, so window ids are unique across entry lifetimes and a removed entry's queued GC check can never match its replacement.

Three spec surfaces still describe the child as having exactly three slots:
- spec/Conventions.md §Reserved runtime-db keys, the `:rf.runtime/resources` row: "closed slot set `:entries` / `:tag-index` / `:owner-index`" (hot zone).
- spec/016-Resources.md §Cache home and write authority: the frame-state shape block and the Runtime Subsystem adherence table row "1 Subtree", which says "closed slot set".
- spec/Spec-Schemas.md `ResourcesRuntime` (hot zone): an open map listing the three slots; it does not reject the fourth, but does not name it.

What the slot is, for the spec text: client-only (a server frame opens no GC window, so it never gets one); never on the SSR wire (the hydration projection carries only `:entries`); it rides epoch snapshots like the rest of runtime-db, so replay reproduces it; it is not recomputable from `:entries`, unlike the two indexes.

title: Delete epoch listener silencing: drop the :rf.epoch.cb/silenced-on-frame-destroy trace, epoch-silence-current? and the generation ledger with its two locks
description:
## Ruling

Delete epoch's listener-silencing mechanism outright. The `:rf.epoch.cb/silenced-on-frame-destroy` trace op goes. So does the public receiver predicate `epoch-silence-current?` (on `re-frame.epoch`, its `re-frame.core` re-export and its `:epoch/epoch-silence-current?` late-bind hook). Also deleted: the callback-generation tokens and observation ledger, the terminal-silence marks with their monotonic sequence and ABA baseline, the outstanding-lineage brackets, the reservation-and-rollback out-of-lock emission, and both monitors that exist for them (`listener-registry-lock` and `silence-lock`). The epoch listener registry becomes a plain `{id -> f}` map. A tool that wants to forget a frame listens for `:rf.frame/destroyed`, which already states the fact.

Kept: process-global registration, replace-by-id, exception isolation with `:rf.epoch.cb/listener-exception`, and terminal `:halted-destroy` record delivery. Core's pre-dissoc `:epoch/snapshot-frame-destroyed` hook (step 7a of `destroy-frame!`) also stays, slimmed so that it binds only the interrupted event's `:halted-destroy` record. That record is real evidence, and deleting silencing does not justify deleting it.

Decided 2026-10-16: Mike directed that every dossier recommendation an independent Codex review agreed with be actioned:

> review all decisions. They now have a "Codex Recomendation" section.  Where the original recomendation matches the Code Recomendation, create a bead to action the decision.  And then remove the file.  Leave behind cases where the two differ materially.

Both recommendations said "D5: yes, now", with the same scope: the whole capability, keeping the terminal snapshot and listener-exception.

**Decisive facts (at trunk 89517e8f54):**

1. **Nothing consumes it.** A tree-wide search for `silenced-on-frame-destroy|epoch-silence-current?` finds no source file under `tools/`, `skills/`, `examples/` or `testbeds/`. The hits are confined to `implementation/`, `spec/`, `docs/api/` and one paragraph of Xray spec. That paragraph, `tools/xray/spec/011-Launch-Modes.md:1105-1108` at trunk 89517e8f54, says Xray "MAY surface this trace in the event log ... but MUST NOT take any additional action on it".
2. **The fact is already on the bus.** `implementation/core/src/re_frame/frame.cljc:4300-4303` at trunk 89517e8f54 (`emit-frame-destroyed-trace!`) emits `:rf.frame/destroyed {:frame id}`. A destroyed frame produces no more records, so every callback that was watching it has gone quiet by definition.
3. **The cost is out of proportion, and the spec has already drifted.** The mechanism is about 850 source lines: `implementation/epoch/src/re_frame/epoch/state.cljc:1122-1853` at trunk 89517e8f54 (the two monitors are at :1332 and :1335) plus `listeners.cljc:303-533`. It also has eight dedicated test files and roughly 2,900 spec words, including 009's "delayed-silence emission linearization law". `spec/Spec-Schemas.md:2121-2122` at trunk 89517e8f54 names a receiver half, `re-frame.epoch/epoch-listener-observing?`, that does not exist.

**Rejected options:**

- **Keep it.** It keeps about 850 lines and a linearizability proof, an already-drifted spec, and a public predicate, all to serve a race no tool has asked to win and a fact `:rf.frame/destroyed` already states.
- **Delete it, and add an opaque incarnation id to `:rf.frame/destroyed` and to records.** No consumer needs one. The `:drain-lock` token is an atom and not EDN, so this would need a new serialisable id. File it as follow-up only if a consumer appears.

**Supersedes:**

- the "listener silencing" row of `spec/Tool-Pair.md` §Surface behaviour against destroyed frames (:311, and its receiver passage through :342);
- `spec/009-Instrumentation.md` §The delayed-silence emission linearization law (:339-368).

It also removes one name, `epoch-silence-current?`, from the facade-door list recorded in ruling rf2-kuky.55, and does not otherwise touch that ruling. No EP covers silencing.

**Not decided here.** The same dossier's incarnation-keyed storage question is still open for Mike, because the two recommendations differ. That question would key epoch's stores by frame incarnation and delete the owner ledger, `frame-owner-lock` and core's pre-dissoc hook. So do NOT touch the owner ledger (`state.cljc:1855-1974`), `frame-owner-lock`, the `continue?` liveness threading, or restore's host-tail token.

## Work

**Delete (source):**

- `implementation/epoch/src/re_frame/epoch/state.cljc`:
  - generation tokens and observation stamps (:1122-1168);
  - terminal-silence marks, the silence sequence and the ABA baseline (:1170-1271);
  - `listener-registry-lock`, `silence-lock` and the claim-lock nesting (:1273-1355);
  - the lineage brackets `open-silence-lineage!` / `close-silence-lineage!` (:1357-1411);
  - `silence-current?` (:1439);
  - the reservation/rollback emission path (:1485-1634);
  - the re-arm and wipe machinery through :1853.

  The listener registry becomes a plain atom of `{id -> f}`. Registration still returns `id`, and re-registering an id still replaces.
- `implementation/epoch/src/re_frame/epoch/listeners.cljc`:
  - Delete the silence emit loop (around :505-533, including the emit at :525-529).
  - In `snapshot-terminal-destroy-evidence!` (:303-375), drop `:silenced-cbs`, `:baseline-silence-seq` and the lineage window. It keeps the `:halted-destroy` `:record`, and the listener set that record fans to if that is still needed for terminal delivery.
  - `on-frame-destroyed!` keeps publishing that record and dropping the frame's stores.
- `implementation/epoch/src/re_frame/epoch.cljc`: delete `epoch-silence-current?` (:193-231), its hook publication (:882-886) and the ns-doc mention (:67).
- `implementation/epoch/src/re_frame/epoch/capture.cljc:40,70`: drop the op from capture's op lists.
- `implementation/core/src/re_frame/core_epoch.cljc:107-127`: delete the `defwrapper`.
- `implementation/core/src/re_frame/core.cljc:2569-2594`: delete the re-export and its docstring.
- `implementation/core/src/re_frame/late_bind/directory.cljc:665-667`: delete the `:epoch/epoch-silence-current?` entry.
- `implementation/core/src/re_frame/frame.cljc:4512`: delete the step-10 docstring mention.
- `implementation/scripts/check-elision.cjs:289-297`: delete the op's sentinel.
- `implementation/core/test/re_frame/elision_probe.cljs:250`: delete the reference.

**Delete (tests):**

- The eight dedicated files in `implementation/epoch/test/re_frame/`:
  - `epoch_silence_contract_test.clj`
  - `epoch_silence_decision_atomicity_test.clj`
  - `epoch_silence_receiver_public_api_test.clj`
  - `epoch_silencing_emit_deadlock_test.clj`
  - `epoch_silencing_generation_emission_test.clj`
  - `epoch_silencing_lineage_285_test.clj`
  - `epoch_silencing_lineage_aba_test.clj`
  - `epoch_silencing_same_generation_rearm_test.clj`
- The silencing deftests and assertions inside `epoch_test.clj`, `epoch_concurrency_stress_test.clj` and `implementation/core/test/re_frame/frame_destroy_incarnation_jvm_test.clj`. Keep their non-silencing coverage: incarnation fencing, terminal-record delivery and depth retention.
- Any test-runner roster entry that names a deleted namespace.

**Spec and docs:**

- `spec/Tool-Pair.md`:
  - Replace the listener-silencing row (:311) and its receiver passage through :342 with one sentence: a callback whose frame is destroyed simply receives no more records for it, a tool that wants to forget a frame listens for `:rf.frame/destroyed`, and a late `:halted-destroy` record is history (keep the existing late-record rule).
  - Also update the mention at :728.
- `spec/009-Instrumentation.md`:
  - :161, the family row (`:rf.epoch.cb` now carries only `listener-exception`);
  - :210, the op row;
  - :339-368, the op paragraph and the whole linearization-law section;
  - :1067, the emitter mention.
- `spec/API.md`:
  - Delete the `epoch-silence-current?` row (:691) and the trace-tags row (:715).
  - Trim the silencing sentences from the epoch-listener paragraph (:695).
  - Hand-edit `spec/api-manifest-metadata.edn`, then regenerate `spec/api-manifest.edn` with `generate!` in `implementation/scripts/api-manifest`. Never hand-edit the generated file.
- `spec/Spec-Schemas.md:2083-2130`: delete the silence tags schema. This also removes the drifted `epoch-listener-observing?` reference.
- `spec/Conventions.md:86`: `:rf.epoch.cb/*` becomes a closed reserved set of one member, `:rf.epoch.cb/listener-exception`.
- `spec/002-Frames.md:778-809`: step 10 becomes "publish the terminal `:halted-destroy` record, if any, and drop the frame's epoch stores". Step 7a stays, now described as binding only that record.
- `tools/xray/spec/011-Launch-Modes.md:1097-1111`: drop the silencing sentences, and keep the `:rf.xray/epoch-history` last-cached-vector rule.
- `docs/api/re-frame.core.md` and `docs/api/re-frame.epoch.md`: remove the entries. Regenerate them if they are generated.

**Deliberately stays:**

- process-global registration and replace-by-id;
- exception isolation and `:rf.epoch.cb/listener-exception`, pinned by `epoch_test.clj:203-221`;
- terminal `:halted-destroy` delivery;
- core's `:epoch/snapshot-frame-destroyed` step-7a hook, slimmed;
- the owner ledger, `frame-owner-lock` and restore's host-tail token;
- the retention lock (`state.cljc:96-101`).

## Sequencing

- **Hot zones:** `spec/Tool-Pair.md`, `spec/009-Instrumentation.md`, `spec/API.md` with both api-manifest sidecars (one holding), `spec/Spec-Schemas.md`, `spec/Conventions.md` and `spec/002-Frames.md`. Run it sequentially with any other bead touching these. It does not touch `spec/011-SSR.md` (the one i/crlf file), `.github/workflows/*`, `implementation/deps.edn`, `implementation/shadow-cljs.edn`, or the changed-surfaces classifier pair.
- **Depends on:** no bead.
- **Within this dossier:** this bead goes first. The write-result envelope bead, filed alongside, depends on it for hot-zone ordering only.
- **Cross-dossier:**
  - Precedes the epoch-monitor step of `jvm-one-writer-per-frame.md`, whose action "Epoch: after the silencing and storage sibling lands" collapses epoch's monitors. This bead removes two of the four. The storage half (`frame-owner-lock`) is still open in `epoch-listener-silencing-and-incarnation-storage.md`.
  - If Mike rules the incarnation-keyed storage question yes, that work follows this bead.
  - `observability-listener-scheduler-and-fan-outs.md` defers the `:epoch` stream's delivery to this work. Hot zones aside, there is no ordering constraint.

## Evidence

**Read in source at trunk 89517e8f54:**

- the consumer census: a tree-wide search for both names hits 32 files, none of them a source file under `tools/`, `skills/`, `examples/` or `testbeds/`;
- the emit at `listeners.cljc:525-529`;
- `epoch-silence-current?` at `epoch.cljc:193`, and its re-export and hook at `core_epoch.cljc:107-127`, `core.cljc:2594` and `directory.cljc:665`;
- the two locks at `state.cljc:1332` and `:1335`;
- the `:rf.frame/destroyed` emit at `frame.cljc:4300-4303`;
- the Xray MUST NOT clause;
- the `check-elision.cjs` sentinel;
- the eight test file names;
- the terminal snapshot's `:silenced-cbs` and `:baseline-silence-seq` fields at `listeners.cljc:303-375`.

The line and word counts (about 850 source lines and about 2,900 spec words) are estimates from the review, not re-measured.

**Still needs a run** (nothing has been run):

- the JVM epoch and core suites;
- `npm run test:cljs`, because epoch's `.cljc` files have `:cljs` branches that the JVM never compiles;
- the elision gate;
- the api-manifest lint;
- `mkdocs build --strict` and `scripts/check_doc_slugs.py`, which catch dangling anchors to `#the-delayed-silence-emission-linearization-law` from other pages.

title: Make an error tap own only the records it claims, so a typo'd :initial-events step prints its :rf.error/no-such-handler line in an untooled dev build
description:
## The defect this bead fixes (the acceptance case)

**A typo'd `:initial-events` step prints nothing in an untooled dev build.** With no `:errors` sink declared and no Xray or other trace tooling attached:

```clojure
(rf/make-frame {:id :app :initial-events [[:app/initalise]]})   ;; typo: no handler registered
```

The frame comes up unseeded, and nothing reaches the console: no `[re-frame2] :rf.error/no-such-handler ...` line, and no setup-step failure either. The chain, read in source at trunk 89517e8f54 but not yet run:

1. The setup step registers a temporary error tap for its `dispatch-sync!` (`implementation/core/src/re_frame/frame.cljc:2894-2899`). The tap captures only the four pre-commit categories in `setup-step-failure-categories` (`frame.cljc:2700`), and only on its own frame.
2. No handler is found, so `router/diagnostics.cljc:66-108` fans out `:rf.error/no-such-handler` through `emit-error-both!`, then `dispatch-on-error!`.
3. The tap ignores the record, because that category is not one of its four. No sink routes it, so `routed` is 0.
4. `report-unowned-error!` prints only when `(empty? @listeners)` (`implementation/core/src/re_frame/error_emit.cljc:326`). That is false while the step's tap is registered, so nothing prints.
5. `dispatch-sync!` returns normally, and nothing was captured, so no setup failure is raised (`frame.cljc:2921`).

The same mechanism also hides two other cases:
- a post-commit `:rf.error/fx-handler-exception` in a setup step, which is deliberately not captured;
- every error during an `:on-destroy` window other than that frame's own handler exception (`frame.cljc:4051-4055`).

## Ruling

Keep the implementation-tier taps: the `re-frame.error-emit` and `re-frame.event-emit` registries stay. They are neither retired nor merged into the frame-owned `:observability` sink route.

Replace arm (a) of the dev console fallback. Today it reads "any registered error tap owns every record, corpus-wide". The new rule is **a tap owns only the records it claims**:
- A tap claims a record by returning an explicit acknowledgement.
- The fan-out aggregates the acknowledgements over the snapshot it actually delivered to.
- A tap that returns no acknowledgement, or throws, does not own the record.
- Sinks keep arm (b) unchanged: a registered sink that was invoked owns the record, even if it throws.

The fallback then prints iff no tap claimed the record and no sink was invoked. This adds no knob: it restores the fallback's own promise. Also rewrite the stale comments that still describe the tap as the production stream.

Decided 2026-10-16: Mike directed that every dossier recommendation an independent Codex review agreed with be actioned. His instruction, verbatim:

> review all decisions. They now have a "Codex Recomendation" section.  Where the original
> recomendation matches the Code Recomendation, create a bead to action the decision.  And then
> remove the file.  Leave behind cases where the two differ materially.

The original dossier and the Codex review agreed on this. Codex added that the acknowledgement must be explicit rather than the incidental return value of `reset!` or `swap!`, and this bead adopts that.

Decisive facts, at trunk 89517e8f54:
1. **The defect above.** The setup tap's four-category filter (`frame.cljc:2700`, `:2894-2899`) combines with the fallback's registry-emptiness test (`error_emit.cljc:326`) to silence a record nobody reads.
2. **EP-0027 promises the opposite.** "A step whose event has **no registered handler** is not a setup-step failure: it reports `:rf.error/no-such-handler`, exactly as any dispatch does, and construction continues" (`docs/EP/EP-0027-frame-initial-events.md:172-174`). Spec 009's console fallback uses a typo'd event id as its own example (`spec/009-Instrumentation.md:1291`).
3. **Tap return values are ignored today.** The `register-error-listener!` docstring says "its return value is ignored" (`error_emit.cljc:86-89`), and the substrate fan-out returns nil (`implementation/core/src/re_frame/emit_substrate.cljc:49-63`). So the claim has to be built as a deliberate, documented protocol.

Rejected options:
- **Leave as is.** The setup-step silence stays.
- **Add `:rf.error/no-such-handler` to `setup-step-failure-categories`.** It fixes only the headline case, and it turns a handler-less step into a construction failure, which EP-0027:172-174 forbids.
- **Read ownership off the existing incidental truthy returns of `reset!`/`swap!`, with no call-site change.** That is a silent trap for programmers and AI edits: a refactor of a tap's last form changes who owns the console.
- **Retire both registries and capture through a dynamic extent (Opus action 2).**
  - It reverses rf2-kuky.22 and rf2-kuky.69 ("not deleted; not merged") without engaging their reasons.
  - Capture must ignore frame sink policy.
  - The mounted test tier's capture stays open across turns until `:stop!` (`implementation/fresco/test_kit/src/re_frame/fresco/test/mounted.cljs:2249-2273`), which a CLJS dynamic binding cannot follow.
- **Fold the two producers into one constructor (F2).** This is deferred, not rejected. Take it the next time the event-tap and handled-event record constructors drift. It is not filed.

This supersedes the arm (a) half of rf2-kuky.18's two-arm console ownership, as restated by rf2-b6g2u ("a listener registration means somebody is watching"). It does NOT supersede rf2-kuky.22 or rf2-kuky.69: the taps stay `^:no-doc` implementation registries, raw and policy-independent, beside the projected sinks.

## Work

Code:
- **The substrate fan-out** (`emit_substrate.cljc:49-63`): make it report whether any tap in the snapshot it delivered to acknowledged the record. A throwing tap acknowledges nothing. Event-emit callers ignore the result.
- **`fan-out!`** (`error_emit.cljc:101-122`): return that result.
- **`dispatch-on-error!`** (`:545`): hand that result to `report-unowned-error!` (`:296-344`), and replace the `(empty? @listeners)` read at `:326`. The fallback prints iff no tap claimed the record and `routed` is zero.
- **`register-error-listener!` docstring** (`:86-89`): state the claim rule.
- **The claim protocol**: an explicit acknowledgement.
  - Prefer a literal `true`, read with `true?`, so that an incidental `swap!`/`reset!` value never claims by accident.
  - About 108 test-path files register error taps. If the strict form turns them into console noise beyond what the quiet node runner buffers on a green run, a truthy rule is acceptable, provided the framework sites still return an explicit `true`. Say in the PR which form you chose.
- **Make each in-tree error tap return the acknowledgement explicitly in its claiming branch:**
  - the setup step, `frame.cljc:2894-2899`;
  - `:on-destroy`, `frame.cljc:4051-4055`, inside `fire-on-destroy-event!` at `:3980`;
  - the Fresco server tap, `implementation/fresco/src/re_frame/fresco/server.cljs:295-308`. It claims every record, since it re-raises what it saw. Also rewrite its docstring, which says that registering any listener "takes corpus-wide ownership";
  - the errors arm of `with-emit-recorder!`, `implementation/core/src/re_frame/test_support.cljc:1330-1384`. It claims exactly when the caller's predicate matched.
- **Present-tense cleanup.** `error_emit.cljc:553-554`, `:811-813` and `:825` still call the tap "the off-box observability stream (Sentry / Datadog / Xray / the SSR error-projection listener)" and "the off-box-shipper + SSR-error-projector source of truth". Both have been false since the sinks became the production door and SSR moved to late-bind hooks. Describe the registry as what it is: an implementation-tier capture registry.

Spec:
- `spec/009-Instrumentation.md:1291`: rewrite arm (a). The clause "a registered sink that THROWS does own it, exactly as a throwing listener does" becomes: a throwing sink owns the record; a throwing or non-claiming tap does not.
- `:1238`: check the tier wording against the new rule.

Tests:
- Add a failing-first test for the defect above. It must be red at the base commit.
- Restate `implementation/core/test/re_frame/error_emit_dev_console_dom_cljs_test.cljs:200`, `ownership-is-implicit-and-corpus-wide`. It currently asserts that a THROWING tap silences the fallback; it now asserts the opposite.
- `:210` (`dropping-the-last-listener-resumes-the-fallback`) and `:268` (`a-throwing-registered-sink-still-owns-the-record`) keep their intent.

Deliberately stays:
- both registries and their implementation-tier verbs, with no public verb;
- the sink ownership rule;
- `setup-step-failure-categories` exactly as it is, so `no-such-handler` stays non-fatal per EP-0027;
- the SSR `:ssr/capture-error-record` late-bind hook, which owns nothing.

## Sequencing

- **Hot zone**: `spec/009-Instrumentation.md`, and no other.
- **Within this dossier**: this is the first of three chained beads, followed by the handled-event vocabulary bead and then the FIFO listener-delivery bead. All three edit Spec 009, so they run one after another, never in parallel. This bead depends on no other bead.
- **Cross-dossier**:
  - `jvm-one-writer-per-frame.md`: its core work deletes the fan-out's `continue?` argument in `emit_substrate.cljc:49-61`, which this bead also edits. Sequence the two, never in parallel. Either order works; the later one rebases onto the other's shape.
  - `ssr-mismatch-detection-hash-channels.md`: its work fans a new always-on record through `error_emit.cljc:1056-1084`, so it edits the same file. Sequence the two. Under this bead's rule, that record prints in dev unless a sink or a claiming tap owns it.
  - rf2-vvtyg, from the dispatch-sync exception-boundary dossier, links to 009:1291 and says its phrasing holds under either ownership rule. No ordering is needed.
- `spec/011-SSR.md`, the one i/crlf file, is not touched.

## Evidence

- **Read in source at trunk 89517e8f54:**
  - `frame.cljc:2700`, `:2894-2921`, `:3980`, `:4051-4055`;
  - `error_emit.cljc:86-89`, `:101-122`, `:296-344`, `:545-560`, `:805-830`;
  - `emit_substrate.cljc:20-63`;
  - `test_support.cljc:1330-1384`;
  - `fresco/server.cljs:295-308`;
  - `docs/EP/EP-0027-frame-initial-events.md:165-186`;
  - `spec/009-Instrumentation.md:1291`;
  - `error_emit_dev_console_dom_cljs_test.cljs:200-210`.
- **Needs a run:** the defect itself. The dossier and the Codex review both reached it by reading, and neither ran it. The failing-first test is that run. **If the defect DOES print at base, stop and report**: the reading is wrong, and this bead loses its motivating case.
- The Codex review executed no tests or gates.
acceptance_criteria:

A failing-first test sets up a dev build with no :errors sink and no trace tooling, and calls (rf/make-frame {:id <f> :initial-events [[<unregistered-event-id>]]}). It asserts exactly one "[re-frame2] :rf.error/no-such-handler ..." console line. The test is red at the base commit and green with the fix. If it is green at base, stop and report instead.

title: Keep snapshot core trace reads usable when the Epoch artefact is absent
description: PR #11362 projects every nonempty snapshot :traces bundle by manufacturing :kind :rf/epoch-record and calling project-egress. That kind requires the optional :epoch/project-record hook. A focused JVM probe against exact merged SHA 5a8e5613719626d88d197f161f8b0c487622bfb3, using the actual new renderer, shows a valid live frame and one core trace bundle now throw :rf.error/epoch-artefact-missing without re-frame.epoch loaded; requiring Epoch makes the identical ordinary-frame control succeed and redact its secret. The Pair preload itself does not require Epoch. Its snapshot-frame-slice at skills/re-frame2-pair/preload/re_frame2_pair/runtime.cljs:3573-3579 reads epochs and core traces independently; snapshot includes both by default. Core register-listener! :epoch deliberately returns nil without Epoch, and skills/re-frame2-pair/references/setup.md:51 documents core-only apps passing discover-app with epoch reads empty. Consequently even a general default snapshot now fails as soon as an otherwise supported core-only app has a trace, because the new traces arm requires an optional artefact; unrelated slices cannot be read in that request. Probe evidence is in ai/pr-audit/11362-behavior-probe.clj and .log in the audit worktree (exit 0). Small correction: handle absent epoch projection capability explicitly and fail closed on only the unavailable trace payload, preserving useful other snapshot slices, or provide the equivalent canonical safe trace projection without imposing Epoch. Keep the off-box privacy floor. Acceptance: a core-only app with a nonempty trace ring can obtain a safe default snapshot, and Epoch-enabled snapshots still use the real projector.
notes:

title: State the rf/ facade rule by role and move the epoch, resource-state and mutation-state surfaces to their feature namespaces
description:
## Ruling

State the `re-frame.core` facade rule by ROLE, so a reader or a model can apply it without a list of exceptions: **what app code authors is on `rf/`; what you use to inspect, replay or tool lives in the feature's own namespace.**

- `rf/` carries the registration macros (all of them, including the optional features' `reg-*`), dispatch and subscribe, the frame basics, and the feature pieces written inside handlers and views — so `route-link` (a view component) and `resolve-resource-scope` (called from a logout handler) stay.
- Feature namespaces carry inspection, history and tooling: the five epoch surfaces move to `re-frame.epoch`, and `resource-state` and `mutation-state` move to `re-frame.resources`.
- The registration macros stay on `rf/` (core-public-api Q3): authoring stays a single import, and the macros carry production provenance through `defreg-macro` (`implementation/core/src/re_frame/core_reg_macros.cljc:249-265`).

Decided 2026-10-16: Mike directed that every dossier recommendation an independent Codex review agreed with be actioned. Mike's instruction, verbatim:

> review all decisions. They now have a "Codex Recomendation" section.  Where the original
> recomendation matches the Code Recomendation, create a bead to action the decision.  And then
> remove the file.  Leave behind cases where the two differ materially.

title: Spec: destroy a frame at the next event boundary, and narrow the JVM contract to one lifecycle writer per frame id
description:
## Ruling

A `destroy-frame!` issued while the target frame's drain is on the current stack becomes a **pending destroy**. The call claims the exact incarnation and takes the per-id reservation at once, then returns. The current event completes normally, and teardown runs at the next event boundary. This covers the frame's own handler and also another frame's handler reached through a nested cross-frame `dispatch-sync`. A self-destroying handler's `:db` and `:fx` therefore land, including a dispatch to another, live frame. Everything still queued behind that event is dropped at the boundary and counted, including the destroying event's own descendants. `:on-destroy` runs once, after the event, against the committed db. The reservation is held until teardown and its terminal publication have finished, so no same-id successor can coexist with any part of the dying incarnation.

On the JVM the contract narrows to **one lifecycle writer per frame id**. Any thread may dispatch to, subscribe to, or read a frame, and the runtime still serialises the frame's drain. Lifecycle writes against one id (`make-frame`, `destroy-frame!`, and the dev-time tool writes `restore-epoch!` / `replace-frame-state!`) are ordered by their caller. Overlapping same-id lifecycle writes from different threads are unsupported. The reservation still turns the common overlap into `:rf.error/frame-construction-in-progress`, and nothing further is promised. Concurrent frames on different ids stay fully supported. "One lifecycle writer" means callers order lifecycle operations; it does not mean one physical thread, nor one writer to every runtime store.

This is option C of the frame-lifetime decision. It also answers core-event-pipeline open question 1: a self-destroying handler's effects land, and its descendants are dropped at the event boundary, not at the family boundary.

This bead is the spec half. It goes first, and the core, reservation and Xray beads implement it.

Decided 2026-10-16: Mike directed that every dossier recommendation an independent Codex review agreed with be actioned. Mike's instruction, verbatim:

> review all decisions. They now have a "Codex Recomendation" section.  Where the original recomendation matches the Code Recomendation, create a bead to action the decision.  And then remove the file.  Leave behind cases where the two differ materially.

The ruling folds in one correction from the independent review. The first draft said the reservation is released "when `destroy-frame!` returns". A pending destroy returns before its teardown runs, so the reservation must instead pass to the pending destroy and be released only after teardown and terminal publication finish, including on exceptional exits.

Decisive facts, read in source at trunk 89517e8f54:

1. **Today's contract is an immediate cutoff, and it is paid for with a fence at every pipeline hop.** Spec 002 says that after the claim "the returned context/output is inert ... no commit, flow, effect, child dispatch, ordinary diagnostic/trailer, normal epoch settlement, or render may follow" (`spec/002-Frames.md:738-745`, restated at Two halts `:1830-1836` and edge case 4 `:2348-2361`). In code, one `dispatch-sync` of a one-line handler resolves the frame registry 124 times, and 105 of those resolutions come from `event-continuation-live?`, "consulted from TWENTY distinct sites in one pipeline run" (`implementation/core/src/re_frame/frame.cljc:1331-1362`). `router.cljc` alone carries 54 `::stale-incarnation` sentinels.
2. **A same-id successor can appear mid-event only on the JVM, and only one way.** Same-thread re-entry is refused by `*handler-scope*` (`frame.cljc:3459-3472`), and a cross-thread destroy already waits out the whole drain through `call-serialized-with-drain!`. What remains is a handler on thread T1 destroying its own frame. Teardown releases the reservation at the registry dissoc, "so the post-dissoc window may seat a fresh same-id incarnation" (`frame.cljc:4864-4870`; spec `002:731`, `:754`), and thread T2 constructs the same id while T1's handler is still on the stack.
3. **The only production JVM consumer already behaves as one lifecycle writer.** `ssr-ring` mints a gensym frame id per request (`implementation/ssr-ring/src/re_frame/ssr/ring/pipeline.clj:306`), constructs and destroys it on the request thread, and destroys it by frame value (`implementation/ssr-ring/src/re_frame/ssr/ring/lifecycle.clj:97`). Ordinary dispatch stays genuinely multi-threaded: `next-tick` drains on a single-thread executor and timers run on a scheduled executor, both under `bound-fn` (`implementation/core/src/re_frame/interop.clj:15-33`, `:164-171`). That is why the drain lock and the enqueue-time token compares stay.

Rejected options:
- **A, keep both promises.** A self-destroying handler silently loses all its effects, including a dispatch to another live frame, and every future pipeline stage must remember its fence.
- **B, boundary destruction with full JVM linearizability kept.** This keeps the post-dissoc window, the destroy-claim retry and the cross-thread barrier suites, all of which defend same-id lifecycle races that no caller in the repo creates.
- **D, thread confinement (a per-frame serial executor).** It collides with `dispatch-sync`'s run-on-caller semantics and with request-thread SSR rendering. That is over-engineering; add no executor and no general lifecycle scheduler.
- **Letting the destroying event's whole family finish.** That runs more handlers in a frame that has been asked to die. Cleanup belongs in `:on-destroy`.

Supersedes: Spec 002's immediate-cutoff contract (§Destroy `:738-745`, Two halts `:1830-1836`, edge case 4 `:2348-2361`), its "post-dissoc window" and "supported successor window" (`:731`, `:754`), and "a competing JVM thread fails immediately" as a promise (`:641`). No EP or ruling bead is overturned.

**Not decided by this ruling, and not to be decided by this bead.** Both questions remain open for Mike in the dossier `jvm-one-writer-per-frame.md`:

**`spec/002-Frames.md`**
- **§Destroy (`:727-797`).**
  - Define the pending destroy. When the target's drain is on the current stack, `destroy-frame!` claims the exact incarnation and takes the per-id reservation, then returns. The event completes: commit, flows, effects and trailers run, and its epoch settles `:ok`. Teardown steps 1-10 run at the next event boundary. Otherwise teardown is immediate, as today.

  - Replace the inert-tail paragraph at `:738-745`.
- **Step 1 (`:748-756`) and `:731`.** The reservation passes to the pending destroy (or is held by the immediate one) and is released only after step 10's terminal publication, including on an exceptional exit. Delete the post-dissoc and successor-window language.
- **Step 2.** `:on-destroy` runs once, after the destroying event, and sees the committed db.
- **Two halts (`:1830-1836`), the halt-boundary paragraph (`:1866`) and edge case 4 (`:2348-2361`).** The destroy halt becomes an event-boundary halt, parallel to the depth halt.   > **JVM threading — one lifecycle writer per frame.** Any thread may dispatch to, subscribe to, or read a frame; the runtime serialises its drain, so work from the executor, timers and async replies is safe. Lifecycle writes against one frame id — `make-frame`, `destroy-frame!`, and the dev-time tool writes `restore-epoch!` / `replace-frame-state!` — are ordered by their caller. A per-request SSR frame satisfies this by construction. Overlapping same-id lifecycle writes from different threads are unsupported: the per-id reservation still turns the common overlap into `:rf.error/frame-construction-in-progress`, and nothing further is promised.

- **Late-predecessor ordering (`:366`).** No same-id successor can be constructed until the predecessor's terminal publication has finished, so the text describing a successor seated before it goes. Do not touch `:368` or the rest of the law (see Ruling).

**`spec/Tool-Pair.md`**
- **The late-record consumer rule (`:340`).** A destroyed incarnation's terminal record can no longer arrive after a same-id successor has begun recording. Shrink the rule to match, and leave the rest of §Silencing under same-id frame churn.

**`spec/Spec-Schemas.md`**
- **The `:halted-destroy` row (`:4500`) and the enum comment (`:4413`).** Redefine them to match 009.

**`spec/Runtime-Architecture.md`**
- **§Run-to-completion guarantee (`:163`).** The destroy boundary is the event boundary.

- the enqueue-time token compares for captured async work (a stale timer or reply for A can fire after B exists, even sequentially on ClojureScript);
