title: skill(re-frame-migration): inventory Step 2 loaded require-graph walk names no tool
description:
Filed from a downstream v1 -> re-frame2 migration's skills retrospective (suggestion, not a work order). Verified at origin/main 2a6fd908a6. Minor.

## Skill file and section

skills/re-frame-migration/references/inventory-and-plan.md, Step 2's first bullet "Blast radius — scope to the LOADED require-graph subset" (line 53), and the leaf's opening paragraph (line 3).

## What it says

- Line 53: "grep the **app's** source for its `require`s of the dependency and walk the reachable graph from those entry points into the dependency — **that loaded subset is the blast radius.**"
- Line 3: Phase 0a "is read-only: it reads the dependency tree and source and searches with `rg`, and it rewrites nothing and builds nothing."

## What happened (generic)

The walk is a transitive closure over `ns` forms across app and dependency sources. Done by hand with `rg` it is slow and easy to get wrong: reader conditionals, `:require-macros`, string requires and aliases all get in the way. The worker on a ~170-file app had to build its own walker. "Builds nothing" also rules out the cheapest source of truth: the unmodified v1 build's own list of the namespaces it compiles.

## Evidence

- `git grep -n -i -E 'build-report|build report|manifest\.edn|reachable graph|require graph|loaded subset|walk the reachable' origin/main -- skills/re-frame-migration/` finds only the prose at inventory-and-plan.md:7 and :53, plus an unrelated `spec/api-manifest.edn` mention.
- No script ships with the skill: `git ls-tree -r origin/main skills/re-frame-migration` lists only .md and .json files and the LICENSE.

## Suggested change

Do one of these:

- Ship a small script that walks the require graph from each build's entry namespaces over the classpath sources. It should read `ns` forms only, handle `:require`, `:require-macros`, `:use` and reader conditionals, and print the loaded namespaces for each dependency.
- Allow the pre-migration build's own namespace list as a read-only Phase 0a input. A shadow-cljs build report of the unmodified v1 build would do, because the v1 tree still compiles before M-0.

title: senior review: story: UI and theme
description:
SENIOR-DEVELOPER REVIEW of one slice of the tree. Part of the review sweep rf2-r5cc2, which partitions implementation/, tools/, examples/ and skills/ into slices; this bead owns exactly the slice below, and its siblings own the rest.

SLICE:
- tools/story/src/**/ui/**, tools/story/src/**/theme/**
- tools/story/test/story/ui/**, tools/story/test/story/panels_e2e/**

FOCUS: Story's workspace UI, panels and theme as a user and as a maintainer meet them.

PERSONA. A senior Clojure/ClojureScript developer who did not write this code, reading it as its next maintainer and as a programmer who has to use it. Judge it against the project stance (CLAUDE.md), quoted verbatim:

> Posture is that we are pre-alpha and focused on elegance, power and a masterpiece.
> But we are not over-engineering or gold plating. Also, we trust the programmer.
> We're trying to facilitate high productivity for them (and the AI they use) via a
> library with excellent ergonomics and low friction. We don't need to litigate every
> last fine detail and drown in the minutiae.

So record material, actionable insights only: a defect, a simplification that removes real weight, an ergonomic sharp edge a programmer (or the AI they use) will hit, a test that cannot go red, a doc or docstring that misleads. Not style preferences, not nagging diagnostics, not defensive belt-and-braces, not renames for taste.

LENSES, in priority order:
1. Correctness — error paths, concurrency, cleanup, and fail-closed behaviour on any security or privacy boundary.
2. Simplicity and clarity — dead code, duplication (within the slice or with another slice), accidental complexity, an abstraction that earns nothing.
3. Ergonomics — the API or tool as a programmer, or the AI they use, actually meets it.
4. Performance — hot spots on real paths, never at the expense of clarity.
5. Test rigour — a test that cannot fail, a gap on a branch that matters.
6. Comments and docstrings — per CLAUDE.md § Conventions & Patterns: present tense, the reason plus a spec pointer, no provenance, no restated spec.

METHOD. Read the slice's source first, then its tests, against the owning spec sections (spec/Ownership.md maps each surface to its spec). A finding is a CLAIM until checked: confirm each one at source, and confirm a behaviour claim with a quick REPL or test run where that is cheap. This is a read-only review: edit no file, and run only read-only commands and the slice's existing test lanes.

OUTPUT, recorded on THIS bead and never in a separate file: write the section to a file and append it with `bd update <this bead> --append-notes "$(cat <file>)"` (never `--notes`, which replaces). Head it `== SENIOR REVIEW FINDINGS (<datetime with zone>, trunk <short sha>)` and include:
- 0 to 15 numbered findings, most important first. Each gives: `path:line` (plus a short quote so it can be re-found by text), what is wrong, why it matters (the concrete failure or cost), the fix (a sketch is fine), size (S/M/L), confidence (verified / probable), and its lens.
- A short "looked at and sound" list, so the review's coverage is visible.
- Cross-slice findings, whose defect lives in another slice's files, in a separate list naming the owning slice. Do not act on them.

Then add the label `findings-recorded` and leave the bead OPEN: its findings become this slice's fix work, which the coordinator dispatches in clusters. If the slice needs nothing, record zero findings with the coverage list and close the bead with that as the reason.
notes:
== ROUTED FROM rf2-r5cc2.2 (core subs/views review, trunk 89f5bbc4de) — an item this slice owns

tools/story/src/re_frame/story/ui/open_in_editor.cljs:262 depends on the core editor-URI predicate (source_coords/editor_uri.cljc), which rf2-r5cc2.2 finding 1 shows a tab, newline or leading control character bypasses. The central fix is in flight (worker core-subs-fix); this slice adds a regression at its own call site if the fix has landed, or records the dependency.
== SENIOR REVIEW FINDINGS (2026-10-29 19:19:04 AUSEST, trunk 2f919a180f)

Scope: tools/story/src/re_frame/story/ui/** (63 files) and theme/** (7), with their tests under tools/story/test/re_frame/story/ui/** (80), panels_e2e/** (18) and theme/** (1). Read-only: no test lane run, so every behaviour claim rests on source reading, and "probable" marks the ones a run would settle. Each finding was re-checked at the cited line on trunk. Paths are relative to tools/story/src/re_frame/story/ unless written in full.

1. A variant whose plan doesn't compile blanks the whole Story shell. [correctness · S · verified]
- Where: ui/canvas.cljs:601 `plan           (rf.story.plan/variant-plan`. It compiles during canvas-inner's render with no try.
- No error boundary sits above the canvas. The only getDerivedStateFromError in ui/ is the per-cell boundary at multi_substrate.cljs:432.
- variant-plan throws on everyday authoring states (plan.cljc:1929-1942): a missing [:arg k]; a missing required view-args key (checked even with no validator, plan.cljc:659-672); an unknown assertion id; a malformed step; an unregistered :compose fragment or :extends parent.
- An uncaught render error unmounts the React root, so one bad variant takes down the sidebar, the toolbar and every other variant. That is the "blank page" shell.cljs:344-345 warns about.
- Docs already guards this with variant-plan-quietly (docs.cljc:205), and the runtime's prepare catches the same throw.
- The same untrapped compile is at multi_substrate.cljs:550 and workspace.cljc:358.
- Fix: catch in all three places and render the :rf.error/id and message inline in the subject slot.

2. The Test/Docs result slot misses every run that isn't announced, so Docs and the Evidence spine show stale verdicts, and Run all / watch drive the live frame outside the run owner. [correctness · M · code path verified, race outcome probable]
- Docs' pill and excerpt (docs.cljc:811, 963) and the spine read one slot, ui/evidence_spine.cljc:870 `(get-in @rf.story.ui.test-mode.state/results-atom [variant-id :result])`.
- Only follow-run! writes that slot (ui/test_mode/state.cljs:243-257). It is fed by announce-run!, which is called only at runtime.cljc:1716 and 1767.
- The headless run-variant (runtime.cljc:1513-1547) neither announces nor claims a generation. Run all and watch re-runs use it (ui/sidebar.cljs:691-755).
- (a) In Docs, watch mode turns a variant's dot red while the Docs pill stays green with the old narrative and no staleness marker. That contradicts docs.cljc:284-285 "Docs can never disagree with Test".
- (b) Saving an edit to the selected variant's script both bumps the canvas run-key (an owner run) and drifts the watch hash (a run-variant on the same frame). Two scripts then drive one frame, and the dot keeps whichever lands last.
- (c) spec/003-Render-Shell.md:284-286 says run-variant claims a generation; the code does not.
- Related (probable): retire-run-attempt! (runtime.cljc:1603-1620, reached from the stepper's prepare-variant at :2250) bumps the generation silently. The in-flight run's settle is dropped by follow-run!'s generation check (state.cljs:254) and :running? never clears, so Re-run sticks at "Running…" and Run all stays disabled.
- Fix here: route run-one-test! for a variant with a live owner entry through runtime/rerun!, or skip the selected variant in watch-rerun!. Have the slot record the generation begin-run! saw, so a stale settle can clear :running?.
- The root fix is cross-slice (below).

3. Test-mode step debugger: the scrubber restores the wrong app-db, and the stepper's teardown is bound to the first variant. [correctness · S · verified]
(a) Scrubber:
- ui/test_mode/pure.cljc:333 `(conj acc (:epoch-id (nth tape ti)))` takes each matched play event's own epoch.
- Core commits one epoch per dequeued event (implementation/core/src/re_frame/epoch.cljc:4-7), so a step's :fx [[:dispatch …]] children commit later epochs, and epoch-id-slice skips them.
- Clicking tick k therefore shows the state before step k's children ran.
- Release (state.cljs:176 `(peek epoch-ids)`) restores the last dispatch step's epoch, not the end of the run. That contradicts "reverts to the post-play app-db" (state.cljs:153-155), and pure.cljc:194-196 "exactly one epoch" is false.
- After a scrub and release, the canvas shows a state the run never ended in.
- Fix: for each tick take the last tape epoch before the next matched event (the tape end for the last tick); store the tape's final :epoch-id and restore it on release.

(b) Stepper teardown:
- ui/test_mode/stepper_view.cljs:284 `(when (get @rf.story.ui.test-mode.stepper-state/results-atom variant-id)`. The will-unmount closes over the id the class was built with.
- view.cljs:730 mounts `[…stepper-section variant-id]` with no key, and view.cljs:691-698 itself says an A→B switch is a prop update.
- So A's auto-play interval keeps stepping A's frame after the switch. On unmount end! runs for A, and B's interval, state entry and trace listener leak.
- Fix: `^{:key (str variant-id)}`, or read the id from (r/argv this).

4. The mode-tab strip re-seeds the tab from localStorage during render, which fights the URL and breaks Back. [correctness · S · verified at source, browser behaviour probable]
- ui/mode_tabs.cljs:169 `(hydrate-from-storage! variant-id)` runs on every render and writes whenever [:active-mode-tab vid] is absent (:94).
- url_state.cljc:291-292 deliberately dissocs that slot when a popped URL has no mode-tab=. The comment at :280-290 describes the very Back-twice-to-Canvas case that dissoc exists for.
- The next render, after the popstate hydration guard has closed, reloads the stored tab, and the watcher (url_state.cljc:559-562) pushes it as a new history entry.
- Result: Back lands on Docs or Tests instead of Canvas, and the forward history is cut. A shared ?variant=x link also opens on the recipient's last-used tab.
- Fix: load the stored tab once, on the selection edge (shell's selection watcher, skipped while url-state/hydrating?). spec/007-Mode-Tabs.md:126-128 ("safe on every render") changes with it.

5. :cannot-run is not shown as a distinct state on three surfaces, and every region except the sidebar ignores the shared status vocabulary. [correctness · S · verified]
spec/017 requires :cannot-run to render distinctly, and spec/018 §12.6 asks for one tool-wide vocabulary.

(a) Assertion strip:
- ui/assertion_strip.cljs:280-290 (row and glyph style maps) and :306 status-glyph have no :cannot-run entry.
- summary-line (:134-154) yields "", and the first-paint open seed (:496) covers only #{:fail :error}.
- test_mode/pure.cljc:119-120 does produce :cannot-run rows, so a refusal renders as an unknown "·" row with no reason.

(b) Play chip:
- play_status.cljs:178-183, :187-192 `(str status)` and :223-228 have no arm for it, although play/runner.cljc:479 finishes runs with :cannot-run.
- Result: idle styling and the literal text ":cannot-run".

(c) Stepper:
- ui/test_mode/stepper_pure.cljc:45 `(false? (:passed? result))  :fail` is checked before any cannot-run test.
- Refused steps carry :passed? false :cannot-run? true (play/runner_events.cljc:456-463).
- Result: a red ✗ while the pane shows ⊘.

Root cause:
- theme/status.cljc's ns docstring (:4-9) says the test-mode rows, evidence beats and play banner use it.
- In fact only sidebar.cljs, sidebar_signals.cljc, sidebar_styles.cljs and test_mode/visual_a11y_view.cljs require it.
- test_mode/view.cljs:168-179 and 347-354, docs.cljc:770-790, play_status.cljs, stepper_view.cljs:59-73 and the strip each keep their own map, and those maps already disagree. :fail is ✗ in the vocabulary but ● at view.cljs:350, and the :pending pill reads "not run yet" in Docs but "no assertions recorded" in Test.
- test_mode/pure.cljc:115-127 and :682-689 also re-derive record status with the fallback opposite to verdict.cljc:60-68 record-status (`:else :fail` against `:else :pass`).

Fix:
- Drive these surfaces from rf.story.theme.status/descriptor and chip-style.
- Make play.runner's cannot-run-step? public and use it in stepper_pure.
- Call verdict/record-status in pure.cljc.
- Add :cannot-run to spec/004-Assertions.md:224-232.

6. A run that judged nothing paints green, and the test that pins "grey" cannot see it. [correctness/test rigour · S · verified]
- ui/state/tests.cljc:131 `(contains? rf.story.verdict/statuses status)` lets the explicit run :status win before the `(zero? total) :pending` check.
- Both writers always pass :status (test_mode/state.cljs:144, sidebar.cljs:720), and result.cljc:45-49 makes a clean zero-assertion run :pass.
- Result: a script-only :test variant gets a green dot and a green "0 passed" pill. spec/009-Test-Mode.md:366-369 says the dot "stays grey", and the :pending pill text (test_mode/view.cljs:178) is unreachable.
- tools/story/test/re_frame/story/ui/test_widget_cljs_test.cljc:46-49 pins the grey case with a summary carrying no :status, which production never sends, so it cannot go red.
- Also view.cljs:179 shows a red "0 failed of N" for a tape-floor :fail in which every assertion passed.
- Fix: map (and (= :pass status) (zero? total)) to :pending in record-test-run and in pure run-status. If the intended rule is the other way, change spec/009 instead; spec/009 and result.cljc cannot both stand.
- Then pin the case with :status :pass in the fixture, and name the cause when the counts don't explain a :fail.

7. The element inspector attaches once, at shell mount, so Inspect mode usually does nothing. [correctness/ergonomics · S · verified]
- ui/shell.cljs:1048 `(rf.story.ui.element-inspector/install!))` is install!'s only caller (git grep), run from a 0ms timer at mount.
- It resolves [data-test="story-canvas-frame"] at that moment (canvas_listeners.cljs:41-49, and a nil root is a no-op at :73). That node exists only for a selected variant on the Canvas or Tests tab.
- First visit with nothing selected, or any Canvas→Docs→Canvas round trip (the bound node is detached), leaves the inspector attached to nothing.
- Effect: the chip turns on and shows the crosshair, but no overlay appears, clicks reach the variant's own handlers (the very thing element_inspector.cljc:39-41 exists to intercept), and Esc does nothing.
- The recorder already re-installs when it starts (recorder.cljs:383).
- Fix: call (install!) in set-active! when turning on (element_inspector.cljc:199).

8. The accessibility scan never runs on a multi-substrate variant, and its violation outlines are never removed. [correctness · S · verified]
(a) Multi-substrate:
- The multi? arm at ui/canvas.cljs:722-725 stamps no data-rf-story-variant-root. It is stamped only at canvas.cljs:781 and in workspace.cljc; multi_substrate.cljs has only a docstring mention.
- So run-axe! takes the :no-root arm (a11y.cljs:498-506), and tells a user who is already in :dev to "switch to :dev mode".
- Fix: stamp the marker on each cell's subject and pass axe an {:include [...]} context.

(b) Outlines:
- a11y.cljs:469 `(.setAttribute el "data-rf-a11y-violation"`. Nothing in tools/story/src removes it; the only removeAttribute is chrome_a11y.cljs:251, which removes its own flag.
- After a re-scan, or a control edit that resets the frame, fixed elements keep their outlines while the panel reads 0 violations. Chrome a11y shares the helper (chrome_a11y.cljs:364).
- Fix: clear [data-rf-a11y-violation] inside the scope before stamping, and in drop-frame-state!.

9. Controls: a keyword arg with no schema turns into a string on the first keystroke. [correctness · S · verified]
- ui/controls.cljs:226 `(keyword? v)  {:widget :text}`. The value-shape fallback drops the :coerce :keyword that the schema path sets (:189).
- So render-text (:457-464) uses on-string-change, and :large becomes the string ":large", then ":larges".
- This hits every story without a props schema, including all Fresco stories (multi_substrate.cljs:84-86), and nested map values (the fallback is reused at :128). coerce-input already accepts the leading colon (schema_form.cljc:245).
- Fix: `{:widget :text :coerce :keyword}`, plus a value-shape test row beside the schema-path ones in controls_scalar_widgets_cljs_test.cljc.
10. Every keystroke in a control pushes a browser history entry. [ergonomics · S · verified at source, throttling probable]
- ui/url_state.cljc:562 `(push! url))))))`. The focused variant's overrides count as URL-relevant (:160), and on-string-change (controls.cljs:402-406) writes on every input event.
- So typing "Hello world" leaves 11 Back-button stops, and a slider drag leaves dozens.
- Browsers throttle bursts of pushState, and push! swallows the error (:469-471), so the address bar (the override-sharing surface) can silently stop tracking edits.
- replace! (:473) has no caller.
- Fix: use replace! when only the focused overrides changed, and push! for selection, tab, mode and chrome. Reword the docstring at :39-44.

11. Share egress overstates reproducibility in two ways. [correctness · S · verified]
(a) Copy EDN:
- ui/share.cljs:355 emits `[:args (pr-str eff)]`, the cell's full effective args.
- Its badge (:807) comes from current-share-report (:290-301 → egress.cljc:259-263), which inspects only the overrides, :world and :script.
- Result: a variant declaring a callback arg (`:args {:on-click (fn …)}`) gets a snippet containing #object[Function] under a "fully reproducible" badge. That breaks spec/022 §3, and the docstring at share.cljs:340-342 ("the badge already flags that case") is false.
- Fix: classify against eff (classify needs an args input, which is cross-slice), or emit only the delta from the parent.

(b) Import hint:
- share.cljs:207-210 sets [:rf.story/share-import-hint vid] when stale overrides are dropped. Nothing clears it when a later hydration drops nothing; only dismiss does (:217).
- The banner and :dropped (read at :292) therefore survive a pop back to a clean entry, and every badge reads "partially reproducible" until the user dismisses it.
- Fix: `(not (seq dropped)) (update :rf.story/share-import-hint dissoc variant-id)`.

FINDINGS (most severe first)

1. P3. Re-making a frame that was built without `:images` under the same id, now with an `:images` vector, keeps serving cached subscriptions its new image does not select.
   - Where: live_frame.cljc:1027-1035 (make-frame calls `invalidate-subs-for-generation-change!` with `(or (:generation displaced) {})`), :1200-1228 (that fn condemns only `:added`/`:changed`/`:removed` from `generation-diff`), :1124-1150 (`generation-diff {} G` names only G's keys, all `:added`).
   - Failure scenario: `(rf/make-frame {:id :app})` resolves the whole store live. A view holds `[:beta/y]` (registered in ns probe.beta). Hot reload then re-evaluates the declaration as `(rf/make-frame {:id :app :images [(rf/image {:select-ns {:include ["probe.alpha"]}})]})`. The new generation does not resolve `:beta/y`, but the slot is never condemned: the held reaction keeps computing the old body, and a FRESH `(rf/subscribe [:beta/y] {:frame :app})` hits the cache and returns it. A frame made with that image from the start reports `:rf.error/no-such-sub`. Spec 002 §Image resolution and composition says a frame that wants a narrower set names it with an explicit image, and the docstring at live_frame.cljc:1152-1199 says the cache's CONTENTS must follow the generation. The comment at :1027-1030 ("compare from an empty generation, which condemns every sub the incoming generation resolves") shows the gap: subs the OLD live resolution answered, outside the new image, are never condemned. The test fixture's `:rf/default`, which also has no `:generation`, takes the same path.
   - Evidence: EXECUTED (probe 1, exit 0).
     - Case A, live-store re-made with `[img-alpha]`: before the re-make, held deref = "beta-body" and cache keys = #{[:beta/y]}. After it, the generation resolves `:beta/y`? = false, cache keys = #{[:beta/y]}, and a fresh subscribe -> reaction, value "beta-body".
     - Control B, made with `[img-alpha]` from the start: fresh subscribe -> `:rf.error/no-such-sub`, value nil.
     - Control C, image-to-image re-make `[img-both]` -> `[img-alpha]` (the diff names `:beta/y` as `:removed`): cache keys = #{} after the re-make, and a fresh subscribe -> `:rf.error/no-such-sub`.
   - Smallest fix: when the displaced record carries no `:generation`, the old resolution cannot be diffed from a generation, so condemn every sub id cached in the frame as well as the incoming generation's: pass the union of `G`'s `:sub` ids and the heads of the frame's cache keys to `rf.subs.cache/invalidate-frame-subs!`. Held reactions then re-acquire through the existing on-dispose seam. Fence: live_frame.cljc (`make-frame` / `invalidate-subs-for-generation-change!`) plus one test. No hot-zone file.
   - Gate: core JVM lane (`clojure -M:test` in implementation/core). A new deftest in live_frame_reload_cljs_test.cljc (.cljc, so the JVM lane runs it) asserting the Case A shape: cache evicted, fresh subscribe -> no-such-sub.
   - Decision needed? No.

2. P3. Under the React-hook spine (UIx, dev builds), a registered view whose output toggles between a React element and nil fires a false `:rf.view/unmounted` on every element-to-nil step, and its next render reports `:mount? true`.
   - Where: spine.cljs:2209-2240 (`with-unmount-sentinel`). The pass-through branch at :2232-2233, `(if (nil? (some-> ^js annotated .-type)) annotated ...)`, pairs the sentinel only with element output. Consequence: views.cljs:319-333 (`emit-view-unmounted!` does `(swap! seen-render-keys disj render-key)`).
   - Failure scenario: a `(defui banner [] (when @(use-sub [:show?]) ($ :div "hi")))` registered through `reg-view`. While `:show?` is true the wrapped render returns Fragment(element, sentinel). When it flips false the render returns bare nil, so React deletes the Fragment, and the sentinel's empty-deps cleanup emits `:rf.view/unmounted` for render key [id K]. The instance is still mounted: componentize-view (spine.cljs:2372-2379) keeps K stable in its `useRef`. The emit evicts K from `seen-render-keys`, so when `:show?` flips back the next render reads as a first render (`:mount? true`). Xray and the Pair MCP, which consume these events, see an unmount and remount on each toggle. rf2-r5cc2.2 finding 2's fix (#11727) closed the sentinel-as-moving-child shape and kept "non-element output passes through unchanged". A view whose ROOT is conditional is the remaining shape, and a common one (`(when …)` roots, loading placeholders that return nil).
   - Evidence: INSPECTED (CLJS-only; no build allowed). Source lines above; React deletes a Fragment child subtree when the parent's output becomes null, running its effect cleanups.
   - Smallest fix, two options:
     (a) On the React-render path, pair non-element output too: return `Fragment(annotated, sentinel)` whenever the shell's `rf.adapter.context/*instance-token*` binding is present (a React render through componentize-view), keeping the raw pass-through only for a headless direct invocation, whose return value callers read.
     (b) Move the unmount effect into the componentize-view shell's React-render branch, which is one real fiber for the instance's whole life and already holds the token. On that path the sentinel is then unnecessary.
     Fence: spine.cljs plus a UIx DOM test. No hot-zone file; spec/006 needs no change.
   - Gate: the UIx browser lane, e.g. a case in implementation/adapters/uix/test/re_frame/adapter/uix_client_root_dom_cljs_test.cljs that toggles a registered view's root between nil and an element and asserts no `:rf.view/unmounted` and a stable `:mount? false`.
   - Decision needed? No; (a) is the smaller change, (b) the structural one.

CONSIDERED AND REJECTED
- `(rf/clear :sub id)` leaves a live-store frame's cached reaction in place, while an image frame drops it through reprojection. This is a documented ruling (registrar.cljc:954-956: "an explicit `(rf/clear :sub id)` is registry-only and leaves the cache to `clear-sub-cache!`"). Not a finding.
- sub_override_context.cljs:74-76 reads only `_currentValue`: declined in rf2-3x7nj.2 and left in rf2-r5cc2.2 NOT SETTLED. Not re-proposed.
- interop.clj:111-124: the `Reaction` deftype's `^:unsynchronized-mutable` callbacks are not thread-safe, but `rf.interop/make-reaction` has no JVM production caller. A grep over implementation/ found only interop_dispose_registry_test.clj and bench/read_attribution.clj, with the definition as the control.
- plain_atom.cljc:132-135: the JVM derived value has no disposed flag. Deliberate, and the comment states why: a re-registered callback fires on the next dispose.
- A JVM first construction's provisional record is invisible to `invalidate-sub-on-replace!` running on another thread, so a sub cached by an `:initial-events` cascade could miss a concurrent `reg-sub` replacement. Needs a subscribe inside setup plus a concurrent reg-sub: minutiae.
- frame.cljc:3174-3209: a failed live-to-image re-registration with an intervening reprojection keeps the reprojected generation beside the restored `:live-store? true`. JVM race, narrow window, and the generation wins resolution: minutiae.
- An `:initial-events` step whose event has no handler is not a strict-construction failure (frame.cljc:2599-2635 excludes `:rf.error/no-such-handler`). Spec 002 is silent on it, so this is not a contract breach.
- Re-checked sound: identity.cljc's set and map duplicate rules on both surfaces after the fix; `with-epoch` closing inside a running drain (spine.cljs:303-355), whose body escape reaches the running drain's per-thunk catch and is not dropped; the use-sub removable on-dispose arm/disarm and its four re-acquisition guards (spine.cljs:3165-3343, subs.cljc:2498-2548); adapter.cljc install/dispose/publish under `capability-lock`, `derived-container?`'s three-way reading, and the nil-container guard; capture_frame.cljc's incarnation pin and `:rf.frame/expected-incarnation` threading; use_frame.cljs's `=`+`identical?` memo; context.cljs's secondary-slot fallback (only on an untouched primary); interop.cljs's LongTimeout hop chain and cancellation; frame.cljc's visibility predicate, the upsert create/re-register/rollback branches, the destroy claim/pending/recipe, and `call-serialized-with-drain!`'s release re-kick.

NOT SETTLED
- Finding 2 and every spine.cljs read are CLJS-only and were not run (no shadow-cljs).
- Not read in this pass: spine.cljs 1038-2141 (client roots, after-render, dispose-adapter, render-to-string, frame-provider element, flush-render!, source-coord injection), 2477-3149 (provisional escrow, the bulk of make-react-spine) and 3346-4165 (use-subscribe forms, make-react-adapter, the ratom spine and adapter); frame.cljc 4035-4084. rf2-r5cc2.2 read spine.cljs at 89f5bbc4de and #11727 fixed what it found. This pass adds nothing about those ranges.
- Whether Fresco installs the spine's `:wrap-view` (rf2-r5cc2.7 raised it) was not checked. If it does, finding 2 applies there too.

CROSS-SLICE
- None. Finding 1's fix lives in live_frame.cljc (this slice); it calls subs/cache.cljc's `invalidate-frame-subs!` unchanged.

DESCRIPTION VS TREE
- The description says rf2-r5cc2.4's fixes "merged in #11726". Its own close reason says PR #11736, with #11726 being an earlier PR that fixed the routed retention item. The fixes are present at source either way (above).
- File list, the 14-file / 13884-line count and the scope-measurement trunk all match: core src is unchanged between 7d82a2f6d3 and c60cec9c20.

close_reason:
Both findings FIXED in PR #11789 (head 3edc7cc8e9, CI green: 72 success / 10 skipped / 0 failed, All required checks passed).

1. FIXED. A live frame (made without :images) re-made under the same id with :images kept serving cached subs its new image does not select. Reproduced at trunk 99eee14cbc. Fix in live_frame.cljc make-frame: when the displaced record has no :generation and the new record has one, every cached slot is condemned via rf.subs.cache/invalidate-frame-subs! (the heads of the frame's cache keys, reason :hot-reload). A re-make that stays live leaves the cache alone. Pinned by implementation/core/test/re_frame/live_frame_remake_with_images_cljs_test.cljc (JVM and CLJS), with the defect case plus three controls: an image from the start reports :rf.error/no-such-sub, an image-to-image re-make evicts the dropped sub, and a live-to-live re-make keeps the reaction identical?. Plant: with the branch disabled, the namespace goes red on the defect case only (evicted? false, no no-such-sub reported). Restore verified by blob hash against HEAD. Core JVM count went from 1438 tests / 4378 assertions to 1442 / 4382, exactly the predicted +4/+4.

2. FIXED. Under the React-hook spine, a view whose root toggles element -> nil fired a false :rf.view/unmounted, and its next render reported :mount? true. Reproduced at trunk by a plant that reverts the fix: under UIx the toggle emitted false unmounts, :mount? read (true false true false), and a real teardown while nil emitted nothing. Fix in spine.cljs with-unmount-sentinel: on a React render every output is paired with the sentinel, nil included. A headless direct invocation still passes non-element output through, as the shared suite pins. Shape chosen: the reviewer's option (a), but recognising a React render by its props object (react-props? on the first argument, the predicate the registered head already uses) instead of the instance-token binding. Fresco installs the spine's :wrap-view but no :componentize-view, so under Fresco a core reg-view head is the bare frame-aware wrapper that React mounts directly. There is no shell and no token on that path, so neither the token check nor option (b) (moving the effect into the componentize shell) would cover it. The props check covers UIx and Fresco alike. Pinned by implementation/adapters/uix/test/re_frame/adapter/uix_view_conditional_root_dom_cljs_test.cljs (UIx head) and implementation/core/test/re_frame/substrate/spine_conditional_root_dom_cljs_test.cljs (a spine adapter with no :componentize-view, Fresco's shape). Each asserts no false unmount, and exactly one unmount at a real teardown taken while the view renders nil. With the fix reverted, the browser lane went red on exactly those two namespaces (5 failures). Restore verified by blob hash.

No spec text change needed: Spec 009 already says one :rf.view/unmounted per instance teardown, and Spec 002 already says a frame wanting a narrower set names it with an explicit image.

Local gates (captured exits): test-jvm-implementation.sh 0; npm run test:cljs 0 (6723 tests / 19619 assertions); npm run test:adapter-smokes 0. npm run test:browser exited 1 on 4 Reagent routing/SSR namespaces that never reach the spine wrap-view. Those 4 passed in the planted re-run and in CI's :browser-test on the same commit, so they were a local-load flake.
